courses.title: Special Topics in Art
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 16 units.
courses.description: Special topics in art.

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Special Topics in Art
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 16 units.
courses.description: Special topics in art.

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Art + Ecology
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 16 units.
courses.description: Explores relationships between art, environment, and sustainability through the lens of Traditional Ecological Knowledge (TEK). Students engage with Indigenous worldviews, gardens, and material processes that reveal how art can sustain reciprocal relationships between humans and the natural world. Requires trips to the Santa Barbara Botanical Garden, UCSB Gardens, and UC Nature Reserves.

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Special Topics in Art
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 16 units.
courses.description: Special topics in art.

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Capstone Design Lab
courses.description: Students in Art 189A-B-C will be working in teams together with mechanical engineering students on a mechanical engineering capstone design project. The teams work under the direction of a faculty advisor in mechanical engineering, and to a lesser extent an advisor from the art department (and possibly an industrial sponsor) to tackle an engineering design project. Engineering communication, such as reports and oral presentations, are covered. Emphasis on practical, hands-on experience, and the integration of analytical and design skills. Students should aim to commit to taking A, B and C in order to work with their team from conception to finalization of a project. This lab is the first of three the series.

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Capstone Design Lab
courses.description: Students in Art 189A-B-C will be working in teams together with mechanical engineering students on a mechanical engineering capstone design project. The teams work under the direction of a faculty advisor in mechanical engineering, and to a lesser extent an advisor from the art department (and possibly an industrial sponsor) to tackle an engineering design project. Engineering communication, such as reports and oral presentations, are covered. Emphasis on practical, hands-on experience, and the integration of analytical and design skills. Students should aim to commit to taking A, B and C in order to work with their team from conception to finalization of a project.This lab is second of three in the series

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Capstone Design Lab
courses.description: Students in Art 189A-B-C will be working in teams together with mechanical engineering students on a mechanical engineering capstone design project. The teams work under the direction of a faculty advisor in mechanical engineering, and to a lesser extent an advisor from the art department (and possibly an industrial sponsor) to tackle an engineering design project. Engineering communication, such as reports and oral presentations, are covered. Emphasis on practical, hands-on experience, and the integration of analytical and design skills. Students should aim to commit to taking A, B and C in order to work with their team from conception to finalization of a project. This lab is third of three in the series.

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Internship in Art
courses.comments: Students must have a 3.0 overall GPA.
courses.description: Opportunities in applied learning related to visual art through local museums, art galleries, and other art related organizations or institutions. Students work under the direction of the faculty sponsor who maintains contact with the supervisor for whom the student is interning.

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Exhibition Studies Internship
courses.comments: Students must have a 3.0 overall GPA.
courses.description: This internship provides pedagogical and practical support for students exhibiting work within the Arts Building and other venues across campus such as Cheadle Hall and the University Library. Among other skills, the course will include intensive training in exhibition scheduling and curating, installation and display, the production of didactic supplements such as information sheets, wall texts and titles, methods of promotion as well as de-installation and art handling.

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Internship in Art
courses.comments: Students must have a 3.0 overall GPA.
courses.description: Opportunities in applied learning related to visual art through local museums, art galleries, and other art related organizations or institutions. Students work under the direction of the faculty sponsor who maintains contact with the supervisor for whom the student is interning.

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Honors Seminar
courses.prereq_text: L&S and CCS Art majors only; upper-division standing; acceptance into department honors program.
courses.comments: Students must have a 3.5 grade-point average in the major and at least a 3.0 grade-point average overall.
courses.description: Seminar designed to focus on criticism of current art work. A total of 12 units in this course required to complete honors program. Completion of seminar units followed by public exhibition of work accomplished.

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Independent Studies
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of two upper-division courses in Art; consent of instructor and department required.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding three quarters and are limited to 5 units per quarter (without petition) and 16 units total in all 199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
courses.description: Independent studies. Advanced independent or collaborative work in consultation with individual faculty; individual tutorial.

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Independent Research Assistance in Art
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division students only; consent of instructor and department.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters and are limited to 5 units per quarter (without petition) and 16 units total in all 199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
courses.description: Coursework shall consist of faculty supervised research assistance.

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Experimental Video & Animation
courses.description: The development of independent, innovative projects that utilize digital and/or post-production and hybrid means to create video-works for screens and surfaces, including projection, installation, distributed platforms. Projects may employ a variety of strategies and methodologies in concept, production, and presentation. Broad exposure to contemporary and pioneering video/film, with an emphasis on experimentation in substance and form.

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Graduate Seminar in Critique
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.
courses.description: A seminar focusing on criticism of current art work.

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Graduate Theory Seminar
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.
courses.description: In-depth look at contemporary media and art discourse framed through a wide range of theoretical approaches: formalism, structuralism, phenomenology, psychoanalysis, Marxism, gender and queer studies, poststructuralism, postcolonial theory, deconstruction, issues of authorship, narratology, and multiculturalism. Specific content varies with instructor.

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Graduate Seminar in Visual Arts
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.
courses.description: A means of making special studies and meeting special curricular problems.

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: All Faculty Graduate Seminar
courses.description: Symposium format course presents contemporary artists' creative projects in relation to recent developments in art and cross-disciplinary practices. Lectures by faculty from UCSB's Art Department supplemented by distinguished guests invited to expand on art, theory and cultural production.

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Teaching Assistant Practicum
courses.description: Practice of teaching art.

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Directed Study in Visual Arts Education
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.
courses.description: Individual tutorial.

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: M.F.A. Thesis Project
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.
courses.description: Individual tutorial.

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Special Studies in Art
courses.description: A means of making special studies and meeting special curricular problems.

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Direct Historical Reading and Research
courses.description: Independent research involving extensive reading and written essay on a particular period, artist, or body of work with a historical context.

courses.subject: ART CS
courses.title: Group Studies
courses.description: Student-directed discussion and study in a variety of subjects within Art.

courses.subject: ART CS
courses.title: Graphic Study of the History of Graphic Ideas: Drawing
courses.comments: May be taken as often as once each quarter.
courses.description: The surviving works of art from the paleolithic period until now constitutean existing order that may be considered the proper material for study by aspiring draughtsmen and painters. Art CS 10 emphasizes drawing.

courses.subject: ART CS
courses.title: Art Colloquium
courses.comments: May be taken as often as once each quarter.
courses.description: Students receiving credit will present talks in their field on material arranged in consultation with the instructor. Credit assigned by the instructor will reflect the extent and quality of participation.

courses.subject: ART CS
courses.title: Drawing and Painting
courses.description: Emphasis on the practice and development of making paintings and drawings.

courses.subject: ART CS
courses.title: Themes
courses.comments: May be taken as often as once each quarter.
courses.description: Drawing and painting in sequences, and according to themes.

courses.subject: ART CS
courses.title: Prints
courses.description: Emphasis on letterpress printing using metal and wooden type; typography; various relief print methods and materials utilized will be determined by particular faculty interest.

courses.subject: ART CS
courses.title: Book Arts
courses.description: The study and practice of the book arts; artists' books; typography; letterpress printing; both traditional and experimental uses of the printing press.

courses.subject: ART CS
courses.title: History, Theory, and Criticism
courses.description: Non-studio emphasis on historical, theoretical, and contemporary ideas and issues. A range of concepts will be discussed, from various approaches,according to the particular interests of faculty and students.

courses.subject: ART CS
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: This special studies course allows faculty to design and execute courses that reflect their particular research and teaching.

courses.subject: ART CS
courses.title: Sculpture
courses.description: Practice in the design and development of making a sculpture using various materials as determined by particular faculty interest.

courses.subject: ART CS
courses.title: Sculpture-Related Studies
courses.description: Non-studio emphasis on generation and development of images, ideas, and imagination through field trips, slides, presentations, and videos. Primarily for sculptors.

courses.subject: ART CS
courses.title: Internship
courses.description: Academic credit for professional experience with an approved organization or individual.

courses.subject: ART CS
courses.title: Independent Studies
courses.comments: Creative Studies students may enroll in a maximum of 24 units of Independent Studies courses per year, with a total of 45 units counted toward graduation.
courses.description: Serious independent study in art with consenting faculty member.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Introduction to Architecture and Environment
courses.description: Architecture is an act of place-making through which humans have constructed their relation with nature. Introduces the history of these strategies of place-making, interpretative concepts, and discipline-specific terminology in order to develop a critical understanding of the relationship between nature and built form.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Introduction to Museum Studies
courses.description: Designed to introduce students to various aspects of Museum Studies- historical, theoretical, and practical- by examining a range of issues and topics with which the field is engaged.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Art Survey II: Renaissance-Baroque Art
courses.description: Renaissance and baroque art in Northern and Southern Europe.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Art Survey III: Modern-Contemporary Art
courses.comments: ARTHIW 6C is the online version of ARTHI 6C.
courses.description: Introduction to the modern era of Western art history, focusing on European and American histories. It begins reviewing the 18th-century European Enlightenment: scientific inquiry and new forms of representation are the models for the course. Proceeding through the 19th-century histories of colonization and land grabs, and then move to the 20th-century, focusing on the rise of urbanism, migration, and new developments in abstract art; additional focus on ethnicity, race, sexuality and gender across the Arts & Crafts Movement, and the rise of internationalism and global art histories in the 21st-century, ending the course by examining the present time period.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Survey: History of Art in China
courses.description: Chronological and thematic overview of the major traditions of Chinese art, Neolithic to modern, including ceramics and bronzes, Buddhist visual culture, paintings, calligraphy, garden design and imperial architecture, with an emphasis on historical context, regional diversity, and intercultural encounters.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: WORLD CULTURES AND CURRENTS
courses.description: Explores how cultural encounters shaped the history of globalization from antiquity to the present by evaluating the long history of Africa-Europe encounters as revealed through visual culture. Uses the landmark publication The Image of the Black in Western Art as a principal framework for exploring the long history of African presence in Europe from classical antiquity to the present. Through analysis of paintings, sculpture, manuscripts, mosaics, prints, decorative arts, and photography, students examine how images of Africans in Western art illuminate commercial exchange, religious devotion, diplomacy, military alliances, migration, artistic patronage, and cultural interaction across continents.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Survey: Architecture and Planning
courses.description: A selective and chronological survey of architecture and urban design in social and historical context. Individual buildings and urban plans from the past to the present will be used as examples.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Survey: History of Photography
courses.description: A critical survey of nineteenth and twentieth century photography as an art form.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Survey: Arts of the Ancient Americas
courses.comments: ARTHI 6H and LAIS 6H are the same course.
courses.description: An introduction to select art traditions from Mesoamerica to Andean South America. Examines architecture, ceramics, sculpture, painting and other classes of material culture for their meaning and function within sociopolitical, religious, and economic contexts.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: The Arts of the Iberian World, 1492-1700
courses.description: This survey course offers an overview of the varied artistic cultures developed under the Spanish Empire during the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, covering, besides the Iberian Peninsula, different parts of Europe and North and West Africa, the Spanish Americas, and a number of transpacific territories. In addition to exposing students to an astoundingly rich set of materials, it introduces them to key theoretical themes, such as Indigenous agency, borderlands and frontier territories, religious intolerance and coercion, cross-cultural exchange, resistance, racialization, and revisions of the center/periphery and hybridity/mestizaje models.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Survey: Contemporary Architecture
courses.description: Global survey of architectural production in the twenty-first century. Emphasis on form and technology, as well as economic, sociopolitical context. Explores built form at a variety of scales (buildings, cities, virtual spaces), as well as the concept of a contemporary.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Survey: Islamic Art and Architecture
courses.description: A survey of Islamic art and architecture.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Playful Spaces: A Cultural History of Games
courses.description: This course introduces students to the history of games. It is organized chronologically as a global survey. We study games and the social, political, and economic conditions that support them, as well as the interface between the human player and the imagined world of the game. Taking as its premise that games are artifacts of culture, this course focuses on the visual and spatial practice of games in social context.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Survey: Eccentric Images
courses.description: This course examines the history of art through some of its strangest images, including spatial illusions, chance images, hidden faces and monsters, reversible images, caricatures and others. Primarily focused on the early modern period (1400-1750), we also consider similar experiments from other cultures.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Introduction to Classical Archaeology
courses.description: Introduces students to the field of Classical Archaeology through case studies drawn from all over the ancient world, with an emphasis on the Mediterranean. Explores both the practical methods of archaeology as well as the artifacts that are found and how they are preserved, displayed, and who owns them.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Ancient Spectacle
courses.description: Explores the worlds of ancient Greece and Rome through the participants in and observers of a variety of spectacles in the ancient world. Examines public spectacles such as bull-leaping, Olympic games, theatrical performances, gladiatorial combats, naval battles, religious rituals, and military triumphs, as well as other more private spectacles such as dinner parties with the gods.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Medieval Architecture: From Constantine to Charlemagne
courses.description: A survey of the architecture in Italy, France, Spain, Germany, and England from the early Christian through the Carolingian periods.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: The Global Middle Ages: Visual and Cultural Encounters in the Medieval Mediterranean
courses.description: Focusing on the Mediterranean, this course considers visual manifestations of exchange. Its goal is to examine the complexity of religious, political, and visual interactions in the Middle Ages, a period that brought together diverse religious communities, generating both social frictions and new cultural forms. Students will study the dynamic interplay among Christian, Jewish, and Islamic visual cultures as they developed and coalesced through commerce, gift exchange, the reinterpretation of pre-existing forms, and the reuse of objects and spaces.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Introduction to Medieval Art and Architecture
courses.description: This course explores the soaring cathedrals, monstrous sculptures, and marvelous images that inspired The Lord of the Rings and Game of Thrones. Beginning with the fourth-century rise of Christian images and ending with the advent of print, it traces how images developed new roles and reinvented old ones over the course of the Middle Ages. Investigating architecture, sculpture, and manuscripts in their historical contexts, it asks why medieval objects look the way the do and how viewers saw them.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Art and War
courses.description: We often think about art as a bridge between cultures and look to masterpieces like the Sistine Chapel as the height of a nations cultural achievements. But during times of war, art can become military targets and destroyed, or used to create enemies. Conversely, art has been employed to resist political establishments, critique violence, and provide therapy for veterans. Drawing examples from different time periods, this course investigates the myriad ways art has been usedand abusedduring military conflict.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Art of Medieval Spain: Visual and Cultural Encounters
courses.description: Focusing on medieval Spain, this course considers visual manifestations of exchange. Its goal is to examine the complexity of religious, political, and visual interactions on the Iberian Peninsula, where Christians, Muslims, and Jews co-existed. Students will study the dynamic interplay among Christian, Jewish, and Islamic visual cultures as they developed and coalesced through conquest, commerce, gift exchange, social intermingling, and diplomatic relations.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Painting in the 15th-Century Netherlands
courses.description: Netherlandish painting from C1400- C1500 examined in its social, religious,and cultural contexts. Van Eyck, Rogier, Bouts and Memling, among others.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Painting in the 16th-Century Netherlands
courses.description: Painting of the low countries from C1500-C1600, placed in its social and cultural contexts. Artists studied include Bosch and Bruegel. continuation from 107A, but may be taken separately.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Renaissance Kunst- and Wunderkammern: the First Museums
courses.description: In the sixteenth century, wealthy merchants and powerful princes in Europe began assembling vast collections that aspired to contain all possible knowledge of all possible things. From these remarkably diverse collections called Kunst- and Wunderkammern (German), studioli (Italian), and curiosity cabinets (English)arose our modern museums of art, science, history and technology, as well as modern research collections in universities. This course explores these fascinating collections, the purposes that they served and the circumstances in which they were created.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Special Topics in Fifteenth and Sixteenth Century Northern European Art
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Specialized classes exploring critical issues in European art from the Netherlands, Germany, France, and/or England. Courses may take the form of in-depth studies of particular artists (e.g. Durer) or themes (e.g. iconoclasm).

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: De-centering Renaissance Art: 1500-1600
courses.description: Developments in a variety of artistic media with attention to issues of geography, empires, religion, workshop culture, and theory.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Art, Science, and Technology in the Renaissance
courses.description: An approach to the art of the Renaissance that focuses on intersections with scientific and technological practices that conditioned its historical development.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Art and the Environment in the Early Modern Period
courses.description: Examines the intersection of artistic practices and environmental thinking during the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries. An introduction to eco-art history, the class is organized around a series of key themes, which will allow us to explore, among other things, the role of empire building and colonialism in the transformation of landscapes worldwide; the formation of a host of ideas about resources and environmental management; the emergence of certain forms of ecological sensibility during the period, including notions of (and actions towards) environmental justice; as well as the ways in which artworks and built environments mediated people’s understanding of and ties to their natural surroundings.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Dutch Art in the Age of Rembrandt
courses.prereq_text: At least one Art History course. Not open to freshman.
courses.description: Visual culture produced in Northern Netherlands between 1579 and 1648. Classes devoted to individual artists (e.g. Rembrandt, Frans Hals) and genres (e.g. landscapes, portraiture, history painting) in relation to material culture and thought of the period.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Seventeenth Century Art in Italy I
courses.comments: Not open to students who have completed Art History 113A.
courses.description: Italian painting, sculpture, architecture, and urbanism from the late sixteenth to late seventeenth centuries examined in its cultural, political, and religious contexts, with emphasis on the relationship between the arts. Focus on the earlier seventeenth century, including the work of Caravaggio, Carracci, and the young Bernini.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Bernini and the Age of the Baroque
courses.description: Examines the life and work of Gianlorenzo Bernini, best known as a brilliant and innovative sculptor, in their historical context. Also considered is the international influence that Bernini exerted on seventeenth- and eighteeth-century art.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: The Grand Tour: Experiencing Italy in the Eighteenth Century
courses.description: In the eighteenth century Italy was a mecca for European travelers who sought to enjoy its culture, diversions, landscape, and society. This course will examine the multifaceted experiences of these travelers and the ways in which they constitute the beginnings of the phenomenon of modern tourism.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Special Topics in Eighteenth Century Art
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Special topics in eighteenth century art.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Impressionism and Post-Impressionism
courses.description: Impressionist and Post-Impressionist movement in France from 1863 through the first decade of the twentieth century and the advent of Cubism. Includes the work of Monet, Manet, Degas, Renoir, Pissarro, Van Gogh, Cezanne, Gauguin, and Seurat.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Special Topics in Nineteenth Century Art
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Special topics in nineteenth century art.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Contemporary Art
courses.description: Study of recent artistic developments, from pop to contemporary movements in painting, sculpture, and photography. Movements studied include minimal art, post-minimalism, process art, conceptual art, earthworks, pluralism, neoexpressionism, and issues of postmodern art and criticism.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Critical Approaches to Visual Culture
courses.prereq_text: A prior course in art history; not open to freshmen.
courses.description: Critical ways of approaching and understanding a wide range of visual materials and images (paintings, ads, videos, etc.). Analytic approaches to culture and representation are used as a means of developing descriptive and interpretive skills.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Special Topics in Twentieth-Century Modern Art
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Special topics in twentieth-century modern art.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Early American Modernism
courses.description: Covering topics in US art from the Civil War (1861) to World War I (1917), with a particular focus on the arts of the American West and California. Students will learn about a wide range of media and movements in painting, photography, sculpture, the decorative arts, and performance.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: African American Art and the African Legacy
courses.description: Examination of the three centuries of African-American art in North America, the Carribean, and Brazil, stressing the African legacy. Colonial metalwork and pottery, folk or outsider genres, and mainstream nineteenth-and twentieth-century work are among traditions studied.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Re-Reading American Photography
courses.description: A focus on the history of photography in the United States starting in 1839 and how contemporary artists are responding to this history now. Students learn about different photographic processes, major historical debates, and important themes that continue to shape our visual world.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Native North American Art
courses.description: A survey of the arts of Native North America, from ancestral processes to contemporary trends. During the first half of the course, we will move across regions to explore different ancestral traditions from basket weaving practices of the Chumash people here in Santa Barbara to wampum belt making of the Haudenosaunee Confederacy in the Northeast. In the remaining weeks, we will shift to pan-Indigenous art debates from the 20th century until today. Students will engage with concepts such as settler colonialism, stereotypes, visual sovereignty, environmental justice, material culture, institutional critique, and the politics of representation.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Mexican Manuscripts
courses.description: This upper division lecture surveys the manuscript traditions of 15th and 16th century Mexico, including Nahua, Mixtec, and Maya codices. Through this course, we explore the importance of books and writing in Mesoamerican cultures; the place of histories, maps, and divinatory almanacs in Mesoamerican thought and society; and the role of Indigenous and European book traditions in shaping the colonial encounter.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: African Art I
courses.description: The relationship of art to life in sub-Saharan Africa. A cross-cultural survey of types, styles, history, and values of arts ranging from personal decoration to the state festival, stressing Ashanti, Ife, Benin, Yoruba, Cameroon.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: African Art II
courses.description: An in-depth continuation of Art History 127A in a seminar/discussion format. Selected topics in masking, figural sculpture, etc., and emphasis on African contexts of ritual and social life.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Art and Archaeology of the Ancient Andes
courses.description: The architecture, ceramics, textiles, and other classes of material culture of Andean societies from 3000 B.C. to the Conquest examined within their cultural contexts with a focus on sociopolitical organization and cultural traditions.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Art and Archaeology of Mesoamerica
courses.description: An introduction to the societies of Ancient Mesoamerica. The course examines sociopolitical, religious, and economic systems from the Olmec through Aztecs via the study of material culture including art, architecture, and artifacts. Explores topics of identity, social status, and exchange.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Art and Architecture of the North Coast of Peru
courses.description: The rise and fall of ancient societies of the north coast of Peru such as the Moche, Sicán, and Chimú as well as their cultural antecedents as understood through the material record including architecture, ceramics, textiles, etc.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Special Topics in Latin American Art
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Special topics in Latin American art.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Art of Colonial Mexico
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Examines the art of colonial Mexico in its major spaces of production: missions, metropolitan churches, colonial cities, indigenous communities, and arenas of global exchange. Discusses a range of art media, including architecture, painting, public festivals, manuscripts, featherworks, and talavera. Also considers how art production in these varied spaces came to form an idea of colonial Mexican art.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Mediterranean Cities
courses.description: An exploration of the most important Medieval cities of the Mediterranean world, their urban forms, layout, architecture, and physical patterns. Venice, Cairo, and Baghdad will be among the cities discussed.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Islamic Architecture 650-1400
courses.description: Islamic architecture between 650 and 1400 in its historical context.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Islamic Architecture 1400-Modern
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Art History 176B.
courses.description: Islamic architecture, 1400-modern, in its historical context.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Art of Empire
courses.description: Studies the visual culture of different empires, alone or in a comparative fashion. For example, Ottoman and Hapsburg; Ottomoman, Safavid, and Mughal; Mughal and British India; or the earlier empire of the Fatimids, Abbasids, and Umayyads of Syria and Spain.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Modern Art of the Arab World
courses.description: Explores modern and contemporary art, artists and art movements of the Arab world from nineteenth century to the present.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Special Topics in Islamic Art
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Special topics in Islamic art.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Chinese Painting I
courses.description: Chinese painting and theory, from beginnings through the fourteenth century. Introduction to major developments and masters in their cultural context with a focus on meaning and agency.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Chinese Painting I
courses.comments: CHIN 134CA and ARTHI 134CA are the same course.
courses.description: Chinese painting and theory, from beginnings through the fourteenth century. Introduction to major developments and masters in their cultural context with a focus on meaning and agency.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Art and Modern China
courses.comments: ARTHI 134D is the same course as CHIN 134D.
courses.description: An exploration of trends and issues in nineteenth and twentieth-century Chinese art, as China awakens and responds to the challenges of modernity and the West. Topics include the continuity of tradition, the exile identity, and trends after Tienanmen (1989).

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: The Art of the Chinese Landscape
courses.description: Chinese approaches to landscape as subject matter in art, with a focus on painting and garden architecture. The course begins with the immortality cult in the Han Dynasty (206 B.C.-A.D.221) and ends with contemporary artists of the twentieth century.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: The Arts of Japan
courses.comments: Same course as Japan 134F.
courses.description: Native traditions and foreign influences in the development of Japanese architecture, sculpture, painting, and minor arts.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Japanese Painting
courses.comments: Same course as Japan 134G.
courses.description: The changing and entwined traditions of Japanese painting: those rooted in native concepts and practices and those derived from the Asian continent or Euro-America.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Ukiyo-e: Pictures of the Floating World
courses.comments: Same course as Japan 134H.
courses.description: Japanese paintings and woodblock prints of the sixteenth through twentieth centuries, with emphasis on issues of genre and format.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: 20C Japanese Arts and Visual Culture
courses.description: Exploration of a wide array of Japanese modern and contemporary visual culture in Japan. Emphasis on cultural cross-pollination and global interchange amidst shifting media environments. Topics may vary by year.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Understanding Manga
courses.comments: Same course as Japan 134J.
courses.description: An introduction to the development of Manga (Japanese comics) in relation to other world-wide graphic narrative traditions, with special emphasis on visual analysis and historical context.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Chinese Calligraphy: History and Aesthetics
courses.description: Examines the different scripts in historical context, surveys significant movements and artists, and considers the ideas, theories and aesthetic principles that have enriched the art of writing to elite status in China.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Special Topics in Japanese Art
courses.description: Special topics in Japanese Art. Varying topics.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Twentieth-Century Architecture
courses.description: The history of architecture from 1900 to the present. Examination of modern and post-modern architecture and city planning in its social, political, and artistic context. The scope is global.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Architecture of the United States
courses.description: History of architecture and urban planning: buildings and builders, patrons and occupants, but especially the historical forces and events that transformed the landscape. Course subjects include art, design, technology, economics, politics, and social forces.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Food Space
courses.description: Introduces the modern history of spaces that have supported the production, supply, and consumption of food since the 19th-c within the global exchange of ideas, commodities, and dissemination of foodways under the aegis of colonialism and capitalism. We look at a range of spaces from the forest and farm to restaurants and residences. Our goal is to understand the role of architecture and planning in supporting the changing connections between different scales of food production and consumption.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: The City in History
courses.description: An historical introduction to the ideas and forms of cities with emphasis on modern urbanism. Examination of social theory to understand the role of industrial capitalism and colonialism in shaping the culture of modern cities, the relationship between the city and the country, the phenomena ofclass, race and ethnic separation.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Modern Architecture in Early Twentieth-Century Europe
courses.description: History of modern architecture in Europe in the early twentieth century. Focuses on movements (for example, Art Nouveau, Futurism, Expressionism, Bauhaus, De Stijl, and Constructivism) and on individual architects (for example, Le Corbusier, Gropius, Mies van der Rohe.)

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Revival Styles in Southern Californian Architecture
courses.description: Examines the history of styles in Californian architecture from the eighteenth century to the present. While the focus is on Southern California, such comparative phenomena as National Romanticism in Western Architecure and Critical Regionalism are incorporated.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Sustainable Architecture: History and Aesthetics
courses.comments: Same course as ENV S 136O
courses.description: Course examines history and theory of sustainable and green architecture since the early twentieth century. Emphasis is placed on the critical analysis of a distinct green architectural aesthetic; the scope is global.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Introduction to 2D/3D Visualizations in Architecture
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; open to majors only.
courses.comments: Same course as Art Studio 106W.
courses.description: Develops skills in reading, interpreting, and visualizing 3D objects and spaces by offering exercises in sketching, perspective, orthographic projections, isometric drawings, and manual rendering practices. Relevant for those interested in history of architecture, sculpture, and such spatial practices as installations and public art.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Modern Architecture in Southern California, C. 1890s to the Present
courses.description: Critically analyzes the changing definitions of modern architecture in Southern California from the 1890s to the present, focusing on the work of architects like Greene and Greene, R.M. Schindler, and R. Neutra, as well as the Case Study Houses.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Special Topics in Architecture
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Special topics in architecture.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Architecture and Theory in Germany and Austria (1770-1870)
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Between 1770 and 1871, the German speaking lands of Europe experienced both political unification and an astounding cultural rebirth (Kant, Hegel, Goethe, Beethoven, Brahms, Wagner, Marx, Nietzsche...). This blossoming extended to architecture and town planning as well, as the region transformed itself into one of Europe's most vibrant laboratories for theory and design. This course will examine this remarkable period of change by examining architecture, town planning, and some architectural theory (in translation) in their larger cultural and political contexts.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Special Topics in Photographic History
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Specialized classes exploring questions of methodology, as well as significant themes and major figures in the history of photography. Emphasis on intensive investigation of research issues as opposed to extensive period coverage.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Special Topics in Photographic History
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Specialized classes exploring questions of methodology, as well as significant themes and major figures in the history of photography. Emphasis on intensive investigation of research issues as opposed to extensive period coverage.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Museum Practices and Techniques
courses.prereq_text: Not open to freshmen; consent of instructor.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to student who have completed Art History 164C.
courses.description: Discussion of various aspects of museum work: management principles, the cataloging and care of art objects, exhibitions and acquisitions, administrative procedures, museum architecture. Specialist lectures and visits of museums and their facilities.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Birth of the Modern Museum
courses.description: Course examines the emergence and development of museums of art in eighteenth-century Europe, tracing their origins to the private collections from which they evolved and studying the practices, such as tourism, that stimulated their growth.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: The Architecture of Museums and Galleries from c. 1800 to the Present
courses.description: Discusses the history of museums and galleries as distinct modern building types by analyzing their architectural developments from approximately 1800 to the present. Beside architectural design issues (sequence of galleries, display of exhibits, lighting, visitor routes, etc.), the course analyzes museums as sites of memory, their intersections with the modern city, and their roles in cultural and societal debates. Geographically, the course focuses on both the museums origin in Europe and its contemporary universal presence.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Museums and History
courses.description: Examines the 20th century museums engagement with history. Explores curatorial strategies for telling stories about the past through historical objects, written narratives, photography, performance, architecture, and art.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Architecture and Planning in Seventeenth-Century Europe
courses.description: How did major changes in politics, science, and religion (absolutism, Scientific Revolution, Counter Reformation) manifest themselves in contemporary architecture and town planning? Architects include Bernini, Borromini, Wren, Mansart. Focus on Rome, Turin, Paris, and London.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Paris and Rome in the Nineteenth Century
courses.description: Comparative history of how two great cities were transformed from pre-modern to modern; focus on architecture and design as well as politics, economics, and culture; emergence of new ideas about the very concept of "the city."

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Gardens, Land, and Landscape in the West: Renaissance to 1900
courses.description: Changing nature of garden and landscape design from the Renaissance to NYC's Central Park, studied as a function of the changing functions and status of land during the long passage from feudalism to industrial capitalism.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Architecture, Planning, and Culture in Eighteenth-Century Paris
courses.description: Paris (and Versailles) from the Sun King to the Revolution, rococo, neoclassicism, origins of urbanism; extensive use of primary texts in translation to study architectural debates in the press and their connection to contemporary political battles.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Architecture, Theory & Town Planning in 19th Century France
courses.description: The French Revolution inspired a total rethinking: one that aspired to construct a new world and make new sense of the past. This rethinking encompassed politics, religion, history, science, technology, economics, government, philosophy - all of which are aspects of architecture, architectural theory, and town planning. This course will approach the history of 19th-century French architectural thought and practice as a lens through which to discern the broader ways in which the world changed in the wake of 1789.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Contemporary Art in Russia and Eastern Europe
courses.comments: Same course as Slavic 130C. Not open for credit to students who have completed Russian 144C or Slavic 144C.
courses.description: Study of central intellectual and aesthetic trends in the late Soviet period and in contemporary post-Soviet Russia and Eastern Europe. Analysis of literary texts and the visual arts. Taught in English.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Art in California
courses.description: As a state, California is the site of tremendous diversity in the visual arts but has consistently suffered from stereotypes that framed it as a regional backwater far from New York and Europe. This lecture-based course addresses the character and role of the post-war art and its developments in and beyond the cities of Los Angeles and San Francisco. Movements studied include Mexican Muralism, the rise of modern photography, Asian American culture, assemblage and sculpture, the Black Arts movement, feminism, as well as pioneering developments in installation, video and performance art.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Digital Visual Studies
courses.comments: Same course as Comparative Literature 163 and German 163.
courses.description: In the past ten years, the scope of the digital humanities has broadened to include the visual world: distant reading became distant viewing. This visual turn has not only facilitated the digital transformation of traditional disciplines like art history but has also introduced a new set of media-technological questions into the digital humanities discourse: questions concerning the nature of digital images, and the modalities of machine seeing. This course serves as an introduction to the emerging discipline of digital visual studies that investigates these questions. Participants will acquire skills in the analysis and critique of digital visual culture and learn to use contemporary digital tools to explore the visual world.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Special topics in Art History
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Special topics in the history of art and architecture.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Seminar in Research Methods
courses.description: A focus on methodological approaches and tools. Topics will vary. Requires weekly readings and discussion, and the writing of a research seminar paper.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Seminar in Ancient Greek & Roman Art/Architecture
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units.Open only to Art History majors during Pass 1.
courses.description: Advanced studies in Ancient Greek and Roman archaeology and architecture. Emphasis on classical heritage of Asia Minor (Turkey). Topics will vary. This course requires weekly readings and discussion, and the writing of a research seminar paper.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Seminar in Medieval Art
courses.comments: Open only to Art History majors during Pass 1.
courses.description: Advanced studies in Medieval art. Topics will vary. This course requires weekly readings and discussion, and the writing of a research seminar paper.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Seminar in Medieval Architecture & Sculpture
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units.Open only to Art History majors during Pass 1.
courses.description: Advanced studies in Medieval architecture and sculpture. Topics will vary. This course requires weekly readings and discussion, and the writing of a research seminar paper.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Seminar in Seventeenth Century Northern European Art
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units with different topic.Open only to Art History majors during Pass 1.
courses.description: Advanced studies in seventeenth century Northern European visual culture. Topics will vary. This course requires weekly readings and discussion, and the writing of a research seminar paper.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Seminar in Seventeenth Century Southern European Art
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units.Open only to Art History majors during Pass 1.
courses.description: Advanced studies in seventeenth century art. Topics will vary. Requires weekly readings and discussion, and the writing of a research seminar paper.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Seminar in Art of the Americas
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units with different topic.Open only to Art History majors during Pass 1.
courses.description: Advanced studies in the art of the Americas. Topics will vary. This course requires weekly readings and discussion, and the writing of a research seminar paper.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Seminar in African Art
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units with different topic.Open only to Art History majors during Pass 1.
courses.description: Advanced studies in African art. Topics will vary. This course requires weekly readings and discussion, and the writing of a research seminar paper.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Seminar in Latin American Art
courses.comments: Open only to Art History majors during Pass 1.
courses.description: Advanced studies in pre-Columbian/colonial art. Topics will vary. This course requires weekly readings and discussion, and the writing of a research seminar paper.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Seminar in Islamic Art and Architecture
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units with different topic.Open only to Art History majors during Pass 1.
courses.description: Advanced studies in Islamic art and architecture. Topics will vary. This course requires weekly readings and discussion, and the writing of a research seminar paper.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Seminar in Japanese Art
courses.comments: Same course as Japan 186RW.
courses.description: Studies in Japanese art. Topics will vary, but emphasis is usually on the various relationships to global movements. Requires weekly readings, discussion, frequent presentations, and the writing of a well-developed research paper.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Seminar in Architectural History
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units.Open only to Art History majors during Pass 1.
courses.description: Advanced studies in architectural history. Topics will vary. This course requires weekly readings and discussion, and the writing of a research seminar paper.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Seminar in Modern Architecture
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units.Open only to Art History majors during Pass 1.
courses.description: Advanced studies in modern architecture. Topics will vary. This course requires weekly readings and discussion, and the writing of a research seminar paper.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Seminar in Photographic History
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units with different topic.Open only to Art History majors during Pass 1.
courses.description: Advanced studies in photographic history. Topics will vary. This course requires weekly readings and discussion, and the writing of a research seminar paper.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Approaches to Objects
courses.description: This seminar introduces students to the potential and different approaches of object-based scholarship drawing on multidisciplinary perspectives and analytic techniques from art history, archaeology, anthropology, object conservation, and the history of collecting and display. Topics and format will vary.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Public Art
courses.description: This seminar explores the history and development of public art and monuments. Together we study examples of various types of public art and consider their purposes, sites, audiences, patronage, and financing. We also discuss important controversies that public art has provoked. Using the background we develop in class, students work on individual projects addressing issues that we examine.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Museum Theory: Collections and Cultural Politics
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; art history majors only.
courses.comments: Open only to Art History majors during Pass 1.
courses.description: Why do museums (whether of art, culture, history, science, religion, technology or otherwise) seem to generate unending controversies concerning ethics, cultural politics, authenticity and ownership? Through the lens of wide-ranging readings in museum theory, this seminar examines the museum as an institution and a set of cultural practices, exploring recent museum controversies and debating the merits of theexhibitions and the efficacy of the responses.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Critical Curation: Culture, Race, and Power
courses.description: This seminar introduces theoretical and practical issues of curatorial practice. "Curating" is understood here as mediation, invention, and problem-solving; a field of production of symbolic representations in as much as political ones, and is used almost indiscriminately to explain exercises of association within the cultural field. Students will analyze case studies and the opportunities of curating, and will acknowledge curating requires skills to trace misunderstandings, omissions, and conflicts of exhibitions. Students will identify the politics of representation at stake in curatorial practice which involve institutions, research methods, aesthetics and design, dynamics of inclusion and exclusion, as well as public participation.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Museums in Transition: From the Early Modern to the Modern Period
courses.description: Examines a range of issuesart historical, cultural, political, practical, and theoreticalthat conditioned the development of museums and collections, primarily in Europe, from the Renaissance to the present day. Topics and format will vary.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Museum Studies Seminar
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; art history majors only.
courses.comments: Open only to Art History majors during Pass 1.
courses.description: Examines a range of historical, theoretical, and practical issues with which the field of Museum Studies is engaged. Topics and format will vary.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: University Art Museum Internship
courses.comments: Enrollment in the course is subject to the student securing an internship. Internships are not provided by the department.
courses.description: Under supervision of History of Art & Architecture faculty, students may obtain credit for work in the University Art Museum. Students earn one unit for every 30 hours of work in their internship. Regular meetings, a final evaluation session, and a written report are required.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Architecture and Design Collective Internship
courses.comments: Enrollment in the course is subject to the student securing an internship. Internships are not provided by the department.
courses.description: Under supervision of History of Art & Architecture faculty, students may obtain credit for work in the Architecture and Design Collection. Students earn one unit for every 30 hours of work in their internship. Regular meetings, a final evaluation session, and a written report are required.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Visual Technologies Internship
courses.comments: Enrollment in the course is subject to the student securing an internship. Internships are not provided by the department.
courses.description: The internship in the Material / Image Research Lab offers an immersive opportunity to develop advanced visual technology skills essential for history of art and architectural history research and digital humanities/digital scholarship. With a commitment of one to three units (total 30 hours/unit), interns may work on innovative projects such as 3D object scanning and the Central Coast Native American Modern to Contemporary Art Archive, for example. Written report required.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: On Campus Internship in the History of Art & Architecture
courses.comments: Enrollment in the course is subject to the student securing an internship. Internships are not provided by the department.
courses.description: Under supervision of History of Art & Architecture faculty, students may obtain credit for internship work on UCSB's campus (excluding ARTHI 192A, 192B, and 192C). Students earn one unit for every 30 hours of work in their internship. Regular meetings, a final evaluation session, and a written report are required.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Off Campus Internship in the History of Art & Architecture
courses.comments: Enrollment in the course is subject to the student securing an internship. Internships are not provided by the department.
courses.description: Under supervision of History of Art & Architecture faculty, students may obtain credit for work in a museum, gallery, or architecture firm. Students earn one unit for every 30 hours of work in their internship. Regular meetings, a final evaluation session, and a written report are required.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Independent Studies
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; two upper-division courses in art history; consent of instructor and department.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 grade-point average for the preceding three quarters and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
courses.description: Advanced individual problems.Each unit requires 30 hours per quarter of work from the student.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Art History Honors
courses.prereq_text: Admission to History of Art & Architecture Honors program; completed at least 3 upper-division History of Art & Architecture courses; completed at least one ARTHI seminar course; have an overall minimum GPA of 3.0.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined. Written proposal required.
courses.description: This honors courses serves to assist in tracking which instructor the capstone project will be completed with. Registration is only allowed after being accepted into the ARTHI Honors program, and will require instructor authorization to enroll. During the quarter, there will be assigned meetings, readings, papers, and more to be assigned by the instructor. This course will not impact GPA, nor will count towards any major/minor requirements. Students who successfully complete the honors program will receive Distinction in the Major at the time of graduation, as well as nominations for Honors and thesis awards.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Undergraduate Research Assistant
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; two upper-division courses in art history; consent of instructor and department.
courses.comments: Students must have a 3.0 cumulative grade-point average and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
courses.description: Undergraduate research assistant.Each unit requires 30 hours per quarter of work from the student.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Proseminar: Introduction to Art-Historical Methods
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing. Art History majors only.
courses.comments: Required of all first-year M.A./Ph.D. students.
courses.description: Introduction to art-historical methods, with emphasis on the historical development of current practices, critical theory, debates within the field, and cross-disciplinary dialogues.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Seminar: Topics in Roman Architecture and Urbanism
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing or senior art history majors with consent of instructor.
courses.description: Special research in Roman and late antique architecture.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Seminar: Topics in Medieval Architecture & Sculpture
courses.description: Special research in Romanesque and/or Gothic architecture and sculpture.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Seminar: Topics in Pre-Columbian/Colonial Latin American Art
courses.description: Special research in pre-Columbian and colonial Latin American art topics.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Seminar: Topics in 15th & 16th C. Art in Northern Europe
courses.description: Special research in northern Renaissance figurative arts of the fifteenth and/or sixteenth centuries.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Seminar: Studies in the History and Theory of Museums
courses.description: Special research in museum history and theory.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Topics in Early Modern Iberian Art
courses.description: This seminar explores a variety of topics in the arts and visual cultures of the Iberian world at large, from 1450 to 1700.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Seminar: Topics in Seventeenth-Century European Art
courses.description: Special topics in seventeenth-century European Art.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Seminar: Topics in American Art
courses.description: Special research in American painting and sculpture, 1700-1950.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Seminar: Topics in Contemporary Art
courses.description: Special research in contemporary art.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Seminar: Topics in Architectural History & Urbanism
courses.description: Special research in the history of architecture.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Seminar: Topics in Early Modern Architecture
courses.description: Special research in early modern architecture.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Seminar: Topics in Modern Architecture
courses.description: Special research in modern architecture.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Seminar: Topics in Islamic Art & Architecture
courses.description: Special research in Islamic art and architecture.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Seminar: Topics on East Asian Art
courses.description: Research on select problems on the arts of China, Japan, or Korea.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Seminar: Topics of Japanese Art
courses.description: Studies in Japanese art in a comparative context. Topics vary, but emphasis is usually on the various relationships to global movements. Requires weekly readings, discussion, frequent presentations, and the writing of a well-developed research paper.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Seminar: Advanced Readings in Art History
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing; consent of instructor; department approval.
courses.description: Source readings for graduate students. Independent reading and research in connection with an undergraduate lecture course.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: READING CRITICAL THEORY AND THE VISUAL ARTS
courses.comments: Same course as German 270.
courses.description: Analysis of theories and critiques of modernism and modernity from Benjaminto Adorno and Derrida, with special focus on the historical avantgarde. Specifics may vary.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Seminar: Getty Consortium
courses.description: Special graduate seminar offered at the Getty Research Institute in Los Angeles, involving faculty and graduate students from the five graduate programs in Art History of Visual Studies located in southern California.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Apprentice Teaching
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing; consent of instructor; department approval.
courses.comments: No credit allowed toward degree.
courses.description: For teaching assistants, course includes directed readings, instruction in use of visual aids, pedagogical techniques, design of materials for discussion sections, and methodological analyses. Attendance at lectures in the course to which the T.A. is assigned is a requirement.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Group Studies
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing; consent of instructor; department approval.
courses.comments: No unit credit allowed toward degree.
courses.description: Informal reading and discussion.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing; consent of instructor; department approval.
courses.description: Individual tutorial. A written proposal must be approved by the department chair.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Reading for Examination
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing; consent of instructor; department approval.
courses.description: Preparation for terminal M.A. or for Ph.D. Minor and Major exams.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Master's Thesis Preparation
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing; consent of instructor; department approval.
courses.comments: No credit allowed toward degree. For Plan 1 student only.
courses.description: Master's Thesis research and preparation.

courses.subject: ARTHI
courses.title: Ph.D. Dissertation Preparation
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing; consent of instructor; department approval.
courses.description: Dissertation research and preparation.

courses.subject: ARTHIW
courses.title: Survey III: Modern-Contemporary Art History (online)
courses.comments: ARTHIW 6C is the online version of ARTHI 6C.
courses.description: Introduction to the modern era of Western art history, focusing on European and American histories. It begins reviewing the 18th-century European Enlightenment: scientific inquiry and new forms of representation are the models for the course. Proceeding through the 19th-century histories of colonization and land grabs, and then move to the 20th-century, focusing on the rise of urbanism, migration, and new developments in abstract art; additional focus on ethnicity, race, sexuality and gender across the Arts & Crafts Movement, and the rise of internationalism and global art histories in the 21st-century, ending the course by examining the present time period.

courses.subject: ARTHIW
courses.title: Introduction to Architecture and Planning
courses.comments: ARTHIW 6F is the online version of ARTHI 6F.
courses.description: A wide-ranging introduction to architecture and urban design around the world from the earliest human constructions to the mid-20th century. Students will encounter a variety of buildings and cities, and be introduced to a range of different ways of understanding and studying them. Writing assignments involve analysis of local architecture and planning. By the end of the course students will have acquired a competent knowledge of the diverse sites, structures, and issues, and an enriched awareness of what can be at stake in an architectural environment, what kinds of issues discussions of architecture may lead to, and how and why these kinds of discussions have varied in different times, places, and cultures.

courses.subject: ARTHIW
courses.title: Rome: The Game
courses.comments: ARTHIW 6R and WRIT W 6R are the same course
courses.description: This online course presented as an adventure game introduces students to the art and archaeology of Rome, with assignments that focus on writing and the research process. The course asks students to determine whether or not a collection of ancient objects from an American museum should remain in the US or be sent back to Italy. Throughout the course, students excavate artifacts at a digital dig site, visit museums, explore Roman monuments, and navigate the shadowy world of the tombaroli (tomb robbers) and mafia-run black market for antiquities.

courses.subject: ARTHIW
courses.title: Rome from Napoleon to Mussolini (1798-1943)
courses.comments: ARTHIW 142B is the online version of ARTHI 142B
courses.description: Between 1798 and 1943, Rome experienced a republican revolution, a Napoleonic occupation, a papal restoration, another republican revolution, another papal restoration, the seizure of Rome from the Pope by the new Italian nation state, the crisis of Italy's Liberal period, and finally the rise of Mussolini's Fascist regime followed by World War II. This course will track these changes as they played out in the form of architectural and urban transformations – in a period when Rome was substantially rebuilt, its population massively enlarged, and its core meanings aggressively redefined by successive governments.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Introduction to Asian American History, 1850-Present
courses.comments: AS AM W 1 is the online version of AS AM 1.
courses.description: Historical survey of Asian Americans in the United States from 1850 to the present. Topics include: Immigration patterns, settlement and employment, race and gender relations, community development, and transnational connections.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Introduction to Asian American History, 1850-Present
courses.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in AS AM 1; consent of instructor.
courses.description: Students receive one unit for the honors discussion section. Intended for highly motivated and well prepared students.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: American Migration Since 1965: Asians and others in the United States
courses.description: An examination of central themes in immigration law and policy, especially after the Immigration Act of 1965. The class focuses on Asian immigrants, but covers immigration trends comparatively. Topics include economic integration, interracial conflict, subsequent immigration reforms and their consequences.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: American Migration Since 1965: Asians and others in the United States
courses.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in AS AM 2; consent of instructor.
courses.description: Students receive one unit for the honors seminar. Intended for highly motivated and well prepared students.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Introduction to Asian American Popular Culture
courses.description: A historical survey of how Asians and Asian Americans have been represented in American popular culture, with an analytical focus on the social and symbolic contents of examples in journalism, literature, theater, and television.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Introduction to Asian American Literature
courses.description: Selected major themes in literary texts from Asian American communities, including Japanese, Chinese, Korean, Filipino and Southeast Asian Americans: dislocation/relocation; finding/inventing a usable past; poetics/politics in language; identities/ethnicities.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Introduction to Asian American Gender and Sexuality
courses.description: Introduction of gendered analysis and intersectionality in the study of Asian Americans from sociological, psychological, and historical perspectives. Major themes include social construction of femininities and masculinities, family formation, productive and reproductive labor, global capitalism, violence regulating gender and sexuality.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Race and Resistance: Asian American, Black, Chicana/o and Indigenous Freedom Struggles
courses.description: Studies US race-based freedom struggles, emphasizing the 1960s-70s, within the context of global decolonization and the study of the long movement from the 1930s to the present. Examines how social movements are studied historically.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Martial Arts in US Culture
courses.comments: AS AMW 10 in the online version of AS AM 10.
courses.description: The proliferation of martial arts in US media and everyday life is a dynamic lens through which students may be introduced to topics fundamental to AsAm studies: histories of colonialism and militarism, both between the West and Asia and amongst Asian countries; patterns of immigration and regional adaptation in the US; racial and gendered representation in Hollywood (i.e., Orientalism), relative to media centers in China and Hong Kong; interracial cross-pollination between minorities in the US, especially during the social justice movements. Students will critique cultural texts and research histories, as they learn about fight-scene choreography in course materials and undertake ethnographic studies of their nearby martial arts studios.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Community Studies Organizing for Change
courses.comments: AS AM 11 and BL ST 11 are the same course.
courses.description: This course examines various aspects of community organizing for equity and justice. The course will introduce models for social change and approaches to leadership development. It will examine case studies of campaigns for justice, within the context of social movement histories.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Introduction to Health Justice & Community
courses.description: This introductory course investigates the social foundations of health justice to critically analyze how we understand health and healing. We focus on the systemic inequality of health and health care; and how the healing of individuals is contingent on the healing of social ills. Engaging an interdisciplinary approach that brings together knowledge across academic disciplines and lived traditions, our objective is to plot out a new intellectual direction for critical health justice that intersects with Asian American Studies

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Introduction to Asian American Religions
courses.comments: AS AM 71 and RG ST 71 are the same course.
courses.description: Survey of the major themes and issues in Asian American religious history, belief, and practice. Topics include the problem of orientalism; Buddhism and race; Asian American forms of Christianity; religion's role in immigrant and second-generation identity; Asian American contextual theologies.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Introduction to Dramatic Writing
courses.comments: THTR 9 and AS AM 79 are the same course.
courses.description: A intensive introduction to playwriting for beginning dramatists. Students will read and analyze the structure of plays, write and stage their own short plays, and gain experience acting in and directing each other's work. Homework for the course includes a series of written and performance-based assignments.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Independent Research Assistant
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 99/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined
courses.description: Coursework consists of faculty-supervised research assistance for students with Freshmen and Sophomore standing.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Specific Asian Ethnic Groups
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided the letter designations are different.
courses.description: The historical and contemporary experiences of specific Asian ethnic groups.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Chinese Americans
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Asian American Studies 51 or 101.
courses.description: The historical and contemporary experiences of specific Asian ethnic groups: Chinese Americans 100AA.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Japanese Americans
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Asian American Studies 52 or 102.
courses.description: The historical and contemporary experiences of specific Asian ethnic groups: Japanese Americans 100BB.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Filipino Americans
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Asian American Studies 53 or 103.
courses.description: The historical and contemporary experiences of specific Asian ethnic groups: Filipino Americans.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Korean Americans
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Asian American Studies 54 or 104.
courses.description: The historical and contemporary experiences of specific Asian ethnic groups: Korean Americans (100DD).

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Vietnamese Americans
