courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Asian American Studies 55 or 105.
courses.description: The historical and contemporary experiences of specific Asian ethnic groups: Vietnamese Americans (100EE).

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: South Asian Americans
courses.comments: May be taken for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided the letter designations are different.
courses.description: The historical and contemporary experiences of specific Asian ethnic groups: South Asian Americans (100FF),

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Southeast Asian Americans
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided the letter designations are different.
courses.description: The historical and contemporary experiences of specific Asian ethnic groups: Southeast Asian Americans (100HH).

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Arab and Muslim Americans: Roots, Representation, Resistance
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided the letter designations are different.
courses.description: Critically analyzes the historical, social, political, and cultural formations and racialized regimes of power that characterize Arabs and Muslims in the US, drawing from interdisciplinary fields such as Ethnic Studies, Asian & Arab American Studies, Decolonial Theory, and Feminist Studies.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Teaching 4 Social Justice
courses.prereq_text: At least one course in one of these departments: Asian American Studies, Black Studies, Chicana/o Studies, Feminist Studies
courses.comments: AS AM 101C, BL ST 101C, CH ST 101C, and FEMST 101C are cross-listed.
courses.description: This interdisciplinary course will highlight how a curriculum focusing on racial, ethnic, gender, and LGBTQ studies is central to teaching and learning within diverse societal contexts. This grounding is essential for K-12 teachers in History and English/Literature. Through a social justice framework, students will learn how classrooms are enhanced by Ethnic and Feminist Studies, placing graduates within the forefront of educational initiatives that position teaching and learning within an inclusive and equitable paradigm.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Sociology of Asian America
courses.prereq_text: One previous course in Asian American Studies or Upper-Division standing
courses.description: This course critically examines contemporary Asian American experiences within a larger social and historical context. Using an Ethnic Studies lens, we will engage sociological understandings of the social, political, and economic conditions that structure the roots of Asian America.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Third World Social Movements
courses.description: Racial comparative analysis of Third World social movements. Study of impact of historical context, political economy, racial formation, and gender dynamics on activism of Asian, Black, Chicana/o, Indigenous, Puerto Rican communities in the United States; also attention to global struggles.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Transnational Asian America
courses.description: Focuses on "deterritorialized" processes that have emerged due to intensified globalization. Emphasis on three distinct schools of thought (diasporic studies, cultural globalization, and transmigration) that illuminate how people, goods, and ideas intersect across multiple spaces and times.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Contemporary Asian American Activism
courses.description: Historical formation of Asian immigrant communities and their social structures and functions; impact of post-1965 Asian immigration on existing communities; issues facing Asian Americans today including education, employment, discrimination, civil rights, political participation, media stereotypes, and anti-Asian violence.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Asian Americans and the Long Civil Rights Movement
courses.description: Examines the Asian American Movement of the 1960s-70s in the long Civil Rights Movement framework, connecting with earlier and later activism. Focuses on leadership development, pan-Asian identity, Third World solidarities, feminism, education, housing, and antiwar, among other critical issues.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Asian Americans in Popular Culture
courses.description: A historical survey of how Asians and Asian Americans have been represented in American popular culture and an analysis of alternative models of popular culture. Texts include literature, theatre, television, and film.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Asian American Fiction
courses.description: Examination of the ways in which Asian American writers create fiction in order to reflect on pertinent issues concerning Asian Americans, such as race, class, gender, and sexuality. Texts include short stories and novels.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Community Studies Knowledge in Action
courses.comments: AS AM 123A and BL ST 123A are the same course.
courses.description: The first in a 2-course series for the Community Studies Pathways Program. Students will gain scholarly knowledge, experiential knowledge, networking experience, and community building skills to facilitate community-based careers. Both courses (123A and 123B) are required for the program.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Community Studies and Career Pathways
courses.comments: AS AM 123B and BL ST 123B are the same course.
courses.description: The second in a 2-course series for the Community Studies Pathways Program. Students will gain scholarly knowledge, experiential knowledge, networking experience, and community building skills to facilitate community-based careers. Both courses (123A and 123B) are required for the program.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Comparative Ethnic American Literature
courses.description: Focuses on literature by Asian American writers alongside texts from one or more of the other ethnic American literary traditions. Generic and thematic coverage will vary. Emphasis on literary analysis in comparative racial context.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Asian American Theater
courses.comments: Same course as THTR 180F.
courses.description: Overview of Asian American theater and its political and artistic achievements, from foundational Asian American theater companies and playwrights to contemporary performance artists. Issues addressed include race and ethnicity, gender and sexuality, and intergenerational conflict.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Asian American Film, Television, and Digital Media
courses.description: Formal, historical, and cultural issues in the study of Asian American film, television, and digital media practices in independent, Hollywood, and transnational contexts. The role of cinema and visual technology in the understanding of Asian Americans in modern and contemporary culture.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Writings by Asian American Women
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Asian American Studies 133 Fall 1996 or prior.
courses.description: Asian American women's writing covering a variety of genres and cultural communities; emphasis on literary analysis of works in relation to central themes of race, family and gender.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Colonialism and Migration
courses.description: Examines the impact of Western imperialism and colonialism on Asian people and nations, and then the subsequent migrations of Asians to the United States. The course examines the root causes of migration, the response of the United States to Asians immigrants, and changes to immigration law and policy from 1850 to 1965.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Migration and Critical Mental Health
courses.description: This course takes a multidisciplinary approach to examine the relationship between mental health and forced migration at the intersection of power, race, capitalism, colonization, borders, and psychopolitics. It critically examines how the medicalization of bodies, psyches, and lands shape racialized policies, discourse, and conditions. This course centers community-based knowledge, lived experiences, and social movements to reimagine alternative frameworks and practices of care, wellness, and healing justice.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Science, Technology, and Asian America
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Asian American 171HH with a grade of C or above.
courses.description: The origins and development of Asian American representation in science-based fields and the consequences of that phenomenon in US politics, immigration, counterespionage, and images of Asian Americans in popular culture.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Asian American Queer Theory
courses.description: A focus on Asian American queer theory from the lived experiences, histories, and activisms of queer Asian and Pacific Islander Americans. From the colonial era and formations of war and imperialism to modern pop culture, it explores ‘Asian American’, ‘Pacific Islander American’ and ‘queer’ not as fixed identities but as a critical paradigm (‘queering’) with which to interrogate and challenge normative notions of gender, sex, race, sexuality, citizenship, and ‘Asian-ness' as well as settler colonial frameworks sutured into liberal formulations of queer Asian and Pacific Islander American subjectivities.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Asian American Families
courses.description: The importance of the family in the East and Southeast Asian cultural heritage; family formation in the United States; contemporary Asian American family dynamics; interracial families; changing gender roles and relationships; the family and the life cycle.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Multiethnic Asian Americans
courses.description: The history, identities, and social relations of multiethnic Asian Americans. Uses fiction, autobiography, sociological and psychological studies of people of mixed racial or ethnic parentage. Considers cognate issues such as interracial marriage.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Asian American Sexualities
courses.description: Examines the critical lens of sexuality in studying Asian American culture, history, and politics. Survey of interdisciplinary texts on concepts of sexuality in Asia and America, constructions of sexual difference, denaturalizing heterosexuality and queer theory.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Introductory Asian American Performance Workshop
courses.description: An introductory performance workshop focusing on Asian American themes. Students write original pieces, learn the basic techniques of stage performance, and participate in presenting a public performance at the end of the quarter.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Health, Culture, and Social Change
courses.description: This course critically analyzes health, culture, and social change. Readings focus on community agency, knowledge, and power, and center marginalized world views and collective activism. Students examine interdisciplinary scholarly work, cultural productions, and case studies, working together to carry out collaborative projects. The goal is to learn and apply innovative understandings of health, culture, and social change efforts that support culturally-grounded care and healing.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Asian American Cultural Nights
courses.description: Surveys the origins, development, and contemporary iterations of Asian American cultural night performances. Explores critiques of these and similar forms of cultural production and guides students in building their own intellectual framework for analyzing performances of racial and ethnic identity.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Environmental Entanglements in Asian America
courses.prereq_text: One previous course in Asian American Studies or Upper-Division standing.
courses.description: What happens to our understanding of environmentalism when we center the experiences of Asian Americans? This interdisciplinary course engages environmental justice through an Ethnic Studies lens to reckon with harmful forms of resource extraction.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Race and Law in Early American History
courses.description: Early race relations in the American colonies and in the formation of the United States. The course examines the interrelationship of Native Americans, Africans, Asians, and Europeans in American public law before the Civil War

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Racial Segregation from the Civil War to the Civil Rights Movement
courses.description: Examines the legal dimensions of white supremacy in American public law after the Civil War. The course reviews commonly recurring rules and principles about segregation and racial subordination in American society before the 1960's.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Race and Law in Modern America
courses.comments: Recommended for juniors and seniors.
courses.description: This course reviews the Civil Rights Movement and American law in the post World War II era, and it concludes with an overview of contemporary debates about race and law. We examine the end of segregation, and review recurring patterns of race-based inequality.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Asian Americans and Education
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Asian American 171II.
courses.description: A historical and sociological examination of the effects of race and power on Asian American educational experiences. The role of critical pedagogy in the creation of knowledge. The development and impact of ethnic studies and the model minority image.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Asian American Aesthetics
courses.comments: One prior Asian American Studies course.
courses.description: Questions, arguments and ideas regarding Asian American aesthetics. How can we apply traditional western concepts such as beauty, the sublime, and the imagination when considering Asian American cultural production? Explores the employment of realism, modernism and postmodernism across different genres.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Environmental Justice and Community Health
courses.comments: AS AM 159 is the same course as ESS 159.
courses.description: Examines intersection of environmental racism and health justice. With particular focus on California, course explores the political economic infrastructure of urban and rural communities as they confront environmental racism and challenge its impact on community health.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Asian American Politics
courses.prereq_text: Political Science 12 or Asian American Studies 1 or Asian American Studies 2.
courses.description: Survey of the historical and contemporary political experiences of Asian Americans and their pursuits for immigration, equality, citizenship, political identity, racial justice, cross-racial/ethnic coalition building and incorporation into the U. S. political system.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Asian American Religions
courses.prereq_text: Upper Division Standing or permission of instructor.
courses.comments: Same course as Religious Studies 123.
courses.description: Historical and interdisciplinary approach to the themes and issues in the religious traditions of Asian Americans. Topics: the civil religious context, the transplantation of Asian traditions into the U.S., Asian American Christianity, Asian American theology.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Filpinx/Filipinx American Religions
courses.prereq_text: Upper Division standing or instructor approval
courses.description: Examines how Filipinx/Filipinx American religious histories, beliefs and practices have been researched, assessed, theorized, and represented. Topics include cultural Southeast Asian foundations, Spanish colonialism, American occupation, emigration to the U.S, Filipino innovations in religion and spirituality, contemporary indigenous revival.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Asian American Mental Health
courses.description: Examination of the current theory and research on the specific psychological issues that affect Asian Americans. Special emphasis on how immigration experiences,cultural values, ethnic identity, and racism influence various aspects of psychosocial functioning.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: The Politics of The Global War on Terror
courses.description: The course examines the historical, social, media, and political dimensions of the so-called ‘Global War on Terror’ post-9/11, focusing on how those forces impact Arab, Palestinian, South-West Asian, South Asian, and Muslim Americans in the U.S. and the transnational dimensions of U.S. empire.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Ethnographic Research Methods in Asian America
courses.description: Examines the politics of Asian America through ethnographic texts. Discusses the construction of the category Asian American, including conflicts and coalitions across groups. What can ethnographic texts teach us about the everyday life of living in Asian America?

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: The Cultural Politics of Sports
courses.description: Uses sports as a cultural text in order to examine larger critical debates around race, gender, class, nationalism, fandom, consumerism, amongst other topics. While considering these debates in the broader American context, this class will particularly examine the cultural politics of sports within Asian America.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Special Topics in Asian American Studies - Arts & Humanities
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units will apply to the major.
courses.description: Courses focusing on various arts & humanities topics not covered in other Asian American Studies courses.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Special Topics in Asian American Studies - Social Science and History
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units, provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units will apply to the major.
courses.description: Focuses on various social science and history topics not offered in other Asian American studies courses.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Special Topics in Asian American Studies - Social Science and History
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units, provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units will apply to the major.
courses.description: What happens to our understanding of environmentalism when we center the experiences of Asian Americans? This course begins with the premise that the call for environmental justice is part of a broader call to revisit our covenant to the world, our relationships to it, and our responsibilities to one another. Approaching environmental justice through an Ethnic Studies lens requires an engagement with racial justice and decolonial struggles to reckon with the harmful ideological and economic forms of resource extraction. For Asian American communities, whose environmental entanglements are all but erased, this is more pressing than ever.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Human Centered Design for Equity
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units, provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units will apply to the major.
courses.description: Training in the methods, rationale, and background of Human Centered Design. Practical experience applying this method to address an equity issue in today's world as defined by the students and faculty. Class is collaborative and project-based.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Asian American and Women of Color Speculative Fiction and Film
courses.description: We study speculative fiction and film (sci fi, fantasy, etc.) to address contemporary environmental, social, and health crises and imagine individual and collective antidotes. We identify new forms of resistance and worldmaking that can lead to feminist futures.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Poetics of Decoloniality
courses.description: An in-depth look into the poetics of decoloniality by African, Arab, Asian, Caribbean, Chicanx, Indigenous, Latin American, and Pacific Islander writers such as Aimé Césaire, Edward Said, Frantz Fanon, Haunani-Kay Trask, and María Lugones. It asks: What is decolonization, decolonial theory, and decolonial feminism, and are we truly 'post-colonial'? How may a decolonial poetics help us understand our current existence in a time of ongoing genocide, settler colonialism, and endless war?

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Theory and Method in Asian American Studies
courses.comments: Course is intended for students excelling in the major or minor. Instructor approval is required.
courses.description: Exploration of the main theoretical orientations that have shaped Asian American studies; race and ethnicity, diasporas, international labor migration, etc. Introduction to several methodologies, including historiography, quantitative social science, literary criticism and ethnography.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Human Centered Design for Equity
courses.description: Training in the methods, rationale, and background of Human Centered Design. Practical experience applying this method to address an equity issue in today's world as defined by the students and faculty. Class is collaborative and project-based.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Asian American Academic Rhetoric
courses.prereq_text: Junior standing or higher. Instructor approval required.
courses.comments: AS AM 108 is the former number for AS AM 182.
courses.description: Advanced workshop for refining academic writing skills. Students will assess scholarly essays from various disciplines in Asian American studies. Course will refine mechanics of argumentation and analysis, but especially use of language, to produce academic prose that is rigorous: precise, concise, clear.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: From Guantánamo to Gaza: Critical Approaches to War, Detention, and Empire
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing and instructor approval required to finalize registration.
courses.description: This practicum-based seminar examines how carceral practices such as immigration detention, border policing, and racialized violence are central to US empire and militarism in domestic and transnational contexts. Topics include ICE detention, immigration rights/justice, Guantánamo, and Palestine.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Introductory Asian American Performance Workshop
courses.comments: AS AM 142 is the former number of AS AM 184.
courses.description: An introductory performance workshop focusing on Asian American themes. Students write original pieces, learn the basic techniques of stage performance, and participate in presenting a public performance at the end of the quarter.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Asian American Creative Writing
courses.description: A creative writing workshop focusing on Asian American themes. Different genres are emphasized depending on the instructor's preference and expertise.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Creating AAS Open Educational Resources
courses.prereq_text: A prior Upper Division course in Asian American Studies.
courses.comments: Priorities: AsAm majors and minors, open to non-majors. Students with lower-division standing (or without a prior upper-div AsAm course) may be admitted at instructor discretion.
courses.description: Asian American Studies should reach far beyond academia. How do we make it more accessible? In this course, we will make open educational resources (OER) about Asian Americans and Pacific Islanders for high school, college and lifelong learners. As Ethnic Studies courses become integrated into K-12 education, we need to ensure that there are public educational resources. In this course, we will build on and deepen our knowledge about Asian American Studies to collectively create Asian American Studies OER projects.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Doing Research on Asian American Activism
courses.description: Through this class, we will contribute to the recovery of Asian American activism by studying and producing knowledge on grassroots movements for liberation. We will read research studies on Asian American political movements and conduct original research on Asian American activism. Students will produce a research paper and a public intellectual project.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Comm Asian America
courses.description: Explores the central role that language and discourse play in the Asian American experience. Examines how everyday communication and interaction shape Asian American identities and structure how Asian American communities form and organize. Critically engages with historical and contemporary social discourses about Asian Americans, including the linguistic and discursive repertoires found in corporate, media, and popular culture that shape the relationships among members within Asian American communities, as well as their relationships with external, broader publics. We observe tensions and attend to problems of misrepresentation and to the openings they create for social transformation and community empowerment.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Health Justice Research
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; AS AM 20 or instructor permission.
courses.description: In this practicum seminar, students are expected to carry out a quarter-long, culturally-relevant and community-engaged research project or creative work focused on health justice. The course offers an interactive learning environment to understand the foundations of research, analysis, and dissemination in the process of conducting independent or collaborative health justice projects.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Ethic Studies Teacher Education Seminar
courses.prereq_text: At least one course in one of these departments: Asian American Studies, Black Studies, Chicana/o Studies, Feminist Studies.
courses.description: Designed for students who are Black Studies, Chicana/o Studies, Asian American and/or Feminist Studies majors in the XITO (Educational eXcellence and Inclusion Training Opportunities) program. Central to the year-long seminar will be preparations for students pursuit for a career as K-12 Ethnic Studies educators. Students will have direct assistance for preparing and applying to Masters/Teacher Education Programs as well as professionalization workshops.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Ethnic Studies Teacher Education Seminar
courses.prereq_text: At least one course in one of these departments: Asian American Studies, Black Studies, Chicana/o Studies, Feminist Studies.
courses.description: Designed for students who are Black Studies, Chicana/o Studies, Asian American and/or Feminist Studies majors in the XITO (Educational eXcellence and Inclusion Training Opportunities) program. Central to the year-long seminar will be preparations for students pursuit for a career as K-12 Ethnic Studies educators. Students will have direct assistance for preparing and applying to Masters/Teacher Education Programs as well as professionalization workshops.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Ethnic Studies Teacher Education Seminar
courses.prereq_text: At least one course in one of these departments: Asian American Studies, Black Studies, Chicana/o Studies, Feminist Studies.
courses.description: Designed for students who are Black Studies, Chicana/o Studies, Asian American and/or Feminist Studies majors in the XITO (Educational eXcellence and Inclusion Training Opportunities) program. Central to the year-long seminar will be preparations for students pursuit for a career as K-12 Ethnic Studies educators. Students will have direct assistance for preparing and applying to Masters/Teacher Education Programs as well as professionalization workshops.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Senior Honors Project
courses.prereq_text: Open only to Asian American Studies majors, Junior standing or higher.
courses.comments: Must have a 3.0 overall grade-point average and a 3.5 grade-point average in courses in the major.
courses.description: Offers an opportunity for students who meet the prerequisites to do independent research and to write an honors thesis or produce an honors film/video or performance.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Independent Studies
courses.prereq_text: A lower-division Asian American Studies course and 2 upper-division courses; upper-division standing.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters and are limited to 5 units per quarter, and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined. No more than 4 units per quarter and no more than 12 units total may be applied to the major.
courses.description: Independent study of topics not covered in the regular curriculum under the guidance of approved faculty member.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Independent Research Assistance in Asian American Studies
courses.description: Coursework consists of faculty supervised research assistance.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Critical Issues in Asian American Studies
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing in the social sciences or humanities or instructor consent.
courses.description: Graduate Seminar exploring critical themes and major debate in Asian American Studies. Readings cover perspectives that may include history, literature, sociology, anthropology, cultural studies, political science, gender and sexuality studies, psychology, and religious studies.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Laboratory for Teaching Assistants
courses.prereq_text: Appointment as a teaching assistant in an Asian American Studies course.
courses.comments: No unit credit allowed toward advanced degree.
courses.description: Supervised teaching of Asian American studies lower-division courses.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Group Studies
courses.description: Colloquium series in which graduate students attend lectures and engage in discussion of topics central to the discipline and participate in professional development activities, such as presenting papers, evaluating arguments, and advancing interdisciplinary knowledge.

courses.subject: AS AM
courses.title: Directed Reading and Research
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.
courses.description: Reading and research in special topics in Asian American studies.

courses.subject: AS AMW
courses.title: Introduction to Asian American History, 1850-Present
courses.comments: AS AM W 1 is the online version of AS AM 1.
courses.description: Historical survey of Asian Americans in the United States from 1850 to the present. Topics include: Immigration patterns, settlement and employment, race and gender relations, community development, and transnational connections.

courses.subject: AS AMW
courses.title: Martial Arts in U.S. Culture
courses.description: How did martial arts come to suffuse Hollywood action films? How did taekwondo studios crop up in Midwestern suburbs? This cultural-studies course explores those questions and more while engaging students in a range of research methods ethnography, textual analysis, phenomenology to contribute to collective knowledge about these histories and practices.

courses.subject: ASTRO
courses.title: Basic Astronomy
courses.comments: ASTROW 1 is the online version of ASTRO 1.
courses.description: A survey of the development of astronomy with an emphasis on understanding the observable properties of the solar system, the sun and other stars, our own and other galaxies, and the entire universe. Topics of current interest will be discussed as time permits.

courses.subject: ASTRO
courses.title: Honors Supplement to Basic Astronomy
courses.prereq_text: Honors standing. Concurrent enrollment in ASTRO 1.
courses.description: A supplement to Astronomy 1 emphasizing fundamental concepts and additional topics in astronomy. Intended for highly motivated and well prepared students.

courses.subject: ASTRO
courses.title: History of the Universe
courses.description: Content will vary with the professor and student interests. Course has included modern extragalactic astronomy and cosmology, quasars, active galactic nuclei, dark matter, gravitational lenses, the early universe, the origins of life, and the possibility of extraterrestrial intelligence.

courses.subject: ASTROW
courses.title: Basic Astronomy
courses.comments: ASTROW 1 is the online version of ASTRO 1.
courses.description: A survey of the development of astronomy with an emphasis on understanding the observable properties of the solar system, the sun and other stars, our own and other galaxies, and the entire universe. Topics of current interest will be discussed as time permits.

courses.subject: BIOE
courses.title: Responsible Conduct of Research
courses.description: The responsible conduct of research (RCR) is essential to good science. Examples of goals of RCR education and training are to:Develop, foster, and maintain a culture of integrity in science;discourage and prevent unethical conduct; empower researchers to hold themselves and others accountable to high ethical standards; increase knowledge of, and sensitivity to, ethical issues surrounding the conduct of research by researchers with diverse backgrounds; improve the ability to make responsible choices when faced with ethical dilemmas involving research; provide an appreciation for the range of accepted scientific practices for conducting research; inform scientists and research trainees about the regulations, policies, and statutes.

courses.subject: BIOE
courses.title: Molecular Bioengineering
courses.prereq_text: Chemistry 1B or 3B, Chemistry 2AL, Math 6B, and Physics 7B
courses.description: Introduces students to molecular components of biology with application of engineering principles for analysis. Topics include: molecular components of cells, DNA/RNA structure and function, protein structure/function/folding, gene and protein regulation, DNA replication, and experimental and computational research methods.

courses.subject: BIOE
courses.title: Cellular Bioengineering
courses.prereq_text: BIOE 120A, or ENGR 120A, or consent of Instructor
courses.description: Introduces students to structural components of cells with application of engineering principles for analysis. Topics include: biomembrane structure and function, membrane proteins, membrane transport, intracellular compartments, intracellular trafficking, chemotaxis, cell cycle, apoptosis, and stem cells.

courses.subject: BIOE
courses.title: Responsible Conduct of Research
courses.description: The responsible conduct of research (RCR) is essential to good science. Examples of goals of RCR education and training are to: Develop, foster, and maintain a culture of integrity in science; discourage and prevent unethical conduct; empower researchers to hold themselves and others accountable to high ethical standards; increase knowledge of, and sensitivity to, ethical issues surrounding the conduct of research by researchers with diverse backgrounds; improve the ability to make responsible choices when faced with ethical dilemmas involving research; provide an appreciation for the range of accepted scientific practices for conducting research; inform scientists and research trainees about the regulations, policies, and statutes.

courses.subject: BIOE
courses.title: Biomolecular and Biochemical Methods
courses.prereq_text: General biology, general chemistry, and differential equations
courses.description: The goal of the course is to generate in our students an understanding of the logic behind the key tools used to characterize biomolecules and biosystems. Both the mechanisms by which these techniques work, and the rationale for why each would be employed (strengths, weaknesses, potential pitfalls).

courses.subject: BIOE
courses.title: Quantitative Experiments
courses.prereq_text: At least one undergraduate course in biochemistry/cell biology and differential equations, or consent of the instructor.
courses.description: This course is built around experimental design, data analysis, and quantitative modeling of biological processes and phenomena. Topics including experimental design considerations and a priori assumptions, probability, dimensional reduction, hypothesis testing, statistical analysis, and quantitative modeling through ordinary and partial differential equations. Case studies of recent and classic research papers in Bioengineering are used to illustrate key course topics through class discussions.

courses.subject: BIOE
courses.title: Great Experiments
courses.prereq_text: BIOE 210 and BIOE 211 or consent of instructor.
courses.description: Reviews groundbreaking bioengineering experiments and discusses the writing and design of experiments, selection of experimental methods and controls, statistical data analysis, and hypothesis formulation. Students will ultimately create a draft experiment design based on their research interests and perform a peer review.

courses.subject: BIOE
courses.title: Molecular Bioengineering
courses.comments: Designed for graduate students enrolled in the bioengineering emphasis.
courses.description: Introduces students to molecular components of biology and application of engineering principles for their analysis. Topics include: molecular components of cells; DNA structure and function, including replication; gene regulation; protein structure, function, and folding; chemical kinetics; signal transduction and mathematical descriptions thereof; and mechanics of biomolecules and subcellular structures (membranes, cytoskeleton).

courses.subject: BIOE
courses.title: Cell and Tissue Bioengineering
courses.comments: Designed for graduate students enrolled in the optional bioengineering emphasis.
courses.description: Introduces students to structural components of cells, tissues, and organ systems, and the application of engineering principles for analysis. Topics include: biomembrane structure, function, and transport; intracellular compartments and trafficking; cell proliferation and death; cell-cell communication; biomaterials and stem cells; quantitative physiology of major organ systems (transport, mechanics, and electrical signaling); and homeostasis.

courses.subject: BIOE
courses.title: Current Topics in Bioengineering
courses.description: Seminar series highlighting current topics and advances in bioengineering presented by UCSB faculty or visiting scientists providing context and motivation for bioengineering learning, introducing students to concepts outside of their primary research specialty, and promoting interdisciplinary thinking and research collaboration.

courses.subject: BIOE
courses.title: Bioengineering Student Seminar
courses.comments: Designed for graduate students with a bioengineering emphasis
courses.description: Seminar series where students present their original thesis research and also review journal articles that critically analyze contemporary bioengineering research. Three quarters of BIOE 230 are required for the optional BioE graduate emphasis. Presentations are evaluated and feedback isprovided.

courses.subject: BIOE
courses.title: Bioengineering Faculty Seminar
courses.comments: Designed for graduate students with a bioengineering emphasis
courses.description: Seminar series where bioengineering faculty present ongoing research in their lab to provide graduate students insight into the work going on in the department.

courses.subject: BIOE
courses.title: Professional Development in Bioengineering
courses.comments: Designed for graduate students with a bioengineering emphasis
courses.description: Introduces students to non-technical topics (writing, figure preparation, etc.) important to the professional development of bioengineering graduate students.

courses.subject: BIOE
courses.title: Haptics: Touch Perception, Interaction, and Engineering
courses.description: Haptics lies at the intersection of robotics, human-computer interaction, and computational and human perception. The term haptics is often used to refer to science and engineering related to the sense of touch. This course introduces human haptics, including sensory specializations and touch perception. It reviews the engineering of electronic technologies for haptic (touch) feedback, emerging technologies, and the design of haptic systems for human-computer interaction, sensory substitution, virtual reality, augmented reality, and other emerging areas. The class involves a mix of readings, hands-on activities, lecture/discussion, and projects.

courses.subject: BIOE
courses.title: Engineering Biomaterials
courses.comments: ME 241 and BIOE 241 are the same course.
courses.description: This lecture-based course provides an overview of material structure-property relationships, processing, and characterization techniques for metals, polymers, and ceramics. We discuss the unique design constraints imposed by the human body and discuss strategies to enhance biocompatibility. Throughout the course, emphasis is placed on applications of biomaterials engineering in medical devices.

courses.subject: BIOE
courses.title: Tissue Engineering and Regenerative Medicine
courses.description: An introduction to the principles of tissue engineering: interplay and design of cells, biomaterials, and bioactive molecules to assist the body in the repair of damaged tissues. This includes concepts such as examining material fabrication approaches, engineering cells and their behavior, studying tissue microenvironments from diverse organ systems, the role of the extracellular matrix in repair, in vitro approaches to tissue engineering, and delivery of bioactive molecules (growth factors, extracellular vesicles, etc.), among others. By the end of this course, students will be able to design and evaluate tissue engineered constructs to repair a specific organ system.

courses.subject: BIOE
courses.title: Protein Engineering
courses.prereq_text: General chemistry (CHEM 1A-C or equivalent), organic chemistry (CHEM 109A or equivalent), and introductory biology (MCDB 1A or equivalent), and, for undergraduates, consent of the instructor.
courses.description: Introduces students to current methods and general principles of engineering proteins, in the design, build, test, learn (DBTL) framework, with a secondary goal of providing students a framework that they might extend to other biomolecules of interest (e.g., nucleic acids). Topics covered include protein basics, library design, library generation, library screening and selection, sequencing, and extracting design principles from library datasets.

courses.subject: BIOE
courses.title: Introduction to Machine Learning  for Processing of Biological Images and Structural Biology
courses.comments: IQB 206 and BIOE 244 are the same course
courses.description: Provides a general introduction to modern Machine Learning techniques with a focus on neural networks with relevance for biological image processing and structural biology applications across scales from the atomic level to organisms. Introductions to relevant concepts in biological image processing and structural biology will be part of the curriculum as well.

courses.subject: BIOE
courses.title: Special Topics in Biological Engineering
courses.description: Instruction in these variable unit courses may be carried out by lecture, by laboratory, or by a combination of these. These courses provide a study of topics of current interest in various areas of biological engineering.

courses.subject: BIOE
courses.title: Tissue Engineering and Regenerative Medicine
courses.description: An introduction to the principles of tissue engineering: interplay and design of cells, biomaterials, and bioactive molecules to assist the body in the repair of damaged tissues. This includes concepts such as examining material fabrication approaches, engineering cells and their behavior, studying tissue microenvironments from diverse organ systems, the role of the extracellular matrix in repair, in vitro approaches to tissue engineering, and delivery of bioactive molecules (growth factors, extracellular vesicles, etc.), among others. By the end of this course, students will be able to design and evaluate tissue engineered constructs to repair a specific organ system.

courses.subject: BIOE
courses.title: Protein Engineering
courses.prereq_text: General chemistry (CHEM 1A-C or equivalent), organic chemistry (CHEM 109A or equivalent), and introductory biology (MCDB 1A or equivalent), and, for undergraduates, consent of the instructor.
courses.description: Introduces students to current methods and general principles of engineering proteins, in the design, build, test, learn (DBTL) framework, with a secondary goal of providing students a framework that they might extend to other biomolecules of interest (e.g., nucleic acids). Topics covered include protein basics, library design, library generation, library screening and selection, sequencing, and extracting design principles from library datasets.

courses.subject: BIOE
courses.title: Introduction to Machine Learning  for Processing of Biological Images and Structural Biology
courses.description: Provides a general introduction to modern Machine Learning techniques with a focus on neural networks with relevance for biological image processing and structural biology applications across scales from the atomic level to organisms. Introductions to relevant concepts in biological image processing and structural biology will be part of the curriculum as well.

courses.subject: BIOE
courses.title: Special Topics in Biological Computing
courses.description: Introduces the basics of design of synthetic biological systems, including the architecture of genetic networks, circuits, and pathways controlling engineered biological function, as well as single-cell microbial behavior, and microbe population dynamics. Also provides a gentle introduction to workflows in biomolecular engineering, genetic circuit design, genomicediting, as well as principles of experimental design. An overview of various engineered and natural biological functions is provided, including multi-stability, biological oscillations, stochasticeffects in genetic circuits, robustness of circuit performance, and cellular capacity.

courses.subject: BIOE
courses.title: Gene Therapy
courses.description: Developing therapies using nucleic acids for human diseases is a high-risk, high-reward endeavor in bioengineering and medicine, with many challenges remaining to be addressed. However, once these obstacles have been overcome and widespread clinical success has been achieved, gene therapy will offer unparalleled opportunities for treating a range of disorders that are currently untreatable by conventional medical practices. The proposed course will explore the field of gene therapy, covering a wide range of topics, including gene delivery, noninvasive reporter gene imaging, genetic editing, clinical trials, and the social and ethical considerations of gene therapy.

courses.subject: BIOE
courses.title: Microalgae: Biotechnology and Applications
courses.description: Explores the biology, ecology, and biotechnological applications of microalgae, emphasizing their pivotal role in renewable energy, water treatment, and sustainable innovation. Students will gain foundational knowledge in microalgal classification, cell biology, growth dynamics, and ecological significance. Practical applications include biofuel production, wastewater remediation, and environmental sustainability strategies. The course blends theoretical frameworks with real-world case studies to prepare students for advanced research and industrial applications.

courses.subject: BIOE
courses.title: 3D Printing for Bioengineering
courses.description: 3D printing and bioprinting are critical tools used in bioengineering, from studying cell interactions to creating organs. Students learn the basics of mammalian cell culture and how it integrates with bioprinting, how to use CAD software to develop 3D prints through workshops during class, and ultimately design and print their own biological model, which will be used in an interactive demo for a local public outreach event. Students learn materials selection, multi-material printing, various types of printers, and what parameters are important to consider in 3D printing for biol. applications. While this course covers 3D printing, the focus is largely on biomedical and bioengineering applications of 3D printing and bioprinting.

courses.subject: BIOE
courses.title: Engineering Approaches to Systems Biology
courses.description: Applications of engineering tools and methods to solve problems in systems biology. Emphasis is placed on integrative approaches that address multi-scale and multi-rate phenomena in biological regulation. Modeling, optimization, and sensitivity analysis tools are introduced.

courses.subject: BIOE
courses.title: Stem Cell Biology
courses.comments: Graduate Course. Qualified undergraduate students may petition to enroll with instructor approval.
courses.description: Focuses on the latest developments in stem cell biology, including ongoing clinical trials using stem cell therapies to treat unmet medical needs. In depth analysis of the current literature in stem cell biology, bioengineering and biophysical analyses is also covered. The discipline of stem cell biology and applications of cell therapy have elements of bioengineering, biomaterials, and biophysics.

courses.subject: BIOE
courses.title: Methods in Mechanobiology and Biofabrication
courses.prereq_text: The course assumes an engineering background but is structured to be accessible to graduate students in life sciences who have a strong physics and math background, and to engineering graduate students with basic biology knowledge.
courses.comments: BIOE 258, BMSE 258, and ME 258 are the same course.
courses.description: Cell mechanobiology topics including cell structure, mechanical models, and chemo-mechanical signaling. Review methods for controlling and analyzing the biomechanics of cells using traction force microscopy, AFM, micropatterning, and cell stimulation. Weekly lecture with final project in the form of a research proposal.

courses.subject: BIOE
courses.title: Omics-enabled Biotechnology
courses.comments: Molecular and Cell Biology (undergraduate level)
courses.description: Integrates genomic, transcriptomic, metabolomic, and proteomic approaches to quantify and understand intricate biological systems. Complementary bioinformatics approaches to curate the large datasets associated with these experiments are also discussed. Recent examples from the literature reinforce core concepts, ranging from applications to human health to the environment. By the end of the course, students should be able to design an integrated experiment that capitalizes on these omics-based approaches to enhance the scope of their research.

courses.subject: BIOE
courses.title: Model-Guided Engineering of Biological Systems
courses.description: Introduction to fundamental principles underlying synthetic biology with an emphasis on mathematical modeling of gene regulation using ordinary differential equations and mass action kinetics. Students are introduced to foundational concepts in molecular and cellular engineering, synthetic biology, quantitative modeling of various genetic circuits, as well as cutting edge applications of innovative molecular biotechnologies such as cancer immunotherapy and cell-based diagnostics. Students will also learn to design and predict the functional outcomes of synthetic gene circuits and review primary literature in the field. Graduate students enrolled will be required to submit an additional project.

courses.subject: BIOE
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Independent study related to pursuit of a research project related to the field of Bioengineering under the advisement of a BioE faculty mentor.

courses.subject: BIOE
courses.title: Internship in Industry
courses.description: This course is an internship experience to be carried out an external company, government, or another private organization apart from UCSB. Students will work alongside working professionals to gain applied experience and skills in industry.

courses.subject: BIOE
courses.title: Directed Research
courses.prereq_text: Must be a graduate student enrolled in the Biological Engineering PhD Program.
courses.description: Experimental or theoretical research undertaken under the direction of a faculty member for graduate students who have not yet advanced to candidacy.

courses.subject: BIOL CS
courses.title: Group Studies
courses.description: Student-directed discussion and study in a variety of subjects within Biology.

courses.subject: BIOL CS
courses.title: Biology Colloquium
courses.comments: May be taken as often as once each quarter.
courses.description: Students receiving credit will present talks in their field on material arranged in consultation with the instructor. Credit assigned by the instructor will reflect the extent and quality of participation.

courses.subject: BIOL CS
courses.title: CCS Introductory Biology I
courses.comments: This variable unit course is normally taken for 1 unit.
courses.description: This course is supplementary to MCDB 1A. It is intended for and open only to CCS students enrolled in MCDB 1A. Students will attend MCDB 1A lectures and also meet for more in-depth consideration and analysis of the lecture materials and their broader implications.

courses.subject: BIOL CS
courses.title: CCS Introductory Biology II - Evolution and Diversity
courses.comments: This variable unit course is normally taken for 5 units.
courses.description: Lecture, field and laboratory activities explore the evolutionary origin and diversification of life in a phylogenetic context, from bacteria and archaea to plants, fungi and animals.

courses.subject: BIOL CS
courses.title: Walking Biology
courses.comments: This variable unit course is normally taken for 4 units.
courses.description: Field course introducing students to the ecological communities in Santa Barbara County, including oak woodlands, chaparral, coastal dune, salt marsh, sandy beach, rocky inter-tidal, and stream.

courses.subject: BIOL CS
courses.title: CCS Introductory Biology III - Ecology and Physiology
courses.comments: This variable unit course is normally taken for 5 units.
courses.description: An integrative approach introduces students to fundamental concepts of population and community ecology, and to plant and animal physiology. Field and laboratory activities illustrate basic principles in ecology and physiology as they influence the distribution and abundance or organisms.

courses.subject: BIOL CS
courses.title: Models and Experiments
courses.comments: May be taken as often as once each quarter.
courses.description: Interplay between models and experimentation in the development of an understanding of the principles of biology.

courses.subject: BIOL CS
courses.title: Presentation Literacy
courses.comments: This variable unit course is normally taken for 2 units.
courses.description: Introduction to the major methods of presenting research results: formal talks, research papers and posters. Students will practice presenting their research in different formats for different audiences.

courses.subject: BIOL CS
courses.title: Independent Studies
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit. Creative Studies students may enroll in a maximum of 24 units of Independent Studies courses per year, with a maximum of 45 units counted toward graduation.
courses.description: Serious independent study in biology with consenting faculty member.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Introduction to African-American Studies
courses.description: Explores historical and current social conditions of Black people in the United States. Topics include the following: origins of Black Studies; chattel slavery and resistance; Reconstruction; Jim Crow segregation; Harlem Renaissance; Black Nationalism; structural racism and anti-Blackness; Civil Rights and Black Power Movements; racial wealth gap; critical race theory and Neo-liberalism; carcerality and the prison industrial complex; white privilege and rage; and the intersection of race, gender, class, and sexuality in shaping Black identity and life chances. As a 5 unit course, BLST 1 is reading and writing intensive, with a focus on developing research skills through a Black Studies lens.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Global Blackness: Race, Repair and Reparation
courses.comments: LAIS 2 and BL ST 2 are the same course.
courses.description: Discusses historical and contemporary conditions of Black and racialized communities living under economic and militarized oppression in a global perspective. Texts, films and lecture presentations foregrounds the critical role of Black subjects in the expansion of global capitalism. Explores current global conditions of Black and racialized communities living under militarized and economic apartheid. Spotlights the role of culture in shaping struggles of Black communities around the world for self-determination, the (im)possibilities of colonial repair and collective demands for reparation.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Introduction to African Studies
courses.description: A survey of the subject matter, themes, and methods of African Studies. While briefly surveying the prehistory and early states of Africa, the course focuses on the culture and society of the colonial and independence eras.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Critical Race Theory
courses.description: Critically examines historical and contemporary manifestations of racism and anti-racism, as well as theoretical approaches to understand the social, cultural, political and economic aspects of race and race relations.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: The Civil Rights Movement
courses.description: History of the modern civil rights movements, its organization and ideology from its origins in the post reconstruction era to its triumphs with the end of legal racial segregation, and its recognition in the civil rights legislation in the 1960s.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Introduction to Caribbean Studies
courses.comments: LAIS 7 and BL ST 7 are the same course. Students who have received credit for Black Studies 1B may not take this course for credit.
courses.description: A survey of the culture and society of the Caribbean. After surveying Amerindian communities and examining the impact of the Atlantic slave trade, focus will be on slavery, emancipation, African and Creole cultures,and the issues accompanying an independent nationhood status.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Community Studies Organizing for Change
courses.comments: AS AM 11 and BL ST 11 are the same course.
courses.description: This course examines various aspects of community organizing for equity and justice. The course will introduce models for social change and approaches to leadership development. It will examine case studies of campaigns for justice, within the context of social movement histories.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: The History of Jazz
courses.description: A survey of the historical origins and development of jazz, beginning with the West African heritage and the African-American folk tradition, and examining the social and cultural context of this twentieth-century music.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: African American Psychology
courses.description: Examines manifestations of psychological characteristics of people of African decent, cultural and behavioral norms, and ways that race, class, gender and sexuality affect their cognitive, social, and emotional development. Connections between Africa, the Caribbean, and Afro-America are explored.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Capoeira: Arts, History & Resistance in the African Diaspora
courses.description: Examines the role of music, dance and spirituality in informing Black resistance in the African Diaspora. Balancing between theory and practicum, the course explores the aesthetics of Black resistance through the medium of dance and music, with particular focus on Afro-Brazilian cultural repertoire, and also involves learning and practicing Capoeira techniques. A primary goal is to enhance awareness of the history of racial subjugation and racial resistance in the making of contemporary Black performances through dance and music. Students will learn history, techniques and styles of Afro-dance, capoeira and other cultural repertoire including contemporary and historical practices inherited from the struggle for abolition.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Major Works of African Literatures
courses.comments: Comparative Literature 33 and Black Studies 33 are the same course.
courses.description: An introduction to the diverse literary traditions of Africa through an examination of selected works. Regional focus on North, West, East, Central, and South Africa varies.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Introduction to African-American Literature (Part 1)
courses.comments: Black Studies 38A and English 38A are the same course.
courses.description: African-American literature from colonial times through the Harlem Renaissance.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Black Arts Expressions
courses.description: A comparative examination of the traditions of African American music, literature, dance, folklore, cinema, the visual arts, and musical theatre. No prior musical background is required, though some musicological concepts and nomenclature are employed.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Survey of African History
courses.comments: History 49A and Black Studies 49A are the same course.
courses.description: Prehistory to c. 1800. History 49-A- B-C is a general survey course designed to introduce students to major themes in African history. The course focuses on organization of production, state formation, African civilizations and identities, science and technology, beliefs and knowledge systems, Africas interaction with the world economy, such as through enslavement and slave trades. Weekly discussion sections are an important feature of this course, enabling students to develop and expand upon material presented during lecture.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Survey of African History
courses.comments: History 49B and Black Studies 49B are the same course.
courses.description: 1800 - 1945. History 49-A-B-C is a general survey course designed to introduce students to major themes in African history. The course focuses on African civilizations and identities, European colonial conquests, governance and colonial economies, African resistance and engagement with global capitalism. Weekly discussion sections are an important feature of this course, enabling students to develop and expand upon material presented during lecture.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Survey of African History
courses.comments: History 49C and Black Studies 49C are the same course.
courses.description: 1945 to present. History 49-A- B-C is a general survey course designed to introduce students to major themes in African history. The course focuses on colonialism and decolonization, nationalism and self-liberation, development and neocolonialism, Cold War contexts, as well as African experiences of independence and the everyday in our contemporary, global world. Weekly discussion sections are an important feature of this course, enabling students to develop and expand upon material presented during lecture.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Mass Media, Blackness and the Politics of Representation
courses.description: The development of Black stereotypes. Studying literature, comic books, comic strips, cartoons, music, theater, cinema, broadcasting, and television, students analyze the mythical imageries which have created stereotypes.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Roots & Routes: History, Politics, Reinventions
courses.description: Rooted in the rich intellectual tradition of Black Studies—and routed in our commitment to make the national narrative “liberty and justice for all” a reality—this gateway course offers students grounded and cutting-edge knowledge in areas including law, education, politics, geography, music, film, media, technology, ecology + environment, health + wellness + science, art for social justice, AI for social justice, and more. In gaining such knowledge, students will learn/sharpen logical deduction skills through social science explorations in interesting and innovative ways with high applicability across majors. Join the journey as we experience Black freedom dreams of the past, present, and future!

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Independent Studies in Black Studies
courses.description: Independent studies and mentorship in Black Studies under the direction of a faculty member in the department.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Independent Research Assistance in Black Studies
courses.description: Coursework shall consist of faculty supervised research assistance.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Africa and United States Policy
courses.description: Post-World War II Africa and United States foreign policy. Special attention is devoted to southern Africa and parallels between social movements in that part of the world and the United States civil rights movement.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Teaching 4 Social Justice
courses.prereq_text: At least one course in one of these departments: Asian American Studies, Black Studies, Chicana/o Studies, Feminist Studies
courses.comments: AS AM 101C, BL ST 101C, CH ST 101C, and FEMST 101C are cross-listed.
courses.description: This interdisciplinary course will highlight how a curriculum focusing on racial, ethnic, gender, and LGBTQ studies is central to teaching and learning within diverse societal contexts. This grounding is essential for K-12 teachers in History and English/Literature. Through a social justice framework, students will learn how classrooms are enhanced by Ethnic and Feminist Studies, placing graduates within the forefront of educational initiatives that position teaching and learning within an inclusive and equitable paradigm.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: The Black Radical Tradition
courses.description: This course examines the tradition of radical thought and the relevance of this thought to the needs and interests of the Black community.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: From Malcolm X to #BlackLivesMatter
courses.description: Provides an analysis of Black liberation efforts and their attending ideologies and strategies from the 1960s Black Power organizations to contemporary Black Lives Matter movements. Study of grassroots organizations and their struggles shedding light on their pedagogies of resistance and the intransigence of entrenched American racism.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Black Marxism
courses.description: A theoretical explication and critique of the diverse Marxian analyses developed in Africa and the African Diaspora from the early 20th century. The course traces and analyzes the divergences of Black Marxisms from Western Marxism.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Women, Wellness and Politics of the Body
courses.comments: BL ST 106 and ESS 106 are the same course.
courses.description: Examines the relationship between race and gender in the construction of bodily politics that include perceptions of beauty, femininity and access to wellness. In understanding how race and gender matter in conceptualizations of beauty and wellness, this course centers Black women's bodies as important sites of resistance.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Black Politics: From People to Presidents
courses.description: Examines the historical, cultural and political nature of Black electoral politics. Given the historical nexus of race, gender and class in the United States, the course will explore the historical implications of Black president(s) and Black presidential candidates in the country's modern history.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Empire: the Geopolitics of Race
courses.description: Examines the historical and contemporary role of the United States' foreign policy in the constitution of domestic and global racial orders. Special attention is devoted to the US intervention in Africa and Latin America and parallels between Pan African social movements in these parts of the world and the struggle for Black liberation in the United States. Analysis of current foreign policies oriented by the "war on terror" and energy security provides the context for exploring the continuous re-making of imperial geographies of anti-Blackness and white supremacy.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Slavery and Modernity
courses.description: An interdisciplinary examination of Black slavery as both a historical event and an enduring condition. The course highlights the foundational role of colonialism and the transatlantic slave trade in the making of European modernity, the white subject of rights and the black dispossessed nonbeing, liberal democracy, and contemporary regimes of black captivities. Special focus is given to the political and economic history of the United States, the Caribbean and Brazil as slavocracies and to the incomplete project of emancipation that renders Black citizenship at best elusive. Critical transnational perspective highlights the spatio-temporal continuum between plantation regimes and contemporary global racial apartheid.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Comparative Rebellion
courses.description: Examines key events in Brown/Black resistance and rebellion in the U. S. and the Borderlands. Using primary and secondary sources, the course emphasizes parallel rebellions, transnational revolutionary thought, and cross-racial alliances.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Black Youth, Development, and Critical Education Studies
courses.description: Explores the effects of social, political, and economic forces on the history of Black education. Examines ways of challenging the impacts of race, class, gender, and language in the educational achievement of Black children. Focuses on anti-bias/multicultural curricula in urban settings. Fieldwork required.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Community Studies Knowledge in Action
courses.comments: AS AM 123A and BL ST 123A are the same course.
courses.description: The first in a 2-course series for the Community Studies Pathways Program. Students will gain scholarly knowledge, experiential knowledge, networking experience, and community building skills to facilitate community-based careers. Both courses (123A and 123B) are required for the program.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Community Studies and Career Pathways
courses.comments: AS AM 123B and BL ST 123B are the same course.
courses.description: The second in a 2-course series for the Community Studies Pathways Program. Students will gain scholarly knowledge, experiential knowledge, networking experience, and community building skills to facilitate community-based careers. Both courses (123A and 123B) are required for the program.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Housing, Debt, and Race
courses.description: Housing discrimination systematically skews opportunities and life chances in the United States across racial lines. This course examines the origins and evolution of fair housing laws, and the role that housing plays in asset accumulation, inheritance, and wealth.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Queer Black Studies
courses.description: An exploration of the intersection of Black Studies and Queer Studies from various theoretical, literary, historical, and multi-media perspectives. Cultural producers studied include: Audre Lorde, Marlon Riggs, Bayard Rustin, and Bruce Nugent.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Comparative Black Literatures
courses.comments: Black Studies 126 and Comparative Literature 126 are the same course.
courses.description: Using a social constructionist approach to race, this course examines the multiple ways in which racial discourses operate in global literary cultures. It emphasizes that blackness need not be a homogeneous concept in order to continue to be a powerful agent in the postmodern world.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Black Women Writers
courses.description: Examines the significance of race, class, gender, sexuality, and place as experienced and articulated in the literature of Black women of the African diaspora.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: The Black Experience in Southern California
courses.description: An interdisciplinary examination of the history, culture, economic conditions, policy debates, and social movements of Blacks in Southern California from 1781 to the present. Music, literature, film, autobiography, and social theory are used to analyze the processes of regional and racial transformation.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Black Cities: Spatial Politics of Violence, Power and Resistance
courses.description: Examines spatial dynamics of anti-Blackness and spatial politics of resistance in relational and comparative geographical perspectives. Study of colonial histories of spatial violence and current patterns of residential segregation, homelessness, and police brutality, as well as the struggle for urban citizenship in societies of the African Diaspora. The goal of the course is threefold: a) it analyzes institutional policies and mundane practices that produce cityscapes as anti-Black; b) it interrogates the Marxist-oriented framework on the right to the city; and c) it gives visibility to Black gendered spatial praxes that challenge exclusionary city politics and their attending geographies of anti-Blackness.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Negritude and African Literature
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have taken Black Studies 30A.
courses.description: History of Francophone West Indian and African literature from the 1920s through the 1950s. Writers studied include Aime and Suzanne Cesaire, Leon Gontran Damas, Leopold Sedar Senghor, and Jane and Paulette Nardal.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: The Black Francophone Novel
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have taken Black Studies 30B.
courses.description: A study of theoretical and literary discourses of decolonization that appeared simultaneously in Africa and the West Indies after the second World War. Writers studied include Mongo Beti, Camara Laye, Aime Cesaire, Ferdinand Oyono, Miriam Warner-Viegyra, Maryse Conde, and Simone Schwartz-Bart.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Race and Public Policy
courses.description: Provides a theoretical overview of the role of race and ethnicity in local, national, and international public policy debates. Examines critical case studies of several policies: regional development, social welfare, environment, criminal justice, etc. Student policy projects with fieldwork component included.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Gender and Sexuality in Black Studies
courses.description: Examines the intersection of gender, sexuality, race, and class in creating disadvantage and advantage. In examining how racism, sexism, and heterosexism shape Black life chances in a 21st century context, this course focuses on systems of oppression that exist within and outside Black communities.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Black Feminist Thought
courses.description: Examines past and contemporary scholarship in Black feminist thought. By examining the intervention of Black feminist thought within mainstream feminist theory and the field of Black Studies, this course presents a critical examination of the theoretical and practical contributions of Black feminist scholars.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Black Family, Community, and Society
courses.description: Sociological overview of the experiences of Black families in the United States from enslavement to more contemporary eras. Sociological analysis of the changing historical significance of Black families in the United States will be presented.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: African Religions in the Americas
courses.comments: Same course as Religious Studies 156.
courses.description: A study of Neo-African religions in the Americas, with special emphasis on Haitian Vodou. Beliefs, myths, philosophical perspectives, moral order, rituals and practices as well as social and political dynamics are examined in various contemporary religious communities. Women's roles and sexuality issues are also explored.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Hip-Hop: Power, Poetics and Protest
courses.description: Designed to introduce students to the history and contemporary influence of hip hop, including rap music, break dancing, graffiti, Bboying, djing, fashion, global marketing, etc. Traces the history of hip hop from its early emergence in the Bronx in the 1970s to its emergence as the global soundtrack of the 21st century. Students will also study the particular urban geographies of hip hop culture and its critique of social, political, and economic conditions of Black life.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Survey of Theories of Performance and Identity
courses.description: Course examines theories of performance, identity and culture. It queries the way the categories through which we live are themselves performative and examines the relationship between these and more conventional forms of staged and public performances.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Black Performance: Practices, Histories and Genres
courses.description: Practices, traditions, histories, methodologies, and genres of Black performance as chosen by instructor. Radical traditions might focus on plays, spoken word, or oratory; a methodological topic might focus on ethnography. A genre might be dance; a history, Shakespeare or burlesque.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Performance of Literature
courses.comments: Same Course as English 176PL
courses.description: Explores relationships between performances of identity, literary analysis, and the staging of literature. Students conceptualize the performance of identity, space, and text through original dramatization of literary materials that they prepare, stage, and embody. No theater experience required.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Gender, Sexuality and Slavery
courses.comments: BL ST 193GS is the former number of BL ST 151. Students who have completed BL ST 193GS with a C- or below may take BL ST 151 as a legal repeat.
courses.description: Critical explorations of aesthetic, narrative, thematic, ideological, cultural and interdisciplinary configurations which frame representations of femininities, masculinities, and sexualities under slavery. The complex dynamics between art and society, issues of identity, difference, agency, resistance, and change, will be explored.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Music of the African Diaspora
courses.description: A survey of select African derived musical traditions from the Caribbean, North and South America, and Africa.

courses.subject: BL ST
