courses.title: Black Feminism and Popular Music
courses.description: This course engages the music of Black women recording artists as popular, accessible expressions of African American feminisms that reach worldwide audiences. Beginning with close analysis of women artists songs and videos, we read their oeuvre in conversation with Black feminist theoretical works. The course provides students with an introduction to media studies methodology as well as Black feminist theory, and to challenge us to close the gap between popular and academic expressions of Black womens concerns.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Environmental Racism and Environmental Justice
courses.description: This course investigates environmental injusticethat some people, especially poorer people, bear a disproportionate burden of living in communities with environmental hazardsand environmental racismthat a high coincidence exists between the location of toxic waste sites and Black and Brown communities, even when they are predominantly middle class.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Black Aesthetics:  History, Art and Visuality
courses.description: Enables students to think critically about how visual politics have shaped the landscape of race, how visual arts are related to other expressions of culture, such as media, music, theatre, and dance, and how Black artists have embodied and contested regimes of racial knowledge anchored in the visualization of Blackness.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Haiti: Local Realities, Global Influences
courses.comments: GLOBL 147 and BL ST 157 are the same course.
courses.description: Since the January 2010 Earthquake in Haiti, the country has been widely recognized as a Nation of NGO's. This course explores local realities as well as global issues and influences that contribute to Haiti's poverty and weakened state.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Race, Gender and Medicine in the United States
courses.description: In-depth analysis of the history, ideological and scientific origins of racism in the United States from the nineteenth century. The effects of institutional racism on social policy, desegregation, integration, and affirmative action programs are also examined.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: African Cinema
courses.description: Critical perspectives on African cinema from its inception to the present. Production contexts, aesthetic/narrative strategies, ideological/ representational concerns are examined along with issues of authorship, culture, gender, identity, post-coloniality, etc.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Antiblack Hair Injustice: History, Law, & Politics
courses.description: Examines how black hair discrimination is a perfect example of antiblack racism in employment and schools during the era of integration, despite civil rights legislation and protections under Title VII. By examining court cases brought against employers, schools, and companies that produce toxic haircare products, the course illuminates how antiblack hair injustice upends civil rights law.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: African-American History
courses.prereq_text: Black Studies 1 or 5 or History 17A or 17B or 17C or upper-division standing.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Black Studies 169A.
courses.description: Influence/experience of Africans/African-Americans in United States history. Origins and developments of slavery and racism in British colonies.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: African-American History
courses.prereq_text: Any lower-division course in Black Studies or History, or upper-division standing.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Black Studies 169B or History 169BR.
courses.description: Influence/experience of Africans/African-Americans in United States history. Nineteenth-century expansion of slavery, anti-slavery, civil war, reconstruction and development of segregation.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: African-American History
courses.prereq_text: Black Studies 1 or 5 or History 17A or 17B or 17C or upper-division standing.
courses.comments: Same course as History 169CR.
courses.description: Influence/experience of Africans/African-Americans in United States history. Twentieth-century New South, urban migration and desegregation.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Framing Blackness: African-Americans in the American Cinema
courses.description: An examination of the representation of African-Americans in the Hollywood feature film from 1915 to the present. The course explores the relationship between screen icons and the racial attitudes held by Black and White Americans.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Africa in Film
courses.description: Explores, with examples from the dominant cinema industry, the relationship between ideology and representation, especially how Africa functions as a site of complex and conflicting meanings under the Hollywoodian gaze.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Contemporary Black Cinema
courses.description: The course explores the new directions in African-American cinema with emphasis on the directors, the aesthetics and the social content of contemporary Black film. The problems of production, distribution, and exhibition will be examined.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: From Plantations to Prisons: Policing, Carcerality, and Abolition
courses.description: Provides a critical perspective on current patterns of policing and mass incarceration in the United States and beyond. The course examines the historical roots and ideological justifications for police and prison and how notions of crime and order shape the ways we understand and justify and justify anti-Black policing policies. Focuses on fighting-crime strategies (such as one-strike, zero tolerance and the war on drugs) and their deepening of social vulnerabilities along gender, race, sexuality and class lines. Engages with abolitionist responses to neoliberal carcerality and its prison industrial complex.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Black Diaspora Cinema
courses.description: Survey of Black cinematic expressions from the Americas, Europe and Africa as they articulate and negotiate racial, cultural and gendered identities. Analysis of these films will be related to specific national cinemas, narrative categories, representational strategies and aesthetic forms.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Black Film Production
courses.description: This course is designed to teach students Black film history as a production workshop. Students will learn the technologies used by Black filmmakers from Oscar Micheaux to Ava DuVernay. The class will write and produce scenes on iMovie reflecting the styles and techniques of a particular period in Black film production.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Professional Development Seminar
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing. Two courses from BLST 1, 2, 3, 7 must be completed before enrolling in BLST 180.
courses.comments: This course is currently offered to BLST majors and minors.
courses.description: Professional development seminar for majors and minors designed to strengthen students' reasoning, writing, and research skills. The seminar also assists majors and minors with skills needed in applying for jobs and graduate or professional school, as well as highlights how Black Studies will add value to occupational and educational objectives in a variety of areas upon graduating with a Bachelor’s degree.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Senior Thesis Seminar in Black Studies
courses.prereq_text: Open to senior Black Studies majors who have completed most of the degree requirements.
courses.comments: BL ST 190A, formerly BL ST 190, is now part of the Black Studies senior thesis series. Students must be a BL ST major, senior standing, and receive consent from the department to enroll.
courses.description: Focus on producing a research proposal by identifying a research topic and research question, argumentation (why the study matters), methods and methodology, and literature search and review.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Honors Thesis Seminar in Black Studies
courses.prereq_text: By Department invitation only. Open to senior Black Studies majors who have completed most of the degree requirements.
courses.comments: BL ST 190AH was formerly BL ST 195A. Students must be a BL ST major, senior standing, and receive consent from the department to enroll.
courses.description: Focus on producing a research proposal by identifying a research topic and research question, argumentation (why the study matters), methods and methodology, and literature search and review.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Senior Thesis Seminar in Black Studies
courses.prereq_text: Open to senior Black Studies majors who have completed most of the degree requirements.
courses.comments: BL ST 190B is part of the Black Studies senior thesis series. Students must be a BL ST major, senior standing, and receive consent from the department to enroll.
courses.description: Focus on method/methodology (in connection to data collection), data collection, and initial analysis of data.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Honors Thesis Seminar in Black Studies
courses.prereq_text: By Department invitation only. Open to senior Black Studies majors who have completed most of the degree requirements.
courses.comments: BL ST 190BH was formerly BL ST 195B. Students must be a BL ST major, senior standing, and receive consent from the department to enroll.
courses.description: Focus on method/methodology (in connection to data collection), data collection, and initial analysis of data.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Senior Thesis Seminar in Black Studies
courses.prereq_text: Open to senior Black Studies majors who have completed most of the degree requirements.
courses.comments: BL ST 190C is part of the Black Studies senior thesis series. Students must be a BL ST major, senior standing, and receive consent from the department to enroll.
courses.description: Focus on continuing analysis and data discussion and completing the senior thesis.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Honors Thesis Seminar in Black Studies
courses.prereq_text: By Department invitation only. Open to senior Black Studies majors who have completed most of the degree requirements.
courses.comments: BL ST 190CH was formerly BL ST 195C. Students must be a BL ST major, senior standing, and receive consent from the department to enroll.
courses.description: Focus on continuing analysis and data discussion, completing the senior honors thesis, and preparing to present an academic paper at the departmental Spring Colloquium for earning distinction (honors) in the major.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Special Topics in Black Studies.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 16 units provided letter designations are different (only 4 units may be applied toward the major from BL ST 191AA-ZZ and BL ST 193AA-ZZ combined.)
courses.description: Designed to broaden opportunities for students by offering topics related to the Black experience.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Special Topics in Black Studies.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 16 units provided letter designations are different (only 12 units may be applied toward the major).
courses.description: Designed to broaden opportunities for students by offering topics related to the Black experience.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Seminars in Black Studies
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different (only 4 units may be applied toward the major from BL ST 191AA-ZZ and BL ST 193AA-ZZ combined).
courses.description: Seminars focus on a specific topic chosen by the professor, involve in-depth reading of a number of works and the writing of papers on subjects chosen in consultation with the instructor. See department website for seminar titles.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Afro-American History.
courses.prereq_text: upper-division standing and consent of instructor. may be repeated for cred
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different (only 8 units may be applied toward the major).
courses.description: Seminars will focus on a specific topic chosen by the professor and will involve in-depth reading of a number of works and the writing of a paper on a subject chosen in consultation with the instructor.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Ethnic Studies Teacher Education Seminar
courses.prereq_text: At least one course in one of these departments: Asian American Studies, Black Studies, Chicana/o Studies, Feminist Studies.
courses.description: Designed for students who are Black Studies, Chicana/o Studies, Asian American and/or Feminist Studies majors in the XITO (Educational eXcellence and Inclusion Training Opportunities) program. Central to the year-long seminar will be preparations for students pursuit for a career as K-12 Ethnic Studies educators. Students will have direct assistance for preparing and applying to Masters/Teacher Education Programs as well as professionalization workshops.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Ethnic Studies Teacher Education Seminar
courses.prereq_text: At least one course in one of these departments: Asian American Studies, Black Studies, Chicana/o Studies, Feminist Studies.
courses.description: Designed for students who are Black Studies, Chicana/o Studies, Asian American and/or Feminist Studies majors in the XITO (Educational eXcellence and Inclusion Training Opportunities) program. Central to the year-long seminar will be preparations for students pursuit for a career as K-12 Ethnic Studies educators. Students will have direct assistance for preparing and applying to Masters/Teacher Education Programs as well as professionalization workshops.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Ethnic Studies Teacher Education Seminar
courses.prereq_text: At least one course in one of these departments: Asian American Studies, Black Studies, Chicana/o Studies, Feminist Studies.
courses.description: Designed for students who are Black Studies, Chicana/o Studies, Asian American and/or Feminist Studies majors in the XITO (Educational eXcellence and Inclusion Training Opportunities) program. Central to the year-long seminar will be preparations for students pursuit for a career as K-12 Ethnic Studies educators. Students will have direct assistance for preparing and applying to Masters/Teacher Education Programs as well as professionalization workshops.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Research Seminar
courses.description: Directed field research or writing seminar on a topic in Black Studies.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Independent Studies in Black Studies
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing and consent of instructor.
courses.description: Independent Studies in Black Studies

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Independent Research Assistance in Black Studies
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing and consent of instructor.
courses.description: Coursework shall consist of faculty supervised research assistance.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Graduate Proseminar
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing. Completion of at least 12 upper-division units related to the subject matter of the course.
courses.description: Critical inquiry based on dissertation related research addressing several issues in the curricular development of black studies: research writing, formal presentation, postdoctoral programs, revision, and journal publication process.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Issues in Black Studies Epistemology and Pedagogy
courses.description: Introduces students to Black Studies as a field with its own logic and history of inquiry. Students gain a methodology for creating paradigms, organizing and interpreting data, and constructing knowledge through research and teaching in Black Studies.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Harlem and Other Renaissances in Global Perspective
courses.description: Examines renaissances as a social, economic, political, and cultural phenomena in comparative world perspective. Interrogates Harlem, Irish, Italian, Mexican renaissances.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Environmental Racism and Environmental Justice
courses.description: This course investigates environmental injusticethat some people, especially poorer people, bear a disproportionate burden of living in communities with environmental hazardsand environmental racismthat a high coincidence exists between location of toxic waste sites and Black and Brown communities, even when they are predominantly middle class.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Teaching Methodology in Black Studies
courses.prereq_text: To enroll, must have an active appointment as a Teaching Assistant in Black Studies.
courses.description: For graduate students who serve as teaching assistants: analyses of texts and materials; discussion of teaching techniques; conducting discussion sections; formulation of topics and questions for papers and examinations; and grading papers and examinations under supervision of instructor assigned to course.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Directed Reading and Research
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit on approval from the Department Chair.
courses.description: Individual tutorial. Plan of study must be approved by the Department Chair.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: Master's Thesis Research and Preparation
courses.description: To assist graduate students who are doing research or writing their master's thesis in African area studies and/or Black Studies.

courses.subject: BL ST
courses.title: PhD Dissertation Research and Preparation
courses.description: PhD Dissertation Research and Preparation

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Memory: Bridging the Humanities and Neurosciences
courses.comments: French 40X and Comparative Literature 27 are the same course.
courses.description: Neurosciences now ask some of the same profound questions posed by writers, artists and philosophers for centuries, thus opening surprising perspectives on memory and morality, dreams and perception, identity and agency. This course explores this emerging concordance.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Major Works in European Literature
courses.description: A survey of European literature. Classical and medieval literature from Homer to Dante.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Major Works in European Literature
courses.comments: ENGL 30B and C LIT 30B are the same course.
courses.description: A survey of European literature. Renaissance and Neoclassical literature from Petrarch to Diderot.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Major Works in European Literature
courses.description: A survey of European literature. Romantic and modern literature from Rousseau to Solzhenitsyn.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Honors Section
courses.description: Seminar course for honors students enrolled in Comparative Literature 30 designed to enrich the large lecture experience and to supplement the weekly seminar meetings. May include additional readings, more intensive study of syllabus selections, and supplemental writings.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Major Works of Asian Literatures
courses.description: An introduction to the diverse literary traditions of Asia through an examination of selected works. Regional focus on East, South, and SoutheastAsia varies.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Major Works of Middle Eastern Literatures
courses.description: An introduction to the diverse literary traditions of the Middle East through an examination of selected works. Regional focus on North Africa, the Middle East, and Central Asia varies.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Major Works of African Literatures
courses.comments: Comparative Literature 33 and Black Studies 33 are the same course.
courses.description: An introduction to the diverse literary traditions of Africa through an examination of selected works. Regional focus on North, West, East, Central, and South Africa varies.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Literature of the Americas
courses.comments: French 34 and Comparative Literature 34 are the same course.
courses.description: An introduction to the diverse literary traditions of the Americas through an examination of selected works. Regional focus on North America, the Caribbean, and Latin America varies.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: The Making of the Modern World
courses.comments: Comparative Literature 35 and German 35 are the same course.
courses.description: Description and analysis of decisive events contributing to the world we are inhabiting. Various themes presented: City planning, war and industrial warfare, technology and media-technology, ideologies of modernity, and modern master theories.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Global Humanities
courses.comments: English 36 and Comparative Literature 36 are the same course.
courses.description: What do literature and critical theory contribute to the reflection on human rights and the analysis of their violation? Inquiry into different ways in which the humanities can re-frame the debate on human rights and act as a social force.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Comparative Media
courses.comments: Comparative Literature 37 and German 37 are the same course.
courses.description: Introduces media in the context of Comparative Literature. Students learn to analyze media forms as cultural texts while emphasizing the social, political, and environmental dimensions of media technologies. Topics vary and may include Media Theories, Algorithmic Media, Digital Humanities, Postcolonial and Environmental Media, or Film & Literature. Taught in English.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Young Humans: Introduction to Childhood Studies
courses.comments: EACS 41 and C LIT 40 are the same course.
courses.description: An introduction to interdisciplinary approaches to understanding and analyzing childhood and youth, including history of childhood, and childrens literature research, this course considers the role of childhood in human life, its construction across different periods and regions, different disciplinary perspectives on childhood, and contemporary approaches to deepening the understanding of children and their own views. By examining key critical texts, it considers childhood through multiple disciplinary perspectives, as well as childrens own co-creation of the performance of childhood and childrens voice, agency, activism, and rights.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Dreaming Revolutions: Introduction to Marx, Nietzsche, and Freud
courses.comments: Comparative Literature 43A and German 43A are the same course. Not open for credit to students who have completed German 41.
courses.description: Introduction to the revolutionary theories of Karl Marx, Friedrich Nietzsche, and Sigmund Freud. Explorations of three authors whose writing has profoundly changed our world.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Love in the Western World, from Plato to Dating Apps
courses.description: From ancient Eros to the divine union of mystics, from medieval chivalry to romantic passion and the scientific study of sexuality, Western societies have been reinventing the meaning and experience of love. These reinventions offer an insight into the arrangements, needs, and purposes of these societies. The course proposes to investigate how, why, and to what end a social order defines and understands love at a particular historical junction. Readings include Plato and Neoplatonism, the Christian Gospel, medieval mysticism, romances of chivalry, Renaissance theatre and poetry, the romantic novel, and contemporary culture.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Tales of Love in the Western Tradition
courses.comments: French 50AX and Comparative Literature 50A are the same course.
courses.description: A comparative and interdisciplinary approach to the literatures and philosophies of love, desire, and sexuality in the western world, in antiquity, the Middle Ages, and the Renaissance. In English.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Tales of Love in the Western Tradition
courses.comments: French 50BX and Comparative Literature 50B are the same course.
courses.description: A comparative and interdisciplinary approach to the literatures and philosophies of love, desire, and sexuality in the western world in the 17th and 18th centuries. In English.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Tales of Love in the Western Tradition
courses.comments: French 50CX and Comparative Literature 50C are the same course.
courses.description: A comparative and interdisciplinary approach to the literatures and philosophies of love, desire, and sexuality in the western world in the 19th and 20th centuries. In English.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Culture and Revolution in the Americas
courses.description: What is a revolution? What do art and literature tell us about revolutionary movements and the hopes, promises, and memories associated with them? This course will examine these questions focusing on some of the major revolutionary episodes in the history of the Americas: the Haitian Revolution (1791-1804), the Wars of Independence in Spanish America (1810-1824), the Mexican Revolution (1910-1920), and the Cuban Revolution (1959). Through the analysis of artistic and literary pieces across various genres and media, we will delve into topics such as identity, liberty, governance, legitimacy, violence, trauma, and the construction of history. Taught in English. There may be a discussion section in Spanish depending on the enrollment.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Introduction to Disability Studies
courses.description: Focus on the common representations of the disabled bodies and minds in historical perspectives, theories of disability and culture, and disability in literature, art, the media, and medicine. Content will vary according to instructors.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Modern Chinese Literature
courses.comments: Chinese 82 and Comparative Literature 82 are the same course.
courses.description: This course, taught in English, surveys an archive of seminal short fiction, novellas, novels, and poems that tell the story of China and the Chinese from the end of the Qing dynasty to the present. What has been the place of literature in China in the modern era? What vision of modern China do we find in its literature? How, moreover, does literature subvert the national narrative? Through literature as a window on the history of modern China, students gain a better understanding of Chinese history and culture with regard to its social reform, revolution, war, cultural revolution, cultural revival, and economic growth.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.prereq_text: 8 units from any Comparative Literature courses numbered 30 to 36; minimum 3.0 cumulative GPA; consent of instructor and department.
courses.comments: Students must have a 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters and are limited to 30 units total in all 99/199 courses combined.
courses.description: Independent research under the guidance of a faculty member in the program. Course offers motivated students the opportunity to undertake independent research or work in a research group.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Introduction to Comparative Literature
courses.description: Focus on various practices and methodologies of Comparative Literature as a cross-disciplinary and transnational endeavor, including recent developments and debates on translation studies and world literature in an era of cultural globalization. Content will vary with instructor.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Introduction to Literary and Critical Theory
courses.description: How does critical theory help us to read and write literature? Potential foci include structuralism, semiotics, social theory, psychoanalysis, deconstruction, cultural criticism, gender studies and feminism, queer studies, postcolonial criticism, ecocriticism. Content will vary with instructor.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Introduction to Translation I
courses.comments: Same course as Spanish 115.
courses.description: Comprises topics necessary to develop skills that are needed for writing at a specialized level and to carry out written translation into and from Spanish, mostly texts on business and medical topics.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Introduction to Interpreting
courses.prereq_text: Spanish 25 OR Spanish 16B (may be taken concurrently).
courses.comments: Same course as Spanish 116.
courses.description: Comprised of topics necessary in developing skills for interpretation to and from Spanish. Intended mostly for proficient Spanish-language speakers.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Specialized Translation - Technical
courses.comments: Comparative Literature 102C and Spanish 117C are the same course
courses.description: Comprised of topics necessary in developing skills for writing at a specialized level, and with specialized vocabulary and format, for the translation of different types of technical texts (instruction manuals, medical, patents, etc.).

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Lusophone Cityscapes: Cultures, Histories, and Urban Imaginaries
courses.comments: Comparative Literature 106 and Portuguese 107 are the same course.
courses.description: This course examines the urban landscapes of cities in the Portuguese-speaking world across Europe, Africa, Asia, and the Americas, exploring their histories, cultural productions, and evolving identities. From Lisbon to Luanda, Rio de Janeiro to Maputo, and Goa to Dili, we delve into the architecture, literature, music, and cinema that shape these urban centers. Themes include colonial and postcolonial transformations, social inequality, migration, and the intersection of urban life with environmental challenges. Students will analyze how cityscapes serve as spaces of memory, resistance, and creativity, revealing the complexities of urban life across this interconnected planetary network. Taught in English

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Survey of Brazilian Literature from its Beginnings to the Present
courses.description: A survey of the main works of literature produced in Brazil and about Brazil from its beginnings up to the present. Involves travel literature about Brazil, written in the sixteenth century, at the time of its discovery, as well as the literature produced in Brazil up to the present, represented by significant authors and periods. Designed to give the student a historical, cultural and literary context, a chronological panel, in order to prepare the student for more specific and focused courses within the area of Portuguese. Also prepares the student for the understanding of cultural contexts in order to apply the knowledge acquired in this survey to other fields of interest. Taught in English.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Voyages to the Unknown
courses.comments: Same course as French 154A.
courses.description: The impact of the voyages of discovery on late 15th and 16th century Europe. Readings on real and imaginary voyages: Columbus, Cartier, Lery, More, Rabelais, Montaigne.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Crossreadings : French and Italian Cultures in Dialogue and Translation
courses.comments: French 158, Italian 158X, and Comparative Literature 108 are the same course.
courses.description: Ever since the Renaissance, when the notion of a national culture had taken hold, the historic, literary and intellectual trajectories of France and Italy have been intimately entangled. Taking a chronological approach from the Renaissance to the post-modern period, this course will embark on a number of comparative readings from these two countries: from Rabelais carnivalesque uptake of Boccaccios humor and vulgarity; to Italys attempt at emulating the French Revolution; to Giuseppe Ungarettis debt to avant-garde literary figures, and more. Our goal will be to reveal that cultures and intellectual traditions exist not in isolation but emerge out of a perpetual conversation withand translation ofeach other. Taught in English.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Trauma, Memory, Historiography
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit up to a maximum of 8 units with consent of department chair.
courses.description: How do individuals, communities, cultures, nations remember and/or forget, preserve and/or erase, traumatic events?

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Dante's Divine Comedy
courses.prereq_text: Upper division standing or instructor approval required
courses.comments: Same course as Italian 114X
courses.description: Dante's masterpiece, The Divine Comedy, remains among the most astonishing works of world literature. This course follows the pilgrim's progress through Inferno, Purgatorio and Paradiso in search of love that moves the sun and the other stars.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Representations of the Holocaust
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed German 116A.
courses.description: Close reading of post-Holocaust literature. Taught in English.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Holocaust in Italy
courses.description: Through readings of memoir, fiction, and film, this course investigates the fate of Jews under the Italian Fascists of Benito Mussolini (1922-1945). Topics include Fascism, Communism, anti-Semitism, Italian cooperation with the Nazis, the Catholic Church, the Resistance Movement, deportations and extermination camps, and individual / collective memory after World War II. Students will be exposed to great literary and cinematographic works and through them develop a thorough understanding of this pivotal period in modern Italian history.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Comparative Black Literatures
courses.comments: Black Studies 126 and Comparative Literature 126 are the same course.
courses.description: Using a social constructionist approach to race, this course examines the multiple ways in which racial discourses operate in global literary cultures. It emphasizes that blackness need not be a homogeneous concept in order to continue to be a powerful agent in the postmodern world.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Children's Literature
courses.description: Classic texts and theories of children's literature, from Perrault and Wilde to Freud and Propp. Examination of narrative and ideological strategies for constructing and representing childhood in modernity, with emphasis on their relationship to the family and the marketplace.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Understanding Brazilian Music in its Cultural Context
courses.comments: MUS 178BR, C LIT 131B, and PORT 110 are the same course.
courses.description: This course enables students to understand what Brazilian music is, and what is the role of Music in Brazilian culture. It offers a comprehensive panel of the history of music in Brazil. The course also provides students with a full cultural context, discussing the role of music during the two dictatorship periods in Brazil, 1930-1945 and 1964-1985 and the political impact of censorship. It also discusses the contributions of the Africans, brought to Brazil by the Portuguese colonizers, and the impact African culture has both in music and religion. Taught in English.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Beyond the Cold War: European Culture and Daily Life Onscreen, 1945-1991
courses.prereq_text: Sophomore standing or higher, or consent of instructor.
courses.description: This course will examine the major social, political, and economic trends in postwar and Cold War Europe, 1945-1991, through their effects on daily life across the region, as represented in films produced during the period. It will survey the changes in filmmaking practices during this time, focusing on movements and directors that aimed to capture and critique modernitys effects on ordinary people.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Transpacific Literature
courses.comments: ENGL 133TL, C LIT 133, and EACS 133 are the same course.
courses.description: Looks at the Pacific as the primary location for literary and historical imagination since the Age of Exploration. Studies the crisscross, transpacific field of inscriptions ranging from Captain Cook to Herman Melville, Mark Twain, Jack London, and Maxine Hong Kingston.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Poetics of the Second Language
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing or instructor approval required
courses.description: What is the effect of writing in a language other than ones own? Why choose to do so in the first place? In this course, we explore the works of various novelists and poets who, for one reason or another, choose to write in a foreign language, turning their back on their so-called mother tongue. We consider this gesture from many angles, first and foremost that of translation, and, more specifically, self-translation.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: China in Translation: Theory, Art, History
courses.comments: CHIN 139 and C LIT 139 are the same course.
courses.description: Uses case studies of translations into and out of China--long regarded as a civilization distinct from the West--to explore themes in translation studies. Topics include ideograms, orientalism, modernization, world literature, annotation, musicality, poetic license, and adaptation.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Italy as Destination: Italian Travel Literature
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 16 units provided letter designation is different.
courses.description: Taught in English, this course is a study of Italian travel literature within Italy and abroad, from Marco Polo to the present day.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Literary Adaptation in East Asia
courses.description: Explores literary adaptation and intertextuality in East Asia through primary texts and readings from critical theory. Among the texts considered are traditional poetry, The Tale of Genji, Chinese "strange tales," and representations of history and literature in film. Taught in English, with readings in English translation; no knowledge of Chinese or Japanese necessary.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Creative Chaos
courses.description: Chaos: is it primordial mayhem and confusion? Or does chaos permit the possibility of form and creativity? Course explores the order and disorder of chaos within literary, scientific, and philosophical narratives. From Hesiod and Ovid through Diderot, Wordsworth, and Pynchon.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Digital Humanities Practice
courses.comments: Same course as German 152.
courses.description: In the 21st century, scholars have increasingly turned to computational methods for the analysis of large corpora of art and literature. While early methods of distant reading and distant viewing could be realized with off-the-shelf software, contemporary research in the digital humanities requires technical skills beyond ready-made tools. This course provides an introduction to computer programming for the humanities, including, but not limited to concepts from natural language processing, computer vision, and machine learning.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: French Theatre in Translation
courses.description: A study of French theatre through the centuries, considered within the cultural context of the day (Classicism, the Enlightenment, Romanticism, the Absurd, etc). Plays by Molire, Marivaux, Beaumarchais, Hugo, Musset, Ionesco, and Beckett. Lectures and readings in English.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Science Fiction in Eastern Europe
courses.comments: Same course as Slavic 154.
courses.description: The genre of science fiction and its development in literature and film in the various cultures of eastern europe. Topics include utopia, dystopia,technology, the mad scientist, etc. Taught in English.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Economic Fictions: Literature, Film, and Theory
courses.comments: French 154I and Comparative Literature 154I are the same course.
courses.description: How have Western thinkers represented economic concepts since the eighteenth century? Themes may include free market liberalism, labor theories of value, household and family economics, currency/monetary policy, associationism/socialism, globalism/expansionism/colonialism, protectionism, and others. In English.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Critical Artificial Intelligence
courses.comments: German 155, Comparative Literature 155, and ENGL 155AI are the same course.
courses.description: Artificial intelligence now affects nearly all aspects of human life and knowledge production, from labor to language, and from fundamental physics to the arts. The pivotal role of the humanities lies in the critical analysis of the specific cultural techniques emerging from this technical revolution: new methods of language processing, image production, scientific reasoning, and social control require new critical and historical approaches. This course provides an introduction to the history and theory of artificial intelligence from the perspective of the humanities. Participants will acquire the skills to analyze and understand the design and construction of machine learning systems, and their philosophical and political implications.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Caribbean Women Writers and Migratory Subjects
courses.comments: Comparative Literature 156 and Global Studies 148 are the same course.
courses.description: This course examines the implications of migration and the formation of transnational identity. We will read novels by Anglophone and Francophone Caribbean Women writers who speak to the interlinked relationship between migration, racism, sexism and economic deprivation.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Literature of Central Europe
courses.comments: Same course as German 151C and Slavic 151C.
courses.description: Investigation of the prolific literatures of central Europe, one of the culturally and linguistically most diverse regions of the European continent that has produced writers such as Italo Svevo, Franz Kafka, Robert Musil, Bruno Schultz, and others. Readings in English.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Sexuality and Globalization
courses.description: Examines globalizing cultural politics of sexuality through literature, popular media, subaltern performances, and press discourse from Global South; engages questions of "universalized" LGBTQ identities, Islamic law and sexual rights, militarized masculinities, recognition oftransexualities, and queer, anti-racist and feminist globalisms.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Desire, Sex, and Romance in Traditions of India
courses.prereq_text: Upper Division standing and one course from the following: RGST 19, 20, 140D, 158C, 159 G-H-J-K-L-M-N-O, 160A, 161D, 169 or equivalent; or instructor approval.
courses.comments: Cross listed with Religious Studies 162I.
courses.description: Explores questions of love and sex across two thousand years of Indian religious thought. The reading list includes some of the most famous voices in South Asian literary history. We will tour various genres: moral teachings, epic narrative, drama, devotional and mystical poetry, and modern fiction. Yes, we will read the Kama Sutra, and yes, there will be Bollywood films.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Digital Visual Studies
courses.comments: Same course as German 163 and History of Art and Architecture 163.
courses.description: In the past ten years, the scope of the digital humanities has broadened to include the visual world: distant reading became distant viewing. This visual turn has not only facilitated the digital transformation of traditional disciplines like art history but has also introduced a new set of media-technological questions into the digital humanities discourse: questions concerning the nature of digital images, and the modalities of machine seeing. This course serves as an introduction to the emerging discipline of digital visual studies that investigates these questions. Participants will acquire skills in the analysis and critique of digital visual culture and learn to use contemporary digital tools to explore the visual world.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: East Asian Buddhist Poetry
courses.description: Introduces Buddhist poetry of China, Japan, and Korea. Emphasizes the diversity of literary encounters with the teachings and practices of Buddhism. Topics include Hanshan, Basho, Zen koans, Gary Snyder, and monastery cats.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Translation as Metaphor: Introduction to Translation Theory and Practice
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; and completion of quarter 5 or equivalent of the language of study.
courses.description: The course aims to develop skills in terminology and technologies of translation; it also examines the practical and theoretical issues pertaining to translation as an artistic, cultural, and ethical process. Focus on literary translation as creative research and practice.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Post-Colonial Cultures
courses.comments: Same course as French 154G.
courses.description: Study of fiction from the Caribbean, West Africa, and the Maghreb. Born of the conflict between and hybridization of widely differing cultural traditions, this course provides insights into the vibrancy of contemporary post-colonial societies, the ongoing legacy of colonialism, and the meaning of multiculturalism. In English.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: From Confession to Autofiction (Inventions of the Self I)
courses.prereq_text: Writing 2 or 50 or 109 or English 10 or upper-division standing.
courses.description: This course follows a genealogy of confessional and autobiographical writing in the West, from Rousseau's tussles with the concept of authenticity to the playful auto-fictional experiments by authors such as Coetzee and Heti. It traces how the western self's confidence in its capacity to articulate its own truth, or to ‘confess,’ was progressively undermined — first by the emergence of the psychoanalytic theory of the unconscious mind, and more recently by the science of affect and memory — and characterizes the rise of auto-fiction as a creative response to the demise of secular confession, one that incorporates and thematizes the precariousness of our beliefs about authenticity, creativity, truth, and the very idea of the self.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Literatures of Eurasia: Armenian Literature
courses.description: Examines literature and culture from a region or regions situated at the crossroads between Europe and Asia, such as Central Asia (Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan), the Caucasus (Armenia, Azerbaijan, Georgia, and parts of Southern Russia), or other cultural crossroads in Eurasia. It thus departs from a historic focus on western regions to accommodate the richness and diversity of literature and culture in Eurasia. Topics will vary by instructor. Topics may include: Armenian Literature, Literatures of Central Asia, or Literatures of the Caucasus. Taught in English.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Mysticism
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed German 169. Same course as German 179B and Religious Studies 179B.
courses.description: Analysis of German mystical writing, its roots in ancient Greek texts, revolutionary impact, links with other mystical traditions, and influence on secular literature. Texts include Hildegard von Bingen, Meister Eckhart, Mechthild von Magdeburg, Novalis, Rilke, etc. Taught in English.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Mediatechnology
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed German 180. Same course as German 179C and ART 179C.
courses.description: Telegraph, telephone, phonograph, and film are techniques that have engendered new forms of representation, communication, and thinking. Course studies the impact of these transformations in literature and on literature. Taught in English.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Special Topics in Russian, East European, and Eurasian Studies
courses.description: In-depth examination of specialized topics with contemporary relevance or historical significance within the study of Russian, East European, or Eurasian literature, culture, and thought. Topics will vary by instructor. Topics may include: Holy Fools, Childhood in Russian Culture, Russian and East European Literary Theory, and Russian Literature and Translation. Taught in English

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Ukrainian Cinema and Culture
courses.comments: Comparative Literature 181B, Slavic Studies 181B, and Film Studies 122UK are the same course.
courses.description: This seminar explores the history of Ukrainian cinema and culture from the early 20th century to the ongoing Russo-Ukrainian War, examining how it relates to the broader political, social, regional, and cultural contexts. Taught in English.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Southeastern European Literature
courses.description: A special topics course covering a selection from the southeast European canon. Selections determined by instructor

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Critical Childhood Studies
courses.comments: C LIT 182 and EACS 182 are the same course
courses.description: This seminar/capstone course on critical childhood studies will examine the burgeoning field of childhood studies across time periods and regions, employing varied disciplinary approaches to the study of childhood, including literary studies, history, art history, sociology, and other disciplines. Assignments will include weekly responses, leading a discussion of a scholarly work, a final paper on a subject related to student interest, and a presentation of the final paper topic.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Identity, Feminism, and Secularism in Hebrew Literature
courses.comments: Comparative Literature 184C and Religious Studies 133E are the same course.
courses.description: Provides a broad overview of Modern Hebrew literature, spanning from its origins in the eighteenth century to the contemporary era. Aims to shed light on the factors that make this literature distinctive and fascinating. The course delves into various themes, such as Jewish identity, feminism, secularism, and Zionism, while examining the interplay and conflicts between different generations of literary works. The readings for the course comprise a selection of short stories in translation, but will be available in Hebrew for interested students. All lectures and discussions will be held in English.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Major Works in German Literature: Kafka
courses.description: A selection of Franz Kafka's novels, short stories and diaries will be closely read and analyzed. Readings, lecture and discussion in English.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Science and Technology in European Philosophy
courses.description: Introduces various positions from the history and present of European philosophy that speak to questions of science and technology. Readings may include Aristotle, Descartes, Kant, Nietzsche, Freud, Heidegger, Arendt, Bachelard, Koyr, Caillois, Foucault, Canguilhem, Blumenberg, Serres, Malabou, Stiegler. Topics may include: machine theories, cybernetics, structuralism in science, techniques of simulation, artificial intelligence.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Interdisciplinary Comparative Literature Studies
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Interdisciplinary examination of selected topics, theories, disciplinary issues, and/or methodological questions in the combined study of literature, and other areas of the humanities and humanistic sciences. Course focus will be determined by the instructor(s).

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Gender in Basque Culture
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Using Basque culture as a case study, this course explores how gender intersects with other crucial issues such as ethnicity, nationhood, and globalization.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Bulgakov
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Intensive study of Bulgakov. Readings supplemented by selected criticism. Taught in English.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: The Basques Through Film
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: The Basques through Film. Provides a critical examination of the history and poetics of Basque film from the last three decades.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Conflict and Memory in Cultural Production
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Conflict, Memory and Cultural Production. Explores how Basque writers and artists engage and create memory narratives in times of war and violence.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Basque Studies Through Literature and Culture in Translation (Spanish/English)
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: The course delves deeper into the diversity of topics that make up Basque Studies, analyzing historical, but also contemporary socio-cultural topics related to the Basque Country and the Basque diaspora abroad. The course can be taken either as a continuation of SPAN 153E or a self-standing course on Basque Studies, where literary and cultural materials will be presented in their English, Spanish, and possibly also French translations depending on student interest and language choice.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Exile, Displacement, and Estrangement in Literature and Film
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: A focus on contemporary representations of exile and displacement, and exiled authors and thinkers from Latin America and Europe. Primary sources include texts about European exiles in the Americas, Latin American exiles in Europe, and the turn from exile to migrant literature in the Americas. We also look to how contemporary authors adapt early exile motifs and respond to literary forerunners by including issues of gender, labor, racism, sexuality, and more.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Vegetarianism: Food, Literature, Philosophy
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: The philosophical, religious and literary history of vegetarianism and animal ethics from the Antiquity to the present. Topics include the debate on animal consumption in the Buddhist canon and recent representations of vegetarianism in western literature.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Dostoevsky
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Intensive study of Dostoevsky. Readings supplemented by select criticism. Readings and lectures in English.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Literatures in the Juvenile Justice System - Theory into Practice
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Students in the course will be reading a range of materials from multiple genres, among them fiction and non-fiction, critical race theory, poetry & plays (among other offerings), while forming mentoring relationships with youth at Los Prietos Boys Camp & writing about both their academic inquiries & experiences with community practice.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Literatures of the Sea
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: The premodern Mediterranean was a site of civilizational confluence, conflict, and transformation, which historians have characterized as both fragmentation and connectivity. This course addresses tales of love, sex, and slavery in medieval and early modern Mediterranean literatures. Love and slaverytwo forms of captivityallow us to study religious and cultural interactions, voluntary and involuntary movement across the sea, and the production and articulation of difference. Adopting a Mediterranean Studies lens, this course aims to define what it means to think Mediterranean by reading and analyzing texts from a diverse body of languages and literatures, including Arabic, Aljamiado, French, Italian, Latin, Persian, and Spanish.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Poetry & Community Practice
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Poetry & Community Practice honors a connection between poetry and citizenship, assuming that poetry is a wisdom medium or vehicle toward more enlightened thinking and public practice. Poetry is an ideal medium for extending our study and practice beyond UCSB, and students will conduct workshops in schools, community centers, and assisted living facilities as part of their work for the course. Students will extend their own learning through teachinga natural stretchwhile also being of benefit elsewhere.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Many Ramayanas: Ancient and Modern
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: India’s Ramayana is a rip-roaring adventure story, with kings, queens, heroes, villains, lovers, monsters, magic, and miracles. Over thousands of years across South Asia, it has also been the master narrative defining issues of critical ideological importance: power, gender, race, caste, divinity, dharma. In this course we will study the canonical Sanskrit text in translation and sample some of the epic’s tellings in vernacular media, including comic books, live performance, and television. The emphasis, however, will be on cinema, with a lineup of films featuring several spectacular recent Bollywood productions. How does this story, popular for more than two thousand years, speak to the politics of the present?

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Reading, Writing, and Reimagining the Literatures of Social Change
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: This course uses literature as a basis for reigniting our passion for and faith insocial change. It assumes that our service and action programs, together with awhole host of academic inquiry and research practices, are failing that oureducational and social change missions, for example, can no longer adequatelyaddress the massive social and ecological problems and political initiatives wenow face. Rigorous readings by thinkers as diverse as Angela Davis, Paulo Freire,bell hooks, Gabriel Garcia Marquez, Joanna Macy, Abraham Rodriguez, DerrickJensen, Martn Prechtel, together with equally rigorous field-work in localschools will offer up new models for addressing social, ecological and educationalchallenges.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Wild Literature in the Urban Landscape
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Combines study of ecological writing with service to schools and community centers in Santa Barbara. Through exploration of both local and global ecological challenges, students will conduct weekly workshops combining literature and ecology in order to better understand local issues like drought, erosion and land-use, with an emphasis on eco-industrial histories. The curriculum will serve as an existing approach to environmental education through the lens of literary arts, providing an initial foundation for lesson development elsewhere.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: The Devil in Literature
courses.description: Explores the rich literature around making deals with the devil while focusing on the enduring influence of older literature on modern conceptions of the diabolic.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Autobiographies and Life Stories
courses.description: Considers autobiographies, memoirs, testimonials, life writing, and other works of narrative fiction and nonfiction often written in the first person. Topics include self-portrait, the portrayal of childhood and family, childhood and youth narratives, women's autobiography, first-person accounts of illness and disability in comics, and more. Texts and course foci vary with the instructor.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Disability and Culture
courses.description: With a view of integrating disability as a critical category into teaching and research, courses approach physical, sensory, and psychological impairments as well as bodily and mental differences in literary, visual, artistic, and popular forms across classical and modern periods. The main fields of study include world literature, art, film studies, philosophy, linguistics, history, and religious studies in conjunction with adjacent fields that help reconfigure the concept of ability and normalcy. Content will vary according to instructors.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Disability and Literature
courses.description: Readings of canonical and non-canonical texts (fiction, memoir, poetry) through a variety of critical approaches, covering a wide range of impairments and the innovations that disability requires in literary and artistic forms. Content will vary according to instructors.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Fantasy and the Fantastic
courses.comments: Same course as French 153D.
courses.description: Course explores the creation of a space where a fantastic perception of reality developed and thrived, hesitating between the real and the supernatural, in the intermediate space of the unexplained and unexplainable. Works by Balzac, Poe, Stevenson, James, and Borges.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Literature & Politics in China
courses.prereq_text: UPPER-DIVISION STANDING. MAY BE REPEATED FOR CREDIT TO A MAXIMUM OF 12 UNITS
courses.description: Surveys politically-themed Chinese literature (in English). Studying texts from classical China, modern China, and contemporary China and Taiwan, the course encourages consideration of two questions: What makes literature on politics unique and different from, say, historical and philosophical treatises on politics? What role could literature play in politics?

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Research in Translation Studies
courses.comments: This course will not be applied to the Comparative Literature major or minor requirements.
courses.description: Individualized instruction to complete the capstone translation project for the Minor in Translation Studies. To be completed with the faculty advisor from the language department of the student's focus.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Capstone Project in Childhood and Youth Studies
courses.prereq_text: Comparative Literature 128A and Comparative Literature 40 or W 40.
courses.comments: This course will not be applied to the Comparative Literature major or minor requirements.
courses.description: Individualized or small-group instruction to complete the capstone childhood or youth studies project for the Minor in Childhood and Youth Studies. The capstone project may be academic research, community-based work, or a creative project, with advance approval from the advisor. To be completed with a faculty advisor from a relevant department.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Internship
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; Comparative Literature majors only; consent of department.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit for a maximum of 8 units, but only 4 units may be applied to the major.
courses.description: Under supervision of Comparative Literature faculty, Comparative Literature majors may obtain credit for work without pay in publishing, editing, journalism, or other employment related to Comparative Literature, World Literature, and/or Translation Studies. Requirements include work hours, regular meetings with professor-mentor, and a final paper presenting and analyzing the student's learning from the internship pertaining to specialization in world literary studies.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Senior Honors Independent Research
courses.description: Student engages in research leading to a paper of considerable depth and complexity on a topic dealing with the literature of the student's focus.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Junior/Senior Seminar
courses.comments: Formerly numbered Comparative Literature 198.
courses.description: Selected methodological issues in comparative literature. Topics vary with each instructor.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Senior Honors Seminar
courses.description: This seminar is concurrently offered with graduate seminars. It is designed to expand research skills through an investigation of theoretical issues and readings of both literary and critical texts. It involves extensive research, sophisticated analysis, and creative reflection.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Independent Studies in Comparative Literature
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division courses in Comparative Literature.
courses.comments: Students must have a cumulative 3.0 for the proceeding 3 quarter(s). Limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
courses.description: Independent studies with any faculty member. To permit study of a subject desired by the student but not covered in course offerings.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Independent Research Assistance
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of two upper-division courses in Comparative Literature; and, consent of instructor.
courses.comments: Students are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
courses.description: Independent research under supervision of a faculty member. May be linked to internship.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Seminar in Comparative Literature
courses.description: Addresses issues of methodology and literary theory. Specific authors and topics vary from class to class.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Proseminar in Comparative Literature
courses.description: Addresses topics relevant to comparative literary study,including scholarly approaches and practices, the discipline of comparative literature broadly conceived, and the specific resources and intellectual culture of UCSB. Course format will range from seminar style discussions, workshops, and formal presentations.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Media History Theory
courses.description: Interweaves a study of the emergence of several kinds of twentieth century media including radio, film, television, and the internet, with keytexts of media theory including Benjamin, Adorno, MdLuhan, Debord, Hall, and others.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Literary Translation: Theory and Practice
courses.description: Examination of translation and the canon, questioning the hierarchical division between translation and original, illustrating the concept of the original as translation and the literary text as "work-in-progress" in which translation forms part of the creative process.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Contemporary Theory in Translation
courses.description: Survey of contemporary theory: structuralism and poststructuralism; psychoanalysis and trauma studies; gender and queer studies; ethnic, indigenous, post-colonial, and transnational studies; cognition, emotion, affect; the biological and the ecological turns. In English.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Media Techniques of Wonder
courses.comments: Comparative Literature 280 and Film Studies 280 are the same course.
courses.description: Media Techniques of Wonder is focused on themes of media archaeology and their emergent literary context. The exchange between literature and media techniques serves as the focus, with literary texts creating a basis for real and imagined media technologies that radically reshape literary practices. Historical devices will serve as a basis along with visits to media collections.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Teaching Assistant Practicum
courses.comments: Units earned do not apply toward completion of advanced degrees.
courses.description: Supervised teaching of lower-division comparative literature courses at UCSB. Participation in occasional workshops related to the field of teaching will be required.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Directed Reading and Research
courses.prereq_text: Minimum of two units per quarter. Letter grade only.
courses.comments: No more than half of units required for M.A. may be taken in 596 series.
courses.description: Individual tutorial. A written proposal for each tutorial must be approved by the program chair.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Translation Studies Independent Studies
courses.prereq_text: Comparative Literature 260 or approval of the emphasis adviser.
courses.description: Individual reading and research. A written proposal for each tutorial must be approved by the faculty emphasis adviser.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Individual study for M.A. Comprehensive and Ph.D. Exams
courses.comments: No unit credit allowed toward advanced degree. Enrollment limited to 24 uniunits per examination (12 units maximum in any one examination quarter). S/U grading only.
courses.description: For individual study with major professor or chair or director of student'sprogram.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Master's Thesis Research and Preparation
courses.comments: No unit credit allowed toward advanced degree. S/U grading only.
courses.description: For research and writing of the master's thesis.

courses.subject: C LIT
courses.title: Ph.D. Dissertation Research and Preparation
courses.comments: S/U grading only. Twelve units maximum.
courses.description: For research and writing of the doctoral dissertation. Instructor should be chair of the student's doctoral committee.

courses.subject: C LITW
courses.title: Young Humans: Introduction to Childhood Studies
courses.comments: EACS 41 and C LIT 40 are the same course.
courses.description: An introduction to interdisciplinary approaches to understanding and analyzing childhood and youth, including history of childhood, and childrens literature research, this course considers the role of childhood in human life, its construction across different periods and regions, different disciplinary perspectives on childhood, and contemporary approaches to deepening the understanding of children and their own views. By examining key critical texts, it considers childhood through multiple disciplinary perspectives, as well as childrens own co-creation of the performance of childhood and childrens voice, agency, activism, and rights.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Introduction to Chemical Engineering Design
courses.prereq_text: Registration is restricted to Chemical Engineering majors only for passes 1 & 2.
courses.comments: ChE W 5 is the online version of ChE 5.
courses.description: Introduction to the design and analysis of processes involving chemical change in the context of chemical and biomolecular engineering. Students learn mathematical, empirical, and conceptual strategies to analyze chemical processes to assess product quality, economics, safety, and environmental issues. Focus topics include an overview of chemical and biomolecular engineering, evaluating and analyzing data, flowsheets, material and energy balances, economics, and unit operations.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Material and Energy Balances
courses.prereq_text: Chemical Engineering 5 (may be taken concurrently); Chemistry 1A-B or 3A-B; Mathematics 2A or 3A, Mathematics 2B or 3B and Mathematics 4A or 4AI
courses.comments: Space may be limited and registration priority will be given to Chemical Engineering and COE majors.
courses.description: Elementary principles and problem solving skills required for quantitative analysis of chemical processes. Topics to be covered include macroscopic material and energy balances, reaction stoichiometry, elementary thermodynamics, and phase equilibria associated with chemical engineering processes and unit operations.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Introduction to Research
courses.prereq_text: Consent of instructor and undergraduate advisor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 6 units. Students are limited to5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199DC/199RA courses combined.
courses.description: Directed study, normally experimental, to be arranged with individual faculty members. Course offers exceptional students an opportunity to participate in a research group.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Introduction to Biological Processing
courses.description: Familiarizes engineering students with biological processing and production at multiple scales. Chemical engineering principles will be infused with key biological concepts, including an introduction to biochemistry, cell biology, and molecular biology.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Chemical Engineering Thermodynamics
courses.prereq_text: Chemical Engineering 5; Chemical Engineering 10; Mathematics 4B or 4BI; Chemistry 1C or 3C.
courses.comments: Space may be limited and registration priority will be given to Chemical Engineering and CoE majors.
courses.description: Use of the laws of thermodynamics to analyze processes encountered in engineering practice, including cycles and flows. Equations-of-state for describing properties of fluids and mixtures. Applications, including engines, turbines, refrigeration and power plant cycles, phase equilibria, and chemical-reaction equilibria.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Chemical Engineering Thermodynamics
courses.prereq_text: Chemical Engineering 110A with a minimum grade of C-; Mathematics 4B or 4BI.
courses.description: Extension of Chemical Engineering 110A to cover mixtures and multiphase equilibrium. Liquid-vapor separations calculations are emphasized. Introduction to equations of state for mixtures.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Technical Communication of Chemical Engineering
courses.description: Provides an introduction to technical communication in the form of writing reports and oral presentations. Emphasis placed on how to analyze and present data; critical thinking; organization, logic and constructing a technical narrative; literature searching and citations for written reports; and how to give oral presentations. Includes various lectures on technical communication, individual and group assignments, and peer-review exercises.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Transport Processes
courses.prereq_text: Chemical Engineering 10 with a minimum grade of C- (may be taken concurrently); Mathematics 4B or 4BI; Mathematics 6A or 6AI and Mathematics 6B.
courses.description: Introductory course in conceptual understanding and mathematical analysis of problems in fluid dynamics of relevance to Chemical Engineering. Emphasis is placed on performing microscopic and macroscopic mathematical analysis to understand fluid motion in response to forces.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Transport Processes
courses.prereq_text: Chemical Engineering 10 with minimum grade of C-; Chemical Engineering 110A with minimum grade of C- (may be taken concurrently); Chemical Engineering 120A.
courses.description: Introductory course in the mathematical analysis of conductive, convective and radiative heat transfer with practical applications to design of heat exchange equipment and use.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Transport Processes
courses.prereq_text: Chemical Engineering 10 with a minimum grade of C-; Chemical Engineering 110A with minimum grade of C-; Chemical Engineering 110B (may be taken concurrently) and Chemical Engineering 120B.
courses.description: Introductory course in the fundamentals of mass transfer with applications to the design of mass transfer equipment.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Colloids and Biosurfaces
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Chemical Enginerring 102.
courses.description: Basic forces and interactions between atoms, molecules, small particles and extended surfaces. Special features and interactions associated with (soft) biological molecules, biomaterials and surfaces: lipids, proteins, fibrous molecules (DNA), biological membranes, hydrophobic and hydrophilic interactions, bio-specific and non-equilibrium interactions.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Non-Newtonian Fluids, Soft Materials and Chemical Products
courses.description: Overview of soft materials (suspensions, gels, polymers, surfactants, emulsions, powders and granules) that arise in diverse industries, including consumer products, foods, advanced materials, biotechnology, and mineral and energy production. Influence of non-Newtonian rheology (shear-thickening and thinning, viscoelasticity, extension-thickening, yield stresses, normal stress differences, and metastability) upon handling, processing, production, and performance of chemical products. Strategies to design chemical products that meet performance targets, and to scale-up production. Real-world case studies and classroom demonstrations.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Separation Processes
courses.prereq_text: Chemical Engineering 10, and 110A-B; open to Engineering majors only.
courses.description: Basic principles and design techniques of equilibrium-stage separation processes. Emphasis is placed on binary distillation, liquid-liquid extraction, and multicomponent distillation.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Analytical Methods in Chemical Engineering
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 4B or 4BI; Mathematics 6A or 6AI. Space may be limited, and registration priority will be given to Chemical Engineering majors.
courses.description: Develop analytical tools to solve elementary partial differential equations and boundary value problems. Separation of variables, Laplace transforms, Sturm-Liouville theory, generalized Fourier analysis, and computer math tools.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Computational Methods in Chemical Engineering
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 4B or 4BI; Mathematics 6A or 6AI; Mathematics 6B and Engineering 3.
