courses.description: Numerical methods for solution of linear and nonlinear algebraic equations, optimization, interpolation, numerical integration and differentiation, initial-value problems in ordinary and partial differential equations, and boundary-value problems. Emphasis on computational tools for chemical engineering applications.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Statistical Methods in Chemical Engineering
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 4B or 4BI; Mathematics 6A or 6AI and Mathematics 6B.
courses.description: Probability concepts and distributions, random variables, error analysis, point estimation and confidence intervals, hypothesis testing, development of empirical chemical engineering models using regression techniques, design of experiments, process monitoring based on statistical quality control techniques.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Chemical Reaction Engineering
courses.prereq_text: Chemical Engineering 10 with minimum grade of C-; Chemical Engineering 110A with a minimum grade of C-; Chemical Engineering 110B (may be taken concurrently). Chemical Engineering 120A-B.
courses.description: Fundamentals of chemical reaction engineering with emphasis on kinetics of homogenous and heterogeneous reacting systems. A microkinetic understanding of reaction rates is linked to reactor design, chemical conversion, and selectivity. Batch and continuous reactor designs with and without catalysts are examined.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Chemical Reaction Engineering
courses.description: Thermodynamics, kinetics, mass and energy transport considerations associated with complex homogeneous and heterogeneous reacting systems. Catalysts and catalytic reaction rates and mechanisms. Adsorption and reaction at solid surfaces, including effects of diffusion in porous materials. Chemical reactors using heterogeneous catalysts.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: The Science and Engineering of Energy Conversion
courses.prereq_text: ChE 110A (or equivalent thermodynamics) and ChE 140A (or equivalent chemical kinetics); OR Chem 112A-B-C or Chem 113A-B-C; OR consent of instructor.
courses.comments: Equivalent upper-division coursework in thermodynamics and kinetics from outside of department will be considered. CHEM 104 and CH E 141 are the same course.
courses.description: Framework for understanding the energy supply issues facing society with a focus on the science, engineering, and economic principles of the major alternatives. Emphasis is on the physical and chemical fundamentals of energy conversion technologies.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Heterogeneous Catalysis
courses.prereq_text: Chemical Engineering 140A and B or consent of instructor.
courses.description: Concepts and definitions. Applications of heterogeneous catalysis. Performance metrics. Analysis of surface reaction mechanisms and complex reaction networks. Structure-function relationships for supported metal and zeolite catalysts. Synthesis and characterization of heterogeneous catalysts.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Process Dynamics and Control
courses.description: Development of theoretical and empirical models for chemical and physical processes, dynamic behavior of processes, transfer function and block diagram representation, process instrumentation, control system design and analysis, stability analysis, computer simulation of controlled processes.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Advanced Process Control
courses.description: The theory, design, and experimental application of advanced process control strategies including feedforward control, cascade control, enhanced single-loop strategies, and model predictive control. Analysis of multi-loop control systems. Introduction to on-line optimization.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Engineering Approaches to Systems Biology
courses.prereq_text: Chemical Engineering 170 or Chemical Engineering 107; Mathematics 4B or 4BI; Mathematics 6A or 6AI and Mathematics 6B.
courses.description: Applications of engineering tools and methods to solve problems in systems biology. Emphasis is placed on integrative approaches that address multi_scale and multi-rate phenomena in biological regulation. Modeling, optimization, and sensitivity analysis tools are introduced.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Introduction to Polymer Science
courses.prereq_text: Chemical Engineering 110A or Chemistry 113A or equivalent.
courses.comments: Same course as Materials 160.
courses.description: Introductory course covering synthesis, characterization, structure, and mechanical properties of polymers. The course is taught from a materials perspective and includes polymer thermodynamics, chain architecture, measurement and control of molecular weight as well as crystallization and glass transitions.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Mechatronics and Instrumentation for Chemical Engineers
courses.prereq_text: Engineering 3 and Chemical Engineering 110A and B, or consent of instructor
courses.description: Introduction to electromechanical systems and instrumentation used in Chemical Engineering. Fundamentals of transducers, sensors and actuators; interfacing and controlling hardware with software (Labview & Matlab programming); analog and digital circuits; hands-on electrical and mechanical design, prototyping, and construction. Students produce a final computer-controlled electromechanical project of their own design, or in conjunction with a ChE-faculty research laboratory.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Omics-enabled Biotechnology
courses.prereq_text: Chemical Engineering 170 or Chemical Engineering 107 or MCDB 1A and consent of instructor.
courses.description: Integrates genomic, transcriptomic, metabolomic, and proteomic approaches to quantify and understand intricate biological systems. Complementary bioinformatics approaches to curate the large datasets associated with these experiments will also be discussed. Recent examples from the literature will reinforce core concepts, ranging from applications to human health to the environment. By the end of the course, students should be able to design an integrated experiment that capitalizes on these omics-based approaches to enhance the scope of their research.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Biocircuit Design for Engineers
courses.prereq_text: Chemical Engineering 10, Chemical Engineering 107 or equivalent or consent of instructor.
courses.description: Introduction to fundamental principles underlying synthetic biology with an emphasis on mathematical modeling of gene regulation using ordinary differential equations and mass action kinetics. Students are introduced to foundational concepts in molecular and cellular engineering, synthetic biology, quantitative modeling of various genetic circuits, as well as cutting edge applications of innovative molecular biotechnologies such as cancer immunotherapy and cell-based diagnostics. Students will also learn to design and predict the functional outcomes of synthetic gene circuits and review primary literature in the field. At the end of this course, students are expected to develop a quantitative understanding of genetic circuit design.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Chemical Engineering Laboratory
courses.description: Experiments in thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, heat transfer, mass transfer, and chemical processing. Analysis of results, and preparation of reports.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Chemical Engineering Laboratory
courses.description: Experiments in mass transfer, reactor kinetics, process control, and chemical and biochemical processing. Analysis of results, and preparation of reports.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Design of Chemical Processes
courses.description: Applications of chemical engineering principles to reactor and plant design. Conceptual design of chemical processes. Flowsheeting methods. Engineering cost principles and economic aspects.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Design of Chemical Processes
courses.description: The solution to comprehensive plant design problems. Use of computer process simulators. Optimization of plant design, investment and operations.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Internship in Industry
courses.comments: Student must have a minimum 3.0 GPA. May not be used as departmental elective. May be repeated to a maximum of 12 units.
courses.description: Special projects for selected students. Offered in conjunction with engineering practice in selected industrial and research firms, under direct faculty supervision. A 2-4 page paper and an evaluation from the supervisor will be required for credit.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Undergraduate Research
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing, completion of 2 upper-division courses in Chemical Engineering; consent of the instructor.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters. May be repeated for up to 12 units. Not more than 3 units may be applied to departmental electives.
courses.description: Research opportunities for undergraduate students. Students are expected to give regular oral presentations, actively participate in a weekly seminar, and prepare at least one written report on their research.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Independent Studies in Chemical Engineering
courses.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division courses in Chemical Engineering.
courses.comments: Students must have a 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters. May be repeated up to 12 units. Not more than 3 units may be applied to departmental electives. Students are limited to five units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199DC/199RA courses combined.
courses.description: Directed individual studies.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Biomaterials and Biosurfaces
courses.comments: Same course as BMSE 202 and MATRL 270.
courses.description: Fundamentals of natural and artificial biomaterials and biosurfaces with emphasis on molecular level structure and function and their interactions with the body. Design issues of grafts and biopolymers. Basic biological, biophysical and biochemical systems reviewed for nonbiologists.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Fundamentals and Applications of Classical Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics
courses.description: Fundamental concepts in classical thermodynamics and statistical mechanics for engineering students. Establishes the framework within which problems can be solved using methodologies that start with molecular level understanding.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Equilibrium Statistical Mechanics
courses.comments: Same course as Materials 214.
courses.description: Application of the principles of statistical mechanics and thermodynamics to treat classical fluid systems at equilibrium. Topics include liquid state theory, computer simulation methods, critical phenomena and scaling principles, interfacial statistical mechanics, and electrolyte theory.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Statistical Mechanics
courses.description: Fundamentals of non-equilibrium statistical mechanics, kinetic theory of gases, Boltzmann equation, correlation functions, linear response theory, fluctuation-dissipation theorem, Langevin and Fokker-Planck equations.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Principles of Modern Molecular Simulation Methods
courses.description: Provides a broad overview of modern methods for computing the properties of multibody molecular systems. The course will cover: ab initio techniques, classical potential energy functions, Monte Carlo and molecular dynamics methods, free energy calculations, phase equilibria, and self-assembly/organization.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Matrix Analysis and Computation
courses.comments: Students should be proficient in basic numerical methods,linear algebra, mathematically rigorous proofs, and some programming language. Same course as Computer Science 211A, ECE 210A, Geology 251A, ME 210A and Mathematics 206A.
courses.description: Graduate level-matrix theory with introduction to matrix computations. SVD's, pseudoinverses, variational characterization of eigenvalues, perturbation theory, direct and iterative methods for matrix computations.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Numerical Simulation
courses.comments: Students should be proficient in basic numerical methods, linear algebra, mathematically rigorous proofs, and some programming language. Same course as Computer Science 211B, ECE 210B, Geology 251B, ME 210B and Mathematics 206B.
courses.description: Linear multistep methods and Runge-Kutta methods for ordinary differential equations: stability, order and convergence. Stiffness. Differential algebraic equations. Numerical solution of boundary value problems.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Numerical Solution of Partial Differential Equations--Finite Difference Methods
courses.comments: Students should be proficient in basic numerical methods,linear algebra, mathematically rigorous proofs, and some programming language. Same course as Computer Science 211C, ECE 210C, Geology 251C, ME 210C and Mathematics 206C.
courses.description: Finite difference methods for hyperbolic, parabolic and elliptic PDE's, with application to problems in science and engineering. Convergence, consistency, order and stability of finite difference methods. Dissipation and dispersion. Finite volume methods. Software design and adaptivity.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Numerical Solution of Partial Differential Equations--Finite Element Methods
courses.comments: Students should be proficient in basic numerical methods, linear algebra, mathematically rigorous proofs, and some programming language. Same course as Computer Science 211D, ECE 210D, Geology 251D, ME 210D, and Mathematics 206D.
courses.description: Weighted residual and finite element methods for the solution of hyperbolic, parabolic and elliptical partial differential equations, with application to problems in science and engineering. Error estimates. Standard and discontinuous Galerkin methods.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Introduction to Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy Techniques
courses.description: An introduction to magnetic resonance theory and experimental techniques, with emphasis on quantum-mechanical descriptions of basic NMR methods for solid-state applications.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Advanced Methods of Magnetic Resonance with Applications to Materials Science
courses.description: This course is intended to provide an understanding of advanced methods of magnetic resonance spectroscopy and imaging, emphasizing new applications to current issues in materials research.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Advanced Transport Processes-Laminar Flow and Convective Transport Processes
courses.description: Basic principles of fluid mechanics and convective transport processes. Governing equations and boundary conditions. Non-dimensionalization and scaling. Self-similar solutions and similarity transformations. Unidirectional flows. The thin gap approximation, lubrication theory and thin film dynamics. Low Reynolds number flows.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Advanced Transport Processes-Laminar Flow and Convective Transport Processes
courses.description: Continuation of ChE 220A. Viscous flows. Application of scaling and asymptotic methods to transport problems and fluid motions; Weak convection effects; Boundary layer theories for fluid mechanics and transport processes. Introduction to Linear stability theory for interfacial and buoyancy-driven flows.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Complex Fluids and Rheology
courses.description: Microstructural basis of constitutive models for simple complex fluids (dilute suspensions of non-spherical Brownian particles). Qualitative physics that leads to viscoelastic behavior in a variety of complex fluids, including polymeric liquids (dilute solutions and melts), wormlike micelle solutions, liquid crystalline fluids, emulsions, gels, and suspensions of vesicles or cells. Relationship between microscale physics and macroscopic rheology of materials in flow, including spatial non-uniformities in material properties that arise when flow couples to concentration or molecular weight.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Colloids and Biosurfaces
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Chemical Engineering 102.
courses.description: Basic forces and interactions between atoms, molecules, small particles and extended surfaces. Special features and interactions associated with (soft) biological molecules, biomaterials and surfaces: lipids, proteins, fibrous molecules (DNA), biological membranes, hydrophobic and hydrophilic interactions, bio-specific and non-equilibrium interactions. Graduate students do a project on a topic to be proposed by the students, and with a report to be presented to the class at the end of the quarter.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Colloids and Interfaces I
courses.comments: Same course as Materials 222A and BMSE 222A.
courses.description: Introduction to the various intermolecular interactions in solutions and in colloidal systems: Van Der Waals, electrostatic, hydrophobic, solvation, H-bonding. Introduction to colloidal systems.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Colloids and Interfaces II
courses.comments: Materials 222A or Chemical Engineering 222A recommended. Same course as BMSE 222B and Materials 222B.
courses.description: Continuation of 222A. Interparticle interactions, coagulation, DLVO theory, steric interactions, polymer-coated surfaces, polymers in solution, thin film viscosity. Surfactant and lipid self-assembly: micelles, microemulsions. Surfaces: wetting, contact angles, surface tension. Surfactants on surfaces: langmuir-blodgett films, adsorption, adhesion. Non-equilibrium and dynamic interactions.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Non-Newtonian Fluids, Soft Materials and Chemical Products
courses.description: Overview of soft materials (suspensions, gels, polymers, surfactants, emulsions, powders and granules) that arise in diverse industries, including consumer products, foods, advanced materials, biotechnology, and mineral and energy production. Influence of non-Newtonian rheology (shear-thickening and thinning, viscoelasticity, extension-thickening, yield stresses, normal stress differences, and metastability) upon handling, processing, production, and performance of chemical products. Strategies to design chemical products that meet performance targets, and to scale-up production. Real-world case studies and classroom demonstrations.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Advanced Theoretical Methods in Engineering
courses.comments: Same course as ME 244A.
courses.description: Methods of solution of partial differential equations and boundary value problems. Linear vector and function spaces, generalized fourier analysis, Sturm-Liouville theory, calculus of variations, and conformal mapping techniques.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Advanced Theoretical Methods in Engineering
courses.prereq_text: Chemical Engineering 230A and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: Same course as ME 244B.
courses.description: Advanced mathematical methods for engineers and scientists. Complex analysis, integral equations and green's functions. Asymptotic analysis of integrals and sums. Boundary layer methods and WKB theory.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Statistical Methods in Chemical Engineering
courses.description: An introduction to basic and intermediate statistical, probabilistic, and data analysis methods in engineering: probability functions and their properties, sampling distributions and limits, data collection and statistical inference, hypothesis testing, design of experiments, maximum likelihood and Bayesian methods, linear regression and regularization techniques, nonlinear regression, classification methods, error analysis and model assessment/validation, clustering and data reduction.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Advanced Chemical Reaction Engineering
courses.description: Following review of the theory of reaction kinetics for catalyzed and noncatalyzed systems, detailed consideration is given to design and performance of catalysts and chemical reactors. Mathematical studies of stability and optimization are emphasized in relationship to mass, energy, and momentum transport.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Advanced Chemical Reaction Engineering
courses.description: Following review of the theory of reaction kinetics for catalyzed and noncatalyzed systems, detailed consideration is given to design and performance of catalysts and chemical reactors. Mathematical studies of stability and optimization are emphasized in relationship to mass, energy, and momentum transport.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Advanced Catalysis
courses.description: Theories of reaction rates. Heterogeneous and homogenous catalysis, including physical structure and characterization of catalysts. Catalyst poisoning.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Advanced Science and Engineering of Energy Conversion
courses.comments: Same course as CHEM 204.
courses.description: The course provides a framework for understanding the energy supply issues facing society with a focus on the science, engineering, and economic principles of the major alternatives. Emphasis will be on the physical and chemical fundamentals of energy conversion technologies.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Introduction to Polymer Science
courses.description: Introductory course covering synthesis, characterization, structure, and mechanical properties of polymers. The course is taught from a materials perspective and includes polymer thermodynamics, chain architecture, measurement and control of molecular weight as well as crystallization and glass transitions.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Mechatronics and Instrumentation for Chemical Engineers
courses.description: Introduction to electromechanical systems and instrumentation used in Chemical Engineering. Fundamentals of transducers, sensors and actuators; interfacing and controlling hardware with software (Labview & Matlab programming); analog and digital circuits; hands-on electrical and mechanical design, prototyping, and construction. Students produce a final computer-controlled electromechanical project of their own design, or in conjunction with a ChE-faculty research laboratory. Graduate students taking the course will have an extensive final design project related to some aspect of their thesis research involving automated data acquisition and/or control of instrumentation.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Omics-enabled Biotechnology
courses.comments: Molecular and Cell Biology (undergraduate level)
courses.description: Integrates genomic, transcriptomic, metabolomic, and proteomic approaches to quantify and understand intricate biological systems. Complementary bioinformatics approaches to curate the large datasets associated with these experiments are also discussed. Recent examples from the literature reinforce core concepts, ranging from applications to human health to the environment. By the end of the course, students should be able to design an integrated experiment that capitalizes on these omics-based approaches to enhance the scope of their research.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Model-Guided Engineering of Biological Systems
courses.description: Introduction to fundamental principles underlying synthetic biology with an emphasis on mathematical modeling of gene regulation using ordinary differential equations and mass action kinetics. Students are introduced to foundational concepts in molecular and cellular engineering, synthetic biology, quantitative modeling of various genetic circuits, as well as cutting edge applications of innovative molecular biotechnologies such as cancer immunotherapy and cell-based diagnostics. Students will also learn to design and predict the functional outcomes of synthetic gene circuits and review primary literature in the field. Graduate students enrolled will be required to submit an additional project.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Model Predictive Control and Moving Horizon Estimation
courses.prereq_text: Linear systems I (ECE 230A or ME 243A) or consent of instructor.
courses.description: Analysis, design and computation of model predictive control applied toconstrained linear, and nonlinear systems. Analysis and design of movinghorizon state estimation of nonlinear systems. As time permits, selectedadditional topics include: robust model predictive, stochastic model predictivecontrol, and identification methods for offset-free model predictive control.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Chemical Engineering Forum
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit.
courses.description: Seminars and workshops focusing on current research topics and graduate student education.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Research Group Studies
courses.description: Students or instructors present recently published papers and/or results relevant to their own research.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Bioengineering: Career and Development Opportunities at the Interface between Biotechnology and Engineering
courses.comments: Same as BMSE 294B and MCDB 294B.
courses.description: Based on presentations by experts from the bioengineering industry. Presenters describe their companies' technologies and developments, including biosensors, therapeutics, tissue engineering, quantum dots and advanced instrumentation. Training and educational requirements for different career tracks are discussed.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Group Studies: Controls, Dynamical Systems, and Computation
courses.description: A series of weekly lectures given by university staff and outside experts in the fields of control systems, dynamical systems, and computation.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Internship in Industry
courses.description: Special projects for selected students. Students pursue practical engineering experience in selected industrial and research firms, under faculty supervision.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Special seminar on research subjects of current interest.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Directed Reading and Research
courses.comments: Not applicable to course requirements for PhD degree
courses.description: Experimental or theoretical research undertaken under the direction of a faculty member for graduate students who have not yet advanced to candidacy.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Individual Study for Master's Comprehensive Examinations and Ph.D.
courses.comments: Maximum of 12 units per quarter. Instructor should be the student's major professor or chairman of his doctoral committee. No unit credit allowed toward advanced degree(s).
courses.description: Examinations.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Master's Thesis Research and Preparation
courses.comments: Not applicable to course requirement for M.S. degree.
courses.description: Only for research underlying the thesis and writing the thesis.

courses.subject: CH E
courses.title: Dissertation Research and Preparation
courses.comments: Not applicable to course requirements for PhD degree
courses.description: Only for research underlying the dissertation and writing the disseration.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Introduction to Chicano/a Studies
courses.description: Introduction to the historical and contemporary development of the Chicano/a community. Course is interdisciplinary in nature. Focuses by quarter on A. history, B. gender, and C. culture.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Introduction to Chicano/a Studies
courses.description: Introduction to the historical and contemporary development of the Chicano/a community. Course is interdisciplinary in nature. Focuses by quarter on A. history, B. gender, and C. culture.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Introduction to Chicano/a Studies
courses.description: Introduction to the historical and contemporary development of the Chicano/a community. Course is interdisciplinary in nature. Focuses by quarter on A. history, B. gender, and C. culture.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Special Topics in Chicano Studies
courses.comments: Course may be taken up to three times (12 units) providing the letter designations are different.
courses.description: Designed to allow courses of varying topics in areas of expertise of visiting professors to broaden opportunities for students. Examples might be: immigration, Native American, Mexican, or Latin American influences on the Chicano, legal issues, the migrants.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Independent Studies
courses.comments: Students are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
courses.description: Independent study under the guidance of a faculty member in the department. Course offers students the opportunity to undertake independent study or work in a group.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Teaching 4 Social Justice
courses.prereq_text: At least one course in one of these departments: Asian American Studies, Black Studies, Chicana/o Studies, Feminist Studies
courses.comments: AS AM 101C, BL ST 101C, CH ST 101C, and FEMST 101C are cross-listed.
courses.description: This interdisciplinary course will highlight how a curriculum focusing on racial, ethnic, gender, and LGBTQ studies is central to teaching and learning within diverse societal contexts. This grounding is essential for K-12 teachers in History and English/Literature. Through a social justice framework, students will learn how classrooms are enhanced by Ethnic and Feminist Studies, placing graduates within the forefront of educational initiatives that position teaching and learning within an inclusive and equitable paradigm.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Indigenous People and the Nation State in the Americas
courses.comments: CH ST 109 and ANTH 113 are the same course.
courses.description: The changing relationship between indigenous people and the state. Compare the differences and similarities between indigenous peoples' mobilizations in the cases of Canada, USA, Ecuador, Chile, Guatemala, Bolivia and Mexico.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Research Methods in Chicano Studies
courses.prereq_text: Chicano Studies 1A or 1B or 1C or upper-division standing.
courses.description: Using Chicano studies topics, the course will introduce students to: (1) the epistemology of scientific inquiry (its history and contemporary movements); (2) the strengths and weaknesses of quantitative and qualitative methodologies; and (3) the mechanisms of research design (transforming an idea into a research plan).

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Critical Introduction to Ancient Mesoamerica
courses.description: Broad survey of ancient Mesoamerica (Olmec, Zapotec, Teotihuacan, Maya, Aztec). Investigates these cultures along with factors that have influenced their contemporary interpretation, including the forms of data available and contexts and motivations of the people who have generated them.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Cultural and Critical Theory
courses.prereq_text: Chicano Studies 1A or 1B or 1C or upper-division standing.
courses.description: Introduction to the various modes, techniques, terminologies, and methodologies fundamental to cultural studies.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Indigenous Studies Internships
courses.prereq_text: Any Ethnic Studies or Feminist Studies course recommended (not required).
courses.description: Introduction to NAGPRA(s) and campus repatriation efforts toward compliance through supporting and/or contributing to the work of the UCSB Repository of Archaeological and Ethnographic Collections. Students learn about local indigenous community issues and allyship and acquire archival, collections, database and/or GIS experience based on interest. (Internships comprise attendance at a 1-hour seminar each week and flexible hours of supervised work.)

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Maya History & Resistance
courses.description: The course examines Maya History and Resistance in the Mayab’, or where the Maya live/are. It attempts to de-center the nation-state, while also recognizing the ways that governments have played a role in repressing Indigenous Peoples. The course analyzes the Maya through time and space, with each week focusing on a particular topic.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Aztec and Maya Mythologies
courses.description: Explores ancient Mesoamerican mythology in both its indigenous and modern Chicana representations from archeological, historical, and Chicano perspectives. Emphasizes consideration of the various forms by which mythologies are maintained.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: The Scientific Revolution and Non-Western Epistemologies
courses.prereq_text: Chicano Studies 1A or 1B or 1C or upper-division standing.
courses.description: Overview of the Scientific Revolution and its impact both within Western Europe and outside of the Mediterranean region through colonialism. Contrast of resulting "Western" scientific perspective with non-Western epistemologies, principally of the indigenous Western Hemisphere.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Introduction to U.S. Xicana(x) and Latinx Public Art and Studio
courses.prereq_text: Chicano Studies 1A or 1B or 1C. Concurrent enrollment in Chicano Studies 124L required.
courses.description: Explores examples of public and site-specific artwork created by Chicano/Latinx artists challenging museum and gallery spaces. The history of displacement and marginalization traditionally suffered by Chicano/Latinx communities had lead these artists to create public art as a form of decolonization.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Introduction to U.S. Xicana(x) and Latinx Public Art and Studio
courses.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in Chicano Studies 124 required.
courses.description: After visiting the Chicana/Latinx museum and gallery spaces, the lab supports students in producing their own public and site-specific artwork. Other students describe, arrange, and curate a gallery showing by the end of the quarter.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: MeXicana/o(x) Art History (18481975)
courses.prereq_text: Chicano Studies 1A or 1B or 1C or upper-division standing.
courses.description: A look at the body of Chicana/o artistic production, from mid-1960 to the mid-1970s, through an examination of the historical, aesthetic and philosophical foundations of Chicana/o art theory and practice that evolved out of Mexican and Latin American Modernism. Revisits Mexican modernist ideas on race and gender, culture, identity and nation, revolution and class conflict; and sifts through the Indigenous values and concepts Chicana/os encountered through their study of Mexican history and culture during the mid 1960s and early 1970s.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Contemporary Chicano and Chicana Art
courses.description: Examination and appraisal of the Chicana/o art movement within the context of contemporary American art and the contemporary art of Mexico. A survey of major Chicano and Chicana artists and developments in Chicano painting, sculpture, graphic, and conceptual art from the late 1960's to the present.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Art Praxis - Chicana/o Art Education as Social Practice: Politics, Methods, and Practice for Community-Based Work
courses.prereq_text: Chicano Studies 1A or 1B or 1C or upper-division standing. Concurrent enrollment in Chicano Studies 127L required.
courses.description: Examines the work and ideas that artists of color have integrated into their art practice to educate, expose, and address the concerns of oppressed communities, such as racism, the effects of war, state violence, labor struggles, forced migration, immigration, sexism, and economic disparity. This overview is the basis for examining the intersections and differences that have informed the strategies and tactics we explore in the development of our approach to community art practice.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Xicana(x) Visual Traditions
courses.description: Introduces students to the development of art as a social practice specifically in the MeXicana[x], Latina[x], and Indigenous communities. Students will study the oral/visual traditions, art forms, and costumbres that are still in practice today in the transnational communities surrounding us.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Struggles for Equality in Chicana/o Education
courses.description: Investigates Chicana/o struggles for educational equality in the U.S. Presentations, discussions, written assignments analyze historical and contemporary examples of Chicana/o communities responding to and resisting subordination based on intersections of race with gender, class, language, immigrant status, and sexuality.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Critical Race Theory in Chicana/o Education
courses.description: Examines Critical Race Theory (CRT) as an emerging analytical framework in the field of education. Course investigates how a CRT framework might address and challenge the impacts of race, class, gender, language, immigrant status, accent, and sexual orientation on Chicana/o, Latina/o educational attainment and achievement.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Barrio Popular Culture
courses.description: Explores various manifestations of popular and mass culture in Chicano urban and semi-rural communities throughout the Southwest. Both secular and religious cultural phenomena are analyzed (lowriders, saints, music, etc.). Relationships to mainstream culture is examined.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Chicana/o Mexican Cultural Heritage
courses.prereq_text: Chicano Studies 1A or 1B or 1C or upper-division standing.
courses.description: A panoramic view of present-day Chicana/o traditions analyzed from a Mexican cultural heritage perspective in order to comprehend and appreciate the uniqueness and difference of present-day Chicano/o culture, its achievements, and contribution to the overall American culture.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Central Americans in the United States
courses.description: Provides an interdisciplinary historical overview of Central American migrations to the U.S., and a cultural and political analysis of resulting individual and group identities. Transnationalism, diasporas, politics, and community building among Central Americans, or "Central American-Americans" are explored.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Chicano/a Film Studies
courses.description: Study of Chicano/a cinema to view film as an art form and projection of the filmmaker. Techniques, messages, and ideology stressed as instruments which propose film truth within the context of Chicano/a experience.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Chicana Art and Feminism
courses.prereq_text: Chicano Studies 1A or 1B or 1C or upper-division standing.
courses.description: An overview of contemporary Chicana art and feminist theory from the late 1960s to the present placed within the context of the Chicano movement and other historical events.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: De-Colonizing Feminism
courses.prereq_text: Department approval required to finalize registration.
courses.description: Surveys contemporary forms of feminist consciousness expressed U.S. women of color. Can U.S. women of color be considered a political class? What relations exist between women of color across race, culture, sex, and class differences?

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Gender and Sexuality in the Americas
courses.prereq_text: Departmental approval required to finalize registration.
courses.description: Examines cultural, social, political and representational aspects of gender and sexuality across the Americas. Organized around various themes--control and repression; the politics and culture of resistance; and sexual transgression as affirmation of marginalized identities--this course challenges conceptions of gender and sexuality across the Americas. Covering topics ranging from normative sexuality, transgender expression, gay sexuality, and lesbian expression, the course is designed to examine developments in gender and sexuality within the U.S. and across the Americas.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Latinidades
courses.description: What it means to be Latina/o/x varies not only based on class, nationality, and citizenship status but also on race and ethnicity. This undergraduate seminar interrogates Latinidad as a historical, political, and racial project. Students will trace the origins of Hispanic and Latina/o/x identities to the settler logics from which they emerged, particularly those that rely on the erasure of Indigenous and Afro-descendent populations. Special attention will be placed on how race and racism manifest in the material conditions and lived experiences of Indigenous, Afro-Indigenous, Afro/Black Latinxs.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Afro-Latina/o Diasporic Performance
courses.description: Offers an introduction to performance practices rooted in the African diaspora of the Americas focusing on the United States, Latin America, and the Caribbean. Interrogates identity articulation in dance, music, literature, visual art, and theatrical texts. Examine how performers negotiate race, ethnicity, gender, class, and sexuality with attention to what constitutes performance. Employingtransnational frameworks, explore how these performances have historically functioned and continue to inspire social transformation and the recovery of shared histories of Afro-Latina/o diasporas.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Ethnic Studies Teacher Education Seminar
courses.prereq_text: At least one course in one of these departments: Asian American Studies, Black Studies, Chicana/o Studies, Feminist Studies.
courses.description: Designed for students who are Black Studies, Chicana/o Studies, Asian American Studies, and/or Feminist Studies majors in the ÉXITO program. Central to the year-long seminar will be preparations for students’ pursuit for a career as K-12 Ethnic Studies educators. Students are placed in a local K-12 classroom to participate in and observe firsthand the fundamental aspects of teaching and learning Ethnic Studies. Students will have direct assistance for preparing and applying to Masters/Teacher Education Programs, professionalization workshops, and conducting independent research.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Ethnic Studies Teacher Education Seminar
courses.prereq_text: At least one course in one of these departments: Asian American Studies, Black Studies, Chicana/o Studies, Feminist Studies.
courses.description: Designed for students who are Black Studies, Chicana/o Studies, Asian American Studies, and/or Feminist Studies majors in the ÉXITO program. Central to the year-long seminar will be preparations for students’ pursuit for a career as K-12 Ethnic Studies educators. Students are placed in a local K-12 classroom to participate in and observe firsthand the fundamental aspects of teaching and learning Ethnic Studies. Students will have direct assistance for preparing and applying to Masters/Teacher Education Programs, professionalization workshops, and conducting independent research.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Ethnic Studies Teacher Education Seminar
courses.prereq_text: At least one course in one of these departments: Asian American Studies, Black Studies, Chicana/o Studies, Feminist Studies.
courses.description: Designed for students who are Black Studies, Chicana/o Studies, Asian American Studies, and/or Feminist Studies majors in the ÉXITO program. Central to the year-long seminar will be preparations for students’ pursuit for a career as K-12 Ethnic Studies educators. Students will have direct assistance for preparing and presenting their original research projects at URCA Day.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Storytelling as Activism (SWAPA)
courses.prereq_text: Chicano Studies 1A or 1B or 1C; a previous upper-division course in Chicano Studies.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units.
courses.description: Storytelling as Activism (SWAPA) introduces students to a method for reading, writing, thinking, and performing before an audience of peers. This method is based on the shaman-witness ritual proposed by Chicana theorist and writer, Gloria Anzaldua.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Storytelling as Activism Lab
courses.description: Accompanies Storytelling as Activism (SWAPA) course. Focuses on creative production, atriculation, and vocal expression.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Latinx Youth
courses.prereq_text: Departmental approval required to finalize registration.
courses.description: Focuses on Latinx immigrant youth and the children of Latinx immigrants’ experiences with identity formation, assimilation, race and ethnicity, and media representation. Delves into how racial ideologies inform the U.S. immigration system, as well as how racial ideologies from Latin America and the United States converge to inform the lives of people of Latin American descent.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Xican* Indigena Media
courses.prereq_text: Chicano Studies 1A or 1B or 1C; two upper division courses in Chicana and Chicano Studies; Concurrent enrollment in Chicano Studies 162L.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit.
courses.description: Low cost digital tools have created a revolution in video. Course explores creative approaches to practical techniques of independent digital video production. Students establish a production strategy by employing "guerrilla tactics" for creative and unconventional uses of digital machineries.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Xican* Indigena Media Lab
courses.description: Lab for producing guerrilla digital video.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Exposing Health Inequities
courses.description: Given the continuous rise of anti-immigrant sentiment felt across the United States and across the globe, this course brings the realities of immigrants of color to the forefront by exposing health inequities. It especially focuses attention on the structural inequities, drawing on Latinx Critical Race Theory, Chicana/o/x feminist epistemologies, and sociological insights into how and why ‘illegality,’ racism, and health converge and their critical intersections in exposing larger health inequities.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: History of the Chicano
courses.prereq_text: History 17A or 17B or 17C or Chicano Studies 1A or 1B or 1C or upper-division standing.
courses.comments: Same course as History 168A.
courses.description: The history of the Chicanos from the indigenous/colonial past to 1900. Explores the evolving history of Mexican descent people during the Pre-Columbian, Spanish, Mexican, and the U.S. periods.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: History of the Chicanos
courses.prereq_text: History 17A or 17B or 17C or Chicano Studies 1A or 1B or 1C or HIST 56 or upper-division standing.
courses.comments: Chicano Studies 168B and History 168B are the same course.
courses.description: The history of the Chicanos from 1900 to the present. Explores issues such as immigration, second-generation experience, civil rights struggles, the Chicano Movement, the post-Chicano Movement, the role of women in Chicano history, and the new Latino millennials of the 21st century.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: History of the Chicano Movement
courses.prereq_text: Chicano Studies 1A or 1B or 1C or upper-division standing.
courses.comments: Same course as History 168E.
courses.description: History of the Chicano Movement. An examination of the Chicano movement in the United States from the mid-1960s to the mid-1970s. Topics will include the student movement, the farmworker movement, the Plande Aztlan, the Raza Unida Party, Chicana feminists, the anti-war movement, and Chicanostudies.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Latino Religious Traditions in Historical Perspective
courses.prereq_text: A previous course in History or Chicano Studies.
courses.comments: Same course as History 168T. Not open for credit to students who have taken CH ST 168R or HIST 168R.
courses.description: Focuses on the role of religion in the Chicano/Latino historical experience. Includes pre-Columbian traditions, Spanish colonial traditions, religion of the U.S.-Mexico borderlands, immigrant religious traditions, the changing nature of Latino religions in the twentieth century.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: The Brown/Black Metropolis: Race, Class, & Resistance in the City
courses.description: Traces the transition of Browns/Blacks from a rural urban population and examines trends in family size, language, usage, segregation and social inequality. Issues of urban decay and community conflict are also examined.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Global Migration, Transnationalism in Chicana/o Contexts
courses.description: This course considers Chicana/o and U.S. Latina/o culture(s) within the context of transnational practices and patterns including both hemispheric and global migration trajectories.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Survey of Chicano Literature
courses.description: The course encompasses a general overview of all genres (poetry, novel, theater, short story and essay) of Chicano literature. A people's socio-historical experiences are examined to understand ethnicity, creativity, and world view.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Chicana/o Novels
courses.comments: Spanish 179 and Chicano Studies 181 are the same course.
courses.description: Reading, analysis and critique of the contemporary Chicano novel as it pertains to the Chicano experience.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Contemporary Chicanx Environmental Justice Writers
courses.prereq_text: Chicano Studies 1A or 1B or 1C or upper-division standing.
courses.description: Examination of literary works by Chicana writers. Centers on engagement with ecological themes. Feminist, queer, and environmental justice theories as well as other contemporary critical theories are applied to the analysis of prose, poetry, drama, and other narrative works written by such authors as María Amparo Ruiz de Burton, Jovita González, Cherríe Moraga, Ana Castillo, Helena María Viramontes, and others.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Border Narrative
courses.description: Reading and analysis of U.S./Mexico border narratives (novels, essays, short stories, autobiographies) focusing on the problems associated with relations between countries.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Chicana Writers
courses.prereq_text: Department approval required to finalize registration.
courses.description: Examination of literary works by Chicana writers. Feminist theories as well as other contemporary critical theories are applied to the analysis of prose, poetry and dramatic works written by such authors as Sandra Cisneros, Ana Castillo, Helen Viramontes, and others.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Decolonial CyberCinema
courses.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in Chicano Studies 185L; upper-division standing.
courses.description: Cybercinema is one of the most recent and innovative technologies for representing reality. What are its aesthetic forms, and how do they work to de-colonize the imagination under postcolonial conditions? Can we identify a specific "Chicana/o" criticism or aesthetics?

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Decolonial Cyber Cinema Lab
courses.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in Chicano Studies 185; upper-division standing.
courses.description: Mandatory Laboratory for CHST 185.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Language, Power, and Learning
courses.prereq_text: Departmental Approval Required to Finalize Registration.
courses.comments: Same course as LING 187.
courses.description: Critical examination of institutional power related to education and linguistic and cultural diversity. Focus on Latinx communities; formal and informal learning; family practices; bilingual education; heritage languages; language and labor; language and racism; immigrant languages; racialized varieties of English.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Chicano Theater Workshop
courses.prereq_text: Chicano Studies 1A or 1B or 1C or upper-division standing.
courses.description: Reading and analysis of contemporary bilingual chicano plays, in conjunction with acting and technical training. A dramatic piece will be rehearsed and performed.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Immigration and the U.S. Border
courses.description: Immigration and the U.S. border. An analysis of the socioeconomic and political factors which have determined and continue to form the basis for the development of United States immigration policies and practices toward Mexico and the U.S.-Mexican border.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: El Plan de Santa Barbara, El Centro Arnulfo Casillas, and UCSB Chicanx/Latinx Student Activism, 1960s-Present
courses.description: Examines the history of UCSB Chicanx/Latinx student activism on campus from the late 1960s until the present. Starting with the April 1969 El Plan de Santa Barbara conference, the class examines critical events such as the 1968 and 1975 North Hall protests, the 1989 and 1994 hunger strikes, and the student-led movement to save El Centro from demolition in the mid-2010s. Special focus is placed on conducting archival research on Chicanx/Latinx student activism and solidifying El Centro Arnulfo Casillas a sacred site/home for future generations of students, particularly those engaged in struggles to decolonize the university.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Special Topics in Chicano Studies
courses.comments: Course may be taken up to three times (12 units) providing the letter designations are different.
courses.description: Designed to allow courses of varying topics in areas of expertise of visiting professors to broaden opportunities for students. Examples might be: immigration, Native American, Mexican, or Latin American influences on the Chicano, legal issues, the migrants.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Special Topics in Chicano Studies
courses.description: Designed to allow courses of varying topics in areas of expertise of visiting professors, to broaden opportunities for students. Examples might be: immigration, Native American, Mexican, or Latin Smerican influences onthe Chicano, legal issues, the migrants.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Latinidades
courses.comments: Course may be taken up to three times (12 units) providing the letter designations are different.
courses.description: What it means to be Latina/o/x varies not only based on class, nationality, and citizenship status but also on race and ethnicity. This undergraduate seminar interrogates Latinidad as a historical, political, and racial project. In this course, students will trace the origins of Hispanic and Latina/o/x identities to the settler logics from which they emerged, particularly those that rely on the erasure of Indigenous and Afro-descendent populations. Special attention will be placed on how race and racism manifest in the material conditions and lived experiences of Indigenous, Afro-Indigenous, Afro/Black Latinxs.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Maya History & Resistance
courses.comments: Course may be taken up to three times (12 units) providing the letter designations are different.
courses.description: The course examines Maya History and Resistance in the Mayab’, or where the Maya live/are. It attempts to de-center the nation-state, while also recognizing the ways that governments have played a role in repressing Indigenous Peoples. The course analyzes the Maya through time and space, with each week focusing on a particular topic.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Environmental Justice in Central America
courses.comments: Course may be taken up to three times (12 units) providing the letter designations are different.
courses.description: Examine environmental justice issues in Central America through the history of environmental social movements, with a focus on campesino, Indigenous, and Black resistance to extractivist industries such as mining and hydroelectric projects. Topics covered include environmental degradation, climate change, forced displacement and alternative forms of development.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Indigenous Latinx Migrations
courses.comments: Course may be taken up to three times (12 units) providing the letter designations are different.
courses.description: Through an examination of national and Indigenous contexts, this course considers how race and migration to the United States affects Indigenous peoples from Latin America. For many Indigenous Latinx immigrants, the racism and discrimination they experience in the United States is informed by both settler colonialism in the United States as well as the racist logics of their home countries. Given that both contexts shape Indigenous immigrants’ experiences, students will think about injustice and resistance across borders. Students will explore how Indigenous migration complicates and transforms notions of Latinidad in ways that are generative and that have shaped labor, social movements, gender dynamics, and the field of Chicana/o Studies.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Special Topics in Chicano Studies
courses.comments: Course may be taken up to three times (12 units) providing the letter designations are different.
courses.description: Designed to allow courses of varying topics in areas of expertise of visiting professors to broaden opportunities for students. Examples might be: immigration, Native American, Mexican, or Latin American influences on the Chicano, legal issues, the migrants.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: UCSB-Universidad Ixil (Guatemala): Caminos Futuros
courses.comments: Course may be taken up to three times (12 units) providing the letter designations are different.
courses.description: Examines Indigenous ways of knowing and education, and decolonizing knowledges, and is taught in collaboration with the Ixil University in Guatemala. The course is a result of years or organizing and seeks committed students who will collectively examine a range of themes and topics related to Maya history, culture, representation, resistance, and other indigenous concepts. The course and readings are taught in Spanish, and students are required to have a fluency in Spanish.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Special Topics in Chicano Studies
courses.comments: Course may be taken up to three times (12 units) providing the letter designations are different.
courses.description: Designed to allow courses of varying topics in areas of expertise of visiting professors to broaden opportunities for students. Examples might be: immigration, Native American, Mexican, or Latin American influences on the Chicano, legal issues, the migrants.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Special Topics in Chicano Studies
courses.comments: Course may be taken up to three times (12 units) providing the letter designations are different.
courses.description: Designed to allow courses of varying topics in areas of expertise of visiting professors to broaden opportunities for students. Examples might be: immigration, Native American, Mexican, or Latin American influences on the Chicano, legal issues, the migrants.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Group Studies for Advanced Students
courses.prereq_text: Chicana/o Studies 1A or 1B or 1C or upper-division standing.
courses.comments: Students may apply a maximum of 8 units of Chicana/o Studies 192/195A-B-C-D/198/199 courses combined to the Chicana/o Studies major.
courses.description: Intensive study and research.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Senior Seminar
courses.prereq_text: Two courses in Chicana/o Studies; consent of instructor; and senior standing.
courses.comments: To be offered intermittently.
courses.description: Capstone course for Chicana and Chicano Studies majors. Goal is to produce a thoroughly documented and professionally crafted Chicana/o Studies research paper (or creative project).

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Ethnic Studies Teacher Education Seminar
courses.prereq_text: At least one course in one of these departments: Asian American Studies, Black Studies, Chicana/o Studies, Feminist Studies.
courses.description: Designed for students who are Black Studies, Chicana/o Studies, Asian American and/or Feminist Studies majors in the XITO (Educational eXcellence and Inclusion Training Opportunities) program. Central to the year-long seminar will be preparations for students pursuit for a career as K-12 Ethnic Studies educators. Students will have direct assistance for preparing and applying to Masters/Teacher Education Programs as well as professionalization workshops.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Ethnic Studies Teacher Education Seminar
courses.prereq_text: At least one course in one of these departments: Asian American Studies, Black Studies, Chicana/o Studies, Feminist Studies.
courses.description: Designed for students who are Black Studies, Chicana/o Studies, Asian American and/or Feminist Studies majors in the XITO (Educational eXcellence and Inclusion Training Opportunities) program. Central to the year-long seminar will be preparations for students pursuit for a career as K-12 Ethnic Studies educators. Students will have direct assistance for preparing and applying to Masters/Teacher Education Programs as well as professionalization workshops.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Ethnic Studies Teacher Education Seminar
courses.prereq_text: At least one course in one of these departments: Asian American Studies, Black Studies, Chicana/o Studies, Feminist Studies.
courses.description: Designed for students who are Black Studies, Chicana/o Studies, Asian American and/or Feminist Studies majors in the XITO (Educational eXcellence and Inclusion Training Opportunities) program. Central to the year-long seminar will be preparations for students pursuit for a career as K-12 Ethnic Studies educators. Students will have direct assistance for preparing and applying to Masters/Teacher Education Programs as well as professionalization workshops.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Internship in Poverty, Inequality, and Social Justice
courses.comments: This course fulfills a requirement for the Minor in Poverty, Inequality, and Social Justice (HIST). Must be taken for a letter grade. CH ST 196SJ, HIST 196SJ, & GLOBL 196SJ are the same course.
courses.description: Students gain practical experience by working in organizations or initiatives engaged in addressing poverty and inequality through policy analysis, advocacy, direct social provision, community action, and/or political organizing. Opportunities to cultivate problem-solving, communication, organizational, and interpersonal skills needed to work effectively in institutional or collectively organized settings and to gain exposure to professional, post-graduate education and training, and related career opportunities in anti-poverty and social justice fields. Students work under faculty supervision to produce reports, a research paper, or other types of creative material based on their experiences.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Honors Project Seminar
courses.prereq_text: Acceptance into the Chicana and Chicano Studies honors program; senior standing; consent of department; open to Chicana and Chicano Studies majors only.
courses.description: Seminar for the development of the honors research project. Emphasis is on the design of the project and the establishment of methodologies to be utilized. Background and initial research is undertaken.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Honors Project Research
courses.prereq_text: Chicana/o Studies 197HA; acceptance into the Chicana and Chicano Studies honors program; senior standing; consent of department; open to Chicana and Chicano Studies majors only.
courses.description: Independent research comprising the bulk of the data acquisition and organization for the honors project.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Honors Project Writing
courses.prereq_text: Chicana/o Studies 197HB; acceptance into Chicana and Chicano Studies honors program; senior standing; consent of department; open to Chicana and Chicano Studies majors only.
courses.description: Allows students to complete the writing of the honors thesis. Time is allotted to prepare a presentation of the project before an audience of peers and faculty members.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Independent Studies
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of two upper-division courses in Chicana/o Studies.
courses.comments: Students are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined. Students may apply a maximum of 8 units of Chicana/o Studies 192/195A-B-C-D/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined to the Chicana/o Studies major.
courses.description: Independent studies in Chicana/o students under the guidance of a faculty member in the department. Students wishing to enroll should prepare a short plan of study.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Independent Research Assistance in Chicana/o Studies
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division courses in Chicana/o Studies; consent of instructor and department.
courses.comments: Students are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined. Chicana/o Studies 199RA may not be used for credit in the major.
courses.description: Coursework consists of faculty supervised research assistance.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: History and Narrativity
courses.description: Examines critical theories and methods in the production of historical narratives, social myths, and ideologies of racialization and ethnicity. Special attention is given to employment strategies, tropes, and allegorical forms in the construction of historical events and narratives.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Social Processes
courses.description: Explores critical theories and methods in the production of knowledge relevant to social, political, economic, and institutional structures. Special attention is given to interdisciplinary articulations with theories and methods in the humanities.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Cultural Texts
courses.description: Explores critical theories and methods in the production of cultural knowledge in the humanities. Special attention is given to interdisciplinary articulations with theories and methods in the social sciences.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Research Seminar
courses.description: Introduces students to the practice of original research in the interdisciplinary field of Chicana and Chicano Studies, including articulating a research problem, placing it within theoretical discussions, selecting appropriate methods, and analyzing and writing data, results, and/or findings.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Interdisciplinary Methods
courses.description: A critical introduction to a broad range of approaches and methodologies used in Chicana and Chicano Studies. These methods include (but are not limited to) fieldwork, archival and historical research, textual analysis, action research, visual production, political economy, and statistics.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Ethnography & Ethnographic Methods
courses.description: This course examines the epistemology, ethics, and politics of ethnographic fieldwork and is designed to provide students with the methodological tools to conduct ethnographic research. Through close reading and seminar discussions, students reflect on the origins of ethnographic inquiry and engage with decolonial responses to Western ethnographic inquiry. Having developed a critical understanding of ethnographic research as theory and method in the first half of the course, students develop and workshop their own ethnographic research project and gain hands-on experience collecting, analyzing, and writing up ethnographic data.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: De-Colonizing Feminism
courses.description: Key writings by US feminists-of-color have transformed intellectual and cultural production, and re-generated new modes of de-colonizing philosophy. Graduate students write a substantial paper. They also participate in organizing and leading class discussions on a rotating basis.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Indigenous Texts
courses.description: Treats translations of primary indigenous documents. Investigates the oral performance inherent to written indigenous records. Attention focuses on the Popol Vuh and the Codex Chimalpopoca, but Classic Maya hieroglyphic texts and Aztec codices are considered as well.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Reading Anzalda: Text, Context, and Interpretation
courses.description: Seminar surveys the major and minor works of Chicana feminist thinker Gloria Anzalda and considers the influence that her work has had in a range of disciplines, from Chicana/o Studies and queer theory to political science and philosophy.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Globalization and Immigration
courses.description: Tracks the migration of people and cultures across national boundaries, focusing on the itinerary of Mexican migrations to the U.S., with selected examples of migrations into Europe. Attention is paid to the changing significance of the nation.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Teaching Assistant and Associate Training
courses.comments: Units earned do not apply toward completion of advanced degrees. S/U grading only. Required of all teaching assistants in Chicana and Chicano Studies.
courses.description: Supervised teaching of lower division Chicana/o Studies courses. Required participation in occasional workshops related to teaching.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Teaching Assistant Practicum
courses.comments: Units earned do not apply toward completion of advanced degrees. S/U grading only.
courses.description: Introduces incoming Teaching Assistants to key campus resources and services available to graduate and undergraduate students. It is intended to foster an ongoing dialogue about teaching within the academy.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Introduction to Graduate School
courses.description: Introduces the new cohort of graduate students to the graduate program. The purpose is broadly defined as providing information, discussing Department norms, answering questions from graduate students, attending Department events and discussions to explore questions on research and graduate training. This course is open to new directions and incorporation of new topics and activities according to each new graduate cohort.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Directed Reading
courses.description: Course content variable; may be repeated. Special readings selected under guidance of individual instructor to help students make up particular gaps in their intellectual backgrounds that are pertinent to their graduate program.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Special seminar on research subjects of current interest.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Directed Reading and Research
courses.comments: May be repeated an indefinite number of times due to independent nature of course.
courses.description: An independent research or individually guided tutorial in an area not covered by existing courses.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Individual Study for Master's or Ph.D. Examinations for Advancement to Candidacy
courses.comments: May be repeated an indefinite number of times due to independent nature of course.
courses.description: Normally taken with the students committee chair in preparation for Masters or Ph.D. examinations. Units do not count toward graduate degrees.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Master's Research and Writing
courses.comments: May be repeated an indefinite number of times due to independent nature of course.
courses.description: Open to graduate students conduction masters research.

courses.subject: CH ST
courses.title: Dissertation Research and Writing
courses.prereq_text: Open to graduate students conducting doctoral thesis research.
courses.comments: May be repeated an indefinite number of times due to independent nature of thesis research and writing.
courses.description: Open to graduate students conducting doctoral research.

courses.subject: CH STW
courses.title: Introduction to Chicano/a Studies
courses.description: Introduction to the historical and contemporary development of the Chicano/a community. Course is interdisciplinary in nature. Focuses by quarter on A. history, B. gender, and C. culture.

courses.subject: CH STW
courses.title: Introduction to Chicano/a Studies
courses.description: This course explores contemporary Chicana/x cultural practices—from music, fashion, poster art, and murals to perspectives on social identities and sexualities. Focusing on culture, race, class, gender, and ideas of “home,” we examine how traditions and rituals reflect national and transnational politics. Drawing from Chicana/o Studies, Sound Studies, Feminist Studies, Art, and Media Studies, we analyze how communities use cultural practices to navigate, resist, and speak against injustice.

courses.subject: CH STW
courses.title: Maya History & Resistance
courses.comments: CH STW 116 is the online version of CH ST 116
courses.description: The course examines Maya History and Resistance in the Mayab’, or where the Maya live/are. It attempts to de-center the nation-state, while also recognizing the ways that governments have played a role in repressing Indigenous Peoples. The course analyzes the Maya through time and space, with each week focusing on a particular topic.

courses.subject: CH STW
courses.title: Chicana Writers
courses.prereq_text: Department approval required to finalize registration.
courses.comments: CH STW 184A is the online version of CH ST 184A.
courses.description: Examination of literary works by Chicana writers. Feminist theories as well as other contemporary critical theories are applied to the analysis of prose, poetry and dramatic works written by such authors as Sandra Cisneros, Ana Castillo, Helen Viramontes, and others.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: General Chemistry
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed CHEM 2A or CHEM 3A and the course may not be taken concurrently.
courses.description: Topics covered: atomic structure of matter; reaction stoichiometry; solution stoichiometry; gasses; quantum chemistry and the electronic structure of atoms; chemical bonding (molecular shapes, hybridization, and molecular orbital theory).

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: General Chemistry
courses.prereq_text: CHEM 1A, CHEM 2A or CHEM 3A with a minimum grade of C-.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed CHEM 2B or CHEM 3B, and the courses may not be taken concurrently.
courses.description: Topics covered: equilibrium; acids, bases, and buffers; thermochemistry (energy, enthalpy, entropy, and free energy); electrochemistry.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: General Chemistry
courses.prereq_text: CHEM 1B, CHEM 2B or CHEM 3B with a minimum grade of C-.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed CHEM 2C or CHEM 3C , and the courses may not be taken concurrently.
courses.description: Topics covered: kinetics; intermolecular forces, liquids and solids; properties of solutions; transition metals and coordination complexes; organic chemistry and polymers; nuclear chemistry.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: General Chemistry (Honors)
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed CHEM 1A or CHEM 3A and the courses may not be taken concurrently.
courses.description: The sequence of topics will be similar to that in Chemistry 1A. Calculus will be used as needed, at the level of the concurrent Mathematics 3A course.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: General Chemistry Lab (Part A)
courses.prereq_text: CHEM 1A, CHEM 2A, or CHEM 3A with a minimum grade of C-. Concurrent enrollment, or a grade of C- or higher in CHEM 1B, CHEM 2B, or CHEM 3B.
courses.comments: Lab fee required.
courses.description: Qualitative and quantitative measurements to develop laboratory techniques and demonstrate the basic concepts of stoichiometry, gas laws, atomic spectroscopy, chemical equilibrium, and acid-base chemistry.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: General Chemistry (Honors)
courses.prereq_text: CHEM 2A or CHEM 1A or CHEM 3A with a minimum grade of B.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed CHEM 1B or CHEM 3B and the courses may not be taken concurrently.
courses.description: Thermodynamics (first and second law), electrochemistry, chemical kinetics, atomic and molecular structure, and chemical bonding.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: General Chemistry Laboratory (Part B)
courses.prereq_text: CHEM 1B, CHEM 2B, or CHEM 3B with a minimum grade of C-. Concurrent enrollment, or a grade of C- or higher in CHEM 1C, CHEM 2C, or CHEM 3C. CHEM 2AL (may be taken concurrently).
courses.comments: Second half of general chemistry laboratory. Lab fee required.
courses.description: Qualitative and quantitative measurements to develop laboratory techniques and demonstrate the basic concepts of buffers, thermochemistry, electrochemistry, kinetics, and colligative properties.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: General Chemistry (Honors)
courses.prereq_text: CHEM 2B or CHEM 1B or CHEM 3B with a minimum grade of B.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have taken CHEM 1C or CHEM 3C and the courses may not be taken concurrently.
courses.description: Structure and dynamics of the elements and their compounds. Aspects of technology and environmental problems.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: General Chemistry (Majors)
courses.comments: Highly recommended and open only to Chemistry Pre-Majors and Chemical Engineering Majors. Not open for credit to students who have completed CHEM 1A or CHEM 2A.
courses.description: Topics covered: atomic structure of matter; reaction stoichiometry; solution stoichiometry; gasses; quantum chemistry and the electronic structure of atoms; chemical bonding (molecular shapes, hybridization, and molecular orbital theory). First quarter of general chemistry intended for Chemistry Pre-Majors and Chemical Engineering Majors and others requiring a strong basis in chemistry.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: General Chemistry (Majors)
courses.prereq_text: CHEM 1A, CHEM 2A, or CHEM 3A with a minimum grade of C-.
courses.comments: Highly recommended and open only to Chemistry Pre-Majors and Chemical Engineering Majors. Not open for credit to students who have completed CHEM 1B or CHEM 2B.
courses.description: Topics covered: equilibrium; acids, bases, and buffers; thermochemistry (energy, enthalpy, entropy, and free energy); electrochemistry.
