Second quarter of general chemistry intended for Chemistry Pre-Majors and Chemical Engineering Majors and others requiring a strong basis in chemistry.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: General Chemistry (Majors)
courses.prereq_text: CHEM 1B, CHEM 2B, or CHEM 3B with a minimum grade of C-.
courses.comments: Highly recommended and open only to Chemistry Pre-Majors and Chemical Engineering Majors. Not open for credit to students who have completed CHEM 1C or CHEM 2C.
courses.description: Topics covered: kinetics; intermolecular forces, liquids and solids; properties of solutions; transition metals and coordination complexes; organic chemistry and polymers; nuclear chemistry. Third quarter of general chemistry intended for Chemistry Pre-Majors and Chemical Engineering Majors and others requiring a strong basis in chemistry.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Introduction Into Advanced Laboratory Practices
courses.prereq_text: CHEM 1C, 2C, or 3C with a grade of C- or better; and CHEM 2AL and 2BL
courses.comments: Lab fee required.
courses.description: Qualitative and quantitative measurements to develop advanced laboratory techniques. Students will also develop science literacy skills by learning how to present experimental results and perform literature reviews. This course is intended for chemical science majors.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Laboratory Methods of Organic Chemistry
courses.prereq_text: Chemistry 1AL or 2AC, 1BL or 2BC, and 1CL or 2CC, or Chemistry 2AL and 2BL; 109A or 109AH or 130A with a minimum grade of a C-; and Chemistry 109B or 109BH or 130B (may be taken concurrently).
courses.description: Distillation, crystallization, extraction, determination of physical properties, spectroscopy, and instrumental methods in organic chemistry.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Laboratory Methods of Organic Chemistry (Independent Research)
courses.prereq_text: Chemistry 6AL and 109A or 109AH; and Chemistry 109B or 130B or 109BH (may be taken concurrently); open to chemistry, biochemistry and creative studies majors only; consent of instructor.
courses.description: Independent research involving distillation, crystallization, extraction, determination of physical properties, organic synthesis, and use of instrumental methods in organic chemistry.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Laboratory Methods of Organic Chemistry
courses.prereq_text: Chemistry 6AL and 109A or 109AH or 130A with a minimum grade of C-; and Chemistry 130B (can be taken concurrently) or Chemistry 109B or 109BH.
courses.description: Distillation, crystallization, extraction, determination of physical properties, organic synthesis, instrumental methods in organic chemistry.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Organic Chemistry Labs
courses.prereq_text: Chemistry 6BL or 6BH and 109B or 109BH; and Chemistry 109C or 130C or CHEM 109CH (may be taken concurrently); open to chemistry, biochemistry and creative studies majors only; consent of instructor.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Chemistry 7C. Lab fee required.
courses.description: Independent research involving distillation, crystallization, extraction, determination of physical properties, organic synthesis, and use of instrumental methods in organic chemistry for the purposes of multistep synthesis.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Organic Chemistry Labs
courses.prereq_text: Chemistry 6BL or 6BH and 109B or 109BH or 130B with a minimum grade of C-; and Chemistry 109C or 109CH or 130C (may be taken concurrently).
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Chemistry 7C. Lab fee required.
courses.description: Distillation, crystallization, extraction, determination of physical properties, organic synthesis, instrumental methods in organic chemistry.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Introductory Chemistry
courses.prereq_text: Not open to students who have completed Natural Science 1B or Chemistry 1A or Chemistry 2A. Cannot be taken concurrently with Chemistry 1A or Chemistry 2A.
courses.comments: Designed as a preparatory�course for Chemistry 1A. Intended for students with limited or no high school chemistry background, and/or students who received an SAT Math Score of 550 or below.
courses.description: Includes fundamental topics, such as matter, measurements, atomic/electronic structure, atomic theories, bonding, reactions, and stoichiometry.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Undergraduate Seminar
courses.description: Seminars for undergraduates presented by faculty, guest speakers, and/or students.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: SciTrek 2nd-12th Science Outreach
courses.description: This course allows students to earn 1 unit of credit for serving as a mentor in the SciTrek program, a 2nd -12th grade science outreach program. Students will receive activity specific training on working with elementary or secondary students and then implement that training in an elementary or secondary classroom.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Introduction to Research
courses.comments: May be repeated to a maximum of 6 units. Students are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
courses.description: Directed study, normally experimental, to be arranged with individual faculty members. Course offers exceptional students an opportunity to participate in a research group. Basic techniques and the operation of instruments used in research. A few students in chemistry are quite advanced having had extensive laboratory training in high school or elsewhere. This course allows them the opportunity to participate in a research group before they acquire 84 units and are then eligible for and capable of handling 199, Independent Studies.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Teaching Chemistry at the High School/Junior High Level
courses.comments: Upper Division course credit toward Science and Mathematics Education minor. Will not count towards the Biochemistry, Chemistry BA or Chemistry BS major requirements.
courses.description: Students will work to develop a high school/junior high curriculum unit. In addition, students will work in either a high school or junior high classroom and share their experiences through class discussions. Students will also have the opportunity to participate in one of two elementary outreach programs that are run out of the chemistry department.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: The Science and Engineering of Energy Conversion
courses.prereq_text: ChE 110A (or equivalent thermodynamics) and ChE 140A (or equivalent chemical kinetics); OR Chem 112A-B-C or Chem 113A-B-C; OR consent of instructor.
courses.comments: Equivalent upper-division coursework in thermodynamics and kinetics from outside of department will be considered. CHEM 104 and CH E 141 are the same course.
courses.description: Framework for understanding the energy supply issues facing society with a focus on the science, engineering, and economic principles of the major alternatives. Emphasis is on the physical and chemical fundamentals of energy conversion technologies.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Organic Chemistry
courses.prereq_text: Chemistry 1C or 2C or 3C with a minimum grade of C-; or Chemistry 1B or 2B or 3B with a minimum grade of B-.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Chemistry 109AH.
courses.description: Introduction to organic chemistry. Topics include acid/base chemistry, conformational analysis, stereoisomers, thermodynamics and kinetics, aromaticity and resonance, and multistep synthesis as well as the nomenclature, structure, reactivity, and mechanisms of alkenes, alkynes, and alkyl halides. Reaction mechanisms include electrophilic addition, substitution, and elimination reactions.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Organic Chemistry (H)
courses.prereq_text: Chemistry 1B/2B or 1C/2C with a minimum grade of B.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Chemistry 109A or 130A.
courses.description: Structure, nomenclature, stereochemistry, and reactivity of organic molecules. Suitable for undergraduates requiring strong understanding of organic chemistry and possessing strong background in science, such as honors students, majors in chemistry, biochemistry-chem, chemical engineering, etc. This course cannot be repeated.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Organic Chemistry
courses.prereq_text: Chemistry 130A, 109A or 109AH with a minimum grade of C-.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Chemistry 109BH.
courses.description: Structure, reactivity, mechanisms, synthesis, and nomenclature of organic molecules including alcohols, radicals, aldehydes, ketones, carboxylic acids and carboxylic acid derivatives, and aromatic rings. Other topics include organometallic compounds and reactions at the alpha carbon.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Organic Chemistry (H)
courses.prereq_text: Chemistry 109A with a minimum grade of B+ or Chemistry 109AH with a minimum grade of B.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Chemistry 109B or 130B.
courses.description: Structure, nomenclature, stereochemistry, and reactivity of organic molecules. Suitable for undergraduates requiring strong understanding of organic chemistry and possessing strong background in science, such as honors students, majors in chemistry, biochemistry-chem, chemical engineering, etc. This course cannot be repeated.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Organic Chemistry
courses.prereq_text: Chemistry 130B or 109B or 109BH with a minimum grade of C-.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed 109CH.
courses.description: Structure, reactivity and synthesis of organic molecules including nomenclature, reaction mechanisms, and stereochemistry. Topics include organometallics, polymers, carbohydrates, amino acids, proteins, nucleic acids, coenzymes and their mechanisms.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Organic Chemistry (H)
courses.prereq_text: Chemistry 109B with a minimum grade of B+ or Chemistry 109BH with a minimum grade of B.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Chemistry 109C or 130C.
courses.description: Structure, reactivity, mechanisms, synthesis, nomenclature, and spectroscopic identification of the principal classes of organic compounds as well as organometallics, amino acids, proteins, and carbohydrates. This course is intended for chemistry majors and others requiring a strong basis in organic chemistry.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Introductory Biochemistry Laboratory
courses.prereq_text: Chemistry 142A or Chemistry W 142A (may be taken concurrently).
courses.comments: Lab fee required.
courses.description: Gives students hands-on experience with modern methods of separation, identification, and study of biomolecules and macromolecular structures. Focus is on techniques but the course also gives an introduction to computer-based bioinformatics tools.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Chemical Kinetics
courses.description: The laws and theories governing rates of chemical reactions and reaction mechanisms. Empirical treatment of reaction rates, treatment of data, gas-phase reactions, reactions in solution, catalysis, complex reactions, chain reactions. Collision theory and potential energy surfaces.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Biophysical Chemistry
courses.prereq_text: Chemistry 1C or 2C or 3C; and, Mathematics 2A-B or 3A-B, and 6A; and, Physics 7A-B-C-L, or, Physics 1, 2, 3, 3L, 4, and 4L, or, Physics 6A-AL-B-BL-C-CL; Chemistry 142A, Chem W 142A or MCDB 108A (may be taken concurrently).
courses.description: Laws of thermodynamics, chemical equilibria and ligand binding, phase equilibria, electrochemistry, nonelectrolyte solutions, applications to biochemical problems.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Biophysical Chemistry
courses.prereq_text: Chemistry 112A; Chemistry 142A or Chemistry W 142A or MCDB 108A; Chemistry 142B or MCDB 108B (may be taken concurrently); Math 4A.
courses.comments: Not open to students who have completed Chemistry 113B
courses.description: Forces influencing macromolecular conformation, microscopy and diffraction methods, quantum mechanics, statistical mechanics.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Biophysical Chemistry
courses.prereq_text: Chemistry 112B; Chemistry 142B or MCDB 108B; Chemistry 142C or MCDB 108C (may be taken concurrently).
courses.comments: Not open to students who have completed Chemistry 113C.
courses.description: Biological spectroscopy, nuclear magnetic resonance, mass transport dynamics in solution, chemical and biochemical kinetics.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Biophysical and Bioanalytical Laboratory
courses.prereq_text: Chemistry 125L and Chemistry 142C (may be taken concurrently).
courses.comments: Lab fee required.
courses.description: Application of modern biophysical and bioanalytical techniques to study the structure, function, and properties of biomolecules. Fluorescence spectroscopy, mass spectroscopy, FTIR, 2D-NMR, diffraction techniques, circular dichroism.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Physical Chemistry
courses.prereq_text: Chemistry 1C or 2C; and, Mathematics 2A-B or 3A-B, and 6A; and, Physics 7A-B-C-L, or, Physics 1-2-3-3L-4-4L, or, Physics 6A-AL-B-BL-C-CL.
courses.comments: Not open to students who have completed Chemistry 112A.
courses.description: Chemical thermodynamics: laws of thermodynamics, phase equilibria, chemical equilibria, equations of state.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Physical Chemistry Laboratory
courses.description: Lecture: instrumental techniques, data analysis, error analysis, instruction in Mathematica-R. Laboratory: Mathematica-R, a symbolic programming language, is taught in the computer laboratory.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Physical Chemistry
courses.comments: Not open to students who have completed Chemistry 112B.
courses.description: Quantum theory and spectroscopy: introduction to quantum mechanics; symmetry, molecular structure, and spectroscopy.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Physical Chemistry
courses.comments: Not open to students who have completed Chemistry 112C.
courses.description: Kinetic theory of gases, chemical kinetics, statistical mechanics, photochemistry.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Electrochemistry
courses.comments: Not open to students who have completed CHEM 114AL or 214AL
courses.description: Theory and applications of electrochemistry. Thermodynamics and kinetics. Discussion of practical technologies, including batteries, fuel cells, electrolysis, electroplating, biosensors and/or other selected topics.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Fundamentals of Quantum Chemistry
courses.comments: Offered concurrently with Chemistry 222A-B-C.
courses.description: Introduction to quantum mechanics-postulatory approach; particle in box, on ring, harmonic oscillator; linear operator theory, matrix algebra; hydrogen atom; perturbation theory, variation theory; applications.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Fundamentals of Quantum Chemistry
courses.description: Molecular orbital theory and valence bond theory; Huckel theory (secular eqn.) applications to conjugated systems, electronic spectra, and term symbols; introduction to infrared, Raman, and microwave spectroscopy.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Fundamentals of Quantum Chemistry
courses.description: Introduction to NMR, EPR, group theory; and applications.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Quantitative Analytical and Physical Methods Laboratory
courses.comments: Lab fee required.
courses.description: Principles of analytical chemistry including spectroscopy, classical techniques and separation processes. Quantitative analysis of unknowns. Introduction to instrumental analysis.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Advanced Physical Chemistry Laboratory
courses.comments: Lab fee required.
courses.description: Experiments in thermodynamics, spectroscopy, and electrochemistry. Synthesis and study of inorganic complexes. Instrumental techniques such as NMR, fluorescence, Raman and laser flash photolysis are explored. Methods of data and error analysis.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Inorganic Synthesis and Physical Characterization Laboratory
courses.prereq_text: Chemistry 113C and 116BL; Chemistry 173A (may be taken concurrently).
courses.comments: Lab fee required.
courses.description: Synthesis of inorganic and organometallic complexes including techniques for air-sensitive materials. Instrumental characterization and study of synthesized compounds in a research-like setting.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Statistical Mechanics
courses.description: Fundamentals of statistical thermodynamics, partition functions for ideal gases and crystals, quantum statistics, calculations of thermodynamic properties.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Photochemistry and Radiation Chemistry
courses.description: Interaction of light and matter, reaction paths from electronically excited molecules, flash photolysis, high energy radiation.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Fundamentals of Environmental Chemistry
courses.description: Study of Earth's biogeochemical cycles with respect to carbon, nitrogen, and sulfur. Introduction to the science of climate change, including effects of global warming on terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems. Environmental impacts of fossil fuel and biofuel technologies. Chemistry of the atmosphere, hydrosphere, and lithosphere, with emphasis on ozone depletion, photochemical smog, acid rain, global ocean acidification, soil and groundwater contamination, and environmental costs of industrialized agriculture.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Organic Spectroscopic Analysis
courses.description: Structure determination of complex organic molecules. Topics covered include NMR, IR, UV, and mass spectrometry.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Laboratory Techniques in Biochemistry
courses.prereq_text: Chemistry 110L; and Chemistry 142A or Chemistry W 142A; and Chemistry 142B (may be taken concurrently).
courses.comments: Lab fee required.
courses.description: Application of molecular biology techniques to perform mutagenesis and cloning; restriction endonucleases, PCR, plasmid purification and DNA analysis. Protein purification and analysis methods: expression of proteins in bacterial systems.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Computation Chemistry and Molecular Modeling
courses.comments: Same course as EEMB 126MM.
courses.description: Introduction to computational chemistry and molecular modeling. Application of molecular mechanics, quantum mechanics and computer graphical interfaces to problems in chemistry, biochemistry, drug design and pharmacology.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Structure and Reactivity in Organic Chemistry
courses.description: Electronic structure, resonance, acid/base chemistry, thermodynamics, kinetics, transition state theory, and isotope effects.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Organic Reaction Mechanisms
courses.description: Mechanisms of thermal, photochemical, organometallic, electrochemical asymmetric or other processes in organic chemistry.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Synthetic Organic Reactions
courses.description: A survey of reactions of organic substances with emphasis on those with practical synthetic utility, including discussion of mechanism, scope and limitations, and steriochemical issues.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Organic Chemistry for Majors
courses.prereq_text: Chemistry 1C or 2C or 3C with a minimum grade of C-.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Chemistry 109A or 109AH.
courses.description: Introduction to organic chemistry. Topics include acid/base chemistry, conformational analysis, stereoisomers, thermodynamics and kinetics, aromaticity and resonance, and multistep synthesis as well as the nomenclature, structure, reactivity, and mechanisms of alkenes, alkynes, and alkyl halides. Reaction mechanisms include electrophilic addition, substitution, and elimination reactions. This course is intended for chemistry majors and others requiring a strong basis in organic chemistry.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Organic Chemistry for Majors
courses.prereq_text: Chemistry 130A, 109A or 109AH with a minimum grade of C-.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Chemistry 109B or 109BH.
courses.description: Structure, reactivity, mechanisms, synthesis, and nomenclature of organic molecules including alcohols, radicals, aldehydes, ketones, carboxylic acids and carboxylic acid derivatives, and aromatic rings. Other topics include organometallic compounds and reactions at the alpha carbon. This course is intended for chemistry majors and others requiring a strong basis in organic chemistry.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Organic Chemistry for Majors
courses.prereq_text: Chemistry 130B, 109B or 109BH with a minimum grade of C-.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed 109CH.
courses.description: Structure, reactivity, mechanisms, synthesis and nomenclature of organic molecules including aromatic heterocycles, carbohydrates, amino acids, proteins, nucleic acids, coenzymes, lipids, polymers, and their mechanisms. This course is intended for chemistry majors and others requiring a strong basis in organic chemistry.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Organometallics in Organic Synthesis
courses.description: Synthetic methods and applications to natural products total syntheses involving transition metals.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Advanced Synthetic Chemistry
courses.prereq_text: Chemistry 109A-B-C; upper-division standing; open to chemistry, biochemistry, and CCS chemistry and biochemistry majors only.
courses.description: A comprehensive discussion of modern synthetic organic methods, including the applications of addition, condensation, substitution, and rearrangement reactions for building complicated molecules from scratch.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Chemical Synthesis of Biological Molecules
courses.description: The synthesis, manipulation, and modification of biological molecules including peptides, carbohydrates, nucleic acids, and other metabolites are essential to advances in biomedicine. This course surveys chemical methods for the production of these molecules and their application to biological problems.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Epigenetics: Biology, Mechanisms and Therapies
courses.prereq_text: Chemistry W142A or 142A, 142B-C; or, MCDB 108A-B-C; upper-division standing.
courses.description: Covers epigenetic processes and molecular mechanisms in bacteria, fungi, plants, mammals, imprinting, gene regulation, repeat-induced point mutation (RIP), X-chromosome inactivation, epigenetic mechanisms including DNA methylation, histone modification, chromatin remodeling, RNA silencing, and epigentically based therapeutics and pharmaco-epigenetics.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Biochemistry
courses.prereq_text: Chemistry 107A-B-C or 109A or 109AH-109B or 109BH-109C or 109CH or W 109C
courses.description: Macromolecules of biological importance. A survey of the physical and chemical properties of proteins, nucleic acids, and carbohydrates. Methods of preparation, chemical synthesis, degradation, and characterization of biomolecules.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Biochemistry
courses.description: Chemical aspects of intermediary metabolism. The chemistry and elementary dynamic properties of enzymes; study of enzyme active sites; characterization of metabolic pathways and methods of examining cellular regulation.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Biochemistry
courses.description: Macromolecular biosynthesis and specialized cellular processes. A survey of nucleic acid and protein biosynthesis, characterization of lipids and membranes; function of membranes in transport, energy transduction, and cellular control; mechanisms of muscle contraction and cell motility.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: The RNA World
courses.description: Introduction to RNA structure and thermodynamics. Biological roles of RNA in contemporary organisms. Implications for the origins of life.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Computational Biochemistry
courses.prereq_text: Chemistry 113A-B or Chemistry 112A-B; and, Chemistry 142A or Chem W142A or MCDB 108A.
courses.comments: Offered concurrently with Chemistry 245 and BMB 245.
courses.description: Introduction to molecular modeling and molecular dynamics. Discussion of practical considerations of energy minimization, solvent modeling, structure-based drug design. Practical computer graphics experience.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Astrobiology and the Origins of Life
courses.prereq_text: Chemistry 142A or Chem W142A or MCDB 108A.
courses.description: Discusses the origins and evolution of the solar system and the earth, the origins and evolution of life on earth, and the possibilities for life elsewhere in the cosmos, all from the perspective of contemporary, terrain biochemistry.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: How Science Works
courses.comments: This course requires attendance/participation in a lab once (three to four hours) during three different weeks of the quarter.
courses.description: Combined lab and discussion course on how science works. Includes three labs on student-generated questions. Discussions include the analysis of research papers, science controversies, how science defines new areas of ignorance, and the observation of research group meetings.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Analytical Chemistry
courses.description: Principles of analytical chemistry including classical techniques, spectrophotochemistry, electroanalytical techniques, and separation processes.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Post-translational Protein Processing
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 108A or MCDB W 108A or CHEM 142A or CHEM W142A with a grade of C or better.
courses.comments: Same course as MCDB 145.
courses.description: Structure/function relationships in interesting macromolecules isolated from marine organisms. Focus is on well-characterized pathways from horseshoe crabs, abolones, mussels, and fish as well as others.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Advanced Analytical Techniques
courses.comments: Designed for graduating seniors.
courses.description: Principles of analytical methodology, as in spectroscopy, electroanalysis, and chromatography. Applications to environmental problems, forensic and clinical analysis, and industry. Analysis of solids and surfaces.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Enzyme Mechanisms
courses.description: Chemistry, structure and function of enzymes; theory, experimental design, and data analysis. Enzyme models and non-classical enzymes.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Drug Design
courses.description: Sources for new drugs. Biochemistry of diseases. Target validation techniques. Mechanism of action of enzymes and receptors. Enzyme inhibition and receptor binding studies. Structure based drug design: conformational analysis, docking and binding affinity calculations. Course also teaches proposal writing skills.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Drug Design
courses.description: Medical chemistry for lead optimization, combinatorial synthesis, quantitative structure-activity relationships, pharmocokinetics, drug metabolism and toxicity, pharmacogenomics. Drugs that interact with DNA and protein drugs. Clinical trials, intellectual property in drug design. Students develop their own drug design project.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Arrow Pushing in Organic Chemistry
courses.prereq_text: Chemistry 109A-B-C; upper-division standing; open to chemistry, biochemistry, and CCS chemistry and biochemistry majors only.
courses.description: Covers the arrow pushing formalism and addresses organic reactions from this perspective.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Bioinorganic Chemistry
courses.description: Selected topics in bioinorganic chemistry, and metallo-biochemistry. Discussions of metalloproteins and corresponding model compound investigations. Emphasis will be on reaction mechanisms and spectroscopy or properties of metal sites.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Structure Determination by X-ray Diffraction
courses.description: The use of x-ray and neutron scattering to characterize solid state materials. Subjects include the crystal unit cell, space groups, structure determination and refinement. It is recommended that the student have an elementary introduction to vectors, matrices and Fourier series

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Advanced Inorganic Chemistry
courses.description: Electronic structure of atoms and molecules. Models for bonding in molecules of nontransition and transition elements. Applications of symmetry to bonding, electronic and vibrational spectroscopy. Stereochemistry of transition metal complexes and introduction to organometallics.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Advanced Inorganic Chemistry
courses.description: Structures of ordered crystalline solids, X-Ray crystallography. Introduction to solid state chemistry, inorganic materials and chemical catalysis. Bioinorganic chemistry.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Physical-Inorganic Chemistry
courses.comments: Offered concurrently with Chemistry 275.
courses.description: Bonding theory, thermodynamics, and structure of inorganic compounds. Applications of physical techniques to the study of inorganic (and organometallic) reactions and their mechanisms.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Photochemical and Photophysical Properties of Inorganic and Organometallic Compounds and Materials
courses.comments: Offered concurrently with Chemistry 276.
courses.description: Discussion of the mechanisms of fundamental physical and chemical events which follow absorption of light by inorganic and organometallic chromophores. Consideration of homogeneous and heterogeneous systems as well as the design and operation of photo-optical and photoelectrical devices.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Protein Crystallography
courses.description: Introduction to diffraction techniques. Protein crystal growth and morphology. Data collection and reduction strategies. Approaches for solving the phase problem. Crystallographic refinement, including molecular dynamics. Interpretation of crystal structures.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Introduction to Teaching in Chemistry
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing, a chemistry grade point average of 3.5 or above and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 5 units. May not be applied toward the major.
courses.description: Students will assist the teaching assistant in teaching a lab course in which the student previously received a grade of A- or better. Activities will be determined in consultation with the instructor and include instruction of 1 or 2 lab sections per week. Undergraduates enrolled in Chem 183 are learning assistants (LAs) in the general chemistry laboratory. LAs teach and mentor first-year university students. LAs assist students with experiments, lab technique, data analysis, calculations, learning chemistry concepts, and problem solving. As the LAs learn STEM education pedagogy, they can practice what they learn as LAs in the chemistry lab.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Chemical Literature
courses.description: Lectures and exercises on the literature and other information resources of use in chemistry.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Organometallic Chemistry: Structure, Bonding, and Applications
courses.description: Synthesis, structure, and reactivity of organometallic complexes, with an emphasis on bonding and electronic structure. Homogeneous catalysis and small molecule activation, especially in the context of the energy conversion and storage, will also be discussed.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Honors Research Seminar
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; consent of instructor and department.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.5 GPA. No units may be applied to the major. An application must be completed and submitted to the undergrad advisor early in the first quarter of the senior year. Students successfully completing the program are eligible to graduate with Distinction in the Major.
courses.description: Independent research project carried out under the supervision of faculty member. Goal is to write an original, publishable, research paper. The project can be on a topic of the student's choice, or it can be an extension of an ongoing research project under the direction of a faculty member in the department.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Internship in Chemistry
courses.prereq_text: Chem 1AL, 1BL, 1CL, and consent of Chem instructor.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA. No units may be applied to the major. An application must be completed and submitted to the department chair.
courses.description: Opportunity to obtain practical non paid chemistry-related research and work experience by working under faculty and/or staff direction as an intern.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Teaching, Mentoring, or Research in K-12 STEM Education
courses.description: This course allows students to earn 1 unit per 32-40 hours of work in a given quarter with a K-12 science outreach program. Students will do one or more of the following activities with the program: mentor K-12 students, help with program operations, or help with research on the program.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.comments: Chem 196 may apply to major requirements by petition only.
courses.description: Special topics and courses as a means of meeting special curriculum needs.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Research in Chemical Education
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing in a physical science, life science, or engineering major.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters.
courses.description: Coursework shall consist of research in chemical education supervised by a faculty member. This course is not intended for internship credit.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Independent Studies
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing in the major; completion of two upper division courses in chemistry.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
courses.description: Coursework shall consist of academic research supervised by a faculty member. This course is not intended for internship credit.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Advanced Science and Engineering of Energy Conversion
courses.comments: Same course as Ch E 241.
courses.description: The course provides a framework for understanding the energy supply issues facing society with a focus on the science, engineering, and economic principles of the major alternatives. Emphasis will be on the physical and chemical fundamentals of energy conversion technologies.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Electrochemistry
courses.comments: Not open to students who have completed CHEM 114AL or 214AL
courses.description: Theory and applications of electrochemistry. Thermodynamics and kinetics. Discussion of practical technologies, including batteries, fuel cells, electrolysis, electroplating, biosensors and/or other selected topics.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Statistical Mechanics
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Chemistry 117A.
courses.description: Fundamentals of statistical thermodynamics, partition functions for ideal gases and crystals, quantum statistics, calculations of thermodynamic properties.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Statistical Mechanics
courses.description: Fundamentals of non-equilibrium statistical mechanics, kinetic theory of gases, Boltzmann equation, correlation functions, linear response theory, fluctuation-dissipation theorem, Langevin and Fokker-Planck equations.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Photochemistry and Radiation Chemistry
courses.prereq_text: Open only by consent of the chemistry graduate advisor.
courses.description: Interaction of light and matter, reaction paths from electonically excited molecules, flash photolysis, high energy radiation.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Selected Topics in Physical Chemistry
courses.comments: Course may be repeated with a different topic (18 units maximum).
courses.description: The content of this course will vary and will cover a range of topics and disciplines, including: orbital symmetry rules for chemical reactions; classical theory of light, radiation, and spectroscopy; electronic structure theory, catalysis, biophysics, and theoretical chemistry.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Fundamentals of Quantum Chemistry
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Chemistry 115A-B-C.
courses.description: Introduction to quantum mechanics-postulatory approach; particle in box, on ring, harmonic oscillator; lineral operator theory, matrix algebra; hydrogen atom; perturbation theory, variation theory; applications.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Fundamentals of Quantum Chemistry
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Chemistry 115A-B-C.
courses.description: Molecular Orbital theory and Valence Bond theory (Secular Equ.) applications to conjugated systems, electronic spectra, and term symbols; introduction to infrared, raman, and microwave spectroscopy.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Fundamentals of Quantum Chemistry
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Chemistry 115A-B-C.
courses.description: Introduction to NMR, EPR, group theory; applications.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Current Events in Organic Chemistry
courses.description: Faculty and students present and critically discuss current chemical literature.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Organic Spectroscopic Analysis
courses.description: Structure determination of complex organic molecules. Topics include NMR, IR, UV, and mass spectrometry.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Computational Chemistry
courses.description: Introduction to computational chemistry and molecular modeling. Applications of molecular mechanics, quantum mechanics, and computer graphical interfaces to problems in chemistry, biochemistry, drug design, and pharmacology.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Structure and Reactivity in Organic Chemistry
courses.description: Electronic structure, resonance, acid/base chemistry, thermodynamics, kinetics, transition state theory, and isotope effects.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Organic Reaction Mechanisms
courses.description: Mechanisms of thermal, photochemical, organometallic, electrochemical, asymmetric or other processes in organic chemistry.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Synthetic Organic Reactions
courses.description: A survey of reactions of organic substances with emphasis on those with practical synthetic utility, including discussion of mechanism, scope and limitations, and stereochemical issues.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Organometallics in Organic Synthesis
courses.comments: Designed for majors. Concurrently offered with 132. Quarters usually offered: Spring.
courses.description: Synthetic methods and applications to natural products total syntheses involving transition metals.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Chemical Synthesis of Biological Molecules
courses.description: The synthesis, manipulation, and modification of biological molecules including peptides, carbohydrates, nucleic acids, and other metabolites are essential to advances in biomedicine. This course surveys chemical methods for the production of these molecules and their application to biological problems.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Selected Topics in Organic Chemistry
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit providing letter designations are different. Only 18 units of total credit may apply to the major.
courses.description: Selected topics from organic chemistry. Contents of the course will vary.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Complex Molecule Synthesis
courses.comments: May be repeated provided topics are different. Only 18 units of total credit may apply to the major.
courses.description: Original contributions in the area of complex molecule total synthesis based on the most recent literature. Focus is on synthesis strategy and design, and any unusual chemistry transpired in the course of synthesis with complex substrates and intermediates.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Molecular Photoswitches: Chemistry, Properties and Applications
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit providing letter designations are different. Only 18 units of total credit may apply to the major.
courses.description: This course covers the emerging field of photoswitches and their applications in materials science and biology.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Methods for Asymmetric Synthesis
courses.comments: May be repeated provided topics are different. Only 18 units of total credit may apply to the major.
courses.description: Surveys synthetically useful methods for stereoselective organic synthesis. The general principles underlying these processes are discussed. Applications of these methods are then examined in the context of target oriented synthesis.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Carbohydrate Synthesis and Basic Glycobiology
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit providing letter designations are different. Only 18 units of total credit may apply to the major.
courses.description: Course topics include: Monosaccharide, oligosaccharides and polysaccharides – structure, biosynthesis and function; Chemical glycosylation: general synthetic approaches and the state-of-the-art stereoselective glycosylation; Chemoenzymatic glycan synthesis; Bioactive glycosylated nature products and examples of their synthesis; Glycomedicine and carbohydrate-based vaccines.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Epigenetics: Biology, Mechanisms and Therapies
courses.prereq_text: Chemistry W142A or 142A, 142B-C; or, MCDB 108A-B-C; graduate standing.
courses.description: Covers epigenetic processes and molecular mechanisms in bacteria, fungi, plants, mammals, imprinting, gene regulation, repeat-induced point mutation (RIP), X-chromosome inactivation, epigenetic mechanisms including DNA methylation, histone modification, chromatin remodeling, RNA silencing, and epigentically based therapeutics and pharmaco-epigenetics.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Chemical Aspects of Biological Systems
courses.prereq_text: Open only by consent of the chemistry graduate advisor.
courses.description: Macromolecules of biological importance. A survey of the physical and chemical properties of proteins, nucleic acids, and carbohydrates. Methods of preparation, chemical synthesis, degradation, and characterization of biomolecules.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Chemical Aspects of Biological Systems
courses.description: Chemical aspects of intermediary metabolism. The chemistry and elementary dynamic properties of enzymes; study of enzyme active sites; characterization of metabolic pathways and methods of examining cellular regulation.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Chemical Aspects of Biological Systems
courses.description: Macromolecular biosynthesis and specialized cellular processes. A survey of nucleic acid and protein biosynthesis, characterization of lipids and membranes; function of membranes in transport, energy transduction, and cellular control; mechanisms of muscle contraction and cell motility; neurochemistry.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: The RNA World
courses.description: Introduction to RNA structure and thermodynamics. Biological roles of RNA in contemporary organisms. Implications for the origins of life.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Informational Macro- and Supra-Molecules
courses.comments: Same course as BMSE 244.
courses.description: Selected topics at the interface of chemistry and biology; informational molecular coding, molecular machines, self-assembling and self-replicating molecular systems, evolution and selection of molecules with binding and catalytic properties, biopolymer-based materials, special emphasis on cutting-edge technologies.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Computational Biochemistry
courses.comments: CHEM 245 and IQB 245 are the same course.
courses.description: Introduction to molecular modeling and molecular dynamics. Discussion of practical considerations of energy minimization, solvent modeling, structure-based drug design. Practical computer graphics experience.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Membrane Biochemistry
courses.comments: Same course as BMSE 246
courses.description: Introduction to the structures and roles of lipids an their behavior, liposomes, membrane proteins and kinetics, protein sorting, and signal transduction.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Strategy in Organic Synthesis and Methodology
courses.description: The design, development, presentation, and organization of new concepts for organic synthesis and methodologies is an essential skill for graduate students. Course focuses on advances in these areas and developing skills for writing and presenting research proposals.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Selected Topics in Biological Chemistry
courses.comments: CHEM 259 and IQB 259 are the same course.
courses.description: Selected topics from bio-organic, biophysical, or biological chemistry. The content of this course will vary.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Stimuli-Responsive Materials for Biomedical Applications
courses.description: Stimuli-responsive chemistries and materials are programmed to react in the presence of changes in their surrounding environment to produce a measurable output, such as a change in shape, release of active moiety, assembly, or mechanical output. Examples of stimuli can include electric field, magnetic, thermal, light,** mechanical, pH, ROS, enzyme, glucose, and others (e.g. salts, solvents, electron beam). We will discuss the properties, design, and applications of these stimuli-responsive materials that have aided the development of active-, as opposed to passive, biomaterials for the advancement of biomedicine. This course makes use of modern scientific literature to discuss the topics at hand.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Bioenergetics
courses.comments: Same course as BMSE 259.
courses.description: The study of biological energy transduction, with emphasis on physical constraints, raw materials, mechanisms, and evolution of metabolism.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Emerging Methods and Applications of Cryogenic Three-Dimensional Transmission Electron Microscopy
courses.description: Course covers the fundamentals and current state of the art of 3D cryogenic electron microscopy, the theory and a diverse set of applications: 3D single particle methods, correlative light and electron microscopy & cryogenic in situ tomography; provides a solid foundation for 3D cryo-EM and an opportunity to network with the cryo-EM community; features lecturers and renowned leaders in the field presenting their work, interactive and practical exercises: basic sample handling, sample preparation protocols & an introduction to computational analysis on a preselected dataset. Course requirements: reading classic and/or representative papers, presenting papers prior to respective lectures and a final written report on a chosen cryo-EM topic.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: ENZYME, COENZYME & METABOLIC PATHWAYS
courses.comments: Same course as BMSE 259.
courses.description: This course reviews the latest discoveries in biochemistry, including new enzymatic functions, cofactor biosynthesis, and metabolic pathways for secondary metabolites. Students with a strong background in organic chemistry and a keen interest in biochemistry are encouraged to take this course.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Gene Therapy
courses.comments: Same course as BMSE 259.
courses.description: The field of gene therapy is inherently interdisciplinary, drawing on concepts and tools from molecular biology, biochemistry, materials science, chemical engineering, and synthetic biology. This course will delve into a wide array of topics at the intersection of the aforementioned disciplines, including gene delivery, reporter gene imaging, viral and non-viral vectors, genetic editing, metabolic disease, clinical trial design, FDA-approved gene therapies, and the social/ethical considerations surrounding gene therapy.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Epigenetics
courses.comments: Same course as BMSE 259.
courses.description: Covers epigenetic processes and molecular mechanisms in bacteria, fungi, plants and mammals. Topics include: Epigenetic processes - Parental and maternal imprinting, Gene regulation, Repeat-induced point mutation, X-chromosome inactivation Epigenetic mechanisms - DNA methylation/histone modification/chromatin remodeling, RNA silencing, Methods of detection including patterns of DNA methylation Applications - Epigentically based therapeutics, Pharmaco-epigenetics

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Enzyme Mechanisms
courses.description: Chemistry, structure, and function of enzymes; theory, experimental design,and data analysis. Enzyme models and non-classical enzymes.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Drug Design
courses.description: Sources for new drugs. Biochemistry of diseases. Target validation techniques. Mechanism of action of enzymes and receptors. Enzyme inhibition and receptor binding studies. Structure base drug design: conformational analysis, docking and binding affinity calculations. Course also teaches proposal writing skills.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Drug Design
courses.description: Medicinal chemistry for lead optimization, combinatorial synthesis, quantitative structure-activity relationships, pharmacokinetics, drug metabolism and toxicity, pharmacogenomics. Drugs that interact with DNA and Protein drugs. Clinical trials, intellectual property in drug design. Students develop their own drug design project.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Arrow Pushing in Organic Chemistry
courses.description: Covers the arrow pushing fomulasism and addresses molecular rearrangements and other organic reactions from this perspective.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Advanced Catalysis
courses.description: Theories of reaction rates. Heterogeneous and homogenous catalysis, including physical structure and characterization of catalysts. Catalyst poisoning.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Photophysics and Device Science of Organic Materials
courses.description: Examination of what happens when organic molecules absorb a photon or when they are incorporated within an optoelectric device. Specific subjects include phtoexcitation and relaxation processes, energy transfer, flourescence depolarization, the design of flourescence-based biosensors, organic light emitting diodes and field effect transistors.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Advanced Inorganic Chemistry
courses.prereq_text: Consent of the chemistry graduate advisor.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Chemistry 173A, or 272A.
courses.description: Electronic structure of atoms and molecules. Models for bonding in molecules of nontransition and transition elements. Applications of symmetry to bonding, electronic and vibrational spectroscopy. Stereochemistry of transition metal complexes and introduction to organo- metallics.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Advanced Inorganic Chemistry
courses.prereq_text: Consent of the chemistry graduate advisor.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Chemistry 173B or 272B.
courses.description: Structures of ordered crystalline solids, x-ray crystallography. Introduction to solid state chemistry, inorganic materials and chemical catalysis. Bioinorganic chemistry.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Bioinorganic Chemistry
courses.description: Selected topics in bioinorganic chemistry and metal-lobiochemistry with a major focus on recent developments. Topics will include discussions of metalloproteins and corresponding model compound investigations. Emphasis will be on reaction mechanisms and spectroscopic properties of metal sites.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Synthesis and Properties of Macromolecules
courses.description: Basics of preparation of polymer and macromolecular assemblies, and characterization of large molecules and assemblies. Discussion of chemical structure, bonding, and reactivity.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Reaction Mechanisms in Organometallic and Inorganic Chemistry
courses.description: Discussion of chemical reaction mechanisms. Emphasis will be on fundamental reactions of metal compounds such as substitution, addition, elimination, and redox reactions for homogenous catalysis mechanisms and other complex systems.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Structural Inorganic Chemistry
courses.comments: Same course as Materials 241.
courses.description: The use of x-ray and neutron scattering to characterize solid state materials. Subjects include the crystal unit cell, space groups, structure determination and refinement. It is recommended that the student have an elementary introduction to vectors, matrices and fourier series.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Solid State Inorganic/Materials
courses.comments: Same course as Materials 274.
courses.description: An introductory course describing the synthesis, physical characterization, structure, electronic properties and uses of solid state materials.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Physical-Inorganic Chemistry
courses.description: Bonding theory, thermodynamics, and structure of inorganic compounds. Applications of physical techniques to the study of inorganic (and organometallic) reactions and their mechanisms.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Photochemical and Photophysical Properties of Inorganic and Organometallic Compounds and Materials
courses.description: Discussion of the mechanics of fundamental physical and chemical events which follow absorption of light by inorganic or organometallic chromophores. Consideration of homogeneous and heterogeneous systems as well as the design and operation of photo-optical and photoelectrical devices.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Introduction to Inorganic Materials
courses.comments: Same course as Materials 218.
courses.description: Structures of inorganic materials: close-packing, linking of simple polyhedra. Factors that control structure: ionic radii, covalency, ligand field effects, metal-metal bonding, electron/ atom ratios. Structure-property relationships in e.g. spinels, garnets, perovskites, rutiles, flourites, zeolites, b-aluminas, graphites, common inorganic glasses.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Selected Topics in Inorganic Chemistry
courses.description: This course is designed to reflect recent developments in inorganic chemistry.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Nuclear and Radiochemistry
courses.description: Radioactive decay kinetics and energetics, nuclear models, nuclear reactions, radiation detection, radiochemical techniques, and applications of radioactivity.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Sustainability (with a Chemistry Emphasis)
courses.description: This course will address and identify a number of issues in sustainability that are challenging a sustainable world and the potential research and technical opportunities for addressing these. Topics include: Climate Change—causes and effects; Environmental Monitoring; Energy – production and storage; Chemical resources - challenges and solutions; Recycling; Sustainable Materials; Research and Development Opportunities; Intellectual Property and Innovation.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Protein Crystallography
courses.description: Introduction to diffraction techniques. protein crystal growth and morphology. Data collection and reduction strategies. Approaches for solving the phase problem. Crystallographic refinement, including molecular dynamics. Interpretation of crystal structures.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Synthesis and Bonding of Small Conjugated Molecules
courses.description: Examination of small organic molecules used in optoelectronic devices: film transistors; light emitting diodes and solar cells. Methods for their synthesis. Influence of molecular structure on energies of molecular orbitals. Development of structure/function relationships based on solid state arrangements.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Instrumental Methods in Materials Chemistry
courses.description: Principles and practice of advanced research instrumentation for soft materials characterization including spectroscopy, microscopy, and X-ray techniques

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Chemical Literature
courses.comments: Does not count toward core academic units for the Chemistry PhD program.
courses.description: Lectures and exercises on the literature and other information resources of use in chemistry.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Organometallic Chemistry: Structure, Bonding, and Applications
courses.description: Synthesis, structure, and reactivity of organometallic complexes, with an emphasis on bonding and electronic structure. Homogeneous catalysis and small molecule activation, especially in the context of the energy conversion and storage, will also be discussed. Graduate students will be required to demonstrate a deeper understanding of the course material during class discussions and in submitted work. Graduate students will additionally be graded separately on all course work, including exams.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Seminar in Chemistry and Biochemistry
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit.
courses.description: Presentation of seminar required of all departmental graduate students.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Special Seminar in Chemistry
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit.
courses.description: Specialized seminar topics.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Faculty Research Seminar
courses.description: A series of seminars by departmental faculty describ ing their active research projects.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Techniques of Teaching
courses.description: Weekly discussion to cover topics concerning class management, student engagement, supervising experiments and safety (if applicable), leading discussions, advising, and grading.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Techniques of Teaching and Laboratory Class Supervision
courses.comments: S/U grade.
courses.description: An initial two-three day workshop is followed by weekly discussion. Topics covered: laboratory organization, supervising experiments, safety, presentations, leading discussions, writing quizzes, advising, and grading. Aimed at new teaching assistants.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Techniques of Teaching and Laboratory Class Supervision
courses.comments: S/U grade.
courses.description: An initial two-three day workshop is followed by weekly discussion. Topics covered: laboratory organization, supervising experiments, safety, presentations, leading discussions, writing quizzes, advising, and grading. Aimed at new teaching assistants.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Organic Chemistry Techniques of Teaching and Laboratory Class Supervision
courses.description: Weekly discussion to cover topics concerning class management, student engagement, supervising experiments and safety, leading discussions, advising, and grading in the organic chemistry laboratory.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Organic Chemistry Techniques of Teaching and Laboratory Class Supervision
courses.comments: S/U grade.
courses.description: An initial two-three day workshop is followed by weekly discussion. Topics covered: laboratory organization, supervising experiments, safety, presentations, leading discussions, writing quizzes, advising, and grading. Aimed at new teaching assistants in Organic Chemistry.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Organic Chemistry Techniques of Teaching and Laboratory Class Supervision
courses.comments: S/U grade.
courses.description: An initial two-three day workshop is followed by weekly discussion. Topics covered: laboratory organization, supervising experiments, safety, presentations, leading discussions, writing quizzes, advising, and grading. Aimed at new teaching assistants in Organic Chemistry.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Group Studies
courses.description: Critical review of research in selected fields. Regular meetings are held in which the student presents for discussion information from the recent chemical literature.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Directed Reading and Research
courses.comments: No more than half the units necessary for the master's degree may be taken in Chemistry 596. Same course as BMB 596.
courses.description: Individual tutorial. Instructor is usually the student's major research advisor. Each faculty member has a unique number designation.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Individual Study for Master's Comprehensive Examinations and Ph.D. Examinations.
courses.comments: No unit credit allowed toward advanced degree(s).
courses.description: Instructor should be the student's major professor or chairman of the doctoral committee.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Master's Thesis Research and Preparation
courses.comments: No unit credit will be given.
courses.description: Only for research underlying the thesis, writing the thesis. Instructor should be the chairman of the student's thesis committee.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Ph.D. Dissertation Research and Preparation
courses.description: Only for research underlying the dissertation, writing the dissertation. Instructor should be the chair of the student's doctoral committee.

courses.subject: CHEM CS
courses.title: CCS General Chemistry
courses.prereq_text: Consent of instructor required for non-majors.
courses.description: The sequence of topics will be similar to that in Chemistry 1A. Calculus will be used as needed, at the level of the concurrent MATH 3A course.

courses.subject: CHEM CS
courses.title: CCS General Chemistry
courses.prereq_text: Consent of instructor for non-majors. CHEM 1A or CHEM 2A, or a Pass with a minimum of 3.0 units earned in CHEM CS 11A.
courses.description: The sequence of topics will be similar to that in Chemistry 1B. Calculus will be used as needed, at the level of the concurrent MATH 3B course.

courses.subject: CHEM CS
courses.title: CCS General Chemistry
courses.prereq_text: Consent of instructor for non-majors. CHEM 1B or CHEM 2B, or a Pass with a minimum of 3.0 units earned in CHEM CS 11B.
courses.description: The sequence of topics will be similar to that in Chemistry 1C. Calculus will be used as needed, at the level of preceding MATH 3A and 3B courses.

courses.subject: CHEM CS
courses.title: Independent Studies
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit. Creative Studies students may enroll in a maximum of 24 units of Independent Studies courses per year, with a maximum of 45 units counted toward graduation.
courses.description: Serious independent study in chemistry with consenting faculty member.

courses.subject: CHEM W
courses.title: Organic Chemistry
courses.prereq_text: Chemistry 130B or 109B or 109BH with a minimum grade of C-.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed 109CH or 109C (CHEM W 109C is the online version of CHEM 109C).
courses.description: An online class that studies the structure, reactivity, mechanisms, synthesis and nomenclature of organic molecules including aromatic heterocycles, carbohydrates, amino acids, proteins, nucleic acids, coenzymes, lipids, polymers, and their mechanisms.

courses.subject: CHEM W
courses.title: Biochemistry
courses.prereq_text: Chemistry 107A-B-C or 109A or 109AH-109B or 109BH-109C or 109CH or W 109C
courses.description: Macromolecules of biological importance. A survey of the physical and chemical properties of proteins, nucleic acids, and carbohydrates. Methods of preparation, chemical synthesis, degradation, and characterization of biomolecules.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Elementary Modern Chinese
courses.description: The beginning course in Chinese. The student acquires a basic knowledge of the grammar, a limited general vocabulary, correct pronunciation, and an ability to read and understand simple texts. Weekly laboratory assignments support and enhance classroom learning.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: First Year Chinese Heritage
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Chinese 1N.
courses.description: Intended for Chinese heritage speakers who wish to learn to read and write Chinese. Content is similar to Chinese 1 with less emphasis on developing oral skills.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Elementary Modern Chinese
courses.description: Continuation of Chinese 1.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: First Year Chinese Heritage
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Chinese 2N.
courses.description: Continuation of Chinese 1NH.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Elementary Modern Chinese
courses.description: Continuation of Chinese 2.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: First Year Chinese Heritage
courses.comments: Not open to students who have completed Chinese 3N.
courses.description: Continuation of Chinese 2NH.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Intermediate Modern Chinese
courses.description: Continuation of Chinese 3.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Second Year Chinese Heritage
courses.description: Continuation of Chinese 3NH.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Intermediate Modern Chinese
courses.description: Continuation of Chinese 4.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Second Year Chinese Heritage
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Chinese 5N.
courses.description: Continuation of Chinese 4NH.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Intermediate Modern Chinese
courses.description: Continuation of Chinese 5.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Contemporary Chinese Religions
courses.comments: Chinese 32 and Religious Studies 32 are the same course.
courses.description: Examines Chinese popular religion, Daoism, Buddhism, Confucianism, Christianity, and Islam as shaped and transformed by revolution and nationalism, and the recent rapid commercialization, urbanization, and globalization of China. Religiosity and changing notions of self, family, gender, community, and citizenship.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Popular Culture in Modern Chinese Societies
courses.description: Provides an overview of Chinese popular culture from PRC, Taiwan, and Hong Kong, covering various media and genres such as popular literature, film, online culture, music, video games, and cartoons.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Introduction to Chinese Medicine
courses.comments: Religious Studies 41 and Chinese 41 are the same course.
courses.description: Looks at major concepts and practices that inform the plural traditions of Chinese medicine. Also considers the cultural and historical contexts in which these therapeutic traditions emerged as well as, briefly, their relation to other medical systems in Asia.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Global Yoga
courses.comments: Religious Studies 42 and Chinese 42 are the same course.
courses.description: This course examines the complex, transcultural, and entangled history of the contemporary global yoga phenomenon. It sheds light on the connection between modern transnational yoga and various posture-based systems of self-cultivation from Asia (India, Tibet, China) to Europe. It also considers the basic features of primarily physical modes of spiritual refinement.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Nature and Ethics in Chinese Philosophy
courses.comments: Religious Studies 48 and Chinese 48 are the same course.
courses.description: A look at how major thinkers in classical Chinese thought grappled with questions related to the individual's place in society and their relationship to their environment. Highlighting their relevance, classical views will be applied to contemporary ethical, social, and environmental debates.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Masterpieces in Chinese Literature
courses.description: Examines a selection of works from Chinese literature, with the goal of understanding the major genres and their development over time. The cultural roles of literature, as well as criteria for critical evaluation, are also addressed.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Modern Chinese Literature
courses.comments: Chinese 82 and Comparative Literature 82 are the same course.
courses.description: This course, taught in English, surveys an archive of seminal short fiction, novellas, novels, and poems that tell the story of China and the Chinese from the end of the Qing dynasty to the present. What has been the place of literature in China in the modern era? What vision of modern China do we find in its literature? How, moreover, does literature subvert the national narrative? Through literature as a window on the history of modern China, students gain a better understanding of Chinese history and culture with regard to its social reform, revolution, war, cultural revolution, cultural revival, and economic growth.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Topics on China
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit providing letter designations are different
courses.description: Introduction to an aspect of China i.e., culture, history. Contact Department of East Asian Languages and Culture for the specific topic.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Independent Study in Chinese
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA. Limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
courses.description: Introduction to independent research in Chinese. Topic and content are decided by the supervising Professor in the Department of East Asian Languages and Cultural Studies.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Introduction to Classical Chinese
courses.description: The grammar and vocabulary of classical Chinese. Readings concentrate on philosophical and historical works from the pre-Han period, with some selections from later prose and poetry. Students with some familiarity with Chinese characters (through another Asian language) but not modern Chinese will be accommodated.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Introduction to Classical Chinese
courses.description: The grammar and vocabulary of classical Chinese. Readings concentrate on philosophical and historical works from the Pre-Han period, with some selections from later prose and poetry. Students with some familiarity with Chinese characters (through another Asian language) but not modern Chinese will be accommodated.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Reading and Writing in Chinese
courses.description: Designed to enhance reading and writing skills in Chinese for students who have finished second year Chinese.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Chinese Media: Chinese Conversation on Film and TV
courses.description: Designed to enable students to master advanced-level Chinese language structures, expressive styles, and conventions of communication through topics that reflect multiple aspects of society and culture. Materials will be drawn from various authentic multimedia, including TV shows, videos, movies, film clips and documentary films in different linguistic registers.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Third-Year Chinese I
courses.description: Advanced practice in grammar and composition.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Third-Year Chinese II
courses.description: Advanced practice in grammar and composition.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Third-Year Chinese III
courses.description: Advanced practice in grammar and composition.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Readings in Modern Chinese Literature
courses.description: Advanced readings in the Chinese language in fiction, drama, and poetry written after 1919. Designed for students with advanced Chinese background.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Readings in Taiwan Literature
courses.description: Offers a close reading of postwar Taiwan and exile literature from the 1940s to the present, and provides a basic introduction to literary criticism and analysis. Taught in English, the assigned texts are in traditional Chinese and English translations will be provided.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Readings in Taiwan Literature
courses.description: Offers an in-depth study of Taiwans nativist literature from select authors and provides a basic introduction to literary criticism and analysis. Examines the motifs and visual expression in the readings and how these texts contributed to the distinct Taiwanese cultural identity. Taught in English, the assigned texts are in traditional Chinese and English translations will be provided.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Advanced Chinese in Practice I
courses.comments: Heritage and high-proficiency Chinese language students can contact the instructor for approval to enroll.
courses.description: Course series for students who have advanced levels in Chinese. Extensive reading and discussion of various styles and practices of the Chinese language in addition to topics on modern and contemporary China. Teaching materials from literary works, newspapers, internet, and films.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Advanced Chinese in Practice II
courses.comments: Heritage and high-proficiency Chinese language students can contact the instructor for approval to enroll.
courses.description: Course series for students who have advanced levels in Chinese. Extensive reading and discussion of various styles and practices of the Chinese language in addition to topics on modern and contemporary China. Teaching materials from literary works, newspapers, internet, and films.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Advanced Chinese in Practice III
courses.comments: Heritage and high-proficiency Chinese language students can contact the instructor for approval to enroll.
courses.description: Course series for students who have advanced levels in Chinese. Extensive reading and discussion of various styles and practices of the Chinese language in addition to topics on modern and contemporary China. Teaching materials from newspaper, internet, and films.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Chinese Painting I
courses.comments: CHIN 134CA and ARTHI 134CA are the same course.
courses.description: Chinese painting and theory, from beginnings through the fourteenth century. Introduction to major developments and masters in their cultural context with a focus on meaning and agency.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Art and Modern China
courses.comments: ARTHI 134D is the same course as CHIN 134D.
courses.description: An exploration of trends and issues in nineteenth and twentieth-century Chinese art, as China awakens and responds to the challenges of modernity and the West. Topics include the continuity of tradition, the exile of identity, and the trends after Tiananmen (1989)

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Chinese Calligraphy- History and Aesthetics
courses.description: Examines the different scripts in historical context, surveys significant movements and artists, and considers the ideas, theories and aesthetic principles that have enriched the art of writing to elite status in China.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Special Topics in Taiwan Studies - Humanities
courses.description: Special topics in Taiwan studies with respect to literature, history, and culture from the period of Japanese rule (1895-1945) to the present, including modernity, national identity, intellectual movements, and popular culture. Topics and reads will vary with instructors.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Special Topics in Taiwan Studies - Social Science
courses.description: Special topics in Taiwan studies with respect to historical, economic, political, cultural, and social changes in Taiwan from the period of Japanese rule (1895-1945) to the present. Topics and readings will vary with instructors.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: China in Translation: Theory, Art, History
courses.comments: CHIN 139 and C LIT 139 are the same course.
courses.description: Uses case studies of translations into and out of China--long regarded as a civilization distinct from the West--to explore themes in translation studies. Topics include ideograms, orientalism, modernization, world literature, annotation, musicality, poetic license, and adaptation.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Tang Literary History
courses.description: Examines the history of literature during the celebrated Tang dynasty (618907). Focus on changes in literary norms, practices, and theory as they intersected with societal, political, intellectual, and religious developments. Also considers problems of historiography. Emphasis varies by quarter.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Urban Legends: Traditional Chinese Stories and Their Afterlives
courses.description: Masterworks of fiction from the Ming and Qing periods as products of urban culture in late imperial and contemporary China. Stories by Feng Menglong, Li Yu, tales by Pu Songling, and excerpts from classic novels.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Women Writers of Late Imperial China
courses.description: A study of Chinese women writers in the late imperial period (roughly 1500-1900), a newly rediscovered part of China's literary history. Examination of their personal lives and writings in relation to the Chinese literary tradition, women's history and feminist criticism.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Poetic Culture in late Imperial China and Beyond
courses.description: An examination of the role poetry played in both social and individual lives in late imperial China, with particular attention to self-expression and literary community. Relevant practices in later times and in Japan and Korea are also covered.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Storytelling and Chinese Culture
courses.prereq_text: Reading knowledge and skills in advanced modern Chinese
courses.description: Taught in Chinese, this course is designed to elucidate Chinese history and culture from the perspective of storytelling. Readings are original narrative texts from the Tang, Song, and Ming-Qing eras.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: History of Sexuality in China
courses.description: Examines the role of gender and sexual relations in the development of politics, society, culture, and personal life in China and the Sinophone world.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Queer China, Crip China
