courses.description: In this course we study the representation of non-normative bodyminds and desires (e.g. disability and homosexuality) in modern Chinese literature and film. We discuss the meanings embedded in Chinese discourses of gender, sexuality, and disability; investigate how these discourses have been appropriated in the construction of a modern Chinese national identity; and connect our specific inquiry into Queer China and Crip China to our general attempt to answer the broader question of how the modern nation-state China has been imagined into being over the past century. Our approach is interdisciplinary, comparative, and transnational.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Taiwan Cinema
courses.description: Explores Taiwan cinema in socio-political contexts. Emphasis on the creation of a cinematic experience that resonates globally while reflecting Taiwans unique identity, cultural heritage, and artistic vision. Specific themes or topics will vary depending on the instructor.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Fiction and Film in Contemporary China
courses.description: Presents a critical historical overview of Chinese literature and film from 1949 to the present. In addition to writers and filmmakers from mainland China such as Mo Yan and Zhang Yimou, course considers literary and cinematic development from Hong Kong, Taiwan, and the Chinese diaspora.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Chinese Cinema: Nationalism and Globalism
courses.prereq_text: upper division standing or instructor approval
courses.description: A critical overview of some of the major cinematic trends in Chinese-language film over the past several decades. Works from the PRC, Taiwan and Hong Kong, as well as Chinese cinema will be considered in a global context.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Special Topics in Chinese Studies
courses.description: Special topics in Chinese Studies. Course content varies.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Chinese Media: Chinese Conversation on Film and TV
courses.description: Designed to enable students to master advanced-level Chinese language structures, expressive styles, and conventions of communication through topics that reflect multiple aspects of society and culture. Materials will be drawn from various authentic multimedia, including TV shows, videos, movies, film clips and documentary films in different linguistic registers.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Religious Practice and the State in China
courses.comments: Same course as Religious Studies 183B.
courses.description: Historical and anthropological approaches to the interaction between religious practice and state forces, with emphasis on popular religion and the decline and revival of religion in Chinese modernity.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Qing Empire
courses.prereq_text: A prior course in History or upper-division standing.
courses.comments: HIST 185A and CHIN 185A are the same course.
courses.description: The Qing period saw the doubling of China's territory, the enormous population growth, and the many encounters with the West. We will examine the politics, cultures, social norms, and different peoples, with a focus on the problem of modernization.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Modern China (since 1911)
courses.prereq_text: Any lower-division course in History or upper-division standing.
courses.comments: Same course as History 185B.
courses.description: The fall of the dynastic system, the revolution against traditional values, the rise of the Nationalist Party, the challenge from the Communists, the founding of the People's Republic, and the Post-Mao reform, with a focus on the theme of revolution.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Undergrad Research Seminar on Modern China
courses.prereq_text: History 185A or 185B or Chin 185A or Chin 185B or HIST 185CQ or CHIN 185CQ and upper division standing.
courses.description: Research seminar in the history of modern China. Students will conduct historical research in a seminar context, using both primary and secondary source materials, to produce an original and substantial research paper.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: History of Modern Chinese Thought
courses.prereq_text: HIST 2A-B-C or HIST 80 or HIST/CHIN 184A-B or HIST/CHIN 185A-B or EACS 4A-B
courses.comments: HIST 185T is the same course as CHIN 185T.
courses.description: Leads students to understand some of the most important ideas, theories, and concepts in Modern China.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: History of Women in China: From the Ancient Period to the Nineteenth Century
courses.description: Exploration of the diverse roles women have played in Chinese culture and society up to the 19th century by examining the many contexts within which women operated: the family, the imperial court, literati and popular culture.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Senior Honors Project
courses.prereq_text: Open to senior majors only; consent of instructor.
courses.comments: Students must have a 3.0 overall grade-point average and a 3.5 grade-point average in the major.
courses.description: An independent study course (1 to 3 quarters) directed by a faculty member with a carefully chosen topic and bibliography which will result in a documented project or a senior thesis.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Readings in Chinese
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division courses in Chinese.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding three quarters and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined. May be repeated up to 12 units.
courses.description: Readings in Chinese.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Independent Studies in Chinese
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division courses in Chinese major; Minimum major GPA of 3.5 or higher
courses.comments: Students must have a 3.0 cumulative GPA for the preceding 3 quarters and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
courses.description: Independent studies in Chinese. Individual investigations in literary fields.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Readings in Selected Texts
courses.prereq_text: Ability to read Chinese at graduate level; consent of instructor.
courses.comments: Normally graduate status is required.
courses.description: Course will center on readings of Chinese texts; type and period to depend on needs of students and wishes of instructor. Research methods to be taught as appropriate.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Bibliography and Research Methodology
courses.description: Introduction to the bibliography, reference works, and methodologies of sinological research.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Topics in Tang Literature
courses.description: Explores themes and issues in the literature of the Tang dynasty, with an emphasis on close reading and translation of original texts in Classical Chinese. Topical focus varies.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Gender and Expression in Pre-Modern Chinese Literature
courses.description: This graduate seminar examines Chinese literary tradition from the perspective of gender, discussing the gendering of new modes of expression in de/constructing men and women as social categories over the long course of Chinese literary history. Discussion and readings are mainly in English (and Chinese, depending on the backgrounds of students).

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Poetic Culture in Late Imperial China and Beyond
courses.description: An examination of the role poetry played in both social and individual lives in late imperial China. Relevant practices in later times and in Japan and Korea are also covered. Graduate student paper is required.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: New Directions in Chinese Literary and Cultural Studies
courses.description: This seminar discusses research methods and critical concepts emergent in the most recent studies of Chinese literature and culture. Concentrating on the 16th to the 20th centuries, it is intended to bridge studies of pre-modern and modern periods.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Readings in Taoism
courses.comments: Same course as RG ST 260.
courses.description: Selected readings from important Taoist texts. Depending on the year, primary sources will be read in original Chinese or in translation.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: (Chinese) Aesthetics and Critical Theory
courses.description: What does it mean to aestheticize politics? Is politics inherently aesthetic? Is there such a thing as “apolitical aesthetic”? Why and how to study aesthetic theory comparatively? What is the relationship between aesthetics, modernity, and critical theory? This course explores the major issues and frameworks of critical theory by probing into the question of aesthetics; it also treats modern Chinese culture as an aesthetic and political project, focusing on theories of (Chinese) modernity, media, literature, film, and the relation of aesthetics and politics.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: World Literature and Modern China
courses.description: This course investigates the histories and theories of World Literature as a world-making ideology and as a discipline in comparative literary studies. It focuses on modern Chinese literature and culture while joining current debates on globalization and cosmopolitanism

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Readings in Chinese Buddhism
courses.comments: Same course as RG ST 266F.
courses.description: Selected readings in important Buddhist texts which were either originally written in Chinese or translated into that language. Depending on the year, primary sources will be read in original Chinese or in translation.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Seminar in special areas of interest in Chinese cultural studies. Specific course titles and topics to be announced by the department each quarter offered. Course content will vary.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Directed Reading and Research
courses.comments: Letter grade; minimum of two units per quarter.
courses.description: Individual tutorial. A written proposal for each tutorial must be approved by department chair and filed with graduate division.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Preparation for Comprehensive Examinations
courses.comments: No unit credit allowed toward degree.
courses.description: Study for master's comprehensive examinations and Ph.D examinations.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Master's Thesis Research and Preparation
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: Maximum of 12 units total. No unit credit allowed toward master's degree.
courses.description: Instructor should be chair of the student's thesis committee.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Ph.D. Dissertation Preparation
courses.description: Terminal preparation of the dissertation.

courses.subject: CHIN W
courses.title: Masterpieces in Chinese Literature
courses.description: Examines a selection of works from Chinese literature, with the goal of understanding the major genres and their development over time. The cultural roles of literature, as well as criteria for critical evaluation, are also addressed.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: The Ancient Greeks
courses.description: An introduction to the literature and culture of ancient Greece. The study of literary and material remains will illustrate how the Greeks lived and the values they expressed through literature and the arts. Topics may include the rituals and festivals of Greek religion, the conflict between heroic ideals and democratic ideology, the institutions that shaped public and private life, and the competitive nature of law, drama, athletics and politics.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: The Ancient Greeks - Honors
courses.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in Classics 20A and consent of instructor.
courses.description: A discussion section led by the instructor, provided for students in the honors program. Students receive one unit for the honors seminar (20AH) in addition to four units for Classics 20A.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: The Romans
courses.description: An introduction to the civilization of the ancient Romans. Topics such as Romes legends of male and female virtue, Augustuss ingenious transformation of the republic into a monarchy, gladiators and chariot racing, slavery, Rome and the Christians, and the competing philosophical systems of Stoicism and Epicureanism will be explored through literary texts and archaeological remains. Encounter a range of sources from Livy, Virgil, and Seneca to monuments of the emperors, and examine the complex legacies of Roman culture across time.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: The World of Heroes
courses.description: A study of the Iliad, the Odyssey, the Aeneid and other ancient epics, and of the place of these works in Greek and Roman society. The course explores how the epic hero embodies a cultures ideals concerning the individual, the community, and the universe.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: World of Heroes - Honors
courses.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in Classics 36; consent of instructor.
courses.description: A discussion section led by the instructor, provided for students in the honors program. Students receive one unit for the honors seminar (36H) in addition to four units for Classics 36.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: Gender and Sexuality in Greece and Rome
courses.description: Study of gender and sexuality in a wide range of Greek and Latin texts and contexts, exploring diverse ideals of masculinity and femininity, and sexual codes, norms, and practices.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: Greek Mythology
courses.description: Introduction to the principal myths of ancient Greece and the ways in which these myths have been understood. Format and readings vary.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: Greek Mythology--Honors
courses.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in Classics 40 and consent of instructor.
courses.description: A discussion section led by the professor is available to students in the honors program. Students will receive one unit for the honors seminar (40H) in addition to four units for Classics 40.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: Introduction to Classical Archaeology
courses.description: Examines the techniques and methods of classical archaeology as revealed through an examination of the major monuments and artifacts of the Greco-Roman world from prehistory to the Late Empire.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: Troy
courses.description: Troy and the Trojan War hold a central place in the imagination, from the ancient Greek world to the present. What was the connection between heroic ideals and a Bronze Age world of palaces and archives? This course will consider the Trojan War through different lenses -- the archaeology of Bronze Age Greece, Homers epic poems the Iliad and Odyssey, trade and commerce with the Near East, and contemporary re-imaginings.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: Science and Medicine in Ancient Greece
courses.description: An examination of the origins and development of ancient science, especially Greek medicine and science in the Classical and Hellenistic periods. Topics may include scientific methodologies, the first atomic theory, the science of warfare, and the politics of science.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: Introduction To Research
courses.prereq_text: Consent of instructor and department chair.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters. May be repeated to a maximum of six units. Students are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
courses.description: Directed study, oriented toward research, to be arranged with individual faculty members. Course offers exceptional students an opportunity to participate in a research project or group.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: Greek Intellectual Revolutions
courses.description: A wide-ranging introduction to innovative ancient Greek thinking as it transformed over several centuries. Topics may include theories of justice, the nature of the gods, the quarrel between poetry and philosophy, and the invention of history. Reading in translation of poetic, historical, and philosophical texts.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: Understanding Greek Tragedy
courses.description: Greek tragedy was a dramatic phenomenon first performed in ancient Athens. It is obsessively concerned with desire, betrayal, and loss, and with civic and democratic values. This course studies the original contexts in which Greek tragedy was first seen -- religious, theatrical, military, political, and philosophical -- and the magnetic force it still holds for us today. Introduces students to some of the most important moments in the modern reception of Greek tragedy, in theory, politics, and drama.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: Ancient Magic and Modern Revivals
courses.description: Explores the practice of magic in classical antiquity, beginning with the archaic period and ending in the seventh century CE. This historicized survey of practices, laws, and literary representations serves as a springboard for reflecting on magic as a social phenomenon and category of thought, and for discussion of the modern reception and contemporary revivals of Greco-Roman magic.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: Race and Ethnicity in the Graeco-Roman World
courses.description: A study of cultural interactions and attitudes focusing upon the ancient Greeks. How or when did Greeks think of themselves as a people unified by language, ethnicity, and cultural practices and values? How did they view differences between themselves and other peoples, and among their own communities?

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: From Homer To Harlequin: Masculine, Feminine And The Romance
courses.description: The romance, from Homer's Odyssey to the contemporary romance novel, creates images of masculinity and femininity. This course considers these gender representations and questions whether they vary among ancient novels, and between the romances of antiquity and those of today.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: Humor and Laughter in the Classical World
courses.description: This is a course about laughter in ancient Greece and Rome. We will discuss ritual laughter, enjoy the Dionysian frivolity of Aristophanes and Plautus, appreciate the elegant humor of Menander and Terence, and read the jokes from Philogelus collection. This exploration offers an opportunity to ask questions about the nature of laughter: Why do we laugh? What are the functions of laughter? Is humor universal or determined by cultural circumstances?

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: Slavery and Freedom in the Ancient World
courses.description: Examination of the nature and impact of chattel slavery in the ancient Mediterranean, with emphasis on classical Greece and imperial Rome. How did ancient thinkers like Aristotle and Seneca define slavery in opposition to freedom? What modes of slave labor thrived in antiquity and why? How did the enslaved resist subjugation, whether through outright rebellion like the revolt led by Spartacus or by other means? Primary sources and comparative evidence will guide discussion of these and other key questions.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: Ciceros Toughest Trials
courses.description: Cicero, Romes greatest trial lawyer and sharpest wit, faced many tough cases in his long career at the bar (81-43 BC). Students will read a selection of Ciceros most famed speeches against the background of Roman handbooks on forensic argument, compare his strategy with that of opposing counsel, and consider the similarities as well as differences between Roman procedures and our own. Aspiring lawyers are very welcome, as are all students interested in persuasive speaking or Roman culture.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: The Fall of the Ancient Republic: Cicero, Caesar, and Rome
courses.description: The tumultuous end of the Roman Republic, from Tiberius Gracchus (133 BC) to the Rubicon (49 BC), had profound importance for the history of the West and produced a fascinating literature of crisis in the writings of Sallust, Cicero, Catullus, and Caesar.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: Greek Religion and Identity
courses.description: The ancient Greeks defined themselves through their religion, and this course examines different forms of Greek identity from the standpoint of religious practice and belief. Topics addressed include the role of animal sacrifice, material objects dedicated to the gods, gender and class distinctions among the worshippers, the built environment, athletics, and local myths and variations in practice. By considering ancient evidence through the lens of contemporary theory, we will attempt to reconstruct the richness and diversity of Greek religious experience.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: Greek Painting
courses.description: Examines the art of painting and its social context in Greek antiquity, including monumental wall painting, vase painting, and the relationship between these and other media from prehistory to the Hellenistic period.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: Pompeii
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Classics 170B.
courses.description: A study of the history, buildings, and people of Pompeii, a city buried by the eruption of Mt. Vesuvius.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: Artifact and Text: The Archaeology and Literature of Early Greece
courses.description: A survey of the archaeological record and literature of early Greece from the Late Bronze Age to the end of the Archaic Age, with special attention paid to the interconnection of artifact and text for our understanding of this period.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: Environmental Interactions in the Ancient Mediterranean World
courses.description: An investigation into primarily the ancient Greek and Roman history of interaction with the environment. How did the ancient Greek poets, playwrights, and philosophers imagine and describe the relationship between humans and the nonhuman world? In what ways did the Romans engage with the environment as they forged an empire across land and sea? From divine mountains to the subjugation of animals and widespread deforestation, we will explore literary, cultural, and archaeological sources to assess how and to what extent ancient perspectives on human-environment interactions have influenced and inform, or can help us to think differently, about the ways we imagine our relationship to the environment today.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: Advanced Study in Classical Civilization
courses.comments: For Classical Civilization and Greek and Roman Culture majors.
courses.description: Specialized study in classical civilization addressing central themes or genres in detail. Topics vary and may include subjects such as The Family in Ancient Rome, Greek Oracles and Politics, and Imperial Theology: Augustus, Politics and Religion.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: Interfaces in Classical Civilization
courses.comments: For Classical Civilization and Greek and Roman Culture majors.
courses.description: Specialized study in classical civilization addressing influence or reception of classical culture, or meeting and competition of cultures. Topics vary and may include subjects such as Greek Tragedy and Western Theater, Greek and Roman Comedy and Reception, and Julius Caesars: Ancient and Modern.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: Undergraduate Seminar
courses.prereq_text: Consent of instructor and upper-division standing.
courses.comments: Priority given to Classics majors, Classics minors, and students in the honors program. May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units.
courses.description: Study and research of special topics in classical literature, civilization, and culture. Topics may include: Rome: the ancient city, food in antiquity, the Roman family, religious thought and practice in Rome, culture and crisis in Athens, culture and crisis in Rome, etc.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: Literary Text Mining
courses.comments: Freshman can only enroll with Instructor approval.
courses.description: Literary text-mining is a decades-old field that uses quantitative methods to answer enduring literary questions about texts meaning, significance, politics, context, and more. Text- mining methods offer researchers the chance to answer new questions at larger scales. This course introduces students to a variety of computational methods, from foundational counting methods to machine-learning. We will investigate several literary datasets from the ancient world using Python programming language. No prior experience in Classics, literary theory or Python is required; different paths through the course are available for students with significant coding experience.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: Computational Linguistics Lab
courses.prereq_text: Instructor approval required. Not open to Freshmen
courses.description: Directed and/or collaborative reading, research, or theoretical work in computational linguistics. Participation may include obtaining and organizing data, constructing open-source software packages, conducting original research projects in computational linguistics, or contributing to the research publication process. Instructor permission required. JH- Updated with Departmental Approval

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: Senior Honors Thesis in Classics
courses.prereq_text: Must have been in residence as a Classics major for at least one full quarter.Must have a grade point average of 3.6 or better in the major.Approval of the department's chair.
courses.description: Research and writing of a senior thesis paper under the close supervision of a Classics faculty member.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: Senior Honors Thesis in Classics
courses.prereq_text: Must have been in residence as a Classics major for at least two full quarters.Must have a grade point average of 3.6 or better in the major.Approval of the department's chair.
courses.description: Research and writing of a senior thesis paper under the close supervision of a Classics faculty member.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: Special Readings.
courses.prereq_text: Consent of instructor and department chair; upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division courses in Classics.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined. Total credit for this course is limited to six units.
courses.description: Individual or small group reading and study in subjects not included in the regular curriculum.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: Independent Studies In Greek And Latin.
courses.prereq_text: Consent of instructor and department chair; upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division courses in Classics.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
courses.description: Independent study in areas in which both Greek and Latin are necessary.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: Independent Research Assistant.
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division courses in Classics consent of instructor and department.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
courses.description: To cooperate on an active basis with a professor on a research project involving the Classics.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: Proseminar
courses.description: Bibliography, methodology, and history of classical scholarship.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: History of Greek and Latin Literature
courses.description: Survey of development of poetry and prose; major authors. Special readings and reports.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: History of Greek and Latin Literature
courses.description: Survey of development of poetry and prose; major authors. Special readings and reports.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: History of Greek and Latin Literature
courses.description: Survey of development of poetry and prose; major authors. Special readings and reports.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: Seminar in Literary Studies
courses.description: A graduate-level course in Greek and Roman authors, themes, or genres. Topics vary and may include, Aristotle's De Anima, construction of gender in Augustan poetry, texts and intertexts, and Roman tragedy.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: Seminar in Cultural Studies
courses.description: A graduate-level course in the culture and cultures of the ancient Mediterranean. Topics vary and may include animals and ethics in the ancient world, religion and politics in the Roman Republic, and performance on and off the stage.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: Seminar in Ancient History
courses.description: Advanced study in the scholarship, methods, and ancillary disciplines of Greek and Roman history. Topics may include slavery in ancient Greece, naval strategy in classical Greece, current problems and debates in Roman history, and Augustus and foundation of the Principate.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: Seminar in Archaeology
courses.description: Advanced study in the material culture of the ancient Mediterranean, examining the scholarship, techniques, and methods of classical archaeology. Topics may include "Greeks in Southern Italy," "Athens in the Age of Pericles," and "The rise of the Greek city-state."

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: Computational Linguistics Lab
courses.description: Directed and/or collaborative reading, research, or theoretical work in computational linguistics for graduate students. Participation may include obtaining and organizing data, constructing open-source software packages, conducting original research projects in computational linguistics, or contributing to the research publication process. Instructor permission required.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: Teaching Assistant Practicum
courses.description: Weekly discussions, directed by faculty, of topics especially relevant for teaching assistants assigned to Classics 40 (Greek Mythology). Includes analyses of texts and materials, discussion of teaching techniques, formulation of exam questions and paper topics, grading, and pedagogical ethics.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: Language Teaching Practicum
courses.description: Weekly discussions, directed by faculty, of topics relevant for graduate students assigned to introductory language courses. Includes design of syllabi, quizzes and exams, and especially discussion of teaching techniques and evaluation of teaching methods by observation and follow-up consultations.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: Directed Reading and Research
courses.prereq_text: Written proposal approved by department chair and graduate advisor.
courses.description: Individual tutorial.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: Preparation for Comprehensive Exams
courses.prereq_text: Consent of graduate advisor and chair.
courses.comments: No unit credit allowed toward degree.
courses.description: Study for master's examinations and Ph.D. examinations.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: Master's Thesis Research and Preparation
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing and consent of instructor and graduate advisor.
courses.comments: No unit credit allowed toward degree.
courses.description: Independent research.

courses.subject: CLASS
courses.title: Ph.D Dissertation Preparation
courses.description: Ph.D. dissertation presentation. Preparation of the dissertation.

courses.subject: CLASSW
courses.title: World of Heroes
courses.description: A study of the Iliad, the Odyssey, the Aeneid and other ancient epics, and of the place of these works in Greek and Roman society. The course explores how the epic hero embodies a cultures ideals concerning the individual, the community, and the universe.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Seminar on the Field of Computer Science
courses.prereq_text: Open to computer science majors only.
courses.description: Overviews the potential of, and opportunities available from, the field of computer science. Topics include an overview of how computers work and the interesting ways in which computers can be applied to solve important and high-impact technological, social, and cutting-edge research problems.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Artificial Intelligence Seminar
courses.description: Introductory seminar designed to immerse students in the diverse interdisciplinary field of Artificial Intelligence (AI). Features guest lectures by faculty members from various departments affiliated with AI centers and research initiatives. Students gain exposure to foundational AI techniques and their wide-ranging applications, preparing them for potential engagement in AI research and related academic opportunities. Students complete reading assignments to deepen their understanding and participate actively in seminar discussions.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Introduction to Data Science 1
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed or enrolled concurrently in CMPSC 8, CMPSC W 8, CMPSC 16, ENGR 3, ENGR W 3, ECE 3, or equivalent (including AP CS A with a score of 4 or higher).
courses.description: Introduction to data science methods and Python programming language for students with little to no experience in the subjects. Topics include foundational programming concepts, problem-solving strategies and code design, and data science concepts as table operations, exploratory data analysis, basic probability.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Introduction to Data Science 2
courses.prereq_text: Computer Science 5A or Computer Science 8 or ECE 3 with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Students explore the data science lifecycle, including question formulation, data collection and cleaning, exploratory data analysis and visualization, statistical inference and prediction, and decision-making. The course focus is on transforming and analyzing data; machine learning methods including regression, classification and clustering; principles behind data visualizations; concepts of measurement error and prediction; and techniques for scalable data processing.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Introduction to Computer Science
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed CMPSC 16 or ENGR 3 or ENGR W3 or ECE 3.
courses.description: Introduction to computer program development for students with little to no programming experience. Basic programming concepts, variables and expressions, data and control structures, algorithms, debugging, program design, and documentation.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Intermediate Python Programming
courses.prereq_text: CMPSC 8 or CMPSC W8 or ENGR 3 or ENGR W3 or ECE 3 with a grade of C or better.
courses.comments: CMPSCW 9 is the online version of CMPSC 9
courses.description: Intermediate topics in Computer Science using the Python programming language. Topics include object oriented programming, runtime analysis, data structures, and software testing methodologies.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Programming Language Laboratory
courses.prereq_text: Knowledge of at least one programming language.
courses.comments: Different sections may be repeated. Sections not always offered.
courses.description: A self-paced course to allow a student who already possesses a working knowledge of at least one programming language an opportunity to learn other languages of interest. Each section studies a different programming language.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Problem Solving with Computers I
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 3A or 2A with a grade of C or better (may be taken concurrently), CS 8 or Engineering 3 or ECE 3 with a grade of C or better, or significant prior programming experience.
courses.description: Fundamental building blocks for solving problems using computers. Topics include basic computer organization and programming constructs: memory CPU, binary arithmetic, variables, expressions, statements, conditionals, iteration, functions, parameters, recursion, primitive and composite data types, and basic operating system and debugging tools.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Problem Solving with Computers II
courses.prereq_text: Computer Science 16 with a grade of C or better; and Mathematics 3B or 2B with a grade of C or better (may be taken concurrently).
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Computer Science 20.
courses.description: Intermediate building blocks for solving problems using computers. Topics include intermediate object-oriented programming, data structures, object-oriented design, algorithms for manipulating these data structures and their run-time analyses. Data structures introduced include stacks, queues, lists, trees, and sets.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Data Programming and Analytics for Artificial Intelligence
courses.prereq_text: CMPSC 9 or CMPSC 24 with a grade of C or better; and, Mathematics 3A or 2A with a grade of C or better (may be taken concurrently).
courses.description: Course delves into essential programming, algorithmic, and data analytics techniques foundational to artificial intelligence. Topics include data acquisition, cleaning, transformation, modeling, sampling, visualization and simulation, statistical programming, hypothesis testing, inference, with applications in artificial intelligence. Students will apply these concepts through hands-on Python projects, gaining practical experience in using data analytics to develop intelligent systems.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Object Oriented Design and Implementation
courses.prereq_text: Computer Science 24 with a grade of C or better
courses.description: Advanced topics in object-oriented computing. Topics include encapsulation, data hiding, inheritance, polymorphism, compilation, linking and loading, memory management, and debugging; recent advances in design and development tools, practices, libraries, and operating system support.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Foundations of Computer Science
courses.prereq_text: Computer Science 16 with a grade of C or better and Mathematics 4A with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Introduction to the theoretical underpinnings of computer science. Topics include propositional predicate logic, set theory, functions and relations, counting, mathematical induction and recursion (generating functions).

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Discrete Mathematics for Computer Science
courses.prereq_text: Computer Science 16 with a grade of C or better and Mathematics 4A with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Introductory discrete mathematics. Topics include fundamental principles of counting (permutations, combinations), sets, graph theory, elementary probability, and number theory.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Logic and Automata
courses.prereq_text: Computer Science 41; open to Computer Science and Computer Engineering majors only.
courses.description: Introduction to formal logic and computational theory. Covers propositional and predicate logic and select topics from formal languages and automata theory, including regular, context-free languages, and Turing Machines.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Computer Organization and Logic Design
courses.prereq_text: Computer Science 16 with a grade of C or better; and Mathematics 3C or 4A with a grade of C or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Computer Science 30.
courses.description: Assembly language programming and advanced computer organization; Digital logic design topics including gates, combinational circuits, flip-flops, and the design and analysis of sequential circuits.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Special Topics in Computer Science
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 32 units provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Provides for the study of topics of current interest in computer science: A. Foundations; B. Software Systems; C. Programming Languages and Software Engineering; D. Information Management; E. Architecture; F. Networking; G. Security; H. Scientific Computing; I. Intelligent and Interactive Systems; N. General.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Undergraduate Research
courses.comments: May be repeated for up to 12 units total. Does not apply toward any CS major degree requirements.
courses.description: Research opportunities for undergraduate students. Students will be expected to give regular oral presentations, actively participate in a weekly seminar, and prepare at least one written report on their research.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Independent Studies in Computer Science
courses.comments: Must have a minimum 3.0 grade point average. May be repeated. Students are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 99/198/199 courses combined.
courses.description: Independent studies in computer science for advanced students.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Introduction to Research in Computer Science
courses.prereq_text: Computer Science 40 and Computer Science 32; consent of instructor.
courses.description: Defining a CS research problem, finding and reading technical papers, oral communication, technical writing, and independent learning. Course participants work in teams as they apprentice with a CS research group to propose an original research problem and write a research proposal.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Introduction to Computational Science
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 4B with a grade of C or better; Mathematics 6A with a grade of C or better; Computer Science 24 with a grade of C or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Computer Science 110A.
courses.description: Introduction to the numerical algorithms that form the foundations of data science, machine learning, and computational science and engineering. Matrix computation, linear equation systems, eigenvalue and singular value decompositions, numerical optimization. The informed use of mathematical software environments and libraries, such as python/numpy/scipy.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Data Structures and Algorithms
courses.prereq_text: CMPSC 40 or CMPSC 41 or MATH 8 with a grade of C or better; CMPSC 24 or CMPSC 25 with a grade of C or better; PSTAT 120A or ECE 139 (may be taken concurrently with CMPSC 130A); open to Computer Science Department majors, and Electrical and Computer Engineering Department majors only.
courses.description: Data structures and applications with proofs of correctness and analysis. Hash Tables, Priority Queues (heaps); Balanced Search Trees. Graph Traversal techniques and their applications.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Algorithm Design and Analysis
courses.description: Design and analysis of computer algorithms. Correctness proofs and solution of recurrence relations. Design techniques; divide and conquer, greedy strategies, dynamic programming. Applications of techniques to problems from several disciplines. NP - completeness.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Algorithms Engineering
courses.comments: Not open for enrollment or credit to students who have previously completed "CMPSC 190A: Special Topics - Algorithms Engineering" in Winter 2023 or Winter 2024 with Prof Daniel Lokshtanov.
courses.description: Applying theoretical knowledge about algorithms, data structures, and complexity to performing the complete process of analyzing a computational problem, estimating the running time of suggested solutions, and implementing an effective and correct program for the computational problem.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Randomized Algorithms
courses.prereq_text: CMPSC 130B with a letter grade of B or better.
courses.comments: Not open for enrollment or credit to students who have previously completed "CMPSC 190A: Special Topics - Randomized Algorithms" in Spring 2023 with Prof Eric Vigoda.
courses.description: Covers advanced algorithmic ideas, focusing on randomized algorithms. Explores how randomization can be used to make algorithms simpler and more efficient, and to understand the probabilistic analysis of algorithms.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Mathematics of Artificial Intelligence
courses.prereq_text: Math 4A; CMPSC 25 or CMPSC 24; and ECE 139.
courses.description: Comprehensive mathematical foundation for machine learning and AI. Covers key topics in statistics, linear algebra, and optimization as applied to modern AI systems. Topics include quantifying bias and variance, estimation theory (e.g., maximum likelihood estimation, ensemble methods), statistics on graphs, including the configuration model, probability distributions on graphs, summary statistics, and random walks. Optimization topics include gradient descent, continuous and convex optimization, backpropagation, kernel methods, and practical aspects of optimization.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Automata and Formal Languages
courses.prereq_text: Computer Science 40 or Computer Science 41 with a grade of C or better; open to Computer Science and Computer Engineering majors only.
courses.description: Formal languages; finite automata and regular expressions; properties of regular languages; pushdown automata and context-free grammars; properties of context-free languages; introduction to Turing machines and computability.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Parallel Computing
courses.prereq_text: MATH 4A with a grade C or better; and, CMPSC 32 or CMPSC 130A.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Computer Science 110B.
courses.description: Fundamentals of parallel programming and algorithm design to speedup machine learning and scientific computation. Topics include parallel architectures with shared memory machines and clusters, GPUs, message-passing and thread programming, parallel performance evaluation and optimization, parallelization of core matrix algorithms in machine learning and scientific computing applications, and MapReduce programming for data-intensive cloud computing.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Computer Science Project
courses.prereq_text: Computer Science 32 with a grade of C or better; open to Computer Science majors only.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Computer Science 48 with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Team-based project development. Topics include software engineering and professional development practices, interface design, advanced library support; techniques for team oriented design and development, testing and test driven development, and software reliability and robustness. Students present and demonstrate final projects.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Hardware/Software Interface
courses.prereq_text: Upper division standing in Computer Science, ComputerEngineering, or Electrical Engineering. Familiarity with C, FiniteAutomata, and Computer Architecture.
courses.comments: Same course as ECE 153A.
courses.description: Design and coding of embedded programs. Real-time constraints and management of resources. Practical I/O interfaces and protocols, polling, interrupt maintenance, atomic code, blocking and non-blocking tasks. Static and dynamic task scheduling under real-time and limited resource constraints.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Computer Architecture
courses.prereq_text: Computer Science 32 with a grade of C or better; Computer Science 64 with a grade of C or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have received credit for ECE 154 or ECE 154A or ECE 154B.
courses.description: Introduction to the architecture of computer systems. Topics include: central processing units, memory systems, channels and controllers, peripheral devices, interrupt systems, software versus hardware tradeoffs.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Advanced Applications Programming
courses.prereq_text: Computer Science 24 and 32 with a grade of C or better; open to Computer Science and Computer Engineering majors only.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Computer Science 20. Not open for credit to students who have completed Computer Science 56 with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Advanced application programming using a high-level, virtual-machine-based language. Topics include generic programming, exception handling, automatic memory management, and application development, management, and maintenance tools, third-party library use, version control, software testing, issue tracking, code review, and working with legacy code.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Translation of Programming Languages
courses.prereq_text: Computer Science 64 or Electrical Engineering 154 or Electrical Engineering 154A; Computer Science 130A; and Computer Science 138; open to computer science and computer engineering majors only.
courses.description: Study of the structure of compilers. Topics include: lexical analysis; syntax analysis including LL and LR parsers; type checking; run-time environments; intermediate code generation; and compiler-construction tools.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Programming Languages
courses.prereq_text: Computer Science 130A and 138; open to computer science and computer engineering majors only.
courses.description: Concepts of programming languages: scopes, parameter passing, storage management; control flow, exception handling; encapsulation and modularization mechanisms; reusability through genericity and inheritance; type systems; programming paradigms (imperative, object-oriented, functional, and others). Emerging programming languages and their development infrastructures.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: Introduction to the field of artificial intelligence, which seeks to understand and build intelligent computational systems. Topics include intelligent agents, problem solving and heuristic search, knowledge representation and reasoning, uncertainty and probabilistic reasoning, machine learning, reinforcement learning, and responsible AI.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Machine Learning
courses.description: Covers the most important techniques of machine learning (ML) and includes discussions of: well-posed learning problems; artificial neural networks; concept learning and general to specific ordering; decision tree learning; genetic algorithms; Bayesian learning; analytical learning; and others.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Operating Systems
courses.prereq_text: Computer Science 130A; and, Computer Science 154 or ECE 154A (may be taken concurrently); open to computer science, computer engineering or electrical engineering majors only.
courses.description: Basic concepts of operating systems. The notion of a process; interprocess communication and synchronization; input-output, file systems, memory management.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Distributed Systems
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed ECE 151.
courses.description: Distributed systems architecture, distributed programming, network of computers, message passing, remote procedure calls, group communication, naming and membership problems, asynchrony, logical time, consistency, fault-tolerance, and recovery.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Fundamentals of Database Systems
courses.description: Database system architectures, relational data model, relational algebra, relational calculus, SQL, QBE, query processing, integrity constraints (key constraints, referential integrity), database design, ER and object- oriented data model, functional dependence, lossless join and dependency preserving decompositions, Boyce-Codd and Third Normal Forms.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Design and Implementation Techniques of Database Systems
courses.description: Queries and processing, optimizer, cost models, execution plans, rewriting rules, access methods, spatial indexing; transactions, ACID properties, concurrency control, serializability, two-phase locking, timestamping, logging,checkpointing, transaction abort and commit, crash recovery; distributed databases.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Introduction to Computer Communication Networks
courses.prereq_text: CMPSC 32 with a grade of C or better; PSTAT 120A or ECE 139; open to computer science, electrical engineering, and computer engineering majors only.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Computer Science 176 or ECE 155 or ECE 155A.
courses.description: Basic concepts in networking, the OSI model, error detection codes, flow control, routing, medium access control, and high-speed networks.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Network Computing
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed ECE 155B or 194W.
courses.description: Focus on networking and web technologies used in the Internet. The class covers socket programming and web-based techniques that are used to build distributed applications.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Internet Computing
courses.description: General overview of wireless and mobile networking, multimedia, security, multicast, quality of service, IPv6, and web caching. During the second half of the course, one or more of the above are studied in greater detail.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Computer Security
courses.description: Introduction to the basics of computer security and privacy. Analysis of technical difficulties of producing secure computer information systems that provide guaranteed controlled sharing. Examination and critique of current systems, methods, certification.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Introduction to Cryptography
courses.prereq_text: Computer Science 24 with a grade of C or better; Computer Science 40 or Computer Science 41 with a grade of C or better; and PSTAT 120A or 121A or ECE 139 or permission of instructor.
courses.description: An introduction to the basic concepts and techniques of cryptography and cryptanalysis. Topics include: The Shannon Theory, classical systems, the enigma machine, the data encryption standard, public key systems, digital signatures, file security.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Introduction to Robotics: Planning and Kinematics
courses.comments: CMPSC 179P, ECE 179P, and ME 179P are the same course.
courses.description: Motion planning and kinematics topics with an emphasis on geometric reasoning, programming, and matrix computations. Motion planning: configuration spaces, sensor-based planning, decomposition and sampling methods, and advanced planning algorithms. Kinematics: reference frames, rotations and displacements, kinematic motion models.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Computer Graphics
courses.prereq_text: Computer Science 130A or consent of instructor.
courses.description: Overview of OpenGL graphics standard, OpenGL statemachine, other 3D graphics libraries, 3D graphicspipeline, 3D transformations and clipping, colormodel, shading model, shadow algorithms, texturing,curves and curved surfaces, graphics hardware,interaction devices and techniques

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Introduction to Computer Vision
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Chemical Engineering or Mechanical Engineering.
courses.comments: CMPSC 181 and ECE 181 are the same course.
courses.description: Overview of computer vision problems and techniques for analyzing the content of images and video. Topics include image formation, edge detection, image segmentation, pattern recognition, texture analysis, optical flow, stereo vision, shape representation and recovery techniques, issues in object recognition, and case studies of practical vision systems.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Ethics, Privacy, Fairness, and Bias in AI and Computing
courses.description: Multifaceted ethical considerations of artificial intelligence, focusing on privacy, bias, fairness, and transparency. Students engage in hands-on learning by examining practical tools and frameworks like AWS, Azure, and GCP, gaining insights into best practices for mitigating data privacy risks, detecting and managing bias, ensuring fairness, and monitoring model performance. Through case studies, discussions, and exercises, course addresses real-world challenges such as data poisoning, feature drift, and human oversight in decision-making processes. Explores key algorithms and methodologies for model explainability, including fairness and bias detection techniques, to develop a holistic understanding of responsible AI.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Mobile Application Development
courses.prereq_text: Computer Science 56 or Computer Science 156; and Computer Science 130A.
courses.description: An introduction to programming mobile computing devices. Students will learn about and study the shift in software development from desktop to mobile device applications. Topics will include software engineering and design practices, advances in programming practice, and support tools for mobile application development and testing. Students will develop and deploy mobile applications as part of their course work.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Human-Computer Interaction
courses.prereq_text: Upper division standing; Open to computer science, computer engineering, and electrical engineering majors.
courses.description: The study of human-computer interaction enables system architects to design useful, efficient, and enjoyable computer interfaces. This course teaches the theory, design guidelines, programming practices, and evaluation procedures behind effective human interaction with computers.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Internet of Things (IoT) Systems
courses.comments: Not open for enrollment or credit to students who have previously completed "CMPSC 190B: Special Topics - IoT Systems" in Winter 2023 or Fall 2023 with Prof Chandra Krintz.
courses.description: The Internet of Things (IoT) embeds ordinary physical objects in our environment with digital intelligence -- via sensing, control, communications, and computing capabilities. As such, IoT advances are likely key drivers of the next computing revolution. This course will teach IoT systems end-to-end, including the fundamentals of IoT devices, software architectures, communication protocols, security approaches, distributed, multi-tier (e.g. sensors, edge, and cloud) programming and deployment considerations needed to support emerging IoT applications.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Deep Learning
courses.description: Deep Learning has been driving the progress of AI in the past decade and has found versatile applications in many products and everyday life. This course will introduce general principles, methods, network architectures, and applications of Deep Learning. Covers neural network architectures including convolutional neural networks, recurrent neural networks, Transformer, and graph neural networks. Covers techniques for designing loss, training, and inference methods. Focus on both the principles, analytical skills, and implementation practice. Suitable for undergraduate and graduate students who want to pursue a career in AI or conduct research in deep learning.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Introduction to Natural Language Processing
courses.description: This NLP course explores AI's capability to understand human language, focusing on machine learning algorithms and large language models. It covers language modeling, sentiment analysis, tagging, and machine translation, discussing lexical, syntactic, and semantic processing. Key models include Naive Bayes, logistic regression, and neural networks like RNNs and CNNs. It emphasizes empirical analysis of text corpora and how to evaluate the strengths and limitations of statistical tools, including large language models, in NLP.

courses.title: Senior Computer Systems Project
courses.prereq_text: Computer Science 48 or 56 or 148 or 156 or 172; Senior standing in computer science or computer engineering.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed ECE 189A.
courses.description: This course is the first in the 2-course Computer Science Capstone sequence. Student teams learn about modern software design and engineering techniques and work together to use them and their past educational experiences at UCSB to analyze, specify, design, and prototype innovative solutions to complex, real world problems using computers.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Senior Computer Systems Project
courses.prereq_text: CMPSC 189A; Senior standing in Computer Science or Computer Engineering.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed ECE 189A or ECE 189B.
courses.description: This course is the second in the 2-course Computer Science Capstone sequence. Student teams continue their CMPSC 189A effort by evolving their specifications, design, and prototypes of advanced computer science solutions and systems. The students learn about interfaces, software integration, and testing, and prepare advanced demonstrations for public presentation at the end of the sequence.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Logic and Applications in Computer Science
courses.description: Propositional logic, first order logic, completeness, compactness, incompleteness, undecidability; selected topics from finite model theory, theorem proving, logic programming, program verification, databases, computational complexity.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Matrix Analysis and Computation
courses.comments: Students should be proficient in basic numerical methods, linear algebra, mathematically rigorous proofs, and some programming language. Same course as ECE 210A, ME 210A, Mathematics 206A, Chemical Engineering 211A, and Geology 251A.
courses.description: Graduate level-matrix theory with introduction to matrix computations. SVD's, pseudoinverses, variational characterization of eigenvalues, perturbation theory, direct and iterative methods for matrix computations.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Numerical Simulation
courses.comments: Students should be proficient in basic numerical methods, linear algebra, mathematically rigorous proofs, and some programming language. Same course as ECE 210B, ME 210B, Mathematics 206B, Chemical Engineering 211B, and Geology 251B.
courses.description: Linear multistep methods and Runge-Kutta methods for ordinary differential equations: stability, order and convergence. Stiffness. Differential algebraic equations. Numerical solution of boundary value problems.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Numerical Solution of Partial Differential Equations--Finite Difference Methods
courses.comments: Students should be proficient in basic numerical methods, linear algebra, mathematically rigorous proofs, and some programming language. Same course as ECE 210C, ME 210C, Mathematics 206C, Chemical Engineering 211C, and Geology 251C.
courses.description: Finite difference methods for hyperbolic, parabolic and elliptic PDE's, with application to problems in science and engineering. Convergence, consistency, order and stability offinite difference methods. Dissipation and dispersion. Finite volume methods. Software design and and adaptivity.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Numerical Solution of Partial Differential Equations--Finite Element Methods
courses.comments: Students should be proficient in basic numerical methods, linear algebra, mathematically rigorous proofs, and some programming language. Same course as ECE 210D, ME 210D, Mathematics 206D, Chemical Engineering 211D, and Geology 251D.
courses.description: Weighted residual and finite element methods for the solution of hyperbolic, parabolic and elliptical partial differential equations, with application to problems in science and engineering. Error Estimates. Standard and discontinuous Galerkin methods.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Level Set Methods
courses.prereq_text: CMPSC 211C or CH E 211C or ECE 210C or ME 210C.
courses.comments: Same course as CH E 226, ECE 226, and ME 216.
courses.description: Mathematical description of the level set method and design of the numerical methods used in its implementations (ENO-WENO, Godunov, Lax-Friedrich, etc.). Introduction to the Ghost Fluid Method. Applications in CFD, Materials Sciences, Computer Vision and Computer Graphics.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Information Theory
courses.comments: Same course as ECE 205.
courses.description: Entropy, mutual information, and Shannon's coding theorems; lossless source coding, Huffman, Shannon-Fano-Elias, and arithmetic codes; Channel capacity; rate-distortion theory, and lossy source coding; source-channel coding; algorithmic complexity and information; applications of information theory in various fields.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Approximations, NP-Completeness and Algorithms
courses.description: Epsilon approximations, PTAS and FPTAS. Techniques for the design of approximation algrorithms. P, NP, NP-complete problems, polynomial transformations, Turing reductions, strong NP-completeness, NP-hardness and inapproximability results. Topics in algorithms include: amortized analysis, advanced graph algorithms and data structures.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Topics in Combinatorial Algorithms
courses.description: Advanced topics in algorithm design, including network flows, matchings in graphs, linear and integer programming.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Computational Geometry
courses.description: Algorithms and lower bound techniques in computational geometry; decision tree models of computation; geometric searching; point location and range search; convex hull and maxima of a point set; proximity algorithms; geometric intersections.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Advanced Computer Architecture
courses.description: Advanced instruction set architectures, pipelining, dynamic scheduling, branch prediction, superscalar issue, out-of-order execution, memory-hierarchy design, advanced cache architectures and prefetching. Several real designs are dissected and simulators are developed for performing quantitative evaluations of design decisions.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Program Analysis
courses.description: Theoretical aspects of translation. Topics include: data flow analysis; control flow analysis; interprocedural analysis; optimization; type systems.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Runtime Systems
courses.comments: Computer Science 260 recommended.
courses.description: Topics central to modern programming languages and their implementation: garbage collection; memory system performance; characteristics and optimization of object-oriented languages; type systems and type inference; run-time compilation.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Automated Verification
courses.description: Covers automated verification algorithms and tools. Topics include: temporal logics, fixpoint characterizations of temporal properties, model checking, symbolic verification, explicit-state verification, verification using automated theorem provers, automated abstraction.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Operating Systems
courses.description: Develops an understanding of operating systems and operating systems research at both a conceptual level and from an engineering perspective. Fundamental design principles, culled primarily from the research literature, motivate an analysis of previous and current systems.This analysis is further validated through empirical investigation.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Distributed Systems
courses.description: Covers the fundamental problems in distributed systems and the various tools used to solve them. Of primary interest is the issue of fault-tolerance. Topics include event ordering, clocks, global states, agreement, fault-tolerance, and peer-to-peer systems.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Software Engineering
courses.description: Principles of software engineering disciplines emphasizing requirements analysis, specification design, coding, testing and correctness proofs, maintenance, and management. Students use a number of software engineering tools.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Database Systems
courses.description: Topics include: data models, semantics, data integrity, database design, serializability theory, concurrency control, recovery, distributed databases.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Security
courses.description: Security analysis of networked systems. Analysis of techniques for network scanning, spoofing, hijacking, and denial-of-service attacks. Vulnerability analysis of applications and web-based systems. Intrusion detection and prevention techniques.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Computer Graphics
courses.description: Special topics in computer graphics including: curves and curved surfaces; visual perception of colors and color models; shading models; shadow generation; texture mapping; solid textures; stereographics; helmet-mounteddisplay; graphics hardware/architecture; solid modeling; physically based modeling; fractals and graphtals; volume rendering; scientific visualization.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Computer Vision
courses.comments: Same course as ECE 281B.
courses.description: Advanced topics in computer vision: image sequence analysis, spatio-temporal filtering, camera calibration and hand-eye coordination, robot navigation, shape representation, physically-based modeling, regularization theory, multi-sensory fusion, biological models, expert vision systems, and other topics selected from recent research papers.

courses.subject: CMPSC
courses.title: Advanced Image Synthesis
courses.prereq_text: Computer Graphics desired but not necessary
courses.description: Theory and design of rendering systems for high-end image synthesis and modeling physically-based light transport. Topics include REYES-style architectures, Monte Carlo algorithms, variance reduction methods, path tracing, photon mapping, reflection and volumetric light transport. Students must have good software engineering skills.

courses.title: Introduction to Computer Science
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed CMPSC 16 or ENGR 3 or ENGR W3 or ECE 3. CMPSCW 8 is the online version of CMPSC 8.
courses.description: Introduction to computer program development for students with little to no programming experience. Basic programming concepts, variables and expressions, data and control structures, algorithms, debugging, program design, and documentation.

courses.title: Intermediate Python Programming
courses.prereq_text: CMPSC 8 or CMPSC W8 or ENGR 3 or ENGR W3 or ECE 3 with a grade of C or better.

courses.subject: CMPTGCS

courses.description: Exploratory Research in Computing offers students an accessible entry point into the research process within computer science and engineering. Designed for those curious about research but not yet ready to commit to a fully scoped and ready to execute project, this course supports early-stage engagement in a group setting but with individualized attention.

courses.description: Serious independent study in computer science with consenting faculty member.

courses.subject: CNCSP

courses.subject: CNCSP

courses.description: Introduces students to theory and practice of psychotherapy and other helping relationships. Students learn about counseling, assessment, ethics, and helping skills. Students gain experience by serving as practice counseling clients or by volunteering in a relevant service setting.

courses.subject: CNCSP
courses.title: Research in Applied Psychology
courses.description: Introduces students to research in applied psychology, including approaches to survey, experimental, and qualitative investigation. Students will be exposed to current research in applied psychology through journal articles, presentations, and participation in research studies.

courses.subject: CNCSP
courses.title: Introduction to Educational and Vocational Guidance
courses.description: An overview of the theories and concepts involved in career decision making. Develop working knowledge of career information and field survey techniques for understanding the job market in relation to economic trends.

courses.subject: CNCSP
courses.title: Positive Psychology Across the Lifespan.
courses.description: Positive Psychology examines how people live life well. It looks at those factors associated with living a happy, meaningful life. Course examines key concepts that include hope, gratitude, grit and optimism to promote well-being and authentic happiness.

courses.subject: CNCSP
courses.title: Psychology of Gender
courses.description: Provides an overview of psychological theory and research related to gender issues. Topics include bias in psychology, gender socialization, communication styles, lifespan development, ethnicity, education, careers, relationships, violence and victimization, health and mental health.

courses.subject: CNCSP
courses.title: The Psychology of Flourishing
courses.description: The purpose of this experiential seminar is to explore and critique the empirical literature on the psychology of flourishing including the personal, interpersonal, and contextual factors that impede and/or promote this state of well-being.

courses.subject: CNCSP
courses.title: Disaster Mental Health
courses.description: This course focuses on the impact natural and human-made disasters have on people and their communities. Reviews the research on the influence of disasters on mental health and why, and provides an introduction to disaster mental health services.

courses.subject: CNCSP
courses.title: Spanish in the Helping Professions: Research and Practice
courses.description: Development of professional vocabulary in Spanish and skills pertinent to research and practice within the human helping professionals. Students' own processes as cultural beings seeking to become bilingual within a discipline (i.e. applied psychology) is addressed systematically throughout the course. Taught in Spanish.

courses.subject: CNCSP
courses.title: Introduction to Autism
courses.description: Overview of diagnostic, clinical, and educational approaches used for autism. Intervention procedures in clinical, school, and family settings are discussed in relation to language development, social development, and self-stimulatory behavior, self-injury, and pivotal behaviors related to a favorable prognosis.

courses.subject: CNCSP
courses.title: Special Topics in Applied Psychology
courses.description: Topics vary by instructor.

courses.subject: CNCSP
courses.title: Independent Studies
courses.description: Study of special problems in various fields of Applied Psychology.

courses.subject: CNCSP
courses.title: Independent Research Assistance
courses.description: Faculty supervised research assistance.

courses.subject: CNCSP
courses.title: Research Design and Methods in Professional Psychology
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Education 277B.
courses.description: Examination of both clinical and statistical approaches to professional psychology research. Special attention devoted to conceptualizing and developing research proposals in the area of professional psychology.

courses.subject: CNCSP
courses.title: Research Foundations in School Psychology
courses.description: This course introduces research methods and statistical analytic approaches that are most useful for school psychologists. Includes descriptive and inferential statistics; test development / psychometrics; experimental, descriptive, and mixed method designs, single-subject designs; program evaluation; and research.

courses.subject: CNCSP
courses.title: Qualitative Research Methods in Applied Psychology
courses.description: Introduces graduate students in Counseling, Clinical and School Psychology to qualitative theory and philosophical paradigms, as well as to the most commonly used qualitative methods in applied psychology. Qualitative data management software will also be introduced.

courses.subject: CNCSP
courses.title: Research Practicum I
courses.description: Student works with research team to develop or conduct an on-going research study. Focus on learning the process of planning and carrying out a research program.

courses.subject: CNCSP
courses.title: Neuroanatomy and Psychopharmacology
courses.description: Introduces students to basic neuroanatomy and neurological functioning across lifespan. Relationship of neurological structure to psychiatric disorder is highlighted. Also serves to give students a background in clinical psychopharmacology. Biomedical treatments for child and adult disorders are explored.

courses.subject: CNCSP
courses.title: Social Bases of Behavior for Applied Psychology
courses.description: Course introduces the social bases of behavior. Students have the opportunity to read classics in the field of social psychology, social influence, and social cognition. Application to clinical work, group psychotherapy, and interpersonal behavior are highlighted.

courses.subject: CNCSP
courses.title: Cognitive and Affective Bases of Behavior
courses.description: This seminar emphasizes cognitive and affective bases of human behavior, including knowledge of (a) cognition, (b) theories and empirical bases of learning, memory, motivation, affect, emotion, executive function, and information processing and (c) factors that influence cognitive performance and/or emotional experience and their interaction.

courses.subject: CNCSP
courses.title: Historical and Philosophical Foundations of Professional Psychology
courses.description: Facilitates a selective and critical analysis of the historical/philosophical foundations of western psychology. To this end, attention is directed to those individuals, ideas and events that have shaped the history of psychology.

courses.subject: CNCSP
courses.title: Social, Cognitive, and Affective Bases of Behavior
courses.description: Provides a foundation for examining the historical, theoretical, and empirical perspectives of the social, cognitive, and affective underpinnings of human behavior. Studying these social, cognitive, and affective processes will be conducted through a research, clinical and practical lens.

courses.subject: CNCSP
courses.title: Human Development
