courses.description: Explores issues and questions about computer-mediated communication and social media in a variety of relationship stages (such as impression formation and relational development to relationship maintenance and termination), contexts (friendship and romantic relationships, collaboration and work), and technologies, in order to understand the psychological, interpersonal, professional, social, and cultural impacts of digital communication media on human relationships. The main course objective is to develop a critical and practical view of online communication--how it differs and how it doesnt--by applying the processes and principles from theories and research to issues and patterns of interactive communication technology use.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: The Digital Divide
courses.comments: Open to Communication and Interdisciplinary studies majors only: Open to all students during Summer Session except freshmen. Former number Comm 160DD.
courses.description: Information and communication technologies (ICT) have become essential for survival in the 21st century. Most people in industrialized settings rely on the internet for all aspects of life, including education, employment, healthcare, politics and personal relationships. At the same time, these tools are expensive, fragile, and often complicated to use. As a result, there are inequalities in who has access to digital technology and who can use it successfully. This class examines these inequalities and the ways they influence, and are influenced by, larger socio-economic inequalities. We explore relevant theories, review current data, and consider creative interventions to help reduce digital divides in years to come.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Data Science in Communication
courses.comments: Open to Communication and Interdisciplinary studies majors only: Open to all students during Summer Session except freshmen. Former number COMM 160DS.
courses.description: We are generating massive amounts of data in our daily digital lives. The ability to understand this data, process it, interpret it, visualize it, and communicate it is an increasingly valuable skill today. These data analytical techniques allow us to make sense of people's behavior in many contexts, like when they communicate online, or when they engage in shopping and commerce, or when they vote in elections. In this class, we will learn some basic methods of conducting Data Science using the Python programming language and discuss important aspects of data ethics, social impact of technology, and data storytelling.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: News, Politics, & Democracy
courses.comments: Open to Communication and Interdisciplinary studies majors only: Open to all students during Summer Session except freshmen. Former number COMM 160PD.
courses.description: Explores the role of the news media in sustaining American democracy. Student projects identify the most difficult problems facing American journalism and propose creative solutions for helping the news media fulfill its democratic function. Topics include news industry consolidation, fake news, political polarization, and the role of social media. Students will come away from this course with a more engaged, critical, and empowered view of what the news can do for democracy.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: The Litigation Laboratory
courses.comments: Does NOT count towards UD Comm major requirements. Open to Communication and Interdisciplinary studies majors only: Open to all students during Summer Sessions except freshmen.
courses.description: Examines how psychology, storytelling, theme development, and strategy shape jury decision-making in real trials. Students explore the roles of trial consultants, judges, attorneys, and experts. The course shows how credibility, bias, emotion, and narrative influence verdicts across personal injury, criminal law, corporate defense, family law, and medical malpractice litigation. Taught by one of the most respected trial consultants in the field, it uses real cases and experiential exercises revealing how themes are developed, stories built, witnesses prepped, juries selected, and cases researched, tested, and won. With guest attorneys each week, this is a can’t-miss course for anyone considering law school or litigation.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Applying Communication to Internships in Organizations
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; open to communications majors only; consent of instructor.
courses.comments: Designed for majors.
courses.description: Field experience combined with communication theory and current literature. Students must hold an 8-10 hour internship in the field of communication throughout the quarter in which they are enrolled in the class. Weekly lecture topics include theories of interpersonal communication, organizational structures, management, and communication styles. The extensive term project analyzes, integrates and applies lay and academic approaches to understanding interns' communicative interactions.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Group Studies for Advanced Students
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; open to communications majors only.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units. Designed for majors.
courses.description: Selected topics in accordance with instructor's area of specialization.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Communication Internship
courses.prereq_text: Must be declared as pre-communication or communication major. Students must have 2.0 cumulative GPA.
courses.comments: Students must obtain a communication related internship prior to enrolling. Limited to declared pre-communication and communication majors. Units do NOT count toward communication major.
courses.description: An opportunity for pre-communication and communication majors to obtain credit for career-related experience and application of academic training in a communication-related internship. Required are 50 hours minimum of internship work, a final five-page report, and a supervisor's letter of verification.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Independent Studies in Communication
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; open to communication majors only.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined. Written proposal required.
courses.description: Independent studies in communication.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Independent Research Assistance in Communication
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; Open to Communication majors only, or other majors by exception based on faculty member request.
courses.comments: 3.0 minimum GPA averaged across the preceding 2 quarters. Limited to 5 units/quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined. Maximum credit toward the major is 12 units.
courses.description: Coursework consists of faculty supervised research assistance.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Communication Theory Construction
courses.description: The nature of theory and theory building in human communication.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Research Methods in Communication
courses.description: A survey of research methods in the social sciences applicable to communication research.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Introduction to Applied Statistics
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to applied statistics for communication research with a focus on the theory andpractice of significance testing, correlation and regression, and basic ANOVA modeling. This course prepares graduate students for the understanding of advanced statistics.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Research Methods and Statistical Analysis
courses.description: Provides students with experience in advanced topics in multivariate statistics and computer programs. Analyses includes multiple regression, MANOVA, log linear analyses, and other advanced techniques.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Mixed Methods in Communication Research
courses.description: Mixed methods research is defined as research in which the investigator collects and analyzes data, integrates the findings, and draws inferences using both qualitative and quantitative approaches or methods in a single study or program of inquiry (JMMR, 2008). This class introduces students to advantages and uses of mixed methods designs for multidimensional inquiry. Students become familiar with mixed methods designs, qualitative methods, quantitative and qualitative data integration, pragmatic perspectives and reporting on mixed methods studies.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Group Communication
courses.description: Readings on research concerning group processes from social and behavioral sciences, with special attention to latest communication apporaches to group interaction. Design of research projects on small group communication.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Interpersonal Communication
courses.description: Analysis of theory and research related to interpersonal communication processes.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Seminar: Nonverbal Communication
courses.description: Analysis of nonverbal behavior as communication, with a special emphasis on design and implementation of research.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Content Analysis
courses.description: A methodology course focusing on the planning and execution of social scientific analyses of communication content; begins with the examination of where meaning resides, then moves into procedures for designing a content analysis study, gathering data, analyzing results, and writing the report.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Mass Media, the Individual, and Society
courses.description: The cognitive and social psychological effects of mass media on the individual and society. Focus is on empirical research as it informs communication theory.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Social Media
courses.description: Explores sociotechnical trends prompted by the evolution of technologies of communication and information. Using perspectives from social science, computer science, engineering, and the humanities, the course focuses on evidence, theory, and directions for future research.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Theories of Persuasion
courses.description: Surveys theories and research of persuasion in both interpersonal and mass mediated contexts. Students will be introduced to the major paradigms of persuasion research and will gain some degree of mastery over the sub-field(s) that most interest them.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Organizational Communication
courses.description: Classical/administrative, human relations/resources, systems, interpretive/cultural, and critical approaches to organizational communication. Theory and research on organizational structures and environments; power, authority and influence; communication networks; leadership; decision making; assimilation and socialization; innovation and change; and strategic communication.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Family Communication
courses.description: Examines theory and research on the role of communication in voluntary and involuntary family relationships of diverse forms. Students will learn about the history of family communication scholarship, prominent theories of family communication, and emerging perspectives on contemporary family life. Students will also consider the effects of various social and contextual factors (e.g., culture, developmental stage, and gender) on family communication processes.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Membership: Organization and Group Socialization and Identification
courses.description: Focuses on membership negotiation (organizational socialization, assimilation, and identification). Examination of workplace interaction and communication that develops and maintains workplace relationships. Discussions/readings emphasize theories related to membership negotiation, but also mediating variables such as context and diversity.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Corporate Social Responsibility: A Communication Perspective
courses.description: The study of Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) is burgeoning as CSR is being rapidly transformed from a vision championed by a small number of companies to a widespread global movement that engages corporations, non-governmental and governmental organizations, activists, and civil society. Explores how contemporary environmental, economic, social, and technological changes influence CSR and are affected by interpersonal, stakeholder, organizational, inter-organizational and media communication dynamics.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Survey of Health Communication
courses.description: Students will be introduced to theories and research relating to health communication in intrapersonal, interpersonal, and mass mediated contexts broadly speaking as well as gain some degree of mastery over the sub-field(s) that most interest them.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Qualitative Methods in Communication
courses.description: This course provides an overview of qualitative research methods, including in-depth interviewing, participant observation, and grounded theory. Using exemplars, it also examines approaches to data analysis, specifically, constant comparison method, narrative and discourse analyses, and computer assisted data management.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Teaching College Communication
courses.description: Theory of teaching communication at the college level. Topics include self-presentation, facilitating discussion, constructing examinations, grading examinations and term papers, providing feedback, and professionalism.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Issues in Communication Research
courses.comments: Enrollment is mandatory each quarter that a student is in residence; units do not fulfill degree requirements.
courses.description: Presentation of research completed or in progress by students, faculty and guest speakers followed by critical discussion of the issues raised.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Directed Reading
courses.description: Individual tutorial. Provides students with the same material as a regular course except it is conducted on an individual basis with a faculty member. Written contract describing the course, readings, and assignments should be submitted to the departmental graduate adviser.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing; consent of department for students outside of COMM.
courses.comments: Open to COMM graduate students. Open to graduate students from other departments by approval code from the instructor.
courses.description: Special seminar on research subjects of current interest.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Special Topics: Community-Engaged Communication Research
courses.description: This graduate seminar introduces students to various types of community-engaged research across a wide range of domains within the communication discipline, including interpersonal, organizational, and media and technology. Philosophies, goals, and methods tied to a range of community-focused research are discussed, as are associated benefits and challenges. Students are expected to leave this course with an appreciation for the diversity in what community-engaged research looks like, and exposure to literatures that will allow pursuit of such research should they choose to do so.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Computer Mediated Communication
courses.description: Examines landmark theories from a variety of disciplines, all or most of which preceded digital communication, that provide the theoretical dynamics that inform, embody, or are altered by computer-mediated communication and online social interaction. By studying modern benchmarks in psychology, sociology, anthropology, education, management, nonverbal interaction, and communication, the objectives of the course are to cultivate participants social scientific foundation with which to ground the study of contemporary electronic media in historical and theoretical contexts, enhance their research by improving their ability to recognize and capitalize on existing theories, and to sharpen their conceptual analysis.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Computational Textual Analysis for Communication Research
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing; consent of department for students outside of COMM.
courses.comments: Open to COMM graduate students. Open to graduate students from other departments by approval code from the instructor.
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to computational methods in textual analysis, specifically designed for those in the field of communication research. This course is practical and hands-on in nature and focuses on theoretical and empirical questions we can ask with text-as-data from a social science perspective and learn how to answer them. The course content covers data scraping, text data cleaning and preprocessing, dictionary-based analysis, unsupervised topic modeling, supervised text classification, the use of large language models, and techniques for effective visualization and reporting of findings. To follow this course, basic Python and R knowledge would be beneficial, but advanced programming skills are not required.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: The Digital Divide
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing; consent of department for students outside of COMM.
courses.comments: Open to COMM graduate students. Open to graduate students from other departments by approval code from the instructor.
courses.description: Information and communication technologies (ICT) have become essential for survival in the 21st century. Most people in industrialized settings rely on the internet for all aspects of life, including education, employment, healthcare, politics and personal relationships. At the same time, these tools are expensive, fragile, and often complicated to use. As a result, there are inequalities in who has access to digital technology and who can use it successfully. This class examines these inequalities and the ways they influence, and are influenced by, larger socio-economic inequalities. We explore relevant theories, review current data, and consider creative interventions to help reduce digital divides in years to come.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Special Topics: Emotion and Media Effects
courses.description: Overview of the the ways in which emotion has been integrated into the study of media effects, focusing on emotion as a predictor of media selection, as an outcome of media exposure, and as the mechanism by which other media effects occur. Traditional lines of research covered include mood management, fright-inducing media, and emotional persuasive appeals. More contemporary issues will receive particular emphasis, including emotion and message sharing, emotional effects of social media use, and the relationship between media use and well-being.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Global Communication, International Relations and the Media
courses.description: Explores the nature, role and influence of globalization and technology on communication and international relations. To do so we examine how these impact the media, the audience and policy makers. We begin by considering the context in which this communication occurs and how this has changed over time. Next, we examine how these communication changes have altered the conduct and understanding of international relations as well as the actors in the making of policy and explore public diplomacy by states and citizen diplomacy. Finally, we conclude by considering the implications of current trends in global communication for global relations.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Media Representation of Diversity
courses.description: Explores social scientific theory and research on intergroup dynamics and how media representations of diversity affects these relations. In the beginning of the term, we focus on a) social psychological explanations of intergroup dynamics and biases, and b) theories explaining how media affects outgroup perceptions and attitudes. Next, we explore media effects literature on how racial majority and minority groups are presented in the media and the consequences of these portrayals on intergroup relations. Finally, we focus on how the media can be used to promote positive intergroup relations.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Media & Stereotyping
courses.description: Special seminar on research subjects of current interest.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Political Communication
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing; consent of department for students outside of COMM.
courses.comments: Open to COMM graduate students. Open to graduate students from other departments by approval code from the instructor.
courses.description: This course offers an exploration of foundational and contemporary topics in Political Communication theory and research. We consider questions about the nature of politics and communication as well as diving into key theoretical debates in the subfield. The course aims to provide a broad overview of this area of research, while at the same time foregrounding how politics emerges in interpersonal, intergroup, and organizational settings.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: R Programming for Communication Research
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing; consent of department for students outside of COMM.
courses.comments: Open to COMM graduate students. Open to graduate students from other departments by approval code from the instructor.
courses.description: Covers fundamentals of the R statistical programming language for researchers and students in Communication and related fields. Students learn the basic skills needed to use R as a tool in their research and coursework. Topics include version control, data manipulation, data visualization, basic statistical analyses, and publication-ready output. No prior experience with R is required.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Risk Communication
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing; consent of department for students outside of COMM.
courses.comments: Open to COMM graduate students. Open to graduate students from other departments by approval code from the instructor.
courses.description: Explores theories and models that aid in risk message design, channels of communication, and barriers (psychological, communicative, and structural) to effective risk communication. We use Plough and Krimsky’s (1987) definition of risk communication: “any public or private communication that informs individuals about the existence, nature, form, severity, or acceptability of risks…” and it can go “from any source to any recipient through any channel” (pp. 6-7). Considers how risk communication design, access, and effects can vary based on the audience’s race/ethnicity, age, education, socioeconomic status, geographic location, etc.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Scholarly Writing
courses.description: Special seminar on research subjects of current interest.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Collaborative Technology and Organizing
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing; consent of department for students outside of COMM.
courses.comments: Open to COMM graduate students. Open to graduate students from other departments by approval code from the instructor.
courses.description: Examination of contemporary theory and research on the role of communication technology in organizations and processes of organizing, including remote work, virtual teams, globally distributed organizations, online communities, and online social movements.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Preparation for the Qualifying Examination
courses.prereq_text: Consent of graduate advisor; graduate standing.
courses.comments: No unit credit allowed toward advanced degree.
courses.description: Directed group or individual preparation for the master's or doctoral qualifying examination.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Master's Thesis Research and Preparation
courses.prereq_text: Consent of thesis advisor; graduate standing.
courses.description: The thesis is done under the direction of the chair of a student's thesis committee.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Dissertation Preparation
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing; consent of department; advancement to candidacy.
courses.description: Course is reserved for writing the dissertation.

courses.subject: COMM W
courses.title: Introduction to Interpersonal Communication
courses.comments: Open to Communication and Interdisciplinary studies majors only; Open to all students during Summer Session except freshmen. COMM W 107 is the online version of COMM 107.
courses.description: Survey of theory and research in interpersonal communication, including social and intimate relationships and conversational interaction.

courses.subject: COMM W
courses.title: Media Effects on Individuals
courses.comments: Open to Communication and Interdisciplinary majors only; Open to all students during Summer Session except freshmen. COMM W 113 is the online version of COMM 113.
courses.description: The effects of media communication on individual cognitive processes and the social environment. Emphasis on media effects on individual attitudes, family interaction, children, perceptions of minorities, sex-role stereotyping and other outcomes.

courses.subject: COMM W
courses.title: Persuasion
courses.comments: Open to Communication and Interdisciplinary studies majors only; Open to all students during Summer Session except freshmen.
courses.description: Analysis and synthesis of current persuasion theory to understand how messages influence attitudes and behaviors. Topics covered include: theories for altering attitudes and behaviors, the persuasion process, and the use of persuasion in applied contexts.

courses.subject: COMM W
courses.title: Understanding and Detecting Human Deception
courses.comments: Open to Communication and Interdisciplinary studies majors only; Open to all students during Summer Session except freshmen.
courses.description: An interdisciplinary study of the methods of human deception detection from the perspectives of law enforcement, national security and intelligence analysis, criminal justice, psychology, sociology, and communication. How to accurately determine when someone is lying is a multi-disciplinary problem and requires a variety of technological and data analytic solutions. Our primary goal will be to comprehend a representative picture of the traditional and contemporary theories regarding the intersection of communication, cognition, and emotion in deception detection.

courses.subject: COMM W
courses.title: Social Media: The Good, the Bad & the Ugly
courses.comments: Open to Communication and Interdisciplinary Studies majors only; Open to all students during summer session except freshmen. COMM W 184 is the online version of COMM 184.
courses.description: Examines the beneficial, harmful, and always complicated implications of social media use across micro- and macro- levels of analyses. We focus on how these systems enhance and impede individual and socio-political self-expression, especially for those from marginalized populations (e.g racial/ethnic/religious minorities, immigrants, women, LGBTQ individuals, people with disabilities, etc.). The class focuses on three primary topics: new media and social movements; new media and health; and new media and identity. Students gain both a theoretical and an applied understanding of how social media shape life in the 21st century.

courses.subject: COMM W
courses.title: News, Politics, & Democracy
courses.comments: Open to Communication and Interdisciplinary studies majors only; Open to all students during Summer Session except freshmen. COMM W 188 is the online version of COMM 188.
courses.description: Explores the role of the news media in sustaining American democracy. Student projects identify the most difficult problems facing American journalism and propose creative solutions for helping the news media fulfill its democratic function. Topics include news industry consolidation, fake news, political polarization, and the role of social media. Students will come away from this course with a more engaged, critical, and empowered view of what the news can do for democracy.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: History of Modern Dance and Contemporary Performance
courses.comments: DANCEW 36 is the online version of DANCE 36
courses.description: Historical development of modern dance in the United States and Europe in the twentieth century. Emphasis on visionary, feminist, and radical aspects of the form.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Summer Modern Dance
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 18 units.
courses.description: Fundamentals of modern dance technique.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Continuing Ballet
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 6 units.
courses.description: Further study of basic elements of ballet.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Continuing Ballet
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 6 units.
courses.description: Further study of basic elements of ballet.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Continuing Ballet
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 6 units.
courses.description: Further study of basic elements of ballet.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Beginning Street Dance Forms
courses.description: Introduction to the various forms of street dance including Hip Hop and Isolations.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Beginning Street Dance Forms
courses.description: Introduction to the various forms of street dance including House Dance, Whacking, and Punking.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Continuing Modern Dance
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 6 units.
courses.description: Further study of basic elements of modern dance.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Continuing Modern Dance
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 6 units.
courses.description: Further study of basic elements of modern dance.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: History and Appreciation of Dance
courses.description: Introduction to history and appreciation of dance. Explores dance from a wide cross-cultural perspective of cultural mutuality and diversity, established traditions, and the power of dance to bring about social change, activism and justice.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Introduction to Social Dance: History and Practice
courses.description: An introductory level survey of Social Dance. Studio-based physical practice will be complimented by a survey of the history, theory and/or literature of Social Dance. A beginning level elective dance course, Intro to Social Dance focuses on forms developing in Europe, North and South America, as well as their migration and development across borders. Course work is grounded in the physical study of multiple styles alongside outside classwork comprised of readings, viewings and collaborative group projects.

courses.description: A study of the basic elements pertaining to the craft of choreography. Emphasis on exploration of movement variation, breath rhythm, the development of dance phrases, and the use of stage space. For dance majors.

courses.title: Improvisation
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 6 units.
courses.description: The fundamental exploration of movement potential with particular focus on the individual and group dynamics.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Contact Improvisation
courses.description: Lower division studio course in the fundamentals of Contact Improvisation (as developed by Steve Praxton, and his contemporaries.) Exploring the egalitarian effort of shared weight and mutual support. Contact Improvisation serves as a fundamental step in a dance student's partnering training, and informs a deeper sense of weight and sentimentality in individual dance technique.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Open-Level Ballet
courses.description: This course teaches ballet technique focusing on the concepts of barre practice and warm-up along with center adagio, petite allegro, grand allegro and areas of practice in turning and pirouettes. Analysis of placement for proper ballet form is emphasized along with artistry, strength and flexibility. Historical practices in ballet will be considered and contextualized against modern movements in ballet and the changing aesthetic of the form.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Open-Level Modern
courses.description: This course teaches modern dance technique focusing on the concepts of movement generation, alignment of the body for optimal performance of class material, analysis of the moving body and training in specific modern dance techniques to strengthen the dancer's ability to perform various modern dance modalities. Attention will be paid to artistry, musicality, skill attainment and how to process ideas about embodiment.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Aerial Dance
courses.description: This course teaches the technique of aerial dance on various apparatus including, static trapeze, aerial silks, corde lisse, and aerial sling. Particular attention is given to safety protocols, transitions from floor to the equipment, strength training drills, and aerial skills at the beginning and intermediate level. Various foot, hip and leg locks are taught, along with straddle inversions and variations on different climbing techniques.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Jazz Technique
courses.description: This course teaches jazz technique focusing on warm-up principles, center practice, performance aesthetic and artistry. Various forms of jazz dance will be explored and contextualized against one another as we examine the historical underpinnings and ever changing style of this versatile and all American form of dance.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Tap Technique
courses.description: This course teaches tap dance technique focusing on classical rhythmic and step structures and on improvisation and inventive choreographic principles of this dance form. Attention will be paid to clarity of sound, and rhythmic structure as well as the formal aspects of the visual presentation of the dance steps.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Flamenco Technique
courses.description: This course teaches the structural technical aspects of alignment and strength and flexibility training vital for dancers in all dance disciplines. Particular attention will be paid to full body alignment for optimal performance and body stability.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Pilates Technique
courses.description: This course teaches the structural technical aspects of alignment and strength and flexibility training vital for dancers in all dance disciplines. Particular attention will be paid to full body alignment for optimal performance and body stability.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Special Topics: Physical Practice
courses.description: A Super Course designed to house various forms of physical practice/technique not currently represented in the curriculum. Topics may include: somatic forms such as Alexander Technique, Yoga, Pilates: non-western dance forms such as West African, Flamenco, Kathak, Bhara Natyam, Korean Dance, Cambodian Dance, etc.; percussive forms such as Tap, Hoofing, or Clogging; or many other forms that may be the expertise of faculty, guest artists, visiting lecturers/professors, or graduate students.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Special Topics: Physical Practice Aerial Dance
courses.description: Special Topics: Physical Practice Aerial Dance is an introductory studio-based course focused on exercises to build integrated full body strength while using aerial silks and aerial hammock. Particular focus paid to transitions from the floor to the aerial apparatus and choreographic concepts in developing movement sequences.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Special Topics, Physical Practice: Bartenieff Fundamentals
courses.description: A studio course focused on Bartenieff Fundamentals; a somatic movement system developed by Irmgard Bartenieff. Designed to enhance movement efficiency by balancing functional integration with expressive potential, this method will serve as the foundation for our explorations. We will dive into Bartenieff’s six body developmental patterns, eight principles of action, four core themes, and basic six exercises, investigating how they shape movement connectivity, alignment, and energy flow. The course will also emphasize the sociocultural dimensions of movement practices, fostering critical reflection on how movement intersects with identity, community, and culture.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Special Topics, Physical Practice: Butoh
courses.description: A studio-based introduction to the physical practice and training modality of butoh. Developed in post-WWII Japan, butoh in the 21st century is a contemporary dance theater form with divergent lineages and global aesthetics. Students explore butoh through movement exercises and improvisation scores with an emphasis on presence, imagination, and transformation.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Open-level Ballet Physical Practice
courses.description: Open-level Ballet Physical Practice is an introductory studio-based course focused on various ballet technique forms. This course covers all elements of standard ballet classesincluding barre, center, and petit and grand allegro.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Special Topics, Physical Practice: Conditioning/Pilates
courses.description: A dedicated study and practice or pilates-based body conditioning and injury prevention. Offered early in the day, this course serves as a warm-up, tune-up and injury prevention for a dance students overall practice. Skills and conditioning sequences learned will be helpful beyond the course, and overall a greater awareness and maintenance of the body as the instrument of dance is a central objective.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Physical Practice: Embodying Activism
courses.description: This praxis-based course invites student artists to explore what activism means to them through embodiment tools and movement practices. Emphasizing physicality as a central method of inquiry, students critically examine how activism can be integrated into their creative processes, professional paths, and spheres of influence. By the end of the course, students will have developed a personal, evolving definition of “embodying activism” and identified strategies for practicing activism in their daily lives.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Special Topics: Physical Practice-Flamenco
courses.description: A studio-based, physical practice exploration of flamenco. Using the basic comps (rhythmic structures) of flamenco, we explore the different components of flamenco dance technique: floreo (hand movements) brazeo/braceo (arm movements), palmas (rhythmic hand-clapping), marcaje (marking, or movement through space), vueltas (turns) and zapateado (footwork). Students learn basic technical elements, short sections of choreography and may be offered supplemental readings and viewings by some of flamencos most celebrated artists to contextualize the technical practice of the form.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Special Topics, Physical Practice: Jazz Technique
courses.description: A studio-based dance technique course designed for dance majors. The focus of the class is the study of jazz dance technique including technical basics, progressions, skills, and phrase work rooted in the jazz dance idiom. Styles and approaches will vary by instructor.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Open-level Modern/Contemporary Physical Practice
courses.description: Open-level Modern/Contemporary Physical Practice is an introductory studio-based course exploring various movement modalities in the area of modern and contemporary dance technique. Investigates different initiations for moment within the body, energetic flow, rhythmic form and structure and the building blocks of anatomically healthy movement practices in various styles within modern dance.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Special Topics, Physical Practice:  Artist Performance (Stage/TV/Film)
courses.description: This course will focus on elevating the students' performance by translating the information and history they have learned into performance on stage, tv, and film. Through choreographic exploratory, students will explore the differences in the performance implementations and how it impacts using their artistic voice. Beyond learning choreography, this exploration and practical application will improve and help the student to be more efficient in using their artistic voice to communicate their message to the world through the different media platforms. The student will ultimately improve their performance because they have a more in-depth connection to the history and technical forms of art.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Special Topics: Physical Practice Tap
courses.description: Special Topics: Physical Practice Tap is an introductory studio-based study of percussive dance forms rooted in American Vernacular Dance. Emphasis placed on musicality, expression, improvisation, and rhythmic structure.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Yoga
courses.description: This course provides a physically-accessible movement experience while drawing upon foundational principles, and will introduce the fundamentals of a yoga practice (breath, proper alignment, and mindfulness practices.) With a focus on the foundations of postures, a combination of mobility, strength, and alignment drills that enhance any level of practitioner, this course is designed for those interested in developing more awareness in breath and movement. The course will focus on pranayama, mindful movement, making what we learn on the mat relevant to our daily lives, small meditations, and some chanting. This course is useful for those trying to work around injuries.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Group Studies for Lower-Division Dance Students
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 16 units, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: Group studies in selected areas of emphasis.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Independent Study in Dance
courses.prereq_text: Consent of instructor and department; completion of lower-division dance history course.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
courses.description: Independent study in dance. Projects in pedagogy, choreography or dance research.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Masculinities In/As Performance
courses.description: Upper division seminar exploring the intersection of multiple masculinities IN performance (dance, theater, performance art, film/TV, internet platforms, and more), and AS performance. Topics include maleness/masculinity as a social construct, considerations of masculinity in adolescent development and pedagogy, implications of race and class: marginalized masculinities, female masculinity, trans-masculinity, and more. These lenses are then employed to consider how masculinity forms identity and frames representation in various performative platforms.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Street Dance Forms
courses.description: Focuses on the various forms of street dance: Hip Hop, House Dance, Popping, Locking, Whacking, Punking, Voguing, and Freestyle. Students learn the physical lexicon of the various styles, and are immersed in the cultural aspects of the forms, contextualizing the dances both historically and socially. With a strong focus on accurately embodying the essence of each style, the class breaks down the initiation of motion and pathways of energy that result in these unique and specialized modes.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Critical Topics in Dance History: Ballet in Global Perspective
courses.description: Upper division seminar that studies the historical relationship of ballet dancing to the body politic from the global economies of Italian city-states through Louis XIVs use of ballet as weapon of state to revolutionary Russia whose exiled artists dispersed contemporary ballet worldwide.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Dancing the Diaspora: Dances of the Afro-Caribbean and American Worlds
courses.description: Upper division seminar that traces a genealogy of dance and choreographic practice from West Africa throughout the Afro-Caribbean during the transatlantic slave trade and into the Southern, Midwestern and Northeastern states of the U.S. We will study the Africanist presence in the body from Brazil to Cuba to New Orleans to New York City.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Race, Immigration, and Contemporary American Dance
courses.description: Race, Ballet, and Contemporary American Dance is a quarter-long, upper division Dance Studies course that examines how racism has shaped artistic practice and perception of the dancing body in both classical and contemporary dance.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Dance as Social Protest: Art, Dance & Film, 1955 1975
courses.description: Upper division seminar that traces a history of Postmodern, site-specific dance in California and New York and focuses specifically on 3 seminal American artists: Anna Halprin, Simone Forti and Yvonne Rainer.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Choreography
courses.description: Analysis of the elements of choreographic form; styles and trends; experience in development of dance studies; theory and technique of advanced choreography. Part A focuses on formal devices and developmental tools of dance composition, and introduces duet form.

courses.title: Choreography
courses.description: Analysis of the elements of choreographic form; styles and trends; experience in development of dance studies; theory and technique of advanced group choreography. Part B taps more broadly into the methods and theories behind dance composition and movement invention and interrogates multiple points of entry into the making process. Self-solo, duet and trio form is explored.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Choreography
courses.description: Analysis of the elements of choreographic form; styles and trends; experience in development of dance studies; theory and technique of advanced group choreography. Known as Kinetic Lab, Part C functions as a choreographic workshop for student choreographers to synthesize the creative tools, techniques and methods learned in previous choreography courses to begin to find an individualized aesthetic voice, and approach to creative practice.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Digital Editing for Dance
courses.description: A video skill-building course that introduces students to non-linear editing software and video camera operation. Drawing upon choreographic principles, students will create short film projects expanding their compositional proficiency and their technical knowledge of video editing tools.

courses.title: Advanced Improvisation
courses.comments: May be repeated once for credit for a maximum of 4 units. Only two units may be applied for credit in the major.
courses.description: An Advanced-level studio course focusing on various approaches and applications of dance improvisation. Topics covered include solo and group improvisation, score building and utilization, contact improvisation (CI), and improvisation for performance and site-specificwork. Students are assigned readings and viewings to ground their work in the classroom within past and current theory and improvisational practices.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Integrated Dance Partnering
courses.description: An Upper Division, intermediate/advanced study of the skills, mechanics and intersection of multiple partnering dance forms. Integrated Partnering will draw from contact improvisation, ballet and contemporary partnering in order to develop a broad understanding, and adaptable command of partnering. Beyond foundational mechanics, conditioning and safe practices, the course delves into selected repertory phrase workand partnered work in collaborative, compositional, and improvisational capacities; supporting the practical application of skills in a professional rehearsal context.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Embodied Anatomy
courses.description: For dancers and individuals interested in studying human anatomy from a dancer's perspective, including scientific information, experiential practice, and a focus on both the body's physical structure and its kinetic possibilities. Brings awareness to how we synthesize time and space in order to move rhythmically, create coherent shapes, locomote through space and organize complex coordination of multiple systems within the body. Anatomical awareness helps with injury prevention and offers one a more meaningful relationship to their human form.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Senior Solo Experimental Performance: Workshop in Creative Practice
courses.comments: Course cannot be repeated for additional units.
courses.description: Project development techniques, exploring modes of creative expression through various art disciplines and live performance techniques. Students engage in weekly workshops and discussions to build a tool kit for innovative dance creation.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Senior Solo Experimental Performance: Multimedia Project Development
courses.comments: Course cannot be repeated for additional units.
courses.description: Individually researched performance projects. Engaging with dance, music, theater, object-based storytelling, video projection, visual art and world building techniques. Students create a unique one-person show/presentation to be shared in a live public performance ant the end of the quarter. Based primarily in one on one mentor-ship through the process of devising and refining the final project.
