courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Intermediate Aerial Dance
courses.description: Intermediate Aerial Dance expanding understanding of exercises to build integrated full body strength while using aerial silks and aerial hammock. Particular focus paid to creating longer movement sequences that use both floor elements and apparatus based elements.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Special Topics, Physical Practice: Bartenieff Fundamentals
courses.description: A studio course focused on Bartenieff Fundamentals; a somatic movement system developed by Irmgard Bartenieff. Designed to enhance movement efficiency by balancing functional integration with expressive potential, this method will serve as the foundation for our explorations. We will dive into Bartenieff’s six body developmental patterns, eight principles of action, four core themes, and basic six exercises, investigating how they shape movement connectivity, alignment, and energy flow. The course will also emphasize the sociocultural dimensions of movement practices, fostering critical reflection on how movement intersects with identity, community, and culture.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Special Topics, Physical Practice: Butoh
courses.description: A studio-based introduction to the physical practice and training modality of butoh. Developed in post-WWII Japan, butoh in the 21st century is a contemporary dance theater form with divergent lineages and global aesthetics. Students explore butoh through movement exercises and improvisation scores with an emphasis on presence, imagination, and transformation.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Open-level Ballet Physical Practice
courses.description: Open-level Ballet Physical Practice is an intermediate/advanced studio-based course focused on various ballet technique forms. This course covers all elements of standard ballet classesincluding barre, center, and petit and grand allegro.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Special Topics, Physical Practice: Conditioning/Pilates
courses.description: A dedicated study and practice or pilates-based body conditioning and injury prevention. Offered early in the day, this course serves as a warm-up, tune-up and injury prevention for a dance students overall practice. Skills and conditioning sequences learned will be helpful beyond the course, and overall a greater awareness and maintenance of the body as the instrument of dance is a central objective.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Physical Practice: Embodying Activism
courses.description: This praxis-based course invites student artists to explore what activism means to them through embodiment tools and movement practices. Emphasizing physicality as a central method of inquiry, students critically examine how activism can be integrated into their creative processes, professional paths, and spheres of influence. By the end of the course, students will have developed a personal, evolving definition of “embodying activism” and identified strategies for practicing activism in their daily lives.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Special Topics: Physical Practice-Flamenco
courses.description: A studio-based, physical practice exploration of flamenco. Using the basic comps (rhythmic structures) of flamenco, we explore the different components of flamenco dance technique: floreo (hand movements) brazeo/braceo (arm movements), palmas (rhythmic hand-clapping), marcaje (marking, or movement through space), vueltas (turns) and zapateado (footwork). Students learn basic technical elements, short sections of choreography and may be offered supplemental readings and viewings by some of flamencos most celebrated artists to contextualize the technical practice of the form.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Special Topics, Physical Practice: Jazz Technique
courses.description: A studio-based dance technique course designed for dance majors. The focus of the class is the study of jazz dance technique including technical basics, progressions, skills, and phrase work rooted in the jazz dance idiom. Styles and approaches will vary by instructor.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Open-level Modern/Contemporary Physical Practice
courses.description: Open-level Modern/Contemporary Physical Practice is an intermediate/advanced studio-based course exploring various movement modalities in the area of modern and contemporary dance technique, and builds on the skills learned in the lower-division level. Continued Investigations in different initiations for moment within the body, energetic flow, rhythmic form and structure and the building blocks of anatomically healthy movement practices in various styles within modern dance.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Special Topics, Physical Practice:  Artist Performance (Stage/TV/Film)
courses.description: This course will focus on elevating the students' performance by translating the information and history they have learned into performance on stage, tv, and film. Through choreographic exploratory, students will explore the differences in the performance implementations and how it impacts using their artistic voice. Beyond learning choreography, this exploration and practical application will improve and help the student to be more efficient in using their artistic voice to communicate their message to the world through the different media platforms. The student will ultimately improve their performance because they have a more in-depth connection to the history and technical forms of art.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Special Topics: Physical Practice Tap
courses.description: Special Topics: Physical Practice Tap is an intermediate/advanced studio-based study of percussive dance forms rooted in American Vernacular Dance. Emphasis placed on musicality, expression, improvisation, and rhythmic structure.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Yoga
courses.description: This course provides a physically-accessible movement experience while drawing upon foundational principles, and will introduce the fundamentals of a yoga practice (breath, proper alignment, and mindfulness practices.) With a focus on the foundations of postures, a combination of mobility, strength, and alignment drills that enhance any level of practitioner, this course is designed for those interested in developing more awareness in breath and movement. The course will focus on pranayama, mindful movement, making what we learn on the mat relevant to our daily lives, small meditations, and some chanting. This course is useful for those trying to work around injuries.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Dance Production
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units.
courses.description: Exploration of the process of collaboration between dance choreographers and theatre designers in the development of designs for dance productions. Final project will be a public performance of the choreographers' and designers' work.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: UCSB Dance Company
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit for a maximum of 16 units, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: Selected students work as dancers in the UCSB Dance Company, studying and analyzing choreography through rehearsal and performance. The company performs locally and/or on tour. Students experience the integral workings of a touring dance company.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Senior Project
courses.description: Choreographic or performance project produced as the culminating presentation for the B.F.A. degree. Course includes detailed documentation of the procedure followed during the creation of the final project, and results in a written and visual document following a closely crafted prompt.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Senior Honors Project
courses.comments: This course is for students who will complete their projects in one quarter. A final grade will be assigned upon completion. Students must have a 3.0 university grade-point average; 3.4 departmental grade-point average, unless exempt by petition; faculty nomination.
courses.description: Senior honors project. Advanced thesis project in either academic research or creative activity, supervised by a faculty advisor. Students successfully completing the project, as evaluated by a three-person committee, will graduate with distinction in the major.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Senior Honors Project
courses.comments: Students must have a 3.0 university GPA; 3.4 departmental GPA, unless exempt by petition; faculty nomination. A three quarter "in-progress" course with grades assigned upon completion of Dance 193HC.
courses.description: Senior honors project. Advanced thesis project in either academic research or creative activity, supervised by a faculty advisor. Students successfully completing the project, as evaluated by a three-person committee, graduate with distinction in the major.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Senior Honors Project
courses.comments: Students must have a 3.0 university grade-point average; 3.4 departmental grade-point average, unless exempt by petition; faculty nomination. A three quarter "in-progress" course with grades assigned upon completion of Dance 193HC.
courses.description: Senior honors project. Advanced thesis project in either academic research or creative activity, supervised by a faculty advisor. Students successfully completing the project, as evaluated by a three-person committee, will graduate with distinction in the major.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Senior Honors Project
courses.comments: Students must have a 3.0 university grade-point average; 3.4 departmental grade-point average, unless exempt by petition; faculty nomination. A three quarter "in-progress" course with grades assigned upon completion of Dance 193HC.
courses.description: Senior honors project. Advanced thesis project in either academic research or creative activity, supervised by a faculty advisor. Students successfully completing the project, as evaluated by a three-person committee, will graduate with distinction in the major.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Group Studies in Dance
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units.
courses.description: Group projects in selected areas of emphasis.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: SBDT Apprentice/Mentor Program
courses.description: Prepares students for professional work in the field of dance. Apprentices will join with professional dancers in UC Santa Barbaras resident professional dance company, Santa Barbara Dance Theater, to rehearse choreographic works, with the possibility of performing in studio showings, repertory previews and the companys concerts on and off campus. These experiences are expected to raise each apprentices awareness of collaborative methods and professional standards of performance artistry.The artistic director of Santa Barbara Dance Theater will be designated as the instructor of record, with mentoring and coordinating assistance from one or more company members.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Independent Study in Dance
courses.prereq_text: Consent of instructor and department; upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division courses in Dance.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quaters and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
courses.description: Independent study in dance. Projects in choreography or dance research.

courses.subject: DANCE
courses.title: Independent Research Assistance in Dance
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division courses in Dance; consent of instructor and department.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
courses.description: Independent research assistance in dance. Supervised assistance in faculty research project.

courses.subject: DANCEW
courses.title: History of Modern Dance and Contemporary Performance
courses.comments: This course is the online version of DANCE 36.
courses.description: Historical development of modern dance in the United States and Europe in the twentieth century. Emphasis on visionary, feminist, and radical aspects of the form.

courses.subject: DYNS
courses.title: Special Interest Group Research Seminar
courses.prereq_text: Only students in the Dynamical Neuroscience Program may register for this course. Other students interested in registering must have prior approval of the chair.
courses.description: Research seminar for special interest groups in dynamical neuroscience.

courses.subject: DYNS
courses.title: Directed Reading and Research in Dynamical Neuroscience
courses.description: Provides supervised experience in experimental design and laboratory procedures on selected topics, including the formulation of experimental problems, discussion of relevant literature and the analysis and interpretation of experimental results.

courses.subject: DYNS
courses.title: Dissertation Research and Preparation
courses.description: Empirical and theoretical investigations of special problems in dynamical neuroscience in relation to dissertation research.

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: Introduction to Asian Religious Traditions
courses.comments: EACS 3 and Religious Studies 3 are the same course.
courses.description: An introduction to the basic texts, institutions, and practices of the religious traditions of South Asia and East Asia.

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: East Asian Traditions: Pre-modern
courses.description: An introduction to the social structures, institutions, systems of thought and belief, and the arts and entertainments of China, Japan, Korea and their neighbors during the pre-modern period.

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: East Asian Traditions: Modern
courses.description: An introduction to the study of China, Japan, Korea, and their neighbors in modern times, including the process of modernization, intellectual and political movements, national identity, literature and the arts, and popular culture.

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: Introduction to Buddhism
courses.comments: Religious Studies 5 and East Asian Cultural Studies 5 are the same course.
courses.description: The historical and cross-cultural exploration of Buddhism through the examination of basic texts, institutions, and practices of diverse Buddhist traditions.

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: Zen Buddhism
courses.comments: Religious Studies 21 and EACS 21 are the same course.
courses.description: An introduction to the history and texts of the major lineages of Ch`an Buddhism in China and Zen Buddhism in Japan.

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: Gender and Sexuality in Modern Asia
courses.description: Examines how modern social institutions have constructed and transformed gender and sexuality in China, Japan, Korea, India, and other Asian societies. Topics: marriage and kinship, capitalism, nationalism, modern state, third genders, commercialization of sex, public sphere and mass media.

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: Young Humans: Introduction to Childhood Studies
courses.comments: EACS 41 and C LIT 40 are the same course.
courses.description: An introduction to interdisciplinary approaches to understanding and analyzing childhood and youth, including history of childhood, and childrens literature research, this course considers the role of childhood in human life, its construction across different periods and regions, different disciplinary perspectives on childhood, and contemporary approaches to deepening the understanding of children and their own views. By examining key critical texts, it considers childhood through multiple disciplinary perspectives, as well as childrens own co-creation of the performance of childhood and childrens voice, agency, activism, and rights.

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: Introduction to Daoism
courses.comments: EACS 47 and Religious Studies 47 are the same course.
courses.description: A study of the classical sources of Daoism, followed by a consideration of the varieties of religious practice which developed from those sources.

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: Sex, Science, and Society: A Global History
courses.description: Survey of the relationship between sex, science, and society in the history of the modern world. Emphasis on the development of scientific ideas about the human body against broader social, cultural, and political trends and from a global viewpoint.

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: Chinese Civilization
courses.comments: History 80 and East Asian Cultural Studies 80 are the same course.
courses.description: A survey of the history of Chinese civilization from 2,000 BCE to the present, focusing on the origins and later development of political, social, economic, philosophical, religious, and cultural traditions.

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: Independent Research Assistance on Asia
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA. Limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
courses.description: Research details are decided by the supervising Professor in the Department of East Asian Languages and Cultural Studies.

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: Anthropology of China
courses.description: This course adopts an anthropological approach to contemporary China through ethnographic research. Topics include: Maoist society, rural life, migrant workers, gender and sexuality, media culture, youth culture, the urban work unit, from Maoist class-status system to capitalist class structure.

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: Anthropology of Japan
courses.comments: Same course as Anthropology 103B.
courses.description: This course examines Japan as depicted in contemporary ethnography. We consider how Japan has been imagined as a distinct culture by exploring gender, religion, family structures, the education system, the environment, management of difference, globalization and domestication, immigration, and modernization.

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: Anthropology of Contemporary Korea
courses.comments: Students who have completed KOR 82 should not enroll in EACS 103C.
courses.description: This course is an introduction to contemporary Korea covering the major societal transformations since the Korean War. Topics include nationalism, the creation of national symbols and racial identity, family, marriage, consumption, television dramas, globalization, tourism, and new Korean Wave.

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: Christianity, Judaism, and Islam in China
courses.description: Examines Christian, Jewish, and Muslim communities in the Middle Kingdom from 500 to the present day, debunking the myth of a closed and insular China.

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: Religious Environmentalism in the Anthropocene: Asia & U.S.
courses.description: What can ancient religious traditions do for environmental protection? This class examines doctrinal examples, both potential and actual, of religious environmentalism in China, India, Japan, and the U.S.: with Buddhism, Daoism, Hinduism, Shinto, and Protestantism.

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: Global East Asia
courses.description: Offers an overview of theories about migration and globalization, coupled with the case studies from contemporary East Asia. Students investigate diverse transnational issues in and from this region, including ethnicity, nationalism, kinship, homeland, and colonialism.

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: Social Movements in East Asia
courses.description: This course engages with cultural histories of social movements and political protests in modern and contemporary East Asia. All reading, viewing, and listening material will be available in English translation.

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: Transpacific Literature
courses.comments: ENGL 133TL, C LIT 133, and EACS 133 are the same course.
courses.description: Looks at the Pacific as the primary location for literary and historical imagination since the Age of Exploration. Studies the crisscross, transpacific field of inscriptions ranging from Captain Cook to Herman Melville, Mark Twain, Jack London, and Maxine Hong Kingston.

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: Literary Adaptation in East Asia
courses.description: Explores literary adaptation and intertextuality in East Asia through primary texts and readings from critical theory. Among the texts considered are traditional poetry, The Tale of Genji, Chinese "strange tales" and representations of history and literature in film.

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: Introduction to Daoism
courses.comments: EACS 147T and RG ST 147T are the same course.
courses.description: A study of the classical sources of Daoism, followed by a consideration of the varieties of religious practice which developed from those sources.

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: Medical Humanities in East Asia
courses.description: Major concepts and issues at the intersection of healthcare and the humanities in modern East Asia. Topics may include narrative medicine, medicalization, body/embodiment, medical pluralism, mental health, social justice, and interdisciplinary approaches to systems of treatment and healing.

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: Sinophone Studies
courses.description: The study of Sinitic-language communities and cultures around the world, marked by heterogeneity, placed-based practices, and differentiated relations to geopolitical units. Emphases will be on the questions of power, colonialism, hierarchy, resistance, plurality, and interdisciplinarity.

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: East Asian Buddhist Poetry
courses.description: Introduces Buddhist poetry of China, Japan, and Korea. Emphasizes the diversity of literary encounters with the teachings and practices of Buddhism. Topics include Hanshan, Basho, Zen koans, Gary Snyder, and monastery cats.

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: The Modern Girl Around the World
courses.description: Examines the Modern Girl as a historical phenomenon of the early twentieth century from the combined perspective of global history and gender history.

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: Buddhist Political Thought and Institutions
courses.comments: EACS 176 and RG ST 176 are the same course.
courses.description: Buddhist political theories and practices in various Asian countries from antiquity to the present, with special emphasis on ideas of kinship and republicanism, state-formation process, cultural identity, and the interactions with other religions.

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: Visual Culture of Buddhism
courses.comments: EACS 179 and Religious Studies 179 are the same course.
courses.description: This course explores the rich world of Buddhist visual culture, ranging from meditation to addressing the use of painted images in public performances. It focuses on sacred images, their rituals, and theories of representation behind their creation and use.

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: Special Topics in East Asian Studies
courses.description: Special topics in East Asian Studies. Course content varies.

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: Transnational East Asian Cinemas and Food Culture
courses.description: Examines how food, production and consumption, and the related socio-political issues have been represented in East Asian cinemas. Students specifically look at how films illustrate the relationship between food and culture, familial relationships, generational conflicts, class struggle, and personal identities. Students explore narrative, visual, and symbolic uses of food in the context of popular culture and transnationalism. No prior knowledge of film studies is required. All films are subtitled.

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: Critical Childhood Studies
courses.comments: C LIT 182 and EACS 182 are the same course
courses.description: This seminar/capstone course on critical childhood studies will examine the burgeoning field of childhood studies across time periods and regions, employing varied disciplinary approaches to the study of childhood, including literary studies, history, art history, sociology, and other disciplines. Assignments will include weekly responses, leading a discussion of a scholarly work, a final paper on a subject related to student interest, and a presentation of the final paper topic.

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: Internship
courses.description: This internship allows students to collaborate with philanthropic, non-profit, and for-profit organizations that are based locally, nationally or globally. Working on-site or remotely, students learn practical implications of a degree in EALCS and in the Humanities more generally, and they have the opportunity to utilize their knowledge of technology and of foreign languages and cultures. While contributing to the organization and its initiatives, students gain valuable experience that can lead to career choices after graduation. Up to 4 units of internship can count towards an EALCS major or minor. Please see the EALCS website for information on arranging internships and for expectations regarding receiving internship credit.

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: Independent Study in Asian Studies
courses.prereq_text: Upper division standing; completion of 2 upper division EACS courses; at least one of those two courses taken with the instructor for EACS 199; GPA for those two courses 3.5 or higher.
courses.comments: Students must have 3.0 GPA overall. Limit of 5 units/quarter and 30 units overall of any independent studies.
courses.description: Independent Study under the supervision of a faculty member.

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: Readings in Selected Texts
courses.prereq_text: Consent of instructor, graduate status is required.
courses.description: Course will center on readings of East Asian texts; type and period to depend on needs of students and wishes of instructor. Research methods to be taught as appropriate.

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: Canon Formation, Periodization, and Disciplinarity in East Asian Studies
courses.description: An analysis of classical, medieval, and modern sets of "canons" including myth historiography, literature and the arts, with a view to question the way they were mutually distinguished (disciplinary) and changed through time (periodization) recognizing both internal conceptions and external influences.

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: Topics in East Asian Cultural Studies
courses.description: As a forum for the practice of discussion, critique, and writing, this seminar takes up broad topics within the study of East Asian cultures in an interdisciplinary manner.

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: Sonic Modernities in East Asia
courses.description: Traces the emergent study of sound in modern East Asian studies across literature, music, performance, and media studies. We engage with recent English-language scholarly publications (articles, monographs) as well as archival materials from Japan, Korea, and China.

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: Religious Environmentalism in the Anthropocene
courses.description: What can ancient religious traditions do for environmental protection? This class examines doctrinal potentials and actual examples of religious environmentalism in China, India, Japan, and the U.S.: with Buddhism, Daoism, Hinduism, Shinto, and Protestantism.

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: East Asian Buddhist Poetry
courses.description: Introduces Buddhist poetry of China, Japan, and Korea. Emphasizes the diversity of literary encounters with the teachings and practices of Buddhism. Topics include Hanshan, Basho, Zen koans, Gary Snyder, and monastery cats. Graduate students will receive extra readings from their instructor and will complete a longer research paper at the end of the course

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Seminar in special areas of interest in East Asian cultural studies. Specific course titles and topics to be announced by the department each quarter offered. Course content will vary.

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: Internship
courses.description: These internships allow students to collaborate with philanthropic and non-profit organizations, nationally and globally. Working digitally or on site with the organization, students learn about practical implications of a degree in Religious Studies and in the Humanities more generally. They also have the opportunity to utilize their knowledge of foreign languages and technology. While helping to make the world a better place, students gain valuable experience that can be applied to their chosen career after graduation.

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: Directed Reading and Research
courses.comments: Misc: Letter grade; minimum of two units per quarter.
courses.description: Individual tutorial.

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: Preparation for Comprehensive/Qualifying Examinations
courses.comments: No unit credit allowed toward degree.
courses.description: Preparation for MA comprehensive examinations and/or PhD qualifying examinations.

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: Master's Thesis Research and Preparation
courses.comments: Maximum of 12 units total. No unit credit allowed toward master's degree.
courses.description: Research, preparation, and writing of the master's thesis.

courses.subject: EACS
courses.title: Ph.D. Dissertation Preparation
courses.description: Terminal preparation of the dissertation.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Principles of Physical Geology
courses.comments: Course materials fee charged.
courses.description: Introduction to the science of the Earth; properties and processes of its surface and interior, including plate tectonics, volcanism, earthquakes, glaciation, mountain building, formation of rocks, minerals, and the structural basis of landforms. Lab and lecture each offering. There can be an additional 1 day local field trip.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Principles of Historical Geology
courses.description: Antiquity and history of the Earth from an Earth system history approach. Focus is on processes and changes over time of the Earth's lithosphere, biosphere, atmosphere, and hydrosphere.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Introduction to Oceanography
courses.comments: Course materials fee required.
courses.description: An introduction to oceanography covering the major physical, chemical, and geological features of the oceans, their role in Earth history, and potential use as a natural resource. Lab and lecture.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Mountains, Boots, and Backpacks: Field Study of the High Sierra
courses.comments: Need ability to hike 1-2 hours/day. Course materials fee charged. Instructor approval required to finalize registration. Priority enrollment to freshmen and sophomores.
courses.description: Ten-day, off-campus, field-based investigation of faults, volcanoes, glaciers, rivers, and related geologic processes in the Sierra Nevada and nearby mountains. Emphasis on observations; analysis of geologic and environmental field data. Held in September before the start of Fall Quarter classes.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Dinosaurs
courses.description: The origin and diversification of dinosaurs, including birds. Survey of evolutionary relationships within the group, and between the major groups of vertebrates. Broad introduction including anatomy, geography, climate, and vertebrate contemporaries.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Giant Earthquakes
courses.description: Study of the character and causes of large earthquakes, the hazards they pose, and how society can prepare for and mitigate their impacts. Historical case studies will illuminate why their slip characteristics and destructive effects vary so widely.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Antarctica: The Last Place on Earth
courses.comments: Course materials fee charged.
courses.description: The interrelations of the physical and biological environments on the continent Antarctica; Antarctica as an Earth system. Included are studies of tectonic history, global warming, ozone depletion, mineral resources, and the history of scientific exploration of the continent.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Volcanoes and Humans
courses.description: An introduction to volcanism and its consequences. Origins and physical processes of volcanism; the natural benefits of volcanoes; volcanic hazards and disasters; volcanoes in human history, society, and culture; volcanoes and climate; volcano monitoring and hazard mitigation.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Climate Change: Lessons from the Past
courses.description: Introduction to the fundamental forces that shape and modulate the Earth's climate. Learning about climate forcings (solar insolation, albedo, greenhouse effect, ocean circulation) will provide a scientific basis to understand past, current, and future climate changes.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Field Studies in Geological Sciences
courses.comments: Course Materials Fee charged.
courses.description: Four to five day field trip, fall and/or spring quarters. Field studies under guidance of two or three staff members introducing the geology of California.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Geology of Yosemite Valley
courses.comments: Course materials fee charged. Open to lower division students.
courses.description: Introduction to the geology, surface processes, glacial history, and environmental geology of Yosemite valley. The four-day field trip includes one day in the lower Yosemite valley, and one day in the upper valley.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Geological Catastrophes
courses.comments: Course materials fee required.
courses.description: Course deals with geologic catastrophes, e.g., earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, tsunamis, and landslides. Students will learn the basic physical causes of these naturally occurring events and discuss the consequences.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: The History of Life
courses.description: Examination of the geological and biological processes affecting the evolution of life on Earth from 3.8 billion years ago to the present. Strong emphasis on the nature of the scientific method as a way of understanding natural history.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Geoscience Communication
courses.comments: Students may not enroll in Earth 60W and Earth 160 in the same quarter.
courses.description: Introduction to written and verbal communication skills in the Earth Sciences. Students attend the weekly department colloquium or other Earth Science related presentations, and read and discuss related articles. Weekly assignments develop scientific writing skills.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Readings in Geological Sciences
courses.comments: Students are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
courses.description: Critical reviews and discussions of selected geological subjects.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Independent Studies
courses.description: Independent research conducted under guidance of Earth Science faculty. Topic and scope varies, to be specified by student and supervisory faculty member prior to registration.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Introduction to Geophysics
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 4A and 4B; and Phys 7A and 7B, or Physics 1, 2, and 3 (may be taken concurrently), or Phys 21, 22, and 23, or Physics 6A-B-C (may be taken concurrently).
courses.comments: Concurrently offered with Earth 200
courses.description: Survey of major topics in geophysics at an elementary level; the figure of the Earth, its gravitational and magnetic fields, seismology and the deep structure of the Earth, heat flow, methods of geophysical exploration. The geophysical basis of plate tectonics and sea floor spreading.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Practical Research Skills
courses.comments: Course materials fee charged.
courses.description: A hands-on introduction to research methods in the Earth and other natural sciences. Tools and approaches to identify research questions, design projects, and get involved in research opportunities. Involves a single-day local field trip.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Petrology of Igneous Rocks
courses.prereq_text: Earth 114 and 115 with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Introduction to the occurrence, associations, tectonics, and petrogenesis of plutonic and volcanic rocks. Introduction to the physical chemistry of magma systems; magmatic crystallization and differentiation; pluton emplacement, volcanic eruption mechanisms. Lab and lecture each offering. There can be an additional 1 day local field trip.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Metamorphic Petrology
courses.prereq_text: Earth 114 and 115 with a grade of C or better.
courses.comments: Course materials fee required.
courses.description: Study of metamorphic rocks to understand tectonic processes. Metamorphic minerals, metamorphic textures, physical processes responsible for metamorphism, phase equilibria, thermodynamics, diffusion, thermobarometry, kinetics, geochronology, and high-temperature rock deformation. Lecture and lab.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Fundamentals of Structural Geology
courses.prereq_text: Earth 104A or Earth 104G, and Earth 114 with a grade of C or better; Math 2B or 3B (may be taken concurrently); Physics 6A or 1 or 7A
courses.comments: Course materials fee charged.
courses.description: Deformation of rocks--faulting, folding and flow. Theory and observations at scales ranging from mountain belts to microscopic. Lab, lecture and field trip(s). The field component consists of 1-2 one day trips and an overnight trip lasting 3-4 days.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Field Studies in Geological Methods
courses.comments: Course materials fee charged.
courses.description: Introduction to the methods of geological observations and interpretations, with an emphasis on understanding earth processes in the field and reconstructing the physical history of the earth; the stratigraphic, petrologic, and structural relations of rocks. Lecture, lab and field trips. The field trip portion consists of 6–8 one day trips and commonly an overnight trip lasting 3-4 days.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Field Methods
courses.prereq_text: Earth 114 and 103. All with a C- or better.
courses.comments: Course materials fee required.
courses.description: Geologic mapping on topographic maps and aerial photographs; use of geologic field instruments; field techniques; preparation of geologic maps and reports. Field work is completed during the break and between winter and spring quarters and consists of a 8-10 day overnight field trip.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Digital Analysis and Interpretation of Field Data
courses.description: Introduction to commonly used computer programs and techniques for analyzing and visualizing surface and subsurface spatial and structural data in the Earth Sciences. Local site visits involve hands-on demonstrations in geologic data collection. Introduction to scientific writing. Lecture and Lab. This course includes 2–3 local afternoon field trips.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Earths Climate: Past and Present
courses.description: Description and quantitative analysis of climate processes and paleoclimate proxies. Processes include radiation and the Earths energy budget, the influence of orbital cycles, ocean circulation, monsoons, ENSO, and ice sheets. Paleoclimate reconstructions from tectonic-scale to the last millennium, with emphasis on glacial cycles and Plio-Pleistocene climate evolution.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Introduction to Climate Modeling
courses.description: An introduction to climate models and their application to studies of past, modern, and future climate. Students will learn fundamental modeling concepts, gain experience running several kinds of models, and read/evaluate recent modeling papers. A variety of models will be introduced, with emphasis on atmosphere-ocean General Circulation Models (GCMs) and "simple"(zero-dimensional) models. No previous modeling or programming experience is required.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Geology of California
courses.comments: Course materials fee required. Field Trips required.
courses.description: Introduction to the geology, geologic history, tectonic evolution, and landscape development of California. A brief survey of California's petroleum, mineral, geothermal, and water resources. This course includes one or two overnight field trip(s) consisting of 2-5 days.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Principles of Paleontology
courses.comments: EARTH 111 and EEMB 136 are the same course. Letter grade required for majors. Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 111.
courses.description: The ecological structure and evolution of the biosphere as illustrated by the fossil record.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Principles of Paleontology Laboratory
courses.comments: Same course as EEMB 136L. Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 111L.
courses.description: Exercises and projects in the identification and interpretation of fossil taxa and fossil communities.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Engineering and Environmental Geology
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 3A-B or 2A-B or 34A-B ; and, Physics 1 or 6A or 7A or 21; upper-division standing.
courses.comments: Course fee charged. Environmental Studies 113 and EARTH 113 are the same course.
courses.description: Application of geologic and environmental principles to civil engineering problems. Includes: rock and soil mechanics; landslides; hydrology; earthquakes; and professional practice. Some offerings include a 1-2 day field trip.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Geomaterials
courses.description: Examination of geomaterials at atomic level. Atomic structure, states of matter, bonding, elementary phase equilibria. Composition and structure of atmosphere, hydrosphere, crust, mantle and core. Structure and composition of important geochemical compounds emphasizing rock-forming minerals.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Analytical Methods in Geomaterials
courses.prereq_text: Earth 114 with a grade of C or better
courses.comments: Course materials fee charged.
courses.description: Optical properties of inorganic crystals; techniques of mineral identification using the polarizing microscope; strategies for studying rocks in thin section. Fundamental theory and application of electron and ion-beam instruments in quantitative characterization of geomaterials. Laboratory sessions include lectures as appropriate. Some offerings include a one day field trip.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Earth Surface Processes and Landforms
courses.comments: Additional fieldwork (10 hours) required. Meets writing requirement. Course material fee charged.
courses.description: Introduction to the theory of landscape evolution and the study of the processes that create and modify landforms. Offerings sometimes include a 1-2 day field trip.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Summer Field Geology
courses.prereq_text: Earth 104A or 104G; and Earth 103, 104B, and 122. All prerequisites require a grade of C- or better.
courses.comments: Course materials fee charged.
courses.description: Intensive hands-on training in the collection, interpretation, and presentation of geologic field data. Preparation of geologic maps, sections, and a professional report as tools to understanding geologic processes. Area and focus of investigation changes each year. This is a 6 week field course out of the Santa Barbara area.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Field Investigations in Geology
courses.prereq_text: Earth 104A or 104G; and Earth 103, 104B, and 122. All prerequisites require a grade of C- or better.
courses.comments: Course materials fee charged.
courses.description: Selected field areas are investigated as research problems. Content varies from year to year. This is a 6 week field course out of the Santa Barbara area.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Principles of Evolution
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, MCDB 1B, EEMB 2 and EEMB 3 or EARTH 2 and 3; Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.comments: EARTH 121 and EEMB 131 are the same course. Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 131.
courses.description: A foundation course concerning the mechanisms of evolution at micro- and macroevolutionary levels, and interpretation of the resulting patterns of adaptation and organic diversity.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Sedimentation and Stratigraphy: Processes and Products
courses.prereq_text: Earth 2; and Earth 104A; and Earth 114. Field trip required.
courses.comments: Letter-grade required to apply toward major. Course materials fee required.
courses.description: Transport/depositional processes, sedimentary textures and structures. Sedimentary environments, using facies models for observation & prediction. Principles of lithostratigraphy, biostratigraphy, chronostratigraphy, and magnetostratigraphy. Seismic stratigraphy and sequence stratigraphic principles. Controls of tectonics, sediment supply and eustacy on sedimentation. Lab, lecture and field trip(s). The field component consists of some 1 day field trips and may include a 2-4 day overnight trip.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: The Solar System
courses.description: The nature and evolution of the planets of the solar system. Elementary treatment of cosmochemistry, meteoritics, and comparative planetology with special reference to current ideas on solar system evolution.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Environmental Geochemistry
courses.description: This course focuses on geochemical principles of key processes at Earth's surface environment. Course materials cover topics including the carbon cycle, mineral-water interactions, soil systems, erosion and weathering, and hydrological cycles. Students learn foundational theories, applications, and recent research progress to gain a comprehensive understanding of Earth's environment through the geochemical lens.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Geochronology
courses.comments: Concurrently Offered with Earth 224G.
courses.description: Principles of radiogenic isotope geochronology, and applications of the major geochronological methods to terrestrial and extraterrestrial problems ranging from global climate change to petrology to tectonics to solar system evolution. This is a five week course.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Biogeochemistry of Stable and Cosmogenic Isotopes
courses.prereq_text: Chemistry 1C; Mathematics 2A or 3A; Earth 2 or 3 or 4.
courses.description: Introduction to stable isotope biogeochemistry, including kinetic and thermodynamic fractionation of stable isotopes during evapo-precipitation, photosynthesis, and biogenic calcification. Applications of stable isotope in environmental sciences, Quarternary geology, paleoclimate, archeology. Introduction to mass spectrometry, cosmogenic and radiogenic isotopes and their application in paleoclimatology/paleoceanography.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Introduction to Geochemistry
courses.prereq_text: Earth 2 or 4; and Earth 114; and Chemistry 1A; and Math 3A-B or 2A-2B.
courses.description: Fundamental concepts of geochemistry including radiometric dating, inorganic chemistry, and biogeochemical cycling are introduced. The class examines how chemical principles can be used to solve geological and environmental problems. These concepts are illustrated using classical geology, global change, and hydrology.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Introductory Thermodynamics
courses.prereq_text: Chemistry 1C; and Mathematics 2B or 3B; and Earth 2.
courses.comments: Concurrently offered with Earth 224T.
courses.description: Introduction to thermodynamics and kinetics of rock-water systems. Calculation of mineral equilibria as a function of pressure temperature and fluid compositions. Applied problems at surface and subsurface conditions. This is a five week course.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Field Petrology
courses.prereq_text: Earth 104A and Earth 114; consent of instructor. All prerequisites require a grade of C or better.
courses.comments: Course materials fee charged.
courses.description: Field-based study of igneous, metamorphic and tectonic processes. Investigates different topics in igneous and metamorphic petrology each year, centered around field trips to key localities. Includes lectures, review of scientific literature, on-campus labs and field-based observations and measurements. The field trip for this course ranges from 4-18 days long and varies each offering.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Global Warming - Science and Society
courses.description: Introduction to the scientific and societal issues surrounding global climate change. Includes introduction to physical climatology, greenhouse effect, climate history, anthropogenic changes, and future predictions. Student discussion and debate on the potential societal scenarios available to mitigate future climate change.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Geophysical Time-Series Analysis
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 2A-B or 3A-B; and Mathematics 4A-B; and Physics 1 and 2, or Physics 6A-B-C, or Phys 7A and 7B, or Phys 21 and 22; and Earth 175 or Earth 232 or CMPSCI 8 and CPMSCI 16 or instructor approval.
courses.description: Time-series analysis and digital-signal processing for geophysicists. Course combines theory with practical application using MATLAB and/or Python. Topics include: sampling, the discrete Fourier transform, aliasing, convolution, filtering, power spectral density estimation, multivariate time-series analysis, and array processing.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Plate tectonics and mantle dynamics
courses.prereq_text: Earth 2; Mathematics 2A-B or 3A-B; and Mathematics 4A-B and Mathematics 6A (may be taken concurrently); Physics 7A and 7B and 7C (may be taken concurrently), or Physics 1 and 2, or Physics 6A-B-C, or Phys 21 and 22; and Earth 175 or Earth 232 or CMPSCI 8 and CMPSCI 16 or instructor approval.
courses.description: An advanced undergraduate course that takes a quantitative, physics-based approach to covering the details of plate tectonics and mantle dynamics. Using derivations at the level of Turcotte and Schubert (3Ed., 2014), the course gives undergraduates a high level understanding of the principles that govern plate strength, and the connections between plates and Earth's deep interior. Weekly lectures cover course material, while readings and take-home assignments help reinforce the concepts covered in class; discussion sections give participants the opportunity to talk through the assignments and the readings and to work through practical problem sets.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Introduction to Geological and Geophysical Data Analysis
courses.description: Various numerical methods for analysis of data are developed. Methods are statistical inference, error propagation, least squares, time series as applied to geological and geophysical examples. Lab and lecture.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Principles of Geophysics
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 2A-B or 3A-B; and Mathematics 4A-B; and Mathematics 6A (may be taken concurrently); and, Physics 1 and 2, or Physics 6A-B-C, or Phys 7A and 7B, or Phys 21 and 22; and Earth 175 or Earth 232 or CMPSCI 8 and CMPSCI 16 or instructor approval.
courses.description: Basic principles in geophysics from elasticity theory, fluid dynamics, gravity, magnetism, and heat flow. Their applications to various processes in the Earth.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Geophysics (Seismology)
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 2A-B or 3A-B; and Mathematics 4A-B and Mathematics 6A (may be taken concurrently); Physics 7A and 7B and 7C (may be taken concurrently), or Physics 1 and 2, or Physics 6A-B-C, or Phys 21 and 22 and 23 (may be taken concurrently).
courses.description: Wave propagation in an elastic medium; reflection and refraction, attenuation physics of the earthquake source, magnitude, seismic moment and focal mechanisms.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Quantitative Geomorphology
courses.description: Basic quantitative understanding of processes shaping Earth's surface. In-depth evaluation of hill slope diffusion, mass wasting, and fluvial processes. Applications of quantitative methods are emphasized throughout class. Laboratory provides understanding of isotopic, physical, and remote sensing data.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Plant Paleobiology
courses.comments: Same course as EEMB 137. Letter grade required for majors. Not open for credit to students who have completed Botany 110.
courses.description: Examination of the history of land plants; the systematics, morphology, and phylogeny of major groups. Major evolution and biogeographic patterns.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Plant Paleobiology Laboratory
courses.prereq_text: Upper-Division standing. Earth 141 (may be taken concurrently).
courses.comments: Same course as EEMB 137L. Letter grade required for majors. Not open for credit to students who have completed Botany 110L.
courses.description: Anatomy, morphology, and systematics of fossil plants from the specimens.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: The Early Evolution of Life and its Environmental Context
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A & MCDB 1B & EEMB 2 & EEMB 3 (all with a minimum grade of C- or better) or Earth 3 or 30 or 111
courses.comments: Same course as EEMB 132.
courses.description: The first 3.5 billion years of life and the environmental context in which it evolved. Highly multidisciplinary, drawing on evidence from geology, geochemistry, paleontology, and comparative biology.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Invertebrate Paleobiology
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A & MCDB 1B & EEMB 2 & EEMB 3 or Earth 3 or 30 or 111 (all with a minimum grade of C- or better)
courses.description: Important topics in paleobiology are discussed in the context of the evolutionary history of invertebrate animal life. These include macroevolutionary theory, diversification and extinction events, ecological and geobiological interactions through time, and the incompleteness of the fossil record.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Vertebrate Paleontology
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, MCDB 1B, EEMB 2, EEMB 3 (all with grades of C- or better) or EARTH 2 or 3 or 7 or 30
courses.comments: EEMB 109 and Earth 148 are the same course. Letter grade required for majors.
courses.description: Introduction to the history of vertebrate life, with emphasis on the phylogenetic relationships of the major vertebrate groups.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: The History of Mammals
courses.prereq_text: Earth 3 or 7 or 30; or MCDB 1A-1AL; or EEMB 2.
courses.description: Introduction to the diversity of fossil and living mammals from phylogenetic, stratigraphic, and paleobiogeographic perspectives.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Plate Tectonics
courses.comments: Course materials fee required.
courses.description: Introduction to sea floor spreading, plate tectonics, and continental drift. Geometry and evolution of present day plates. Measurement and calculation of plate motions. Geophysical and geological implications of resulting relative motions at plate boundaries.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Advanced Structural Geology
courses.comments: Course materials fee charged.
courses.description: Analysis of geologic-structures--theory and practice. Rock deformation as a function of crustal environment. Fault mechanics and earthquakes; mineral deformation mechanisms; microstructures, and tectonite fabrics. Finite strain measurement and interpretation of kinematic indicators. Regional structural styles. Includes one to two field trip(s) lasting 1-4 days.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Seminar in Geology
courses.comments: May be repeated to a maximum of 12 units.
courses.description: Attendance at departmental "journal club" (Earth 260, seminar in geology) and brief written evaluations of the three papers which, in the student's judgement, were the best of the quarter.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Earth Resources, Energy and the Environment
courses.comments: Course materials fee charged. Field Trip required.
courses.description: An overview of the energy resources that sustain our economies and their environmental impact. Explores the full life cycle of each resource including its geological origins, methods used to explore and develop it, uses in our economies, and the environmental impacts of these activities.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Organic Matters
courses.description: An introduction to the chemistry of natural organic matter in the ocean, biosphere, and geosphere. Topics include marine organic carbon production and export, fossil fuel formation, tools for identifying ancient life and paleo-environmental conditions (biomarkers, isotopes), and the global impacts of organic carbon burial on global biogeochemical cycles. Some offerings will include a 1 day field trip.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Aqueous Transport of Pollutants
courses.comments: Same course as Environmental Studies 168.
courses.description: Focus on the behavior of dissolved species in rivers. Examination of the basic advection-diffusion model. Particular emphasis on field data.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Tracer and Contaminant Hydrology
courses.comments: Same course as Environmental Studies 169.
courses.description: Introduction to principles of chemical and isotope tracer hydrology. Emphasis on methods of groundwater dating, the use of tracers as management tools, and contaminate plume monitoring.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Groundwater Hydrology
courses.prereq_text: GEOG 3B or 4 or EARTH 2; or consent of instructor.
courses.comments: Same course as Geography 116.
courses.description: Analysis of groundwater flow in complex geologic environments, aquifer properties, wells and groundwater contamination, surface water-groundwater interactions. Laboratory: basic groundwater experiments, Darcy's law, flow nets, solute dispersion, field measurements of bedrock groundwater, analysis of pumping-test data.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Computational Approaches for Geological and Biological Sciences
courses.description: This course offers a comprehensive introduction to data analysis using Python and R. Students will not only learn the fundamentals of coding but also develop skills in basic statistical analysis, data visualization, data management, and machine learning. Lab sessions will be designed to reinforce the concepts learned through hands-on practice. No coding experience is required.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Introduction to MATLAB for Earth Scientists
courses.prereq_text: Earth 2 OR Earth 4 OR Upper division standing
courses.description: A 10-week introduction to coding in MATLAB including: basic programming, analysis using vectors and matrices, logical operations and indexing, data import/export, visualization and plotting, designing functions and packages, interactive user interface, and debugging.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Geological Applications of GIS
courses.comments: Course Material fee charged
courses.description: An intensive introduction to Geographic Information Systems (GIS) with an emphasis on geological applications, including geologic mapping, topographic analysis, modeling surface processes and river networks, importation and interpolation of field data, and spatial analysis and correlation of multiple geologic datasets. Short Lectures are interspersed with the lab exercises.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Ore Deposits and Mineral Resources
courses.comments: Course materials fee charged.
courses.description: Distribution and characteristics of major classes of mineral deposits - their geologic framework, mineralogy, and structure. Lectures explore petrogenetic models for ore-formation. Laboratory exercises and field trips stress recognition of ore and accessory minerals, zoning, and exploration strategies. The field trip ranges from 1-4 days long.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Field Trips in Earth Science
courses.comments: Course materials fee charged.
courses.description: Opportunity to see classic geological localities in the field. Locations vary depending on instructor(s). Lectures through the quarter cover background material needed to understand what is being observed/studied in the field. This material includes specified readings, homework assignments, exercises and exams. Lab work may also be required. Lecture, 3 hours; field, up to 6 weeks.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Field Studies in Marine Bio/Geochemistry
courses.comments: Course materials fee charged.
courses.description: Marine bio/geochemistry with the opportunity of going to sea or into the field on land. Lectures cover techniques of sea-floor mapping using bottom photography, marine bio/geochemical sampling, and method of data reduction and sample analysis. Labs include analysis of data/samples collected.Lecture, 3 hours; labs, up to 7 hours; field, up to 6 weeks.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Field Studies in Marine Bio/Geochemistry
courses.comments: Course materials fee charged.
courses.description: Marine bio/geochemistry with the opportunity of going to sea or into the field on land. Lectures cover techniques of sea-floor mapping using bottom photography, marine bio/geochemical sampling, and method of data reduction and sample analysis. Labs include analysis of data/samples collected.Lecture, 3 hours; lab, up to 7 hours; field, up to 6 weeks.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Principles of Soil Science
courses.prereq_text: Environmental Studies 15A and 15B or Chemistry 1A-B; and Geography 3 or 4 or Earth Science 2 or 4 or 20
courses.comments: Environmental Studies 114A, Geography 114A, and Earth 184A are the same course.
courses.description: Explores core introductory concepts in soil science and how soils relate to global environmental challenges. Includes study of soil physical, biological, and chemical properties, soil development, and fertility, as well as the critical role of soils in fostering thriving communities. Incorporates independent projects and soils excursions.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Soils of California: Formation, Morphology, and Management
courses.prereq_text: Environmental Studies 114A or Geography 114A or Earth Science 184A with a grade C or higher.
courses.comments: Environmental Studies 114B, Geography 114B, and Earth 184B are the same course.
courses.description: Course dives into soil genesis, classification, and sustainable land use in the context of California’s diverse soils. Connects soil characteristics and landscapes to communities, conservation, ecological relationships, agriculture, and climate change. Covers field safety, soil descriptions, and field methods via hands-on field experiences during lab.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Physical Volcanology
courses.comments: Course material fee charged.
courses.description: Overview of volcanic processes, including physical properties of melts, eruptive mechanisms, classification of volcanic deposits, and volcanic- tectonic environments. Lecture emphasizes theoretical aspects of volcanic processes, lab examines major classes of volcanic rocks, field trips emphasize mapping in volcanic terrains. Typically includes one to two overnight trips of 2-4 days each.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Cordilleran Tectonics
courses.comments: Course Material fee charged.
courses.description: Directed readings, weekly seminar, and field trip focused on the phanerozoic tectonic evolution of the North American Cordillera. Emphasis on understanding fundamental orogenic processes (continental extension, shortening, transcurrent motions, magmatism, metamorphism) from a cordilleran perspective. Typically includes one to two overnight trips of 2-4 days each.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Introduction to Teaching in Geological Sciences
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units, but only 4 units may be applied to the major.
courses.description: Students will assist instructors in teaching course in which the student previously received a grade of A- or better. Activities will be determined in consultation with the instructor and may include assisting in laboratories, tutorials, discussion sections and field trips.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Seminar in Paleobiology
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units.
courses.description: Undergraduate seminar in advanced paleobiology involving reading and group discussion of current literature. Option to (with faculty consent) write research papers of varying length or equivalent.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Advanced Studies in Paleobiology
courses.comments: May be repeated for a maximum of 12 units. Course materials fee charged.
courses.description: Designed to meet the interests and needs of individual students. Selected readings and laboratory work in systematic paleontology; field studies of recent or fossil biotas; animal-substrate relations, biostatistics, etc.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Internship in Geological Sciences
courses.prereq_text: Proposal form must be submitted by the end of the 2nd week of the quarter. Applicant must have a minimum overall GPA of 2.70. Student that does not meet this requirement may submit a GPA waiver.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units, but only 4 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: Individualized practical approaches to problems in geological sciences by working under faculty supervision as interns with local, state or federal agencies or private organizations. To receive credit student must turn in an experiential journal, end of quarter evaluation, and complete the internship hours. Units are determined by the number to be completed at the end of the quarter.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Group Studies for Advanced Students
courses.comments: Students may repeat the course; no more than five units will apply to the major.
courses.description: Intensive research or study by a small group of advanced students who share an interest in a topic not included in the regular departmental curriculum.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Seminar in Biogeochemistry
courses.comments: Students may repeat the course; no more than five units will apply to the major.
courses.description: Intensive research or study by a small group of advanced students who share an interest in a topic not included in the regular departmental curriculum.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Carbon Cycle Seminar
courses.comments: Students may repeat the course; no more than five units will apply to the major.
courses.description: Intensive research or study by a small group of advanced students who share an interest in a topic not included in the regular departmental curriculum.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Group Studies for Advanced Students
courses.comments: Students may repeat the course; no more than five units will apply to the major.
courses.description: Intensive research or study by a small group of advanced students who share an interest in a topic not included in the regular departmental curriculum.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Seminar in Geoscience Careers
courses.comments: Students may repeat the course; no more than five units will apply to the major.
courses.description: Intensive research or study by a small group of advanced students who share an interest in a topic not included in the regular departmental curriculum.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Geochronology Lab
courses.comments: Students may repeat the course; no more than five units will apply to the major.
courses.description: Intensive research or study by a small group of advanced students who share an interest in a topic not included in the regular departmental curriculum.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Practical Research Skills
courses.comments: Students may repeat the course; no more than five units will apply to the major.
courses.description: A hands-on introduction to research methods in the Earth and other natural sciences. Tools and approaches to identify research questions, design projects, and get involved in research opportunities. Involves a single-day local field trip.

courses.title: Group Studies for Advanced Students

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Honors Field Studies
courses.prereq_text: Earth Science majors only; honors standing; consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units. Course materials fee charged.
courses.description: Field work in selected areas under the direction of a faculty member. Final report required.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Senior Honors Thesis
courses.prereq_text: Earth Science majors only; consent of instructor; honors standing (minimum overall and major GPA of 3.2).
courses.description: Three quarter individual research project under the direction of a faculty member. Oral defense of written thesis as required by the sponsoring faculty advisor.
