courses.description: Three quarter individual research project under the direction of a faculty member. Oral defense of written thesis as required by the sponsoring faculty advisor.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Senior Honors Thesis
courses.prereq_text: Earth Science majors only; consent of instructor.
courses.description: Three quarter individual research project under the direction of a faculty member. Oral defense of written thesis as required by the sponsoring faculty advisor.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Readings in the Geological Sciences
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; consent of the instructor and the department chair
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 grade-point average for the preceding three quarters. May be repeated for credit, but only 4 units count toward major. Students are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
courses.description: Critical reviews and discussions of selected geological subjects.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Independent Studies in Geology
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing in the major; consent of department and instructor.
courses.comments: Students must have a 3.0 grade-point-average for the preceding three quarters. Students are limited to 5 units per quarter, 15 units per year, and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
courses.description: Course consists of academic research supervised by a faculty member. This course is not intended for internship honors, or Senior Thesis credit.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Independent Research Assistance in Geological Sciences
courses.comments: Students must have a 3.0 grade-point-average for the preceding three quarters and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
courses.description: Coursework shall consist of faculty supervised research assistance.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Introduction to Geophysics
courses.description: Survey of major topics in geophysics at an elementary level; the figure of the earth, its gravitational and magnetic fields, seismology and the deep structure of the earth, heat flow, methods of geophysical exploration. The geophysical basis of plate tectonics and sea floor spreading. Term paper.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Graduate Research and Field Seminar
courses.comments: Required of all entering graduate students. Course materials fee charged.
courses.description: Field, laboratory, and analytical projects serve as an introduction to diverse research foci and techniques in Earth Science.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Graduate Research Seminar
courses.prereq_text: Earth Science 201A; graduate standing in the department of Earth Science.
courses.comments: Required course for all first year graduate students.
courses.description: Conducting research in Earth science: identifying significant problems; designing effective studies; obtaining funding; writing and evaluating research proposals; following scientific ethics; using numerical estimation; and making effective oral and written presentations.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Mathematical Methods in Earth Science
courses.description: Introduces Matlab for plotting and analyzing geologic data and modeling geologic systems. Each student will select data relevant to his/her research for computer exercises. Topics include statistics, Monte Carlo simulations, time series analysis, principal component analysis (EOF), and box models.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Earths Climate: Past and Present
courses.description: Description and quantitative analysis of climate processes and paleoclimate proxies. Processes include radiation and the Earths energy budget, the influence of orbital cycles, ocean circulation, monsoons, ENSO, and ice sheets. Paleoclimate reconstructions from tectonic-scale to the last millennium, with emphasis on glacial cycles and Plio-Pleistocene climate evolution.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Introduction to Climate Modeling
courses.description: An introduction to climate models and their application to studies of past, modern, and future climate. Students will learn fundamental modeling concepts, gain experience running several kinds of models, and read/evaluate recent modeling papers. A variety of models will be introduced, with emphasis on atmosphere-ocean General Circulation Models (GCMs) and "simple" (zero-dimensional) models. No previous modeling or programming experience is required.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Clastic Depositional Environments
courses.comments: Course materials fee required.
courses.description: Emphasis on tectonically active settings, topics change yearly. Clastic depositional models for alluvial fan, fan delta, and turbidite fans. Volcaniclastic successions, including subaerial- to deepwater-erupted pyroclastic rocks and lava flows, as well as volcanic mudflows and sandstones. Field work completed on weekends and over spring break.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Isotope Geochemistry
courses.description: Course will develop isotopic systems as tracers of Earth processes, with a particular focus placed on developing radiogenic isotopic systems. The isotopic tools will be used to establish the chronology of the earliest terrestrial events and the formation and evolution of different reservoirs in the Earth. Applications of isotopic systems to solid Earth evolution, petrology, paleoclimate and ocean chemistry will be explored.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Sedimentation and Stratigraphy: Processes and Products
courses.comments: Course materials fee required. Concurrently offered with Earth122. No credit for students who have had Earth122. Students taking the class for graduate credit must complete an extra project (term paper or field exercise).
courses.description: Transport/depositional processes, sedimentary textures and structures. Sedimentary environments and use of facies models for observation and prediction. Principles of lithostratigraphy, biostratigraphy, chronostratigraphy, and magnetostratigraphy. Seismic stratigraphy and sequence stratigraphic principles. Controls of tectonics, sediment supply and eustacy on sedimentation.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Environmental Geochemistry
courses.description: This course focuses on geochemical principles of key processes at Earth's surface environment. Course materials cover topics including the carbon cycle, mineral-water interactions, soil systems, erosion and weathering, and hydrological cycles. Students will learn foundational theories, applications, and recent research progress to gain a comprehensive understanding of Earth's environment through the geochemical lens. The grad version of this course will contain advanced content in assignments that involve more quantitative materials and rigorous coding work for reproducing important results in classical literatures, and a full term project and a writing report.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Geochronology
courses.prereq_text: Chemistry 1A; and, Earth 2, or 3, or 4, or 4S.
courses.description: Principles of radiogenic isotope geochronology, and applications of the major geochronological methods to terrestrial and extraterrestrial problems ranging from global climate change to petrology to tectonics to solar system evolution. This is a five week course.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Biogeochemistry of Stable and Cosmogenic Isotopes
courses.description: Introduction to stable isotope biogeochemistry, including kinetic and thermodynamic fractionation of stable isotopes during evapo-precipitation, photosynthesis, and biogenic calcification. Applications of stable isotope in environmental sciences, Quarternary geology, paleoclimate, archeology. Introduction to mass spectrometry, cosmogenic and radiogenic isotopes and their application in paleoclimatology/paleoceanography.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Introduction to Geochemistry
courses.description: Fundamental concepts of geochemistry including radiometric dating, inorganic chemistry, and biogeochemical cycling are introduced. The class examines how chemical principles can be used to solve geological and environmental problems. These concepts are illustrated using classical geology, global change, and hydrology.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Field Petrology
courses.comments: Course materials fee charged.
courses.description: Field-based study of igneous, metamorphic and tectonic processes. Investigates different topics in igneous and metamorphic petrology each year, centered around field trips to key localities. Includes lectures, review of scientific literature, on-campus labs and field-based observations and measurements. The field trip for this course ranges from 4-18 days long and varies each offering.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Geophysical Time-Series Analysis
courses.comments: Concurrently offered with Earth 131
courses.description: Time-series analysis and digital-signal processing for geophysicists. Course combines theory with practical application using MATLAB and/or Python. Topics include: Sampling, the discrete Fourier transform, aliasing, convolution, filtering, power spectral density estimation, multivariate time-series analysis, and array processing. Students taking the class for graduate credit must complete an extra project (term paper).

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Introduction to Computing for Earth Science
courses.description: Introduction to computing and common software tools in geophysics and related disciplines. Topics include: UNIX, Python and/or MATLAB, Fortran 90, Generic Mapping Tools (GMT), LaTeX, HTML and CSS web pages, etc.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Advanced Geophysics
courses.comments: Course materials fee required.
courses.description: Application of geophysics principles to processes in the Earth. Use of gravity, elasticity theory, fluid dynamics, geomagnetism, and theory of heat transfer. Term paper required.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Geophysics Seismology
courses.prereq_text: One year of college level calculus and physics.
courses.description: Wave propagation in an elastic medium; reflection and refraction, attenuation. Physics of the earthquake source, magnitude, seismic moment and focal mechanisms.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Quantitative Geomorphology
courses.description: Basic quantitative understanding of processes shaping Earth's surface. In-depth evaluation of hill slope diffusion, mass wasting, and fluvial processes. Applications of quantitative methods are emphasized throughout class. Laboratory provides understanding of isotopic, physical, and remote sensing data.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: The Early Evolution of Life and its Environmental Context
courses.description: The first 3.5 billion years of life and the environmental context in which it evolved. Highly multidisciplinary, drawing on evidence from geology, geochemistry, paleontology, and comparative biology.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Advanced Seismology Seminar
courses.description: Reading and class discussion of basic concepts and methods of seismology, current discoveries and unsolved problems.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Advanced Geophysics
courses.description: Selected topics in advanced geophysics, including seismology, seismo-acoustics and infrasound, gravity, magnetism, geodynamics, volcano geophysics, and the application of techniques for geophysical analysis.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Geophysical Inverse Theory
courses.description: Introduction to basic concepts of inverse theory such as resolution, error and its trade-off. Application to Earth structure study, earthquake source,geodetic data and magnetic field. Reading on key papers. Term paper.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Plate Tectonics Seminar
courses.comments: Course materials fee required.
courses.description: Read recent related articles. Students present and discuss selected topics in separate seminar. Complete term paper and/or problem sets for three or four units.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Advanced Structural Geology
courses.comments: Course materials fee charged.
courses.description: Analysis of geologic-structures--theory and practice. Rock deformation as a function of crustal environment. Fault mechanics and earthquakes; mineral deformation mechanisms; microstructures, and tectonite fabrics. Finite strain measurement and interpretation of kinematic indicators. Regional structural styles. Includes one to two field trip(s) lasting 1-4 days.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Seminar in Geology
courses.comments: Concurrently offered with GEOL 160. Required of all first-year graduate students. May be repeated for credit.
courses.description: Presentation and discussion of current research, and reviews of the literature on selected geologic concepts. Students present material reflecting their interests in geology for critical appraisal, of both content and manner of presentation, by selected members of the seminar. Emphasis is placed on assisting students in developing professional speaking style.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Earth Science Outreach
courses.comments: No units credits allowed towards degree
courses.description: Active participation in an outreach program for local schools, presenting Earth Science concepts, demonstrations, samples and experiments to a diverse group of K-12 students, with the mission to ignite their interest in STEM, and make scientists more approachable.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Organic Matters
courses.description: An introduction to the chemistry of natural organic matter in the ocean, biosphere, and geosphere. Topics include marine organic carbon production and export, fossil fuel formation, tools for identifying ancient life and paleo-environmental conditions (biomarkers, isotopes), and the global impacts of organic carbon burial on global biogeochemical cycles. Some offerings will include a 1 day field trip.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Chemical Oceanography
courses.description: An introduction to the chemistry of the oceans. Topics include composition and chemical equilibria of seawater, biogeochemical cycling, sediment chemistry, atmospheric exchange, circulation and rates of mixing based on chemical tracers, and the impact of ocean chemistry on climate change.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Seminar in Geology-Presentation
courses.description: Presentation of research topics to meeting of Earth 260.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Seminar in Geologic Problems
courses.description: Review and discussion of a current problem in geology. Content is variable and depends on student interest.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Computational Approaches for Geological and Biological Sciences
courses.comments: The graduate section of the course is open to upper division undergraduate students with the consent of the instructor.
courses.description: This course offers a comprehensive introduction to data analysis using Python and R. Students will not only learn the fundamentals of coding but also develop skills in basic statistical analysis, data visualization, data management, and machine learning. Lab sessions will be designed to reinforce the concepts learned through hands-on practice. No coding experience is required. For graduate students, the course places additional emphasis on applying computational techniques and relevant software to analyze biological data, particularly in genomics. Graduate students will also engage in the development of a final project of their choice.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Geological Oceanography
courses.description: Morphology, formation, and evolution of ocean basins; crustal structure and composition of ocean margins; source and composition of marine sediments; marine sediment as repository of paleoclimate and paleo-ocean circulation records. Paleoceanographic changes in relation to tectonics and changes in orbital parameters, links between changes in ocean circulation and climate changes.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Ore Deposits and Mineral Resources
courses.comments: Course materials fee charged.
courses.description: Distribution and characteristics of major classes of mineral deposits - their geologic framework, mineralogy, and structure. Lectures explore petrogenetic models for ore-formation. Laboratory exercises and field trips stress recognition of ore and accessory minerals, zoning, and exploration strategies. The field trip ranges from 1-4 days long

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Field Trips in Earth Science
courses.comments: Course materials fee charged.
courses.description: Opportunity to see classic geological localities in the field. Locations vary depending on instructor(s). Lectures through the quarter cover background material needed to understand what is being observed/studied in the field. This material includes specified readings, homework assignments, exercises and exams. Lab work may also be required. Lecture, 3 hours; field, up to 6 weeks.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Field Studies in Marine Bio/Geochemistry
courses.comments: Course materials fee required.
courses.description: Studies in marine bio/geochemistry with the opportunity of going to sea or into the field on land. Lectures cover techniques of seafloor mapping using bottom photography, marine bio/geochemical sampling, and methods of data reduction and sample analysis. Labs include analysis of data/samples collected.Lecture, 3 hours; lab, up to 7 hours; field, up to 6 weeks.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Field Studies in Marine Bio/Geochemistry
courses.comments: Course materials fee required.
courses.description: Studies in marine bio/geochemistry with the opportunity of going to sea or into the field on land. Lectures cover techniques of seafloor mapping using bottom photography, marine bio/geochemical sampling, and methods of data reduction and sample analysis. Labs include analysis of data/samples collected.Lecture, 3 hours; lab, up to 7 hours; field, up to 6 weeks.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Physical Volcanology
courses.prereq_text: Earth 14 or 114 or 114A-B; and Earth 102A and 104A.
courses.comments: Course materials fee required.
courses.description: Overview of volcanic processes, including physical properties of melts, eruptive mechanisms, classification of volcanic deposits, and volcanic-tectonic environments. Lecture emphasizes theoretical aspects of volcanic processes, lab examines major classification of rocks. Graduate students must complete an independent research project. Typically includes one to two overnight trips of 2-4 days each.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Cordilleran Tectonics
courses.description: Directed readings, weekly seminar, and field trip focused on the phanerozoic tectonic evolution of the North American Cordillera. Emphasis on understanding fundamental orogenic processes (continental extension, shortening, transcurrent motions, magmatism, metamorphism) from a cordilleran perspective. Typically includes one to two overnight trips of 2-4 days each.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Practicum in Instruction
courses.comments: No unit credit allowed toward degree.
courses.description: Practical experience in teaching in geological sciences. Student will have responsibility for one or more laboratory and/or discussion sections. Evaluations will be made by both staff and class.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Practicum in Mentoring
courses.comments: No units credits allowed towards degree
courses.description: Practical experience in mentoring undergraduates in Earth Science. Activities range from teaching laboratory and field skills, to supervising independent research, to advising students in their preparation and application for graduate school or career planning.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Practicum in Research
courses.comments: No unit credit allowed toward degree.
courses.description: Practical experience in research in the geological sciences, under supervision of faculty member.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Directed Reading and Research
courses.prereq_text: Consent of instructor and graduate adviser.
courses.comments: No more than half the units necessary for the master's degree may be taken in Earth 596.
courses.description: Individual tutorial. Written proposal for each tutorial must be approved by the instructor and the department chair.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Individual Study for Master's and Ph.D. Examinations
courses.prereq_text: Consent of instructor and graduate adviser.
courses.comments: No unit credit allowed toward advanced degree.
courses.description: Instructor should be student's major professor or chair of the committee.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Master's Thesis Research and Preparation
courses.prereq_text: Consent of instructor and graduate adviser.
courses.comments: No unit credit allowed toward degree.
courses.description: Instructor normally should be chair of the student's thesis committee. Only for research underlying the thesis, writing the thesis.

courses.subject: EARTH
courses.title: Ph.D. Dissertation Preparation
courses.prereq_text: Consent of instructor and graduate adviser.
courses.description: Instructor normally should be chair of the student's doctoral committee. Only for research underlying the dissertation, writing the dissertation. Limited to terminal preparation.

courses.subject: EARTHW
courses.title: Geological Catastrophes (Online)
courses.description: Course deals with geologic catastrophes, e.g., earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, tsunamis, and landslides. Students will learn the basic physical causes of these naturally occurring events and discuss the consequences.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Computer Engineering Seminar
courses.prereq_text: Open to computer engineering majors only.
courses.description: Introductory seminar to expose students to a broad range of topics in computer engineering.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Ten Puzzling Problems in Computer Engineering
courses.prereq_text: Open to pre-computer engineering and computer engineering majors only.
courses.description: Gaining familiarity with, and motivation to study, the field of computer engineering, through puzzle-like problems that represent a range of challenges facing computer engineers in their daily problem-solving efforts and at the frontiers of research.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Introduction to Python Programming For Engineers
courses.prereq_text: Open to EE and CMPEN majors only.
courses.comments: Open to EE and CMPEN majors only.
courses.description: This course represents a comprehensive foundation for core ECE topics in signal processing, image analysis, machine learning, optimization and control. The lectures present concepts from linear algebra, such as matrix computations, systems of linear equations, eigenspace decomposition, inner-product, orthogonality, least-squares and linear regression. Students actively engage with the technical materials with an introduction to Python programming and associated hands-on sessions. The materials are be motivated by real-world scenarios ranging from medical imaging to autonomous vehicles, from (miscarriage of) justice to brain-machine interfaces, from music analysis to GPS design.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Introduction to Electrical & Computer Engineering
courses.prereq_text: Open only to Electrical Engineering and Computer Engineering majors.
courses.description: Aims at exposing freshmen students to the different sub-fields within Electrical and Computer Engineering. Composed of lectures by different faculty members and a weekly laboratory based on projects that are executed using the Arduino environment.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: The Physics of Energy, Information, and Communication
courses.prereq_text: Open to Electrical Engineering majors only.
courses.description: An introduction to the relationship between the physical nature of matter and modern problems in energy harvesting, energy storage, information storage, and communication. Key emphasis is placed on understanding materials and how materials are used to make functional electronics and photonics. The primary outcome of this course is to enable students to understand the relevance of later Physics, Math, and E&P courses with real-world examples and investigations.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Foundations of Analog and Digital Circuits & Systems
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 2A-B or 3A-B or Mathematics 3AH-BH, and Mathematics 4A or 4AI or 3C, all with a minimum grade of C; and, Math 4B or 4BI or 5A with a minimum grade of C (may be taken concurrently); Physics 3, 7B or 23 (may be taken concurrently); open only to electrical engineering and computer engineering majors.
courses.description: The objective of the course is to establish the foundations of analog and digital circuits. The course will introduce the student to the power of abstraction, resistive networks, network analysis, nonlinear analysis and the digital abstraction.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Foundations of Analog and Digital Circuits and Systems Lab
courses.prereq_text: ECE 10A (may be taken concurrently) with a C- or better grade.
courses.description: The goal of 10AL is to provide the student with a hands-on application of the concepts discussed in ECE 10A. The lab will introduce the use of microcontrollers as a data acquisition system, network analysis, resistors, nonlinear analysis and digital abstraction.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Foundations of Analog and Digital Circuits and Systems
courses.prereq_text: ECE 10A with a C- or better grade.
courses.description: The objective of the course is to introduce the MOSFET both as a simple digital switch and as controlled current source for analog design. The course will cover basic digital design, small-signal analysis, charge storage elements and operational amplifiers.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Foundations of Analog and Digital Circuits and Systems Lab
courses.prereq_text: ECE 10B (may be taken concurrently) with a C- or better grade.
courses.description: The goal of 10BL is to provide the student with a hands-on application of the concepts discussed in ECE 10B. The lab will utilize the microcontroller to introduce students to the understanding of datasheets for both digital and analog circuits, single-stage amplifier design and basic instrumentation.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Foundations of Analog and Digital Circuits and Systems
courses.prereq_text: ECE 10B with a C- or better grade.
courses.description: The objective of the course is to introduce the student to the basics of transient analysis. The course will energy and power dissipation in digital circuits, first-order and second-order linear time invariant circuits, sinusoidal steady state, impedance representation, feedback and resonance.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Foundations of Analog and Digital Circuits and Systems Lab
courses.prereq_text: ECE 10C (may be taken concurrently) with a C- grade or better.
courses.description: The goal of 10CL is to provide the student with a hands-on application of the concepts discussed in ECE 10C. The lab will utilize the microcontroller to introduce students to the understanding of propagation delay in digital circuits and the resulting power dissipation, first order linear networks, second order linear networks, sinusoidal steady-state, impedance analysis and op-amp circuits.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Fundamentals of Logic Design
courses.prereq_text: Open to electrical engineering, computer engineering, and pre-computer engineering majors only.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed ECE 15.
courses.description: Boolean algebra, logic of propositions, minterm and maxterm expansions, Karnaugh maps, Quine-McCluskey method, melti-level circuits, combinational circuit design and simulation, multiplexers, decoders, programmable logic devices.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Projects in Electrical and Computer Engineering
courses.description: Projects in electrical and computer engineering for advanced undergraduate students.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Group Studies in Electrical and Computer Engineering
courses.description: Group studies intended for small number of advanced students who share an interest in a topic not included in the regular departmental curriculum.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Undergraduate Research
courses.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Must have a 3.00 GPA. May be repeated for up to 12 units.
courses.comments: May be repeated for up to 12 units.
courses.description: Research opportunities for undergraduate students. students will be expected to give regular oral presentations, actively participate in a weekly seminar, and prepare at least one written report on their research.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Integrated Circuit Design and Fabrication
courses.prereq_text: ECE 132 with a minimum grade of C-.
courses.description: Theory, fabrication, and characterization of solid state devices including P-N junctions, capacitors, bipolar and MOS devices. Devices are fabricated using modern VLSI processing techniques including lithography, oxidation, diffusion, and evaporation. Physics and performance of processing steps are discussed and analyzed.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Integrated Circuit Design and Fabrication
courses.prereq_text: Either ECE 120A or ECE 124B with a minimum grade of C- or better in each of the courses.
courses.description: Design, simulation, fabrication, and characterization of NMOS integrated circuits. Circuit design and layout is performed using commercial layout software. Circuits are fabricated using modern VLSI processing techniques. Circuit and discrete device electrical performance are analyzed.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: VLSI Principles
courses.prereq_text: ECE 152A with a minimum grade of C-.
courses.description: Introduction to CMOS digital VLSI design: CMOS devices and manufacturing technology; transistor level design of static and dynamic logic gates and components and interconnections; circuit characterization: delay, noise margins, and power dissipation; combinational and sequential circuits; arithmetic operations and memories.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: VLSI Architecture and Design
courses.prereq_text: ECE 124A or ECE 123 or ECE 122A with a minimum grade of C-.
courses.description: Practical issues in VLSI circuit design, pad/pin limitations, clocking and interfacing standards, electrical packaging for high-speed and high-performance design. On-chip noise and crosstalk, clock and power distribution, architectural and circuit design constraints, interconnection limits and transmission line effects.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Signal Analysis and Processing
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 4B or 5A with a minimum of grade of C; open to EE and computer engineering majors only.
courses.description: Analysis of continuous time linear systems in the time and frequency domains. Superposition and convolution. Bilateral and unilateral Laplace transforms. Fourier series and Fourier transforms. Filtering, modulation, and feedback.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Signal Analysis and Processing
courses.prereq_text: ECE 130A with a minimum grade of C- or better; open to EE and computer engineering majors only.
courses.description: Analysis of discrete time linear systems in the time and frequency domains. Z transforms, Discrete Fourier transforms. Sampling and aliasing.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Introduction to Applied Linear Algebra
courses.prereq_text: Math 4B or Math 5A recommended. Open to EE and CE majors only.
courses.description: Introduction to applied linear algebra: matrix arithmetic, vector spaces, orthogonality, matrix factorizations, determinants, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, difference and differential equations.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Introduction to Solid-State Electronic Devices
courses.prereq_text: Physics 4 or 24 or 7D with a minimum grade of C-; Mathematics 4B, 4BI or 5A with a minimum grade of C; open to EE and computer engineering majors only.
courses.description: Electrons and holes in semiconductors; doping (P and N); state occupation statistics, transport properties of electrons and holes; P-N junction diodes; I-V, C-V, and switching properties of P-N junctions; introduction of bipolar transitors, MOSFET's and JFET's.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Introduction to Optimization and Learning
courses.prereq_text: Upper division standing Electrical Engineering and Computer Engineering majors only.
courses.description: Includes an undergraduate level introduction to the theory of optimization, along with relevant applications of optimization in machine learning and statistics, signal processing, decision making and control.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Introduction to Fields and Waves
courses.prereq_text: Physics 3 or 23 or 7B and Physics 4 or 24 or PHYS 7C with a minimum grade of C-; Mathematics 4B or 4BI or 5A and Mathematics 5B or 6A or 6AI with a minimum grade of C in each; and Mathematics 5C or 6B with a minimum grade of C-; open to EE and computer engineering majors only.
courses.description: Introduction to applied electromagnetics and wave phenomena in high frequency electron circuits and systems. Waves on transmission-lines, elements of electrostatics and magnetostatics and applications, plane waves, examples and applications to RF, microwave, and optical systems.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Optical Fiber Communications
courses.prereq_text: ECE 132 and 134 with a minimum grade of C- in both.
courses.description: Optical fiber as a transmission medium, dispersion and nonlinear effects in fiber transmission, fiber and semiconductor optical amplifiers and lasers, optical modulators, photo detectors, optical receivers, wavelength division multiplexing components, optical filters, basic transmission system analysis and design.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Introduction to Optics and Photonics
courses.prereq_text: PHYS 5/PHYS 5L or PHYS 7D/PHYS 7L or PHYS 25 or equivalent.
courses.description: Fundamentals of optical and photonics including lens theory, basics of imaging, microscopes and telescopes, 2-dimensional Fourier Transforms, optical coherence, interferometry, lasers, laser phase noise and laser linewidth.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Optics and Imaging
courses.prereq_text: PHYS 5/PHYS 5L or PHYS 7D/PHYS 7L or PHYS 25 or equivalent.
courses.description: Photonics, with an emphasis on imaging: optical design (Zemax), ray transfer matrices, aberrations, scattering, resolution and optical transfer functions, adaptive optics, polarization, laser scanning, ultrafast pulses, detectors, superresolution, and VR/AR.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Quantum Photonics
courses.prereq_text: PHYS 5/PHYS 5L or PHYS 7D/PHYS 7L or PHYS 25 or equivalent.
courses.description: Introduction to quantum information, fundamentals of quantum photonics, quantum light generation and detection, quantum coherence and superposition, wave-particle duality, qubits, quantum logic, entanglement, quantum measurement.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Circuits and Electronics I
courses.prereq_text: ECE 10A-B-C and 10AL-BL-CL or 2A-B-C, 130A and 132 all with a minimum grade of C-; open to EE majors only.
courses.description: Analysis and design of single stage and multistage transistor circuits including biasing, gain, impedances and maximum signal levels.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Circuits and Electronics II
courses.prereq_text: ECE 10C and 10CL or 2C, and ECE 137A with a minimum grade of C- in all; open to EE majors only.
courses.description: Analysis and design of single stage and multistage transistor circuits at low and high frequencies. Transient response. Analysis and design of feedback circuits. Stability criteria.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Probability and Statistics
courses.prereq_text: Open to Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering and pre-Computer Engineering majors only.
courses.description: Fundamentals of probability, conditional probability, Bayes rule, random variables, functions of random variables, expectation and high-order moments, Markov chains, hypothesis testing.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Introduction to Nanoelectromechanical and Microelectromechanical systems (NEMS/MEMS)
courses.prereq_text: ME 16 or ME W 16 and 17; ME 152A and ME 151A (may be concurrent); or ECE 130A & 137A with a minimum grade of C- in both.
courses.description: Introduction to nano- and microtechnology. Scaling laws and nanoscale physics are stressed. Individual subjects at the nanoscale including materials, mechanics, photonics, electronics, and fluidics will be described, with an emphasis on differences of behavior at the nanoscale and real-world examples.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: MEMS: Processing and Device Characterization
courses.comments: ME 141B and ECE 141B are the same course.
courses.description: Lectures and laboratory on semiconductor-based processing for MEMS. Description of key equipment and characterization tools used for MEMS and design, fabrication, characterization and testing of MEMS. Emphasis on current MEMS devices including accelerometers, comb drives, micro-reactors and capacitor-actuators.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: INTRODUCTION TO POWER ELECTRONICS
courses.prereq_text: ECE 132, ECE 134 and ECE 137A with a minimum grade of C- in all; open to EE majors only.
courses.description: An introduction to modern switched-mode power electronics and associated devices. Covers modern converter/inverter topologies for the control and conversion of electrical power with high efficiency with applications in power supplies, renewable energy systems, lighting, electric/hybrid vehicles, and motor drivers.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Electromagnetic Fields and Waves
courses.prereq_text: ECE 134 with a minimum grade of C-.
courses.description: Waves on transmission lines, Maxwell's equations, skin effect, propagation and reflection of electromagnetic waves, microwave integrated circuit principles, metal and dielectric waveguides, resonant cavities, antennas. Microwave and optical device examples and experiencewith modern microwave and CAD software.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Communication Electronics
courses.prereq_text: ECE 137A-B with a minimum grade of C- in both.
courses.description: RF/Microwave circuits. Transistor, transmission-line, and passive element characteristics. Transmission-line theory and impedance matching. Amplifier design for maximum available gain. Amplifier stability. Gain compression and power limits. Introduction to noise figure, and to intermodulation distortion.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Communication Electronics II
courses.prereq_text: ECE 145A with a minimum grade of C-; EE majors only.
courses.description: RF models for CMOS and BJT. Discrete vs. IC implementation. On-chip passive components. LNAs. PAs. T/R switches. Mixers. VCOs. Poly-phase filters Radio link budget. Analog and digital modulation schemes. Introduction to receiver architectures. I&Q modulation. Image-reject architectures.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Communication Electronics III
courses.prereq_text: ECE 145B with a minimum grade of C-.
courses.description: Modern wireless communication standards. Cellular phone. Wireless LAN. Introduction to multi-access techniques. Advanced modulation schemes. Interference and distortion. Modern transceiver architectures. Direct conversion vs. low IF vs. super-heterodyne. Sub-sampling receiver. Direct polar modulator. Frequency synthesis using PLL.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Digital Communication Fundamentals
courses.prereq_text: ECE 130A-B with a minimum grade of C-; ECE 139 or PSTAT 120A; open to CE & EE majors only.
courses.description: Signal and channel models, with emphasis on wireless systems; digital modulation; demodulation basics; statistical modeling of noise, including review of probability theory and random variables.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Wireless Systems
courses.prereq_text: ECE 146A with a minimum grade of C- or better; open to EE and CE majors only.
courses.description: A selection of topics in advanced wireless communication and sensing systems, including multi-antenna (MIMO) and multicarrier (OFDM) systems, and wideband MIMO radar.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Feedback Control Systems - Theory and Design
courses.prereq_text: ECE 130A-B with a minimum grade of C- in each; open to electrical engineering and computer engineering majors only.
courses.description: Feedback systems design, specifications in time and frequency domains. Analysis and synthesis of closed loope systems. Computer aided analysis anddesign.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Digital Control Systems - Theory and Design
courses.prereq_text: ECE 147A with a minimum grade of C-; open to EE and CE majors only.
courses.description: Analysis of sampled data feedback systems; state space description of linear systems: observability, controllability, pole assignment, state feedback, observers. Design of digital control systems.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Control System Design Project
courses.prereq_text: ECE 147A or ME 155B or ME 173 with a minimum grade of C-.
courses.description: Students are required to design, implement, and document a significant control systems project. The project is implemented in hardware or in high-fidelity numerical simulators. Lectures and laboratories cover special topics related to the practical implementation of control systems.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Applications of Signal Analysis and Processing
courses.prereq_text: ECE 130A and 130B with a minimum grade of C- in both.
courses.description: A sequence of engineering applications of signal analysis and processing techniques; in communications, image processing, analog and digital filter design, signal detection and parameter estimation, holography and tomography, Fourier optics, and microwave and acoustic sensing.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Game Theory for Networked Systems
courses.prereq_text: UPPER DIVISION STANDING OR CONSENT OF INSTRUCTOR.
courses.description: An overview of game theory with an emphasis on application to multiagent systems. Game theory focuses on the study of systems that are comprised of interacting and possibly competing decision-making entities. Examples drawn from engineered, economics, and social systems.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: MOBILE EMBEDDED SYSTEMS
courses.prereq_text: Proficiency in JAVA programming, and a C- in ECE 152A.
courses.description: Architectures of modern smartphones and their key hardware components including mobile application processors, communications chips, display, touchscreen, graphics, camera, battery, GPS,and various sensors; the OS and software development platform of smartphones; smartphone applications; low power design techniques.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Digital Design Principles
courses.prereq_text: ECE 15A and ECE 2A or ECE 10A & ECE 10AL with a minimum grade of C- in each course; or Computer Science 30 or 64 with a minimum grade of C- in each course; open to electrical engineering, computer engineering, and computer science majors only.
courses.description: Design of synchronous digital systems: timing diagrams, propagation delay, latches and flip-flops, shift registers and counters, Mealy/Moore finite state machines, Verilog, 2-phase clocking, timing analysis, CMOS implementation, S-RAM, RAM-based designs, ASM charts, state minimization.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Digital System Design
courses.prereq_text: ECE 152A with a minimum grade of C-; open to EE, CMPEN, and Computer Science majors only.
courses.description: Hierarchical digital design both top-down and bottom-up with special emphasis on the role of wire loading, architecture design with partitioning, planning, and timing closure. Module and system interfaces and communication structural design. Design debugging using on chip JTAG based resources, static timing analysis, multiple clock domains, synchronization and computer peripheral design.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Hardware/Software Interface
courses.prereq_text: Upper division standing in Computer Engineering, Computer Science and Electrical Engineering. Familiarity with C, FiniteAutomata, and Computer Architecture.
courses.comments: Same course as Computer Science 153A.
courses.description: Design and coding of embedded programs. Real-time constraints and management of resources. Practical I/O interfaces and protocols, polling, interrupt maintenance, atomic code, blocking and non-blocking tasks. Static and dynamic task scheduling under real-time and limited resource constraints.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Sensor and Peripheral Interface Design
courses.prereq_text: ECE 152A with a minimum grade of C-.
courses.description: Hardware description languages; field-programmable logic and ASIC design techniques. Mixed-signal techniques: A/D and D/A converter interfaces; video and audio signal acquisition, processing and generation, communication and network interfaces.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Introduction to Computer Architecture
courses.prereq_text: ECE 152A with a minimum grade of C-; open to EE and CMPEN majors only.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Computer Science 154. ECE 154A is the formerly numbered ECE 154. Students who have taken ECE 154 and have received a grade of C- or lower may take ECE 154A for a better grade.
courses.description: Instruction-set architecture (ISA) and computer performance; Machine instructions, assembly, addressing modes; Memory map,arrays, pointers; Procedure calls; Number formats; Simple ALUs; Data path,control, microprogram; Buses, I/O programming, interrupts; Pipelined data paths and control schemes.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Advanced Computer Architecture
courses.prereq_text: ECE 154A with a C- grade or better. Open to EE and CMPEN majors only.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to those who have taken Computer Science 154.
courses.description: ISA variations; Pipeline data and controlhazards; Fast ALU design; Instruction-level parallelism, multithreading, VLIW; Vector and array processing, multi/many-core chips; Cache and virtual memory; Disk arrays; Shared- and distributed-memory systems, supercomputers; Reconfigurable and application-specific circuits.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Machine Learning in Design and Test Automation
courses.prereq_text: ECE 152A with a minimum grade of C-.
courses.description: Introduces the various machine learning techniques and how they are utilized to improve hardware design and test automation processes. The potential benefits and theoretical barriers for implementing a machine learning solution in practice are explained.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Artificial Intelligence in Design and Test Automation
courses.prereq_text: ECE 157A with a minimum grade of C-.
courses.description: Introduces an artificial intelligence system view to apply machine learning in design and test automation processes. The various components for building an Intelligent Engineering Assistant (IEA) to perform an engineering task in an industrial setting are explained.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: AI Agents for the Semiconductor Industry
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; open to Computer Engineering and Electrical Engineering Majors.
courses.description: Covers theories and practices of verification/test for checking hardware correctness and trustworthiness of large language models. A connection between the two is drawn. Students learn the principles of verification and test and how to apply them in both contexts.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Digital Signal Processing
courses.prereq_text: ECE 130A-B with a minimum grade of C-; open to EE majors only.
courses.description: Digital Signal Processing, with Applications: The Fast Fourier transform, discrete cosine transform, and multirate digital signal processing techniques, with applications to digital cellular communications and wireless access points, and audio, voice, still image, video, and biological signal analysis, recognition and compression.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: The Quantum Description of Electronic Materials
courses.prereq_text: ECE 130A-B and 134 with a minimum grade of C- in all; open to EE, seniors in the BS/MS program and Materials graduate students only.
courses.comments: Same course as Materials 162A.
courses.description: Electrons as particles and waves, Schrodinger's equation and illustrative solutions. Tunnelling. Atomic structure, the exclusion principle and the periodic table. Bonds. Free electrons in metals, periodic potentials and energy bands.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Fundamentals of the Solid State
courses.prereq_text: ECE 162A with a minimum grade of C-; open to EE, senior students in the BS/MS programs and Materials graduate students only.
courses.comments: Same course as Materials 162B.
courses.description: Crystal lattices and the structure of solids, with emphasis on semiconductors. Lattice vibrations. Electronic states and energy bands. Electrical and thermal conduction. Dielectric and optical properties. Semiconductor devices: diffusion, P-N junctions and diode behavior.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Optoelectronic Materials and Devices
courses.prereq_text: ECE 162A-B with a minimum grade of C-; open to electrical engineering and materials majors only.
courses.description: Optical transitions in solids. Direct and indirect gap semiconductors. Luminescence. Excitons and photons. Fundamentals of optoelectronic devices: semiconductor lasers, Led's photoconductors, solar cells, photo diodes, modulators. Photoemission. Integrated circuits.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Introduction to Digital Image and Video Processing
courses.prereq_text: Open to electrical engineering, computer engineering, and computer science majors with upper-division standing.
courses.description: Basic concepts in image and video processing. Topics include image formation and sampling, image transforms, image enhancement, and image and video compression including JPEG and MPEG coding standards.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Introduction to Robotics: Dynamics and Control
courses.comments: ME 179D and ECE 179D are the same course.
courses.description: Dynamic modeling and control methods for robotic systems. Lagrangian method for deriving equations of motion, introduction to the Jacobian, and modeling and control of forces and contact dynamics at a robotic end effector. Laboratories encourage a problem-solving approach to control.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Introduction to Robotics: Planning and Kinematics
courses.comments: CMPSC 179P, ECE 179P, and ME 179P are the same course.
courses.description: Motion planning and kinematics topics with an emphasis on geometric reasoning, programming, and matrix computations. Motion planning: configuration spaces, sensor-based planning, decomposition and sampling methods, and advanced planning algorithms. Kinematics: reference frames, rotations and displacements, kinematic motion models.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: INTRODUCTION TO DEEP LEARNING
courses.prereq_text: Open to EE, Computer Engineering and Computer Science with upper-division standing.
courses.description: Introduction to multilayered neural networks, early models of perceptrons and associative memory; back-propagation learning; convolutional neural networks; recurrent neural networks; attention models; applications to natural language processing and computer vision.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Introduction to Computer Vision
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Chemical Engineering or Mechanical Engineering.
courses.comments: CMPSC 181 and ECE 181 are the same course.
courses.description: Overview of computer vision problems and techniques for analyzing the content of images and video. Topics include image formation, edge detection, image segmentation, pattern recognition, texture analysis, optical flow, stereo vision, shape representation and recovery techniques, issues in object recognition, and case studies of practical vision systems.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Nonlinear Phenomena
courses.prereq_text: Physics 105A or Physics 103; or ME 163 or upper-division standing in ECE.
courses.comments: Same course as ME 169 and Physics 106. Not open for credit to students who have completed ECE 163C.
courses.description: Introduction to nonlinear phenomena. Flows and bifurcations in one and two dimensions, chaos, fractals, strange attractors. Applications to physics, engineering, chemistry, and biology.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Introduction to Video Game Development
courses.prereq_text: CS 130A and CS 130B or significant programming experience in large software systems.
courses.description: Introduction to game design, video game architectures, large-scale software design patterns, game aesthetics, user interface design, and playtesting, all within the Unity3D framework. Quarter culminates in a high-quality video game suitable for public release. Pre-requisite for the advanced game-development sequence.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Probabilistic Machine Learning
courses.description: An introductory course to topics in machine learning studied from a probability theory viewpoint. Covers an overview of basic probability, inference and estimation, regression algorithms, Markov chains, inference for Markov models and the EM algorithm, Markov decision process, and reinforcement learning. In addition to covering mathematical and algorithmic details, the course includes several hands-on projects to implement the machine learning algorithms.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Senior Electrical Engineering Project
courses.prereq_text: ECE 153A or ECE 153B. ECE 153A may be taken concurrently with ECE 188A.
courses.description: Student groups design a significant project based on the knowledge and skills acquired in earlier coursework and integrate their technical knowledge through a practical design experience. The project is evaluated through written reports, oral presentations, and demonstrations of performance.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Senior Electrical Engineering Project
courses.prereq_text: ECE 188A with a minimum grade of C-.
courses.description: Student groups design a significant project based on the knowledge and skills acquired in earlier coursework and integrate their technical knowledge through a practical design experience. The project is evaluated through written reports, oral presentations, and demonstrations of performance.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Senior Electrical Engineering Project
courses.prereq_text: ECE 188B with a minimum grade of C-.
courses.description: Student groups design a significant project based on the knowledge and skills acquired in earlier coursework and integrate their technical knowledge through a practical design experience. The project is evaluated through written reports, oral presentations, and demonstrations of performance.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Senior Computer Systems Project
courses.prereq_text: ECE 153B with a minimum grade of C-; senior standing in Computer Engineering, Computer Science or EE.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Computer Science 189A-B.
courses.description: Student groups design a significant computer-based project. The focus will be on designing a significant project based on the knowledge and skills acquired in earlier coursework. Groups work independently with interaction among groups via interface specifications and informal meetings. The project is evaluated through successful completion of milestones and individual/group project reports and presentations.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Senior Computer Systems Project
courses.prereq_text: ECE 189A with a minimum grade of a C- or better; senior standing in Computer Engineering, Computer Science or ECE.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Computer Science 189A-B.
courses.description: Student groups design a significant computer-based project. Focus will be on building and implementing an embedded hardware system. Each group works independently. The project is evaluated through project reports, achieving milestones and through successful demonstration of hardware functionality.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Senior Computer Systems Project
courses.prereq_text: ECE 189B with a minimum grade of a C- or better ; senior standing in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or EE.
courses.description: Student groups design a significant computer-based project. The focus in this course will be on the integration of both hardware and software components. Students continue to work in groups. Apart from project reports and presentations, the evaluation will be based on successful demonstration of both hardware and software aspects of the project.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Projects in Electrical and Computer Engineering
courses.comments: A maximum of 4 units may be used as departmental electives.
courses.description: Projects in electrical and computer engineering for advanced undergraduate students.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Internship in Industry
courses.comments: Student must have a minimum 3.0 GPA. May not be used as departmental elective. May be repeated to a maximum of 12 units.
courses.description: Special projects for selected students. Offered in conjunction with engineering practice in selected industrial and research firms, under direct faculty supervision.

courses.description: Group studies intended for small number of advanced students who share an interest in a topic not included in the regular departmental curriculum.
