courses.title: Group Studies in Electrical and Computer Engineering
courses.description: Group studies intended for small number of advanced students who share an interest in a topic not included in the regular departmental curriculum. Topics are coded as follows: u. optics/optoelectronics.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Undergraduate Research
courses.prereq_text: Students must: (1) have attained upper division standing, (2) have a minimu3.0 grade-point average for preceding three quarters, (3) consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for up to 12 units. Not more than 4 units may be applied todepartmental electives.
courses.description: Research opportunities for undergraduate students. students will be expected to give regular oral presentations, actively participate in a weekly seminar, and prepare at least one written report on their research.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Independent Studies in Electrical and Computer Engineering
courses.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-diviscourse in Electrical and Computer Engineering.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters and are limited to five units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199DC/199RA courses combined.
courses.description: Directed individual study, normally experimental.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Electromagnetic Theory I
courses.description: Basic concepts in electromagnetic theory, energy power, plane waves, guided waves, dielectric and metallic waveguides, radiation, uniqueness, image theory, reciprocity, duality, equivalence principle, induction theorem.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Information Theory
courses.comments: Same course as Computer Science 225.
courses.description: Entropy, mutual information, and Shannon's coding theorems; lossless source coding, Huffman, Shannon-Fano-Elias, and arithmetic codes; channel capacity; rate-distortion theory, and lossy source coding; source-channel coding; algorithmic complexity and information; applications of information theory in various fields.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Matrix Analysis and Computation
courses.comments: Students should be proficient in basic numerical methods, linear algebra, mathematically rigorous proofs, and some programming language. Same course as Computer Science 211A, Mathematics 206A, ME 210A, Chemical Engineering 211A, and Geology 251A.
courses.description: Graduate level-matrix theory with introduction to matrix computations. SVD's, pseudoinverses, variational characterization of eigenvalues, perturbation theory, direct and iterative methods for matrix computations.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Numerical Simulation
courses.comments: Students should be proficient in basic numerical methods, linear algebra, mathematically rigorous proofs, and some programming language. Same course as Computer Science 211B, Mathematics 206B, ME 210B, Chemical Engineering 211B and Geology 251B.
courses.description: Linear multistep methods and Runge-Kutta methods for ordinary differential equations: stability, order and convergence. Stiffness. Differential algebraic equations. Numerical solution of boundary value problems.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Numerical Solution of Partial Differential Equations--Finite Difference Methods
courses.comments: Students should be proficient in basic numerical methods, linear algebra, mathematically rigorous proofs, and some programming language. Same course as Computer Science 211C, Mathematics 206C, ME 210C, Chemical Engineering 211C and Geology 251C.
courses.description: Finite difference methods for hyperbolic, parabolic and elliptic PDE's, with application to problems in science and engineering. Convergence, consistency, order and stability of finite difference methods. Dissipation and dispersion. Finite volume methods. Software design and adaptivity.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Numerical Solution of Partial Differential Equations--Finite Element Methods
courses.comments: Students should be proficient in basic numerical methods, linear algebra, mathematically rigorous proofs, and some programming language. Same course as Computer Science 211D, Mathematics 206D, ME 210D, Chemical Engineering 211D and Geology 251D.
courses.description: Weighted residual and finite element methods for the solution of hyperbolic, parabolic and elliptic partial differential equations, with application to problems in science and engineering. Error estimates. Standard and discontinuous Galerkin methods.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Engineering Quantum Mechanics I
courses.prereq_text: ECE 162A-B. Students must have some knowledge of linear algebra.
courses.comments: Same course as Materials 211A.
courses.description: Wave-particle duality; bound states; uncertainty relations; expectation values and operators; variational principle; eigenfunction expansions; perturbation theory I. Treatment matches needs and background of ECE and Materials students emphasizing solid state or quantum electronics.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Engineering Quantum Mechanics II
courses.prereq_text: ECE 211A or MATRL 211A, or ECE 215A or MATRL 206A.
courses.comments: Same course as Materials 211B.
courses.description: Continutation of ECE 211A; symmetry and degeneracy; electrons in crystals, angular momentum; perturbation theory II; transition probabilites; quantized fields and radiative transitions; magnetic fields; electron spin;indistinguishable particles.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Fundamentals of Electronic Solids I
courses.comments: Same course as Materials 206A.
courses.description: Introduction into the physics of semiconductors, for beginning engineering graduate students. Crystal structure. Reciprocal lattice and crystal diffraction. Electrons in periodic structures. Energy and bands. Semiconductor electrons and probes, fermi statistics.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Fundamentals of Electronic Solids II
courses.comments: Same course as Materials 206B.
courses.description: Phonos, electron scattering, electroni transport, selected optical properties, heterostructures, effective mass, quantum wells, two-dimensional electron gas, quantum wires, deep levels, crystal binding.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Molecular Beam Epitaxy and Band Gap Engineering
courses.comments: Same course as Materials 217.
courses.description: Fundamentals and recent research developmnets in the growth and properties of thin crystalline films of electronic and optical materials bythe process of molecular beam epitaxy. Artificially structured materials with quantized electron confinement and artificially engineered electronic band structure properties.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Communication Electronics
courses.description: RF/Microwave circuits. Transistor, transmission-line, and passive element characteristics. Transmission-line theory and impedance matching. Amplifier design for maximum available gain. Amplifier stability. Gain compression and power limits. Introduction to noise figure, and to intermodulation distortion.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Communication Electronics II
courses.description: RF models for CMOS and BJT. Discrete vs. IC implementation. On-chip passive components. LNAs. PAs. T/R switches. Mixers. VCOs. Poly-phase filters Radio link budget. Analog and digital modulation schemes. Introduction to receiver architectures. I&Q modulation. Image-reject architectures.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Communication Electronics III
courses.description: Modern wireless communication standards. Cellular phone. Wireless LAN. Introduction to multi-access techniques. Advanced modulation schemes. Interference and distortion. Modern transceiver architectures. Direct conversion vs. low IF vs. super-heterodyne. Sub-sampling receiver. Direct polar modulator. Frequency synthesis using PLL.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Semiconductor Device Processing
courses.comments: Same course as Materials 215A.
courses.description: Intensive theoretical and laboratory instruction in solid-state device and integrated circuit fabrication. Topics include 1) semiconductor material properties and characterization; 2) phase diagrams; 3) diffusion; 4) thermal oxidation; 5) vacuum processes; 6) thin-film deposition; 7) scanning electron microscopy. Both gallium arsenide and silicon technologies are presented.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Semiconductor Device Processing
courses.comments: Same course as Materials 215B.
courses.description: Continued theoretical and laboratory instruction in the fundamentals, the design, the fabrication, and the characterization of junction and field-effect devices. Topics will include bipolar characterization, design,fabrication, and testing. The laboratory effort initiated in ECE 220A will be continued in these quarters.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Semiconductor Device Physics I
courses.description: Band diagrams of P-N junctions and heterjunctions; current flow by drift and diffusion; bipolar transistors; recombination and generation. Schottky barriers; heterostructures.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Semiconductor Device Physics II
courses.description: More advanced continuation of ECE 221A: field effect transistors, quantum wells and superlattices; tunneling; avalanche breakdown; physical limitations of bipolar and field effect transistors; two-dimensional current flow problems.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: VLSI Project Design
courses.description: Design, planning and layout of a CMOS/Mixed-Signal VLSI Integrated Circuit for fabrication, characterization and test. Layout rules, topological, and physical issues in the design of integrated systems. Student teams plan, design and test a VLSI project.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: High Speed Digital Integrated Circuit Design
courses.description: Advanced digital VLSI design: CMOS scaling, nanoscale issues including variability, thermal management, interconnects, reliability; non-clocked, clocked and self-timed logic gates; clocked storage elements; high-speed components, PLLs and DLLs; clock and power distribution; memory systems; signaling and I/O design; low-power design.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Level Set Methods
courses.prereq_text: CMPSC 211C or CH E 211C or ECE 210C or ME 210C.
courses.comments: Same course as CH E 226, CMPSC 216, and ME 216.
courses.description: Mathematical description of the level set method and design of the numerical methods used in its implementations (ENO-WENO, Godunov, Lax-Friedrich, etc.). Introduction to the Ghost Fluid Method. Applications in CFD. Materials Sciences, Computer Vision and Computer Graphics.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Semiconductor Lasers I
courses.prereq_text: ECE 162A-B-C, or MATRL 162A-B and ECE 162C, or ECE 144.
courses.description: Review of semiconductor physics, growth technology, and materials properties; double-heterostructure and quantum-well laser structures; carrier and photon rate equations; light vs. current characteristics; scattering and transmission matrices; compound cavity, distributed bragg reflector, and distributed feedback lasers.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Semiconductor Lasers II
courses.prereq_text: ECE 227A or MATRL 268A, or ECE 215A or MATRL 206A.
courses.description: Gain and spontaneous emission vs. injection current in semiconductors; nonradiative recombination; strained-layer quantum wells. Dynamic characteristics of lasers including differential and large signal analysis of the rate equations; relative intensity noise and linewidth; carrier transport and feedback effects.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Fiber Optic Communications
courses.description: Optical fiber structures and guided modes. Effect of dispersion, attenuation and fiber, nonlinearities. Basic transmission design including loss and rise time budgets. Optical transmission system essentials and requirements. Introduction to WDM and TDM components and technologies.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Fiber Optic Components and Systems
courses.description: Photodetector design and receiver characteristics. Optical transmitters, optical amplifiers, optical isolators, optical switches, wavelength converters, regenerators, optical multiplexers and demultiplexers. Advanced transmission link design and performance including bit error rate and signal to noise ratio and fiber transmission impairments.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Hybrid Systems
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing in Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Electric& Computer Engineering, or Computer Science.
courses.description: Introduction to systems that combine continuous dynamics with discrete logic. Topics include a modeling framework that combines elements from automata theory and differential equations, simulations tools, analysis and design techniques for hybrid systems and applications of hybrid control systems.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Linear Systems I
courses.prereq_text: ME 210A, ECE 210A, CH E 211A, CMPSC 211A, or MATH 206A; may be taken concurrently
courses.comments: ME243A and ECE 230A are the same course.
courses.description: Internal and external descriptions. Solution of state equations. Controllability and observability realizations. Pole assignment, assignment, observers; modern compensator design. Disturbance localization and decoupling. Least-squares control. Least-squares estimation; Kalman filters; smoothing. The separation theorem; LQG compensator design. Computational considerations. Selected additional topics.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Linear Systems II
courses.prereq_text: ECE 230A or ME 243A; and ME 210A, ECE 210A, CH E 211A, CMPSC 211A, or MATH 206A
courses.comments: ECE 230B and ME 243B are the same course.
courses.description: Internal and external descriptions. Solution of state equations. Controllability and observability realizations. Pole assignment, assignment, observers; modern compensator design. Distribance localization and decoupling. Least-squares control. Least-squares estimation; Kalman filters; smoothing. The seperation theorem; LQG compensator design. Computational considerations. Selected additional topics.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Algorithmic Game Theory
courses.prereq_text: ECE 149 or ECE 270 or Instructor's consent
courses.description: Algorithmic game theory (AGT) is an area at the intersection of game theory and computer science, with the objective of analyzing and designing algorithms in strategic environments. The class covers recent advances in algorithm game theory, with specific emphasis on applications to engineering systems.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Robust Control Theory
courses.prereq_text: ECE 230A or ME 243A; and, ECE 230B or ME 243B, or consent of instructor.
courses.comments: Same course as Mechanical Engineering 256.
courses.description: Uncertainty modeling; stability of systems in the presence of norm-bounded perturbations; induced norm performance problems; H-infinity and linear quadratic control theory; Integral Quadratic Constraints (IQCs); structured singular value analysis; model reduction; computer aided design projects for control systems.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Stochastic Processes in Engineering
courses.description: A first-year graduate course in stochastic processes, including: review of basic probability; gaussian, poisson, and Weiner processes; wide-sense stationary processes; covariance function and power spectral density; linear systems driven by random inputs; basic Wiener and Kalman filter theory.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Nonlinear Control Systems
courses.comments: ME 236 and ECE 236 are the same course.
courses.description: Analysis and design of nonlinear control systems. Focus on Lyapunov stability theory, with sufficient time devoted to contrasts between linear and nonlinear systems, input-output stability and the describing function method.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Advanced Control Design Laboratory
courses.prereq_text: ME 243A/ECE 230A and at least one class among the following: ME 243B/ECE 230B, ME 236/ECE 236, ME 256/ECE 232, or ME 254/ECE 271C.
courses.description: A laboratory course requiring students to design and implement advanced control systems on a physical experiment. Experiments from any engineering or scientific discipline are chosen by the student.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Optimal Estimation and Filtering
courses.description: Optimal estimation concepts and theory (minimum variance, least squares, and maximum likelihood estimation), optimal recursive algorithms for discrete- and continuous-time filtering of noisy signals and data. Wiener and Kalman filters, stability of recursive optimal filtering algorithms, modeling errors in recursive filters.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Multimedia Compression
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Media Arts and Technology 221.
courses.description: Covers the principle standards of speech, audio, still image and video compression with emphasis on system performance, key underlying algorithms and technologies, current applications and the projected future evolution of the standards.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Digital Signal Compression
courses.description: Principles and techniques of signal compression systems. Basic quantizationtheory, linear prediction, predictive coding, transform and subband coding, entropy coding, and vector quantization. Techniques and algorithms for efficient trade-offs between fidelity, bit-rate, and complexity. applications to speech, audio, image and video.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Digital Communication Fundamentals
courses.prereq_text: Signals and Systems (ECE 130A-B or equivalent); Probability (ECE 139 or equivalent).
courses.description: Signal and channel models, with emphasis on wireless systems; digital modulation; demodulation basics; statistical modeling of noise, including review of probability theory and random variables.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Wireless Communication and Networking
courses.description: Overview of wireless networks, characteristics of wireless medium, physical layer operation (spread spectrum, UWB, OFDM, adaptive modulation, MIMO channel), cellular planning, mobility management, energy-efficient networking, GSM, CDMA, wireless LANs, ad hoc networks, wireless geolocation systems.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: MOBILE EMBEDDED SYSTEMS
courses.prereq_text: Proficiency in JAVA programming, and a C- in ECE 152A.
courses.description: Architectures of modern smartphones and their key hardware components including mobile application processors, communications chips, display, touchscreen, graphics, camera, battery, GPS,and various sensors; the OS and software development platform of smartphones; smartphone applications; low power design techniques.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Computer Arithmetic
courses.description: Standard and unconventional number representations. Design of fast two-operand and multi-operand adders. High-speed mulitplication and division algorithms. Floating-point numbers, algorithms, and errors. Hardware algorithms for function evaluation. Pipelined, digit-serial, and fault-tolerant arithmetic processors.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Embedded System Design
courses.description: Design and application of embedded computing systems, particular attention paid to computation system design in highly constrained environments. System synthesis and modeling techniques including partitioning, scheduling, control and data flow analysis and functional representation. Embedded project design.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Advanced Computer Architecture: Parallel Processing
courses.description: The nature of concurrent computations. Idealized models of parallel systems. Practical realization of concurrency. Interconnection networks. Building-block parallel algorithms. Algorithm design, optimality, and efficiency. Mapping and scheduling of computations. Example mulitprocessors and multicomputers.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Advanced VLSI Architecture and Design
courses.prereq_text: ECE 124A or equivalent or ECE 256A or 256B
courses.description: Large scale VLSI design with attention to performance constraints in real-world designs. Topics include: circuit modeling, communication parasitics, architecture optimization, and packaging. Large scale project will be fabricated using silicon compilation tools.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Fault Tolerant Computing
courses.description: Basic concepts of dependable computing. Reliability of nonredundant and redundant systems. Dealing with circuit-level defects. Logic-level fault testing and tolerance. Error detection and correction. Diagnosis and reconfiguration for system-level malfunctions. Degradation management. Failure modeling and risk assessment.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Multirate Digital Signal Processing
courses.description: Multirate digital signal processing techniques for the analysis, synthesis, and representation of signals, including decimators and interpolators, polyphase decompositions, subband decompositions, analysis and synthesis filter banks, quadrature mirror filter banks, relationship to orthogonal transforms, and wavelet transforms.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: INTRODUCTION TO NANOPHOTONICS
courses.comments: OPEN TO ALL GRADUATE STUDENTS IN SCIENCE, TECHNOLOGY AND ENGINEERING DISCIPLINES.
courses.description: Covers the fundamentals of Nanophotonics. Focuses on reading and evaluating contemporary literature on nanophotonics research. Students work within 3-person groups to read and understand seminal papers in this area. Once a week a group is chosen at random to lead an in-class discussion on the paper(s) assigned for that week. Example topics include surface plasmons, near-field microscopy, Purcell enhancements, photonic crystals, multipole expansions, and metamaterials.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Physics of Solar Cells
courses.comments: OPEN TO GRADUATE STUDENTS IN THE SCIENCE, TECHNOLOGY AND ENGINEERING DISCIPLINES.
courses.description: Covers the fundamentals of Solar Cells, building to an understanding of next-generation Solar Cell concepts. Focuses on reading and evaluating contemporary literature on Solar Cell research. Students work within 3-person groups to read and understand seminal papers in Solar Cell research. Once a week a group is chosen at random to lead an in-class discussion on the paper(s) assigned for that week. Example topics include: perovskite, quantum dot, hot electron, or intermediate band solar cells, multiple exciton generation, thermal photovoltiacs, light trapping, efficiency limits, etc.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Network Systems: Dynamics and Control
courses.description: Motivating socio/economic networks, power grids, multi-agent robotics. Perron-Frobenius matrix theory and algebraic graph theory. Fundamental dynamics in networks: averaging dynamics in discrete and continuous time; positive and compartmental systems; robotic coordination problems; coupled oscillator systems; virus propagation models; population dynamic models.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: NONCOOPERATIVE GAME THEORY
courses.description: Formulation of problems as mathematical games and provides the basic tools to solve them. Covers both static and dynamic games. Intended for graduate students (but is not restricted to) in communications, controls, signal processing, and computer science.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Principles of Optimization
courses.description: Linear programming: simplex and revised simplex method, duality theory, primal-dual algorithms, Karmarkar's algorithm. Network flow problems: max-flow/min-cut theorem, Ford-Fulkerson algorithm, shortest path algorithms. Complexity and NP-completeness theory: the classes of P and NP,reductions between np-complete problems, pseudopolynomial and approximationalgorithms.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Dynamic Programming and Reinforcement Learning
courses.comments: ECE 271C and ME 254 are cross-listed and are the same course.
courses.description: This graduate course provides a comprehensive treatment of dynamic programming (DP) as the fundamental framework for staged optimization problems under uncertainty. Core topics include the principle of optimality, Bellman equations, value and policy iteration, deterministic and stochastic dynamic programming, and Markov decision processes. Applications span linear-quadratic optimal control, inventory control, asset management, hypothesis testing, the Viterbi algorithm, among others. The course concludes with modern reinforcement learning topics including Q-learning, temporal difference learning, and value function approximation, demonstrating how classical DP principles form the theoretical foundation for contemporary AI algorithms.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Machine Learning in Design and Test Automation
courses.description: A introduction to design and test automation processes and how machine learning can be applied to improve certain steps in those processes. Basic machine learning concepts and practices to apply machine learning in those design and test automation steps are discussed. Graduate students are are expected to be able to explore an assignment and discover a problem and then find a way to improve the outcome, hence developing their research ability.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Artificial Intelligence in Design and Test Automation
courses.description: An introduction of artificial intelligence applied to improve design and test processes. The various components to build an artificial intelligence system to assist engineering in design and test are discussed. Theoretical foundation related to those components are also discussed. Graduate students are are expected to be able to explore an assignment and discover a problem and then find a way to improve the outcome, hence developing their research ability.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: AI Agents for the Semiconductor Industry
courses.description: Cover theories and practices of verification/test for checking hardware correctness and trustworthiness of large language models. A connection between the two is drawn. Students learn the principles of verification and test and how to apply them in both contexts.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: TENSOR COMPUTATION FOR MACHINE LEARNING AND BIG DATA
courses.prereq_text: Solid background in linear algebra and statitics/probability, basic programing skills.
courses.description: Tensors have been increasingly used in data-intensive fields such as artificial intelligence and quantum computing. This course covers the notations, optimization and statistical methods of tensor computation, and their applications in machine learning (mainly deep learning) and quantum computing.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Neurally Inspired Computing Systems
courses.description: Basic understanding of computational principles and information coding in biological brains; biologically plausible neural and synaptic models; neutrally inspired network architectures, learning mechanisms, and training algorithms; hardware architectures and circuits for supporting efficient neutrally inspired learning.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: From Statistical Mechanics to Quantum Computing: A Unified View
courses.description: This course intertwines Statistical Mechanics, Probabilistic Graph Models, and Quantum Computing, starting with Boltzmann Law. It delves into machine learning, emphasizing Boltzmann Machines, progressing to quantum computation. This curriculum bridges statistical Machine Learning and Quantum Computing, offering a physics-based perspective.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Geometric AI: Equivariant, Topological and Geometric Deep Learning
courses.prereq_text: Knowledge of linear algebra, machine learning, deep learning, and python.
courses.description: Introduces students to the extensions of deep learning that analyze complex geometric data types, such as graphs, meshes, shapes, and deformations. We present equivariant, geometric, and topological deep learning to uncover the unifying, geometric principles of artificial intelligence.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Pattern Recognition
courses.description: Principles and design of pattern recognition systems. Statistical classifiers: discriminant functions; bayes, minimum risk, k-nearest neighbors, perceptrons. Clustering and estimation; criteria; k-means, fuzzy, hierarchal, graph-theoretic, simulated and determininstic annealing; maximum likelihood and bayesian methods: nonparametric methods. Overview of applications.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Digital Image Processing
courses.description: Two-dimensional signals and systems. Two-dimension al fourier and z-transforms. Discrete fourier transform, two-dimensional digital filters. Image processing basics, image enhancement and restoration. Special image processing software available for laboratory experimentation.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Imaging Systems
courses.description: Generalized holography, backward techniques, resolution limit, x-ray tomography, diffraction tomography, NMR imaging, synthetic-aperture radar, active sonar imaging, acoustic microscopy, imaging algorithms, motion estimation and tracking.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Computer Vision
courses.comments: Same course as Computer Science 281B.
courses.description: Advanced topics in computer vision: image sequence analysis, spatio- temporal filtering, camera calibration and hand-eye coordination, robot navigation, shape representation, physically-based modeling, regularization theory, multi- sensory fusion, biological models, expert vision systems, and other topics selected from recent research papers.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Error Correcting Codes
courses.description: Principles and techniques for combating channel errors in data transmission or storage. Introduction to galois fields. Linear blockcodes (particularly hamming, BCH, reed-solomon). Convolutional codes. Encoding and decoding algorithms (including spectral methods, maximum likelihood and viterbi decoding.)

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: MACHINE LEARNING: A SIGNAL PROCESSING PERSPECTIVE
courses.description: Machine learning algorithms from a signal processing viewpoint; unsupervised learning (K-means, deterministic annealing, EM algorithm); supervised learning (Support Vector Machines, neural networks); regression; Bayesian inference and tracking using Markov chain Monte Carlo and sequential Monte Carlo (particle filter) techniques.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: THEORETICAL MACHINE LEARNING
courses.description: This course studies the mathematical foundations of machine learning, and focuses on understanding the trade-offs between statistical accuracy, scalability, and computation efficiency of distributed machine learning and optimization algorithms. Topics include empirical risk, convexity in learning, convergence analysis of gradient descent algorithm, stochastic gradient descent, neural networks, and reinforcement learning.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: ADVANCED IMAGE SYNTHESIS
courses.prereq_text: Computer Graphics desired but not necessary
courses.description: Theory and design of rendering systems for high-end image synthesis and modeling physically-based light transport. Topics include REYES-style architectures, Monte Carlo algorithms, variance reduction methods, path tracing, photon mapping, reflection and volumetric light transport. Students must have good software engineering skills.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: INTRODUCTION TO ROBOTICS: DYNAMICS AND CONTROL
courses.prereq_text: ECE 130A or ME 155A (may be taken concurrently).
courses.description: Dynamic modeling and control methods for robotic systems. Lagrangian method for deriving equations of motion, introduction to the Jacobian, and modeling and control of forces and contact dynamics at a robotic end effector. Laboratories encourage a problem-solving approach to control.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Group Studies: Controls, Dynamical Systems, and Computation
courses.comments: Same course as Chemical Engineering 295, Computer Science 592, and ME 295.
courses.description: A series of weekly lectures given by university staff and outside experts in the fields of control systems, dynamical systems, and computation.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Internship in Industry
courses.prereq_text: Prior departmental approval needed. ECE majors only.
courses.description: Special projects for selected students. Offered in conjunction with engineering practice in selected industrial and research firms, under direct faculty supervision.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Teaching of Electrical and Computer Engineering
courses.comments: Open to Electrical and Computer Engineering Teaching Assistants only. No unit credit allowed toward advanced degree.
courses.description: Procedures and techniques for teaching electrical engineering or computer engineering gained through actual teaching of lecture courses, leading discussion sections, and/or teaching engineering laboratories. Meetings will be held as needed to discuss problems, methods, and procedures.

courses.title: Directed Research
courses.description: Research, either experimental or theoretical; may be undertaken by properly qualified graduate students under the direction of a faculty member.

courses.title: Individual Studies for M.S. Comprehensive Examinations and Ph.D. Examinations
courses.comments: Maximum of 12 units per quarter. S/U grading. Instructor is normally student's major professor or chairman of doctoral committee. No unit creditallowed toward advanced degree. Enrollment limited to 24 units per exam.
courses.description: Individual studies for M.S. comprehensive examinations and Ph.D. examinations.

courses.title: Master's Thesis Research and Preparation
courses.comments: No unit allowed toward degree.
courses.description: For research underlying the thesis and writing of the thesis.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Ph.D. Dissertation Research and Preparation
courses.prereq_text: Consent of chair of student's doctoral committee.
courses.description: Research and preparation of dissertation.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Principles of Economics-Micro
courses.description: An introduction to microeconomic analysis. Economic theory related to demand, production, competitive and non-competitive product markets, input markets, and welfare. Applications of microeconomic theory including its use in evaluating and forming public policy.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Principles of Economics-Macro
courses.description: An introduction to macroeconomic analysis. Analysis of income, employment, and price level. Applications of macroeconomic theory including its use in evaluating and forming public policy.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Financial Accounting
courses.description: A two-quarter series providing an introduction to the purposes, conceptual framework, measurement principles and reporting issues of accounting. Particular emphasis will be placed on the links between accounting, economics, and finance.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Financial Accounting - Honors
courses.description: Students receive one unit for the honors seminar. Intended for highly motivated and well prepared students.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Financial Accounting
courses.description: A two-quarter series providing an introduction to the purposes, conceptual framework, measurement principles and reporting issues of accounting. Particular emphasis will be placed on the links between accounting, economics, and finance.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Financial Accounting - Honors
courses.description: Students receive one unit for the honors seminar. Intended for highly motivated and well prepared students.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Statistics for Economics
courses.prereq_text: Math 34A-B or Math 2A-B or 3A-B; Math 34B or 2B or 3B can be taken simultaneously. Course cannot be used to satisfy any Actuarial Science, Financial Math & Statistics or Statistical Science major or minor requirements.
courses.comments: Course must be taken at UCSB.Not open for credit to students who have completed PSTAT 109.Cannot be taken concurrently with PSTAT 109.
courses.description: An introduction to probalistic modeling and statistical inference applied to the analysis of economic data for students with basic knowledge of calculus. Topics covered include: probability, discrete and continuous random variables, probability distributions, mean, variance, correlation, sampling, parameter estimation, unbiasedness and efficiency, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing. Computing labs with Excel.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Introduction to Economics
courses.comments: Course cannot be used to satisfy any economics major requirements.
courses.description: A broad survey of economic principles, including both microeconomics and macroeconomics.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Intermediate Microeconomic Theory
courses.comments: Course must be taken at UCSB. ECON W 10A is the online version of ECON 10A.
courses.description: Economic theory relating to demand, production, and competitive product markets with emphasis on applications of theory.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Internship in Economics
courses.comments: Open to Pre-Economics, Pre-Economics and Accounting and Pre-Economics/Mathematics majors only.
courses.description: Course enables students to obtain credit for economics-related internship experience. A seven to ten page written report is required and evaluated for credit.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Introduction to Finance
courses.description: Provides a non-technical introduction to finance and its role in modern economic life. Examines how financial decisions affect individuals, firms, and society as a whole. Topics include risk and return; financial markets, trading, and efficiency; and financial intermediaries and securities.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Sophomore Honors Seminar
courses.prereq_text: Approval by the Department based on performance inEconomics 1 and 2.
courses.description: Small seminar class that gives sophomores interested in pursuing economic research the opportunity to read and discuss selected economics texts and research papers. The objective is to expose students to a wide range of research topics in order to give them a flavor of the research opportunities available.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: New Student Seminar
courses.description: The primary goal of Economics 97 is to assist in a successful transition from high school to university learning. Economics 97 consists of lectures presented by staff, faculty, and current students to provide information about specific campus policies, the Economics major/curriculum, introduction to campus resources, and exploring career options. Economics 97 will allow you to develop time management skills, necessary study habits, and help you apply them to ensure a successful career as a Gaucho and beyond.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Intermediate Microeconomic Theory
courses.prereq_text: Economics 10A or 100A; and, Economics 5 or PSTAT 109 or PSTAT 120A.
courses.comments: No credit will be given to students who have taken Economics 104B.
courses.description: Economic theory relating to imperfectly competitive product markets, input market, and welfare, with emphasis on applications. Includes an introduction to game theory.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Intermediate Microeconomic Theory
courses.description: Covers topics including externalities, law and economics, information technologies, public goods and asymmetric information. These topics are essential to understanding real markets, but are currently not included in the Economics 100A-B sequence.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Intermediate Macroeconomic Theory
courses.prereq_text: Economics 10A or 100A; and, Economics 5 or PSTAT 109 or PSTAT 120A.
courses.comments: Reduced credit of 2 units will be given to students who have taken both Economics 101 and 105.
courses.description: Contemporary analysis of income, employment, price level, and public policy using static general equilibrium framework with emphasis on applications of theory. Long term economic growth is also covered.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Managerial Economics
courses.description: Economic principles will be applied to practical decision-making situations. Methods of price and output determination, capital budgeting, and choices under uncertainty. Methods of economic analysis and their application will be emphasized.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: History of Economics
courses.description: Economic thought from antiquity through John Stuart Mill. Economic thought in the Bible, Greece, Rome, India, and China through the classical economists--Thomas Hobbes, John Locke, Adam Smith, Jeremy Bentham, Thomas Malthus, David Ricardo, and John Stuart Mill. Emphasis on both economic activity and economic thought, including discussion of feudal and mercantilist societies. The economic roles of women and slavery are presented.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: History of Economics
courses.description: Economic thought from Karl Marx to the present, with emphasis on public policy, institutions, and historical circumstances. In addition to Marx economists who are emphasized include John Maynard Keynes, Friedrich Hayek, and Milton Friedman. Features discussions of capitalism, socialism, and communism and student presentations. Other foci include the Great Depression and economic policy and thought in the Reagan administration to the present.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: European Economic History to 1850
courses.description: Analysis of the economic development of Europe from the Middle Ages through the English Industrial Revolution.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Twentieth-Century United States Economic History
courses.description: A survey of U.S. economic development in the twentieth century with emphasis on issues related to the growth, instability, and distribution of income. The impact of public policy on economic growth, instability, and income distribution will be an important theme of the course.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Economic Development
courses.description: Microeconomic issues of developing nations. Applications of analytical tools to the microeconomic problems of developing nations. Topics include poverty and income distributions, population, rural-urban migration, education, nutrition, labor supply, and poverty wages.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Economic Development
courses.description: Macroeconomic issues of developing nations. Applications of analytical tools to the growth of developing nations. The theoretical relationship between factor accumulation, productivity, and growth are examined. Topics include Solow growth model, institutions, culture, and geography.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Environmental Economics
courses.comments: Same course as Environmental Studies 175.
courses.description: provides a rigorous treatment of environment economics. Topics include welfare analysis, ethical dimensions of economic criteria for protecting the environment, measuring the demand for environmental goods, property rights, economic incentives, including marketable permits and emission fees, and regulating risk.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Industrial Organization Principles
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Economics 116.
courses.description: Analysis of competition, monopolistic competition, oligopoly, and monopoly theories and practices.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Law and Economics I
courses.description: Application of economic analysis to the law. Includes an introduction to common law, constitutional law, and legal processes. Topics may include property law, contract law, and tort law.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Financial Accounting Analysis and Planning
courses.comments: Course is equivalent to ECON W 118.
courses.description: An economic analysis of financial statements in a macroeconomic environment. Topics include evaluation of short term and long term liquidity, profitability, capital structure and the forecast of earnings and financial position using financial and economic models.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Financial Accounting Analysis and Planning - Honors
courses.description: Students receive one unit for the honors seminar. Intended for highly motivated and well prepared students.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Urban and Regional Economics
courses.description: Economic analysis applied to current urban and regional problems.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Public Finance
courses.description: Fiscal theory and policy. Incidence and effects of taxation, government expenditure programs, and benefit cost analysis.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Economics and Public Policy
courses.description: Uses economic analysis and empirical evidence to examine a range of public policy issues. Topics may include education, health, inequality, labor markets, crime, environmental policy, and the social safety net. Students learn how economists identify market and policy failures, assess the intended and unintended effects of government interventions, and use data to evaluate whether policies achieve their goals.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Auditing
courses.comments: Not open to students who have successfully completed Economics 132.
courses.description: Developing an understanding of concepts and practices for audits of financial statements. Studying professional standards, ethics, and legal liability. The audit process is covered in-depth: planning, internal control, audit risk, materiality, evidence, program design, sampling, completing the audit, and reporting.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Auditing - Honors
courses.description: Students receive one unit for the honors seminar. Intended for highly motivated and well prepared students.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Topics in Macroeconomic Theory
courses.description: Topics may include fiscal policy and government budget deficits, monetary policy and inflation, investment and economic growth, theories of the business cycle, rational expectations and the Lucas critique, optimal taxation and the time consistency of government policies. Content may vary from year to year.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Financial Management
courses.description: Discounting of certain future cash flows. Principles of evaluation of investment projects. Demand and supply of investment funds. Risk and the valuation of asset prices. Analysis of a firm's debt and dividend policies;the effect of taxes and inflation on these policies.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Behavioral Finance
courses.description: Describes several puzzles in financial markets, including phenomena that are hard to explain using standard economic models. Develops several alternatives to standard economic models in which agents make errors or have preferences that differ from those typically assumed by economists. These "behavioral models" are motivated by evidence from psychology, lab experiments in economics, and field experiments, some of which are reviewed. Explores how such behavioral models can explain puzzles both at the level of individual investing and at an aggregate level (market volume and pricing).

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Monetary Economics
courses.description: Survey of monetary theory, the banking system and the supply of money, monetary policy, and current issues.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Intermediate Accounting
courses.prereq_text: Economics 3B; and, Economics 10A or 100A; and, Economics 5 or PSTAT 109 or PSTAT 120A.
courses.description: An in-depth analysis of recognition, measurement, classification, and valuation issues in financial reporting within the framework of generally accepted accounting principles. Case studies and microcomputer analysis software will be integrated into the course.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Intermediate Accounting - Honors
courses.description: Students receive one unit for the honors seminar. Intended for highly motivated and well prepared students.

courses.title: Intermediate Accounting
courses.description: An in-depth analysis of recognition, measurement, classification, and valuation issues in financial reporting within the framework of generally accepted accounting principles. Case studies and microcomputer analysis software will be integrated into the course.

courses.title: Intermediate Accounting - Honors
courses.description: Students receive one unit for the honors seminar. Intended for highly motivated and well prepared students.

courses.title: Intermediate Accounting
courses.description: An in-depth analysis of recognition, measurement, classification, and valuation issues in financial reporting within the framework of generally accepted accounting principles. Case studies and microcomputer analysis software will be integrated into the course.

courses.title: Intermediate Accounting - Honors
courses.description: Students receive one unit for the honors seminar. Intended for highly motivated and well prepared students.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Managerial Accounting
courses.prereq_text: Economics 3B; and, Economics 10A or 100A; and, Economics 5 or PSTAT 109 or PSTAT 120A.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Economics 137.
courses.description: A two quarter series covering the theory and application of managerial accounting concepts. The course investigates the interaction between economic theory, financial accounting, and management decision making for planning and control.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Managerial Accounting - Honors
courses.description: Students receive one unit for the honors seminar. Intended for highly motivated and well prepared students.

courses.title: Managerial Accounting
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Economics 137.
courses.description: A two-quarter series covering the theory and application of managerial accounting concepts. The course investigates the interaction between economic theory, financial accounting, and management decision making for planning and control.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Managerial Accounting - Honors
courses.description: Students receive one unit for the honors seminar. Intended for highly motivated and well prepared students.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Income Taxation
courses.prereq_text: Economics 3B; and, Economics 10A or 100A; and, Economics 5 or PSTAT 109 or PSTAT 120A.
courses.description: An introduction to taxation. The basic theories, concepts, and general rules of federal income tax and their interrelationships with personal, business, and financial transactions. The course provides an understanding of tax policies and the interrelationship between tax and financial decisions.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Income Taxation
courses.description: An introduction to taxation. The basic theories, concepts, and general rules of federal income tax and their interrelationships with personal, business, and financial transactions. The course provides an understanding of tax policies and the interrelationship between tax and financial decisions.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Advanced Accounting
courses.description: Accounting for business combinations and preparation of consolidated financial statements, principles of fund accounting (governmental and non-profit entities), foreign currency translation and transactions, partnership formation, operation, and liquidation.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Advanced Accounting - Honors
courses.description: Students receive one unit for the honors seminar. Intended for highly motivated and well prepared students.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Introduction to Econometrics
courses.prereq_text: Economics 10A or 100A; and, Economics 5 or PSTAT 109 or PSTAT 120A.
courses.description: Introduction to econometrics for data analysis in economics and social sciences. The goal of the course is to learn how to use simple and multivariate linear regression for analyzing the relationship between economic variables, for prediction and for causal inference, understanding its underlying assumptions, advantages and pitfalls.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Introduction to Econometrics
courses.description: Topics in econometrics including regression specification, time series econometrics, panel data, and instrumental variables.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: An introduction to core machine learning and nonparametric tools for economics, emphasizing prediction, classification, and causal inference. Students learn how to build, tune, and evaluate modern methods such as partitioned regression and splines, binned scatter plots, LASSO and ridge regression, decision trees, random forests, and neural networks. Time permitting the course covers embeddings, transformers, and attention. Computation using R is emphasized using real-world data.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Data Wrangling for Economics
courses.prereq_text: Open to ECON and ECACC majors or by consent of instructor.
courses.comments: During Pass 3 students in the Pre-Economics and Pre-Economics & Accounting majors who have earned a minimum grade of B in ECON 1 or a minimum grade of B in ECON 2 can request add codes to enroll.
courses.description: Students develop skills in organizing economic data, learning how to summarize and display data to answer substantive economic questions. Emphasis is placed on communication of results.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Labor Economics
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Economics 150B.
courses.description: Analyzes the determinants of labor supply, labor demand, equilibrium, and the structure of wages. Topics include compensating differentials, education, labor mobility, and discrimination.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Economics of Gender
courses.description: Addresses issues of gender and family in the economy from a theoretical and empirical perspective. Economic models of marriage, divorce, and fertility with the goal of understanding the large changes in family structure that have occurred in the US will be studied. Womens behavior in the labor force, and issues of poverty and gender gaps in labor market outcomes will be examined. Current policy issues of teen childbearing, parental leave, welfare reform and child support will be discussed.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Personnel Economics
courses.description: Studies the allocation and pricing of labor within firms. Topics covered include employee selection, design of optimal piece rates, advantages and disadvantages of seniority-based pay, tournaments and promotions, and incentives in team production.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Topics in Applied Economics
courses.description: The objective of this course is to integrate and apply the economic insights learned in the major to various topics of real-world relevance. Topics are presented from theoretical and empirical perspectives, and ethical considerations will be discussed. Possible topics include antitrust and collusion, statistical and preference-based discrimination, affirmative action, and the design of markets.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Behavioral Economics
courses.description: Studies the psychological processes and biases underlying economic decision-making, with a focus on the ways in which decisions deviate from “optimal” choices (from the viewpoint of standard economic theory) and the consequences of such deviations for consumers, managers, firms, and policymakers. Builds on the analytical foundation provided by Econ 100B - Intermediate Microeconomic Theory.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Health Economics
courses.description: Application of economic and statistical principles to health and health services. Topics may include the determinants of health, supply of and demand for health care and health insurance, health disparities, public policy, and international comparisons, among other relevant topics.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Introduction to Game Theory
courses.description: A rigorous study of strategic interaction. Topics include normal and extensive form games, existence and uniqueness of equilibrium, randomization, minimax, dynamics and equilibrium selection, auctions and bargaining, principle-agent incentives, voting, private contributions to public goods, oligopoly competition, market entry and burning money, wars of attrition.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Negotiations
courses.description: Applied theories as guides to improving negotiations. Develop and sharpen negotiating skills by participating in realistic negotiating simulations. A number of cases will be presented; individuals make choices about actions and tactics within the negotiation.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Experimental Economics
courses.description: Introduction to the idea that economics, like all of the natural sciences, can be a laboratory science. Focus on performing and engaging in experiments. Students design experiments and discuss the designs of others.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Auction
courses.description: Auction theory and its applications. Gain insight into how different auction rules influence bidding behavior and impact seller revenue. The course covers private and common value auctions. Topics include the revenue equivalence theorem and the winner's curse.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: International Trade
courses.description: International trade theory and policies with examples from current issues and problems.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: International Finance
courses.description: International money and capital markets and their impact on the domestic and world economies; international financial institutions and policies.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Entrepreneurial Insights
courses.description: A seminar-style course oriented around external speakers, representing a wide range of entrepreneurial experiences (different backgrounds, different phases of their careers, different company types, and so on). Intensive research and question development required for each speaker.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Audit Data Analytics in Accounting Information Systems
courses.prereq_text: Economics 3B; and Economics 10A; and Economics 5 or PSTAT 120A
courses.description: A study of the analysis, design, and implementation of accounting information systems. This includes auditing information processed by the IT environment and performing data analytics.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Topics in Personnel Economics
courses.description: The goal of the course is to help students learn about how personnel economists think about key topics in human resources. We will focus on the topics of hiring, managers, management practices, workplace amenities, workplace communication, and monitoring. The course is a complement to Professor Peter Kuhn's class on Personnel Economics. Relative to Professor Kuhn's class, we will focus on different topics. We will also focus on reading and discussing academic papers, and there is no textbook. The ultimate goal is for you to be fully acquainted with insights from personnel economics, and for you to gain experience evaluating evidence and claims about how to manage the workforce.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Business Law and Ethics in Accounting
courses.prereq_text: Economics 3B; and, Economics 10A or 100A; and, Economics 5 or PSTAT 109 or PSTAT 120A.
courses.comments: *This course cannot be used as an elective for the ECON major. This class is only usable as a major elective for the ECACC major.
courses.description: Provides a basic understanding of ethics and the legal framework within which U.S. businesses operate. Includes a broad overview of court procedures and in-depth coverage of selected topics including contracts, securities, and property rights.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Business Law and Ethics - Honors
courses.description: Students receive one unit for the honors seminar. Intended for highly motivated and well prepared students.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Special Topics in Economics
courses.comments: Open to economics majors only.
courses.description: Lectures in special areas of interest in economics. Consult the department office regarding proposed course topics.

courses.comments: Open to economics majors only.
courses.description: Lectures in special areas of interest in economics. Consult the department office regarding proposed course topics.

courses.title: Special Topics in Economics
courses.comments: Open to economics majors only. May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units. Up to 8 units may be applied to the major providing letter designations are different.
courses.description: Lectures in special areas of interest in economics. Consult the department office regarding proposed course topics.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Internship in Economics
courses.comments: Open to Business Economics, Economics, Economics and Accounting and Economics/Mathematics majors only.
courses.description: Course enables students to obtain credit for economics-related internship experience. An eight to ten page written report is required and evaluated for credit.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Group Studies
courses.comments: Subject to departmental approval, students my repeat this course; however, only four units may count toward major.
courses.description: Intensive study and research on a topic in economics selected by the student with the guidance and approval of a faculty member.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Dean's Investment Group
courses.comments: Subject to departmental approval, students my repeat this course; however, only four units may count toward major.
courses.description: Students participate in the Dean's Investment Group (DIG). DIG members do extensive research to design and manage the Dean's Investment Fund. They have primary responsibility for all investment decisions and have the opportunity to meet regularly with industry experts on the Board of Advisors.

courses.comments: Subject to departmental approval, students my repeat this course; however, only four units may count toward major.
courses.description: Intensive study and research on a topic in economics selected by the student with the guidance and approval of a faculty member.

courses.comments: Subject to departmental approval, students my repeat this course; however, only four units may count toward major.
courses.description: Intensive study and research on a topic in economics selected by the student with the guidance and approval of a faculty member.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Senior Honors Seminar
courses.prereq_text: 3.5 GPA in Economics 10A, 100B, 101, 140A and 140B. Concurrent enrollment in 140B allowed.
courses.description: Students undertake independent research project under direction of faculty member. The research results are presented as an honors paper at the end of the second term (196B). Enrollment in this course is application-based. The application will be sent directly to students who have completed the honors seminars Econ 96 and 194S, and priority consideration will be given to these students. Students who have not taken Econ 96 or 194S may request access to the application form by emailing the Economics Department Undergraduate Advising Office.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Senior Honors Seminar
courses.description: Students undertake independent research project(s) under direction of faculty member. The research results are presented as an honors paper at the end of the second term (196B).

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Independent Studies in Economics
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing in the major; 3.0 UD major GPA and 3.0 GPA in preceding 3 quarters; completion of 2 upper-division courses in Economics; consent of department and instructor.
courses.comments: Only 12 units of Econ 199 may apply to the major
courses.description: Coursework shall consist of academic research supervised by a faculty member. This course is not intended for internships.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Independent Research in Economics
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division courses in Economics; consent of instructor and department.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined. Does not count towards the upper-division major.
courses.description: Course work shall consist of faculty supervised research.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Macroeconomic Theory
courses.description: Introduction to modern macroeconomics. Study of economic growth and dynamic optimization. Representative agent, overlapping generations and monetary models will be covered.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Macroeconomic Theory
courses.description: Introduction to dynamic programming. Arrow-Debreu Equilibria, Sequences of Market Equilibria, Recursive Competitive Equilibria. First and second welfare theorems. Real Business Cycles.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Macroeconomic Theory
courses.description: Focus on frictional economics. Topics to include: economies with incomplete markets, private information, search and matching.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Theory of Consumption and Production
courses.description: Constrained optimization; consumer theory and theory of the firm; uncertainty, risk and expected utility.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Game Theory
courses.description: Non-cooperative and cooperative game theory; bargaining and auctions; topics in asymmetric information including adverse selection, signaling and screening.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Markets and Incentives
courses.description: Partial and general equilibrium of competitive and non-competitive markets. Topics to include uncertainty; welfare theorems for competitive markets; imperfect competition; externalities and public goods.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Economic Growth and Economic Development
courses.prereq_text: Second-year Ph.D. in Economics graduate student standing.
courses.description: This course introduces several of the main economic issues that developing countries confront today. The primary focus is on understanding macroeconomic aspects of economic growth through traditional economic growth models. The class examines the theoretical foundations of these models but also examines their validity using relevant data and empirical tests.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Beyond Economic Growth
courses.prereq_text: Second-year Ph.D. in Economics graduate student standing.
courses.description: This course introduces a macroeconomic analysis of demographic changes and changes in the economic structure during the process of economic development. Topics include the demographic transition; the shift from agrarian to industrial economies, including the rise of the service sector; and a macroeconomic analysis of economic growth and income inequality.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Behavioral Development Economics
courses.prereq_text: Second year PhD in Economics graduate student standing, or Second year in Bren PhD EES student standing.
courses.description: This course applies theories from behavioral economics to questions related to poverty, inequality and economic development, and asks whether the behavioral economics of poverty and development is different. The course emphasizes the use of empirical designs including field experiments, applied econometric methods and structural estimation to test theory.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Bounded Rationality
courses.prereq_text: Second year Ph.D. in Economics graduate student standing.�
courses.description: Studies the behavior of individuals who face limits to their thinking capacity. Topics include: decision theory, costly information acquisition and processing, bounded memory, and bounded rationality in games.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Behavioral Economics
courses.prereq_text: Second year Ph.D. in Economics graduate student standing.�
courses.description: Studies the effects of psychological, social, cognitive and emotional factors on economic decisions of individuals and institutions and the consequences for market prices and the allocation of resources. Topics include: values, preferences and choices, beliefs, heuristics and biases, prospect theory, decision making under risk and uncertainty, mental accounting, hyperbolic discounting, and social preferences.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Topics in Firm Dynamics
courses.prereq_text: Economics 204A, Economics 204B, Economics 204C (all three courses required)
courses.description: Explores both theoretical and empirical aspects of firm dynamics. Covers classical and contemporary research on firms' dynamic decisions in areas such as innovation, corporate finance, and international trade. Students will develop skills in modeling and data analysis to study firm behavior and its implications for aggregate outcomes, including economic growth, market concentration, and trade patterns.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Computational Methods for Macroeconomics
courses.prereq_text: Second-year Ph.D. in Economics graduate student standing.
courses.description: Covers the tools required to solve state-of-the-art models in quantitative macroeconomics: dynamic programming, projection, perturbation, and deep learning algorithms. Special emphasis is given to learning contemporary programming techniques and modern software engineering workflows. Although most examples will come from macro, students in other fields (IO, international, etc.) can follow the material, and the main ideas also apply to their problems. Evaluations will be based on homework assignments, and a replication exercise.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Aggregate Economics
courses.prereq_text: Economics 204A, Economics 204B, Economics 204C and Second year Ph.D. graduate student standing.
courses.description: Develop and use model abstractions obtaining quantitative answers to questions in aggregate economics. Focus is theoretical, quantitative, & empirical analyses across several areas; Great Depressions, Mobility and Unemployment, Demographics, Financial Frictions, Output, & Labor Markets, and Money & Monetary Policy.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Public Economics I
courses.prereq_text: Second-year Ph.D. in Economics graduate student standing.
courses.description: Theory of public goods. Government and non-government policies for management of externalities.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Public Economics II
courses.prereq_text: Second-year Ph.D. in Economics graduate student standing.
courses.description: Theory of social choice and voting. Benefit-cost analysis. Introduction to mechanism design theory. Assorted topics in public policy.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Individual Taxation
courses.prereq_text: Second year Ph.D. in Economics graduate student standing.�
courses.description: After a brief overview of optimal labor income taxation, the course focuses on empirical analysis of behavioral responses to individual taxes. Empirical topics include labor supply responses to taxes and transfers, taxable income elasticities, tax avoidance, evasion, and tax enforcement.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Capital Taxation
courses.prereq_text: Second year Ph.D. in Economics graduate student standing.�
courses.description: Covers the theory and empirical analysis of capital taxes. In the first part, we cover optimal capital taxation and we derive theoretical predictions of responses to capital income taxes such as corporate, dividend and capital gains taxes. The second part focuses on empirical analysis of existing capital tax structures.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Tax Incidence
courses.prereq_text: Second year Ph.D. in Economics graduate student standing.�
courses.description: Covers the theory and empirical analysis of tax incidence. Theoretical models will focus on the incidence of taxes in partial and general equilibrium models. The empirical analysis will focus on recent advances in estimating the incidence of consumption taxes, payroll taxes, corporate taxes and income taxes.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Health Economics
courses.prereq_text: Second year Ph.D. in Economics graduate student standing.
courses.description: Introduction to the economics of health, health services and insurance. It applies economic, statistical principles, and techniques, to the production of health and the closely related markets for health insurance and services. Emphasis on applying I.O. principles and analyzing policy relevant to the health insurance and services markets. Focus on topics, not methods, and will cater to students especially interested in applied micro. Goal is to take students close to the research frontier, educate about the history and institutions of US healthcare, and generate research topics. Most research in health economics is heavily empirical, and course highlights theory to guide hypothesis testing and the specification of empirical models.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Health Economics II
courses.prereq_text: Second-year Ph.D. in Economics graduate student standing.
courses.description: Introduction to health economics, second half. We will apply economic principles and econometric techniques to the production of health and health care. Emphasis on reduced-form methods for analyzing policy relevant to health care markets. Focus on topics, not methods, and will cater to students especially interested in applied micro. The goal is to take students close to the research frontier, educate them about the history and institutions of US healthcare, and generate research topics. Most research in health economics is heavily empirical, and the course will highlight theory to guide hypothesis testing and the specification of empirical models.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Econometrics
courses.description: Elements of probability and statistics for econometrics. Probability density functions, moment-generating functions, central limit theorems, method of maximum likelihood.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Econometrics
courses.description: The intuition and theory underpinning estimation of single and multiple equation regression models.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Econometrics
courses.description: Econometric foundations and practical aspects of some of the most commonly used empirical research methods including instrumental variables, GMM, panel data and nonlinear models.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Panel Data and Difference-in-Differences
courses.prereq_text: Second year Ph.D. in Economics graduate student standing.�
courses.description: How to control for endogeneity through the analysis of panel data. We begin with fixed (and random) effects models. We then treat approaches developed for experimental settings difference-in-differences and synthetic controls. These two approaches are examples of matrix completion problems and we discuss the appropriate completion methods in light of the underlying norm, or loss function.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Clustering, Bootstrapping, and Multiple Comparisons
courses.prereq_text: Second year Ph.D. in Economics graduate student standing.�
courses.description: Accurate hypothesis testing with focus on best procedures for estimating standard errors and approximating the distribution of test statistics. Central focus on linear models with a wide range of correlation structures, including cluster correlation. Use of the bootstrap to produce finite sample approximations of test statistics. Multiple comparison tests.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Regression Discontinuity
courses.prereq_text: Second year Ph.D. in Economics graduate student standing.�
courses.description: Covers both classical results and recent advances in identification, estimation and inference for regression discontinuity (RD) designs. Provides rigorous econometric foundations to understand how to conduct and improve empirical practice (e.g., how to find an optimal bandwidth, construct valid confidence intervals, etc). Along the course, ideas are illustrated using a collection of software packages specifically designed to incorporate these recent advances in RD into applied research.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Field Experiments
courses.prereq_text: Second year Ph.D. in Economics graduate student standing.
courses.description: Reviews several topics related to the analysis of field experiments. How to handle attrition, and differential attrition in field experiments? How to estimate heterogeneous treatment effects in field experiments? How to select the controls that should be included in the estimation of the treatment effect? How to estimate spillover effects on untreated units? How to estimate standard errors in field experiments where randomization occurs within pairs of units?

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Nonparametric Econometrics
courses.prereq_text: Second year Ph.D. in Economics graduate student standing.
courses.description: An introduction to nonparametric econometrics. The goal is to learn how to estimate parameters of interest by "letting the data speak", that is, imposing as few modeling assumptions as possible. The course starts with simple density and distribution function estimators, and then moves on to methods for nonparametric and semiparametric regression such as kernel regression, local polynomials and series estimators.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Economics Data Wrangling
courses.prereq_text: Second year Ph.D. in Economics graduate student standing.
courses.description: Organize, filter, and clean data. Estimate statistical models and learn to create reproducible research results. Course includes instruction in the R language.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Causal Machine Learning
courses.prereq_text: Second-year Ph.D. in Economics graduate student standing.
courses.description: This course will bring students to the cutting edge in causal inference using machine learning, giving them a solid theoretical understanding and ready-to-deploy tools for research. Using machine learning for estimation and inference of treatment effects has become an important part of modern academic economics. Students will learn to implement deep learning and conduct semiparametric inference using double machine learning. Students in this class will learn the theoretical underpinnings of this material as well as how to carefully and correctly apply the techniques in research.
