The course will prepare students for both theoretical and applied dissertation research.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Population Economics
courses.prereq_text: Second year Ph.D. graduate student standing.
courses.description: Course examines the determinants of population change and demographic behavior including household formation and dissolution, marriage and decision-making within households, child bearing and rearing, mortality (including infant mortality) and key forms of human capital investment including schooling and migration. Well apply theoretical and empirical tools to investigate the sources and consequences of demographic transitions including recent phenomena such as population aging, the emergence of lowest low fertility, and consider the role of policy instruments in changing demographic behavior.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Labor Supply
courses.prereq_text: Second year Ph.D. in Economics graduate student standing.
courses.description: Theory of static and dynamic labor supply. Testing model implications with lab experiments, field experiments, natural experiments and observational data. Quantifying the partial and general equilibrium impacts of taxes and income support programs on labor supply, income and welfare. Classical and behavioral models of the supply of effort, including reference points, procrastination, fairness concerns and reciprocity.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Economics of Education
courses.prereq_text: Second year Ph.D. in Economics graduate student standing.�
courses.description: Examines a range of topics related to education. These include the return to education, the quality of education, the role of peer groups, the market for teachers, school choice, and the importance of institutional structures.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Human Capital
courses.prereq_text: Second year Ph.D. in Economics graduate student standing.�
courses.description: Focuses on identifying the key factors that influence the development of human capital from the prenatal period through adulthood. Explores the important roles played by families, peers, schools, and communities.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Personnel Economics
courses.prereq_text: Second year Ph.D. in Economics graduate student standing.
courses.description: A formal economic approach to the design of incentives and the selection and retention of personnel within organizations, including both classical and behavioral approaches. Includes static and dynamic principal-agent models with risk-neutral and risk-averse agents, the economics of tournaments and teams, multi-task agency problems, ratchet effects and career concerns. Optimal testing and monitoring of employees and efficiency wage models.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Personnel Economics II
courses.prereq_text: Second-year Ph.D. in Economics graduate student standing.
courses.description: This course provides a treatment of personnel economics, and the application of labor economics to issues inside of firms. We focus on topics covered less in the course by Professor Peter Kuhn, including hiring, workplace amenities, workplace communication, management practices, managers, monitoring, and time use. The majority of papers we will read will be empirical papers. However, much of personnel economics is grounded in economic theory, so we will also go through theoretical ideas and some theory papers. We will also spend time developing our taste for what constitutes a quality empirical research paper. The ultimate goal is for you to leave prepared to undertake your own empirical research.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Job Search Theory
courses.prereq_text: Second year Ph.D. in Economics graduate student standing.�
courses.description: Theoretical and quantitative aspects of search theory as it applies to labor markets. Includes topics such as bargaining and models of wage determination, vacancies and unemployment.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Topics in Search and Matching
courses.description: Surveys topics in search and matching theory with a particular emphasis on unemployment and the labor market. As far as possible, the topics will be chosen to complement the material covered in Economics 253A. Examples of topics covered are: (1) Competitive search with particular emphasis on markets with asymmetric information, (2) Applications of search theory to the housing market and (3) Applications of search theory to informal labor markets in Latin America.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Natural Resource Economics: Dynamic Programming Methods
courses.prereq_text: Second year Ph.D. in Economics graduate student standing.�
courses.description: Students develop analytical and numerical dynamic programming methods to solve dynamic natural resource management problems. Applications include fisheries, water, forestry, spatial resource use, and stochastic extraction problems.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Natural Resource Economics: Continuous-Time Methods
courses.prereq_text: Second year Ph.D. in Economics graduate student standing.�
courses.description: Covers methods of continuous-time dynamic optimization and its application to natural resource management. Classic models of renewable and nonrenewable resources are examined, together with related empirical applications.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Environmental Externalities and Regulation
courses.prereq_text: Second year Ph.D. in Economics graduate student standing.�
courses.description: Covers the theory and empirical analysis of environmental regulation. Theoretical models will focus on the optimal regulation of environmental public goods in first and various second-best settings. Empirical applications will include the estimation of environmental policy costs in partial and general equilibrium, as well as the unintended consequences of such policies.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Time, Uncertainty, and Environmental Policy
courses.prereq_text: Second year Ph.D. in Economics graduate student standing.�
courses.description: Economic analysis of environmental problems often requires us to evaluate policies with very long run, highly uncertainty consequences. This course covers developments in the theory of intertemporal choice and choice under uncertainty and their applications in environmental economics. Topics include social discounting, intergenerational ethics, precautionary policies, learning, ambiguity, and catastrophic risks.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Environmental and Development Economics
courses.prereq_text: Second year PhD in Economics graduate student standing, or Second year in Bren PhD EES student standing.
courses.description: The intersection of environmental and development economics raises new theoretical and empirical questions. This course examines the causes and consequences of poor environmental quality in low and middle income countries, including poverty, weak state capacity, political economy and incomplete markets. Students gain exposure to recent literature, new and unanswered research questions, and applications of empirical research methods.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Experimental Methods
courses.prereq_text: Second year Ph.D. in Economics graduate student standing.�
courses.description: Introduction to the methodology of Experimental Economics. Topics include: motivations for experiments in economics, types of experimental designs, inducing preferences and beliefs, designing experiments with inference in mind, calibration of parameters, implementing an experiment, implementing moves by nature, elicitation techniques, framing, dealing with risk aversion in the laboratory, cognition tests, design of payments.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Games in the Laboratory
courses.prereq_text: Second year Ph.D. in Economics graduate student standing.�
courses.description: Focuses on experimental tests of behavior in games. Topics include: dictator, ultimatum and trust games, bargaining games, coordination problems, communication in games, cooperation in games, signaling games, public goods games, behavioral mechanism design, behavior in auctions, and behavior in games of oligopolistic competition.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Individual Decision Making in the Laboratory
courses.prereq_text: Second year Ph.D. in Economics graduate student standing.
courses.description: Focuses on experimental tests of individual decision-making problems. Topics include: tests of bounded rationality, perception and memory biases, tests of Bayesian updating, confirmation bias, expectations formation, testing the axioms of expected utility, the Allais paradoxes, subjective expected utility and the Ellsberg paradox, choice over time, endowment effects and framing effects.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Attention and Perception
courses.prereq_text: Second-year Ph.D. in Economics graduate student standing.
courses.description: Individuals face limitations in their ability to process all relevant information and they are very sensitive to the way this information is framed. A growing literature on attention and perception in economics, psychology, and neuroscience has documented these bounds and biases and has begun to incorporate them into alternative models of decision-making and strategic interaction. This course reviews the evidence (from the lab and field) on individual departures from the standard economic paradigm, analyzes these phenomena with rigorous formal models, and discusses how these biases impact markets and allocations.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Special Research Topics in Economics
courses.prereq_text: Second year Ph.D. in Economics graduate student standing.
courses.description: Faculty led seminar focusing on graduate student research in various fields of specialization within Economics. Students will typically produce a research draft each quarter. Second year students will be required to produce a formal written proposal for a research paper, which will be evaluated and enforced within the working group structure. Proposal must clearly articulate a research question of interest and the methodological approach. Written proposals must receive a passing grade (B or above) no later than the end of winter quarter of the second year.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Research Topics in Demography
courses.prereq_text: 2nd year Ph.D. standing in Anthropology, Economics, Geography or Sociology.
courses.description: Demography seminar research/reading group that focuses on reading and discussing key research in demography across the participating disciplines (Anthropology, Economics, Geography and/or Sociology). All students in the Interdisciplinary PhD Emphasis in Demography must register in this group at least once, usually in the spring quarter of their first year in the Emphasis program.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Microeconomics Seminar
courses.description: Current topics in microeconomics.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Macroeconomics Seminar
courses.prereq_text: Second year Ph.D. in Economics graduate student standing.
courses.description: Invited speakers on the topics of Macroeconomics

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Seminar on the Teaching of Economics
courses.description: Graduate Teaching Assistants are vitally important to the educational experience of UCSB undergraduates and graduates. As a Teaching Assistant, your role is potentially multifold: designing and teaching your own sections, assisting a professor by leading quiz sections, grading, or working directly with students in a capacity that is less formal and beneficial to students. This discussion based course covers the tools needed: planning, FERPA, testing, learning styles, evaluations, academic dishonesty, sexual harassment, presenting and evaluating of instruction.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Special Topics in Economics
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.
courses.description: Special seminar on research subjects of current interest.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Directed Reading and Research
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.
courses.description: Individual tutorial.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Individual study for the Ph.D. Comprehensive Examinations.
courses.prereq_text: Ph.D. in Economics graduate student standing and consent of Director of Graduate Studies.
courses.comments: No credit allowed toward advanced degree.
courses.description: Individual study for the three Ph.D. level Preliminary Examinations in either Microeconomics, Macroeconomics and/or Econometrics. Instructor should be the Economics department Director of Graduate Studies.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Dissertation Research and Preparation
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.
courses.description: Only for research underlying the dissertation, writing the dissertation. Instructor should be the chair of the student's doctoral committee.

courses.subject: ECON W
courses.title: Introduction to Economics
courses.comments: ECON W 9 is the online version of ECON 9. Course cannot be used to satisfy any economics major requirements.
courses.description: A broad survey of economic principles, including both microeconomics and macroeconomics.

courses.subject: ECON W
courses.title: Intermediate Microeconomic Theory *ONLINE COURSE W/ IN PERSON EXAMS*
courses.comments: Course must be taken at UCSB. ECON W 10A is the online version of ECON 10A.
courses.description: Economic theory relating to demand, production, and competitive product markets with emphasis on applications of theory. Please note that this course is conducted online, but exams will be held in person.

courses.subject: ECON W
courses.title: Financial Accounting Analysis
courses.comments: ECON W 118 is the online version of ECON 118
courses.description: An economic analysis of financial statements in a macroeconomic environment. Topics include evaluation of short term and long term liquidity, profitability, capital structure and the forecast of earnings and financial position using financial and economic models.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Introduction to the University Experience
courses.comments: Not open to students who have completed INT 20.
courses.description: Introduces first-year students to the mission of the research university, the role of higher education in society and their role, as students, within the community of scholars. Topics cover academic, social and personal issues relevant to the college experience. Undergraduate research opportunities will be promoted.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Introduction to the Research University for International Students
courses.comments: Not open to students who have completed INT 20.
courses.description: Course introduces first-year international students to US higher education systems with a specific focus on achieving academic success at UCSB through the process of academic writing enhancement, critical thinking and exploring university resources for personal development and academic success.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Learning Across the Lifespan
courses.description: Introduces theories of learning from different perspectives – behavioral, cognitive, sociocultural, sociopolitical, neuroscience, and artificial intelligence - and explores the implications of these perspectives to understand how people learn over their lifespan in various contexts of engagement and participation.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Education and Human Diversity
courses.description: Explores the neuro-biological, linguistic, developmental, and structural aspects of human diversity. Students examine how societies organize and respond to such diversity, with a focus on the role of education in shaping the social and cultural functions of diversity.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Educational Research in an Informed Society
courses.description: Discusses the intersection between society and educational research, including school reform, ethnicity and race, higher education, teaching and teachers, and the curriculum. Offers an overview of educational research and introduces inquiry methods in education and social/behavioral sciences.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Independent Studies
courses.description: Study of special problems in various fields of education and/or faculty supervised research assistance.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Health Education
courses.prereq_text: Admission to the Teacher Education Program; upper-division standing.
courses.description: Introduces physiological, psychological, and sociological factors that promote health and prevent disease including alcohol, narcotic, drug, and tobacco abuse: nutrition, chronic and infectious diseases; reproductive health and stress management. General educational applications lectures.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Introduction to Child and Adolescent Development
courses.description: An introductory course on the development of children from infancy to adolescence. Examines developmental changes and basic developmental theories (e.g., Piaget, Vygotsky) in four general areas: cognitive, social, language, and physical development. Fulfills TEP developmental course prerequisite or Education minor.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Race, Inequality, and Education
courses.description: This undergraduate level course highlights how race and racism shape education in the U.S. To do so, students learn about critical theories of race that can be used to study and understand educational inequality.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: The Research University and The Transfer Student Experience
courses.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; must be a new transfer student.
courses.description: Introduces new transfer students to the mission of the research university, the role of higher education in society and their role, as students, within the community of scholars. Topics cover academic, social and personal issues relevant to college students, specifically transfer students.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Practicum in Teaching in Higher Education
courses.description: A course designed for undergraduate students who were selected to serve as co-leaders in one of our large courses (ED 20, ED 118, ED 173.) Students will learn about adult development theories, pedagogical techniques, and learning assessment. Students will create lesson plans, facilitate discussions, grade assignments, and foster positive learning environments.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Introduction to K-12 Teaching
courses.comments: No prior experience or instructor approval required. After registration, students will be contacted by the instructor for K-12 classroom placement instructions.
courses.description: Provides students the opportunity to explore the teaching profession. Students gain firsthand experience in a local K-12 classroom, examine the California Standards for the Teaching Profession, and practice lesson planning and other fundamental aspects of the teaching profession.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Pre-professional Work in the K-12 Classroom
courses.comments: No prior experience or instructor approval required. After registration, students will be contacted by the instructor for K-12 classroom placement instructions. Classroom time counts towards the pre-professional requirement for UCSB's and other teacher education programs. Course may be repeated for a maximum of four credits.
courses.description: Students are placed in a local K-12 classroom to participate in and observe firsthand the fundamental aspects of teaching and learning. Through independent coursework, students reflect upon their classroom experiences within the framework of the California Standards for the Teaching Profession.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Culture, Development, and Education
courses.comments: Priority enrollment will be given to seniors.
courses.description: An examination of culturally constructed beliefs, attitudes, and values. Course examines how culture shapes human development, behavior, and interpersonal relations in culturally pluralistic environments, with an emphasis on educational settings.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Practicum in Community Based Learning
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units.
courses.description: Students do practicum hours in the local community and schools, read relevant articles and examine results from related research projects.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Schooling in the U.S.
courses.comments: Priority enrollment will be given to seniors.
courses.description: A study of the relationship between school and society. Social and political influences on education historically and currently are examined as well as schools as complex organizations and their unique roles in society.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Social Connectedness, Motivation, and Self-Regulation in Education
courses.description: This course explores three fundamental student needs: to be connected to others socially, to be motivated, and to be self-regulated. The course investigates how educators might address these needs, and explores how interventions might improve these student outcomes.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Teaching for Climate Justice and Sustainability
courses.description: Examines the teaching of climate justice and sustainability in K-12 classrooms. It is interactive and project-based. Students will increase their understanding and use of interdisciplinary resources for taking climate action. Students from all majors are invited to enroll.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: CalTeach, Elementary Mathematics Education
courses.description: Introduction to learning and teaching mathematics in grades K-8. The course requires attending a weekly on-campus seminar and participating in 15 hours of field placement in a local school.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: CalTeach, Elementary Science Education
courses.description: Introduction to learning and teaching science in grades K-8. The course requires attending a weekly on-campus seminar and participating in 15 hours of field placement in a local school.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: CalTeach, Secondary Mathematics Education
courses.description: Introduction to learning and teaching mathematics in grades 7-12. The course requires attending a weekly on-campus seminar and participating in 15 hours of field placement in a local school.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: CalTeach, Secondary Science Education
courses.description: Introduction to learning and teaching science in grade 7-12. The course requires attending a weekly on-campus seminar and participating in 15 hours of field placement in a local school.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Advanced Problem Solving in Mathematical, Historical and Pedagogical Contexts
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 8 with a minimum grade of C.
courses.description: Focuses on the strategies, representations, and language learners use to conceptualize and develop fundamental ideas of mathematics. Includes advanced mathematical problem solving and its implications for teaching and learning at the secondary level. Especially suitable for prospective middle school and high school teachers.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Advanced Problem Solving in Mathematical, Historical and Pedagogical Contexts
courses.prereq_text: Math 181A or ED 134 with a minimum grade of C.
courses.description: Continuation of Math 181A or ED 134. Focuses on the representations, strategies, and language learners use to conceptualize and develop fundamental ideas of mathematics. Includes advanced mathematical problem solving and its implications for teaching and learning at the secondary level. Especially suitable for prospective middle and high school teachers.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Green Works- Exploring Technology and the Search for Sustainability
courses.comments: Same course as Environmental Studies 136.
courses.description: A multi-disciplinary class examining the interplay of technology, society, science, and history. Investigate green technologies in an interactive class format designed to encourage discussion and debate. Innovative science and social science labs provide hands-on learning.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Community Based Coastal Literacies: Exploring Culturally Responsive Texts and Tools for a Maritime Learning Community
courses.description: The undergraduate course focuses on local K-12 learning and building a critical, culturally responsive framework for developing textual materials and assessments related to the following topics: oceanic/aquatic life and sustainability, environmental studies, marine biology, and local environmental issues and sustainability.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Introduction to Research Methods
courses.description: Provides an overview of methods used to conduct educational research. Skills learned help students conduct their own research projects. No previous coursework or research experience is required.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Evaluating Programs and Policies
courses.description: Provides students with an understanding of how large-scale policies or small-scale programs can be evaluated. Students learn various evaluation approaches to help determine the effectiveness, efficiency, and impact of public policies and social programs in education.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Supporting Multilingual Language and Literacy Development and Home Language Maintenance in Early Childhood Settings
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; consent of instructor. Students are required to have skills in a language other than English matched to home languages of children at the participating preschools. Prior or concurrent course in child development such as ED 111 or ED 123 is recommended.
courses.description: Provides UCSB students with guiding principles for designing teaching activities to help young children build multilingual language and literacy skills in their home languages and English. Students conduct bilingual activities with bi/multilingual children at a local preschool.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Teaching and Teachers
courses.description: Provides a basic foundation for understanding both (a) the nature of teaching as a specialized human activity (as distinct from other human activities) and (b) the organization and conduct of teaching in contemporary U.S. schools.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Introduction to Leadership Development
courses.description: This course is an overview of theoretical constructs and practical applications of leadership. Through lectures, readings, discussions, and projects, the course will assist students in developing individual approaches to effective leadership.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Practicum in Individual Differences
courses.comments: Class attendance is mandatory. Students must have access to an email account and web browser.
courses.description: Students study and discuss important educational policy issues while tutoring with elementary school students with learning problems in mathematics, reading, and language development.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Health and Well-Being
courses.description: Explores how personal, family, school, community and environmental factors are related to academic, physical, emotional and social well-being. Topics include physiological and sociological effects of mental health, nutrition; sexual health; relationships; alcohol, tobacco, drug abuse. Covers children through emerging adults.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Special Topics in Education
courses.description: Topics vary by instructor.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Independent Studies
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division courses in Education; and/or consent of department.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters and are limited to five units per quarter and 30 units total in all 99/199/199RA courses combined.
courses.description: Study of special problems in various fields of education.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Independent Research Assistance
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division courses in Education; and/or consent of department.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters and are limited to five units per quarter and 30 units total in all 99/199/199RA courses combined.
courses.description: Coursework shall consist of faculty supervised research assistance.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Education Proseminar
courses.description: Introduction to both graduate student life and research in Education. Includes information about campus resources, trainings in campus requirements, and an introduction to the basic principles of qualitative and quantitative research in Education.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Education Proseminar II
courses.description: This course helps to build community among Education graduate students. It explores research and community outreach projects led by Education faculty and colleagues. It also provides opportunities to strengthen research skills and present emergent research ideas.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Issues in Research Methodology
courses.description: In-depth consideration of emerging topics in research methodology in education.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Bilingual Language Development
courses.description: This course describes theoretical and empirical accounts of the knowledge representations and psychological processes underlying language comprehension and production. Representative topics include discourse processing; conversational interaction; memory for words, sentences, and text; metalinguistic skills, language development.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Language Socialization and Education
courses.description: Examines how children and youth, in contexts of migration and postcolonialism, become socialized through discourse to become competent members of communities, and how children (and institutions) navigate discontinuities in cultural and linguistic practices across home and school settings.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Literacy Assessment
courses.description: Issues of writing assessment from micro (student papers) to macro (large-scale assessment: NAEP, UC Subject A Examinations), and writing program assessment. Exploration of different research paradigms in writing assessment: empirical and hermeneutic are also discussed.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Foundations of Education in the U.S.
courses.description: Students will develop a rigorous way of thinking about, talking about, and practicing education for a diverse society. Explores the complex relationship among culture, society, and the organization of school. Considers the complex relations among teachers and learners within the context of U.S. schools.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Anthropological/Sociological Perspectives on Education
courses.description: Examination of anthropological and sociological approaches that have education as a central theoretical issue. Use of a comparative perspective to explore a series of issues of relevance to U.S. education and to education in a variety of other countries.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Research Seminar in Human Development
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit.
courses.description: Seminar for students engaged in the conceptualization, conduct, or analysis of research on child and adolescent development.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Ethnic Identity
courses.description: Seminar examines the development of ethnic and racial identity among children and adolescents. Topics include self-concept, family socialization, language, peers, and inter-and-intra group relations. Specific attention given to theories pertinent to this area of development.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Introduction to Learning, Teaching, and Teacher Education
courses.description: Provides an overview of critical issues in teaching, learning, and teacher education, including: the role of schools in U.S. society; analysis of learners in school; seminal learning theories and their applications to content learning and teaching theory; and teacher learning.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Introduction to Children's Thinking
courses.description: Presents a broad perspective of cognitive development and focuses on topics such as perception; problem solving; meta cognition; etc. The educational application of cognitive research is also covered.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Seminar in Cultural Perspectives of Education
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit.
courses.description: In-depth consideration of emerging topics in cultural perspectives of education.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Foundations of Sociocultural Learning Theory
courses.description: Examination of founding theoretical texts of sociocultural theory of learning in both Russia and the West and their application to current issues in education.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Theories of Human Development
courses.description: Course presents a comprehensive overview of the major theoretical perspectives that guide research and thinking on human growth and change across cultures and contexts. Students will discuss and analyze selected theories guiding the scientific study of cognitive development, social development, and lifespan development.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Quantitative Methods in the Social Sciences Colloquium
courses.comments: Same course as Sociology 212Q, PSTAT 250, and Geography 201Q. May be repeated.
courses.description: Required course for students in the Interdisciplinary Quantitative Methods in the Social Science emphasis.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Introductory Statistics
courses.description: Introduction to the application of descriptive and and basic inferential statistics in educational research. Topics include experimental and survey design principles, measures of central tendency and variability, elementary probability concepts, basic hypothesis testing, and procedures for testing the difference between two means.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Inferential Statistics
courses.description: Hypothesis testing and interval estimation techniques for application of educational research. Includes bivariate correlation and regression, one-way analysis of variance, and elementary techniques for categorical data analysis.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Linear Models for Data Analysis
courses.description: Intermediate data analysis methods, all of which can be considered to be instances of a general linear model. Selected topics in multiple regression and analysis of variance (ANOVA), including regression with qualitative independent variables, logistic regression models, one- and two-way ANOVA models and analysis of covariance.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Psychometrics
courses.description: Introduction to classical test theory and item response theory which provide tools for understanding and analyzing data from educational and psychological tests. Topics include test scoring, validity, reliability, test bias and the development of tests and questionnaires.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Advanced Multivariate Statistics
courses.description: The theory and application of multivariate statistics, including multivariate analysis of variance, discriminant analysis, and canonical correlation. Instruction in the necessary matrix algebra will be provided.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Factor Analysis
courses.description: The theory and application of exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis models.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Structural Equation Models
courses.description: The theory and application of structural equation modeling (also called analysis of covariance structures).

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Introduction to Applied Mixture Modeling
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to the theory and practice of mixture modeling.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Constructing Measures
courses.description: Covers foundational issues in the design and evaluation of measurement instruments in education and psychology. Students design and pilot-test an instrument (e.g. an academic test, attitudinal survey, observation protocol, etc.) and evaluate its reliability and validity.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Introduction to Program Evaluation
courses.description: This course is an overview of the field of program evaluation and its various aspects (planning, collecting, analyzing information, and reporting), as well as various evaluation strategies (i.e., qualitative, quantitative, formative, and summative), including those employing experimental and quasi-experimental designs.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Introduction to Qualitative Research Methods
courses.description: Provides an introduction to qualitative research methods, including techniques for data collection and analysis within various disciplinary perspectives, experience participating in field research methods, and qualitative data analysis programs.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Qualitative Interviewing
courses.description: Provides an introduction to qualitative interviewing traditions, including ethnographic interviews, life history interviews, cognitive interviews, and focus group interviews. Includes examination of the nuts and bolts of conducting and analyzing interviews as well.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Video Analysis
courses.description: Examines ways of analyzing classroom ethnography data, sociolinguistic and ethnographic approaches to data analysis, and issues in data analysis. Involves participants in the process of video data analysis.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Discourse Analysis in Educational Settings
courses.description: Examines the nature of discourse, linguistic constructs, and how they apply to student discourse in educational settings. Includes issues in transcribing and analyzing classroom talk.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Community Ethnography
courses.description: Explores how to carry out ethnographic research in order to investigate the relationships among schools, families, and communities.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Case Study Methods: Research and Practice
courses.description: Focuses on case study methodology. Students learn the different types of case studies and the value of using a multiple case design. Also provides students with tools for preparing their dissertation proposal.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Design-Based Research and Research-Based Design
courses.description: Examines the concurrent design of learning contexts and research on learning. Combines many different research methods. The readings and topics are subject to change based on students' interest.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Qualitative Analysis
courses.prereq_text: ED 221A (Intro to Qualitative Research) or permission of instructor
courses.description: This course aims to build students’ understanding of the relationship among qualitative research design, theoretical frameworks, data collection, and analysis and introduce a range of qualitative data analytic strategies that students will use to analyze their own data.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Academic and Cognitive Characteristics of Learners with Mild to Moderate Support Needs
courses.description: Study of the academic and cognitive characteristics of children who are at risk or have mild disabilities. Interventions for these students will also be covered.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Law, Ethics, and History of Special Education
courses.description: Intensive look at the laws governing special education and civil rights for people with disabilities in the U.S. The ethics of special education and key historical developments are also covered. Topics include current controversies and historical trends.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Inclusive Education
courses.description: Explores critical issues in inclusive education, the participation of students with disabilities in general education settings. The class explores the history of inclusion within social justice movements, Multi-Tiered Systems of Support (MTSS) and Universal Design for Learning.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Evaluation Procedures
courses.description: Evaluation practice integrated of three facets: 1) program context, 2) evaluator skills, and 3) evaluation methods. This class is designed to illustrate how these three facets connect when designing an evaluation that is theoretically grounded, feasible, and useful.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Mixed Methods
courses.description: This course provides an overview of mixed methods research and consists of defining mixed methods research, describing its history and foundations. We examine the types of mixed methods designs available along with how and when to utilize them.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Learners with Extensive Support Needs: Skills Instruction
courses.description: Learning and motivational characteristics, assessments for screening, diagnosis, instructional planning, and functional analysis of behavioral problems. Procedures for teaching functional skills and recent research arecovered.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Learners with Extensive Support Needs: Communication
courses.description: Teaching and research on instruction of communication and language competence and social competance. Research theory, and instructional practice are covered. The course is designed for masters and doctoral students.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Learners with Extensive Support Needs: Inclusion
courses.description: Functional academics and social academics as well as managerial aspects of inclusion. Along with practical skills, students learn key theories and review recent research on social and academic inclusion.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Direct Instruction and Strategy Instruction
courses.description: Theory, practice, effectiveness and controversy. Two of the major research-based approaches to teaching academic skills to students with learning disabilities are covered.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Families and Disabilities
courses.description: An overview of theories about the family, contemporary research regarding family issues, and home-school interactions. Designed for doctoral students who are interested in research and masters students who want to learn practical school-related methods.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Working with Families and Educational Partners in Special Education
courses.description: Provides special educators with information and skills for working with the many stakeholders in special education. Content includes how to communicate with parents, administrators, paraprofessionals, and teachers.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Individualized Education Programs, Assessment, and Transitions in Special Education
courses.description: This course provides special educators applied and background knowledge in Individualized Education Programs for students with disabilities in schools, as well as information on related issues of assessment and transitions.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Including Students with Disabilities in Meaningful Mathematics
courses.description: Designed for teacher candidates in special education. Topics include: socioemotional and identity development in mathematics; developmental sequence, how children learn mathematics; standards for mathematical practice; instructional routines; intervention in mathematics.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Assessment for Special Educators
courses.description: Course topics include: procedures to assess academic achievement, psycho-perceptual processes, and environmental factors; assessing core academic skills; how to communicate a variety of tests used to measure academic achievement; making data-based decisions to evaluate or develop academic programs or interventions.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Research in Teaching, Learning, and Assessment in Special Education I
courses.description: Students explore research in teaching, learning and assessment in educational research with a focus on students with Extensive Support Needs, such as intellectual disabilities, traumatic-brain injury, Cerebral Palsy, Autism, Downs Syndrome, and other developmental disabilities.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Research in Teaching, Learning, and Assessment in Special Education II
courses.description: Students will explore research in teaching, learning and assessment in educational research with a focus on students with disabilities such as learning disabilities/dyslexia, Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder, speech and language, and emotional disabilities.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Practicum in Special Education
courses.description: Supervised field-based practicum in instruction and management of special education programs for severely handicapped pupils.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Applied Systematic Instruction and Assessment
courses.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in Education 229C or Education E392; consent of instructor.
courses.description: Students read research and best practice studies, discuss current work in practicum placements, and develop documentation of performance and knowledge competencies.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Education Policy
courses.description: An introduction to education policy that will examine both the process of education policy and a series of substantive issues that are commonly the focus of education policy at the state and federal levels.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Organizational Theories
courses.description: Survey of prominent theories about how organization function, how and why some organizations flourish while others might flounder, how organizations encourage as well as discourage innovation and creativity, and how different theories project different realities about organizations.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Higher Education Systems
courses.description: Examines U.S. higher education’s structure, governance, and funding. Students critically analyze how external pressures and stakeholders influence institutional decision-making, identifying the multiple systems that function within the field.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Educational Leadership
courses.description: Systematic analysis of the antecedents and consequences of administrator behavior in a variety of educational settings.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Doctoral Seminar in Policy and Leadership
courses.description: A seminar for post-comprehensive exam students with the intent of helping to define areas, problems, specific questions, and methodologies for doctoral research. Topics and instructors may vary from quarter to quarter.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Seminar in Teaching and Learning
courses.comments: May be repeated.
courses.description: In-depth consideration of emerging topics in teaching and learning. Course content may vary.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Technology and Learning Contexts
courses.description: Critical consideration of research on how technologychanges the learning context. Specifically, issues about how technology may be used to facilitate student learning andchallenges to integrating technology.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Seminar in Curriculum: Development and Analysis
courses.description: This seminar examines past and current research on curriculum in K-12 education. It discusses curriculum theory, development, analysis, and implementation - in light of the history of education and current reform movements.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Foundations of Democracy and Justice in Education
courses.prereq_text: Graduate Standing and enrollment in the Multiple or Single Subject Credential Program.
courses.description: Explores the effect of language, culture, background, and values on learning processes and the implications for the development of appropriate instructional strategies.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Adolescent Development and Learning
courses.prereq_text: Admission to Single Subject Teaching Credential Program; and consent of instructor.
courses.description: An introduction to psychological principles of learning and development of the adolescent. Explores dimensions of development indicative of adolescence, and the ways in which development and learning are interwoven with social and cultural contexts in the educative process.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Child Development and Learning
courses.prereq_text: Graduate Standing and enrollment in the Multiple or Single Subject Credential Program.
courses.description: An introduction to psychological principles of learning and development of the elementary age child. Explores dimensions of development indicative of middle childhood, and ways in which development and learning are interwoven with social and cultural contexts in the educative process.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Behavioral Assessment and Intervention in Educational Settings
courses.description: History and philosophy of behavior management approaches, behavioral assessment procedures, treatment delivery paradigms, parent-training, nonaversive/aversive issues, generalization and maintenance of treatment gains, causes, evaluation of behavior changes, medicine, self-management.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Foundation of Teacher Inquiry
courses.prereq_text: Graduate Standing and enrollment in the Multiple or Single Subject Credential Program.
courses.description: An introduction to teacher inquiry for professional growth. Topics include: the relationship between teacher inquiry and classroom practice, systematic data analysis, visual representation of findings and writing for research purposes.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Teacher Inquiry and Classroom Practice I
courses.prereq_text: Graduate Standing and enrollment in the Multiple or Single Subject Credential Program.
courses.description: Teacher candidates work on an independent inquiry into classroom practice. Students will refine a research topic, plan and perform multiple layers of data collection and analysis, work in critical research groups, and prepare a final written report.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Teacher Inquiry and Classroom Practice II
courses.prereq_text: Graduate Standing and enrollment in the Multiple or Single Subject Credential Program.
courses.description: Teacher candidates work on an independent inquiry into classroom practice. Students will refine a research topic, plan and perform multiple layers of data collection and analysis, work in critical research groups, and prepare a final written report.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Special Topics in the Teaching Profession
courses.prereq_text: Admission to Single Subject Teaching Credential Program; and consent of instructor.
courses.description: This course allows for more in-depth and advanced investigations into educative processes that build on prior learning in the Teacher Education program's foundations courses, methods courses, and student teaching.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Foundations of Teaching
courses.prereq_text: Graduate Standing and enrollment in the Multiple or Single Subject Credential Program.
courses.description: Students develop a rigorous way of thinking about, talking about and practicing education for a diverse society. Explores the complex relationship among culture, society and school organization. Considers complex relations among teachers and learners within U.S. schools.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Second Langage Learning in Educational Contexts
courses.description: Overview of linguistic, psychological, cognitive, and sociocultural approaches to second language acquisition. Students will critically review past and current SLA theories and research and develop an understanding of how language proficiency is conceptualized and assessed.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Language, Culture & Learning
courses.description: Explores the effect of language, culture, background, and values on learning processes and the implications for development of appropriate instructional strategies.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Critical Race Theory in Education: An Introduction
courses.description: This course serves as an overview of the Critical Race Theory in education framework. The course will provide an intellectual genealogy of Critical Race Theory and its development, continuing evolution, and application in education in K-16 settings.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Proseminar in Language, Interaction and Social Organization
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit. Same course as Sociology 274and Linguistics 274.
courses.description: Discussion of current research, literature, and theoretical and methodological issues in language and social interaction.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Immigrant Education and Literacy Development
courses.description: This course covers recent theories, empirical research, and strategic interventions in the area of immigrant education with special attention to sociocultural, critical pedagogy, and new literacies approaches to learning and development of immigrant adults and youths.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Latino Children and Their Families
courses.description: This course will provide an overview of the normative development and challenges experienced by Latino children and adolescents in the United States underscoring the importance of contexts- families, schools, communities.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Foundations of Teacher Education
courses.description: Course for Ph.D. candidates in Education with a focus on pre-service and in-service teacher development. Students read professional literature, research and hear from those doing the work of teacher educators.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Learning Theories and Instructional Practices in STEM
courses.description: Exploration of contemporary theories of learning and instruction in science education. Students examine and critique research on constructivism, groupwork, inquiry, project-based science, multicultural science education and science-technology-society approaches.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Research in Informal STEM Education
courses.description: The goals of this class are to introduce students to issues and research in informal science education (specifically museums), provide opportunities to develop research skills, engage in a research-practice partnership, and produce publishable research.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Behavior Analysis
courses.description: Study of professional issues and development of projects in the areas of clinical work with children and families, experimental analyses of severe behavior problems, preparation of articles for publication, organization of national conventions and grant writing.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Equity in STEM
courses.description: Investigation of mathematics instructions and achievements from a cross-national perspective. Both formal and informal mathematics applications will be reviewed. Sources of information will include the International Education Assessment (IEA) studies of mathematics as well as sources from anthropology, sociology, and educational journals.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Context for Child Development and Learning
courses.prereq_text: Graduate Standing and enrollment in the Multiple or Single Subject Credential Program.
courses.description: Prepares teacher candidates to create a supportive and healthy learning environment for student learning. Helps candidates learn how personal, family, school, community, and other contexts are related to student's academic, physical, emotional, and social well-being.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Context for Adolescent Development and Learning
courses.prereq_text: Admission to Single Subject Teaching Credential Program; and consent of instructor.
courses.description: Prepares teacher candidates to create a supportive and healthy learning environment for student learning. Helps candidates learn how personal, family, school, community, and other contexts are related to student's academic, physical, emotional, and social well-being.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Instructional Design for Elementary Teachers
courses.prereq_text: Graduate Standing and enrollment in the Multiple Credential Program.
courses.description: Introduces teacher candidate to concepts of effective curriculum development including lesson design and assessment as part of the teach-assess-reflect cycles. Also prepares and supports candidates for the Performance Assessment of California Teachers (PACT).

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Instructional Design for Secondary Teachers
courses.prereq_text: Admission to Single Subject Teaching Credential Program; and consent of instructor.
courses.description: Introduces teacher candidates to concepts of effective curriculum development including lesson design and assessment as part of the teach-assess-reflect cycles. Also prepares and supports candidates for the Performance Assessment of California Teachers (PACT).

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Inclusive Technology
courses.prereq_text: Graduate Standing and enrollment in the Multiple or Single Subject Credential Program.
courses.description: Exploration of issues related to use of computer-based technologies in schools, including their access, use and control in a democratic society; their use for development of problem solving, critical thinking, and creativity; and their integration into the school curriculum.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Practicum in Classroom Management: Elementary
courses.prereq_text: Graduate Standing and enrollment in the Multiple or Single Subject Credential Program.
courses.description: Designed to raise awareness of often-transparent classroom management strategies to help teacher candidates facilitate learning among students with diverse backgrounds and learning needs. Learn research-based strategies that assist in building positive classroom atmospheres and more productive classroom observations.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Practicum in Classroom Management: Secondary
courses.prereq_text: Graduate Standing and enrollment in the Multiple or Single Subject Credential Program.
courses.description: To raise awareness of often-transparent classroom management strategies to help teacher candidates facilitate learning among students with diverse backgrounds and learning needs, learn research-based strategies to build positive classroom atmospheres, and prepare them for more productive classroom observations.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Writing Project Approaches to Teaching Composition, K-College
courses.prereq_text: Graduate Standing and enrollment in the Multiple or Single Subject Credential Program.
courses.description: Experimental approach to learning in a community of writers. Features theory and practice for integrating informal and formal writing activities into the learning process and reading/writing development in all disciplines and grade levels. Let be South Coast Writing Project Fellows.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Student Teaching: Elementary Schools
courses.prereq_text: Admission to the Multiple Subject Credential Program.
courses.description: Supervised fieldwork and student teaching in elementary schools (grades K-6)

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Student Teaching - Introduction to Secondary Instruction
courses.prereq_text: Admission to Single Subject Teaching Credential Program; and consent of instructor.
courses.description: Supervised fieldwork and student teaching in secondary classrooms (grades 7-12).

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Multicultural Reading Field Experiences
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing and enrollment in The Teacher Education Program.
courses.description: Supervised field experience of teaching content reading skills in multicultural settings for secondary teacher candidates.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: ELD/SDAIE Methods and Procedures
courses.prereq_text: Enrollment in Multiple Subject or Special Education Teaching Credential Program.
courses.description: Goal is to prepare educators who can articulately advocate for and enact effective educational practices to ensure English Language proficiency and academic progress for student who are designated as English Learners.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: ELD/SDAIE Methods and Procedures
courses.prereq_text: Enrollment in Multiple Subject Teaching Credential Program.
courses.description: Goal is to prepare educators who can articulately advocate for and enact effective educational practices to ensure English Language proficiency and academic progress for student who are designated as English Learners.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: ELD/SDAIE Methods and Procedures
courses.prereq_text: Admission to Single Subject Teaching Credential Program; and consent of instructor.
courses.description: Goal is to prepare educators who can articulately advocate for and enact effective educational practices to ensure English language proficiently and academic progress for student who are designated as English learners.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: ELD/SDAIE Methods and Procedures
courses.prereq_text: Admission to Single Subject Teaching Credential Program; and consent of instructor.
courses.description: Goal is to prepare educators who can articulately advocate for and enact effective educational practices to ensure English language proficiently and academic progress for student who are designated as English learners.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Exceptional Children, Inclusive Classrooms
courses.prereq_text: Graduate Standing and enrollment in the Multiple or Single Subject Credential Program.
courses.description: A survey course in special education for students preparing to teach at the elementary school level. Topics include educational policy, instructional modifications and the role of the teaching in supporting children with special needs.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Exceptional Adolescents, Inclusive Classrooms
courses.prereq_text: Graduate Standing and enrollment in the Multiple or Single Subject Credential Program.
courses.description: A survey course in special education for students preparing to teach at the high school level. Topics include educational policy, instructional modification, and the role of the teacher in supporting adolescents with special needs.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Assistive Technology for Students with Accessibility Needs
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing and enrollment in The Teacher Education Program OR The Department of Education; ED 222A.
courses.description: Offers teacher candidates exposure to adaptive and assistive technologies, as well as state-of-the-art software and hardware used by and for children with exceptional learning needs. Students learn hands-on skills of designing technology-based instructional materials for children with disabilities.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Professional Seminar in Teaching: Elementary
courses.prereq_text: Graduate Standing and enrollment in the Multiple Credential Program.
courses.description: This seminar focuses on practice-based issues linked to student teaching and includes such topics as classroom environmental, assessment centered teaching, lesson design, integration of the arts, and uses around school policy. Topics differ each quarter, building on student teachers developing expertise.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Teaching Strategies for Bilingual/Cross-Cultural Education
courses.prereq_text: Admission to Teaching Credential Program; and consent of instructor.
