courses.subject: EDS
courses.title: Essential Math for Environmental Data Science
courses.description: Quantitative skills and understanding are critical when working with, understanding, analyzing and gaining insights from environmental data. In the intensive EDS 212 course, students will refresh fundamental skills in basic math (algebra, uni- and multivariate functions, units and unit conversions), derivative and integral calculus, differential equations, linear algebra, and reading, writing and evaluating logical operations.

courses.subject: EDS
courses.title: Databases and Data Management
courses.description: Teaches students how to store and manage environmental information. The course focuses on relational database structure, schemas and data relationships, and introduces SQL as a means to create and query databases. Also covers the concept of metadata as well as archiving data products on data repositories to make them available to the broader community.

courses.subject: EDS
courses.title: Analytical Workflows and Scientific Reproducibility
courses.description: The generation and analysis of environmental data is often a complex, multi-step process that may involve the collaboration of many people. Increasingly, data scientists use tools that document and help to organize workflows to ensure reproducibility, shareability, and transparency of the results. The goal of this course is to enable MEDS students to collaboratively create reproducible analyses. Essential skills and concepts are: 1) Automate the steps in an analytical workflow using scripts, 2) Organize workflow components modularly, 3) Document individual components and their relationships, 4) Scale workflows for computational performance and large datasets, 5) Collaborate in a team to develop a workflow.

courses.subject: EDS
courses.title: Python for Environmental Data Science
courses.description: This course teaches the fundamentals of programming in Python. Students learn foundational skills and concepts including data structures, programming basics, and how to clean, subset, aggregate, transform and visualize data. Course materials demonstrate the application of these techniques for environmental data analysis and problem solving.

courses.subject: EDS
courses.title: Working with Environmental Data
courses.description: Introduces students to the broad range of data sets used to monitor and understand human and natural systems. Covers field and station data, remote sensing products, and large-scale climate datasets including climate model projections. Skills include evaluating data collection and quality control methods used in existing datasets, and working with existing databases of time-series and spatial information including cloud computing databases and new repositories of environmental datasets. Students learn basic workflows for selecting, obtaining, and visualizing datasets, and best practices for reliable data intercomparisons.

courses.subject: EDS
courses.title: Scientific Programming Essentials
courses.description: This course teaches scientific programming skills and demonstrates the application of these techniques to environmental data analysis and problem solving. Topics include fundamental programming concepts, transforming and visualizing data, and exposure to modern data science tools. The course will be taught in R.

courses.subject: EDS
courses.title: Statistics for Environmental Data Science
courses.description: Teaches a variety of statistical techniques commonly used to analyze environmental data sets and quantitatively address environmental questions with empirical data. Covers fundamental statistical concepts and tools, including sampling and study design, linear regression, inference, and time series analysis, as well as foundational concepts of spatial and space-time dependency and associated impacts on inference.

courses.subject: EDS
courses.title: Geospatial Analysis and Remote Sensing
courses.description: Introduces the spatial modeling and analytic techniques of geographic information science to data science students. The emphasis is on deep understanding of spatial data models and the analytic operations they enable. Recognizing remotely sensed data as a key data type within environmental data science, this course also introduces fundamental concepts and applications of remote sensing. In addition to this theoretical background, students become familiar with libraries, packages, and APIs that support spatial analysis in R.

courses.subject: EDS
courses.title: Modeling Environmental Systems
courses.description: Computer-based modeling and simulation for practical environmental problem solving and environmental research. The course covers both the selection and application of existing models and best practices for designing new models. Topics include conceptual models, static and dynamic models, spatial models, and models of diffusion, growth and disturbance. Techniques include sensitivity analysis, calibration and model scenario design.

courses.subject: EDS
courses.title: Text and Sentiment Analysis for Environmental Problems
courses.description: Covers foundations and applications of natural language processing. Problem sets and class projects leverage common and emerging text-based data sources relevant to environmental problems, including but not limited to social media feeds (e.g., twitter) and text documents (e.g., agency reports), and builds capacity and experience in common tools, including text processing and classification, semantics, and natural language parsing.

courses.subject: EDS
courses.title: Machine Learning in Environmental Science
courses.description: Machine learning (ML) can help process big or complex data and extract knowledge. It forms one of the foundations in data science. This course provides a broad introduction to classic machine learning and statistical pattern recognition. Topics include supervised learning (decision trees, random forest, support vector machines, neural networks) and unsupervised learning (clustering, dimensionality reduction). Problems and exercises are framed within environmental science applications. The course will be taught using Python.

courses.subject: EDS
courses.title: Data Visualization and Communication
courses.description: Effectively communicating your work in a responsible, accessible and visually-pleasing way is often (if not, always) a central part of data science. This course focuses on the basic principles for effective communication through data visualization and using technical tools and workflows for creating and sharing data visualizations with diverse audiences.

courses.subject: EDS
courses.title: Environmental Policy Evaluation
courses.description: This course presents state of the art program evaluation techniques necessary to evaluate the impact of environmental policies. The program evaluation methods presented aim at identifying and measuring the causal effect of policies, regulations, and interventions on environmental outcomes of interest. Students learn the research designs and methods for estimating causal effects with experimental and non-experimental data. This will prepare students for interpreting and conducting high-quality empirical research, with applications in cross-sectional data and panel data settings.

courses.subject: EDS
courses.title: Ethics & Bias in Environmental Data Science
courses.description: This course focuses on ethical considerations in collecting, using, and reporting environmental data, and how to recognize and account for biases in algorithms, training data, and methodologies. Students also examine the human and societal implications of these issues within environmental data science.

courses.subject: EDS
courses.title: Advanced Special Topics in Environmental Data Science
courses.description: Advanced, special topics in environmental data science. May be repeated for credit with changes in content.

courses.subject: EDS
courses.title: Capstone Project
courses.description: First quarter of a two-quarter group study/analysis of how to apply data science and tools to an environmental problem. In this quarter, students are expected to work with their project client to finalize project plans, develop a project plan and deliverables, and make significant headway on implementing those plans.

courses.subject: EDS
courses.title: Capstone Project
courses.description: Second quarter of a two-quarter group study/analysis of how to apply data science and tools to an environmental problem. In this quarter, students are expected to complete all project plans and deliverables, develop and submit a project repository and technical documentation, and present the research to a general audience.

courses.subject: EDS
courses.title: Workshop in Environmental Data Science
courses.description: Workshops to develop professional skills for careers in Environmental Data Science

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Introductory Biology II--Ecology and Evolution
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A with a grade of C- or better.
courses.comments: Concurrent enrollment in EEMB 7 not allowed. Reduced credit of 2.0 units will be given for those who have received credit for EEMB 7.
courses.description: Introduction to population and community ecology, and evolution.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Introductory Biology Laboratory II
courses.prereq_text: Grade of C- or better in EEMB 2 (maybe taken concurrently).
courses.description: Laboratory investigation s illustrate basis principles of ecology, evolution and biodiversity.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Selected Topics from EEMB 2
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 4BZ or EEMB 4BZ or 5BZ or MCDB 4BZ or 5BZ.
courses.description: Designed for transfer students who have completed part of EEMB 2 through transfer work. Topics will be selected by the department, as appropriate, to fulfill the introductory biology requirement at UCSB.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Introductory Biology III
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A-B and EEMB 2 with a grade of C- or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 4C or EEMB 4C or 5C.
courses.description: Introduction to the major groups of microbes, plants, and animals.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Selected Topics from EEMB 3
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 4CZ or EEMB 4CZ or 5CZ.
courses.description: Designed for transfer students who have completed part of EEMB 3 through transfer work. Topics will be selected by the department, as appropriate, to fulfill the introductory biology requirement at UCSB.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Principles of Evolution and Animal Physiology for Brain Sciences
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 6 or MCDB 1A all with a grade of C- or better
courses.comments: Not open to Prebio/EEMB/MCDB majors. Can't be used in lieu of EEMB 2 for prereqs. Unsuitable for health professions requiring 1 yr of intro bio. Can't take concurrently MCDB 1B/EEMB 2 or if completed.
courses.description: Introduction to the principles of evolution and animal physiology. Topics in evolution include the evidence for evolution, the process of microevolution, macroevolution, and basic phylogeny. Topics in animal physiology include tissues and organ systems, neural control, sensory perception, endocrine control, structural support and movement, circulation, immunity, respiration, digestion, reproduction, and development. This course is designed for psychological and brain sciences majors.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Applying Mathematics in the Life Sciences
courses.description: This course for first-year Pre-Bio majors supplements MATH 2A, MATH 3A, and MATH 34A. Weekly course discussions apply calculus concepts to biological models of topics such as metabolism, population growth, and disease dynamics. Students are taught how to code and evaluate mathematical models and introduced to research in mathematical ecology and evolution.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Biology Mentoring and Engagement I
courses.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in Chemistry 1A or Chemistry 2A.
courses.description: Seminar for first year pre-biology students. Focus is on developing scientific study skills and fostering the confidence and motivation involved in higher cognitive learning. Students will engage in peer mentoring activities, problem-solving exercises and relevant discussion promoting academic success.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Biology Mentoring and Engagement II
courses.comments: EEMB 12 and MCDB 12 are the same course.
courses.description: Seminar for first year pre-biology students. Emphasis on developing critical thinking skills by utilizing interactive panel discussions ascertaining why biologists care about subjects like chemistry and math. Deliberation on biology news articles designed to get students thinking like scientists.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Biology Mentoring and Engagement III
courses.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in Chemistry 1C or Chemistry 2C.
courses.comments: EEMB 13 and MCDB 13 are the same course.
courses.description: Seminar for first year pre-biology students. Active learning enhancement via topics exploring students' self-identifying themselves as scientists, conversation on careers within the sciences and health professions, and discussion regarding the research process in order spark motivation and questions.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Biology Mentoring and Engagement IV
courses.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in Chemistry 1C or Chemistry 2C.
courses.description: Seminar for first year pre-biology students. A laboratory course designed to be a research experience for undergraduate students where they learn to apply the scientific method, critical thinking and experimental design to test relevant hypotheses in molecular biology.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Ecology of Infectious Disease
courses.description: Uses topical examples of emerging and resurgent diseases to illustrate key principles in ecology and epidemiology. Examines how changing disease ecology influences disease prevalence and how such changing patterns of disease have influenced human history.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Biology of Non-Infectious Disease
courses.description: An overview of both the biology and the history of the major non-infectious diseases affecting humans. Diseases covered will include cancer, heart disease, and diabetes. An emphasis will be on changing patterns of disease.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Internship in Biological Sciences
courses.prereq_text: Lower-division standing; instructor and departmental approval required.
courses.comments: Students must have a 2.5 cumulative grade-point average. May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 15 units, but no units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: Opportunity to obtain practical biological-related research experience by working under faculty direction as an intern with local, state, federal, or private agencies. A written report will be submitted for evaluation.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: EEMB Colloquium
courses.description: Exposes students to current research in ecology, evolution, behavioral ecology, evolutionary ecology, physiological ecology, and marine biology, by eminent and nationally and internationally well-known biologists. Students attend the EEMB departmental seminar each week and participate in a discussion of the seminar research. Students complete a short weekly quiz regarding the content of each seminar presentation.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Getting into the Environment: Introduction to Ecological Science and Careers
courses.comments: Open to biology majors only. Not major applicable.
courses.description: Part of a NSF funded grant focused on improving STEM at Hispanic Serving Institutes (HSIs), called FUERTE, the course supports students as they transition into college, helps them choose their major and direction of study at UCSB, and forms a learning community. It also serves as an introduction to the FUERTE program, presents logistical information regarding program scheduling and requirements, and introduces students to ecological research, and research methods and tools.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Getting into the Environment: Introduction to Ecological Science and Careers II
courses.comments: Open to biology majors only. Not major applicable.
courses.description: Part of an NSF funded grant funded focused on improving STEM at Hispanic Serving Institutes (HSIs), called FUERTE, the course will continue to support students as they seek to pursue careers in environmental sciences. The course will focus on practical career skills development ranging from CV building, to graduate school applications, to finding internships, and will continue to increase exposure to research methods and tools in ecology.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Getting into the Environment: Introduction to Ecological Science and Careers III
courses.description: This course is for students involved in the third year of the FUERTE program to help develop research projects they have begun in the field aspects of program or elsewhere into written research products. A number of career skills are also taught.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Special Topics in Biology
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 4 units.
courses.description: Special topics in ecology, evolution and marine biology. Course content varies. Information may be obtained in department office.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Introduction to Curation of Natural History Collections
courses.comments: Same course as ENV S 96.
courses.description: Introduction to curation of natural history collections including vertebrate, plants, algae and lichen. Learn to collect, prepare, catalog, and preserve specimens via lectures, hands-on activities, and field trips. Collection focus changes quarterly. Internships available at conclusion of the course.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Readings in Biological Sciences
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 grade-point average and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined. Students are limited to 6 units of Biology 98 and EEMB 98combined. Maximum units 6 (3 per quarter). Biology 98 = EEMB + MCDB 98.
courses.description: Special readings on selected topics in biology. Individual conferences one one hour every week. Designed to broaden the out look and experience of advanced lower-division students. Hours and credit by arrangement with any member of the staff.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Introduction to Research
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 grade-point average and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined. Students are limited to 6 units of Biology 99 and EEMB 99combined. Maximum units 6 (3 per quarter). Biology 99 = EEMB + MCDB 99.
courses.description: Laboratory or field experience for advanced lower-division students. Hours and credit by arrangement with any member of the staff.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Genomics and Molecular Evolution
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, MCDB 1B, EEMB 2 and EEMB 3; Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.description: Molecular evolution is a modern field of biology aiming to understand processes of evolution using molecular and genomic tools. This course provides basic concepts in molecular evolution including models of sequence evolution, genome evolution across the tree of life, concepts in molecular population genetics, molecular tests of natural selection, and regulatory evolution. These concepts are learned through the usage of classic examples of molecular evolution, as well as recent, timely studies (such as evolution of SARS-CoV2).

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Macroevolution: Biodiversity in Deep Time
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, MCDB 1B, EEMB 2 and EEMB 3. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.description: An introduction to the scientific methods used to study the tempo and mode of evolution above the species level and important topics in macroevolution such as the Cambrian explosion, the origin of novelties, the evolution of development, and phylogenetics.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Macroevolution-Honors
courses.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in EEMB 102; consent of instructor
courses.description: Honors component of EEMB 102. An in depth study of Macroevolution.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Flora and Vegetation of California
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, MCDB 1B, EEMB 2 and EEMB 3. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.comments: Same course as ENV S 103A.
courses.description: An introduction to the plant diversity and plant communities of California. The floristic composition and ecology of California plant communities will be examined through lectures and field observations. Methods of plant identification will be applied in the laboratory. Two Saturday field trips are required.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Biology of Fishes
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, MCDB 1B, EEMB 2 and EEMB 3. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Zoology 161.
courses.description: The evolution, systematics, biogeography, and ecology of fishes.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Parasitology
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, MCDB 1B, EEMB 2 and EEMB 3. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Zoology 111.
courses.description: An ecological approach to parasitism. Survey of parasites of humans and other animals. Discussion of evolutionary, genetic, immunological, sociological, political, and economic aspects. Laboratory stresses anatomy and life cycles of living material.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Parasitology-Honors
courses.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in EEMB 111; consent of instructor
courses.description: Honors component of EEMB 111. An in depth study of a topic in parasitology. A written report and an annotated bibliography are required.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Invertebrate Zoology
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, MCDB 1B, EEMB 2 and EEMB 3. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Zoology 112A.
courses.description: An introduction to the classification, structure, life histories, and habits of the major phyla of invertebrate animals (excluding annelids and arthropods), with emphasis on marine fauna of Santa Barbara area.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Vertebrate Biology, Ecology and Evolution
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, and EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B, and EEMB 3; Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Zoology 113A.
courses.description: Evolutionary and ecological principles as demonstrated by amphibians, reptiles, birds, and mammals; competition and other species interactions; diversity and systematics with special emphasis on speciation theory.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Laboratory in Vertebrate Biology, Ecology, and Evolution
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Zoology 113AL.
courses.description: Weekly field trips to numerous locations and laboratory work emphasizing classification, identification, and observation of local terrestrial vertebrates. Introduction to techniques such as trapping and banding to study vertebrates in the field.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Invertebrate Zoology: Higher Invertebrates
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, MCDB 1B, EEMB 2 and EEMB 3. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Zoology 112B.
courses.description: An introduction to the classification, structure, life histories, and habits of annelids and arthropods, with emphasis on the aquatic fauna of the Santa Barbara area.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Ecology and Management of California Wildlands
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, MCDB 1B, EEMB 2, and EEMB 3; or ENVS 1, 2, 3 and 60 or 100, and either Chem 1A, 1AL, 1B, or ENVS 15A, 15B, and 15BL. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.comments: ENV S 119 and EEMB 119 are the same course. One weekend fieldtrip is mandatory.
courses.description: Explore ecological processes in California habitats and the challenges of their management through field trips, discussions with land managers, lectures and readings. Focus on regional habitats including specialized habitats such as coastal salt marsh and vernal pools, and more widespread such as oak savanna and chaparral.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Introduction to Ecology
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, and EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B, and EEMB 3; Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.comments: Letter grade required for majors. Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 120.
courses.description: Major concepts in population and evolutionary ecology. Theoretical, experimental, and field studies pertaining to population growth and regulation, competition, predation, diversity, adaptation and life history strategies.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Field and Laboratory Studies in Ecology
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 120AL-BL. Individual projects.
courses.description: Practical studies in ecology in both field and laboratory, emphasizing the design and analysis of experiments.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Field and Laboratory Studies in Ecology
courses.prereq_text: EEMB 120AL; Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 120AL-BL. Individual projects.
courses.description: Practical studies in ecology in both field and laboratory. Individual projects are emphasized.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Terrestrial Carbon Cycle
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, EEMB 2, MCDB 1B, EEMB 3, and EEMB 120; Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.description: Explores the terrestrial carbon cycle as a central component of the Earth system and a critical frontier for climate solutions. It examines the biological and physical processes that govern terrestrial carbon fluxes and storage, and how these processes respond to global change. The course also engages students in analyzing nature-based solutions and critically evaluating strategies to protect and enhance terrestrial carbon sinks in a rapidly changing world.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Plant Biology and Biodiversity
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, MCDB 1B, EEMB 2 and EEMB 3. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 127.
courses.description: Introduction to plant biology; the importance of plants to humans; taxonomic and ecological diversity; and evolutionary processes. Will serve as a foundation for all upper-division plant biology courses. Emphasis on life history variation; pollination; reproduction and mating strategies.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Plant Biology and Biodiversity Lab
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, MCDB 1B, EEMB 2, EEMB 3 and EEMB 127. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 127L.
courses.description: Computer, lab, greenhouse, and field experience in studies of plant anatomy, physiology, reproduction, pollination, morphology, and adaptation to different environments. Live material and herbarium collections used to demonstrate plant diversity, speciation, and genetic variation. Independent and team projects.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Foundations of Ecosystem Restoration
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, MCDB 1B, EEMB 2, and EEMB 3; or ENVS 1, 2, 3 and 60 or 100, and either Chem 1A, 1AL, 1B, or ENVS 15A, 15B, and 15BL. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.comments: EEMB 128 and Environmental Studies 128 are the same course.
courses.description: Integrates ecological principles with practical issues involved in ecosystem restoration. Beginning with the challenge of selecting goals and establishing a target trajectory, students evaluate how ecological knowledge can guide restoration and whether sustainable states or trajectories can be achieved.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Introductory Genetics
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, and EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B, and EEMB 3 with a grade of C or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed MCDB 101A-B. Concurrent enrollment in MCDB 101A or MCDB 101B not allowed. Reduced credit (2.0 units) to students who have credit for MCDB 101A.
courses.description: Introduction to genetics. Mendel's laws, structure, replication and expression of DNA, linkage and chromosomal aberrations, mutation and recombination, concepts of genetic variability, quantitative and populationgenetics.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Principles of Evolution
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, MCDB 1B, EEMB 2 and EEMB 3 or EARTH 2 and 3; Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.comments: EARTH 121 and EEMB 131 are the same course. Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 131.
courses.description: A foundation course concerning the mechanisms of evolution at micro- and macroevolutionary levels, and interpretation of the resulting patterns of adaptation and organic diversity.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Comparative Genomics
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, MCDB 1B, EEMB 2 and EEMB 3; Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.description: This hands-on laboratory course introduces students to the rapidly advancing field of comparative genomics, focusing on how large-scale genomic data is generated, analyzed, and applied in scientific research. Students gain practical experience using bioinformatics tools to compare genomes across species, explore evolutionary relationships, investigate genome structure and function. Emphasis will be placed on real-world applications in biological research.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Biodiversity and Conservation Biology
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, MCDB 1B, EEMB 2, and EEMB 3; or ENVS 1, 2, 3 and 60 or 100, and either Chem 1A, 1AL, 1B, or ENVS 15A, 15B, and 15BL. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.comments: EEMB 133 and Environmental Studies 133 are the same course.
courses.description: An integration of concepts central to effectively describing biodiversity patterns on our planet and better understanding the dynamics by which wildlife and ecosystems are altered by people. Includes exposure to topics such a extinction dynamics, climate change, and the human dimensions of biodiversity change. Course reviews classical and next-generation tools for conserving nature.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Principles of Paleontology
courses.comments: EARTH 111 and EEMB 136 are the same course. Letter grade required for majors. Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 111.
courses.description: The ecological structure and evolution of the biosphere as illustrated by the fossil record.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Principles of Paleontology Laboratory
courses.comments: Same course as EARTH 111L. Letter grade required for majors. Not open for credit to students who have have completed Biology 111L.
courses.description: Exercises and projects in the identification and interpretation of fossil taxa and fossil communities.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Plant Paleobiology
courses.comments: Same course as EARTH 141. Letter grade required for majors. Not open for credit to students who have completed Botany 110, or Geol 141.
courses.description: Examination of the history of land plants; the systematics, morphology, and phylogeny of major groups. Major evolution and biogeographic patterns.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Plant Paleobiology Laboratory
courses.prereq_text: EEMB 137 or EARTH 141 (may be taken concurrently).
courses.comments: Same course as EARTH 141L. Letter grade required for majors. Not open for credit to students who have completed Botany 110L or Geol 111L.
courses.description: Anatomy, morphology, and systematics of fossil plants from the specimens.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Ethology and Behavioral Ecology
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, MCDB 1B, EEMB 2 and EEMB 3. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Zoology 138.
courses.description: Animal behavior and social organization viewed from evolutionary and whole animal perspectives. Specific topics stress environmental influences and natural selection and include: classical ethology, development and learning, communication, foraging, aggression, territoriality, mating systems, parental care, altruism, and sociobiology.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: General Plant Ecology
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B, and EEMB 3; completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Botany 140.
courses.description: An introduction to the principles of plant ecology.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: General Plant Ecology Lab
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B, and EEMB 3; and, EEMB 140 (may be taken concurrently); Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Botany 140L.
courses.description: Field and laboratory research techniques.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Aquatic Communities
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B, and EEMB 3; Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed EEMB 145C.
courses.description: A survey of the patterns of distribution, diversity, an abundance of species in marine and freshwater communities, with an emphasis on the dynamic interactions which shape these patterns.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Methods in Aquatic Community Ecology
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 145CL.
courses.description: Experience in the field techniques of aquatic community ecology.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Environmental Processes in Oceans and Lakes
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, and EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B, and EEMB 3; Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 145A.
courses.description: A discussion of biological, chemical, physical, and optical processes in marine and freshwater environments and the linkage between these processes. Emphasis on primary production, global biogeochemical cycles, nutrient dynamics, and synoptic mapping of biological and physical patterns.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Chemical and Physical Methods of Aquatic Environments
courses.prereq_text: EEMB 142B (may be taken concurrently); Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 145AL. To complete the laboratory and field protion of EEMB 145AL requires at least 8 hrs/wk. of in-class time (i.e., 0900 to 1700). Two field trips require 10 hours. Oral presentations are also required.
courses.description: A survey of physical and chemical methods used by limnologists and oceanographers supplemented with field observations.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Environmental Processes in Oceans and Lakes
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, MCDB 1B, EEMB 2 and EEMB 3. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 145B.
courses.description: A continuation of EEMB 142B with emphasis on secondary productivity, ecology of higher trophic levels including zoo plankton and fish, food web dynamics, benthic-pelagic coupling, ocean circulation, and biogeographical aspects of pelagic communities.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Methods of Aquatic Biology
courses.prereq_text: EEMB 142C (may be taken concurrently); Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed EEMB 145BL.
courses.description: Laboratory and field techniques used to measure various biological processes including productivity, and to sample, identify, enumerate, and culture marine organisms.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Marine Microbiology
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B, and EEMB 3; Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.comments: EEMB 145A-B or MCDB 131 strongly recommended.
courses.description: Exploration of evolution, ecology, biochemistry, and genetics of marine bacteria. Topics include: historical perspective, molecular approaches in microbial ecology, trophic interactions/biogeochemistry, physiological adaptations, and biochemistry and genetics of selected systems bioluminescence, deep-sea adaptations, cell-surface interactions, starvation survival).

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Marine Microbiology Lab
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B, and EEMB 3; concurrent enrollment in EEMB 144 or 142B; Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.description: A laboratory survey of the diversity, physiology and ecology of marine prokaryotes, and methods used to identify, quantify and measure their activities.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Terrestrial Microbiology
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, MCDB 1B, EEMB 2, and EEMB 3 all with a grade of C- or better
courses.description: Exploration of the diversity of archaea, bacteria, and fungi associated with humans, animals, plants, and extreme terrestrial environments. Topics include ecology, evolution, genetics, systematics, and physiology with special focus on species interactions among microbes or between hosts and microbes.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Biometry
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 2A-B or 3A-B or 34A-B or 34LA-LB; and PSTAT 5A or PSTAT 5LS or PSTAT 109 or Math 4A or Psy 5; Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 146A or EEMB 146A.
courses.description: Linear models and least squares fitting: simple and multiple linear regression; analysis of variance (fixed, random and mixed models; crossed and nested effects; balanced and unbalanced designs); analysis of covariance, factorial designs; incomplete layouts; use of transformations.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Coral Reef Biology and Ecology
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, MCDB 1B, EEMB 2 and EEMB 3. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.description: Coral reefs are highly diverse ecosystems that provide important ecosystem services across many areas of the tropics. Introduction to the taxonomy, biology, and ecology of the main groups of coral reef inhabitants. Analysis and discussion of the biology and ecological relationships of reef algae, plants and animals as well as contemporary challenges to the health and resilience of reefs, and potential conservation strategies to mitigate stressors on reefs.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Ecology of Running Waters
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B, and EEMB 3; Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 148.
courses.description: Introduction to the structure and function of river ecosystems, including physical and chemical characteristics, nutrient cycling and transport, biodiversity, biological interactions, conservation, and restoration. Discussion of bioassessment as a tool for measuring biological integrity (water quality and habitat health).

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Microbial Diversity I
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, EEMB 2, MCDB 1B, and EEMB 3; Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.description: An investigation of the metabolic diversity of bacteria and archaea with an emphasis on microbial evolution, energetics, and the ecological implications of diversity. Required laboratory is an inquiry-based introduction to classical methods of enrichment and isolation of diverse microbes from the environment and molecular identification of isolates. Basic introduction to bioinformatic analysis of microbial phylogeny using sequence data generated in the course.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Microbial Diversity II
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, MCDB 1B, EEMB 2, EEMB 3 and either EEMB 150A or EEMB 145 or EEMB 157A or MCDB 131. All completed with a grade of C- or better.
courses.description: A hands-on investigation of the genomic diversity of bacteria and archaea. Students will undertake genomic or metagenomic DNA sequencing , analysis of environmental isolates and enrichments and gain experience preparing this data for public release.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Applied Marine Ecology
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, MCDB 1B, EEMB 2, and EEMB 3; or ENVS 1, 2, 3 and 60 or 100, and either Chem 1A, 1AL, 1B, or ENVS 15A, 15B, and 15BL. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.comments: EEMB 152 and Environmental Studies 152 are the same course.
courses.description: Introduction to the application of ecological principles and methods to environmental problems in marine habitats. Focus on problems that are local, regional, and global in scale. Concepts illustrated with case studies.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Ecology of Lakes and Wetlands
courses.prereq_text: EEMB 142B; and, EEMB 142A or EEMB 120; Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.description: An examination of ecological aspects of lakes, wetlands, and their catchments integrating biogeochemical processes, biological-physical coupling, and population and community ecology. Applications of remote sensing and ecological models; human-caused impacts and their management.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Global Change Biology
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, MCDB 1B, EEMB 2 and EEMB 3. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.description: Explores the impact of environmental change (e.g., global warming, ocean acidification, drought) on ecosystems and organisms. Case studies and readings from the primary literature are used. The course covers both terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Cell Physiology
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, and EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B, and EEMB 3; Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.description: An analysis of processes fundamental to the functioning of cells, using actual examples from the protista. These processes include, but are not limited to, membrane structure and function, motility, metabolite transport, protein trafficking, energy acquisition and utilization.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Animal Physiology
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, MCDB 1B, EEMB 2 and EEMB 3; Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.description: Fundamentals of animal physiology. Covers the major systems including nervous, circulatory, respiratory, osmoregulatory, digestion, locomotion, and reproduction with an emphasis on animal diversity.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Plant Physiology
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, MCDB 1B, EEMB 2 and EEMB 3; Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.description: A study of the link between structure and function that contributes to the development, reproduction, and diversity of plants. There will be a special emphasis on primary literature reading and analyses.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Environmental Change Impacts on Marine Ecosystems
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, MCDB 1B, EEMB 2 and EEMB 3. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.description: Explores the impacts of climate change and other types of anthropogenic perturbation on organisms and processes in marine ecosystems. Emphasis is placed on ocean acidification, warming and deoxygenation, as well as plastic and oil pollution. Topics discussed include threats to marine diversity and ecosystem function, latitudinal shifts in productivity and diversity, changes in the global cycling of elements such as carbon, and the cost of climate change on food security.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Environmental Change Impacts on Marine Ecosystems Lab
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B, and EEMB 3; concurrent enrollment in EEMB 158; Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.description: Explores methods to assess environmental change impacts on seawater chemistry and biology. Students conduct experiments including testing the impact of ocean acidification (OA) on marine coccolithophores and explore ocean alkalinity enhancement (OAE) as a method to mitigate OA and remove carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. By the end of the quarter students should be able to (1) understand the impacts of OA and OAE on marine chemistry and biology; (2) understanding relevant measurements and sampling techniques; (3) conduct laboratory procedures using OA and OAE best practice guides; (4) demonstrate proficiency in data synthesis and analysis and (5) gain experience in paper writing.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Tropical Ecology
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A and MCDB 1B and EEMB 2 and EEMB 3; Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.description: Introduction to the structure and function of tropical ecosystems, including physical and chemical characteristics, nutrient cycling and transport, biodiversity, biological interactions, conservation, and restoration. Discussion of case studies and the use ecological models as tools for exploring the dynamics of habitat fragmentation, coral reef degradation, and the spread of infectious disease as it relates to climate change.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Fungi & Enterprise
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, 1B, EEMB 2, EEMB 3 all with grades of 'C-' or better)
courses.description: Explores how fungal biology, physiology, and ecology contribute to innovation across industries like textiles, aerospace, pharmaceuticals, and agriculture. This course examines fungi’s critical role in sustainability, product development, and scientific breakthroughs, revealing their hidden influence in modern enterprise. Students will engage with real-world applications, connecting mycology to industrial solutions that address today’s challenges.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Deep-Sea Biology
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, and EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B, and EEMB 3; Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 153.
courses.description: Consideration of the biology of midwater and benthic organisms living beneath the euphotic zone. Emphasis on dynamic aspects of biological processes in this unique environment. Surveys of major deep-sea taxa and the history of deep-sea biology are included.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Fields Studies in Marine Ecological Physiology
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A-1B, EEMB 2 and 3; Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.description: An integration of fields and laboratory approaches to questions in marine ecological physiology. Using local coastal field sites, participants conduct a team research project. Participants collect, analyze, and present the results. Involves occasional field trips and lab work.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Applied Freshwater Ecology
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, MCDB 1B, EEMB 2 and EEMB 3; Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.description: Providing sufficient quantities of high quality freshwater will be the single biggest challenge facing humanity in the next century. The course explores the scientific basis for evaluating and addressing the impacts of environmental change of freshwater ecosystems.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Conservation Ecology
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, MCDB 1B, EEMB 2 and EEMB 3. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.description: Introduction to the practical application of biological principles to conserving biodiversity. Covers tools and theory derived from both ecology and evolutionary biology such as metapopulation theory and population viability analysis as applied to real world examples.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Biology of the Marine-Land Interface
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, and EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B, and EEMB 3; Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 141. Offered during summer session only. Course Materials Fee charged.
courses.description: Influence of physical factors on adaptations of shoreline organisms with emphasis on the arthropods.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Ecosystem Processes
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, MCDB 1B, EEMB 2, and EEMB 3; or ENVS 1, 2, 3 and 60 or 100, and either Chem 1A, 1AL, 1B, and 1C or ENVS 15A, 15B, and 15BL. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.comments: EEMB 171 and Environmental Studies 171 are the same course. Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 171.
courses.description: An examination of the key processes that regulate ecosystem productivity and function in terrestrial ecosystems. Specific foci include: plant- soil linkages including decomposition and nutrient supply, and the role of above- and below-ground community composition on element cycles.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Advanced Biostatistics using Bayesian Methods
courses.prereq_text: EEMB 146 with a grade of C- or better.
courses.description: A model-based approach to modern methods in data analysis. Comparison of statistical approaches including frequentist, likelihood, and Bayesian techniques. Methods for simulating data, estimating parameters for single variable models, constructing multivariate and hierarchical models, model comparison using information criteria, and model suitability using posterior predictive analysis.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Ecological Modeling
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 34A-B or 34LA-LB or 3A-B or 2A-B; completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 179.
courses.description: An introduction to mathematical and computer models in studies of the natural environment with emphasis on population dynamics and species interactions. Case studies of interacting physical, chemical and biological phenomena.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Ecological Modeling - Honors
courses.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in EEMB 179 and consent of instructor.
courses.description: Honors component of EEMB 179 designed to permit an in-depth study involvingformulation, analysis and interpretation of an ecological model. A written report on the work is required.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Evolutionary theory and models of behavioral processes
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A-B; EEMB 2-3; Math 3A-B or Math 34A-B or 34LA-LB or Math 2A-B; C- or better in all listed prerequisites.
courses.description: A mathematical approach to understanding the process of evolutionary change with an emphasis on behavioral strategies starting wtih natural selection, frequency dependent selection, sex ratio, and selection for local adaptation. Using an evolutionary framework, the consequences of behavioral strategies will be studied, including foraging strategies, mating behavior, and social behavior.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Introduction to Teaching in Biology
courses.prereq_text: Completion of MCDB 1A, MCDB1B, EEMB 2, EEMB 3 all with a grade of C- or better. Consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit in combination with MCDB 183 to a maximum of 8.0 units but no units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: Explores evidence-based, asset-focused strategies to support effective near-peer learning in biology. Students will develop skills in metacognition, communication, and student-centered teaching practices through readings, discussions, and self-reflection. Emphasis is placed on understanding how students learn, fostering engagement, and promoting academic success through inclusive, reflective approaches.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Internship in Biological Sciences
courses.comments: Students must have a 2.5 cumulative grade-point average. May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 15 units.
courses.description: Opportunity to obtain practical biological related experience by working under faculty direction as an intern with local, state, federal, or private agencies. A written report will be submitted for evaluation.

Presentations and discussions may include model ecosystem studies, hands on restoration or conservation projects & lessons learned, and political, economic and philosophical issues.

courses.comments: Up to 2.0 units may apply to the major.
courses.description: Exposes students to current research topics in ecology and evolutionary biology. Students will attend the EEMB departmental seminar each week and participate in a discussion of the seminar research, critiquing the presentation and the content, and drawing parallels with topics from other courses. Students will write a term paper describing and critiquing one seminar.

Source material will be a mixture of graduate-level texts, review articles and primary literature. Weekly meetings will be interactive and student-led. Our focus will be on fundamental processes in the metabolism and interactions of microbes (from foundational knowledge to recent discoveries), but we will also analyze the methods used to study these processes in diverse natural ecosystems (e.g. sequencing, bioinformatics, microscopy, stable isotopes).

courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing and consent of instructor.

courses.description: Explores the use of biological collections—such as herbaria, vertebrate and invertebrate museums, and paleontological —in biodiversity research. Globally, biological collections house around 3 billion specimens that provide historical and geographic context that can enhance studies in ecology and evolution. Topics include emerging specimen-based research methods (e.g., CT scanning, isotopes, ancient DNA, machine learning), and practical consideration in specimen uses (e.g., permits and regulations, destructive sampling, data curation). Students will gain practical skills for accessing, analyzing, and contributing to collections-based science using both traditional and emerging techniques.

courses.description: Explore the R programming environment for statistical analysis, data visualization, data management, and more. Stay up to date with current packages, learn new techniques, share invaluable tips and tricks. Exact topics will be determined by class participants. courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Remote Sensing of Aquatic Environments Using the new Surface Water and Ocean Topography Satellite
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: Maximum units for credit in major: 8 BS; 4 BA. See also credit limits with other courses in description of major requirements.
courses.description: In this course, we review papers coming out from the new Surface Water and Ocean Topography Mission (SWOT) launched in December 2022. SWOT uses radar interferometry to observe sub-mesoscale eddies and small motion features on the ocean as well as water surface heights and extents from inland water bodies (lakes, wetlands, and rivers) on a global scale. Undergraduate students will learn about the new satellite technology, what the data is best used for, how to download the datafiles from publicly available databases, and how to apply it to their research. This course is meant to benefit both those actively using remote sensing in their work and those who are curious if they can use this data for their research.

courses.title: Writing Grants-in-Aid of Research
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit in combination with Biology 194AA-ZZ and MCDB 194AA-ZZ to a maximum of 8 units. Individual letter designations may be repeated for credit to a maximum of 4 units.
courses.description: Teaches students the basics of crafting small grant proposals, by introducing them to how to locate suitable funding opportunities, craft compelling narratives for funding, and justify budget requests. Each student will, over the course of the quarter, craft a small grant in aid of research (most likely Sigma Xi's Grant in Aid of Research for submission Sigma Xi's annual Spring deadline, but other funding opportunities will be considered on a case by case basis). We will use peer review circles and mock grant review panels to help refine their proposals before submission.

Maximum units for credit defined on major sheets. See also credit limits with other courses in description of major requirements.

courses.description: Individual conferences one hour every two weeks. Special readings designed to broaden the outlook of students and to knit into a cohesive whole the basic principles underlying the major disciplines in the field.

Maximum units for credit in major: 8 BS; 4 BA. See also credit limits with other courses in description of major requirements. Tutorial, 1-3 hours; field, 1-5 hours.
courses.description: Hours and credit by arrangement with any faculty member. Laboratory or field.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Molecular Evolution
courses.prereq_text: EEMB 2 or MCDB 1A or Geol 3 or instructor approval
courses.description: Major concepts in evolutionary biology, presented with a genetic emphasis. Provides an introduction to the study of population genetic processes and the patterns of genomic evolution, adaptation, and speciation that result from these processes.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Marine Ecology and Conservation
courses.description: Provides an in-depth understanding of the biotic and abiotic interactions that determine ecological processes in marine environments, how these processes shape the structure of marine ecosystems, and how these principles are used to direct marine conservation and management.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Biological Oceanography
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 243.
courses.description: Current concepts in biological oceanography focusin on the coupling of biotic processes to ocean physics, chemistry and sedimentation. Emphasis on areas of active research with critical evaluation of current and seminalliterature.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Quantitative Methods in Biology
courses.description: A review of quantitative methods required to develop models of biological and ecological systems. Topics illustrated through computer exercises.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Microbial Diversity I
courses.description: An investigation of the metabolic diversity of bacteria and archaea with an emphasis on microbial evolution, energetics, and the ecological implications of diversity. Required laboratory is an inquiry-based introduction to classical methods of enrichment and isolation of diverse microbes from the environment and molecular identification of isolates. Basic introduction to bioinformatic analysis of microbial phylogeny using sequence data generated in the course.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Fungi & Enterprise
courses.description: Explores how fungal biology, physiology, and ecology contribute to innovation across industries like textiles, aerospace, pharmaceuticals, and agriculture. This course examines fungi’s critical role in sustainability, product development, and scientific breakthroughs, revealing their hidden influence in modern enterprise. Students will engage with real-world applications, connecting mycology to industrial solutions that address today’s challenges.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Advanced Biostatistics using Bayesian Methods
courses.description: A model-based approach to modern methods in data analysis. Comparison of statistical approaches including frequentist, likelihood, and Bayesian techniques. Methods for simulating data, estimating parameters for single variable models, constructing multivariate and hierarchical models, model comparison using information criteria, and model suitability using posterior predictive analysis.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Environmental Adaptation
courses.description: Introduction to the concepts and literature concerning mechanisms underlying physiological and evolutionary adaptations that allow animals to exploit various environments and adapt to environmental change. Open to graduate students from various disciplines. Lectures and student presentations.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Ecological Modeling
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 279.
courses.description: An introduction to mathematical and computer models in studies of the natural environment with emphasis on population dynamics and species interactions. Case studies of interacting physical, chemical and biological phenomena.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Field Work in Oceanography
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division courses in aquatic biology and/or geology.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 285.
courses.description: Participation as a member of the scientific part on Scripps institution (UCSD), NMFS, and UCSB oceanographic cruises. Cruise duration is variable (7 to 60 days), and course units will vary with cruise duration. Supervision by scientific party leader. Report required.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Restoration Ecology Seminar
courses.description: Seminar explores current topics in restoration ecology including model projects, techniques, structured research, performance criteria, political and philosophical issues and may include site visits.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Introduction to Faculty Research
courses.prereq_text: Strongly encouraged for all first year graduate students; open to continuingraduate students. Undergraduates by consent of instructor.
courses.description: Presentation and discussion of current EEMB faculty research. Informal discussions follow weekly faculty member research presentations. This seminar exposes graduate students to the breadth of departmental research, facilitates graduate-faculty interaction, and offers an intellectual setting for student interaction.

courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit in combination with Biology 292.
courses.description: Special topics of current importance in biological sciences. Course content will vary. Information on course content may be obtained in the department office.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Teaching Assistant Orientation
courses.comments: Required of all teaching assistants. No unit credit allowed toward advanceddegree. May be repeated for credit in combination with Biology 500.
courses.description: General orientation regarding the University of California and the Santa Barbara campus; various pertinent regulations, officials and their functions, staff and functions; services available to teaching assistants and to students. Prospective teaching assistants are encouraged to take this course during the fall quarter prior to their employment.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Practicum in Instruction
courses.comments: No unit credit allowed toward advanced degree. May be repeated for credit in combination with Biology 501.
courses.description: Practical experience in teaching within specified areas of biology. Students will have responsibility for one or more laboratory and/or discussion sections. Staff will periodically observe teaching assistants in actual teaching situations. Evaluation forms will be completed by members of the class sections.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Techniques of Teaching and Laboratory Class Supervision
courses.comments: Required of all teaching assistants. No unit credit allowed toward advanceddegree. May be repeated for credit in combination with Biology 502.
courses.description: Weekly discussion and readings on techniques of teaching including lecturing, leading discussions, writing and grading exams, student-teacher interactions classroom dynamics, and teaching philosophy.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Introduction to Graduate Research
courses.description: Introduction to research at the graduate level for first-year EEMB graduate students Topics include navigating degree requirements, keeping up to date with the scientific literature, building a professional network, and scientific ethics.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Foundations in Ecology
courses.description: This is the first in a set of advanced courses in ecology and evolution, and includes modules on organismal, population, community, and ecosystem ecology. The course includes discussion of foundational papers in the field, as well as weekly tutorials contextualizing topics using R, group discussions, and mathematical models.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Foundations in Evolutionary Biology
courses.description: This is the second in a set of advanced courses in ecology and evolution, and includes modules on the origins of genetic variation, models of evolution, and evolutionary forces affecting variability, including natural selection and genetic drift. The course also touches upon the example of human evolution and some case studies of ecological evolutionary genetics.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Writing Science
courses.description: A hands-on workshop to polish writing skills. Modules focus on story telling to make ideas compelling, streamlining to make writing compact and effective, and developing flow of ideas and paragraphs. Students work on a chapter, paper, or proposal.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Scientific Teaching
courses.description: This graduate seminar explores scientific teaching, an approach that encourages educators to bring the spirit and rigor of scientific research into the classroom to transform how students learn science. Through readings, discussion, and applied activities, students examine evidence from the learning sciences and consider how it informs instructional design, assessment, and inclusive teaching practices. The course is discussion-driven and reflective, emphasizing critical engagement with research and connections to participants’ own teaching contexts, with the goal of developing thoughtful, evidence-based approaches to STEM education.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: EEMB Colloquium
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit in combination with Biology 590.
courses.description: Presentation and discussion of recent work in ecology, evolution, behavioral ecology, evolutionary ecology, physiological ecology, and marine biology, by eminent and nationally and internationally well known biologists. Optional individual discussion in addition to formal lecture.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Evolutionary Biology

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Contentious Topics in Fisheries & Aquaculture
courses.comments: Individual letter designations may be repeated for credit to a maximum of 108 units.
courses.description: A number of topics in fisheries, aquaculture, and marine ecology have become major points of contention in the literature, with growing bodies of evidence that appear to contradict or refute each other without resolution. This seminar introduces the main conflicting topics and key principles of the field. Students weigh the scientific evidence and discuss the broader implications of the unsettled science.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Foundations and Frontiers in Ecology
courses.comments: Individual letter designations may be repeated for credit to a maximum of 108 units.
courses.description: Provides an overview of fundamental concepts in ecology and discussion of recent works on these subjects. Topics include population growth and regulation, population structure, metapopulations, metacommunities, coexistence mechanisms, neutral theory, invasibility, predator-prey dynamics, disease, food webs, phenotypic plasticity, metabolic theory, and diversity-ecosystem function relationships.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Advanced Population Ecology
courses.comments: Individual letter designations may be repeated for credit to a maximum of 36 units.
courses.description: A critical review of research in selected fields of biology.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Plant Evolution & Genomics
courses.comments: Individual letter designations may be repeated for credit to a maximum of 108 units.
courses.description: Course provides an overview of fundamental concepts in evolution and genomics and discussion of recent works on these subjects. Topics include population genetic structure, genetic diversity, adaptation, genetic causes of adaptation, genome evolution, conservation genomics and landscape genetics.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: R Seminar - Coding for Ecological and Evolutionary Analyses
courses.comments: Individual letter designations may be repeated for credit to a maximum of 108 units.
courses.description: Explore the R programing environment for statistical analysis, data visualization, data management, and more. Stay up to date with current packages, learn new techniques, share invaluable tips and tricks. Exact topics will be determined by class participants. R can be used for a variety of applications (GIS, simulation modeling, web app development). Course will focus on hands-on application, with coding clinic and shared coding resources.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Research Reviews in Aquatic Ecology
courses.comments: Individual letter designations may be repeated for credit to a maximum of 36 units.
courses.description: A critical review of research in selected fields of biology.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Remote Sensing of Aquatic Environments Using the new Surface Water and Ocean Topography Satellite
courses.comments: Individual letter designations may be repeated for credit to a maximum of 108 units.
courses.description: In this course, we review papers coming out from the new Surface Water and Ocean Topography Mission (SWOT) launched in December 2022. SWOT uses radar interferometry to observe sub-mesoscale eddies and small motion features on the ocean as well as water surface heights and extents from inland water bodies (lakes, wetlands, and rivers) on a global scale. Graduate students will learn about the new satellite technology, what the data is best used for, how to download the datafiles from publicly available databases, and how to apply it to their research. This course is meant to benefit both those actively using remote sensing in their work and those who are curious if they can use this data for their research.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Parasitology
courses.comments: Individual letter designations may be repeated for credit to a maximum of 36 units.
courses.description: A critical review of research in selected fields of biology.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Theoretical Ecology and Evolution
courses.comments: Individual letter designations may be repeated for credit to a maximum of 36 units.
courses.description: A critical review of research in selected fields of biology.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Post PhD Preparation
courses.comments: Individual letter designations may be repeated for credit to a maximum of 108 units.
courses.description: This seminar explores career options for ecology and evolution PhDs, including identifying transferable skills and building industry-ready application materials. The seminar will include discussions with speakers who have pursued a variety of career paths after graduation, professionals from Career Counseling, and program alumni. The goal is to help students develop a roadmap for their career path after graduation, particularly for non-academic careers.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Directed Reading and Research
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit in combination with Biology 596 up to half of the graduate units required for the M.A. degree.
courses.description: Hours and credit by arrangement with faculty.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Individual Study for Master's Comprehensive Examinations and Ph.D. Examinations
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: No unit credit allowed toward advanced degree. Students are limited to 24 units per examination, and 12 units per quarter. May be repeated for creditin combination with Biology 597.
courses.description: Individual study for M.A. comprehensive examinations and Ph.D. examinations.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Master's Thesis Research and Preparation
courses.prereq_text: M.A. (thesis) candidate and consent of committee chair.
courses.comments: May be repeated forcredit in combination with Biology 598 to a maximum of 12 units. No unit credit allowed toward advanced degree.
courses.description: For research underlying the thesis and writing of the thesis.

courses.subject: EEMB
courses.title: Ph.D. Dissertation Preparation
courses.prereq_text: Ph.D. candidate and consent of instructor.
courses.description: For writing of the dissertation.

courses.subject: EEMB W
courses.title: Concepts and Controversies in the Biological Sciences
courses.comments: Not open for credit toward graduation to students who completed EEMB 20, MCDB 20, EEMB 22, MCDB 1A, EEMB 2, MCDB 1B, or EEMB 3. Concurrent enrollment in MCDB 20 or MCDB 1A not allowed.
courses.description: Introduction to the principles of evolution, physiology and ecology; emphasizing fundamental concepts and processes such as natural selection and speciation, photosynthesis and cellular respiration, animal and plant interactions, population dynamics, community structure, and biodiversity. Examines perspectives on currently relevant and biologically based topics such as evolution / scientific creationism, sociobiology, biotechnology, reproductive rights, pandemic disease, climate change, exobiology, and overpopulation.

courses.subject: EEMB W
courses.title: Biometry
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 2A-B or 3A-B or 34A-B or 34LA-LB; and PSTAT 5A or PSTAT 5LS or PSTAT 109 or Math 4A or Psy 5; Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C- or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 146A or EEMB 146A. Same course as EEMB 146.
courses.description: Linear models and least squares fitting: simple and multiple linear regression; analysis of variance (fixed, random and mixed models; crossed and nested effects; balanced and unbalanced designs); analysis of covariance, factorial designs; incomplete layouts; use of transformations.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Introduction to Literary Study
courses.comments: Course recommended as alternative to Writing 50 or 109 for students who plan to major in English or literary study. Not open for credit to students who have completed English 10AC, 10EM, or 10LC.
courses.description: Acquaints students with purposes and tools of literary interpretation. Introduces techniques and vocabulary of analytic discussion and critical writing. Some emphasis on poetry with attention also to drama, essay, and the novel.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Seminar for Introduction to Literature
courses.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in English 10; consent of instructor.
courses.description: A seminar course for a select number of students enrolled in English 10 designed to enrich the large lecture experience for the motivated student. Course will include either supplementary readings or more intensive study of the English 10 reading list, as well as supplemental writing.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Literature and its Uses
courses.description: Introduces students to literary studys unique perspectives on social knowledge, public issues, ethics, and global developments. Special emphasis on how literary practice serves as a gateway to the professions, including writing, teaching, law, journalism, counseling, business, medicine, and technological fields.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Introduction to Shakespeare as Popular Culture
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed English 15SH.
courses.description: Shakespeare's plays are designed to entertain. They were written for the popular stage, and over the last four centuries they have been taken up in a variety of media for audiences all around the world. This course investigates Shakespeare's art in relation to the commercial theater for which he wrote and the popular culture of the modern world: film, theater, and radio, but also graphic novels, tv shows, and pop music. As we discuss these plays and their creative reworkings, we will touch on topics ranging from the politics of voice to the performance of mind and emotion, from the ethics of revenge to the fluidity of gendered identity.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Seminar on Shakespeare
courses.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in English 15; consent of instructor.
courses.description: Seminar course for a select number of students enrolled in English 15 designed to enrich the large lecture experience for the motivated student. Course includes either supplementary reading or more intensive study of the English 15 reading list, as well as supplemental writing.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Shakespeare as Popular Culture
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed English 15.
courses.description: Shakespeare's plays are designed to entertain. They were written for the popular stage, and over the last four centuries they have been taken up in a variety of media for audiences all around the world.
