We will study the foundations of the Motion Pictures Producers and Distributors of America, the Production Code Administration, the studio ratings system, and approaches to content regulation that have occurred since the ratings system was adopted in 1968. In the second half, we will take on case studies from around the world, examining films and controversies related to politics, religion, and sex.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Film and Social Reality: The Essay Film
courses.prereq_text: Film Studies 46 or upper-division standing; consent of department.
courses.description: In this course we analyze the category of films referred to as essay films. Described as resisting classification, interrogating boundaries between fact and fiction, and transgressing dominant ways of seeing and thinking, essay films draw on a range of established practices including documentary, narrative, and avant-garde cinema forms. We emphasize the films’ relation to the archive and traditional research methods; history; political intervention and reflection; and critical engagement with visual representation and image making.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Film and Social Reality
courses.prereq_text: Film Studies 46 or upper-division standing; consent of department.
courses.description: An inquiry into the interrelationships between film and history and/or film and ideology. The course examines how cinema reflects and/or influences the attitudes of a society.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Special Topics in Cultural Studies
courses.prereq_text: Film and Media Studies 46 or 70 or upper-division standing.
courses.description: Uses cultural studies as a critical paradigm to closely examine a particular topic or theme.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Asian American Digital Media
courses.prereq_text: Film and Media Studies 46 or 70 or upper-division standing.
courses.description: Explores Asian American digital media through a consideration of how Asian American racialization and technology have been co-constituted. This course covers a range of Asian American digital media from YouTube skits to makeup artistry to food creators and more.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Alchemy and Imagination
courses.description: Uses cultural studies as a critical paradigm to closely examine a particular topic or theme.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Border Media
courses.prereq_text: Film and Media Studies 46 or 70 or upper-division standing.
courses.description: Examines the proliferation of border security technologies used to surveil, detect, categorize, detain, and deport people who cross borders without state permission. Together we explore global examples of border security regimes and resistance movements, including artist and activist media practices that expose and disrupt the violence of state borders, while inviting students to consider their own proximity to and lived experience of the US-Mexico border here in California.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Cinema in the Digital Age
courses.description: Explores a range of issues related to the digitization of cinema’s production, distribution, and exhibition. Topics include digital cinematography’s relation to cinematic realism, the politics of digital special effects, and the representation of social media and digital devices in films.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Special Topics in Cultural Studies: Green Games
courses.description: This course puts game studies in conversation with environmental science and media. Explore whether analog and digital games present unique opportunities to engage with ecological crisis and human-environment relations, and work with others to develop your own green game prototypes.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Gender and Sexuality in Film
courses.prereq_text: Film and Media Studies 46 or 70 or upper-division standing.
courses.description: A survey of gender and sexuality in film that traverses the onscreen and industrial representation of configurations of both gender and sexuality throughout history and transnationally. Along with film theory informed by feminist, queer, and critical race studies, topics may include the male gaze, the monstrous feminine, female subjectivity, the oppositional gaze, New Queer Cinema, industry inequities, and female and/or queer filmmakers. Each week, students will attend lecture and screening to become familiar with feminist and queer critical analytical tools to augment film analysis related to the many permutations of gender and sexuality articulated in film from early cinema to the present.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Queer Media Histories and Historiography
courses.description: This class explores the means by which queer filmmakers have used the work of others to reimagine their own individual and collective pasts, presents, and future possibilities.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Special Topics in Cultural Studies: Media, Technology and Society
courses.description: This critical studies course explores how technology functions as part of media industries, societies, and cultures. Through lectures, screenings, and assignments, the course will help students understand technology as an array of objects, ideologies, fantasies, labor practices, and industrial formations.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Film Noir
courses.description: Study of the conventional themes, structures, and visual motifs of the detective film. American films of the forties and fifties and contemporary American and European works will be considered.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Experimental Film
courses.description: A survey of the experimental film tracing the major stylistic and thematic trends in the diverse movements that have considered themselves outside of the commercial narrative cinema. Bunuel, Dulac, Cocteau, Leger, Deren, Brakhage, Baillie, Frampton, Snow, Rainer, and others.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Introduction to Environmental Media
courses.description: Ties the acquisition of critical viewing skills for film to the practice of conceiving and writing short environmental documentaries. Students screen narrative films and documentaries, deconstruct them, and use their new proficiency to write their own documentary treatments.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Film Music
courses.description: Examines the musical score as an integral structural element of cinema. topics include the model of "silent" cinema; the theoretical basis of soundand image synchronicity; the narrative functions of film music; and contemporary development of the film score.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis
courses.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: A seminar for advanced students examining in-depth a particular problem or issue in the analysis of film, television, digital media, and the consequences for history, theory, or aesthetics.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Critical Approaches to Animation
courses.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: This seminar examines animated films as sites for critical intervention. Research methods integrate historical, theoretical and formal analysis, and discussions explore the ways in which the practices and aesthetics of animation actively engage their social, cultural and political contexts.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Artificial Intelligence and Media Industries
courses.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: In this seminar, students will read and discuss current research articles and writings related to AI and the media industries. The course will consider AI tools and systems in relation to media production, distribution, and exhibition. Topics addressed include: ownership and capacities of AI tools and systems; changing work roles and labor relations; authorship, creativity, and copyright issues; AI-related modes of storytelling and aesthetics; impacts of AI on streaming and distribution; and infrastructural requirements of AI in the media industries.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Humane Cinema: Media and Animal Studies
courses.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: From Eadweard Muybridge’s equine motion photography experiments to lions and tigers and bears (oh my), to an internet made of cats, animals and media have always been inextricably linked. This course takes a multifaceted, interdisciplinary approach to the study of onscreen beasts. How have animals been used as characters, as actors, as metaphors? What are the ethics of putting real animals onscreen? What do stories about animals tell us about ourselves? We will consider fictional and nonfictional modes of storytelling, historical and contemporary works, real and computer-generated creatures in our global cinematic safari. Screenings may include Nope, Jaws, Princess Mononoke, Grizzly Man, and EO.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Buster Keaton
courses.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: Buster Keaton's silent comedies in depth. Topics include: the history of comic performance styles, narrative and non-narrative comic film forms, the imagery and themes of modernity in American art and culture, and pragmatism as an aesthetic and philosophical stance.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis
courses.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: A seminar for advanced students examining in-depth a particular problem or issue in the analysis of film and its consequences for history, theory, or aesthetics of film, television and digital media.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Theories of Comedy
courses.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: This seminar explores historical developments in screen comedy through the lens of various explanations for the human phenomena of comedy and laughter, with attention to questions of social and political context and changing processes of technological mediation.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Cinema and Revolution: Media Forensics, Surveillance, and Contemporary Global Protests
courses.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: Examines the cinema of contemporary protest, tracking successive waves of revolt from the 2011 Arab Spring to recent uprisings in Eastern Europe, East Asia, and the Middle East. We trace a spectrum of moving-image practice, from anonymous citizen footage and mobile livestreams to festival documentaries and dramatic features, treating protest footage as at once evidence and artifact. Throughout, the course asks who gets to document an uprising, whose visibility is claimed and whose is withheld, and how facial recognition, surveillance, and digital forensics now reshape events and their representation. Students complete an original research project analyzing the visual record of a single movement.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis
courses.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: A seminar for advanced students examining in-depth a particular problem or issue in the analysis of film and its consequences for history, theory, or aesthetics of film, television and digital media.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Essay Film
courses.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: In this hybrid theory/practice seminar, we analyze the category of films referred to as essay films. Described as resisting classification, interrogating boundaries between fact and fiction, and transgressing dominant ways of seeing and thinking, essay films draw from and subvert a range of established practices, including nonfiction, narrative, and avant-garde cinema. What is the history of essayistic filmmaking? What does the essayistic mode offer filmmakers and scholars today? Through readings, screenings, student-led presentations, and exercises, students will gain both a conceptual foundation and hands-on experience with the essay film. The course culminates in a final independent project.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Fan Culture
courses.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: This course allows students to closely examine and analyze the communities that arise around the shared enjoyment of an aspect of popular culture.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: The Future of Media
courses.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: This seminar takes a critical-industrial approach to analyzing 21st century digital media culture. We survey ongoing developments related to social media, streaming media, advertising, business models, and content development, among other topics, throughout the quarter. We also look at the various stakeholders ranging from Hollywood studios, Big Tech corporations, music and gaming companies, and YOU - the user - in order to understand the forces controlling, directing, creating, obstructing, and/or unleashing whatever is on the horizon for medias future.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis Global Cinema Going
courses.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: Explores prevailing themes in contemporary and historical film exhibition in a variety of global contexts. Readings include scholarly work and popular sources to assist students in reflecting on the research process and preparing a high-quality paper.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Global Genres
courses.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: Discusses the transnational iterations of diverse genrescomedy, melodrama, science fiction, action cinema, and horror to situate genres as expressive forms that respond to popular anxieties around change, movement, and dislocation engendered by the geopolitical flux.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Gender, Romance, and Cinema
courses.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: Explores how films about romantic love shape, reinforce, or challenge cultural norms of gender and sexuality. Focusing on romantic comedies, melodramas, and global reworkings of these genres, the course traces how constructions and critiques of romance appear in cinema from classical Hollywood to the present. Readings from feminist film theory, queer theory, and sociology guide discussions on spectatorship, heteronormativity, gender performativity, race and masculinity, and more.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Latin American Cinema
courses.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: Study of the central issues in contemporary Latin American cinema from 1990 to the present with an emphasis on aesthetics, social and political cultures, and global networks.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Marxist Film
courses.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: Is Marx still useful in addressing social inequalities still prevalent in our times? This course aims to answer this question by examining a series of political films that attempt to challenge the logic of modern capitalism from a Marxist perspective.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Media and Violence
courses.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: This seminar examines several of the issues related to representations of and discourses about violence in film and media. We begin with a consideration of the precursors to and emergence and consolidation of the so-called "ultraviolent" aesthetic (in the mid-to-late 1960s), then we consider a few of the film genres whose most prominent conventions include representations of violence (such as the gangster, horror, war, and boxing genres). In addition, the seminar includes a comparative approach to the issue of violent representations in film and media (especially television) by surveying the terms and themes that characterize both social scientific and humanities discourses.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Oil Culture
courses.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: This seminar examines how our dependency on oil shapes modern ways of seeing and being. The course traces the media worlds of oil, from the origins of documentary film to contemporary contemplations of a world after oil.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Occult and Psychedelic Horror
courses.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: Focuses on the occult and/or psychedelic dimensions of horror films and popular culture. Critical, historical, and theoretical approaches to fear, disgust, the monster, the supernatural, delirium, esotericism, limit experiences, “good” and “bad trips.”

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Pakistani Cinema: Exploring the Nation through Cinema from 1947-Present
courses.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: What do you think when you think of “Pakistan?” What feelings does it engender? What visions does it (re)create? What about “Pakistan” and “cinema?” This course examines the idea of a national culture and the cinema of Pakistan in terms of major periods, themes, formal parameters, and institutions in relation to both national and international cultural histories. In choosing Pakistan and its cinema history which correlates with a complex political history of constantly changing regimes as our locale, we will both problematize and work through the concept of a national cinema culture through a burgeoning subfield of film studies, Pakistani cinema.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Russian War Films, 1911Present
courses.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: Examines the genre of war films in Russian and Soviet cinema from the pre-revolutionary era to the present. Together, we explore films on Russian military conflicts from World War I to the ongoing war in Ukraine. Following the evolution of a wide range of cinematic styles through the historic peripeteia of Russian imperialist, Soviet, and post-Soviet societies, we explore how movies have shaped the countrys popular historical narratives. In addition to viewing and discussing a feature-length film each week, we discuss short readings on the history of Russian cinema. Students also write weekly posts on the viewing assignments, which will go towards the creation of a collective zine.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis
courses.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: A seminar for advanced students examining in-depth a particular problem or issue in the analysis of film and its consequences for history, theory, or aesthetics of film, television and digital media.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Screendance
courses.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: This course asks students to consider dance-like rhythmic movement to be integral to its representation as screen media. In addition to written assignments, students are asked to produce a short video production drawing on the reading and weekly screenings.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis:Adaptation Studies: Screening Shakespeare
courses.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: This seminar investigates how to study screen adaptations, focusing on Shakespeare, arguably the most adapted author. Film and TV-focused topics covered include intertextuality, critical race theory (#ShakeRace), and queer theory. Screenings may include: Haider, Romeo + Juliet, Game of Thrones.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Critical Encounters with "True Crime"
courses.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: Investigates the history and theory of "true crime" as an evolving intermedial genre from early modern broadsides to 19th-century penny dreadfuls to contemporary podcasts, docuseries, and amateur digital investigations. Students will analyze "true crime" case studies through different lenses, such as economics and industry, aesthetics and pleasure, and ethics and representation.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: The Selfie from Caravaggio to the Present
courses.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: The digital “selfie" is ubiquitous. But what constitutes the lure of reproducing one’s image through technical media in the first place? This course examines histories and theories of self-imaging media, tracing how widespread concepts of selfhood have shifted over time alongside––and in relation to––the development of specific media technologies: from paintings to daguerreotypes, snapshots, cinema, video, and digital media. By analyzing broad tends and “case studies” of specific artists, filmmakers, and theorists; we will ultimately consider the historical context, and develop the conceptual skills, needed to survey and scrutinize ethical problems and potentials posed by selfies in the present.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Youth Culture
courses.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: This seminar examines the origins and development of the American media's many preoccupations with youth, including as on-screen protagonists and a key demographic off-screen. Issues explored include: the terms and meanings of "youth media" and "youth culture"; themes associated with youth; and the ways producers have sought to attract youth.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Basic Screenwriting
courses.prereq_text: Consent of instructor, writing sample, upper-division standing.
courses.description: A study of the creativity and the technique of screenwriting for the conventional narrative film and for TV. Students will be required to complete writing exercises, a treatment, and master scenes of a full-lengthproject.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Advanced Screenwriting
courses.description: A course intended for students who have successfully completed Film Studies188A and have a full-length screenplay in process which they want to complete.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Musical Theatre
courses.description: An introduction to the unique techniques and challenges of writing for musical theatre, focusing on the collaborative art of telling a story through music, lyrics, script (the “book”) and dance. A historical overview of musical theater from early operetta to contemporary Broadway and West End hits, will inform our exploration of both the “show” and the “business.” Students will learn foundational vocabulary, analyze how songs advance character and plot, and develop scenes and songs in weekly, hands-on exercises, culminating in a workshop presentation of original works-in-progress.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Short Form Comedy
courses.description: A fast-paced, writing-intensive dive into the world of sketch-writing, digital shorts, monologues, and stand-up comedy. We explore the foundational principals of scene-structure, joke-structure, and comedic voice through analysis of classic and contemporary examples, with an emphasis on developing your own unique point-of-view. Through in-class collaboration and a supportive “room-writing” environment, writers practice pitching, punching-up, producing, and performing individual, team, and group-generated material on a professional deadline, culminating in a performance/portfolio of written work, as well as tools to take a funny idea from concept to completion.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Storytelling for the Screen
courses.prereq_text: Consent of instructor, writing sample, upper-division standing.
courses.description: Part one of a two-part program. Aimed at students who already have basic screenwriting strengths, and are in the intermediate-to-advanced skill range. While focus will depend on the writer-in-residence, the course will include sessions in plot and structure, character and dialogue, tension and conflict, tone and symbolism, and revision strategies.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Writing for Television
courses.comments: Students are required to submit a writing sample.
courses.description: Introduction to fundamentals of writing for television including: the situation comedy, the hour-long drama, the MOW, the miniseries, and children's programming. Investigation of the practical and creative tools necessary for programming. Investigation of the practical and creative tools necessary for navigating successful television scripts.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: The Writers Room
courses.description: A writing-intensive practicum in creative collaboration. Working together, students will develop skills of improvisation, team-ideation, and room-writing to harness the power of diverse perspectives as we conceptualize, develop, and generate scripted material.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Workshop for the Screen
courses.prereq_text: Consent of instructor, writing sample, upper-division standing.
courses.description: Part two of a two-part program. Team workshop structure will allow students to expand their screenwriting skills through a fundamental and intensive story-writing experience, an immersive and craft-focused writing calendar, with access to seasoned writers. Emphasis on multiple rounds of table-readings and group critiques.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Topics in Contemporary Media Theory
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: Topics vary each year and may include such problems as the relation of film and other media to globalization, feminist aesthetics, critical race theories, technologies, algorithms, and the writings of key authors.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Topics in Contemporary Media Theory: Algorithms and Culture
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: In this seminar, students take a critical design approach to analyze various algorithms (i.e., Search, PageRank), their relationship with their structured data (i.e., tweets), and their impact on contemporary infrastructures and social flows.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Alternative Media Futures
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: Topics vary each year and may include such problems as the relation of film and other media to structuralism, semiotics, metaphor/metonymy, point of view, and the writings of Burch, Barthes, Metz, Heath, Bordwell, Willemen, Wollen.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Cozy Games
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: Provides an opportunity to probe deeply into the genre of “cozy” games, which came to prominence during the COVID-19 pandemic with games like Animal Crossing: New Horizons (2020). We consider not only how gentle, wholesome, and domestic games predated the “cozy” label, but also how the moniker “cozy” predates cozy games (for instance, in cozy mysteries). In addition to questioning the typical gender coding of these games and their players, we will read and play extensively in order to think about the genre’s contested boundaries and why its classic themes of comfort, domesticity, and interpersonal relations often dovetail with (implied) violence, nature and the outdoors, and even death.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Topics in Contemporary Media Theory: FemTech Lab
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: FemTech Lab is a theory/practice seminar on feminism, cyberfeminism, and feminist theories of technology. We engage the political potency of feminist media practicethe use of installations, performance, public engagements, and web-based platforms appealing for change or hacking systemic bias.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Invisible Labors: The Past, Present, and Future of Media Technology and Work
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: Explores how media and communications technologies, ranging from the telegraph and early computers to social media platforms and artificial intelligence, have shaped the politics of work and workplace control. Introduces students to theories of race, gender, and work, as well as literature from science and technology studies, the history of technology, and labor studies.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Topics in Contemporary Media Theory: Japanese American Internment Media
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: Explores the role of visual and print media in the WWII incarceration of Japanese Americans through various historical and theoretical perspectives. Topics include the production and remediation of domestic wartime propaganda, race and representation, and public and private memory.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Topics in Contemporary Media Theory: Media and Globalization
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: This theory course explores medias constitutive role in our experiences of globalization. Topics include: accumulation of capital and forms of dispossession; borders and migration; flows and frictions; geographies of displacement; global media conglomerates and piracy; risk and securitization; resource extraction, the commons, and grassroots mobilization.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Media In/Through Iran
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: Explores how Iran's cultural, technological, and political landscape offers generative ways of studying media: their alternative histories, adaptive practices, and subversive circulations. Engaging with an eclectic range of Iranian objects and practices from the nineteenth century to the present, students examine the role of media in forming identity and negotiating power while considering the material conditions that transform communications technologies.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Topics in Contemporary Media Theory – Film & Media and Policing
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: This seminar investigates the relationship between police power and film and media from the late nineteenth century to the present. Students will analyze a range of media including, photography, silent cinema, American and international studio and independent features, avant-garde film, dash cam, body cam, and cell phone footage, and digital technologies that employ crime statistics and predictive policing. In addition to film and media theory, students will study theories of criminality, punishment, and abolition.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Sports, Media and Modernity
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: Explores the relationship between sport, media, and modernity through two critical lenses: first, how sport acts as a cultural apparatus mediating institutions, collective identities, and power structures of modern societies; second, how evolving media technologies (from print cultures to data-driven platforms) transform how sport is staged, performed, and experienced today. Thinking through the topics of colonialism, nationalism, race, gender, technology, and spectatorship, students examine how sport both expresses and structures the cultural dynamics of modern life.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Occult Media
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: In this seminar, we will contend with definitions of media and how they interface with the occult. Throughout the quarter, students will conduct archival research, learn about media archaeology, and discover occult media in its many forms, including horror films, online folklore, divination tools, Ouija boards, tabloid reports of the Satanic Panic, magic lantern shows, spiritualist and countercultural periodicals, optical toys, podcast episodes, popular music, religious technology like Scientology’s E-Meter, and more. Each student will be guided through a personalized archival research project that includes a trip to special collections at UCSB Library.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Plant Humanities
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: In a world dominated by humans and other animals, plants have become an unlikely but productive focus of academic attention. Scientists and humanists are unearthing neglected aspects of plant life and being in everything from digital design and fire suppression to philosophy, history, literature, food, culture, and archives. Our class explores what thinking through and with plants offers to film and media studies, but will also draw on botany, feminist science and technology studies, and work on indigeneity, colonialism, and extraction.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Race and/in AI
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: Critical work on artificial intelligence has, by now, revealed it as an intense tool of surveillance, policing, and racialization. This work has demonstrated the vastly unequal distributions of the political effects of race; however, this work has also demonstrated alternative practices, both current and speculative, with, alongside, and/or against AI. This course traces these diverse accounts of race and/in AI with the goal of answering the following three questions: What, when, and where is race in AI?

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Topics in Contemporary Media Theory: Sound, Media, and Society
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: Builds conceptual and analytical tools for a critical understanding of sound, media, and auditory cultures. Special attention is paid to how social and historical factors inform sound media and how sound media, in turn, inform cultural perceptions and practices.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Software and Society
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: If “data is the new oil”—a phrase often championed by venture capitalists, Big Tech advocates, and engineers—then software might be likened to refineries that transform raw data into commodities, video games, and social media platforms. But what exactly is software, and how does it interact with social, political, and cultural forces? This course explores these questions by tracing software's history from the mid-20th century to today’s Artificial Intelligence systems. We will examine primary and secondary sources to understand software’s role in everything from surveillance and warfare to art and finance. Our central goal will be to develop our understanding of how, as one popular commentary puts it, “software is eating the world.”

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Television Studies - Technologies, Theories, and Methods
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: This advanced seminar functions as an intro to TV Studies thru an analysis of the key developments, formats, genres, &infrastructures of the televisual medium. As a medium w/ continually shifting meanings&in relation to an ever-changing landscape of technologies, examining TV in a global context offers a chance to think thru the cultural, political, aesthetic, &technological structures which function on the level of region&intersect w/ transnational &global media trends. Drawing from infrastructural studies, globalization studies, cultural studies,&media industry approaches, this class will provide a critical examination of the history &structures of TV, as well as the discipline of TV Studies thru an interdisciplinary&intersectional lens

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Topics in Contemporary Media Theory: The Wire: TV in Focus
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: Examines HBOs crime drama television series, The Wire (2002-2008). Discusses the series through critical, historical, and theoretical approaches from fields like urban studies and television studies. Students work on projects related to city media of their choice.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Studies in Film, Media and the Other Arts
courses.prereq_text: Film Studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided the letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: An analysis of film and other media in relation to literary and plastic arts such as photography, architecture, and the novel. Topics vary.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Studies in Film, Media and the Other Arts:  Anti-War Media
courses.prereq_text: Film Studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided the letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: In this seminar, we focus on global and local oppositional media and crafts practices that seek to prevent, stop, and undermine the death-making of war, offering ways to sustain life for civilians, heal the survivors, and commemorate the dead: From memoirs and photographs to zines and social media, from carpets and cooking recipes to apps and video games. By Interrogating warfare through anti-war media, we closely engage with the ethics of witnessing, limits of representation, and militarization of everyday life. Simultaneously, by studying media through anti-war frameworks we consider less-discussed aspects, kinds, and practices of media such as failure and repair, handmade and low-tech, and tactical and communal.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Studies in Film, Media and the Other Arts
courses.prereq_text: Film Studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: An analysis of film and other media in relation to literary and plastic arts such as photography, architecture, and the novel. Topics vary.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Women, Work, and Gambling
courses.prereq_text: Film Studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided the letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: This rigorous, interdisciplinary seminar examines contemporary gaming, gambling, and digital media platforms. In this course we ask: How are entertainment and work shaped by capitalism and mediated by digital platforms? Who works and plays on digital platforms? How does digital media change, distort, warp, or adapt our work lives and leisure time? Drawing from texts in feminist studies, history, sociology, critical theory, gaming and gambling studies, political economy, and film theory, students will develop a high-quality, well-argued, original final paper throughout the quarter. Students will closely engage with course texts and fellow classmates’ written work in writing workshops.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Topics in Film and Media Theory
courses.prereq_text: Film and Media 96 with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Addresses film, television and/or digital media from a variety of theoretical perspectives; topics will vary depending on instructor. Critical analytical papers will be required. Emphases have included classical, contemporary and comparative theories of film and media.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Topics in Film and Media Theory: Cultural Thory
courses.prereq_text: Film and Media 96 with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: This course introduces students to theoretical approaches and frameworks that are crucial to understanding our social and cultural contemporaneity. Topics include ideology and social determination; knowledge and power; history, memory, and trauma; postcolonial/decolonial critique; neoliberal globalization; biopolitics; risk and precarity.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Topics in Film and Media Theory: Digital Theory
courses.prereq_text: Film and Media 96 with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Histories and theories of digital media and their users, from early computers and networks to video games and selfies. Approaches include comparative media analysis, cultural studies, science and technology studies, software/platform studies, and environmental media critique.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Theories of Filmgoing and Mass Culture
courses.prereq_text: Film and Media 96 with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: In our age of online streaming platforms, diminishing theatrical ticket sales, and individual media devices, one may reasonably ask: what is the value of filmgoing in a space shared with others? This course will help us consider this pressing question by engaging past and present theories of cinema’s effect on landscapes of mass culture. Beginning with film photography at the cusp of modernity, before tracing positive and negative appraisals of cinema’s ideological power, we will ultimately consider arguments for why public filmgoing should matter: insofar as collective viewership may challenge insufficient assumptions, open up newfound ethical possibilities, and incite astonishing alternatives to the status quo.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Topics in Film and Media Theory
courses.prereq_text: Film and Media 96 with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Addresses film, television and/or digital media from a variety of theoretical perspectives; topics will vary depending on instructor. Critical analytical papers will be required. Emphases have included classical, contemporary and comparative theories of film and media.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Genre Theory
courses.prereq_text: Film and Media 96 with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Examines the study of film genres through a theoretical lens. Topics include semiotic, structuralist, psychoanalytic, and phenomenological theories of the musical, the horror film, melodrama, and the concept of genre itself.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Topics in Film and Media Theory: Popular Music and Youth Culture
courses.prereq_text: Film and Media 96 with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Explores the social history and cultural politics of popular music and youth culture, with an emphasis on the relations between musical meaning, technological mediation, cultural value, and social power.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: The Carsey-Wolf Center Practicum: Contemporary Programming, Distribution, and Exhibition.
courses.prereq_text: Film Studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
courses.description: This course will use the Pollock Theater and its programming as a laboratory for studying contemporary programming and exhibition practices. Topics under consideration will include media distribution and exhibition contexts, constructing programming series and conducting interviews with guests, and the way contemporary tastes are shaped through algorithms and curation practices. Students will have opportunities to gain hands-on experience with camera equipment. Regular attendance at Carsey-Wolf Center events in the Pollock Theater will be required.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Focus Media Journal
courses.comments: Not for credit in the global major.
courses.description: For members of the editorial board of the Focus Media Journal at UCSB. UCSB Focus Media Journal is an annual scholarly journal issued every spring quarter. As a literary publication for the Film and Media Studies Department, the journal’s goal is to engage students from all disciplines, with a focus on media forms.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Internship in Film/Television
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters.
courses.description: An opportunity for training, career sampling, and contacts in the film or television industry. Required are approximately 100 hours of work a quarter, a final five-page report, and a supervisor's letter of verification.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Independent Studies
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division courses in film studies; consent of instructor and department.
courses.comments: Students must have a 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
courses.description: Selected research under the direction of a faculty member.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Independent Research Assistance in Film Studies
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division courses in film studies; consent of instructor and department.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
courses.description: Course work shall consist of faculty supervised research assistance.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Critical Analysis and Method
courses.description: Seminar examining a range of methodologies and critical approaches to the study of film and media, with the specific topics chosen by the instructor.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Special Topics in Film Analysis
courses.description: Close examination of an element of film style - such as sound, color, or camera movement - and its impact on interpretation.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: National Cinemas
courses.description: Close analysis of theories of nation, nationalism, and national cinema, with a focus on the contentious relations between culture, history, media capital and the state. Topics include evolving genres, styles, movements and institutions; local lifeworlds and cultural difference within a post-national context; and the spectral nature of contemporary national formations.Offered concurrently with Film Studies 187AA-ZZ.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Philosophy of Film History
courses.description: Studies works and concepts in the philosophy of history that have informed the researching and writing of film and media history. Will also consider the ways in which film and media texts have extended debates and concepts of historiographic practice.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Media Historiographies
courses.description: Comparative analysis of various historical accounts of cinema, television, and digital media that have shaped the field of film and media studies. Emphasis on issues and debates that have dominated efforts to write rigorous, methodologically explicit histories of different media.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Special Topics in Film and Media History
courses.description: Close examination of a topic in film and/or media history.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Special Topics in Film and Media History: Global Film Exhibition
courses.description: Examines the industrial, social, cultural, and racial practices employed in theatrical and non-theatrical exhibition venues around the world and the local, national, and transnational film cultures developed around moviegoing and other consumption activities related to cinema.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Special Topics in Film and Media History: Revisiting Weimar Culture
courses.description: This course explores the art, politics and culture of the Weimar Republic, the period between the defeat of Germany in World War I and Hitler’s rise to power in 1933. It focuses on film and visual culture, with attention to questions of gender, sexuality, and class. It examines questions of history and historiography as well as the work of theorists who proposed new ways of thinking about art, popular culture, and technological innovation that remain resonant today.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Film Theory
courses.description: Examines the history and rhetoric of thinking about the ontology, epistemology, ideology, and aesthetics of film.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Television and Digital Media Theory
courses.description: Explores important theoretical writings concerning electronic and digital media. Course readings define the unique properties of these mediums, consider their ontological status, and discuss how they differ from one another and other cultural forms.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Special Topics in Film and Media Theory
courses.description: Close examination of a topic in film and/or media theory.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Adaptation Theory
courses.description: This graduate seminar examines key theoretical concepts in adaptation studies. Focusing on literature-to-film adaptation, FAMST 242AT takes a long-historical, diachronic approach to adaptation theory, engaging with classical and early modern thinking about imitatio as well as with contemporary theoretical arguments in the subject.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Cloud Infrastructure: Pipelines, Platforms, and Data
courses.description: This course examines cloud infrastructure in the form of Internet pipelines, digital platforms, and data. We look at the various histories, forms of governance, and impact of these sociotechnical systems on digital civil liberties and cultural formations of access, truth, privacy, and free speech. Studying this array of infrastructural affordances and their development also allows us to look at values of de/centralization, privatization, scarcity and abundance, competition, networks, and public utility in relation to the concept of being in the cloud. We will embrace a humanistic and historical perspective but we will also rely on interdisciplinary materials and methods throughout the course.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Computing Power: Computation and Society from Babbage to Bitcoin
courses.description: Examines the historical and contemporary relationship between computing and social power. Students learn about influential historiographical and theoretical developments within social studies of computing, including recent intersections with the study of race, sexuality and gender, and global capitalism.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Game Studies
courses.description: Provides a general, graduate-level introduction to the academic field of game studies, ideal for students working on interactive digital media objects or platforms and/or cultures of play. We will discuss select foundational texts in order to consider the field’s initially contested relationship to literary and film studies and turn-of-the-century new media theory. We will also examine a plethora of recent work that simultaneously expands and critiques canonical game studies through the lenses of the analog, race, queer theory, feminism, ecology, affect, historical preservation, and labor. Students will be encouraged to read and play, and to consider research, presentation, and pedagogical methods specific to this field.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Special Topics in Film and Media Theory
courses.description: Close examination of a topic in film and/or media theory.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Media and Policing
courses.description: An examination of the relationship between police power and modern image-making technologies from a variety of critical historiographical and theoretical perspectives. We will trace a genealogy of the present by putting eighteenth- and nineteenth-century methodologies and visual culture in conversation with new research methods and media. Topics to be discussed include: the production of criminality, physiognomy and phrenology, carceral geography, crime statistics and predictive policing, carceral aesthetics, counter forensics, and abolition. Course readings will be discussed in relation to screenings and close study of artifacts and technologies that operate at the intersection of policing and media.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Special Topics in Film and Media Theory: Science and Technology Studies
courses.description: Introduces theories and methods in science and technology studies. Students learn about scholars, texts, and schools of thought that have shaped this interdisciplinary field, as well as more recent intersections with gender/sexuality, race, indigeneity, media, medicine, and the environment.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Special Topics in Critical Thinkers
courses.description: Explores in depth the work of one particular thinker relevant to the field of media and cultural studies, for example, Freud, Barthes, Benjamin, and others.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Cultural Theory
courses.description: Explores key ideas, issues, and developments in cultural studies and critical theory through close readings of primary texts. Possible approaches include the Frankfurt School, the Birmingham School, Freudianism/Lacanianism, semiotics/structuralism, and postmodernism/post-structuralism.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Special Topics in Cultural Studies
courses.description: Close examination of a topic in cultural studies.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Special Topics in Cultural Studies
courses.description: Close examination of a topic in cultural studies.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Special Topics in Cultural Studies
courses.description: Close examination of a topic in cultural studies.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Sound and Aurality
courses.description: Explores the interdisciplinary field of sound studies from a variety of critical historiographical and theoretical perspectives. Topics include architectural acoustics, eco-sonic media, vibrational ontologies, sound-reproduction technologies, noise and feedback, sonic warfare, aurality and modern rationality.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Special Topics in Film and/or Media Globalization
courses.description: Close examination of a topic in globalization of film and/or media.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Global Hollywood
courses.description: Close examination of a topic in globalization of film and/or media.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Creative-Critical Praxis
courses.description: This graduate seminar explores the use of creative, artistic, and experimental methods in the production of interdisciplinary scholarly research through the examination of a variety of creative-critical modes, including filmmaking, game design, critical cartography, poetic practice, speculative non-fiction, and art curation.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Media Techniques of Wonder
courses.comments: Comparative Literature 280 and Film Studies 280 are the same course.
courses.description: Media Techniques of Wonder is focused on themes of media archaeology and their emergent literary context. The exchange between literature and media techniques serves as the focus, with literary texts creating a basis for real and imagined media technologies that radically reshape literary practices. Historical devices will serve as a basis along with visits to media collections.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Dissertation Development
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different. No credit allowed toward advanced degrees.
courses.description: Provides guidance, training, a forum, and a common center for various research endeavors.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Preparation for Dissertation Prospectus
courses.prereq_text: To be taken prior to the qualifying exam.
courses.description: Preparation for the Ph.D. qualifying exam and writing of the dissertation prospectus.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Teaching Assistant Practicum
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit.
courses.description: Designed to accommodate graduate students who serve as teaching assistants. Includes analyses of texts and materials, discussion section teaching techniques, formulation of topics and questions for papers and examinations, and grading papers and examinations under instructor supervision.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Programming and Curation Practicum
courses.comments: Graduate students from any department are eligible to enroll in 1 or 2 units. For elective credit toward the Film and Media Studies PhD, students must register for 2 units in each of the two terms.
courses.description: Examines issues related to curation, including the construction of canons, cultural value, and economies of prestige. Students work with the CWC director in curating programs for the Pollock Theater and related research events. Class discusses readings, screen media, research potential guests, writes questions for Q&A sessions with invited guests, and writes program notes for the CWCs website and Pollock programs. Students register for one unit per quarter. If taken for elective credit toward the Film and Media Studies PhD, it must be taken for two terms in a row, two units in each of the two terms.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Special Topics in Film and Media
courses.description: A seminar on research subjects of current interest.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Group Studies
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different. No credit allowed toward advanced degrees.
courses.description: Provides guidance, training, a forum, and a common center for various research endeavors.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Group Studies
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different. No credit allowed toward advanced degrees.
courses.description: Provides guidance, training, a forum, and a common center for various research endeavors.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Directed Reading and Research
courses.description: Individual tutorial.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: MA Orals and PhD Exam Preparation
courses.comments: No unit credit allowed toward advanced degree.
courses.description: Master's Oral Exam and PhD Qualifying Exam preparation.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Preparation for Dissertation Prospectus
courses.prereq_text: To be taken prior to the qualifying exam.
courses.description: Preparation for the Ph.D. qualifying exam and writing of the dissertation prospectus.

courses.subject: FAMST
courses.title: Dissertation Research and Writing
courses.description: Only for the research and writing of dissertation. Instructor should be chair of the student's doctoral committee.

courses.subject: FAMSTW
courses.title: Hollywood Anatomy of an Industry: Television Narrative Form and Style
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 6 units.
courses.description: This course functions as a hybrid production studies and critical studies class. The course asks a central question: How is narrative and stylistic meaning produced in television, and how should we evaluate the evidentiary value of what creatives say about their own work? Using a sustained case study, this course closely studies television narrative form and the process of narration by studying the contributions of component departments within a coordinated system of creative decision-making.

courses.subject: FAMSTW
courses.title: Fairy Tale Cinema
courses.description: Online course that addresses a number of fairy tales & related films. It examines the ways in which tales of wonder provide a metaphoric context for human adaptation and interpretation. Fairy tales evoke themes of childhood, development, & home, as well as critical methods including structuralism and psychoanalysis. Through a focus on films, presented weekly for screening, along w/ relevant descriptive, theoretical, & literary texts, we take a critical approach to fairy tales. You will be required to respond to writing prompts related to a weekly screening, write weekly forums along w/ a midterm & final for the course. Your active participation in the course activities & attendance for the synchronous portions of the course are essential.

courses.subject: FEMST
courses.title: Gender and Power: Introduction to Feminist Studies
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Feminist Studies 20H.
courses.description: Introduction to central concepts and issues in feminist studies from the perspective of the social sciences. Explores the construction of gender and sexuality and the lives of diverse groups of women in the contemporary U.S. within a global context.

courses.subject: FEMST
courses.title: Women, Development and Globalization
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Feminist Studies 30H.
courses.description: Examines the impact of development policy and globalization on women's lives. Emphasis is placed on women's activism and feminist critiques of neo-liberal measures intended to rid the third world of poverty.

courses.subject: FEMST
courses.title: Women, Representation, and Cultural Production
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Feminist Studies 40H.
courses.description: Examines cultural representations of diverse women's lives from a humanities perspective. The focus is on women as cultural producers, subjects, and critics in literature, film, the visual arts, and music. Includes mandatory weekly film screening.

courses.subject: FEMST
courses.title: Global Feminisms and Social Justice
courses.description: Historical and contemporary examination of women's activism around the globe in a variety of struggles, including self-named feminist movements and other movements for social justice.

courses.subject: FEMST
courses.title: Women of Color: Race, Class, and Ethnicity
courses.description: Examination of the interlocking dynamics and politics of gender, race, sexuality, class, and culture in the experience of U.S. women of color. Readings focus on oppositional consciousness and resistance to oppression in the scholarship and literature by women of color.

courses.subject: FEMST
courses.title: Misogyny, Violence, and UCSB
courses.description: Uses UCSB and Isla Vista as a case study for examining the persistence of misogyny and patriarchal violence in the 21st century.

courses.subject: FEMST
courses.title: Introduction to LGBTQ Studies
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Feminist Studies 80H or Women's Studies 80H.
courses.description: An overview of the interdisciplinary field of lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and queer studies, including historical and cross-cultural perspectives on same-sex sexuality, queer theory, intersectionality, gender and sexual identities, communities, culture, contemporary social policy, and LGBTQ movements.

courses.subject: FEMST
courses.title: Independent Studies
courses.prereq_text: One 1-4 unit Feminist Studies lower division course; consent of instructor and department chair.
courses.comments: Students must have a 3.0 GPA for preceding 3 quarters. May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units. Students limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in 98/99/198/199/199AA combined.
courses.description: Research under the direction of a faculty member. Students are offered an opportunity to conduct independent or collaborative research or to act as interns for faculty-directed research projects.

courses.subject: FEMST
courses.title: Teaching 4 Social Justice
courses.prereq_text: At least one course in one of these departments: Asian American Studies, Black Studies, Chicana/o Studies, Feminist Studies
courses.comments: AS AM 101C, BL ST 101C, CH ST 101C, and FEMST 101C are cross-listed.
courses.description: This interdisciplinary course will highlight how a curriculum focusing on racial, ethnic, gender, and LGBTQ studies is central to teaching and learning within diverse societal contexts. This grounding is essential for K-12 teachers in History and English/Literature. Through a social justice framework, students will learn how classrooms are enhanced by Ethnic and Feminist Studies, placing graduates within the forefront of educational initiatives that position teaching and learning within an inclusive and equitable paradigm.

courses.subject: FEMST
courses.title: Women's Labors
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Women's Studies 120 or Feminist Studies 186EB. Letter grade required for majors and minors.
courses.description: What is women's work? How has it changed over time? How is it valued? Explores wage-earning, caregiving, sex work, housework, double days, glass ceilings, and strategies of survival and resistance among American women from various demographic, racial, and ethnic groups.

courses.subject: FEMST
courses.title: Feminisms
courses.description: Special topics course focused on key feminist issues, histories of feminist knowledge, and social justice movements.

courses.subject: FEMST
courses.title: Critical Heterosexuality Studies
courses.description: Critically examines the origins and evolution of heterosexuality as a sexological category. Draws on queer theory to analyze heterosexuality as a contested sexual, cultural, racial, and political institution.

courses.subject: FEMST
courses.title: Witches, Nature, and Decolonial Healing
courses.description: Examines the broad range of gendered and racialized practices associated with witchcraft, including medicine, political revolt, environmental preservation, and trauma healing. Focus is on colonization and other global transformations, both historical and contemporary, that influence anti-witch violence and feminist resistance.

courses.subject: FEMST
courses.title: Feminist Perspectives on Health
courses.comments: FEMST 130 and ESS 129 are the same course. Letter grade required for majors and minors.
courses.description: Investigation of the power that medicine has in shaping health experts' and lay individuals' understandings of health and health practices. Particular attention is paid to how women's health issues come to be seen as "social problems", past and present.

courses.subject: FEMST
courses.title: The Politics of Reproduction and Reproductive Technologies
courses.comments: Letter grade required for majors and minors.
courses.description: Exploration of theoretical, popular, and political debates over reproductive technologies in terms of women's power and choices. Investigation of how cultural and historical changes in reproductive practices influence ideas about nature, society, and progress. Examination of case studies on current controversies.

courses.subject: FEMST
courses.title: Bodies
courses.description: Special topics course focused on bodies, embodiment, politics and performance.

courses.subject: FEMST
courses.title: Introduction to Critical Disability Studies
courses.description: We examine historical, socio-cultural, and political meanings of disability through essays, literature, film, and media. We ask what is normal, how does ableism shape our lives, what is disability justice, and how is disability entangled with race and gender.

courses.subject: FEMST
courses.title: Cultural Analysis of Reproduction and Science
courses.description: Develop tools to analyze cultural productions, narratives, images, and arguments about women, gender, reproduction, and science. Topics may vary.

courses.subject: FEMST
courses.title: Participatory Research, Community Organizing, and Popular Education
courses.description: Considers models for good social science research and how such research can support community organizing for social justice. Examines reports emerging from such research, documentation of campaigns facilitated by research, and popular education making research more widely accessible.

courses.subject: FEMST
courses.title: Fat Studies
courses.description: Examines the social experience of people living in fat bodies. This course specifically focus on how these experiences are further shaped by institutions like science and medicine, race, gender, sexuality, ability and more.

courses.subject: FEMST
courses.title: Black Women Filmmakers
courses.description: An opportunity to view films (animation, documentary, experimental and narrative), examine the specifics of media production, compare the various works produced by black women, and acquire the skills necessary for media criticism.

courses.subject: FEMST
courses.title: Representation and Activism
courses.comments: Letter grade required for majors and minors.
courses.description: Exploration of the strategies by which social groups resist systems of oppression through readings and works from independent filmmakers.

courses.subject: FEMST
courses.title: Women of Color Resisting Violence
courses.comments: Letter grade required for majors and minors.
courses.description: This is a study of women of color and other marginalized women's experiences of psychological, sexual, physical, social, economic and legal violence, and the personal and collective resistance to these forms of violence in intimate relationships and in broader society.

courses.subject: FEMST
courses.title: Sex, Love, and Romance
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Feminist Studies 150H.
courses.description: An examination from historical and global perspectives of sex, love, desire, and intimate relationships in diverse cultures in the contemporary U.S.

courses.subject: FEMST
courses.title: Sexual Cultures
courses.comments: Letter grade required for majors and minors. May be repeated provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Seminars focus on the political, social, and cultural dynamics of sexuality in modern society. Offerings may explore sexual representations, economies, laws, identities, performances, literatures, technologies, relationships, communities, and customs in the United States or abroad. Topics may vary.
