courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Protein Engineering and Design
courses.description: Rational design of protein structure, activity, and stability. Current methods and applications of protein engineering including protein evolution, unnatural amino acids, and combinatorial methods.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Post-translational Protein Processing
courses.description: Structure/function relationships in interesting macromolecules isolated from marine organisms. Focus is on well-characterized pathways from horseshoe crabs, abalones, mussels, and fish as well as others.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Biochemical Techniques
courses.prereq_text: One year of undergraduate biochemistry (e.g., MCDB 108A-B-C) or equivalent.
courses.description: Practical theory and application of basic biochemical techniques. Topics include SDS-PAGE, buffers, centrifugation, antibody methods, spectroscopy and fluorescence techniques.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Strategies in Protein Characterization
courses.prereq_text: A grade of B- or better in MCDB 108A or 208A, or the equivalent.
courses.description: A presentation of traditional and state-of-the-art approaches for characterizing the primary structure of proteins and polysaccharides. Techniques to be included are amino acid analysis, mass spectrometry, gas-phase sequencing, capillary electrophoresis, and covalent modification chemistry.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Introduction to Machine Learning  for Processing of Biological Images and Structural Biology
courses.comments: IQB 206 and BIOE 244 are the same course
courses.description: Provides a general introduction to modern Machine Learning techniques with a focus on neural networks with relevance for biological image processing and structural biology applications across scales from the atomic level to organisms. Introductions to relevant concepts in biological image processing and structural biology will be part of the curriculum as well.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Enzyme Mechanisms
courses.description: Chemical mechanisms of enzyme catalysis. Enzyme models and non-classical enzymes. Theory, experimental design, and data analysis.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Quantitative Biosciences iQB2 Techniques and Theory
courses.description: An intensive laboratory course for physical science and engineering students providing background knowledge and laboratory experience in standard molecular biology and protein purification techniques, as well as techniques for characterizing purified proteins.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Quantitative Biosciences iQB2 Laboratory Course
courses.prereq_text: For first-year IPQB (formerly BMSE) graduate students only. Grad students from other programs will be considered but they should seek for the approval of the teaching coordinators. Number of participants will be limited to 12 or the number of first-year IPQB (formerly BMSE) students, whichever is smaller.
courses.comments: Formerly offered as IQB 224
courses.description: This hands-on research course integrates investigation of diverse biological phenomena in the lab with quantitative analysis of hypotheses related to the function of living systems. Analysis across different length scales and levels of complexity invokes a synergistic combination of tool building, quantitative data acquisition, complementary theoretical model building. Students work in subgroups on modules developed by different IQB faculty to illustrate current research topic in Quantitative Biology.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Biophysical Thermodynamics
courses.prereq_text: Undergraduate course in Physical Chemistry (e.g., Chem 113A-B-C).
courses.description: An overview of those parts of chemical thermodynamics relevant to the study of biomolecules and biological systems. Topics include fundamental biopolymer structure formation.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Diffraction of Biological Molecules
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 108A-B-C; and, Chemistry 113A or 142A or 142B or 142C.
courses.description: Single-crystal macromolecular crystallography methods; crystal growth, geometric and physical basis of diffraction, approaches to phasing and refinement. Xray and neutron solution scattering.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Electrostatics of Biopolymers
courses.prereq_text: Knowledge of elementary ideas and methods of electrostatics and statisticalmechanics.
courses.description: Electrostatics of highly charged sufaces in contact with a polar solvent with application to biopolymers (e.g., DNA, f-actin).

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Methods and Logic in Molecular Cell Biology I
courses.comments: Required for MCDB Graduate students.
courses.description: Molecular genetics and gene regulation. Experimental design and approaches, and a focus on critical thinking and problem solving, will reveal how fundamental, highly significant biological problems are unraveled using molecular genetic strategies. Reading will be assigned from a mix of classic and current peer-reviewed papers.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Methods and Logic in Molecular Cell Biology II
courses.comments: Required for MCDB Graduate students.
courses.description: Molecular cellular biology in a variety of model systems and contexts from an integrated perspective. A collection of approaches, and a focus on critical thinking and problem solving, will reveal how highly significant biological problems are unraveled using cutting edge technologies. Includes an introduction to bioinformatics, computational, and systems biology. Reading will be assigned from a mix of classic and current peer-reviewed papers.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Basic Microscopy for Quantitative Biology
courses.prereq_text: Course is limited to 10 students, preference is given to students with interest in applying microscopy methods in their own research.
courses.description: Fluorescence live imaging is a powerful tool to study dynamics of living matter. This course provides an overview on geometric & Fourier optics, bright field microscopy, and fluorescence & absorption spectroscopy. Practicing these concepts students will construct a light-sheet microscope.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Chromosomes and Cell Cycle
courses.description: Structure and organization of the nucleus, Chromatin and chromosome structure, organization, and function; DNA replication and replication origins; Eukaryotic cell cycle regulation.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Cell Biology - Cytoskeleton & Membrane Trafficking
courses.description: Structure and function of the eukaryotic cytoskeleton. Intracellular protein transport and membrane trafficking.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: From RNA to Membranes
courses.description: Structure and dynamics of biological membranes and membrane proteins, protein translocation and sorting in the endomembrane system of eukaryotic cells, extracellular matrix protein structure/function, cell-matrix and cell-cell interactions, cell adhesion receptors, transmembrane signaling by cell adhesion receptors.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Colloids and Interfaces I
courses.comments: Same course as Materials 222A and Chemical Engineering 222A.
courses.description: Introduction to the various intermolecular interactions in solution and in colloidal systems: Van der Waals, electrostatic, hydrophobic, solvation, H-bonding. Introduction to colloidal systems.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Colloids and Interfaces II
courses.comments: Materials 222A or Chemical Engineering 222A recommended. Same course as Materials 222B or Chemical Engineering 222B.
courses.description: Continuation of 222A. Interparticle interactions, coagulation, DLVO theory, steric interactions, polymer-coated surfaces, polymers in solution, thin film viscosity. Surfactant and lipid self-assembly: micelles,microemulsions. Surfaces: wetting, contact angles, surface tension. Surfactants on surfaces: langmuir-blodgett films, adsorption, adhesion. Non-equilibrium and dynamic interactions.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Signal Transduction
courses.description: A cell's growth is controlled by positive and negative cues from its surroundings. A discussion of the cell's signaling mechanisms that recognize these cues and initiate and intracellular set of events that generates a response.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Quantitative Biology iQB2 Laboratory Course
courses.prereq_text: For first-year BMSE graduate students only. Grad students from other programs will be considered but they should seek for the approval of the teaching coordinators. Number of participants will be limited to 12 or the number of first-year BMSE students, whichever is smaller.
courses.description: This hands-on research course will integrate investigation of diverse biological phenomena in the lab with quantitative analysis of hypotheses related to the function of living systems. Analysis across different length scales and levels of complexity invokes a synergistic combination of tool building, quantitative data acquisition, complementary theoretical model building. Students will work in subgroups on modules developed by different BMSE faculty to illustrate current research topic in Quantitative Biology.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Development
courses.description: The molecular mechanisms of pattern formation and cellular differentiation that underline developmental processes in a variety of important model systems.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Signal Transduction and Development in Multicellular Systems
courses.comments: IQB 226 and MCDB 224 are the same course.
courses.description: Cellular and organismal growth and other responses are controlled by positive and negative cues from both internal and external sources. We discuss the signaling mechanisms that recognize these cues and initiate an intracellular set of events that generates a response. We also discuss the molecular mechanisms of pattern formation and cellular differentiation that underlie developmental processes in a variety of important multicellular model systems.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Protein Biochemistry
courses.comments: Same course as MCDB 229.
courses.description: Discussion topics relevant to structure-function relationships in proteins including the chemical reactivity of amino acid side chains, posttranslational modifications, and the covalent and noncovalent interactions of multimeric structures. Case studies involve recent advances in structure-function relationships of mechanoproteins.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Gene Regulation
courses.description: Mechanisms and regulation of transcription and translation in prokaryotic and eukaryotic organisms and their viruses.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Bacterial Pathogenesis
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 228.
courses.description: The mechanisms by which bacterial pathogens cause disease. Investigation of the bacterial gene products produced during infection to understand the metabolic, physiological, and genetic factors that contribute to the virulence of bacterial pathogens.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Cell Biology
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A-AL or MCDB 1B-BL or EEMB 2-2L, or equivalents, or consent of instructor
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 237.
courses.description: Introduction to the structure and function of cell organelles: membranes, nucleus, mitochondria, chloroplasts, endoplasmic reticulum, golgi apparatus, lysosomes, microbodies, microtubules, cilia, centrioles, and microfilaments.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Experimental Strategies in Molecular Genetics
courses.description: Discussion of experimental strategies used to purify, analyze, and manipulate nucleic acids, isolate molecular clones from complex genomes, physically map genomes, analyze gene expression, and perform reverse genetics.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Soft Matter Physics
courses.comments: IQB 238 and Physics 238 are the same course.
courses.description: A physics-based approach to study the structure, assembly and dynamical properties of a variety of soft materials, such as simple and complex fluids, colloidal systems, liquid crystals, polymers, granular matter and gels, including biological examples. Topics covered will include elasticity, viscosity and viscoelasticity, capillarity and wetting, phases and phase diagrams of soft materials, entropy-driven phase transitions, Brownian motion and active matter.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Physical Biology of the Cell
courses.comments: PHYS 239 and IQB 239 are the same course.
courses.description: The role of physics in biology through quantitative measurements and modeling, the organization of a cell, and exemplary quantitative results of biological model systems. The physics of biologically relevant macromolecules, including DNA, RNA and mechanisms of transcription and translation; introduction to protein folding and the role of electrostatics in biology. The physics of the cytoskeleton including beam theory, persistence length, molecular motors, instrumentation used to characterize motor properties, as well as the role of active stresses in cell biology. If time permits, a brief introduction to cell motility and the structure of epithelial tissue.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Informational Macro- and Supra-Molecules
courses.comments: Same course as Chemistry 244.
courses.description: Selected topics at the interface of chemistry and biology; informational molecular coding, molecular machines, self-assembling and self-replicating molecular systems, evolution and selection of molecules with binding and catalytic properties, biopolymer-based materials, special emphasis on cutting-edge technologies.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Computational Biochemistry
courses.comments: CHEM 245 and IQB 245 are the same course.
courses.description: Introduction to molecular modeling and molecular dynamics. Discussion of practical considerations of energy minimization, solvent modeling, structure-based drug design. Practical computer graphics experience.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Membrane Biochemistry
courses.comments: Same course as Chemistry 246.
courses.description: Introduction to the structures and roles of lipids and their behavior, liposomes, membrane proteins and kinetics, protein sorting, and signal transduction.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Quantitative Methods in Biology
courses.description: A review of quantitative methods required to develop models of biological and ecological systems. Topics illustrated through computer exercises.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Practical Statistics for Biologists
courses.description: Introduces fundamental concepts in biostatistics such as sources of technical and biological variation, types of statistical tests (ANOVA, non-parametric, linear regression), sampling techniques, power calculations, and how to decide which test is appropriate.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Bionanotechnology
courses.description: Introduction to macromolecular assemblies and force generation strategies. Topics may also include but are not limited to: conformations and behavior of protein polymers; nucleic acid superstructures and membranes; structure, motility and mechanism of linear and rotary motor proteins; and macromolecular switches.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Biopharmaceutical Process Engineering
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 5A or equivalent; background in biochemistry.
courses.description: An introduction to the design bioprocess for large-scale production of biopharmaceuticals. Emphasis is placed upon biopharmaceutical products, protein expression systems, host cell optimization, and reactor selection and design.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Principles of Bioengineering
courses.description: An overview of various aspects of bioengineering including modeling of physiological functions, biomedical devices, drug delivery, and tissue engineering.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Methods in System Biology
courses.prereq_text: Prior course work in cellular biology, mathematics; consent of instuctor.
courses.comments: Same course as Chemical Engineering 255.
courses.description: Fundamentals of dynamic network organization in biology (genes, metabolites). Emphasis on mathematical approaches to model and analyze complex biophysical network systems. Detailed case studies demonstrating successes of systems biology. Basic biological systems reviewed for nonbiologists.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Stem Cell Biology
courses.comments: Graduate Course. Qualified undergraduate students may petition to enroll with instructor approval.
courses.description: Focuses on the latest developments in stem cell biology, including ongoing clinical trials using stem cell therapies to treat unmet medical needs. In depth analysis of the current literature in stem cell biology, bioengineering and biophysical analyses is also covered. The discipline of stem cell biology and applications of cell therapy have elements of bioengineering, biomaterials, and biophysics.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Special Topics in Biophysics
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided topics are different. Same course as Physics 257.
courses.description: Course varies from year to year according to the currents of the times.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Methods in Mechanobiology and Biofabrication
courses.prereq_text: The course assumes an engineering background but is structured to be accessible to graduate students in life sciences who have a strong physics and math background, and to engineering graduate students with basic biology knowledge.
courses.comments: BIOE 258, IQB 258, and ME 258 are the same course.
courses.description: Cell mechanobiology topics including cell structure, mechanical models, and chemo-mechanical signaling. Review methods for controlling and analyzing the biomechanics of cells using traction force microscopy, AFM, micropatterning, and cell stimulation. Weekly lecture with final project in the form of a research proposal.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Selected Topics in Biological Chemistry
courses.comments: Same course as Chemistry 259. Course may be repeated with a different topic (18 units maximum).
courses.description: Selected topics from bio-organic, biophysical, or biological chemistry. Thecontent of this course will vary.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Research Progress in Biomolecular Science and Engineering
courses.description: Research presentations by postdoctoral fellows and advanced Ph.D. students of research progress in the department.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Literature in Signal Transduction
courses.description: Critical reading and presentation of the literature on signal transduction mechanisms that control cell growth and differentiation.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: BMSE Seminar Discussion Group
courses.description: A weekly seminar discussion group to review, in advance, relevant literature of participating BMSE seminar guests.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Mechanical Force and Biomolecules
courses.description: Explores single-molecule biophysics and the role of mechanical force in biomolecular behavior. Emphasis is placed on modern experimental techniques and the effects of mechanical stress on DNA conformation, protein unfolding, and force-generation by motor proteins. Recent literature is used throughout.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Biomolecular Materials I: Structure and Function
courses.description: Survey of classes of biomolecules (lipids, carbohydrates, proteins, nucleic acids). Structure and function of molecular machines (enzymes for biosynthesis, motors, pumps).

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Biomolecular Materials II: Applications
courses.description: Interactions and self assembly in biomolecular materials. Chemical and drug delivery systems. Tissue engineering. Protein synthesis using recombinant nucleic acid methods: advanced materials development. Nonviral gene therapy.

courses.title: Group Studies
courses.description: Presentation and discussion of current research, to be selected from the following list: A. Biomolecular Materials Synthesis; B. Biomineralization; BP. Bacterial Pathogenesis; CE. C. elegans Development; DN. Developmental Neurobiology; HW. Marine Structural Proteins; PM. Molecular Plant-Microbe Interactions; PR. Protein-Nucleic Acid Interactions; S. Molecular Virology and Interferon Action.

courses.description: Presentation and discussion of current research, to be selected from the following list: PR. Protein-Nucleic Acid Interactions.

courses.title: Group Studies: Molecular Virology and Interferon Action
courses.description: Presentation and discussion of current research, to be selected from the following list: S. Molecular Virology and Interferon Action.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Computational Methods in Biochemistry-Molecular Biology
courses.description: Survey of computational methods in molecular biology. Topics include analysis and presentation of data, database searching, quantitative image analysis, and protein homology modeling. Emphaisis is on utilizing accessible software tools that are designed for non-programmers.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Bioengineering: Career and Development Opportunities at the Interface between Biotechnology and Engineering
courses.comments: Same as MCDB 294B and CH E 294B
courses.description: Based on presentations by experts from the bioengineering industry. Presenters describe their companies' technologies and developments, including biosensors, therapeutics, tissue engineering, quantum dots and advanced instrumentation. Training and educational requirements for different career tracks are discussed.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Laboratory Research Rotation in Biochemistry
courses.prereq_text: Enrollment in the BMSE Ph.D. program; open to first year graduate students only.
courses.comments: May be repeated up to 4 times.
courses.description: Laboratory rotation project in BMSE faculty laboratories.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Biochemistry/Molecular Biology Literature Seminar
courses.description: A critical review of research in selected areas of biochemistry-molecular biology.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Bacterial Genetics
courses.comments: Same course as MCDB 595BG. May be repeated for credit in combination with EEMB 595AA-ZZ to a maximum of 8 units. Individual letter designations may be repeated for credit to a maximum of 4 units.
courses.description: A critical review of research in selected fields of biology.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Directed Reading and Research
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit up to half of the graduate units required for the M.S. degree. Same course as Chemistry 596.
courses.description: Individual tutorial. Instructor is usually the student's major research advisor. Each faculty member has a unique number designation.

courses.subject: IQB
courses.title: Ph.D. Dissertation Preparation
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing as a Ph.D. student and advancement to Doctoral Candidacy.
courses.comments: Instructor should be the chair of the student's doctoral committee.
courses.description: Writing of the Ph.D. dissertation.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Elementary Italian
courses.comments: No credit can be earned if more advanced credit in the language has been awarded. If earned grade of C- or lower in Italian 1HY, then Italian 1 can be used as a legal repeat.
courses.description: Introduction to the most basic elements of Italian grammar. Articles, adjectives, gender. Verbs in the present tense.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Elementary Italian 1 Hybrid
courses.comments: No credit can be earned if more advanced credit in the language has already been awarded. If earned a grade of C- or lower in Italian 1, then Italian 1HY can be used as a legal repeat.
courses.description: Beginning Italian in areas of grammar and basic language skills. Face-to-face classroom contact combined with online work. ITAL 1HY, ITAL 2HY, and ITAL 3HY form a three-course series equivalent to ITAL 1, 2, & 3, Elementary Italian series.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Italian for Spanish Speakers I
courses.prereq_text: 1 year of college Spanish; or 3 years of high school Spanish; or be native or heritage speaker of Spanish.
courses.description: Intensive introductory course sequence on the fundamentals of speaking, reading, writing, and comprehending Italian, with an emphasis on structural similarities between Italian and Spanish. This 2-course sequence covers the first full year of Italian.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Elementary Italian
courses.comments: No credit can be earned if more advanced credit in the language has already been awarded. If earned a grade of C- or lower in Italian 2HY, then Italian 2 can be used as a legal repeat.
courses.description: Logical continuation of Italian 1. Direct and indirect pronouns. Verbs in the past tense and the imperfect. Emphasis on the correct writing and speaking of Italian.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Elementary Italian 2 Hybrid
courses.prereq_text: Completion of Italian 1 or Italian 1HY with a grade of P or a grade of C or higher.
courses.comments: No credit can be earned if more advanced credit in the language has already been awarded. If earned a grade of C- or lower in Italian 2, then Italian 2HY can be used as a legal repeat.
courses.description: Continuation of ITAL 1HY in areas of grammar and basic language skills. Face-to-face classroom contact combined with online work. ITAL 1HY, 2HY, and 3HY form a three-course series equivalent to the ITAL 1, 2, and 3 or ITAL 16A and 16B Elementary Italian series.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Italian for Spanish Speakers II
courses.prereq_text: Italian 16A or Italian 1SP with a grade of P or a grade of C or higher; or ITA1 and ITA2 with one year of college Spanish or 3 years of high school Spanish; or be native or heritage speaker of Spanish.
courses.description: Intensive introductory course sequence on the fundamentals of speaking, reading, writing, and comprehending Italian, with an emphasis on structural similarities between Italian and Spanish. This 2-course sequence covers the first full year of Italian.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Elementary Italian
courses.comments: No credit can be earned if more advanced credit in the language has already been awarded. If earned a grade of C- or lower in Italian 3HY, then Italian 3 can be used as a legal repeat.
courses.description: Continuation of Italian 2. Verbs in the future, conditional. Introduction to subjunctive. Further emphasis on the correct writing and speaking of Italian.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Elementary Italian 3 Hybrid
courses.prereq_text: Completion of Italian 2 or Italian 2HY with a grade of P or a grade of C or higher.
courses.comments: No credit can be earned if more advanced credit in the language has already been awarded. If earned a grade of C- or lower in Italian 3, then Italian 3HY can be used as a legal repeat.
courses.description: Continuation of ITAL 2HY in areas of grammar and basic language skills. Face-to-face classroom contact combined with online work. ITAL 1HY, 2HY, and 3HY form a three-course series equivalent to ITAL 1, 2, and 3 or ITAL 16A and 16B, Elementary Italian series.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Intermediate Italian
courses.description: Intended to develop the linguistic skills of students who have completed the first year. Review of basic grammar structures with emphasis on exceptions, enrichment of vocabulary, reading comprehension, and discussion of modern short stories. In Italian.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Intermediate Italian
courses.description: Increases the students' reading, writing, and speaking skills. Review of more complex grammar structures through written exercises, enrichment of vocabulary, reading comprehension and discussion of contemporary short stories. In Italian.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Intermediate Italian
courses.description: Further develops the students' reading, writing, and speaking skills. Intensive review of the most advanced grammar structures: subjunctive, passive voice, indirect discourse. Reading and discussion of contemporary short stories. In Italian.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Italian Conversation
courses.comments: Not open to native speakers of Italian.
courses.description: Improves comprehension and conversational skills through the discussion of contemporary issues selected by the instructor.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Italian Conversation
courses.comments: Not open to native speakers of Italian.
courses.description: Improves comprehension and conversational skills through the discussion of contemporary issues selected by the instructor.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Italian for Graduate Students
courses.description: A service course for graduate students from other departments who need to satisfy language requirements. Class meets twice weekly. Focus is on grammatical preparation and translation skills, not spoken fluency.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Introduction to Italian Culture
courses.description: A sweeping inquiry into Italian culture, from its origins to its current trends. Exploration of the media, sports, gastronomy, art, music, politics, language, regional and ethnic identity, sexuality, the family, and urban life. Taught in English.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Italy in Film
courses.description: An introduction to the great directors of the Italian cinema including Rossellini, de Sica, Fellini, Visconti, Antonioni, Pasolini, Rosi, and Pontecorvo. Overview of the chief social and aesthetic issues of postwar Europe. Taught in English (films subtitled).

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Advanced Reading and Composition: Italian Culture and Literature
courses.comments: Designed for majors and minors. Non-majors and -minors can enroll with instructor’s consent
courses.description: (Taught in Italian) Focused on literary texts and movies. Students are expected to do oral presentations and write original compositions in Italian.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Advanced Reading and Composition: Medieval and Renaissance Italy
courses.description: (Taught in Italian) Interdisciplinary introduction to Medieval and Renaissance Italian culture, art, and society, through readings, oral presentations, and composition. Advanced grammar topics are coordinated with cultural themes, such as courtly love, the development of Italian city-states, humanism, the role of women, art and artists.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Advanced Communication: Travel, Tourism, and Mobility
courses.comments: Designed for majors and minors. Non-majors and -minors can enroll with Instructor’s consent
courses.description: (Taught in Italian) Focused on the themes of mobility and travel in contemporary Italy. Students will practice both composition and conversation skills through the production of cross-disciplinary and multimedia projects.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Advanced Communication: Business Italian
courses.comments: Designed for majors and minors. Non-majors and -minors can enroll with instructor's consent.
courses.description: (Taught in Italian) Thematically focused on “Made in Italy.” Students will practice written and oral skills through multidisciplinary projects, oral presentations, and discussions.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Advanced Italian Conversation
courses.prereq_text: Italian 5. Concurrent enrollment in Italian 6 or upper-division standing.
courses.description: (Taught in Italian) Discussion of contemporary issues selected by the instructor. Emphasis on idiomatic speech and vocabulary building.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Italian Short Fiction
courses.description: (Taught in Italian) A study of the briefest forms of Italian narrative fiction ranging from the exemplum to the TV script, the short story, and the novella, leading to an exercise in creative writing in Italian.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Dante's Divine Comedy
courses.comments: Same course as Comparative Literature 114
courses.description: (Taught in English) Dante's masterpiece, The Divine Comedy, remains among the most astonishing works of world literature. This course follows the pilgram's progress through Inferno, Pergatorio and Paradiso in search of love that moves the sun and the other stars.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: The Art of Translation
courses.description: (Taught in Italian) An intensive workshop exploring the theory and practice of translation. Students work at translating literary texts from Italian to English and vice versa.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Italian Culture in Translation
courses.description: (Taught in Italian) Focuses on forms of cultural translation between Italy and America. Examples of these translations: American travelers in Italy to nineteenth-century translators of Dante, from emigrant culture to the mafia to the 'spaghetti' western to Italian hip-hop.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Transnational Italian Studies
courses.description: An introduction to transnational identity formation through examples of how both Italians abroad and foreign constructions of Italian-ness have contributed to the formation of Italian culture and identity from the age of the Grand Tour to the present.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Italian Theatre
courses.description: A study of the most important Italian theatrical texts and practices from the Renaissance comedy and the commedia dell'arte to contemporary works for the stage. In English.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Literature in Italian
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 16 units provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: The literatures of Italy do not constitute a single canon but include many overlooked regional, migrant,and postcolonial texts all written in various forms of Italian. Consult the department for specific topics.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Holocaust in Italy
courses.description: Through readings of memoir, fiction, and film, this course investigates the fate of Jews under the Italian Fascists of Benito Mussolini (1922-1945). Topics include Fascism, Communism, anti-Semitism, Italian cooperation with the Nazis, the Catholic Church, the Resistance Movement, deportations and extermination camps, and individual / collective memory after World War II. Students will be exposed to great literary and cinematographic works and through them develop a thorough understanding of this pivotal period in modern Italian history.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Made in Italy
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 16 units provided letter designation is different.
courses.description: (Taught in Italian) An interdisciplinary study of the ways in which representational practices (texts, images, sounds) have affected Italian culture over the ages.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Italy as Destination: Italian Travel Literature
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 16 units provided letter designation is different.
courses.description: Taught in Italian, this course is a study of Italian travel literature within Italy and abroad, from Marco Polo to the present day.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Transnational Italian Culture
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 16 units provided letter designation is different.
courses.description: (Taught in English) A super series of lecture courses taught from an interdisciplinary and transnational perspective, focusing on representational practices (texts, images, sounds) from within and without Italy that have contributed to the formation of Italian identities, and or ideas of Italian-ness over the ages.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Italian Colonialism
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 16 units provided letter designation is different.
courses.description: (Taught in English) A study of Italian colonialism in Africa and the Mediterranean from 1861-1945, including Libya, Rhodes & the Dodecanese, and the Horn of Africa (Eritrea, Somalia, Ethiopia).

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Representing the South
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 16 units provided letter designation is different.
courses.description: (Taught in English) Lecture course on representations of Southern-ness in Italian literature and film culture through the ages.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Gastronomic Italy: Italian Food Culture in Transnational Perspective
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 16 units provided letter designation is different.
courses.description: (Taught in English) Focused on the transnational spread of the Italian Gastronomy.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Italy as Destination: Italian Travel Literature
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 16 units provided letter designation is different.
courses.description: Taught in English, this course is a study of Italian travel literature within Italy and abroad, from Marco Polo to the present day.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Biopolitics and Medical Humanities
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 16 units provided letter designation is different.
courses.description: (Taught in English) Lecture course exploring the theory and practice of biopolitics in Italy. Biopolitics, is defined as the sphere whereby politics intervene in biological life. Key themes in the course are mobility, immunization, and resilience.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Crime Italian Style
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 16 units provided letter designation is different.
courses.description: (Taught in English) Considers the reality and representation of Italian organized crime (Mafia, Camorra, Ndrangheta, etc) in a transnational perspective, and in specific reference to Italian immigration in the US and American popular culture.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Women in Italy
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: TAUGHT IN ITALIAN. Studies in the production of gender and the functions of sexuality in Italian culture including plays, films, painting, and literary texts.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Women, Gender, and Sexuality in Italy
courses.prereq_text: Note: ITAL 144XX is the "in translation (in English) version of this
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: (Taught in Italian) Studies in the representation of women, gender, and sexuality in Italian culture including plays, films, painting, and literary texts.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Gender and Sexuality in Italian Culture
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: TAUGHT IN ENGLISH. Studies in the production of gender and the functions of sexuality in Italian culture including plays, films, painting, and literary texts.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Gender and Sexuality in Italian Culture
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: (Taught in English) Studies in the production of gender and the functions of sexuality in Italian culture through literature and media.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Crossreadings : French and Italian Cultures in Dialogue and Translation
courses.comments: French 158, Italian 158X, and Comparative Literature 108 are the same course.
courses.description: Ever since the Renaissance, when the notion of a national culture had taken hold, the historic, literary and intellectual trajectories of France and Italy have been intimately entangled. Taking a chronological approach from the Renaissance to the post-modern period, this course will embark on a number of comparative readings from these two countries: from Rabelais carnivalesque uptake of Boccaccios humor and vulgarity; to Italys attempt at emulating the French Revolution; to Giuseppe Ungarettis debt to avant-garde literary figures, and more. Our goal will be to reveal that cultures and intellectual traditions exist not in isolation but emerge out of a perpetual conversation withand translation ofeach other. Taught in English.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: The European Union
courses.comments: POL S 145 and ITAL 161X are the same course
courses.description: Introduction to the history and organization of the European Union (the institutions, policies, goals, and successes of the EU). Focus on the ongoing process of economical, political, social, and cultural integration in Europe since the Second World War. In English.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Italian History in Fiction and Film
courses.description: (Taught in English) A course focusing on and comparing the representation of Italian history in film and literature.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Italian Cinema
courses.comments: Formerly offered as ITAL 180Z.
courses.description: A survey of the major trends and directors in Italian cinema since World War II. Directors to be studied include: Rossellini, De Sica, Visconti, Fellini, Antonioni, and Rosi. In English.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Italy in the Mediterranean: History, Arts, and Culture
courses.comments: Course is open only to students who do not intend to enroll in the EAP Summer Program �Mediterranean Crossroads.� ITAL 189A is the former number for ITAL 189X.
courses.description: (Taught in English) The history, culture, and arts of Italy, and in particular of the greater Gulf of Naples area, seen from and exclusively Mediterranean perspective from antiquity to the present.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Enhancement Seminar in Italian
courses.prereq_text: Instructor approval and concurrent enrollment in any Italian UD course taught in English (marked with an X).
courses.description: Designed for Italian majors or minors enrolled in any Italian UD course taught in English (marked with X). Students will read materials in Italian, meet with the instructor to discuss them and complete assignments in Italian in order to improve their linguistic and cultural fluency.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Senior Honors Independent Studies in Italian
courses.prereq_text: Senior standing; completion of 24 upper-division units in Italian.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.5 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters.
courses.description: Individual investigations in literary and related fields to Italian Studies in fulfillment of senior honors thesis. Limited to honors students only.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Independent Studies in Italian
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division courses in Italian.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters and limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined. 16 units max w/only 8 towards major.

courses.description: Independent research, under the supervision of a consenting faculty member.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Teaching Assistant Practicum

courses.description: Supervised teaching of lower-division Italian courses. Includes orientation workshop, weekly meetings with supervisor, preparation and correction of examinations, preparations of discussion sections, class observations.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: First-Year Japanese I
courses.description: An introduction to modern Japanese. Students will develop basic communicative skills based on the fundamentals of grammar, vocabulary, and conversational expressions. Emphasis on both oral-aural proficiency andwriting-reading skills. Introduction to Hiragana and Katakana syllabaries, and Kanji.

courses.prereq_text: Japanese 1 with grade C or better, or equivalent.
courses.description: Continuation of Japanese 1.

courses.subject: JAPAN

courses.description: Continuation of Japanese 3. Course emphasizes the further development of both oral-aural proficiency and reading-writing skills with an intensive review of basic grammar as well as an introduction to more advanced grammar, vocabulary, and Kanji.

courses.title: Second-Year Japanese

courses.description: Continuation of Japanese 4.

courses.description: Continuation of Japanese 5.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Imagining the Samurai
courses.description: A critical exploration of the image and myth of the samurai, Japan's hereditary warrior class, as constructed in Japanese literature, film, drama and art.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Violence and the Japanese State
courses.comments: History 25, Japanese 25, and Anthropology 25 are the same course.
courses.description: Examines historiographically and sociologically the Japanese State's various engagements in violent acts during war and peace times.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Sociology of Japan
courses.description: Sociological macro- and micro-analysis of Japanese society in the twentieth century.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Introduction to Japanese Religion: Texts, Concepts, and Representations
courses.comments: Religious Studies 73 and Japan 73 are the same course.
courses.description: A survey of the main authors, themes, and styles of the Japanese religious and philosophical traditions through readings from and analysis of some significant and influential original texts in English translation.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Masterpieces of Japanese Literature
courses.description: Examines a selection of works from Japanese literature, with the goal of understanding the major genres and their development over time. The cultural roles of literature, as well as criteria for critical evaluation, are also addressed.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Independent Research Assistance in Japanese
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA. Limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
courses.description: Research details are decided by the supervising Professor in the Department of East Asian Languages and Cultural Studies.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Japanese Folklore
courses.description: Introduction to Japanese folklore and folklore studies. Concepts, categories, and methodologies of folklore studies will be applied to the narrative, life cycle, and material forms of Japanese folklore. Course also examines motives and aims of Japanese folklorists over time.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Survey of Modern Japanese Literature
courses.description: A survey of Japanese literature after contact with the West, from 1868 to the present. Readings, lectures, and discussions in English.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Topics in Twentieth-Century Japanese
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units.
courses.description: Topics to be considered will include: the Japanese novelist as intellectual and social critic; representations of the self and similarities and differences between the shosetsu and the western novel; and Japanese literature in and outside Japan.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Third-Year Japanese I
courses.prereq_text: Japanese 6 with grade C or better, or equivalent
courses.comments: JAPANW 120A is the online version of JAPAN 120A.
courses.description: Develops an intermediate to advanced level of aural-oral skills to carry on conversations on diverse topics with linguistic accuracy and cultural appropriateness, reading skills to comprehend authentic materials, and writing skills with grammatical accuracy and an increasing number of Kanji.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Third-Year Japanese II
courses.prereq_text: Japanese 120A with grade C or better, or equivalent
courses.comments: JAPANW 120B is the online version of JAPAN 120B.
courses.description: Continuation of Japanese 120A.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Third-Year Japanese III
courses.prereq_text: Japanese 120B with grade C or better, or equivalent.
courses.comments: JAPANW 120C is the online version of JAPAN 120C.
courses.description: Continuation of Japanese 120B.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Early Modern Japanese Literature
courses.description: A survey (in English translation) of Japanese fiction, poetry, and drama from the early modern period, or approximately 1600 to 1868. Topics include popular fiction, supernatural tales, travel literature, haikai and haiku, and puppet theater and kabuki.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Japanese Humor
courses.description: An examination of humor and the comic tradition in Japanese culture and literature from earliest times through the present. Topics include comic fiction and poetry, parody and satire, comic storytelling and jokes, standup and slapstick, and TV variety shows.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Japanese Diasporas
courses.description: This course explores the diverse people of Japanese descent in North America, Latin America, and Asia in the modern and contemporary periods. Students investigate how movements shape identities by analyzing a multicultural array of sources including books, articles, and movies.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Critical Theory Through Anime and Manga
courses.description: This course teaches critical theories by combining academic texts by scholars and popular culture products such as anime and manga. The topics include power, hegemony, agency, ritual, magic, hybridity, among others.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Curiosity and Spectacle in Early Modern Japan
courses.description: Cultural and intellectual movements of early modern (Edo) Japan explored through the themes of curiosity and spectacle. Travel, material culture, print media, popular fiction and theater, sideshows and street performers, natural history, the supernatural, the study of foreign cultures and of the past.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Advanced Japanese Readings I
courses.comments: Not open for students who have a Japanese high school education.
courses.description: Designed to further develop skills in reading by focusing on analysis of Japanese sentence structure.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Advanced Japanese Readings II
courses.description: Introduces advanced students to selected prose and poetry from post-World War II period.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Death, Love & Money in Modern Japan
courses.description: How does capitalism remake intimacy and love? How does kinship shape the experiences of aging and death? What is relationship between gender and economy? Students explore these key questions by examining theoretical texts, movies, anime, and manga, among others.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: The Cultural Roots of the Japanese Horror Film
courses.description: From classical tales of noblemen and warriors to ghost dramas of medieval and early modern Japan, we will explore premodern creative expression concerning ghosts and their modern appearances in horror films and anime. Texts, images, and film will be used.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Japanese Cinema
courses.comments: Same course as Film and Media Studies 120.
courses.description: An introductory scrutiny of major Japanese directors: Mizoguchi, Ozu, Oshima, and Kurosawa. Close attention to their film composition, choices ofsubject and character, their ideas of the cinematic, and the relationship of cinema to Japanese culture and society.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Ethnic and Social Diversity in Japan
courses.description: Examines how difference is conceptualized and camouflaged in Japan despite an ideology of ethnic homogeneity. Considers the history and development of, and contemporary politics within internal and external minority communities and their diasporas across Japan.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Representations of Sexuality in Modern Japan
courses.comments: Same course as History 188S and Anthropology 176.
courses.description: This course examines the main ideologies guiding the establishment of various representations of sexuality from prewar scientific writings to contemporary popular culture.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Modernity and the Masses of Taisho Japan
courses.prereq_text: History 80 or 87 or Upper Division Standing
courses.comments: Same course as History 188T.
courses.description: Examines the beginnings of a modern mass culture in early twentieth- century Japan. Central topics are political and social movements, the new woman and the modern girl, westernization, new media and censorship, modernism and nationalism.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Popular Culture in Japan
courses.description: Examines popular culture in present-day Japan: advertising, music, fashion, television, animation, comics, sports. Integrates visual and acoustic material.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Body and Self in Japanese Culture
courses.description: Addresses how historians, anthropologists, artists, creators of popular culture, film makers, and literary authors have attached meanings to the human body and its relation to selfhood since the 19th century.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Religion in Japanese Culture
courses.comments: Japan 167A and Religious Studies 167A are the same course.
courses.description: A historical analysis of the major components of the classical and medieval religious systems of Japan, through investigation of texts, rituals, and institutions.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Seminar in Traditional Japanese Theater
courses.description: Survey and in-depth examinations of specific selected topics in traditional Japanese theater. Knowledge of Japanese not required.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Shinto through the Ages
courses.comments: RG ST175B and JAPAN 175B are the same course.
courses.description: Explores the diversity of the Shinto tradition through an analysis of representative original texts in English translation ranging from ancient mythology (Kojiki, Nihon shoki, and Fudoki) and medieval syncretic discourses, to modern forms of Shinto nationalism.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Special Topics in Japanese Studies
courses.comments: Misc: May be repeated for credit providing letter designations are different.
courses.description: Special topics in Japanese Studies. Course content varies.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Imagining Edo/Tokyo
courses.comments: Misc: May be repeated for credit providing letter designations are different.
courses.description: An interdisciplinary exploration of the city formerly known as Edo, and now known as Tokyo, from the nineteenth century to the present. Sources include literature, films, maps, photographs, and woodblock prints. All readings will be in English translation; no knowledge of Japanese is required.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Japanese TV: History, Genres, and Content
courses.comments: Misc: May be repeated for credit providing letter designations are different.
courses.description: Surveys the history of Japanese TV and the development of the most important genres, including rom-com, detective drama, and variety shows. We will analyze content for how they depict social issues, including work culture, gender, and conflict resolution.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Introduction to Classical Japanese
courses.description: Introduction to classical Japanese grammar, vocabulary, and major genres. Foundation for the study of premodern through prewar texts. Prerequisite for JAPAN 183.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Readings in Premodern through Meiji Japanese Texts
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units. Not open for credit to students who have completed Japanese 101C.
courses.description: Selected readings in medieval, early modern, and Meiji texts.

courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division courses in Japaneseconsent of instructor.
courses.comments: Students must have a 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters and are limited limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined. May be repeated up to 12 units.
courses.description: Guided reading in Japanese on a subject not covered in the regularly offered courses.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Independent Studies in Japanese

courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Readings in Selected Texts
courses.prereq_text: Ability to read japanese at graduate level; consent of instructor. Normallygraduate status is required.
courses.description: Course will center on readings of japanese texts type and period to depend on needs of students and wishes of instructor. Research methods to be taught as appropriate.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Bibliography and Research Methodology
courses.description: Introduction to bibliographies, reference works, and methodologies of research in japanese studies.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Japan Modern
courses.description: Examines Japanese modernity from the mid-nineteenth century to today and analyzes theoretical and methodological approaches to the study of modern Japanese history and society.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Anthropology of Japan
courses.description: This course focuses on the history, methods, theories, and politics pertaining to the anthropological study of Japan. It primarily covers the postwar academic texts in English, and occasionally engages sources in Japanese, in alternative formats, and/or from earlier historical periods.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Early Modern Japan
courses.description: Examines the literature, theater, and popular culture of Japan during the early modern period (1600-1868), with particular attention to recent scholarship and new methodological approaches.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Graduate Seminar in Shinto Studies
courses.description: This seminar addresses various issues in Shinto studies, including the history of Shinto, Western perceptions of Shinto, Shinto art and theories of the representation of the sacred, and features of Shinto Nativism.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Body and Self in Japanese Culture
courses.description: Addresses how historians, anthropologists, artists, creators of popular culture, film makers, and literary authors have attached meanings to the human body and its relation to selfhood since the 19th century.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Seminar in Traditional Japanese Theater
courses.description: Survey and in-depth examinations of specific selected topics in traditional Japanese theater.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Reinventing "Japan" Colloquium
courses.comments: History 287 and Japan 287 are cross-listed and are the same course.
courses.description: This year long interdisciplinary colloquium brings together graduate students who study Japanese history and culture. It introduces current scholarship on Japan via readings, discussions and presentations by visiting scholars, UCSB scholars and graduate students. The colloquium meets bi-weekly. Students will prepare readings for discussion, write a seminar-length paper and present their paper to the colloquium once during the year.

courses.subject: JAPAN
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Seminar in special areas of interest in Japanese cultural studies. Specific course titles and topics to be announced by the department each quarter offered. Course content will vary.

courses.title: Directed Reading and Research
courses.comments: Letter grade; minimum of two units per quarter.
courses.description: Individual tutorial. A written proposal for each tutorial must be approved by department chair and filed with graduate division.

courses.description: Study for master's comprehensive examinations and Ph.D examinations.

courses.description: For research underlying the thesis writing the thesis. Instructor should bethe chair of the student's thesis committee.

courses.description: Terminal preparation of the dissertation.

courses.subject: KOR
courses.title: First Year Korean
courses.comments: No credit can be earned if more advanced credit in the language has already been awarded. KOR W 1 is the online version of KOR 1.
courses.description: The beginning course in Korean. The student acquires a basic knowledge of the grammar, a limited general vocabulary, correct pronunciation, and an ability to read and understand simple texts. Weekly laboratory assignments support and enhance classroom learning.

courses.title: First Year Korean
courses.comments: No credit can be earned if more advanced credit in the language has already been awarded. KOR W 2 is the online version of KOR 2.
courses.description: Continuation of Korean 1.

courses.title: First Year Korean
courses.comments: No credit can be earned if more advanced credit in the language has already been awarded. KOR W 3 is the online version of KOR 3.
