courses.subject: KOR
courses.title: Second Year Korean
courses.comments: No credit can be earned if more advanced credit in the language has already been awarded.
courses.description: Continuation of Korean 5.

courses.subject: KOR
courses.title: The New Korean Wave
courses.description: Surveys the major social, economic, and cultural impact of the globalization, and consumption of Korean popular cultural exports and music genres. Adopting a case study approach, the lectures will analyze history of K-pop, its stars, fandom, entertainment industry and media induced tourism.

courses.subject: KOR
courses.title: Introduction to Korean Popular Culture
courses.description: Provides an overview of popular culture in modern and contemporary Korea through film, popular music, television, and new media.

courses.subject: KOR
courses.title: Korean Literature Survey
courses.description: Introduces Korea's award winning authors from the 17th century romance to contemporary period women's literature. Topics include class stratification in Yangban society, Japanese occupation, the Korean War, the politics of division, urbanization, prostitution, and alienation.

courses.subject: KOR
courses.title: Advanced Korean
courses.description: A course designed to develop ability in reading contemporary Korean essays,literary works, magazines, and newspapers. Emphasis on solidfying students' grammatical foundation, mastery of Hanja and vocabulary, and proficiency in writing and oral skills.

courses.subject: KOR
courses.title: Advanced Korean
courses.description: A course designed to develop ability in reading contemporary Korean essays,literary works, magazines, and newspapers. Emphasis on solidifying students' grammatical foundation, mastery of Hanja and vocabulary, and proficiency in writing and oral skills.

courses.subject: KOR
courses.title: Advanced Korean
courses.description: A course designed to develop ability in reading contemporary Korean essays,literary works, magazines, and newspapers. Emphasis on solidifying students' grammatical foundation, mastery of Hanja and vocabulary, and proficiency in writing and oral skills.

courses.subject: KOR
courses.title: Korean War in Literature and Film
courses.description: Examines the representations of the Korean War in transnational literature and film. All reading, viewing, and listening material will be available in English translation.

courses.subject: KOR
courses.title: Cultures of Protest in South Korea
courses.description: This course engages with diverse medialiterature, music, film, digital mediato explore how culture is mobilized as an active site of protest in South Korea. All reading, viewing, and listening material will be available in English translation.

courses.subject: KOR
courses.title: Korean Popular Culture
courses.description: This course engages with diverse media—literature, music, film, digital media—as active sites of cultural production, distribution, and consumption in modern and contemporary Korea. All reading, viewing, and listening material will be available in English translation.

courses.subject: KOR
courses.title: Special Topics in Korean Studies
courses.description: Special Topics in Korean Studies. Course content varies.

courses.subject: KOR
courses.title: Readings in Korean
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division courses in Korean. Consent of instructor.
courses.comments: Students must have a 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters and are limited limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined. May be repeated up to 12 units.
courses.description: Guided reading in Korean on a subject not covered in the regularly offered courses.

courses.subject: KOR W
courses.title: First Year Korean
courses.comments: No credit can be earned if more advanced credit in the language has already been awarded. KOR W 1 is the online version of KOR 1
courses.description: KOREAN 1 is the first part of First Year Korean and is designed for students with no prior background in Korean. This course introduces the Korean writing system (Hangul), pronunciation, and essential grammar and vocabulary for basic communication. Students will learn to understand, speak, read, and write short sentences and paragraphs on familiar topics such as self-introduction, school and classes, daily activities, and past experiences.

courses.subject: KOR W
courses.title: First Year Korean
courses.comments: No credit can be earned if more advanced credit in the language has already been awarded. KOR W 2 is the online version of KOR 2.
courses.description: KOREAN 2 is the second part of First Year Korean. This course aims to train students to perform appropriate spoken and written communication in most essential daily life situations. This course will focus on introducing Korean sounds, writing system, and basic vocabulary and grammar used in carrying out simple tasks; students will learn how to speak, understand, read and write short sentences and paragraphs on concrete and familiar topics such as self-introduction, school and classes, daily activities, past experiences and future plans.

courses.subject: KOR W
courses.title: First Year Korean
courses.comments: No credit can be earned if more advanced credit in the language has already been awarded. KOR W 3 is the online version of KOR 3.
courses.description: KOREAN 3 is the third part of First Year Korean. This course aims to train students to perform appropriate spoken and written communication in most essential daily life situations. This course will focus on introducing basic vocabulary and grammar used in carrying out simple tasks; students will learn how to speak, understand, read and write short sentences and paragraphs on concrete and familiar topics such as self-introduction, school and classes, daily activities, past experiences and future plans. In addition, this course will introduce the Korean honorific system.

courses.subject: KOR W
courses.title: Korean Popular Culture
courses.description: Korean popular culture has gained global momentum over the past two decades, creating the phenomenon known as Hallyu [the Korean Wave]. This course explores the technological innovations, sociopolitical changes, and historical forces behind South Korea's cultural rise and what it reveals about global cultural shifts. We will engage with various forms of Korean popular culture—graphic novels, folk songs, music, TV, film, digital media, and food—as both reflections of contemporary Korean society and active sites of cultural production and exchange. The course includes theories on media politics, authorship, and cultural consumption. No prior knowledge of Korean history or culture is required.

courses.subject: LAIS
courses.title: Global Blackness: Race, Repair and Reparation
courses.comments: LAIS 2 and BL ST 2 are the same course.
courses.description: Discusses historical and contemporary conditions of Black and racialized communities living under economic and militarized oppression in a global perspective. Texts, films and lecture presentations foregrounds the critical role of Black subjects in the expansion of global capitalism. Explores current global conditions of Black and racialized communities living under militarized and economic apartheid. Spotlights the role of culture in shaping struggles of Black communities around the world for self-determination, the (im)possibilities of colonial repair and collective demands for reparation.

courses.subject: LAIS
courses.title: Survey: Arts of the Ancient Americas
courses.comments: ARTHI 6H and LAIS 6H are the same course.
courses.description: An introduction to select art traditions from Mesoamerica to Andean South America. Examines architecture, ceramics, sculpture, painting and other classes of material culture for their meaning and function within sociopolitical, religious, and economic contexts.

courses.subject: LAIS
courses.title: Introduction to Caribbean Studies
courses.comments: LAIS 7 and BL ST 7 are the same course. Students who have received credit for Black Studies 1B may not take this course for credit.
courses.description: A survey of the culture and society of the Caribbean. After surveying Amerindian communities and examining the impact of the Atlantic slave trade, focus will be on slavery, emancipation, African and Creole cultures,and the issues accompanying an independent nationhood status.

courses.subject: LAIS
courses.title: Introduction to the Latin American and Iberian World
courses.description: Introduction to issues debates, and approaches in the study of Latin America, Spain and Portugal, and the Latinx world, from an interdisciplinary perspective. Topics considered include history, culture, society, and literature from various places and times.

courses.subject: LAIS
courses.title: Introduction to Latin American and Iberian Studies
courses.comments: SPAN 106, LAIS 100, and HIST 100 are the same courses. LAIS 100S is the Spanish-language version of SPAN 106, LAIS 100, HIST 100 and is a legal-repeat.
courses.description: Designed to acquaint students with current research on the main areas of Latin American and Iberian Studies.

courses.subject: LAIS
courses.title: Introduction to Latin American and Iberian Studies - Honors Section
courses.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in SPAN 106 or LAIS 100; honors standing in LAIS or the College of Letters and Science.
courses.description: Eligible students are invited to enroll in the honors seminar, which is generally taught by the course instructor.

courses.subject: LAIS
courses.title: Interdisciplinary Approaches to the History and Societies of Latin America and Iberia
courses.comments: ANTH 134A, LAIS 101, and SPAN 107 are the same course. LAIS 101S is a legal repeat of ANTH 134A, LAIS 101, and SPAN 107.
courses.description: Issues central to the study of Latin America and Iberia across the social sciences and history. Topics include nationalism, revolution, politics and the state, economic development and international relations, labor, popular culture, race, gender, religion, migration, environment, imperialism, and colonialism.

courses.subject: LAIS
courses.title: Interdisciplinary Approaches to the Cultures, Languages, and Literatures of Latin America and Iberia
courses.comments: LAIS 102, LING 133, and SPAN 108 are the same course. LAIS 102S is the Spanish-language version of LAIS 102, LING 133, and SPAN 108, and is a legal repeat.
courses.description: Issues pertinent to the diverse cultures, languages, and literatures of Latin America and Iberia. Disciplines and approaches may include: pre-Columbian studies, Spanish and Spanish American literatures, Portuguese and Brazilian literatures, translation studies, cultural, gender, and queer studies, romance language and linguistics.

courses.subject: LAIS
courses.title: Media, Culture, and Society in Latin America and Iberia
courses.comments: LAIS 103 and FAMST 129 are the same course.
courses.description: Introduces students to Latin American theories, practices and representations about the media, analyzing from a cross-cultural and comparative perspective various cultural productions of the Spanish-speaking world that cross the domains of word, image, and sound.

courses.subject: LAIS
courses.title: Gastronomy of the Americas through Literature
courses.comments: LAIS/SPAN 127 is the Spanish language version of LAIS/SPAN 127E.
courses.description: An in-depth look at the gastronomy of specific geographical and cultural regions of Latin America through a selection of literary texts and films. From Pre-Columbian to current gastronomical influences from around the world, students will learn about ancient grains, protein alternatives, non-wheat carbohydrates, common herbs and spices in connection with the region in which native people grow, preserve and consume them. Other cultural and culinary influences that have shaped the gastronomy of Latin American today will be emphasized to highlight the fusion and a culinary syncretism observed within the rich and diverse Latin American cuisine. A culinary selection of traditional dishes will be prepared.

courses.subject: LAIS
courses.title: Gastronomy of the Americas through Literature
courses.comments: Spanish/LAIS 127E is the English version of Spanish/LAIS 127. LAIS 127E and Spanish 127E are the same course.
courses.description: An in-depth look at the gastronomy of specific geographical and cultural regions of Latin America through a selection of literary texts and films. From Pre-Columbian to current gastronomical influences from around the world, students will learn about ancient grains, protein alternatives, non-wheat carbohydrates, common herbs and spices in connection with the region in which native people grow, preserve and consume them. Other cultural and culinary influences that have shaped the gastronomy of Latin American today will be emphasized to highlight the fusion and a culinary syncretism observed within the rich and diverse Latin American cuisine. A culinary selection of traditional dishes will be prepared. Taught in English.

courses.subject: LAIS
courses.title: Spanish for Healthcare
courses.comments: Spanish 145 and LAIS 145 are the same course.
courses.description: Designed for students interested in expanding and applying their knowledge of Spanish to the medical field. Students will learn and apply targeted vocabulary/grammar and develop bicultural/bilingual competency of healthcare issues in Hispanic countries and the US.

courses.subject: LAIS
courses.title: Blackness in Latin America, An Introduction
courses.prereq_text: History 8 or 49A or 49B or upper-division standing.
courses.comments: Same course as History 149AD.
courses.description: Explores the experiences of Africans and their descendants in the Americas, mostly in Latin America and the Caribbean. Looks at ways in which men and women (enslaved and free) negotiated their imposed conditions from the colonial period to the present. Considers the methodological challenges of writing a history of people who did not produce primary sources. Underscores the contribution that people of African-descent have made and the debates that continue shaping the discipline.

courses.subject: LAIS
courses.title: Gender and Sexuality in Latin America
courses.prereq_text: HIST 8A or HIST 8B or upper division standing.
courses.comments: HIST 151GS and LAIS 151GS are the same course.
courses.description: An examination of gender and sexuality in Latin America from independence to the present. The course pays particular attention to how individuals exercised power and how gender, race, and class intersected. Themes include popular conceptions of sexuality, masculinity, and femininity, religion, work, health, and women's movements.

courses.subject: LAIS
courses.title: Health and Healing in Latin America
courses.prereq_text: HIST 8A or 8B or upper division standing.
courses.comments: HIST 151H and LAIS 151H are the same course.
courses.description: An overview of histories of health and healing in Latin America from independence to the present. For centuries, local healers have practiced popular and traditional medicine alongside the professionally trained. These diverse and varied medical authorities informed each other’s practices and at times came into conflict. Main questions to consider include: How have approaches to healing and disease shifted across time and space? In what ways did Indigenous, African, and Asian healers figure into everyday life and national programs? How have gender and race shaped public health policies and structures? Finally, how have local peoples responded to these various institutions, practitioners, and programs?

courses.subject: LAIS
courses.title: History of Mexico: Pre-Hispanic and Colonial Periods
courses.comments: Same course as History 156A.
courses.description: The history of colonial New Spain, from California to Central America and from the Philippines to the Caribbean. Topics include pre-Columbian societies, including the Aztecs; the formation and development of colonial societies; religion; the economy; and global connections.

courses.subject: LAIS
courses.title: Andean Literature, Music, and Culture
courses.comments: LAIS 165 and SPAN 165 are the same course.
courses.description: This course focuses on literature, music and culture of certain ethnic groups inhabiting the Andean region of South America including, but not limited to, the Aymara and Quechua peoples, their cosmovision and their languages. Through literary texts belonging to different genres, and through films, special attention is placed on expressions of syncretism in seasonal festivals in which pre-Hispanic, European, and African music traditions and religions were shaped due to forced migration, wars and colonization. A strong emphasis on the ecological regions of the nations that share the Andean mountain range contextualizes current indigenous movements of resistance against the degradation of its environment and the impact on its culture.

courses.subject: LAIS
courses.title: The Hispanic Novel and Cinema
courses.comments: Same course are SPAN 174.
courses.description: Study of three or four Hispanic novels vis-a-vis their film versions, permitting analysis of narrative in both genres, using existing films and videos based on masterpieces of Hispanic literature. Taught in Spanish.

courses.subject: LAIS
courses.title: Vanguard Poetry in Spanish America
courses.comments: LAIS 189 and SPAN 189 are the same course.
courses.description: A survey of the poetry of the Spanish-American avant-guarde focusing on its three main tendencies: colloquial or antipoetic poetry, existentially or politically committed poetry, and self-referential, narcissistic poetry.

courses.subject: LAIS
courses.title: Spanish American Women's Writing
courses.comments: LAIS 194 and SPAN 194 are the same course.
courses.description: An introduction to nineteenth- and twentieth-century Spanish American women's writings. Themes may include women's participation in the formation of national literatures, their engagement with a tradition of women's writing, and issues of authorship and authority.

courses.subject: LAIS
courses.title: Senior Honors Thesis
courses.prereq_text: Admission to honors program; consent of department.
courses.comments: Students must have a 3.5 grade-point average for courses in Latin American & Iberian Studies.
courses.description: Individual study with the advisor for the purpose of writing a major interdisciplinary research paper on a topic of sufficient depth and sophistication.

courses.subject: LAIS
courses.title: Senior Honors Thesis
courses.prereq_text: Admission to honors program; consent of department.
courses.comments: Students must have a 3.5 grade-point average for courses in Latin American & Iberian Studies.
courses.description: Individual study with the advisor for the purpose of writing a major interdisciplinary research paper on a topic of sufficient depth and sophistication.

courses.subject: LAIS
courses.title: Independent Studies
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division courses in LAIS.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 grade-point average for the preceding three quarters and are limited to five units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined. May b
courses.description: Independent studies in the LAIS department.

courses.subject: LAIS
courses.title: Introduction to Latin American and Iberian Studies
courses.comments: Required for all graduate students in the program.
courses.description: This is a year-long colloquium designed to acquaint students with current research on the main areas of Latin American and Iberian studies as well as the faculty associated with the program. Knowledge of Spanish is highly desirable.

courses.subject: LAIS
courses.title: Library and Archival Resources and Research in Latin American and Iberian Studies
courses.description: Introduces students to information access and retrieval of primary and secondary sources in Latin American and Iberian Studies and related fields, using databases and other tools. The course discuss how software programs are not neutral tools for research but human-designed and may reflect programmers' unconscious bias, and how it is necessary to understand how they work to improve research results. Furthermore, the course explores not only how to do archival research, but how to do it ethically. At the end of the term, students will know effective ways to conduct library and archival research and become reflective scholars.

courses.subject: LAIS
courses.title: Teaching Assistant Practicum
courses.comments: Units earned do not apply toward completion of advanced degrees. S/U grading only. Required of TAs in LAIS. Participation in occasional workshops related to the field of teaching is required.
courses.description: Supervised teaching of LAIS discussion sessions at UCSB.

courses.subject: LAIS
courses.title: Directed Reading and Research
courses.description: Individual independent study which could include work with EAP. A written proposal for each tutorial must be approved by student's program adviser and by the department chair. The number of units that a student may take depends on the nature of the program and the consent of the adviser or the graduate committee.

courses.subject: LAIS
courses.title: IND STD M.A. COMP
courses.prereq_text: graduate standing. no unit credit allowed toward advanced degrees.

courses.subject: LAIS
courses.title: Master's Thesis Research and Preparation
courses.prereq_text: Fulfillment of all graduate requirements except the thesis.
courses.description: Only for research and writing of the thesis under the direction of a faculty member in the program and with the approval of the chair.

courses.subject: LAIS W
courses.title: Introduction to the Latin American and Iberian World
courses.comments: LAIS W 10 is the online version of LAIS 10.
courses.description: Introduction to issues debates, and approaches in the study of Latin America, Spain and Portugal, and the Latinx world, from an interdisciplinary perspective. Topics considered include history, culture, society, and literature from various places and times.

courses.subject: LAIS W
courses.title: Global Climate Justice from the South
courses.comments: Recommended for students pursuing pre-major requirements in Economics, Economics and Accounting, Political Science, Sociology, Communication, and related majors. Not open to credit for students who have completed GLOBL 195.
courses.description: This online course examines the science, policy, and politics of global climate change with an emphasis on the Global South, and a social science focus on equity and justice. Students will learn directly from expert faculty from across the UC system and beyond. In addition, students will engage with readings and multimedia content to deepen their understanding of the most pressing climate change issues and solutions. Students will be evaluated through a variety of written products (review questions, journal responses, and a final paper) in which they identify connections across seemingly disparate places. Students will gain knowledge and skills needed to identify the larger system changes needed to adequately address the climate crisis.

courses.subject: LATIN
courses.title: Elementary Latin
courses.description: The beginning course in classical Latin, and first in a three-quarter sequence introducing fundamentals of grammar, syntax, and reading skills. Concepts taught using written exercises. Interesting aspects of Ancient Roman society are introduced.

courses.subject: LATIN
courses.title: Elementary Latin
courses.prereq_text: Latin 1 with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: A continuation of Latin 1. Emphasis on mastering grammar and building vocabulary.

courses.subject: LATIN
courses.title: Intermediate Latin
courses.prereq_text: Latin 2 with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Continuation of Latin 2. Emphasis on building a working vocabulary and the syntax of complex sentences. Reading in classical prose introduce students to ancient Roman literature and culture.

courses.subject: LATIN
courses.title: Introduction To Latin Prose
courses.prereq_text: Latin 3 with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Reading and analysis of various Latin prose authors to develop reading skills and introduce study of the style and thought of historical, rhetorical and/or philosophical writers.

courses.subject: LATIN
courses.title: Introduction To Latin Poetry
courses.prereq_text: Latin 100 with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Readings in various authors (often including Catallus and Ovid) to develop reading skills, introduce an understanding of meter, and begin study of the style and thought of Latin poetry.

courses.subject: LATIN
courses.title: Readings In Latin Literature
courses.description: Selected readings in Latin prose and/or poetry are designed to develop reading proficiency, and to help students make the transition to more advanced study of classical Latin literature.

courses.subject: LATIN
courses.title: Medieval Latin Readings
courses.description: Graded and selected reading and study of medieval Latin prose and verse writers.

courses.subject: LATIN
courses.title: Roman Satire
courses.description: Horace, Juvenal, Persius, and Martial.

courses.subject: LATIN
courses.title: Roman Comedy
courses.description: Plautus and Terence. Reading of complete plays and study of the origins of Roman comedy.

courses.subject: LATIN
courses.title: The Roman Novel
courses.description: Reading and study of passages from Petronius and Apuleius with attention to the language and style of their satiric novels and to their social and historical context.

courses.subject: LATIN
courses.title: Cicero: Essays, Letters, And Orations
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units.
courses.description: Reading and study of selected works of Cicero, normally one of the major speeches. Translation; discussion of philological, stylistic, and rhetorical points.

courses.subject: LATIN
courses.title: Sallust
courses.description: Study of one of the extant works of Rome's first great historian: the Bellum Catilinae or the Bellum Iugurthinum. Translation; discussion of philological, stylistic, literary, and historical points.

courses.subject: LATIN
courses.title: Vergil
courses.description: Reading, translation, and discussion of Vergil's epic poem Aeneid, as well as his Georgics and Eclogues.

courses.subject: LATIN
courses.title: Ovid
courses.description: Translation and discussion of Ovid's epic or elegiac poetry (Metamorphoses, Fasti, Ars Amatoria, Tristia, Heroides) in its literary, social and historical contexts.

courses.subject: LATIN
courses.title: Catullus
courses.description: Translation and discussion of Catullus' poetry in its literary, social, and historical contexts.

courses.subject: LATIN
courses.title: Horace
courses.description: Reading, translation, and discussion of selected poems of Horace (Odes, Epodes, Satires, Epistles) in their literary, social, and historical contexts.

courses.subject: LATIN
courses.title: Seneca: Tragedies
courses.description: Reading, translation, and discussion of several tragedies by Seneca.

courses.subject: LATIN
courses.title: Independent Studies In Latin.
courses.prereq_text: Consent of instructor and department chair. upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division courses in Latin.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 4.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
courses.description: Independent investigations in Latin language and literature.

courses.subject: LATIN
courses.title: Introduction to Latin Prose
courses.prereq_text: One year of Latin or more.
courses.description: Reading and analysis of various Latin prose authors to develop reading skills and introduce study of the style and thought of historical, rhetorical and/or philosophical writers.

courses.subject: LATIN
courses.title: Latin Prose Composition
courses.description: Study of Latin grammar and syntax through English composition, combined with analysis of Latin prose style in a variety of authors, including Cato, Caesar, Cicero, Sallust, and Tacitus.

courses.subject: LATIN
courses.title: Roman Satire
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units.
courses.description: Advanced readings in Horace, Juvenal, Persius, and/or Martial.

courses.subject: LATIN
courses.title: Roman Comedy
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units.
courses.description: Advanced study of Plautus and Terence. Reading of complete plays and study of the origins of Roman comedy.

courses.subject: LATIN
courses.title: The Roman Novel
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units.
courses.description: Advanced study of Petronius and/or Apuleius, with attention to the language and style of their satiric novels, and to their social and historical context.

courses.subject: LATIN
courses.title: Cicero: Essays, Letters, and Orations
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units.
courses.description: Advanced reading and study of selected works of Cicero, normally one of the major speeches. Translation; discussion of philological, stylistic, and rhetorical points; introduction to current scholarship.

courses.subject: LATIN
courses.title: Sallust
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units.
courses.description: Advanced study of one of the extant works of Rome's first great historian: The Bellum Catilinae or the Bellum Iugurthinum. Translations; discussion of philological, stylistic, literary, and historical points; introduction to current scholarship.

courses.subject: LATIN
courses.title: Tacitus
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units.
courses.description: Advanced study of portions of one of Tacitus' major histories of the early Empire (Annales, Historiae), or of the shorter works (Agricola, Dialogus, Germania). Translation; discussion of philological, stylistic, literary, and historical points; introduction to current scholarship.

courses.subject: LATIN
courses.title: Vergil
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units.
courses.description: Advanced reading, translation, and discussion of Vergil's epic poem Aeneid, as well as his Georgics and Eclogues.

courses.subject: LATIN
courses.title: Ovid
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units.
courses.description: Advanced study of Ovid's epic or elegiac poetry (Metamorphoses, Fasti, Ars Amatoria, Tristia, Heroides) in its literary, social, and historical contexts.

courses.subject: LATIN
courses.title: Catullus
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units.
courses.description: Advanced study of Catullus' poetry in its literary, social, and historical contexts.

courses.subject: LATIN
courses.title: Horace
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units.
courses.description: Advanced study of selected poems of Horace (Odes, Epodes, Satire Epistles) in their literary, social, and historical contexts, with an introduction to current scholarship.

courses.subject: LATIN
courses.title: Seneca: Tragedies
courses.description: Reading, translation, and discussion of several tragedies by Seneca.

courses.subject: LATIN
courses.title: Directed Reading and Research
courses.prereq_text: Written proposal approved by department chair and graduate advisor.
courses.description: Individual Tutorial.

courses.subject: LATIN
courses.title: Master's Thesis Research and Preparation
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing and consent of instructor and graduate advisor.
courses.comments: No unit credit allowed toward degree.
courses.description: Independent research.

courses.subject: LATIN
courses.title: Ph.D. Dissertation Presentation.
courses.description: Terminal preparation of the dissertation.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: EMS: Intermediate Graduate Writing for International Students
courses.prereq_text: Placement based on English Language Placement Examination.
courses.comments: Workload credit only. May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units.
courses.description: Provides instruction for students needing to improve accuracy and fluency in written academic English. Emphasizes grammar, vocabulary and patterns of organization relevant to academic writing at the graduate level.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: EMS: Academic English
courses.prereq_text: Placement based on Analytical Writing Placement Exam (AWPE)and English Language Placement Examination (ELPE).
courses.description: First of three levels intended to develop proficiency in university-level reading and writing. Emphasizes applying critical approaches to reading, practicing writing in a variety of academic styles, and developing grammatical and lexical resources appropriate to a university setting.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: EMS: Academic English
courses.prereq_text: Open to students who have a Ling 3B placement or a prerequisite of Ling 3A with a pass grade.
courses.comments: LING W 3B is the online version of LING 3B.
courses.description: Second level in a three-course series intended to develop proficiency in university-level reading and writing. Emphasizes applying critical approaches to reading, practicing writing in a variety of academic styles, and developing grammatical and lexical resources appropriate to a university setting.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: EMS: Academic English
courses.prereq_text: Open to students who have a Linguistics 3C placement; or Linguistics 3B with a minimum grade of C.
courses.description: Third level in a three-course series intended to develop proficiency in university-level reading and writing. Emphasizes applying critical approaches to reading, practicing writing in a variety of academic styles, and developing grammatical and lexical resources appropriate to a university setting.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: EMS: Advanced Graduate Writing for International Students
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing. Placement based on English Language Placement Examination scores.
courses.comments: Workload credit only. May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units.
courses.description: Focuses on rhetorical strategies and patterns of development used in a variety of writing typically required for graduate courses. Addresses levels of formality and academic conventions used across disciplines, emphasizing clarity of expression.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: EMS: Individual and Small Group Instruction for International Graduate Students
courses.comments: Workload credit only. May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units.
courses.description: Designed for focused instruction in oral and written academic English. Enrollment by instructor consent. Preference given to students at advanced proficiency levels.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Oral Communication for International Undergraduate Students
courses.description: Develops oral skills to help multilingual undergraduate students, especially international students, participate in classroom activities and engage in campus life. Activities include group discussions, group presentations, interviews, and language focus on vocabulary and pronunciation.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Academic Reading Across the Curriculum
courses.description: Focuses on interrelations between reading and writing in academic content areas across the curriculum. Through engagement with readings in humanities, social sciences and sciences, the course provides essential reading strategies and skills for developing comprehension, genre awareness, and critical thinking.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: EMS: Approaches to University Writing for Multilingual Students
courses.prereq_text: Open to students who have not satisfied the Entry Level Writing Requirement and have a Ling 12 placement or a prerequisite of Ling 3C with a grade of C or better.
courses.comments: Quarters usually offered: Winter, Spring, Fall.
courses.description: Principles of critical reading, thinking and writing in the university. Students analyze academic discourse, develop rhetorical strategies for exposition and argument, practice examination writing, and write and revise papers. Completion of C or better meets Entry Level Writing Requirement.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Vocabulary and Grammar in Academic Writing for Multilingual Students
courses.description: Analysis and practice of English vocabulary and grammatical constructions for a variety of genres in academic writing. Focus on functional language use common across disciplines, such as expressing causation and change of state, creating cohesion, establishing focus and emphasis, qualifying ideas, and reporting research. Attention given to developing language resources and strategies for effective summarizing, paraphrasing and editing.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Language in Life
courses.description: Overview of language and its role in communities at home and around the world. The diversity and history of languages; their norms, conventions, and written traditions; the role of language in culture and identity; language rights and multilingualism, and the implications of technology for language use.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Language And Linguistics
courses.description: Introduction to the scientific study of language: The sounds of language; word and sentence structure; semantics and pragmatics; discourse and conversational speech; the social and cultural functions of language; language change and the reconstruction of languages at earlier stages.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Digital Humanities and Language
courses.description: Focus on fundamental transferable computational and data handling skills, building students’ agency in navigating the modern data-driven academic landscape. Special attention is given to leveraging AI as a research and learning tool. The course is directed at students interested in digital humanities, technology, and language science.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Language and Computers
courses.description: Overview of how computers learn, understand, and generate human language, and how computers can be used to assist in the scientific study of language. Focus on building conceptual understanding of how language can be represented and processed by computers, what aspects of human language present challenges for these approaches, how linguists use computers to study language, and the role of language technologies in society. No technical background assumed.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Data Science and Data communication
courses.description: This class examines the intersection between data science and science communication. What do statistics, graphs, and data visualizations mean to the average person, and as scientists, how can we leverage insights from linguistics to communicate our science better? In this class, students will learn some R fundamentals, improve their data literacy, and reflect on what is communicated by science reporting in the news and popular media from a linguistic perspective.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Black American English
courses.description: Examines the sociolinguistic aspects of English as spoken by African-Americans in the United States. Relationship of African-American English to linguistic theory, education policy, and U.S. culture. Emphasis on mitigating discrimination and improving the educational and social experiences of African-Americans at UCSB and beyond.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: The Mayas: Languages and Cultures
courses.description: This course introduces Mayan languages today. We examine what they are like, how they relate to each other, and who speaks them, as well as the social and cultural context in which those people live.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Language and Power
courses.description: Examines how social identities and relations (nationality, class, ethnicity, age, gender) are constructed, maintained, and challenged via language practices, policies, and ideologies. Considers power dynamics in multiple domains including everyday interaction, education, media (advertising, news, film/tv, online), and political discourse.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Academic Writing in Humanities and Social Sciences
courses.description: Introduction to the fundamentals of academic writing in the humanities and social sciences. Students learn to craft clear, evidence-based arguments and organize ideas into coherent papers while building digital literacy skills in online research, source management, document preparation, responsible use of AI assistants, and basic data presentation. A goal is to develop a versatile toolkit for research, writing, and digital scholarship that supports success across disciplines.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Language in Society
courses.description: How language defines the relationship of the individual to society; the role language plays in constituting power, hierarchy, ethnicity, gender, ideology, and other aspects of social identity; how speakers use language to display identity and define social context. Emphasis on sociolinguistic diversity in American society.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Endangered Languages
courses.description: Examines language endangerment and its impact on the world's speech communities. Topics include: language ecologies; reasons for language shift; social, affective, and linguistic impacts of language contraction; indigenous knowledge systems; biocultural diversity; documentation, revitalization, and reclamation.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Independent Studies in Linguistics
courses.description: Intended for the study of special areas within Linguistics.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Basic Elements of Linguistic Analysis
courses.description: An introduction to the analytic methodology in the study of phonology, morphology, syntax, and semantics. A typologically oriented course designed to demonstrate how linguists analyze languages.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Programming for Linguists
courses.prereq_text: Upper division standing or a prior course in Linguistics.
courses.description: Hands-on introduction to programming in Python, with emphasis on methods for retrieving, structuring, and interacting with textual data. Focus on developing practical programming skills and transferable methodology, such as debugging, task decomposition and abstraction, and best practices for documenting and structuring code. Targeted toward students with no programming background.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Statistical Methods in Linguistics
courses.description: Fundamentals of scientific inquiry and methodology; basics of experimental design, statistical methods (descriptive, analytic, and exploratory) relevant to linguistics.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Predictive Modeling in Linguistics
courses.description: Advanced methods in quantitative linguistics. Topics may include data exploration and visualization, classification trees, random forests, regression modeling, bootstrap methods, and Bayesian data analysis. Emphasis on building predictive models of linguistic data, with a focus on simulation, model comparison, and performance evaluation. Students complete statistical programming assignments and projects using real-world data.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Introduction to Phonetics
courses.description: An introduction to the articulatory and acoustic properties of speech sounds. Survey of speech sounds found in the languages of the world. Emphasis on ear training and transcription using the International Phonetic Alphabet.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Introduction to Phonology
courses.description: Introduction to the description and analysis of the sound patterns of natural language. Focus is on developing analytical skills for approaching data from a typologically diverse set of languages.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Introduction to Morphology
courses.description: How meaning is encoded in words in the languages of the world. Morphological and morphophonemic processes, lexical categories, derivation and inflection, productivity, tense, aspect, mode, case, concord, valence changes (passives, antipassives, benefactives, causatives), morphological typologies.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Introduction to Syntax
courses.description: Similarities and differences among languages in the grammatical devices they use to signal relations between words in phrases and sentences. Data from a range of languages is presented and analyzed.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Foundations of Computational Linguistics
courses.prereq_text: Linguistics 102 or Computer Science 8 or equivalent experience.
courses.description: An introduction to foundational ideas in computational linguistics, such as: n-gram language models; noisy channel models; supervised and unsupervised learning; and distributional semantics. Focus on developing an understanding of the intuitions behind the ideas, including relevant algorithms and math, and implementing this understanding in hands-on programming applications.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Advanced Computational Linguistics: Text Processing
courses.description: Advanced topics in the computational processing of language in text form, such as: neural network language models; parsing; topic modeling; and machine translation. Focus on developing a high-level understanding of modern approaches and how to use them. Discussion of applications to areas such as natural language processing, corpus linguistics, and computational psycholinguistics.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Introduction to Semantics
courses.description: Introduction to the study of meaning in language. Consideration of semantic fields, semantic components, semantic relations, categories, prototypes, frames, metaphor, pragmatics, indexicality, and speech acts.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Introduction to Historical Comparative Linguistics
courses.description: An introduction to linguistic change, genetic classification of languages, and methods of reconstructing parent languages.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: The Structure of Language and Sports
courses.description: Examines the usage of language in organized sports, with analysis at lexical, morphological, syntactic, discursive, and phonological levels. Investigates how linguistic structure adapts to particular communicative contexts, such as media accounts and interactions among participants.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Regional Dialects and Varieties of English Around the World
courses.description: Offers a comprehensive and in-depth survey of regional dialects of English throughout America and around the world. Examines dialect variation through both descriptive analysis as well as socio-historic accounts of the emergence of particular varieties.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Advanced Computational Linguistics: Speech Processing
courses.description: Advanced topics in the computational processing of language in spoken form, such as: forced alignment; speech recognition; speaker recognition; and text-to-speech. Focus on developing a high-level understanding of modern approaches and how to use them. Discussion of applications to areas such as natural language processing, corpus linguistics, and computational psycholinguistics.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Corpus Linguistics
courses.description: An introduction to computerized research methods which are applied to large databases of language used in natural communicative settings to supplement more traditional ways of linguistic analysis in all linguistic subdisciplines.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Discourse Analysis
courses.prereq_text: Linguistics 20 or 109, or consent of instructor.
courses.description: This course introduces students to the hands-on analysis of form and meaning in discourse, especially in naturally occurring conversation. Topics include referent accessibility, co-reference, and anaphora; resonance and coherence in dialogue; dialogue acts; constructions and information structure. Students learn to use basic computational tools for discourse analysis.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Neurolinguistics
courses.description: An examination of how the brain supports language structure and language use, with an emphasis on how electrophysiological, neuroimaging, and lesion data contribute to linguistic theory and to our understanding of the mental representation of language.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Psychology of Language
courses.description: An examination of the psychological foundations of language structure and use, including the cognitive processes involved in the comprehension, production, and recall of words, sentences, and discourse; first and second language acquisition; relationships among language, brain, cognition, and culture.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Sign Languages and Signing Communities
courses.description: An introduction to the linguistics of sign languages and signing communities, including early and current perceptions of deaf people and sign languages. Covers the emergence of sign languages and signing communities as well as the linguistic structures, sociolinguistic contexts, and acquisition of sign languages.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Language as Culture
courses.description: Views language through the lens of culture, exploring language as a sociocultural system that organizes meaning, memory, interpretation, authority, action, practice. How practices of speaking shape culture; intertextuality; linguistic and cultural relativity; relations between language, thought, and culture.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Sociocultural Linguistics
courses.description: The study of language as a social phenomenon, with emphasis on language use outside the U.S. context. Quantitative and qualitative approaches to regional and social dialects, register, linguistic power and solidarity, language contact and change, multilingualism, codeswitching, language shift and loss.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Language, Gender, and Sexuality
courses.description: The study of language as a resource for the production of gender and sexuality across cultures. Topics include: gender differentiation in language structure and use; intragender variation; language and discrimination; linguistic ideologies; language and identity.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Interdisciplinary Approaches to the Cultures, Languages, and Literatures of Latin America and Iberia
courses.comments: LAIS 102, LING 133, and SPAN 108 are the same course. LAIS 102S is the Spanish-language version of LAIS 102, LING 133, and SPAN 108, and is a legal repeat.
courses.description: Issues pertinent to the diverse cultures, languages, and literatures of Latin America and Iberia. Disciplines and approaches may include: pre-Columbian studies, Spanish and Spanish American literatures, Portuguese and Brazilian literatures, translation studies, cultural, gender, and queer studies, romance language and linguistics.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: North American Indigenous Languages
courses.description: Survey of the several hundred native languages of North America, including the history of research on these languages, their classification, special structures, and their oral traditions.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Memes: Theory and Analysis of Cultural Evolution
courses.description: This course examines the meme as the minimum unit of cultural evolution. Equal time is given to the theory of cultural evolution and hands-on analysis of memes. Focus on internet and pre-internet memes, including image-macro memes, videos, humor, proverbs, songs, games, words, technology, and other units of cultural evolution.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Introduction to First Language Acquisition
courses.prereq_text: Linguistics 20 and Linguistics 106; concurrent enrollment accepted.
courses.description: An introduction to the interdisciplinary enterprise of understanding first language acquisition, overview of different theoretical and methodological approaches, and introduction to developmental processes in sub-areas such as phonology, morphology, lexicon, syntax and semantics.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Introduction to Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages
courses.description: Surveys theoretical and methodological issues related to teaching English as a second or foreign language. Students examine current research and pedagogy in TESOL and development in second language acquisition theory and evaluate teaching materials and develop classroom lessons.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: English Grammar for Teachers
courses.description: Covers English grammatical structures commonly the focus of teaching English as an additional language. Also considers key issues related to grammar in language teaching, such as error correction and deductive versus inductive methods of instruction.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Second Language Acquisition
courses.description: An introduction to the theories and principles of how adults acquire a language other than their mother tongue, why it is more difficult than acquiring their first language, and what needs to be learned, from linguistic, psychological and social perspectives.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Phonological Typology
courses.description: An introduction to the diversity of sound systems found in languages of the world. Considers the cross-linguistic distribution of phonological patterns and their treatment in phonological history.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Articulatory Phonetics
courses.description: An introduction to the speech production system, with special focus on the articulatory structure of speech and the relation of this structure to the acoustic properties and perception of speech sounds. Considers the speech of populations with speech communication disorders, and presents an array of experimental techniques used to investigate speech.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Auditory Phonetics
courses.description: Introduction to the auditory processing of speech, including the physiology of hearing, neurological processing of speech, perception of pitch, loudness, and temporal properties, frequency resolution, models of speech perception, and hearing disorders.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Topics in Clinical Linguistics
courses.comments: May be repeated for additional credit provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: An introduction to clinical applications of linguistics relevant to speech-language pathology and audiology.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Introduction to Communication Sciences and Disorders
courses.comments: May be repeated for additional credit provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: An intro to the field of communication sciences and disorders. This course will bridge lectures to clinical application with guided observation hours. Content may vary.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Language Disorders
courses.comments: May be repeated for additional credit provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Introduces a broad overview of the differential characteristics of language disorders and the principles of assessment and treatment.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Speech Sound Disorders
courses.comments: May be repeated for additional credit provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Introduction to phonetic and phonological features of a variety of speech disorders affecting children and adults. Clinical manifestations in the acoustic, articulatory, perceptual, and cognitive domains will be considered with reference to normative baselines in both monolingual and multilingual contexts.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Practicum in Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages
courses.comments: Focused towards TESOL minors. Can be taken twice for up to 8 units total.
courses.description: Designed for students who are interested in teaching/tutoring English as a second or foreign language to adult learners, either abroad or in the United States. Through engagement with course curriculum/materials and through site-based observations, classroom and small group/individual teaching opportunities, and pedagogical feedback from a mentor teacher, practicum students will develop experiential knowledge regarding the applications of theoretical and pedagogical concepts in the teaching and learning of English as an additional language.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: On-site Introductory Practicum
courses.comments: Focused towards TESOL minors. Can be taken twice for up to 8 units total.
courses.description: Designed for students who are interested in teaching/tutoring English as a second or foreign language to adult learners, either abroad or in the United States. Course content will vary.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Intercultural Communication
courses.prereq_text: Any Linguistics or Communications course or consent of instructor.
courses.description: Explores communication (verbal, nonverbal, mediated) between people from different cultural backgrounds. Topics include intersecting identities (national/regional, race/ethnicity, linguistic, gender, sexual orientation, etc.), intercultural relationships, cultural transitions, and intercultural conflict and dialogue. Integrates insights from social scientific, interpretive, and critical research.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Language Documentation
courses.description: Issues in the creation of lasting multipurpose records of a language. Documentation as collaborative, community-based initiative. Description and documentation, archive creation, metadata, technologies, materials, ethics, ethnography, orthography, and multimedia. Students participate in a collaborative documentation project as primary coursework.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Clinical Research in Speech-Language Pathology
courses.comments: Open to LING majors and minors. Students should register for 1 unit per 3 hours of average weekly work they plan to invest in the course. Contact the instructor with any questions about the appropriate unit load.
courses.description: Collaborative and individualized research on clinical applications of linguistics for speech-language pathology. Hands-on training in all aspects of the clinical research process.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Professionalization in Speech-Language Pathology
courses.prereq_text: Open to LING-SLSD majors and minors or by permission of instructor.
courses.comments: Open to LING SLSD majors and minors only; non-SLSD LING majors and minors will need the instructor's permission.
courses.description: Professional preparation for graduate studies and a career in speech-language pathology. Topics include identifying graduate/postbaccalaureate programs, résumé and dossier development, professional memberships and conferences.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Clinical Practicum in Speech-Language Pathology
courses.prereq_text: Open to LING SLSD majors and minors; or by permission of instructor.
courses.description: Observation hours and placement in clinical settings; training in case evaluation and documentation.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Trans Linguistics
courses.prereq_text: Must have taken one of the following courses: LING 130, 131, 132, 136, OR have consent of instructor.
courses.description: An exploration of language in relation to transgender, non-binary, and gender diverse communities and topics. Uses the tools of linguistics to consider pronouns and grammatical gender; inclusive language, linguistic justice, and language activism; gendered bodies and voices; language and transphobia; and trans representation in mediatized contexts.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: The Structure of English
courses.description: Introduction to the phonological, morphological, syntactic and discourse features of contemporary English.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Structuring and Transforming Data
courses.description: Developing essential data science skills for linguistics and related fields. Data modeling, database design, advanced data formats, and tools for transforming, integrating, and aggregating heterogeneous data. Emphasis on collaboration, practical problem-solving, and reproducible workflows that reflect the practices of modern industry and interdisciplinary research. A goal is for students to be able to design, manage, and analyze structured data in diverse research contexts.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Language in Social Interaction
courses.description: What role does language play in social interaction? How do individuals use language to shape relationships with others within or across social groups? How do patterns of linguistic interaction constitute patterns of social organization? Emphasis on hands-on analysis of transcriptions and recordings of face-to-face interactions.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Language, Race, and Ethnicity
courses.description: Linguistic practices of major ethnoracial groups in the United States, including African Americans, Asian Americans, European Americans, Latinxs, and Native Americans; examination of the linguistic effects of immigration and colonialism; bilingualism, translanguaging, language shift, and heritage language learning; linguistic interaction and contact between ethnoracial groups; language as a resource for ethnoracial identity; linguistic racism; linguistic activism.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Languages of the World
courses.description: Introduction to the languages of the world: Geographical distribution; genetic (genealogical) classification, including comparison with genetics and archeology; structural properties and sociolinguistics of selected languages representing different parts of the world.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Language, Power and Learning
courses.prereq_text: Departmental Approval Required to Finalize Registration.
courses.comments: Same course as CH ST 187.
courses.description: Critical examination of institutional power related to education and linguistic and cultural diversity. Focus on Latinx communities; formal and informal learning; family practices; bilingual education; heritage languages; language and labor; language and racism; immigrant languages; racialized varieties of English.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Internship in Linguistics
courses.description: Internship in a language-related work setting. Students apply concepts, methods, and issues from linguistics to professional contexts in education, business, government, nonprofit organizations and other fields.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Capstone Seminar
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division course in linguistics; consent of instructor.
courses.comments: Misc: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 193/199/199RA courses combined.
courses.description: Original individual or collaborative research, creative, or action project in linguistics, typically taken in conjunction with LING 195 or equivalent. Weekly discussion of work in progress and professional preparation for graduate school in a workshop setting.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Group Studies in Linguistics
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units.
courses.description: Limited to small groups whose interest and needs determine the central focus.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Honors Thesis
courses.comments: Students must have a 3.5 GPA in the major. A two-quarter in-sequence course with final grade awarded upon completion of Linguistics 195B.
courses.description: Guided research and writing of an original research paper to meet the requirements of the honors program in Linguistics.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Honors Thesis.
courses.comments: Students must have a 3.5 GPA in the major. A two-quarter in-sequence course with final grade awarded upon completion of Linguistics 195B.
courses.description: Guided research and writing of an original research paper to meet the requirements of the honors program in Linguistics.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Honors Thesis
courses.comments: Students must have a 3.5 GPA in the major.
courses.description: Guided research and writing of an original research paper to meet the requirements of the honors program in Linguistics.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Independent Studies In Linguistics.
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division courses in linguistics; consent of instructor.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 193/199/199RA courses combined. Admission by special arrangement.
courses.description: Intended for the study of special areas within Linguistics.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Research Methodology and Statistics in Linguistics
courses.description: Fundamentals of scientific inquiry and methodology; basics of experimental design, statistical methods (descriptive and analytic) relevant to linguistics such as chi-squared, testing of distributions and means, simple correlation and regression.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Advanced Research Methods and Statistics
courses.description: Multifactorial and multivariate statistical methods for analyzing observational and experimental data in linguistics: basic linear and generalized linear modeling for numeric, categorical, count, and proportion data; exploratory cluster analysis; graphical methods for data exploration.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Statistical Methodology
courses.description: More advanced aspects of (generalized) linear modeling (planned contrasts, polynomials), robust statistics, mixed-effects/multilevel modeling; conditional inference trees; more advanced cluster-analytic methods; bootstrapping.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Foundations of Computational Linguistics
courses.prereq_text: Linguistics 102 or Linguistics 205 or Computer Science 8 or equivalent experience.
courses.description: An introduction to foundational ideas in computational linguistics, such as: n-gram language models; noisy channel models; supervised and unsupervised learning; and distributional semantics. Focus on developing an understanding of the intuitions behind the ideas, including relevant algorithms and math, and implementing this understanding in hands-on programming applications.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Experimental Methods in Linguistics
courses.description: Provides hands-on experience in techniques required for the process of designing and analyzing psycholinguistic experiments. This course provides the opportunity to develop an experiment, from the formulation of a research question to the interpretation of results.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Discourse Transcription
courses.description: Methods for transcribing conversational discourse, with focus on discourse features relevant to linguistic and interactional research. Features include pause, laughter, intonation, voice, speaker overlap, turn-taking, participation, others. Recording natural conversation, computer-assisted transcription, transcription as theory, alternative transcription systems, transcription ethics/politics.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Neural Networks in Linguistics
courses.prereq_text: Linguistics 102 or Linguistics 205 or equivalent background.
courses.description: An overview of symbolic modeling approaches and their use in psycholinguistics/computational linguistics. The course covers the foundational principles behind simulation-based approaches including connectionist models, PDP models, and ANN/RNN models and the insights these give us into the representations and mechanisms supporting language use in the human mind. The course also provides an opportunity to implement a simple symbolic model for the purposes of testing linguistic theory.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Grammar Writing
courses.description: Training in writing a description of a language, including critical review of selected existing grammars, discussion of contents, and practice in writing.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Corpus Linguistics
courses.description: An introduction to computerized research methods, which are applied to large data bases of language used in natural communicative settings to supplement more traditional methods of linguistic analysis in all linguistic subdisciplines.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Corpus Construction
courses.description: Design and construction of electronic corpora to represent spoken or written forms of language. Data collection from electronically available text/transcripts, linguistic fieldwork, archives. Issues of sampling, balancedness, representativity, scale; formatting, markup, annotation, coding, tools; archival preservation, orthography, politics, ethics.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Prosody
courses.description: Perceptual and acoustic aspects of pitch, amplitude, and tempo and their interaction with discourse. Comparison of prosodic theories.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Field Methods
courses.comments: A three-quarter in-progress sequence course with grades for all quarters issued upon completion of Linguistics 221C.
courses.description: Introduction to fieldwork and language documentation. Students work with a speaker of a language unknown to the students for three consecutive quarters. Techniques of data collection, elicitation, management, and analysis. Emphases include collaborative research, theoretical contextualization of field data, and descriptive and theoretical writing.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Field Methods
courses.comments: A three-quarter in-progress sequence course with grades for all quarters issued upon completion of Linguistics 221C.
courses.description: Introduction to fieldwork and language documentation. Students work with a speaker of a language unknown to the students for three consecutive quarters. Techniques of data collection, elicitation, management, and analysis. Emphases include collaborative research, theoretical contextualization of field data, and descriptive and theoretical writing.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Field Methods
courses.comments: A three-quarter in-progress sequence course with grades for all quarters issued upon completion of Linguistics 221C.
courses.description: Introduction to fieldwork and language documentation. Students work with a speaker of a language unknown to the students for three consecutive quarters. Techniques of data collection, elicitation, management, and analysis. Emphases include collaborative research, theoretical contextualization of field data, and descriptive and theoretical writing.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Typology and Universals
courses.description: Reading and discussion of major contributions to the literature in typology and universals, focusing on such problems as lexical categories, systems of case marking, voice, reflexives, tense-aspect-mood, and relative clauses.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Languages in Contact
courses.description: Types, causes, mechanisms, and consequences of contact induced language change, including a consideration of pidgins and creoles.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Cognitive Foundations of Language
courses.description: A psycholinguistic overview of the relationship between language and cognition, including the nature of categories and the process of categorization; processes involved in the production and comprehension of lexicon, syntax and discourse; priming; psycholinguistic models of these processes and of first language acquisition; and the nature of mental representations.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Language as Culture
courses.description: Examines language through the lens of culture, taking culture as the pattern that gives meaning to social life. Culture of linguistic structure, practice, cognition. Classic readings in linguistic anthropology, sociocultural linguistics through current research linking language, thought, culture.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Discourse Practice and Social Interaction
courses.description: This course explores language in action via the practices participants enact in social interaction. Focus on understanding linguistic action in contexts of sequence, activity, stance, field, frame, intersubjectivity, dialogicality, voice, identity, participation, communities of practice. Close analysis of recorded interaction.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Linguistics of Sign Languages
courses.description: A comprehensive introduction to the linguistics of sign languages. Discussion of different theoretical and methodological approaches to investigating lexicons and grammars of sign languages, sociolinguistics of diverse signing communities, and practical, and ethical issues for conducting sign language research.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Methods in Sociocultural Linguistics
courses.description: Field methodologies for research on language, culture, and society. Topics include ethics and politics of research, ethnographic methods, interviewing, audio and video data collection, fieldnotes, relationship between fieldwork and analysis. Students carry out original field research during the quarter.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Foundations of Sociocultural Linguistics
courses.description: Investigates sociocultural theories of language as developed in linguistics, anthropology, sociology, philosophy and other fields. A comparative survey of the major theoretical issues in the field both historically and in the present day, with an emphasis on the relationship between theory and empirical analysis.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Language, Gender, and Sexuality
courses.description: Advanced study of the linguistic dimensions of gender and sexuality. Emphasis on the role of language in feminist theory and gender theory; evaluation and application of research methods.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Advanced Syntax
courses.description: Functional approaches to syntax. Methods of syntactic description and explanation. Survey of clause-level syntactic structures in diverse languages.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Advanced Phonology
courses.description: Review of articulatory and acoustic phonetics and method of phonological description and analysis. Current issues in phonological theory. Survey of phonological patterns and systems in diverse languages.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: African-American Language and Culture
courses.description: This advanced sociolinguistics course examines the linguistic, literary, cultural, and communicative aspects of African-American language across the African-American Diaspora. We blend diachronic and synchronic methodologies in order to create community-based participatory research approaches to the study of African-Americans and their language.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Topics in Phonetics and Phonology
courses.description: Specialized topics in phonetics and phonology.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Topics in Sign Language Lingusitics
courses.description: Specialized topics in sign language linguistics. Topics may include theories and research methods that are specific to sign languages and deaf signing communities, practices of documentation and description of sign languages from grammar to interaction, and research ethics. Students may develop their own new projects, focus on existing projects, or participate in a collaborative project as primary coursework.
