courses.title: Seminar in Sociocultural Linguistics
courses.prereq_text: Linguistics 227 or 228 or 230 or 232; and Linguistics 258A.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit. Must be taken for a letter grade.
courses.description: Specialized topics in sociocultural linguistics.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Trans Linguistics
courses.description: Advanced introduction to the field of trans linguistics. Emphasis on the development of trans linguistic theory; cultivating trans linguistic methods; and opportunities for greater engagement between linguists and trans communities. Considers a range of identities, practices, languages, and cultural contexts.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Advanced Language Change
courses.description: Types of theories of language change. Language families and subgroups. Internal and comparative reconstruction. The interpretation of historical records. Dialectology; sociolinguistic factors in language change and processes of grammaticization. Ramifications of observed changes for synchronic theories of language structure.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Syntax Beyond the Clause
courses.description: Functional approaches to the syntax of multi-clausal constructions, including relative clause structures; complements; adverbial clauses; clause chaining; and issues of clause-combining, co-ordination and subordination.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Writing in Linguistics
courses.description: Academic writing for publication in scholarly journals in linguistics. Individualized meetings and/or small-group workshop format.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Research Orientation
courses.comments: May not be applied toward the M.A. or Ph.D. degree requirements.
courses.description: Sequence of lectures by faculty of the Linguistics Department and closely related departments, to acquaint new graduate students with current faculty research, and with research directions and resources of the campus.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Linguistics Colloquium
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit. May not be applied toward the M.A. or Ph.D. degree requirements.
courses.description: Presentations on current topics in linguistics by visiting scholars, faculty, and graduate students.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Proseminar in Language, Interaction, and Social Organization
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit. Same course as Sociology 274 and Education 274.
courses.description: Discussion of current research, literature, and theoretical and methodological issues in language and social interaction.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Teaching Assistant Seminar
courses.comments: No credit allowed toward advanced degree.
courses.description: Covers development of teaching techniques.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Language Socialization
courses.description: What is the role of language in the process by which a child becomes a member of a particular culture? Topics include the acquisition of culture-specific ways of talking about emotions, enacting gender roles, having arguments and producing narratives.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Seminar in the Discipline of Linguistics
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit.
courses.description: Specialized topics in the discipline of linguistics.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Seminar in the Discipline of Linguistics
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit.
courses.description: Specialized topics in the discipline of linguistics.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Graduate Group Studies in Linguistics
courses.description: Limited to small groups whose interest and needs determine the central focus.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Laboratory Phonetics
courses.description: This course teaches students how to conduct research using an array of experimental protocols examining different aspects of articulatory production, motor control and timing in speech. Students receive training in techniques such as ultrasound, electromagnetic articulography (EMA), electroglottography (EGG), and plethysmography. Special focus will be given to constructing experimental designs fit for each methodology as well as understanding the theoretical goals that can be achieved with each of them. Our discussion will draw extensions across languages and across different types of disordered speech.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Language Documentation Lab
courses.description: Students meet to discuss topics in language documentation, share skills, and present their ongoing research.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Graduate Studies
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit.
courses.description: Graduate credit given for an upper-division course with additional work at the graduate level.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Teaching Assistant Practicum
courses.prereq_text: Appointment as teaching assistant and departmental approval.
courses.comments: No unit credit allowed toward degree.
courses.description: Supervised teaching of undergraduate linguistics courses and instruction-related activities.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Teaching Assistant Seminar
courses.comments: No credit allowed toward advanced degree.
courses.description: Covers development of teaching techniques.

courses.title: Research in Linguistics

courses.description: Research under the direction of a faculty member(s).

courses.title: Seminar Paper

courses.description: The second quarter continuation of a MA-level elective course. May be taken only once during a student's career to satisfy one of the Ph.D. level seminar requirements. May not be taken as the continuation of an MA-level required course.

courses.title: Lab in Linguistics
courses.description: Research and professional development activities in a collaborative lab setting.

courses.title: Directed Reading and Research
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit.
courses.description: Individual tutorial in any area of linguistics.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Individual Study for Master's and Ph.D.
courses.prereq_text: Consent of instructor and graduate advisor.
courses.comments: No unit credit allowed toward advanced degree.
courses.description: Instructor should be student's major professor or chair of the committee.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Master's Thesis Research and Preparation
courses.prereq_text: Consent of instructor and graduate advisor.
courses.description: Instructor normally should be chair of the student's thesis committee. Only for research underlying the thesis, writing the thesis.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Ph.D. Dissertation Research and Preparation
courses.prereq_text: Instructor approval required prior to registration.
courses.description: Ph.D. dissertation research and preparation.

courses.subject: LING W
courses.title: EMS: Academic English
courses.prereq_text: Open to students who have a Ling 3B placement or a prerequisite of Ling 3A with a pass grade.
courses.comments: LING W 3B is the online version of LING 3B.
courses.description: Second level in a three-course series intended to develop proficiency in university-level reading and writing. Emphasizes applying critical approaches to reading, practicing writing in a variety of academic styles, and developing grammatical and lexical resources appropriate to a university setting.

courses.subject: LING W
courses.title: EMS: Academic English
courses.prereq_text: Open to students who have a Ling 3C placement; or Linguistics 3B with a minimum grade of C.
courses.comments: LING W 3C is the online version of LING 3C
courses.description: Third level in a three-course series intended to develop proficiency in university-level reading and writing. Emphasizes applying critical approaches to reading, practicing writing in a variety of academic styles, and developing grammatical and lexical resources appropriate to a university setting.

courses.subject: LING W
courses.title: EMS: Approaches to University Writing for Multilingual Students
courses.prereq_text: Open to students who have not satisfied the Entry Level Writing Requirement and have a Ling 12 placement or a prerequisite of Ling 3C with a grade of C or better.
courses.comments: LING W 12 is the online version of LING 12.
courses.description: Principles of critical reading, thinking and writing in the university. Students analyze academic discourse, develop rhetorical strategies for exposition and argument, practice examination writing, and write and revise papers. Completion of C or better meets Entry Level Writing Requirement.

courses.subject: LING W
courses.title: Language in Life
courses.description: Overview of language and its role in communities at home and around the world. The diversity and history of languages; their norms, conventions, and written traditions; the role of language in culture and identity; language rights and multilingualism, and the implications of technology for language use.

courses.subject: LING W
courses.title: Introduction to Phonetics
courses.description: An introduction to the articulatory and acoustic properties of speech sounds. Survey of speech sounds found in the languages of the world. Emphasis on ear training and transcription using the International Phonetic Alphabet.

courses.subject: LING W
courses.title: Language in Social Interaction
courses.comments: LING W 170 is the online version of LING 170.
courses.description: What role does language play in social interaction? How do individuals use language to shape relationships with others within or across social groups? How do patterns of linguistic interaction constitute patterns of social organization? Emphasis on hands-on analysis of transcriptions and recordings of face-to-face interactions.

courses.subject: LING W
courses.title: Language Construction
courses.description: This course introduces and applies concepts of language construction. Constructed languages are fictionalized systems of linguistic communication, developed for a range of contexts, including for hobbyists, role-playing games, and film & literature. They offer an opportunity to explore fundamentals and diversity within and across real-world languages.

courses.subject: MARINCS
courses.title: Group Studies
courses.description: Student-directed discussion and study in a variety of subjects within Marine Science.

courses.subject: MARINCS
courses.title: Introduction to Marine Science
courses.description: Introduces students to the field of Marine Science. Students will build key skills in reading and writing comprehension within the discipline, navigating marine science research opportunities on campus, and explore diverse ways of knowing in marine science.

courses.subject: MARINCS
courses.title: Modern Practices in Marine Science
courses.description: This modularized course will introduce students to important topics in modern marine science including treatment of data, scientific ethics, scientific writing, scientific presentations, the practice of interdisciplinary research, and the campus marine science research portfolio.

courses.subject: MARINCS
courses.title: Marine Data Science
courses.description: An introduction to scientific computing, reproducibility, and open science in the context of marine science. Emphasis on sources and forms of data commonly used in marine research, including satellite imagery, ocean circulation models, and vessel AIS.

courses.subject: MARINCS
courses.title: Speaker Seminar Series
courses.description: This course will run concurrently with the Graduate Marine Science Speaker Seminar Series and will introduce students to a breadth of marine science topics and cutting-edge research. Student will build foundations in the topic of research, as well practice key professional competencies to prepare for these research seminars.

courses.subject: MARINCS
courses.title: Chemical Oceanography
courses.description: An introduction to the chemistry of the oceans. Topics include composition and chemical equilibria of seawater, biogeochemical cycling, sediment chemistry, atmospheric exchange, circulation and rates of mixing based on chemical tracers, and the impact of ocean chemistry on climate change.

courses.subject: MARINCS
courses.title: Biological Oceanography
courses.description: Current concepts in biological oceanography focusing on the coupling of biotic processes to ocean physics, chemistry and sedimentation. Emphasis on areas of active research with critical evaluation of current and seminal literature.

courses.subject: MARINCS
courses.title: Introduction to Physical Oceanography
courses.description: A quantitative introduction to physical oceanography. Topics discussed include: properties of sea water, derivation and application of the equations of motion for a rotating planet, and the dynamics of wind- and buoyancy-driven general circulation.

courses.subject: MARINCS
courses.title: Geological Oceanography
courses.description: Morphology, formation, and evolution of ocean basins; crustal structure and composition of ocean margins; source and composition of marine sediments; marine sediment as repository of paleoclimate and paleo-ocean circulation records. Paleoceanographic changes in relation to tectonics and changes in orbital parameters, links between changes in ocean circulation and climate changes.

courses.subject: MARINCS
courses.title: Marine Ecology & Conservation Biology
courses.description: Provides an in-depth understanding of the biotic and abiotic interactions that determine ecological processes in marine environments, how these processes shape the structure of marine ecosystems, and how these principles are used to direct marine conservation and management.

courses.subject: MARINCS
courses.title: Biologging Data Science
courses.description: An advanced data science course with applications to biologging technologies. Topics include history of animal tracking technologies, analysis of sensor data (emphasis on GPS, accelerometry, and audio), and modeling approaches for animal movement.

courses.subject: MARINCS
courses.title: Special Topics in Marine Science
courses.description: This course will introduce students to a topical area of marine science. Topics will vary by instructor and quarter.

courses.title: Marine Science Seminar
courses.prereq_text: Designed for majors. Non-majors require consent of the instructor to finalize enrollment.
courses.description: Research seminar in marine science.

courses.title: Marine Science Strategies & Practices for Creating Scientific Presentations
courses.prereq_text: Designed for majors. Non-majors require consent of the instructor to finalize enrollment.
courses.description: Upper division course in which we will explore strategies and practices for creating scientific presentations.

courses.subject: MARINCS
courses.title: Marine Science Rooftop Roundtable
courses.description: This seminar introduces students to the UCSB marine science enterprise through discussions with faculty and staff that comprise the enterprise.

courses.subject: MARINCS
courses.title: Field Studies in Marine Science
courses.description: This course sequence provides students an opportunity to prepare for and conduct individualized marine science field and oceanographic research under the guidance of a faculty member.

courses.title: Marine Science Capstone
courses.description: This course will provide individualized structure and facilitation for research and other creative activities undertaken by the student in their senior year.

courses.description: Serious independent study in marine science with consenting faculty member.

courses.description: A series of lectures and seminars on diverse research topics in marine science.

courses.description: For research underlying the thesis and writing of the thesis.

courses.subject: MARSC
courses.title: Ph.D. Dissertation Preparation
courses.prereq_text: Ph.D. candidate and consent of instructor.
courses.description: For writing of the dissertation.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Introduction into Media, Arts, Design, Engineering, and Science in a Computational Context
courses.description: Introduces students to the technology/art/science/society/creativity/computation matrix. Covers the history of this field, and a set of conceptual and theoretical strategies that will enable them to navigate this complex transdisciplinary environment.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Mediated Worlds: MAT
courses.description: Integrative overview of media arts and technologies, emphasizing the interconnections between technologies and humanities (means and ends), engineering and mathematics (concrete and abstract), and arts and science (synthesis and analysis). The THEMAS model proposes a continuum across disciplines previously separated by narrow specializations. It builds upon the successes of STEM/STEAM, with greater emphasis on the humanities, creativity, and synthesis.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Mediated Worlds/THEMAS Arts+Sciences Emphasis
courses.description: Integrative overview of media arts and technologies, emphasizing the interconnections between technologies and humanities (means and ends), engineering and mathematics (concrete and abstract), and arts and science (synthesis and analysis). The THEMAS model proposes a continuum across disciplines previously separated by narrow specializations. This class emphasizes Arts+Sciences (synthesis/analysis) within the overall model of THEMAS.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Mediated Worlds/THEMAS Engineering+Mathematics Emphasis
courses.description: Integrative overview of media arts and technologies, emphasizing the interconnections between technologies and humanities (means and ends), engineering and mathematics (concrete and abstract), and arts and science (synthesis and analysis). The THEMAS model proposes a continuum across disciplines previously separated by narrow specializations. This class emphasizes Engineering+Mathematics (concrete/abstract) within the overall model of THEMAS.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Mediated Worlds/THEMAS Technologies+Humanities Emphasis
courses.description: Integrative overview of media arts and technologies, emphasizing the interconnections between technologies and humanities (means and ends), engineering and mathematics (concrete and abstract), and arts and science (synthesis and analysis). The THEMAS model proposes a continuum across disciplines previously separated by narrow specializations. This class emphasizes Technologies+Humanities (means/ends) within the overall model of THEMAS.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Mediated Worlds: Enacting the Metaverse - Generative Worldmaking and Virtual Reality
courses.description: Enacting the Metaverse studies the imminent integration of real and virtual worlds. Recent advancements in parallel computation have fueled the growth of transformative new technologies. Artificial intelligence performs tasks at a level that exceeds human ability. Blockchain technology enables virtual ownership of digital assets. Extended reality augments and reconfigures our experience of the world. The metaverse is the outgrowth of these technologies. It is a shared virtual 3D world that intermeshes with the real. We will be the citizens of this new hyper-mediated world. It is our responsibility to confront these developments from technical and critical perspectives. This course develops the knowledge and skills needed.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Mediated Worlds:THEMAS Special Topics:(E)Utopian Design Tools
courses.description: A making-based, creative-computing class examining eutopian (good, possible) vs. utopian (ideal, impossible) design. The course explores the operationalization of positive and innovative change via multimedia worldmaking and speculative design through the transdisciplinary lens of THEMAS (STEM/STEAM+creative Humanities).

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Media Arts and Design Concepts
courses.description: Courses exploring the intersection of art and technology, including its broader social impacts and ethical implications. Topics vary.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Media Arts and Design Concepts: MAD Concepts - Fundamental Concepts of Media Arts and Design
courses.description: Media Arts and Design: Concepts and Fundamentals is an introductory course that covers the principles and practices of media arts and design. Students learn to create digital graphics, audio compositions, and video productions using digital tools and technologies. The course adopts a hands-on approach, emphasizing emerging design techniques such as generative artificial intelligence, parametric design, and algorithmic composition. The course challenges students to critically evaluate the role of media arts and design in contemporary society. The course format includes two in-person lecture sessions and one section per week, with a focus on technological literacy, software proficiency, and computational design.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Media Arts and Design Skills
courses.description: Project-based course with an emphasis on technical skills within the context of digital arts or music. Topics vary.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: MAD Skills: Audio Engineering, Sound Design, and Generative Music Systems
courses.description: This project-based course will cover concepts in audio mixing, editing, and sound design. You will learn fundamentals of audio engineering through recording and producing original audio tracks, develop skills in audio programming to create bespoke audio effects and generative music systems, gain skills using industry-standard audio software Ableton Live as well as Max4Live, get a chance to collaborate and work alongside other creators here on campus, and have your work showcased in an event at the end of the session.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Media Arts and Design Skills: MAD Skills - Fundamental Skills of Media Arts and Design
courses.description: Media Arts and Design Skills - Fundamental Skills is an introductory course that focuses on the skills and practices of media arts and design. Students identify a theme and explore it through reading and making over six weeks. The course emphasizes a hands-on approach and requires physical evidence of students' efforts. Students analyze successful architects, designers, and artists who defined the areas of media, arts, and design. The course format includes two in-person lectures and one in-person section per week, with a focus on producing examples for the final project. The end goal is a successful final project presented in an exhibition format on campus.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Musical Computation & Design
courses.description: Investigates the musical potential in seemingly non-musical systems through computational design principles. Students engage in compositional experimentation by translating patterns from architecture, quantum fields, biology, and linguistics into musical form. Develops both technical and creative competencies, welcoming arts/humanities students exploring computational thinking and STEM students pursuing creative expression. Concepts introduced from first principles with emphasis on discovery and exploration. No prior knowledge of music theory, programming, or referenced fields required.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Designing Technology through Diverse Cultural Practices
courses.description: This course redefines technology by examining Black, Indigenous and other diverse computational contributions to global innovation. Students explore practices like braiding and crocheting as algorithmic design; DJing as data manipulation and signal processing; and sustainable film development as an alternative approach to materials science. Hands-on projects uncover the computational principles embedded in these traditions, challenging students to rethink technology, embrace new paradigms of creativity and develop technical skills and cultural awareness. Students of all levels of familiarity with technology, art and design are welcome.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Physical Computing for Design
courses.description: This introductory course explores the intersection of electronics, computation, and creative practice, empowering students to design interactive systems, instruments, and interfaces using microcontrollers, sensors, and actuators. Emphasizing hands-on learning, it bridges the digital and physical realms to create expressive, multi-sensory experiences. Students will prototype interactive objects and devices, gaining technical skills and a creative mindset to engage with technologies like IoT, wearable computing, and interactive installations. No prior experience is required—only curiosity and enthusiasm for experimentation.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: MAD Skills: Materialize: Prototyping and Fabrication
courses.description: Covers the entire process from concept design to detailed plans, and students navigate it using traditional sketching and cutting-edge AI tools. Practical lessons in laser cutting and 3D printing empower students to create multi-material constructs, emphasizing iterative design processes to refine outcomes. The course is partly held in the Library Makerspace, and it includes hands-on sections promoting active learning. Students culminate their learning in a final project, where they explore innovative form factors, interactive prototypes, and fabrication practices.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: MAD Skills: Web-Based Interactive Narratives
courses.description: This course offers a hands-on approach to learning creative coding, enabling students to design and develop web-based interactive stories with a blend of text, images, sound, and interactions. The curriculum will introduce narrative structures, creative coding techniques, and the basics of web design and development. Projects range from simple animations to complex, user-driven narratives. No prior coding experience is required.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Extended Reality and Worldmaking
courses.description: Extended Reality (XR) shapes how people experience emotion, narrative, and embodiment. This course approaches XR as a worldmaking practice, treating virtual space as an interface through which cultural and experiential meaning emerges. Students explore XR environments as sites of empathy, identity, and relationality, connecting critical theory with hands-on spatial storytelling. Through readings, case studies, and prototyping, students create XR experiences using Unity3D, photogrammetry, Gaussian splatting, and selected AI-based tools. The course culminates in a first-person XR walking simulator presented in VR. Instruction begins from foundational concepts, and no prior coding or XR experience is required.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Media Arts and Design Capstone
courses.description: Capstone course for the Media Arts and Design Minor. Synthesizes learning from other Media Arts and Design courses through the development of a digital portfolio and meetings with guest speakers.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Arts and Technology
courses.description: Overview of the digital media arts field with an emphasis on technological developments and their integration in art research and production. Students are introduced to contemporary and historical directions and methodologies through seminar lectures, research presentation, and a final project.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Music and Technology
courses.description: Overview of music and technology, including historical aspects. Readings and exercises with a range of music software applications. Basics of Internet audio and evolving media, music production, business, technical, and aesthetic aspects.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Digital Media Technology and Engineering
courses.description: This course surveys pattern formation mechanisms. Many complex visual phenomena can be generated from less than 100 lines of code, such as the Mandelbrot set, reaction-diffusion, and the Lorenz attractor. We will study and implement a variety of these phenomena.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Media Signal Processing
courses.description: Basic concepts in digital signal and image processing (transforms, convolutions, etc.), filter design, image enhancement and coding, digital video.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Computing with Media Data
courses.description: Hands-on introduction to developing multimedia applications. Representation and perception of sound, images, and time. Media computing paradigms including OOP, callbacks, multithreading, OpenGL, distributed computing, algorithmic control, indeterminacy, real-time interactivity, and mapping data between sensory modalities. Students develop a series of audiovisual works (as C++ software) leading to a final project.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: CREATE Ensemble
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing in MAT or MUS or consent of instructor
courses.description: Hands on practical approach to composition, improvisation, critique, refinement, and research dedicated to live performance. Open to laptops, new interfaces for artistic expression, audiovisual art, live coding, local and/or wide area networked performance, interactive dance, music for acoustic and electronic instruments, performance art, trans-categorical live performance, etc.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Computational Systems for Visual Art and Design
courses.description: Computational systems of rules, relationships, and behaviors can extend traditional art and design practices or support new creative workflows. We will explore the creation of computational systems for visual art and design.We will use creative coding platforms and algorithms to create visual works that are flexible, dynamic, and generative. In the process, we will touch onthe design philosophy and abstractions of existing creative coding platforms and examine methods to create alternatives. Students learn basic approaches to modify creative programming languages and frameworks or develop new software interfaces for visual expression. Technical production will be complemented by readings on computational art and design theory.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Designing Expressive Technologies
courses.description: Computational tools create new opportunities for making things, yet designing expressive computational systems poses many challenges.Addressing these challenges requires finding ways to integrate rigorous and structured research and development methodologies with observations of real-world creative production, and dialog and collaboration with different kinds of makers. This course is for Ph.D and Masters students with an interest in researching and designingcomputational technologies for art, design, manufacturing, or craft. The course is run as a seminar involving discussion of readings and concepts presented in lecture and exploration of human-computer interaction research methodologies.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Computational Fabrication
courses.description: Computational fabrication enables people to design digital forms by writing code and then construct these forms, at least partially, via fabrication machines, like 3D printers and computer-numerical-controlled (CNC) machines.In this course, students explore tools, workflows, representations, and applications of computational fabrication. Students are instructed in theuse of computer-aided-design software tools and programming languages aimed at the design of physical artifacts. The course also covers the process of converting digital designs to physical form through computer-aided machining (CAM) for different forms of additive and subtractive CNC machines.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Digital Audio Programming: The Series
courses.description: A six-quarter practical programming course devoted to digital audio applications development. The emphasis is on learning to use current state-of-the-art programming methods, tools, and library APIs. Programming assignments are given in the C, C++, Java, Smalltalk and/or SuperCollider programming language. Topics: A. Using Commerical I/O APIs; B. Spectral Transformations; C. Spatial Sound Manipulation; D. Sound Synthesis Techniques; E. Multi-rate Control and Synchronization; F. Media Application Integration.

Spatial Sound Manipulation; D. Sound Synthesis Techniques; E. Multi-rate Control and Synchronization; F. Media Application Integration.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Advanced Lessons in Media Composition
courses.description: This is a studio-based course in media composition for making media art works for advanced students working on their portfolios. We will deal with the compositional process with regard to multimodal content that unfolds over time and space. The object of this seminar is to make, and also to discuss our compositional processes as we build our portfolios. Each student will work on their individual or group project and will present work each week. We can meet as a group and individually as well. During the class/lab sessions, students will also bring in various works and readings from artists and researchers from which their philosophy of making is being drawn.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Arts-Engineering Research
courses.description: Theoretical and applied directions in arts-engineering research.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: AI Image Generation
courses.description: Part I will focus on AI still image production in Stable Diffusion with the ComfyUI interface, and Part II will explore time-based video production. Concurrent with production, the course will review current literature addressing issues of Deep Fakes, and the impact of artificial intelligence on image making, belief, and the broader cultural responses.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Art and Science of Aerospace Culture
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 16 units. Letter grade required for majors.
courses.description: Interdisciplinary course/seminar/practice for artists, academics, engineers, and designers interested in exploring the technological aesthetic, cultural, and political aspects of the space side of the aerospace complex. Design history, space complex aesthetics, cinema intersections, imaging/telecommunications, human spaceflight history, reduced/alternating gravity, experimentation, space systems design/utilization.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Projects in Visualizing Information
courses.description: Project-based course focused on aesthetics of algorithmic visualization. Course concentration on fundamentals of data visualization and design, with an emphasis on data query, analysis, processing and visualization in linear, 2D frequency, and spatial map visualizations.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Transvergence Seminar I
courses.comments: Discourse-driven seminar (with implemented art/research component). Concurrent enrollment in Transvergence Studio I 261B is strongly recommended. Recommended for incoming students.
courses.description: Artistic, philosophical, scientific, and technical foundations of transdisciplinarity, transmodality, and Transvergence. New conceptions of actual, virtual, and informational space and form. Trans-Euclidean geometry, from Gauss to present. Emergence and immanence in algorithmic poetics and information aesthetics. Models of physical, biological, and social complex systems. Worldmaking and epistemology.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Transvergence Seminar II
courses.description: Introduction to Transmodal Continuum. n-dimensional conceptions of space (and form) after Riemann. Scalar, vector, and tensor fields and beyond. Digital, physical, biological, and neurophysiological considerations in the poetics of the very small. Models of morphogenetic and evolutionary developmental emergence. World making and ontology.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Transvergence Studio II
courses.description: Trans Architectures: The Pantopicon, Habitable Cinema, and Invisible Architectures. Multi-agent systems: Implementation of morphogenetic and developmental models of emergence. Design and implementation of everted virtual environments and eversive Worldmaking. Locative Worldmaking: linking locative media, online worlds, tracked/sensed space, and eversive virtual environments.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Transvergence Projects
courses.description: Advanced projects course fusing all modalities of transvergence into implemented works embodying the Transmodal Continuum. Physical Worldmaking: addition of physical computing, spatial sensing, and digital fabrication to immersive, eversive, and locative Worldmaking. Worldmaking and phenomenology.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Open Projects in Optical/Motion - Computational Processes
courses.description: Student defined research projects course focused on optical, or other imaging/sensing device interfaced with a computer such as anamorphs, experiments in multiple exposure, spatial & virtual exploration, distance/presence, reflection and penetration (x-ray, infrared, medical (MRI, PET), etc.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Direct Digital Synthesis - Processing and Composition
courses.prereq_text: MAT majors and graduate non-majors in areas of electrical engineering, computer science, physics and math; consent of instructor.
courses.description: First quarter of general purpose computing for computer music applications. Topics include: music synthesis using computer programs, and score input programs.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Digital Audio Montage
courses.prereq_text: Graduate MAT majors and graduate non-majors in areas of electrical engineering, computer science, physics and math; consent of instructor.
courses.description: First quarter of a three-quarter sequence course concentrates on multi-track recording, mixing, digital signal processing, and studio based composition.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Digital Audio Montage
courses.description: Second quarter of a three-quarter sequence course concentrates on studio based composition.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Digital Audio Montage
courses.description: Third quarter of a three-quarter sequence course concentrates on studio based composition.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Internship in Industry
courses.comments: May be repeated with faculty approval.
courses.description: Special projects for selected students. Offered in conjunction with selected industrial and research under direct faculty supervision. Prior departmental approval required.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Presenting MAT Projects
courses.description: Students develop concise descriptions and practice mock presentations that will be critiqued by faculty and peers in preparation for public exhibition of their work. Emphasis on technical and aesthetic clarity.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.prereq_text: Consent of graduate advisor and Director of graduate studies.
courses.comments: Students are limited to 4 units per quarter. No more than 12 units may be credited toward their Master's degree. Not intended for thesis research.
courses.description: Independent research under the guidance of a faculty member in the department. Offers an opportunity to qualified students to undertake independent research or work in a group laboratory in digital media arts and technology.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Teaching in Media Art & Technology
courses.description: Courses taught or assisted by T.A.'s.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Special Topics in Multimedia Engineering, Visual Arts or Electronic Music
courses.description: Special course in selected problems in multimedia engineering, visual arts, or electronic music.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Special Topics in Multimedia Engineering, Visual Arts or Electronic Music
courses.description: Special course in selected problems in multimedia engineering, visual arts, or electronic music.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Special Topics in Multimedia Engineering, Visual Arts or Electronic Music
courses.description: Special seminar in selected problems in multimedia engineering, visual arts, or electronic music.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Special Topics in Multimedia Engineering, Visual Arts or Electronic Music
courses.description: Special course in selected problems in multimedia engineering, visual arts, or electronic music.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Special Topics in Multimedia Engineering, Visual Arts or Electronic Music
courses.description: Special course in selected problems in multimedia engineering, visual arts, or electronic music.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Special Topics in Soft Robotics
courses.description: Special course in selected problems in multimedia engineering, visual arts, or electronic music.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Special Topics in Multimedia Engineering, Visual Arts or Electronic Music
courses.description: Special course in selected problems in multimedia engineering, visual arts, or electronic music.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Seminar Series
courses.comments: Required of all first year students.
courses.description: Seminar series for advanced topics in multimedia.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Writing, Theory, Lectures, Seminars in Media Arts and Technology
courses.description: A weekly writing, theory and guest lectures seminar, focused on research topics of interest to the wide fields at the intersection of media arts and technology. The seminar is organized in topical modules, covering writing methodologies, media theory, philosophy and critique.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Directed Research
courses.prereq_text: Consent of instructor and Director of graduate studies.
courses.description: Independent research, either experimental or theoretical, may be taken by properly qualified graduate students under the direction of a faculty member.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Individual Study for Ph.D. Examinations
courses.description: Maximum of 12 units per quarter; enrollment limited to 24 units per examination. Instructor is normally student's major advisor or chair of dissertation committee. S/U grading. Individual studies for Ph.D. qualifying examination.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Master's Thesis Research and Project Research
courses.description: For research underlying the thesis/project and writing of the thesis/project.

courses.subject: MAT
courses.title: Ph.D. Dissertation Research and Preparation
courses.description: For research and preparation of the dissertation.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Calculus with Algebra and Trigonometry
courses.prereq_text: Qualifying score on the Mathematics Placement Exam.
courses.comments: Students who have completed Math 34A or 34LA will only receive 3 units for Math 2A. Not open for credit to students who have completed Math 3A or 3AS or have passed the AP Calculus AB or BC exams.
courses.description: Math 3A with precalculus: A function approach integrating algebra, trigonometry, and differential calculus. Topics include: one-on-one and onto functions; inverse functions; properties and graphs of polynomial, rational, exponential, and logarithmic functions; properties and graphs of trigonometric functions; analytic geometry; functions and limits; derivatives; techniques and applications of differentiation; introduction to integration; logarithmic and trigonometric functions.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Calculus with Algebra and Trigonometry
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 2A with a minimum grade of C.
courses.comments: Students who have completed Math 34B or 34LB will only receive 3 units for Math 2B. Not open for credit to students who have completed Math 3B or 3BS or have passed the AP Calculus BC exam.
courses.description: Math 3B with precalculus: A continued review of relevant topics from precalculus (see Math 2A); integral calculus, including definite and indefinite integrals; techniques of integration, introduction to sequences and series; with applications in mathematics and physics.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Calculus with Applications, First Course
courses.prereq_text: Qualifying score on the Mathematics Placement Exam.
courses.comments: Students who have completed Math 34A or 34LA will only receive 2 units for Math 3A. Not open for credit to students who have completed Math 2A or 3AS or have passed the AP Calculus AB or BC exams.
courses.description: Differential Calculus including analytic geometry, functions and limits, derivatives, techniques and applications of differentiation; introduction to integration; logarithmic and trigonometric functions.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Calculus with Applications, Second Course
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 3A with a minimum grade of C.
courses.comments: Students who have completed Math 34B or 34LB will only receive 2 units for Math 3B. Not open for credit to students who have completed Math 2B or 3BS or have passed the AP Calculus BC exam.
courses.description: Integral calculus including definite and indefinite integrals, techniques of integration; introduction to sequences and series; with applications in mathematics and physics.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Linear Algebra with Applications
courses.prereq_text: Math 2B or 3B or 3BI with a minimum grade of C.
courses.description: Systems of linear equations, matrix algebra, determinants, vector spaces and subspaces, basis and dimension, linear transformations, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, diagonalization, and orthogonality.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Differential Equations
courses.prereq_text: Math 4A or Math 4AI with a minimum grade of C.
courses.description: First and second order differential equations, separation of variables, linear differential equations, systems of first order equations, nonlinear differential equations and stability.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Vector Calculus with Applications, First Course
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 4A (or 4AI) with a letter grade of C or better.
courses.description: Calculus of functions of several variables, vector valued functions of one variable, derivative and integrals of vector functions, double and triple integrals, properties and applications of integrals, change of variables.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Vector calculus with Applications, Second Course
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 4B (or 4BI) and Mathematics 6A, each with a minimum grade of C.
courses.description: Scalar and vector fields, integration along paths, integration over surfaces and solid regions, integral theorems of vector calculus, Fourier series, partial differential equations.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Transition to Higher Mathematics
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 4A or 4AI or 4B or 4BI or 6A or 6B with a grade of B or better.
courses.description: Introduction to the elements of propositional logic, techniques of mathematical proof, and fundamental mathematical structures, including sets, functions, relations, and other topics as time permits. Mastery of this material is essential for students planning to major in mathematics.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Calculus for Social and Life Sciences
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Math 2A or 3A or 34LA, or are simultaneously enrolled in 2A or 3A or 34LA, or have passed the AP Calculus AB or BC exams.
courses.description: Introduction to differential and integral calculus with applications to modeling in the biological sciences.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Calculus for Social and Life Sciences
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 2A or 3A or 34A or 34LA with a grade of C or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Math 2B or 3B or 34LB or are simultaneously enrolled in 2B or 3B or 34LB, or have passed the AP Calculus BC exam.
courses.description: Continued study of differential and integral calculus with differential andintegral calculus with applications. Introduction to mathematical modeling with differential equations. Calculus of several variables including an introduction to partial derivatives.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Calculus for the Life Sciences
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Math 2A or 3A or 34A, or are simultaneously enrolled in 2A or 3A or 34A, or have passed the AP Calculus AB or BC exams.
courses.description: Applications of differential and integral calculus to the life sciences. Includes mathematical foundations, biology examples, and computer programming to simulate dynamic systems.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Calculus for the Life Sciences
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 2A or 3A or 34A or 34LA with a grade of C or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Math 2B or 3B or 34B or are simultaneously enrolled in 2B or 3B or 34B, or have passed the AP Calculus BC exam.
courses.description: Applications of differential and integral calculus to the life sciences. Includes mathematical foundations, biology examples, and computer programming to simulate dynamic systems of more than one equation.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Group Studies in Mathematics
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 4A or 4AI or 4B or 4BI or 6A or 6B with a grade of B or better.
courses.comments: Requires concurrent enrollment in MATH 191
courses.description: Lectures and discussions on special topics. Designed for transfer students only.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Classical Number Systems
courses.prereq_text: Math 8 with a minimum grade of C.
courses.description: A development of classical number systems starting with natural numbers and progressing through the integral, rational, real and complex number systems. Includes an introduction to number theory, mathematical induction, the fundamental theorem of arithmetic and the Euclidean algorithm. Especially suitable for prospective middle and high school teachers.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Mathematical Systems
courses.prereq_text: Math 101A with a minimum grade of C.
courses.description: The theory of operations within rings and fields. Polynomials, the fundamental theorem of algebra and other factorization theorems. Analyzing linear, polynomial, rational and exponential functions. Solving algebraic equations and inequalities. Especially suitable for prospective middle and high school teachers.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Modern Euclidean and Noneuclidean Geometry
courses.prereq_text: Math 8 with a minimum grade of C.
courses.description: Topics in plane and solid geometry. The axioms of pure, euclidean, projective, and noneuclidean geometry. Transformational geometry (isometries, dilitations, involutions, perspectivities, and projectivities). The history and the historical implications of these developments in geometry. Especially suitable for prospective middle and high school teachers.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Modern Euclidean and Noneuclidean Geometry
courses.prereq_text: Math 102A with a minimum grade of C.
courses.description: Topics in plane and solid geometry. The axioms of pure, euclidean, projective, and noneuclidean geometry. Transformational geometry (isometries, dilitations, involutions, perspectivities, and projectivities). The history and the historical implications of these developments in geometry. Especially suitable for prospective middle and high school teachers.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Introduction Into Numerical Analysis
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 4B or 4BI, 6A, and 6B; and, Math 8 or PSTAT 8, and Math 117 and, Computer Science 5AA-ZZ or 10 or 8 or 16 or Engineering 3, each with a grade of C or above.
courses.description: Numerical methods for the solution of nonlinear equations (Newton method), for integration (quadrature formulas and composite integration), and for the initial value problem for ordinary differential equations (Euler and Kutta methods).

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Numerical Analysis
courses.prereq_text: Math 104A with a minimum grade of C.
courses.description: Numerical methods for the solution of systems of linear equations (direct and iteractive methods), and the finite difference methods for boundary value problems for (ordinary and partial) differential equations.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Numerical Analysis
courses.prereq_text: Math 104B with a minimum grade of C.
courses.description: Topics in approximation theory; numerical methods for finding eigenvalues of a matrix; and advanced topics in numerical methods for ordinary and partial differential equations.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Linear Algebra
courses.prereq_text: Math 4A and 8 each with a minimum grade of C.
courses.description: Abstract vector spaces and subspaces. Span and linear independence. Basis and dimension. Linear maps. Eigenvalues and eigenvectors.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Linear Algebra
courses.prereq_text: Math 108A with a minimum grade of C.
courses.description: Diagonalization, inner product spaces, projections, least-squares approximations, invariant factors and elementary divisors, canonical forms, topics from advanced matrix theory, applied linear algebra, and group representation theory.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Matrix Analysis
courses.prereq_text: Math 108A with a minimum grade of C
courses.description: Eigenvalues, eigenvectors and similarity; Unitary equivalence and normal matrices; QR factorization; Least squares; Singular Value decomposition; Moore-Penrose generalized inverse; Hermitian and symmetric matrices; Variational characterization of eigenvalues; Positive definite matrices; Nonnegative matrices; Perron-Frobenius Theorem.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Abstract Algebra
courses.prereq_text: Math 108A with a minimum grade of C.
courses.description: An introduction to group theory, focusing on finite groups. Basic algebraic concepts including homomorphisms, normal subgroups, quotients, direct products and group actions. Classification of finitely generated Abelian groups. Other topics such as semidirect products and Sylow theorems as time permits.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Abstract Algebra
courses.prereq_text: Math 111A with a minimum grade of C.
courses.description: Ring theory, ideals, factorization. Examples include number rings and polynomial rings. Module theory if time permits.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Abstract Algebra
courses.prereq_text: Math 111B with a minimum grade of C.
courses.description: Fields, field extensions, Galois theory.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Non-euclidean Geometry
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 8 with a grade of "C" or better.
courses.description: An introduction to hyperbolic geometry with some discussion of other non-euclidean systems.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Introduction to Number Theory
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 8 with a grade of "C" or better.
courses.description: Number-theoretic functions, divisibility, congruences, primitive roots and indices, quadratic residues and the quadratic reciprocity law.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Introduction to Number Theory
courses.prereq_text: Math 115A with a minimum grade of C.
courses.description: Selected topics at the discretion of the instructor. Possibilities include (but are not limited to) Diophantine equations, the distribution of primes, number-theoretic methods in cryptography, quadratic forms, continued fractions, algebraic number theory, and partitions.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Combinatorial Analysis
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 8 with a grade of "C" or better.
courses.description: Elementary counting principles, binomial coefficients, generating functions, recurrence relations, the principle of inclusion and exclusion, distributions and partitions, systems of distinct representatives, applications to computation.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Methods of Analysis
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 8 or PSTAT 8 with a grade of "C" or better.
courses.description: Introduction to methods of proof in analysis. topics include limits, sequences and series, continuity, compactness, as well as other topics. This course is intended to follow Mathematics 8 and to introduce students to the level of sophistication of upper-division mathematics.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Real Analysis
courses.prereq_text: Math 4B, 6A, 108A and 117, each with a minimum grade of C.
courses.description: Axioms of the real numbers, topology of metric spaces, numerical sequences, infinite series.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Real Analysis
courses.prereq_text: Math 108B and 118A, each with a minimum grade of C.
courses.description: Real functions: continuity, differentiability, Riemann integrals, power and trigonometric series.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Real Analysis
courses.prereq_text: Math 118B with a minimum grade of C.
courses.description: Multivariable calculus and a selection of other topics including differential forms or Lebesgue integral.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Ordinary Differential Equations
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 4B or 4BI and 6A with a minimum grade of C; and Math 8 with a minimum grade of C.
courses.description: Existence, uniqueness, and stability; the geometry of phase space; linear systems and hyperbolicity; maps and diffeomorphisms.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Chaotic Dynamics and Bifurcation Theory
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 6B and Math 119A, each with a minimum grade of C
courses.description: Hyperbolic structure and chaos; center manifolds; bifurcation theory; and the Feigenbaum and Ruelle-Takens cascades to strange attractors.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Theory of Complex Variables
courses.prereq_text: Math 6A and 8 each with a minimum grade of C.
courses.description: Complex numbers, complex differentiation, analytic functions, Cauchy-Riemann equations, Taylor and Laurent series, classification of singular points, residues, evaluation of improper integrals.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Theory of Complex Variables
courses.prereq_text: Math 122A with a minimum grade of C.
courses.description: The argument principle, Rouche’s theorem, analytic continuation, conformal mapping, fractional transformations and applications, infinite products, harmonic functions. Other topics at the discretion of the instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Partial Differential Equations
courses.prereq_text: Math 4B or 4BI, 6A, and 6B with a minimum grade of C; and Math 8 with a minimum grade of C.
courses.description: Introduces the derivation and solution of the fundamental linear partial differential equations (PDEs): the wave equation, the heat equation and the Laplace equation. These represent, respectively, hyperbolic, parabolic and elliptic PDEs. Focuses on first and second order PDEs. Students will master methods for initial value problems (IVPs) and boundary value problems (BVPs), including the method of characteristics and the foundational techniques of the Fourier transform and potential theory, providing a rigorous basis for understanding dynamic and steady-state physical systems.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Fourier Series and Numerical Methods for PDEs
courses.prereq_text: Math 4B or 4BI, and 6A, and 6B with a minimum grade of C; and 124A with a minimum grade of C.
courses.description: Introduces specific solution techniques used to solve the wave, heat and Laplace equations. Focuses on separation of variables, namely Fourier series, and a variety of numerical methods. Provides students with modern methods, harmonic analysis and numerical analysis, necessary to study and solve PDEs in a variety of applications. The fast Fourier transform is studied as well as finite difference methods for parabolic and elliptic PDEs and the finite element method for elliptic boundary value problems.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Optimization
courses.prereq_text: Math 6A and 108A, each with a minimum grade of C.
courses.description: Global and local optimization, constrained and unconstrained optimization, convex versus nonconvex optimization, Projection Theorem, linear search methods, gradient methods, Newton and Quasi-Newton methods, trust region methods.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Operations Research
courses.prereq_text: Math 132A with a minimum grade of C.
courses.description: Large scale optimization, stochastic gradient descent, inexact Newton methods, limited memory BSGF, least squares problems, global optimization, optimization in general normed spaces.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Graph and Network Theory
courses.prereq_text: Math 4A and 8, each with a minimum grade of C.
courses.description: Elements of graph and network theory including paths, circuits, trees, coloring, planarity, matching theory, Hall's theorem, applications to scheduling theory, flows in networks, Menger's theorem, and other topics as time permits.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Spectral Graph Theory
courses.prereq_text: Math 108A and 137A, each with a minimum grade of C.
courses.description: The graph Laplacian, eigenvalues of weighted graphs and random walks, the normalized Laplacian and Cheegers inequality, diameters and eigenvalues, expander graphs, eigenvalues of symmetric graphs, heat kernels.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Introduction to Topology
courses.prereq_text: Math 8 with a C or better. Either Math 108A or Math 117 with a minimum grade of C.
courses.description: Metric spaces, continuity, compactness, classification of surfaces, Euler characteristics, and fundamental groups. Additional topics at the discretion of the instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Differential Geometry of Curves and Surfaces
courses.prereq_text: Math 6A with a minimum grade of C; and Math 108A or 117 with a minimum grade of C.
courses.description: Curves and surfaces in three-dimensional Euclidean space, including Frenet formulas, signed curvature of plane curves, first and second fundamental forms, normal curvature and principal curvature, Gaussian and mean curvature, Gauss equation and Theorema Egregium, and a brief introduction to geodesics if time permits.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Differential Geometry of Curves and Surfaces
courses.prereq_text: Math 6B and Math 147A with a minimum grade of C.
courses.description: Parallel transport, geodesics, Gauss-Bonnet Theorem, fundamental theorem of surfaces. Additional topics at the discretion of the instructor may include minimal surfaces, Codazzi equation, surfaces of constant Gaussian curvature, isothermal coordinates, and global theorems for curves.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Introduction to Mathematical Finance
courses.prereq_text: MATH 4B, PSTAT 120A-B, and PSTAT 160A, all completed with a minimum grade of C or better.
courses.comments: PSTAT 170 and Mathematics 170 are the same course.
courses.description: Describes mathematical methods for estimating and evaluating asset pricing models, equilibrium and derivative pricing, options, bonds, and the term-structure of interest rates. Also introduces finance optimization models for risk management and financial engineering.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: History of Mathematics
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 8 with a grade of "C" or better.
courses.description: An examination of the major achievements in mathematical thinking throughout history. Topics may include the history of numerical systems in early civilizations, the development of formal proof, mathematical contributions from diverse populations and the impact of technological innovations on mathematics. Especially suitable for prospective middle and high school teachers.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Special Topics in Mathematics
courses.prereq_text: Math 8 with a grade of C or better.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units.
courses.description: An advanced treatment of mathematics content appropriate for undergraduates. The material for the course may come from algebra, geometry, analysis, applied mathematics or other areas of mathematics. Topics vary by instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Mathematical Reasonings of AI such as GPT and DeepSeek
courses.prereq_text: Math 8 with a grade of C or better.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units.
courses.description: This project-based course explores the mathematical reasonings of AI systems like GPT and DeepSeek. Students will work on exercises drawn from topics in Math 8, linear algebra, and calculus. For each project, the student will obtain an AI-generated solution, carefully examine it for errors, and then analyze and correct the AI's mistakes. Students will submit all project materials. Most projects will be provided by the instructor, but students will also be encouraged to find some on their own, with all projects receiving necessary instruction.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: A First Course in Algebraic K-Theory
courses.prereq_text: Math 8 with a grade of C or better.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units.
courses.description: An introduction to classical algebraic K-theory, focusing on the lower algebraic K-groups K0, K1, and K2 of commutative rings and their basic properties. These groups are fundamental invariants in algebra and geometry and also have connections to number theory and topology. The course explores some of these connections and known computations, and also focuses on relations with Galois cohomology, class field theory, Brauer group, and related arithmetic invariants. Prerequisites include basic knowledge of groups, rings, modules, and fields.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Problem Solving
courses.prereq_text: Math 8 with a grade of C or better.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units.
courses.description: The Problem Solving in Mathematics course is designed to impart students with advanced problem-solving techniques and strategies in mathematics. Students will explore a diverse range of methods, including the application of parity, coloring, ordering, extremality, symmetry, invariants among others. The course emphasizes critical and creative thinking, allowing students to tackle complex mathematical challenges. Through collaboration and presentation exercises, students develop effective communication skills. The goal is to equip students with the basic abilities for research in mathematics.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Mathematics Transition for Transfer Students
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 4A or 4AI or 4B or 4BI or 6A or 6B with a grade of B or better. Concurrent enrollment in Math 94.
courses.description: Provides transfer students with a solid mathematical foundation to ease their transition into a four-year college environment. Students will explore the fundamental axioms of integers and their properties, gaining a deep understanding of this essential mathematical concept. The curriculum extends to the study of rational numbers, real numbers, and complex numbers, emphasizing the properties and principles that underlie these numeric systems. Through a structured approach, this course equips transfer students with the mathematical knowledge and skills necessary to excel in more advanced coursework.

courses.comments: Students should be proficient in basic numerical methods, linear algebra, mathematically rigorous proofs, and some programming language. Same course as Computer Science 211A, ME 210A, ECE 210A, Geology 251A, and Chemical Engineering 211A.
courses.description: Graduate level-matrix theory with introduction to matrix computations. SVD's, pseudoinverses, variational characterization of eigenvalues, perturbation theory, direct and iterative methods for matrix computations.

courses.subject: MATH

courses.comments: Students should be proficient in basic numerical methods, linear algebra, mathematically rigorous proofs, and some programming language. Same course as Computer Science 211B, ME 210B, ECE 210B, Geology 251B, and Chemical Engineering 211B.
courses.description: Linear multistep methods and Runge-Kutta methods for ordinary differential equations: stability, order and convergence. Stiffness. Differential algebraic equations. Numerical solution of boundary value problems.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Numerical Solution of Partial Differential Equations--Finite Difference Methods
courses.comments: Students should be proficient in basic numerical methods, linear algebra, mathematically rigorous proofs, and some programming language. Same course as Computer Science 211C, ME 210C, ECE 210C, Geology 251C, and Chemical Engineering 211C.
courses.description: Finite difference methods for hyperbolic, parabolic and elliptic PDE's, with application to problems in science and engineering. Convergence, consistency, order and stability of finite difference methods. Dissipation and dispersion. Finite volume methods. Software design and adaptivity.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Numerical Solution of Partial Differential Equations - Finite Element Methods
courses.comments: Students should be proficient in basic numerical methods, linear algebra, mathematically rigorous proofs, and some programming language. Same course as Computer Science 211D, ME 210D, ECE 210D, Geology 251D, and Chemical Engineering 211D.
courses.description: Weighted residual and finite element methods for the solution of hyperbolic, parabolic and elliptic partial differential equations, with application to problems in science and engineering. Error estimates. Standard and discontinuous Galerkin methods.

courses.subject: MATH CS
courses.title: Problem Solving I
courses.description: Discussion and solution of nonroutine mathematical problems related with different problem-solving techniques. Possible topics are: Pigeonhole principle, use of invariants and symmetries in problem solving, coloring arguments, parity, recursive arguments, extreme principle, inclusion-exclusion principle.

courses.subject: MATH CS
courses.title: Problem Solving II
courses.description: Discussion and solution of nonroutine problems in different areas of mathematics like Graph Theory, Number Theory, Combinatorics, Geometry, Game Theory, Topology, Algebra, and Analysis.

courses.subject: MATH CS
courses.title: Advanced Linear Algebra I
courses.description: An introduction to the theory of Linear Algebra with topics: Algebra of matrices, linear systems of equations, vector spaces, linear independence, basis and dimension, infinite-dimensional vectors spaces, linear transformations, matrix representation, isomorphisms, quotient spaces, dual spaces, and determinants.

courses.subject: MATH CS
courses.title: Advanced Linear Algebra II
courses.description: Eigenvalues, eigenvectors, and diagonalization. Canonical form under similarity: Jordan canonical form and rational canonical form, inner product and norm. Gram-Schmidt process, adjoint of a linear operator, normal and self-adjoint operators, unitary and orthogonal operators, spectral theorem.

courses.subject: MATH CS
courses.title: Introduction to Real Analysis
courses.description: A rigorous introduction to the elements of analysis. Covers sequences, accumulation points, Bolzano-Weierstrass, Cauchy's criterion, the completeness property of the real number system, limits of functions, continuity, differentiability, compact sets, and the Heine-Borel theorem.

courses.subject: MATH CS
courses.title: Special Topics in Mathematics
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit providing letter designations are different.
courses.description: Lectures on a coherent body of mathematical topics which are not usually presented in standard mathematics courses.

courses.subject: MATH CS
courses.title: Introduction to Data Science and Machine Learning: Foundations and Applications
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit providing letter designations are different.
courses.description: This course provides an accessible introduction to the field of data science and related techniques from machine learning. The course will develop both mathematical foundations and theory behind learning algorithms as well as discussing practical aspects for their use in applications.

courses.subject: MATH CS
courses.title: Math Book Club
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit providing letter designations are different.
courses.description: A collaborative seminar on mathematical topics not ordinarily covered in the standard curriculum. Students work as a cohort under faculty supervision to study a common textbook or collection of research papers. Participants give weekly presentations, lead peer discussions, and solve related problem sets. The course emphasizes independent learning within a shared seminar setting, with focus on mathematical reading, proof analysis, problem solving, and oral communication. Topic varies by term.

courses.subject: MATH CS
courses.title: Special Topics in Mathematics: Combinatorics
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit providing letter designations are different.
courses.description: Combinatorics has its historical roots in mathematical recreations and games. Combinatorics is concerned with arrangements of the objects in a set into patterns satisfying specified rules.

courses.subject: MATH CS
courses.title: Theory of Distributions and their Applications
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit providing letter designations are different.
courses.description: Distributions, also known generalized functions, are objects that generalize the classical notion of functions in mathematical analysis. Distributions make it possible to differentiate functions whose derivatives do not exist in the classical sense. Distributions are widely used in the theory of partial differential equations, in physics and engineering where many problems naturally lead to differential equations whose solutions or initial conditions are singular, such as the Dirac delta function.

courses.subject: MATH CS
courses.title: Special Topics in Mathematics: The Ellipse
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit providing letter designations are different.
courses.description: The course delves into concepts using ellipses as a foundational shape: Synthetic & Projective geometry, theorems like Pascal's, Potential theory encompassing Newton’s cloaking, Elliptic functions aiding arc length computation, Quantization of ellipses involving Jacobi matrices, Moving boundaries (e.g., crystal growth) maintaining ellipses, with potential for broader topics.

courses.subject: MATH CS
courses.title: Algebraic Combinatorics
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit providing letter designations are different.
courses.description: This class discusses applications of algebra (especially linear algebra) to various combinatorial problems.

courses.subject: MATH CS
courses.title: Special Topics in Mathematics: Number Systems
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit providing letter designations are different.
courses.description: An exploration of basic number systems including the integers, rationals, reals, complex and beyond.

courses.subject: MATH CS
courses.title: Special Topics in Mathematics - Linear Optimization
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit providing letter designations are different.
courses.description: In this course, students study optimization techniques in the area of Linear Programming whose goal is to find the maximum or a minimum of a linear function subject to linear constraints. This area of mathematics has broad applications in engineering, in data analysis, in industry, in medicine, etc. The only prerequisite for this class is Linear Algebra and some Multivariable calculus.

courses.subject: MATH CS
courses.title: Topology
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit providing letter designations are different.
courses.description: Basic concepts in point set and algebraic topology, including compactness and fundamental groups.

courses.subject: MATH CS
courses.title: Special Topics in Mathematics - Game Theory
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit providing letter designations are different.
courses.description: Introduction to game theory and related topics. Includes classical game theory and combinatorial game theory up through the Sprague-Grundy Theorem.

courses.subject: MATH CS
courses.title: Knot Theory
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit providing letter designations are different.
courses.description: This course introduces the mathematical study of knots and links focusing on how topology, algebra, and geometry interact to distinguish and classify them. Students will learn both classical and modern knot invariants. A more apt title for this course could be 'Topics in Geometric Topology,' as we will also touch upon the importance of knots and links in the broader field of low-dimensional topology. Possible topics include the study of codimension one embeddings in manifolds, the knot group, Seifert surfaces and Seifert genus, polynomial link invariants, braids, finite and infinite cyclic coverings, the Alexander module, surgery theory, hyperbolic knot theory, and quantum invariants.

courses.subject: MATH CS
courses.title: Number Theory
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit providing letter designations are different.
courses.description: Selected topics in number theory.

courses.subject: MATH CS
courses.title: P-adic analysis and p-adic zeta functions
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit providing letter designations are different.
courses.description: Introduces p-adic numbers which can be obtained by completing rational numbers with respect to an absolute value different from the usual Euclidean absolute value. Discusses p-adic analysis and a p-adic version of Riemann zeta functions.

courses.subject: MATH CS
courses.title: Topological Combinatorics
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit providing letter designations are different.
courses.description: Two thieves have stolen a valuable necklace made of gems of several kinds. They want to divide the necklace so that each gets the same number of each kind of gem. How many cuts do they have to make? In this course you'll learn the answer to this and other combinatorial questions and how algebraic topology is used in the proof.

courses.subject: MATH CS
courses.title: Probability
courses.description: This is a course on probability. It covers discrete and continuous distributions, combinatorial methods, generating functions, conditioning, the law of large numbers, the central limit theorem, stochastic processes, random walks, Brownian motion, and applications in biology, economics, engineering, and physics.

courses.subject: MATH CS
courses.title: Complex Variables I
courses.description: Covers the basics of the topology of the complex plane, series of complex numbers, differentiability of functions of a complex variable, the complex exponential and logarithm functions, contour integration, power series and analytic continuation, among other related topics.

courses.subject: MATH CS
courses.title: Complex Variables II
