courses.description: Covers the basics of the topology of the complex plane, series of complex numbers, differentiability of functions of a complex variable, the complex exponential and logarithm functions, contour integration, power series and analytic continuation, among other related topics.

courses.subject: MATH CS
courses.title: Introduction to the Higher Mathematics
courses.description: A formal introduction to the language and culture of mathematics. Students will learn how to rigorously think about mathematics and write mathematical proofs. Topics covered include: propositional logic, set theory, cardinality, number theory, and various number systems.

courses.subject: MATH CS
courses.title: Independent Studies
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit. Creative Studies students may enroll in a maximum of 24 units of Independent Studies courses per year, with a maximum of 45 units counted toward graduation.
courses.description: Serious independent study in mathematics with consenting faculty member.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Materials in Society, The Stuff of Dreams
courses.prereq_text: Not open to engineering, pre-computer science, or computer science majors.
courses.description: A survey of new technological substances and materials, the scientific methods used in their development, and their relation to society and the economy. Emphasis on uses of new materials in the human body, electronics, optics, sports, transportation, and infrastructure.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Structure and Properties I
courses.comments: Preference for enrollment is given to students in the combined 5-year BS-Engineering/MS-Materials or BS-Chemistry/MS-Materials programs.
courses.description: An introduction to materials in modern technology. The internal structure of materials and its underlying principles: bonding, spatial organization of atoms and molecules, structural defects. Electricial, magnetic and optical properties of materials, and their relationship with structure.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Structures and Properties II
courses.comments: Preference for enrollment is given to students in the combined 5-year BS- Engineering/MS-Materials or BS-Chemistry/MS-Materials programs. Not open for major credit to students who have completed Matrl 101; If students take Matrl 101 and Matrl 100B, they will only receive major credit for one course.
courses.description: Mechanical properties of engineering materials and their relationship to bonding and structure. Elastic, flow, and fracture behavior; time dependent deformation and failure. Stiffening, strengthening, and toughening mechanisms. Thermo-mechanical interactions in materials.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Fundamentals of Structural Evolution
courses.comments: Preference for enrollment is given to students in the combined 5-year BS-Engineering/MS-Materials or BS-Chemistry/MS-Materials programs.
courses.description: An introduction to the thermodynamic and kinetic principles governing structural evolution in materials. Phase equilibria, diffusion and structural transformations. Metastable structures in materials. Self-assembling systems. Structural control through processing and/ or imposed fields. Environmental effects on structure and properties.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Introduction to the Structure and Properties of Materials
courses.comments: Not open for major credit to students who have completed Materials 100B; If students take Matrl 101 and Matrl 100B, they will only receive major credit for one course. Upper-division standing. Students interested in following the BS Engineering/MS Materials program should not take this course.
courses.description: Introduction to the structure of engineering materials and its relationship with their mechanical properties. Structure of solids and defects. Concepts of microstructure and origins. Elastic, plastic flow and fracture properties. Mechanisms of deformation and failure. Stiffening, strengthening, and toughening mechanisms.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Biophysics and Biomolecular Materials
courses.comments: Same course as Physics 135.
courses.description: Structure and function of cellular molecules (lipids, nucleic acids, proteins, and carbohydrates). Genetic engineering techniques of molecular biology. Biomolecular materials and biomedical applications (e.g., bio-sensors, drug delivery systems, gene carrier systems).

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Introduction to Polymer Science
courses.prereq_text: Chemical Engineering 110A or Chemistry 113A or equivalent.
courses.comments: Same course as Chemical Engineering 160.
courses.description: Introductory course covering synthesis, characterization, structure, and mechanical properties of polymers. The course is taught from a materials perspective and includes polymer thermodynamics, chain architecture, measurement and control of molecular weight as well as crystallization and glass transitions.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: The Quantum Description of Electronic Materials
courses.prereq_text: ECE 130A-B and 134 with a minimum grade of C- in all; open to EE, senior students in the BS/MS programs and Materials graduate students only.
courses.comments: Same course as ECE 162A.
courses.description: Electrons as particles and waves, Schrodinger's equation and illustrative solutions. Tunneling. Atomic structures, the exclusion principle and the periodic table. Bonds. Free electrons in metals, periodic potentials and energy bands.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Fundamentals of the Solid State
courses.prereq_text: ECE 162A with a minimum grade of C-; open to EE, senior students in the BS/MS programs and Materials graduate students only.
courses.comments: Same course as ECE 162B.
courses.description: Crystal lattices and the structure of solids, with emphasis on seminconductors. Lattice vibartations. Electronic states and energy bands. Electrical and thermal conduction. Dielectic and optical properties. Semiconductor devices: diffusion, P-N junctions and diode behavior.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Materials in Engineering
courses.comments: Same course as ME 185.
courses.description: Introduces the student to the main families of materials and the principlesbehind their development, selection, and behavior. Discusses the generic properties of metals, ceramics, polymers, and composites more relevant to structural applications. The relationship of properties to structure and processing is emphasized in every case.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Manufacturing and Materials
courses.prereq_text: ME 151C; and ME 15; and Materials 101 or Materials 100C
courses.comments: Same course as ME 186A.
courses.description: Introduction to the fundamentals of common manufacturing processes and their interplay with the structure and properties of materials as they are transformed into products. Emphasis on process understanding and the key physical concepts and basic mathematical relationships involved in each of the processes discussed.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Introduction to Additive Manufacturing
courses.comments: ME 186B and Materials 186B are the same course.
courses.description: Introduction to additive manufacturing processes: review ofmanufacturing methods and process selection consideration, economies of production, common additive manufacturing strategies, and brief description of the physics of photopolymerization, extrusion, selective laser melting and e-beam melting fabrication.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Thermodynamic Foundation of Materials
courses.description: The microscopic statistical mechanical foundations of the macroscopic thermodynamics of materials, with applications to ideal and non-ideal gases, electrons and phonons in solids, multicomponent solutions, phase equilibria in single and multicomponent systems, and capillarity.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Electronic and Atomic Structure of Materials
courses.description: The free electron model; electron levels in periodic potentials. Classification of solids. Role of electronic structure in atomic bonding and atomic packing. Cohesion. Surfaces, interfaces and junction effects. Semiconductors. Transition-metal compounds. Amorphous solids. Liquid crystals. Colloids and soft materials.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Structure Evolution
courses.description: Study of phenomena underlying the evolution of structure across the relevant length and time scales in Materials. Structural defects. Drving forces, mechanisms and kinetics of structural change. Diffusional transport. Fundamentals of phase transformations. Crystallization. Evolution of microstructural features and patterns.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Introduction to Quantum Mechanics for Materials
courses.description: A primer course on quantum mechanics for materials incoming graduate students who have had limited exposure to the subject. Topics include: The Schrodinger equation, wave functions, observables and operators; solutions to a particle in a box, harmonic oscillator and a free particle; the formalism of quantum mechanics, dirac notation; angular momentum, solutions to the hydrogen atom; spin and two state systems; perturbation theory, composite systems, entanglement, Pauli exclusion principle.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Introduction to Structure and Phase Stability
courses.description: A primer course for incoming graduate students with non-MSE background. Basic concepts of structure and descriptors: crystalline and non-crystalline solids, compounds, solid solutions. Structural imperfections: point defects, dislocations and strain fields, surfaces, interfaces. Defects in ionic crystals. Thermodynamic underpinnings of phase diagrams: phase rule, chemical potential, equilibrium conditions, metastability. Unary systems. Fundamentals of binary systems, allotropes, invariant reactions, phase fractions and compositions, relationship with structure evolution. Maps for reacting systems, Ellingham diagrams, predominance diagrams. Introduction to ternary systems: liquidus surfaces and basic invariant reactions.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Introduction to Magnetism and Magnetic Materials
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Materials 288D.
courses.description: Review of elementary magnetostatics. Discussion of quantum mechanical origins of magnetism. Properties of ferro-, para- dia- and antiferro-magnetics and the theories that describe them. Magnetic phenomena and materials manifesting magnetic states in both localized and itinerant limits.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Wide-Band Gap Materials and Devices
courses.description: Optical and electrical properties of wide and ultra-wide band gap semiconductors (Al,In,Ga) N, SiC, Ga2O3, diamond-based semiconductor materials. Theory and practical applications of wide-band materials in electronic and optoelectronic devices. Materials growth techniques of MOCVD and MBE are discussed in the particular context of WBG semiconductors. Applications of these materials in lasers, LEDs, high frequency transistors and power devices emphasized.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Fundamentals of Electronic Solids I
courses.comments: Same course as ECE 215A.
courses.description: Introduction into the physics of semiconductors for beginning engineering graduate students. Crystal structure. Reciprocal lattice and crystal diffraction. Electrons in periodic structures. Energy and bands. Semiconductor electrons and probes, fermi statistics.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Fundamentals of Electronic Solids II
courses.comments: Same course as ECE 215B.
courses.description: Phonons, electron scattering, electro nic transport, selected optical properties, heterostructures, effective mass, quantum wells, two-dimensional electron gas, quantum wires, deep levels, crystal binding.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Mechanics of Materials
courses.comments: Same course as ME 219.
courses.description: Matrices and tensors, stress and deformation, compatibility and equilibrium conditions, constitutive equations, and boundary conditions, applications in elasticity, plasticity and fracture.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Crystallography and Diffraction Fundamentals
courses.description: Diffraction theory: fourier transformation, schrodinger equation, Maxwell's equations, kinematical theory, Fresnel diffraction, Fraunhofer diffraction, scattering of x-rays, electrons and neutrons by isolated atoms and assemblies of atoms, pair correlation and radial distribution functions. Basic symmetry operations, point groups, space groups.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: X-Ray Diffraction II: Advanced Methods
courses.description: Focuses on modern diffraction techniques from crystalline materials. High resolution x-ray diffraction. Analysis of epitaxial layers. X-ray scattering theory. Simulation of x-ray rocking curves. Analysis of thin films and multiple layers. Triple-axis x-ray diffractometry. Topography. Synchrotron techniques.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Electron Microscopy II: Crystalline Materials
courses.description: Electron microscopy to study defect structures, elastic and inelastic scattering, kinematics theory of image contrast, bright and dark field imaging, two-beam conditions, contrast from imperfections, dynamical theory of diffraction and image contrast. Howie Whellan equations, dispersion surface.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Engineering Quantum Mechanics I
courses.prereq_text: ECE 162A-B. Students must have some knowledge of linear algebra.
courses.comments: Same course as ECE 211A.
courses.description: Wave-particle duality; bound states; uncertainty relations; expectation values and operators; variational principle; eigenfunction expansions; perturbation theory I. Treatment matches needs and background of ECE and materials students emphasizing solid state or quantum electronics.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Engineering Quantum Mechanics II
courses.prereq_text: ECE 211A or MATRL 211A, or ECE 215A or MATRL 206A.
courses.comments: Same course as ECE 211B.
courses.description: Continuation of Materials 211A; symmetry and degeneracy; electrons in crystals, angular momentum; perturbation theory II; transition probabilities; quantized fields and radiative transitions; magnetic fields;electron spin; indistinguishable particles.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Semiconductor Device Processing
courses.comments: Same course as ECE 220A.
courses.description: Intensive theoretical and laboratory instruction in solid-state device and integrated circuit fabrication. Topics include 1) semiconductor material properties and characterization; 2) phase diagrams; 3) diffusion; 4) thermal oxidation; 5) vacuum processes; 6) thin-film deposition; 7) scanning electron microscopy. Both gallium arsenide and silicon technologies are presented.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Semiconductor Device Processing
courses.comments: Same course as ECE 220B.
courses.description: Continued theoretical and laboratory instruction and the characterization of junction and field-effect devices. Topics will include bipolar characterization, design fabrication, and testing. The laboratory effort initiated in 215A will be continued in these two quarters.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Molecular Beam Epitaxy and Band Gap Engineering
courses.comments: Same course as ECE 217.
courses.description: Fundamentals and recent research developments in the growth and properties of thin crystalline films of electronic and optical materials bythe process of molecular beam epitaxy. Artificially structured materials with quantized electron confinement and artificially engineered electronic band structure properties.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Introduction to Inorganic Materials
courses.comments: Same course as Chemistry 277.
courses.description: Structures of inorganic materials: close-packing, linking of simple polyhedra. Factors that control structure: ionic radii, covalency, ligand field effects, metal-metal bonding, electron/atom ratios. Structure property relationships in e.g. spinels, garnets, perovskites, rutiles, fluorites, zeolites, b-aluminas, graphites, common inorganic glasses.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Phase Transformations
courses.description: Introduction to the unifying concepts underlying phas transformations in metals, ceramics, polymers, and electronic materials. Includes the thermodyanamics, kinetics, crystallography and microstructural characteristics of displacive and diffusional transformations. Role of elastics, compositional, configurational, electrical, magnetic and gradientenergy contributions.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Mechanical Behavior of Materials
courses.comments: Same course as Mechanical Engineering 264.
courses.description: Concepts of stress and strain. Deformation of metals, polymers, and ceramics. Elasticity, viscoelasticity, plastic flow, and creep. Linear elastic fracture mechanics. Mechanisms of ductile and brittle fracture.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Colloids and Interfaces I
courses.comments: Same course as Chemical Engineering 222A and BMSE 222A.
courses.description: Introduction to the various intermolecular interactions in solutions and in colloidal systems: Van der Waals, electrostatic, hydrophobic, solvation, H-bonding. Introduction to colloidal systems.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Colloids and Interfaces II
courses.comments: Materials 222A, Chemical Engineering 222A or BMSE 222A recommended. Same course as Chemical Engineering 222B & BMSE 222B.
courses.description: Continuation of 222A. Interparticle interactions, coagulation, DLVO theory, steric interactions, polymer-coated surfaces, polymers in solution, thin film viscosity. Surfactant and lipid self-assembly: micelles, microemulsions. Surfaces: wetting, contact angles, surface tension. Surfactants on surfaces: langmuir-blodgett films, adsorption, adhesion. Non-equilibrium and dynamic interactions.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Symmetry and Tensor Properties of Materials
courses.description: Description of the principles of crystal symmetry, functional materials, and their properties, including dielectrics, piezoelectrics, and magnetic and transport phenomena. Fundamental concepts, tensorial and mathematical description of functional behavior.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Metal-Organic Chemical Vapor Deposition
courses.description: Electronic and optical properties of thin films grown by vapor phase transport techniques. Growth mechanisms, kinetics and thermodynamics of vapor phase epitaxy. Special emphasis on the process of metalorganic vapor phase epitaxy for optoelectronic materials and devices.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Computational Materials
courses.description: Basic computational techniques and their application to simulating the behavior of materials. Techniques include: finite difference methods, MonteCarlo, molecular dynamics, cellular automata, and simulated annealing.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Elasticity and Plasticity
courses.comments: Same course as ME 230.
courses.description: Review field equations of elasticity and plasticity. Energy principles and uniqueness theorems. Elementary problems in one and two dimensions, stress functions, and complex variable methods. Plastic stress-strain laws; flow potentials. Torsion and bending of plastic flow, slip line theory. Bounding theorems.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Plasticity
courses.comments: Same course as ME 232.
courses.description: Plastic, creep, and relaxation behavior of solids. Mechanics of inelastically strained bodies, plastic stress-strain laws; flow potentials. Torsion and bending of prismatic bars, expansion of thick shells, plane plastic flow, slip line theory. Variational formulations, approximate methods.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Fracture Mechanics
courses.comments: Same course as ME 275.
courses.description: Analytic solutions of a stationary crack under static loading. Elastic and elastoplastic analysis. The J integral. Energy balance and crack growth. Criteria for crack initiation and growth. Dynamic crack propagation. Fatigue. The micromechanics of fracture.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Finite Element Structural Analysis
courses.comments: Same course as ME 271.
courses.description: Definitions and basic element operations displacement approach in linear elasticity. Element formulation: direct methods and variational methods. Global analysis procedures: assemblage and solution. Plane stress and planestrain. Solids of revolution and general solids. Isoparametric representation and numerical integration. Computer implementation.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Structural Inorganic Chemistry
courses.comments: Same course as Chem 273.
courses.description: The use of x-ray and neutron scattering to characterize solid state materials. Subjects include the crystal unit cell, space groups, structure determination and refinement. It is recommended that the student have an elementary introduction to vectors, matrices and fourier series.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Symmetries and Group Theory
courses.description: Symmetries have profound and far-reaching effects on material properties. This course introduces the fundamentals of symmetry groups as they relate to molecules and crystalline solids. Topics covered include: point and space groups, irreducible representations, tensor properties of materials, Raman and IR selection rules, Landau's theory of phase transitions.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Electrochemistry and Electrochemical Methods
courses.description: Introduction to electrochemistry and electrochemical methods used to study (photo)electrochemical systems for energy storage and conversion (rechargeable batteries, fuel cells, solar cells). Introduction to corrosion electrochemistry.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Processing of Inorganic Materials
courses.comments: Lecture, 3 hours.
courses.description: Fundamental concepts and mathematical models underlying major types of processes for inorganic materials, with emphasis on the relationships between processing and microstructure. Topics include: melting and solidification, powder synthesis and consolidation, coatings and surface treatments.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Liquid Crystal Materials
courses.description: Thermotropic and lyotropic liquid crystals (LC's). Classification and phasetransitions. LC's in display technology. Laboratory experimentation using x-ray diffraction and polarized optical microscopy to characterize LC phases.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Composite Materials
courses.comments: Same course as ME 265.
courses.description: Stress and strain relations in composites. Residual stresses. The fracture resistance of organic and inorganic matrix composites. Statistical aspects of fiber failure. Composite laminates and delamination cracks. Cumulative damage concepts. Interface properties. Design criteria.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Thin Films and Multilayers
courses.prereq_text: Materials 207 (same course as ME 219); consent of instructor
courses.comments: Same course as ME 267
courses.description: The development of stresses in thin films and its relaxation. Edge effects and discontinuities. Cracks in films and at interfaces. Delamination of residually stressed films. Buckling and buckle propagation of compressed films. Cyclic behavior and ratcheting effects.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Semiconductor Lasers I
courses.prereq_text: ECE 162A-B-C; or MATRL 162A-B and ECE 162C; or ECE 144.
courses.comments: Same course as ECE 227A.
courses.description: Review of semiconductor physics, growth technology, and materials properties; double-heterostructure and quantum-well laser structures; carrier and photon rate equations; light vs. current characteristics; scattering and transmission matrices; compound cavity, distributed bragg reflector, and distributed feedback lasers.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Biomaterials and Biosurfaces
courses.comments: Same as ChE 202 and BMSE 202
courses.description: Fundamentals of natural and artificial biomaterials and biosurfaces with emphasis on molecular level structure and function and their interactions with the body. Design issues of grafts and biopolymers.Basic biological, biophysical and biochemical systems reviewed for nonbiologists.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Synthesis and Properties of Macromolecules
courses.description: Basics of preparation of polymer and macromolecular assemblies, and characterization of large molecules and assemblies. Discussion of chemical structure, bonding, and reactivity.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Structure and Characterization of Complex Fluids
courses.description: Structure, phase behavior, and phase transitions in complex fluids. Characterization techniques including x-ray and neutron scattering, and light and microscopy methods. Systems include colloidal and surfactant dispersions (e.g., polyballs, microemulsions, and micells), polymeric solutions and biomolecular materials (e.g., lyotropic liquid crystals).

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Properties of Macromolecules
courses.comments: Lecture, 3 hours.
courses.description: Fundamentals of the properties of macromolecular solutions, melts, and solids. Viscosity, diffusion and light scattering from dilute solutions. Elements of macromolecular solid state structure. Thermal properties and processes. Mechanical and transport properties. Introduction to electrical and optical properties of macromolecules.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Mechanical Forces and Biomolecules
courses.comments: Same course as BMSE 272.
courses.description: Explores single-molecule biophysics and the role of mechanical force in biomolecular behavior. Emphasis is placed on modern experimental techniques and the effects of mechanical stress on DNA conformation, protein unfolding, and force-generation by motor proteins. Recent literature is used throughout.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Experiments in Macromolecular Materials
courses.comments: Lecture, 3 hours; laboratory, 4 hours.
courses.description: Experiments using X-ray and light scattering, optical and electron microscopy. Crystalline, quasi-crystalline and amorphous materials. Solid, solution, and colloidal samples.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Solid State Inorganic Materials
courses.comments: Same course as Chemistry 274.
courses.description: An introductory course describing the synthesis, physical characterization, structure, electronic properties and uses of solid state materials.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Biomolecular Materials I: Structure and Function
courses.description: Survey of classes of biomolecules (lipids, carbohydrates, proteins, nucleic acids). Structure and function of molecular machines (enzymes for biosynthesis, motors, pumps).

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Interaction in Biomolecular Complexes
courses.description: Focuses on the interactions, structures, and functional properties of complexes comprised of supramolecular assemblies of biological molecules. Systems addressed include lipid membranes, lipid-DNA complexes, and assemblies of proteins of the cell cytoskeleton.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: First-Principles Calculations for Materials
courses.description: Basic theory and methods of electronic structure, illustrated with examples of practical computational methods and real-world applications. Topics: Band structure; Uniform electron gas; Density functional theory; Exchange and correlation; Kohn-Sham equations; Pseudopotentials; Basis sets; Predicting materials properties: bulk, surfaces, interfaces, defects.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Introduction to Organic Electronics
courses.description: Electronic properties of organic semiconductors and the effects of molecular structure. Influence of processing on electronic properties. Processing methods for organic optoelectronic devices. Discussion of measurements of transport and exemplary devices including thin film transistors, light emitting diodes, and photovoltaics.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Technical Communication and Presentation Design
courses.description: Focuses on a practical, hands-on, interactive approach to developing communication skills and presentation style. Using current literature and seminars, critical attributes such as clearly explaining complex ideas, the do's and don'ts of presentation will be covered.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Special Topics in Inorganic Materials
courses.description: This course will be offered on an irregular basis and will include in-depthdiscussions of advanced topics in inorganic materials.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: In Situ/ In Operando Methods for Materials Science Research
courses.description: Overview of various in situ / in operando techniques used to characterize functional materials during normal operation, to investigate the processes of materials synthesis and phase transformations, to isolate transient or metastable states. X-ray absorption spectroscopy, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, IR, Raman, diffraction techniques, magnetic resonance techniques, electron microscopy, etc. Advantages and limitations. Important considerations when devising a new in situ set up / probe.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Advanced TEM
courses.description: Intended for graduate students who are using transmission electron microscopy in their research. Covers imaging theory, lens aberrations, contrast transfer functions, dynamical diffraction theories, and diffraction contrast from a wide range of crystal defects (planar defects, dislocations, etc.). Also discusses the basics of scanning transmission electron microscopy techniques. Meant to complement the more practical training in 209C, but 209C is not a pre-requisite.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Two-Dimensional Moiré Materials
courses.description: Explores two-dimensional moiré materials, focusing on how stacking and twisting atomically thin crystals creates highly tunable electronic properties. Small relative rotations produce moiré superlattices and flat electronic bands, enabling strong electron correlations and new quantum phases. Topics include fractional quantum anomalous Hall states, superconductivity, correlated insulators, orbital ferromagnetism, topological order, and model systems such as the triangular Hubbard model. Students develop the concepts needed to critically read current research papers and re-derive their central results.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Fundamental and Applied Concepts in Ceramics for Electrochemical Technologies
courses.description: The objective of this course is to familiarize students with ceramic materials used in state-of-the-art Li ion batteries and that can enable advanced electrochemical technologies such as solid-state and electrical grid batteries. The course will briefly cover fundamental aspects of ceramics and their processing, solid-state electrochemistry, and the design, manufacturing, and characterization of state-of-the-art Li ion and advanced battery concepts. Depending on class size, hands-on learning activities may be planned for the end of the semester where students or student teams will learn how to make and electrochemically characterize Li ion and Li metal electrodes with conventional liquid electrolytes and/or solid-state electrolytes.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Optical Characterization of Materials
courses.description: Optical techniques encompass a wide variety of tools for materials characterization. After reviewing light-matter interactions and optical properties of materials, this course surveys a selection of optical techniques commonly used in materials science, including optical conductivity, Raman and IR spectroscopy, the magneto-optic Kerr effect, and photoemission spectroscopy.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Experiments in Inorganic Materials
courses.description: Experimental methods of interrogating electronic ground states and phase behaviors in inorganic materials are presented. Examples include heat capacity, spin susceptibility, electrical/thermal transport, Raman, and spin resonance techniques. The fundamental physics and materials properties underlying each technique are be taught and illustrated by the states/phase behaviors accessible by each.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Functional Inorganic Oxides
courses.description: Intended to give a broad overview of the properties, chemistry and applications of functional inorganic oxides. The course is organized according to structure types (rocksalts, fluorites, rutiles, spinels, corundums, garnets, perovskites, zeolites, etc.) picking up important themes and properties within each group.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Topics in Quantum Materials Measurement
courses.description: Discusses current topics in Quantum Materials Measurement through journal readings, studies of background materials provided, and student presentations. Examples include mesoscopic and quantum transport phenomena as well as phenomena at interfaces and junctions.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Quantum Phenomena in Mesoscopic Materials and Devices
courses.description: This course develops the physical principles behind quantum behavior in nanoscale solid-state devices where phase coherence, confinement, and interactions dominate transport. Topics include quantum point contacts (quantized conductance and shot noise), quantum dots (Coulomb blockade, single-electron tunneling, and Kondo physics), and focus on real materials like topological insulators and superconductors. The course also introduces superconducting hybrid structures and Josephson junction physics, emphasizing how mesoscopic effects emerge in real devices and measurement setups. Students will connect simplified theoretical models to experimental signatures commonly observed in low-temperature nanoelectronics.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Theoretical Foundations of Quantum Materials
courses.description: A rigorous treatment of selected topics in modern solid state physics, including theoretical frameworks (second quantization, Green's functions, density matrix formalism, response functions), many-body effects (interacting electron gas, Fermi liquid theory, electron-phonon coupling, quantum spin models), superconductivity (Ginzburg-Landau theory, BCS theory, Josephson effect, quantum vortices), and topological phenomena (Landau levels and the quantum Hall effect, Berry phase and curvature, modern theory of polarization, topological insulators and superconductors, Majorana fermions).

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: The Art of Scientific Writing
courses.description: This course is about reading the scientific literature critically, and about writing science that is simultaneously impactful and readable. We will discuss what makes scientific papers compelling without being obscure and ambiguous and will practice through critiquing each other’s written work. Preparing tables and graphics, and formatting text will be an intrinsic part of the discussion. Grades will be assigned based on manuscripts produced before the end of the quarter.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Solid State Ionics and Electrochem Devices
courses.description: The objective of this course is to familiarize students with ceramic materials used in state-of-the-art Li ion batteries and that can enable advanced electrochemical technologies such as solid-state and electrical grid batteries. The course will briefly cover fundamental aspects of ceramics and their processing, solid-state electrochemistry, and the design, manufacturing, and characterization of state-of-the-art Li ion and advanced battery concepts.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Special Topics in Macromolecular Materials
courses.description: This course will be offered on a irregular basis and will concern in-depth discussions of advanced topics in macromolecular materials.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Structure and Symmetry
courses.description: Fundamentals of structure and symmetry commonly observed in soft materials. Direct and reciprocal space lattices, symmetry operations, group theory categorization, and tensor calculations of distances, angles, and coordinate transformations. Experimental structure determination. Complex phases.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Sustainability in Materials Science
courses.description: Survey of the role of materials in sustainability. Overview of topics in materials usage and recycling, materials designs for energy efficiency, and manufacturing. Key concepts and models for sustainability including life cycle/materials flow analysis, and energy content. Considerations for sustainability of major classes of materials including metals, semiconductors, and polymers. Applications in energy conversion and storage.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Special Topics in Electronic Materials
courses.description: This course will be offered on an irregular basis and will concern in-depth discussions of advanced topics in electronic materials.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Special Topics in Materials for Quantum Information Science
courses.description: Selected topics relating to materials issues in Quantum Information Science. Quantum Defects: single-spin centers, single-photon emitters. Natively Entangled Materials. Interfaced Topological States.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Power Semiconductor Materials and Devices
courses.description: Material properties and transport physics relevant to power devices, power rectifiers and transistors, superjunctions, wide bandgap power device technologies, emerging topics in power semiconductors.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Special Topics in Electronic Materials
courses.description: This course will be offered on an irregular basis and will concern in-depth discussions of advanced topics in electronic materials.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Special Topics in Structural Materials
courses.description: This course will be offered on an irregular basis and will concern in-depthdiscussions of advanced topics in structural materials.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Special Topics in Structural Materials
courses.description: This course will be offered on an irregular basis and will concern in-depthdiscussions of advanced topics in structural materials.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Special Topics in Structural Materials
courses.description: This course will be offered on an irregular basis and will concern in-depthdiscussions of advanced topics in structural materials.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Phase Stability & Microstructure Evolution
courses.description: Phase diagrams for binary, ternary and higher order systems: thermodynamic foundation, construction and applications. Metastability upon synthesis and processing far from equilibrium: approaches, thermodynamic and kinetic principles, phase selection, solubility extension. Stability and evolution of metastable phases and microstructures.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Statistical Mechanics of Crystalline Solids
courses.description: Covers first-principles methods to predict thermodynamic and kinetic properties of multi-component crystalline solids. Topics include: (i) a review of thermodynamics and statistical mechanics of crystalline solids; (ii) effective Hamiltonians for configurational and vibrational degrees of freedom with a focus on the Ising model, cluster expansions, harmonic and anharmonic lattice dynamical Hamiltonians; (iii) Monte Carlo methods, low temperature expansions, free energy integration methods; (iv) First-principles methods to calculate multi-component phase diagrams; (v) Order-disorder and structural phase transitions and (vi) Atomic diffusion, transition state theory, kinetic Monte Carlo simulations, Kubo-Green.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Crystal Growth and Solidification
courses.description: Addresses crystallization from the melt and solidification of alloys and compounds. Fundamental macroscopic thermal, fluid and mass transfer aspects of growth. Nucleation, growth, the stability of solid/liquid interfaces and microstructure formation during solidification of multicomponent systems. Crystal growth processes are addressed, including Czrochralski and Bridgman growth, shape casting methods and directed energy processes.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Topics in Engineering Leadership
courses.description: As technology increasingly drives strategy and innovation, technical professionals must nurture leadership skills to effectively guide teams, influence organizational decisions, and translate complex technical concepts into value. This graduate-level course introduces essential skills in self-awareness, team management, strategic communication, effective mentorship, negotiation, feedback delivery, and budget management. Each week combines theoretical foundations with hands-on practice through role-playing case studies and conversations with technical leaders. By course completion, students will have exposure to a comprehensive toolkit for charting their leadership journey and driving organizational success.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Dislocations and Dislocation Dynamics
courses.description: Fundamentals of dislocations in crystalline solids and the dynamical behavior of dislocations. Topics covered include: elastic properties of dislocations, dislocation interactions, intersections, arrays, nucleation and sources. Thermally activated glide and climb are addressed along with statistical aspects of dislocation obstacle interactions. Partial dislocations, faults and unique aspects of dislocations in metals, semiconductors, ceramics and intermetallics are covered.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Machine Learning for Materials Science
courses.description: Covers the fundamentals of machine learning tools used in materials science. Application areas include surrogate models for atomistic simulations as well as machine-learning tools for 3-dimensional image analysis and the analysis of experimental data. The course starts with an overview of probability theory and Bayesian inference followed by treatments of regularized regression, Gaussian process models and neural networks. Concepts of invariance and equivariance in the context of spatial transformations will be developed and neural network architectures that are equivariant to translational and rotational transformations will be analyzed.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Mathematics in Materials Science
courses.description: Introduces mathematical concepts necessary to understand and solve materials-related problems, such as phase transformations, pattern formation, and mechanics of solids. Topics include linear algebra, ordinary and partial differential equations, linear stability analysis, and the calculus of variations.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Foundations of Machine Learning for Materials  Science
courses.description: Covers fundamental machine learning tools for materials science, including surrogate models for atomistic simulations, 3D image analysis, and experimental data analysis. It begins with probability theory and Bayesian inference, followed by regularized regression, Gaussian processes, and neural networks. Concepts of invariance and equivariance are introduced, with equivariant neural network architectures discussed. The course also covers ML methods for image analysis (e.g., variational autoencoders, diffusion models, GANs) and natural language processing.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Introduction of nano- and micro-machining
courses.description: Explores the intersection of functional materials and advanced device engineering in the context of nano- and micro-electro-mechanical systems. Students examine the properties and structures of 0D, 1D, and 2D materials—including quantum dots, nanowires, nanotubes, and thin films—and learn how these materials are leveraged in the design, fabrication, and functionalization of N/MEMS devices. Emphasis is placed on understanding how quantum effects and material characteristics influence the performance of sensors, actuators, and other micro/nano-scale components.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Additive Manufacturing
courses.description: Additive manufacturing (AM) encompasses processing techniques that fabricate three- dimensional objects from computer-generated designs through sequential material deposition. This course will provide an overview of current additive manufacturing processes, explore the principles and models for each process, with an emphasis on material evolution during processing. We will discuss process limitations and challenges, as well as process selection considerations. Additionally, we will review current state-of-the-art in process development, applied AM research, and materials development for AM.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Alloy Systems and Design
courses.description: Overview of major principles to be considered in the design of metallic systems, including thermodynamics, kinetics, physical and mechanical properties, processing approaches and environmental considerations. The structure, properties, properties and applications of major metallic systems will be addressed. Systems to be considered include light alloys, titanium alloys, lithium alloys, refractory metals, nickel and cobalt alloys, platinum group metals, copper and ferrous alloys. New tools to guide design of emerging systems will be covered.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Micromechanics
courses.description: Broad overview of micromechanics, emphasizing the microstructure of materials, its connection to atomic structure, and its consequences on macroscopic properties. Topics include order-disorder transition; phase transformations in crystalline solids, including martensitic, ferroelectric, and diffusional phase transformations, twinning and domain patterns, active materials; kinetics of phase transformation; phase field methods with an emphasis on implementing it numerically; computationally interpret the role of diffusion kinetics and surface energy effects on nucleation and growth mechanisms; interpret the origins of material microstructures; as well as several applications to battery electrodes, ferroelectrics, and soft magnets.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Dynamic Mechanical Behavior
courses.description: Dynamic wave propagation in solids. Elastic, plastic and shock waves. Dynamic test techniques and diagnostic tools. Shock-induced phase transformations. Plastic deformation at high strain rates. Dynamic fracture.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Research Group Studies
courses.description: In this course students or instructors present recently published papers and/or results relevant to their own research.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Internship in Industry
courses.prereq_text: Prior departmental approval needed. Materials majors only.
courses.description: Special projects for selected students. Offered in conjunction with engineering practice in selected industrial and research firms, under direct faculty supervision.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Teaching Assistant Practicum
courses.comments: This course is required for new teaching assistants. No unit credit allowed toward advanced degree.
courses.description: Practical experience in the various activities associated with teaching including: lecturing, supervision of laboratories and discussion sections, preparation, and grading of homework and exams.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Directed Reading and Research
courses.description: Individual tutorial. Instructor usually student's major professor. A written proposal for each tutorial must be approved by the department chair.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Master's Thesis Research and Preparation
courses.description: For research underlying the thesis and writing of the thesis.

courses.subject: MATRL
courses.title: Ph.D. Dissertation Research and Preparation
courses.prereq_text: Consent of chair of student's doctoral committee.
courses.description: Research and preparation of the dissertation.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Introductory Biology I
courses.prereq_text: Chemistry 1A-B-C with a grade of C- or better (Chem 1C may be taken concurrently), or a score of 4 or better on either the Advanced Placement Chemistry or Advanced Placement Biology exams.
courses.comments: Concurrent enrollment in MCDB 6 not allowed. Reduced credit of 2.0 units will be given to those who have credit for MCDB 6.
courses.description: Introduction to biochemistry, cell biology and development, and genetics.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Selected Topics from MCDB 1A
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 4AZ or MCDB 4AZ or 5AZ.
courses.description: Designed for transfer students who have completed part of MCDB 1A through transfer work. Topics will be selected by the department, as appropriate, to fulfill the introductory biology requirement at UCSB.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Introductory Biology II--Physiology
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A and Chemistry 1A-B-C with a grade of C- or better; or MCDB 1A with a grade of C or better.
courses.comments: Concurrent enrollment in EEMB 7 not allowed. Reduced credit of 2.0 units will be given for those who have completed EEMB 7.
courses.description: Introduction to animal and plant physiology.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Selected Topics from MCDB 1B
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 4BZ or EEMB 4BZ or 5BZ or MCDB 4BZ or 5BZ.
courses.description: Designed for transfer students who have completed part of MCDB 1B through transfer work. Topics will be selected by the department, as appropriate, to fulfill the introductory biology requirement at UCSB.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Introductory Biology Laboratory I
courses.prereq_text: Grade of C- or better in MCDB 1A (may be taken concurrently).
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 4A or MCDB 4A or 5AL, or 1AL.
courses.description: Laboratory investigations illustrate basic principles of biochemistry, molecular and cell biology, development, genetics & physiology.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Principles of Molecular and Cellular Biology for Brain Sciences
courses.prereq_text: Chem 1A-B with a minimum grade of C- or better in each.
courses.comments: Not open to Prebio/EEMB/MCDB majors. Can't be used in lieu of MCDB 1A for prereqs. Unsuitable for health professions requiring 1 yr of intro bio. Can't take concurrently or if MCDB 1A completed.
courses.description: Introduction to basic biochemistry, cell biology and genetics. Topics include biological macromolecules, molecular basis of heredity, cell theory, cellular organelles, cell division cycle, mitosis, meiosis, fertilization, early development, Mendelian genetics, and molecular genetics. Biological principles will be taught with examples involving the nervous system where appropriate. Designed for Psychological and Brain Sciences majors.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Biology Mentoring and Engagement I
courses.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in Chemistry 1A or Chemistry 2A.
courses.description: Seminar for first year pre-biology students. Focus is on developing scientific study skills and fostering the confidence and motivation involved in higher cognitive learning. Students will engage in peer mentoring activities, problem-solving exercises and relevant discussion promoting academic success.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Biology Mentoring and Engagement II
courses.comments: EEMB 12 and MCDB 12 are the same course.
courses.description: Seminar for first year pre-biology students. Emphasis on developing critical thinking skills by utilizing interactive panel discussions ascertaining why biologists care about subjects like chemistry and math. Deliberation on biology news articles designed to get students thinking like scientists.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Biology Mentoring and Engagement III
courses.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in Chemistry 1C or Chemistry 2C.
courses.comments: EEMB 13 and MCDB 13 are the same course.
courses.description: Seminar for first year pre-biology students. Active learning enhancement via topics exploring students' self-identifying themselves as scientists, conversation on careers within the sciences and health professions, and discussion regarding the research process in order spark motivation and questions.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Biology Mentoring and Engagement IV
courses.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in Chemistry 1C or Chemistry 2C.
courses.description: Seminar for first year pre-biology students. A laboratory course designed to be a research experience for undergraduate students where they learn to apply the scientific method, critical thinking and experimental design to test relevant hypotheses in molecular biology.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Current Biology Topics for Freshmen
courses.comments: Open to Pre-Bio 1st year freshmen only. MCDB 15AA-ZZ courses may be taken for a Maximum of 3 total units, provided letter designations are different, with a limit of 1 MCDB 15AA-ZZ course per quarter.
courses.description: This seminar series is designed to introduce freshmen biology major students to current topics in the biological sciences. Each instructor will select a specific topic of interest that will be the focus of the course.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Past, Present, and Future of the Human Genome
courses.comments: Open to Pre-Bio 1st year freshmen only. MCDB 15AA-ZZ courses may be taken for a Maximum of 3 total units, provided letter designations are different, with a limit of 1 MCDB 15AA-ZZ course per quarter.
courses.description: This course covers the history of human genetics including the eugenics movement in America, the discovery of the genetic material, and sequencing of the human genome. We then explore current research on personal genomics, ancient humanoid DNA, epigenetics, genetics of human behavior, and advances in human genome engineering. Finally, we explore the implications of humans being the first species on earth that can direct its own evolution.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: SCIENCE/fiction
courses.comments: Open to Pre-Bio 1st year freshmen only. MCDB 15AA-ZZ courses may be taken for a Maximum of 3 total units, provided letter designations are different, with a limit of 1 MCDB 15AA-ZZ course per quarter.
courses.description: This seminar introduces cutting-edge biology, genetics, and neuroscience through primary research papers while encouraging discussion of whats next through short science fiction stories. Sometimes imagination leads science; other times fiction popularizes a scientific discovery, tool, or invention. What is possible, aspirational, or cautionary? Topics include: memory, identity, evolution, humanity, destiny, augmentation. Papers on zombie cockroaches, de-extinction, synthetic life, extra senses, implanted memories; Stories by Borges, Dick, Butler, Murakami, McCaffrey, Jemison, and Chiang

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Sensory Neuroscience at the Dining Table
courses.comments: Open to Pre-Bio 1st year freshmen only. MCDB 15AA-ZZ courses may be taken for a Maximum of 3 total units, provided letter designations are different, with a limit of 1 MCDB 15AA-ZZ course per quarter.
courses.description: Gastronomy and sensory neuroscience share a fundamental interest in perception. In this course, we discuss recent progress made in our understanding of the molecular and cellular inner workings of our gustatory and olfactory systems. We review principles of multisensory integration that affect our everyday life and that are exploited by Michelin star chefs. Finally, we examine how the existence of genetic variability in sensation across individuals can explain differences in the way we interact with food.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Introduction to Regenerative Medicine
courses.comments: Open to Pre-Bio 1st year freshmen only. MCDB 15AA-ZZ courses may be taken for a Maximum of 3 total units, provided letter designations are different, with a limit of 1 MCDB 15AA-ZZ course per quarter.
courses.description: A broad introduction to regenerative medicine and cell and gene therapies. Students learn about the diverse career opportunities within the field and the myriad of resources available to them through the California Institute for Regenerative Medicine. Upperclassmen and faculty will participate as guest speakers to review good study habits and other strategies that students can use to pursue a career in regenerative medicine and succeed. As an interactive seminar series, opportunities to practice networking with other scientists are explored. This class offers a safe space where students challenge themselves to explore new ideas in a supporting environment.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Biology in Science Fiction
courses.comments: Open to Pre-Bio 1st year freshmen only. MCDB 15AA-ZZ courses may be taken for a Maximum of 3 total units, provided letter designations are different, with a limit of 1 MCDB 15AA-ZZ course per quarter.
courses.description: We discuss the scientific underpinnings of Biology as it is portrayed in science fiction literature and film. Class discussion focuses on examining the reality behind the fiction by discussing questions such as: How close are we to living forever? Could we actually build Spiderman or clone armies? Do zombies exist?

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Unraveling the Science of Flavor:  From Genetics and Data to Michelin Stars
courses.comments: Open to Pre-Bio 1st year freshmen only.
courses.description: This introductory course investigates the intersection between gastronomy and neuroscience, focusing on the principles underlying food perception. Through hands-on experiments, we explore the molecular and cellular mechanisms that shape our senses of taste and smell. For instance, we will examine the genetic basis that makes cilantro taste delightful to some and soapy to others. By understanding multi-sensory integration, we will discuss why it is a secret weapon for any skilled cook. During the whole class, theory is presented through interactive demonstrations, offering a practical approach to understanding flavor science. Additionally, the course covers basics of experimental design, data analysis and hypothesis testing.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Concepts of Biology
courses.comments: Not open for credit toward graduation to students who completed EEMB 20, EEMB 22, EEMB W 22, MCDB 1A, EEMB 2, MCDB 1B, or EEMB 3. Concurrent enrollment in MCDB 1A, EEMB 22 or EEMB W 2 not allowed.
courses.description: Introduction to the science of life; cells, genetics, metabolism, molecular biology, physiology, natural selection, evolution, ecosystems; current news and controversial topics in biology.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: The Immune System and Aids
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 21.
courses.description: The basic properties of the immune system; the basic biology of aids and AIDS virus infection; and the biology of other sexually transmitted diseases.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Biology of Cancer
courses.comments: Not open to students who have completed MCDB 1A. Concurrent enrollment in MCDB 1A is not allowed.
courses.description: An introduction to developments regarding the etiology and treatment of various cancers. Lectures compare normal cells and tissues with those which have become malignnant. Discussion of causes, treatment, and prevention of specific cancers.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Contemporary Nutrition
courses.description: Presents the scientific basis for human nutrition including dietary nutrients and requirements, energy balance in health and disease, and needs of various life stages. Food safety, preservation, and undernutrition throughout the world is discussed.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Human Genetics and Society
courses.description: Principles of Mendelian inheritance as illustrated by human traits and diseases; chromosomes and sex determination; distribution of genes in populations; social, cultural and ethical implications of modern genome research are reviewed. Appropriate for non-science majors.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Fundamentals of Biomedical Research
courses.description: Basics of the scientific method as applied to basic biomedical research; examples of how basic research influences human health. Students will develop the intellectual tools to deconstruct primary literature and interpret data.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Internship in Biological Sciences
courses.prereq_text: Lower-division standing; instructor and departmental approval required.
courses.comments: Students must have a 2.5 cumulative grade-point average. May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 15 units, but no units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: Opportunity to obtain practical biological-related research experience by working under faculty direction as an intern with local, state, federal, or private agencies. A written report will be submitted for evaluation.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Honors Forum in Molecular, Cellular, Developmental Biology
courses.prereq_text: Honors standing in College of Letters and Science and consent of instructor
courses.description: Seminar for selected students in molecular, cellular, and developmental biology. Students will be introduced to research opportunities in the department. Focus will center on the use of the science library and the internet as tools to produce a basic research paper.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Special Topics in Biology
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 4 units.
courses.description: Special topics in molecular, cellular, and developmental biology. Course content varies. Information may be obtained in department office.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Readings in Biology
courses.comments: Students are required to have a minimum 3.0 cumulative grade-point average and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined. Students are limited to 6 units of Biology 98 and MCDB 98 combined. Maximum of 3 units/quarter.
courses.description: Special readings on selected topics in biology. Individual conferences one hour every week. Designed to broaden the outlook and experience of advanced lower-division students. Hours and credit by arrangement with any member of the staff.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Introduction to Research
courses.comments: Students are required to have a minimum 3.0 cumulative grade-point average and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined. Students are limited to 6 units of Biology 99 and MCDB 99 combined. Maximum of 3 units/quarter.
courses.description: Laboratory experience for advanced lower-division students. Hours and credit by arrangement with any member of the staff.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Molecular Genetics I: Prokaryotes
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A-B, EEMB 2; and, Chemistry 1A-B-C; completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
courses.comments: Concurrent enrollment in EEMB 129 not allowed. Reduced credit of 2.0 units will be given to students who have received credit for EEMB 129.
courses.description: From the double helix and genetic code to the latest breakthroughs. Structure, function, evolution and manipulation of DNA, RNA. Replication, expression, recombination, complementation, and their regulation in prokaryotes (bacteria, plasmids, viruses). Recombinant DNA technology in medicine, research, agriculture and industry.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Molecular Genetics I: Prokaryotes - Honors
courses.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in MCDB 101A; consent of instructor.
courses.description: Honors section designed to permit an in-depth analysis of topics relating to genetics.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Molecular Genetics II: Eukaryotes
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B, and MCDB 101A. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
courses.comments: Concurrent enrollment in EEMB 129 not allowed. Reduced credit of 2.0 units will be given to students who have received credit for EEMB 129.
courses.description: Mendelian and molecular genetics. Replication, recombination, transmission and expression of DNA in eukaryotic organisms from yeast to man. Uses of traditional genetics and modern molecular techniques, including molecular genetic approaches to the study of human disease.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Molecular Genetics II: Eukaryotes - Honors
courses.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in MCDB 101B; consent of instructor.
courses.description: Honors section designed to permit an in-depth analysis of topics relating to genetics.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Molecular Genetics Laboratory
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 101A-B or EEMB 129; MCDB 101B may be taken concurrently. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Current molecular genetics techniques used to study model organisms. Module1 - Forward genetics: Mutagenesis and genetic mapping of mutants using single nucleotide polymorphisms, classical Mendelian inheritance. 2) Reverse genetics: gene knockdown by RNAi. 3) Genetic analysis of cell signaling. 4) Cellular reprogramming using transgenic strains. Techniques: PCR, gel electrophoresis, Computer based sequence analysis, fluorescence and light microscopy and imaging. Experiments are based on ongoing research at UCSB. Students get to design their own experiment in final module.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Cell Biology
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, and EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B. Completion of all listed prerequisites wita grade of C or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 137.
courses.description: An introduction to the structure and function of cell organelles; membranes, nucleus, mitochondria, chloroplasts, endoplasmic reticulum, golgi apparatus, lysosomes, microbodies, microtubules, cilia, centrioles, and microfilaments.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Cell Biology - Honors
courses.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in MCDB 103; consent of instructor.
courses.description: The overall goal of MCDB 103H is to extend the concepts covered in MCDB 103 and apply them to the context of research. For each selected topic, students read a short review article in the first week which provides the historical background and current consensus, followed by a landmark research article in the following week. The course is in the format of journal club with an emphasis on open discussion. Each week, a group of students give an oral presentation and lead class discussion.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Laboratory in Molecular Cell Biology
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, and EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B, and MCDB 103 (may be taken concurrently). Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 137L.
courses.description: Laboratory techniques of modern cell biology; molecular dissection of cell structure and function.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Biochemistry - Structure and Function of Macromolecules
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, and EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B; and Chemistry 1A-B-C; and Chemistry 109A-B-C (Chem 109C may be taken concurrently). Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 108A or MCDB W 108A. Reduced credit of 2.0 units for those who have completed MCDB 110. Concurrent enrollment in MCDB 110 not allowed.
courses.description: Introduction to the structures and functions of proteins, including enzymes, with emphasis on their basic architecture and biological mechanisms of action and regulation. Methods used for characterizing proteins and analyzing enzyme kinetic data are also emphasized.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Biochemistry - Structure and Function of Macromolecules - Honors
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 108A or MCDB W 108A (may be taken concurrently). Consent of instructor.
courses.description: Honors component of MCDB 108A or W108A designed to permit an in-depth consideration of selected aspects of the structure/function relationships of proteins and nucleic acids.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Biochemistry - Bioenergetics, Enzymology, and Metabolism
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 108A or MCDB W 108A with a grade of C or better.Chem 109C with a grade of C or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 108B. Reduced credit of 2.0 units for those who have completed MCDB 110. Concurrent enrollment in MCDB 110 not allowed.
courses.description: Principles of human energy metabolism. Chemistry and physiology of the major metabolic pathways of energy production. Metabolic interrelationships of the major body organs. Applications to human nutrition and disease, exercise, starvation, obesity, and atherosclerosis.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Biochemistry - Computational & Systems Biology
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 108A-B with a grade of C or better or MCDB W 108A and MCDB 108B with a grade of C or better; Physics 6A-B-C with minimum grade of C (Physics 6C may be taken concurrently); Math 34A-B with a grade of C or better or Math 3A-B with a grade of C or better or Math 2A-B with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Models of Biochemical and Cellular Systems. Introductory systems-biology approach to model the design and the function of biological systems. Students will develop an intuition about physical concepts that are fundamental to discuss how biological organisms acquire and process information from the environment. Those concepts and tools will cover probabilities and basic dynamical systems theory. Students will build models of processes of increasing complexity, ranging from viral dynamics, bacterial resistance to drugs, the maintenance of homeostatic equilibrium (trp operon), biological oscillators (mitotic clock) and genetic switches underlying cellular decisions (bacteriophage lambda and lac operon).

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Laboratory in Biochemistry
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 108A or MCDB W 108A; and MCDB 108B; and MCDB 1A-1B. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 109L.
courses.description: Laboratory techniques in biochemistry. Focus will be on contemporary biochemical techniques used in biomedical research including the analysis of proteins, recombinant DNA expression and protein purification, enzyme regulation, steady-state kinetic analysis and metabolic control. Emphasis will be on both theoretical and practical aspects.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Principles of Biochemistry
courses.prereq_text: Chemistry 1A-B-C; and Chemistry 109A-B. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
courses.comments: Not for MCDB majors & physiology, nor for those who have completed MCDB 108A-B. Reduced credit of 2.0 units for those who have completed MCDB 108A. Concurrent enrollment in MCDB 108A not allowed.
courses.description: An introduction to molecular structures and mechanisms of living systems.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Human Physiology
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, and EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B with a grade of C or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 100.MCDB W 111 is the online version of MCDB 111.
courses.description: Fundamentals of human physiology at the molecular, cellular and organismal levels. Emphasis on homeostatic mechanisms regulating intercellular communication, muscle function, circulation, metabolism and body fluid balance/composition.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Human Physiology - Honors
courses.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in MCDB 111; consent of instructor.
courses.description: Honors section designed to permit an in-depth analysis of topics relating to fundamentals of human physiology at the molecular, cellular and organismal levels. Emphasis on homeostatic mechanisms regulating intercellular communication, muscle function, circulation, metabolism and body fluid balance/composition.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Developmental Biology
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, and EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B, and EEMB 3; and MCDB 101A or EEMB 129. Completion of all listed prerequisties with a grade of C or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Zoology 100.
courses.description: Modern aspects of animal development. Molecular and cellular mechanisms of embroygenesis.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Developmental Biology - Honors
courses.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in MCDB 112; consent of instructor.
courses.description: Honors section designed to permit an in-depth analysis of topics relating to the mechanisms of animal development, from single cells to the whole organism, using examples from vertebrates and invertebrates studied in terms of morphology, physiology, genetics and biochemistry.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Laboratory in Developmental Biology
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B, and EEMB 3, and MCDB 101A, and concurrent enrollment in MCDB 112. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Modern laboratory techniques in developmental biology. Experimental aproaches to development using several animal model systems.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Plant Development
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, and EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B; and, MCDB 101A or EEMB 129. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 112 or Botany 111.
courses.description: Differentiation and morphogenesis of plants: mechanisms of cell-cell interactions.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Experimental Strategies in Physical Biochemistry
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 108A or MCDB W 108A or Chemistry 142A with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Presentation of selected contemporary concepts and methodologies for determining the structure, size, shape, charge, and interactive behavior of biological macromolecules.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Basic Pharmacology
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 101A (may be taken concurrently) or Chemistry 142C; Chemistry 109A-B-C. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Covers a wide range of drugs with a focus on drugs used to treat disorders of the nervous and cardiovascular systems, antibacterial agents, antivirals, and anticancer drugs. Also looks at the pharmacology of inflammation and coagulation. The goal is to understand the underlying physiology behind disorders of these systems and the mechanisms of the drugs used to treat them. Additional out-of-class hours are necessary.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Pharmacology Lab I
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 126 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of C; or MCDB 126A with a minimum grade of C.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed EEMB 126AL.
courses.description: Analysis of drug sites and machanisms of action using isolated tissues, organs, and intact animal preparations.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Basic Pharmacology
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 101A or Chemistry 142C; Chemistry 109A-B-C. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
courses.comments: MCDB 108A is strongly recommended. Not open for credit to students who completed Biology 119B.
courses.description: Receptor signaling mechanisms; pharmacology of neurotransmitter and hormone receptors; molecular and cellular mechanisms of drug-receptor interactions.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Basic Pharmacology II: Hormone and Neurotransmitter Receptors and Signaling- Honors
courses.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in MCDB 126B; consent of instructor.
courses.description: Honors section designed to permit an indepth analysis of topics relating to receptor signaling mechanisms; pharmacology of neurotransmitter and hormone receptors; molecular and cellular mechanisms of drug-receptor interactions.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Pharmacology Laboratory II
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 119BL.
courses.description: An introduction to molecular and biochemical techniques in pharmacology; drug-receptor binding; receptor isolation; pharmacokinetics; techniques to evaluate potency, concentration and effects of hormones and their receptors.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: General Microbiology
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 101A; Chemistry 109A-B-C (Chem 109C may be taken concurrently), or Chemistry 109A-B and MCDB 110. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 104 or 104A.
courses.description: Focuses on the general biology in microbes, primarily prokaryotes. Topics include the structure, physiology, and development of microorganisms and microbial communities, their culture and control, microbial genomics & metagenomics, and the importance of diverse microbes in food, agriculture, ecology and medicine.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Laboratory in General Microbiology
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 104 or 104L.
courses.description: Laboratory experiments dealing with the isolation, cultivation, and physiological, biochemical and genetic analysis of diverse microorganisms.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Bacterial Pathogenesis
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 101A with a grade of C or better.
courses.comments: MCDB 131 recommended. Not open for credit to students who have completed MCDB 139 (MCDB 139 and MCDB 132 cannot be taken concurrently). Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 128.
courses.description: The mechanisms by which bacterial pathogens cause disease. Investigation of the bacterial gene products that are produced during infection to understand the metabolic, physiological, and genetic factors that contribute to the virulence of bacterial pathogens.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Bacterial Pathogenesis Laboratory
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 128L.
courses.description: The latest molecular, biochemical, and genetic techniques available for theidentification of microbial gene products that contribute to infection. Study of the regulatory parameters that govern their expression.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Molecular and Cellular Immunobiology
