courses.prereq_text: MCDB 101A with a grade of C or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 123.
courses.description: Introduction to the current concepts of immunology. Emphasis on immunoglobulin structure and function, cell-cell cooperation in the immune response, and the role of major histocompatibility complex and cytokines in regulating immune responsiveness.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Immunobiology-Honors
courses.description: Honors component of MCDB 133 focusing on selected aspects of the immune system and its components using a web browser to run interactive computer assignments.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Molecular and Cellular Immunobiology Lab
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 133 with a grade of C or better (may be taken concurrently).
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 123L.
courses.description: Introduction to modern laboratory methods in immunology; properties and characterization of immunoglobulins and immunoglobulin-secreting cells; introduction to hybridoma technology; characterization of effector and regulatory T cells using functional assays.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: General Animal Virology
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 101A or EEMB 129 with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: An introduction to the biology of animal viruses with emphasis on the biochemical and biophysical properties of viruses; the mechanisms by which animal viruses replicate; the cellular effects of and response to viral infection; and selected aspects of medical virology.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: General Animal Virology-Honors
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 101A; concurrent enrollment in MCDB 134. Completion of all prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Honors virology course designed to permit an in-depth consideration and analysis of selected aspects of the biology and biochemistry of animal viruses, the mechanisms by which they replicate, and mechanisms of antiviral innate immunity.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Cellular Growth Control and Oncogenesis
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 101A-B with a grade of C or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 138.
courses.description: Focuses on mechanisms of growth control of eukaryotes. Topics include: the properties of mammalian cells in culture and how they relate to malignant cells, growth factors and their receptors, cell cycle control, oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Cellular Growth Control and Oncogenesis - Honors
courses.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in MCDB 135; consent of instructor.
courses.description: Honors section designed to permit an in-depth analysis of topics relating to Cellular Growth Control and Oncogenesis.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Cytokine Action and Viral Pathogenesis
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 101A and MCDB 101B (101B may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of C.
courses.description: Honors virology course designed to permit an in-depth consideration of selected aspects of the mechanisms of action of cytokines, with emphasis on the antiviral properties of interferons and their roles in host to viral infection and viral pathogenesis.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Medical Immunology
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 101A OR EEMB 129 with a grade of C or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed MCDB W 138.
courses.description: By focusing on recent groundbreaking advances in our understanding of the vertebrate immune system, this course explores the contrasting mechanisms of protective immunity against parasites and cancer with various immune disorders that mainly stem from immune dysregulation, such as autoimmunity, acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS), allergies, and other diseases. By engaging in interactive, case-based computer exercises, students will have an opportunity to emulate the discovery of the underlying biological defects that give rise to these and other immune-related diseases.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Medical Microbiology
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, and EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B, and EEMB 3. Completion of all prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed MCDB 132 (MCDB 132 and MCDB 139 cannot be taken concurrently). MCDB 139 should not be taken by Microbiology Majors.
courses.description: Study of the characteristics of bacteria and viruses, both pathogenic and adventitious, as they are associated with diseases of humans.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Medical Microbiology - Honors
courses.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in MCDB 139; consent of instructor.
courses.description: Honors section designed to permit an in-depth analysis of topics relating to Medical Microbiology.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Recombinant DNA Methods
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 101A-B and 110; or MCDB 101A-B and MCDB 108A-B-C (MCDB 108C may be taken concurrently); or MCDB 101A-B and MCDB W 108A and MCDB 108B-C (MCDB 108C may be taken concurrently). Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 132.
courses.description: Basic techniques of molecular cloning. Screening of recombinant cDNA libraries, polymerase chain reaction, restriction endonucleases, gel electrophoresis, DNA sequencing, nucleic acid hybridization.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Post-translational Protein Processing
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 108A or MCDB W 108A or CHEM 142A or CHEM W142A with a grade of C or better.
courses.comments: Same course as Chemistry 151.
courses.description: Structure/function relationships in interesting macromolecules isolated from marine organisms. Focus is on well-characterized pathways from horseshoe crabs, abolones, mussels, and fish as well as others.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Stem Cell Biology in Health and Disease
courses.prereq_text: Chemistry 1A-B-C with a minimum grade of C; MCDB 1A-B, EEMB 2-3 with a minimum grade of C.
courses.description: Basic biology of embryonic and adult stem cells and nuclear transfer, with emphasis on latest findings from the current literature.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Neurobiology I: Cellular Organization and Biophysics of the Nervous System
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A and 1B. Completion of both prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
courses.comments: Not open for students who have completed Biology 105 or MCDB 114 for a C or better.
courses.description: Properties of the nervous system ranging from single cells to the whole organism, using examples from vertebrates and invertebrates studied in terms of morphology, physiology, and behavior.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Neurobiology 1: Cellular Organization and Biophysics of the Nervous System - Honors
courses.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in MCDB 151; consent of instructor.
courses.description: Honors section designed to permit an indepth analysis of topics relating to the properties of the nervous system ranging from single cells to the whole organism, using examples from vertebrates and invertebrates studied in terms of morphology, physiology, and behavior.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Neurobiology II: Molecular and Cellular Neurobiology
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A-1B and MCDB 151; completion of all prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: This second course of a three quarter neurobiology course sequence (151/152/153) covers both top down systems level approaches and bottom up molecular approaches to major topics in neurobiology. These topics include mechanisms of sensory transduction, processing of sensory information within the brain, mechanisms of muscle control, cell signaling, neuronal plasticity, neuronal polarity, and the mapping of neural information to the brain.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Neurobiology III: Developmental Neurobiology
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A-1B; and, MCDB 101A or EEMB 129; completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 106 or MCDB 115. (However, legal repeat policy applies).
courses.description: The course begins with fertilization and moves through sequential stages in the development of the nervous system, including cell migration and differentiation, axon outgrowth and pathfinding, programmed cell death, synaptogenesis, learning, memory, neurodegenerative conditions and current strategies for neuronal regeneration.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Research Immersion in Molecular Biosciences
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A-B with a minimum grade of B in each.
courses.description: Intensive laboratory course covering basic approaches to biomedical research using model systems. Students will learn laboratory techniques as well as hypothesis building, experimental design, data analysis and data presentation.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Programming in Biology
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B; and MCDB 101A or EEMB 129 (may be taken concurrently); and Pstat 5A or Pstat 5LS or Math 4A. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Studying complex biological systems can be greatly facilitated by modern computing technologies. This course introduces essential computer programming concepts and algorithms to biology major students. Students learn logics of programming and apply it to gene sequence analysis (bioinformatics), simulation of dynamic systems (systems biology), and data analysis (statistics in biology).

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Biological Dynamics
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B; and MCDB 101A or EEMB 129; and either Math 4A OR MCDB 108C. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: An introduction to mathematical models and computer simulations used to describe and understand time varying biological systems. Learning Objectives: Survey mathematical methods for describing the dependence on time of biological phenomena. Illustrate how to construct mathematical models to gain insights into complex biological systems. Develop working knowledge of a python code base that enables future evaluation of common classes of models applied to the study of biological dynamics.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Computational Drug Discovery
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B; and MCDB 101A or EEMB 129; and either Math 4A OR MCDB 108C. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Foundation models, large neural networks pretrained on enormous unlabeled corpora, have become the dominant computational tool in biology over the last five years. Protein language models such as ESM-2 and ESM-3 predict 3D structure & design new proteins from sequence alone. Genome-scale models such as Evo 2 predict pathogenicity for clinical variants without supervised fine-tuning. Single-cell models such as Geneformer and Universal Cell Embeddings represent millions of cells across species in shared coordinate spaces. AlphaFold 3 and Boltz-2 unify protein, nucleic acid, and small-molecule structure prediction in single architectures. Phenotypic-profiling models trained on Cell Painting microscopy have entered drug discovery pipelines.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Introduction to Teaching in Biology
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 5 units. may not be applied toward the major.
courses.description: Students will assist instructor in teaching course in which the student previously received a grade of A- or better. Activities will be determined in consultation with the instructor and may include leading discussion, laboratory, or tutorial section(s), attending lectures, and grading exams.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Internship in Biological Sciences
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; instructor and departmental approval required.
courses.comments: Students must have a 2.5 cumulative grade-point average. may be repeated for credit to a maximum of 15 units, but no units may be applied toward the major (except Aquatic Biology, see restrictions in major narrative).
courses.description: Opportunity to obtain practical biological-related research experience by working under faculty direction as an intern with local, state, federal, or private agencies. A written report will be submitted for evaluation.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Pharmacology Colloquia
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B, and EEMB 3 with a minimum grade of C or better in each prereq course.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 4 units, but only 2 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: Research seminars on current research topics in pharmacology presented by invited speakers.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Literature in Plant Molecular Biology
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 168.
courses.description: Critical reading and presentation of the current literature in plant molecular biology, cell biology and development.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.prereq_text: Chem 1A-B-C with a minimum grade of C; MCDB 1A-B and EEMB 2 with a minimum grade of C. Upper-division standing in EEMB or MCDB and consent of instructor or department.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit in combination with Biology 192 and EEMB 192. Maximum units for credit in major: 8 for B.S.; 4 for B.A.
courses.description: Special topics of current importance in biological sciences. Course content will vary. Information may be obtained in department office.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Group Studies for Advanced Students
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit in combination with Biology 194AA-ZZ and EEMB 194AA-ZZ to a maximum of 8 units. Individual letter designations may be repeated for credit to a maximum of 4 units. Maximum units for credit in major: 8 BS; 4 BA. See also credit limits with other courses in description of major requirements.
courses.description: Oral reports by students.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Bacterial Genetics.
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit in combination with Biology 194AA-ZZ and EEMB 194AA-ZZ to a maximum of 8 units. Individual letter designations may be repeated for credit to a maximum of 4 units. Maximum units for credit in major: 8BS; 4 BA. See also credit limits with other courses in description of major requirements.
courses.description: Oral reports by students.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: C. Elegans Development and Behavior
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit in combination with Biology 194AA-ZZ and EEMB 194AA-ZZ to a maximum of 8 units. Individual letter designations may be repeated for credit to a maximum of 4 units. Maximum units for credit in major: 8 BS; 4 BA. See also credit limits with other courses in description of major requirements.
courses.description: Reports by students.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Dissecting the Behavior of Mosquito Disease Vectors
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit in combination with Biology 194AA-ZZ and EEMB 194AA-ZZ to a maximum of 8 units. Individual letter designations may be repeated for credit to a maximum of 4 units. Maximum units for credit in major: 8 BS; 4 BA. See also credit limits with other courses in description of major requirements.
courses.description: This course will focus on the latest developments in understanding how mosquito disease vectors find human host, and mate. The focus will be on mechanistic studies, particularly those that combine molecular genetics with behavior.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Diversity in STEM
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit in combination with Biology 194AA-ZZ and EEMB 194AA-ZZ to a maximum of 8 units. Individual letter designations may be repeated for credit to a maximum of 4 units. Maximum units for credit in major: 8 BS; 4 BA. See also credit limits with other courses in description of major requirements.
courses.description: A seminar-style workshop that introduces students to the contributions, careers, and backgrounds of diverse researchers in STEM fields. The goals of the class are (1) to expose participants to the multicultural and diverse ways of thinking about, performing, and interpreting science; and (2) to foment the appreciation for how We, as a community, can move towards creating a STEM field that is more inclusive of diverse contributions and individuals. Students are responsible for completing short assignments, show-casing a specific scientist, and directed readings on diversity in STEM. Participants are encouraged to reflect on their own experiences and bring their unique perspectives and opinions to each discussion.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Developmental Biology
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit in combination with Biology 194AA-ZZ and EEMB 194AA-ZZ to a maximum of 8 units. Individual letter designations may be repeated for credit to a maximum of 4 units. Maximum units for credit in major: 8 BS; 4 BA. See also credit limits with other courses in descriptionof major requirements.
courses.description: Oral reports by students.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Neurobiology
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit in combination with Biology 194AA-ZZ and EEMB 194AA-ZZ to a maximum of 8 units. Individual letter designations may be repeated for credit to a maximum of 4 units. Maximum units for credit in major: 8 BS; 4 BA. See also credit limits with other courses in description of major requirements.
courses.description: Literature-based exploration of core concepts in modern neuroscience. Skill in training in critical reading of primary literature, science writing, and presentation. Content focus changes each year: past topics include Neuroethology, Neuronal Identity, Motor Control, Sensory Motor Integration, Optogenetics and Functional Imaging.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Bacterial Cell Biology
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit in combination with Biology 194AA-ZZ and EEMB 194AA-ZZ to a maximum of 8 units. Individual letter designations may be repeated for credit to a maximum of 4 units. Maximum units for credit in major: 8 BS; 4 BA. See also credit limits with other courses in description of major requirements.
courses.description: Explore the recent advances in bacterial cell biology with a focus on uncultivated taxa. Also explores the latest development of cultivation-independent techniques allowing scientists to probe these uncultivated microbes.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Science for the Common Good
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit in combination with Biology 194AA-ZZ and EEMB 194AA-ZZ to a maximum of 8 units. Individual letter designations may be repeated for credit to a maximum of 4 units. Maximum units for credit in major: 8 BS; 4 BA. See also credit limits with other courses in description of major requirements.
courses.description: Required non major applicable course for UCSB Beckman Scholars. Designed to introduce outstanding undergraduate researchers to their role as citizen-scientists/engineers and leaders in applying scientific approaches to global problems. Students must be conducting research while taking this course.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Immune Cell Biology and Immunotherapy
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit in combination with Biology 194AA-ZZ and EEMB 194AA-ZZ to a maximum of 8 units. Individual letter designations may be repeated for credit to a maximum of 4 units. Maximum units for credit in major: 8 BS; 4 BA. See also credit limits with other courses in description of major requirements.
courses.description: Will focus on recent literature related to immune cell biology and cancer-immune interactions. Students will read and discuss a paper each week. The students will alternate as discussion leaders. As discussion leader they will prepare a short presentation to facilitate discussion. Some background in immunology, cell biology and genetics is required.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Microbial Pathogenesis
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit in combination with Biology 194AA-ZZ and EEMB 194AA-ZZ to a maximum of 8 units. Individual letter designations may be repeated for credit to a maximum of 4 units. Maximum units for credit in major: 8 BS; 4 BA. See also credit limits with other courses in descriptionof major requirements.
courses.description: Oral reports by students.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Introduction to Microscopy for the Bio-sciences
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit in combination with Biology 194AA-ZZ and EEMB 194AA-ZZ to a maximum of 8 units. Individual letter designations may be repeated for credit to a maximum of 4 units. Maximum units for credit in major: 8 BS; 4 BA. See also credit limits with other courses in description of major requirements.
courses.description: An introduction to microscopy emphasizing light microscopy techniques and principals. A wide variety of microscopy techniques will be introduced while students gain hands-on experience with transmitted light and fluorescence imaging and exposure to high-end imaging instruments.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Neural Circuits
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit in combination with Biology 194AA-ZZ and EEMB 194AA-ZZ to a maximum of 8 units. Individual letter designations may be repeated for credit to a maximum of 4 units. Maximum units for credit in major: 8 BS; 4 BA. See also credit limits with other courses in description of major requirements.
courses.description: Presentation and discussion of current research in circuit-level neuroscience. This course will focus on how neural circuits mediate specific behaviors, drawing on research from a range of species and preparations.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Plant Development Genetics
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit in combination with Biology 194AA-ZZ and EEMB 194AA-ZZ to a maximum of 8 units. Individual letter designations may be repeated for credit to a maximum of 4 units. Maximum units for credit in major: 8 BS; 4 BA. See also credit limits with other courses in descriptionof major requirements.
courses.description: Oral reports by students.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Biostatistics
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit in combination with Biology 194AA-ZZ and EEMB 194AA-ZZ to a maximum of 8 units. Individual letter designations may be repeated for credit to a maximum of 4 units.
courses.description: Statistics is an important tool to convey scientific discoveries with a quantitative measure of significance and confidence. In this group study, practical issues in applying statistics to biological data will be discussed.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Systems Medicine
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit in combination with Biology 194AA-ZZ and EEMB 194AA-ZZ to a maximum of 8 units. Individual letter designations may be repeated for credit to a maximum of 4 units. Maximum units for credit in major: 8 BS; 4 BA. See also credit limits with other courses in description of major requirements.
courses.description: Explores systems medicine through computational modeling of physiological circuits. Students will develop Python simulations to understand hormone circuits, immune system behavior, and aging processes. Combines theoretical foundations with hands-on modeling exercises to examine how diseases emerge from circuit fragilities. Through mathematical modeling and computational analysis, students will investigate complex physiological systems and learn disease classification based on signaling topology. Students will gain both theoretical knowledge and applied computational skills while exploring how feedback, robustness, and emergent behaviors influence health and disease.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Cell Biology Topics
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit in combination with Biology 194AA-ZZ and EEMB 194AA-ZZ to a maximum of 8 units. Individual letter designations may be repeated for credit to a maximum of 4 units. Maximum units for credit in major: 8 BS; 4 BA. See also credit limits with other courses in description of major requirements.
courses.description: Select current topics in the field of cell biology (e.g. cell division, intracellular protein transport, and cytoskeleton dynamics) and discuss how these new findings advance our understanding of cell physiology and behavior.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Directed Studies.
courses.prereq_text: MCDB majors only; and, consent of instructor and department; and upper- division standing; and, two upper-division courses in MCDB or EEMB.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum grade-point average of 2.5 in upper-division major courses and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 197/198/199/199RA courses combined. Maximum units for credit defined on major sheets. See also credit limits with other courses in description of major requirements.
courses.description: Hours and credit by arrangement with any faculty member.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Directed Readings
courses.prereq_text: MCDB majors only; and, consent of instructor and department; and upper- division standing; and, two upper-division courses in MCDB or EEMB.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum grade-point average of 3.0 in upper-division major courses and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined. Maximum units for credit in major: 8 BS; 4 BA. See also credit limits with other courses in description of major requirements.
courses.description: Individual conferences one hour every two weeks. special readings designed to broaden the outlook of students and to knit into a cohesive whole the basic principles underlying the major disciplines in the field.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Independent Studies
courses.prereq_text: MCDB majors only; and, consent of instructor and department; and upper-division standing; and, two upper-division courses in MCDB or EEMB.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum grade-point average of 3.0 in upper-division major courses and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined. Maximum units for credit in major: 8 BS; 4 BA. See also credit limits with other courses in description of major requirements. Tutorial, 1-3 hours; field, 1-5 hours.
courses.description: Hours and credit by arrangement with any faculty member. Laboratory or field.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Cell Biology
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A-AL or MCDB 1B-BL or EEMB 2-2L, or equivalents.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 237.
courses.description: Introduction to the structure and function of cell organelles: membranes, nucleus, mitochondria, chloroplasts, endoplasmic reticulum, golgi apparatus, lysosomes, microbodies, microtubules, cilia, centrioles, and microfilaments.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Biochemistry - Computational & Systems Biology
courses.comments: Interactions between students at all levels will be fostered so that graduate students will have an opportunity to develop their communication and mentorship skills with undergraduates.
courses.description: Models of Biochemical and Cellular Systems. Introductory systems-biology approach to model the design and the function of biological systems. Students will develop an intuition about physical concepts that are fundamental to discuss how biological organisms acquire and process information from the environment. Those concepts and tools will cover probabilities and basic dynamical systems theory. Students will build models of processes of increasing complexity, ranging from viral dynamics, bacterial resistance to drugs, the maintenance of homeostatic equilibrium (trp operon), biological oscillators (mitotic clock) and genetic switches underlying cellular decisions (bacteriophage lambda and lac operon).

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Molecular Virology
courses.description: Consideration of selected animal viruses in terms of structure, mechanism of genetic expression, and effects of viral gene expression on cell function, as well as aspects of the virus-host interaction including viral persistence, interference, and interferon.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Methods and Logic in Molecular Cell Biology I
courses.comments: Required for MCDB Graduate students.
courses.description: Molecular genetics and gene regulation. Experimental design and approaches, and a focus on critical thinking and problem solving, will reveal how fundamental, highly significant biological problems are unraveled using molecular genetic strategies. Reading will be assigned from a mix of classic and current peer-reviewed papers.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Methods and Logic in Molecular Cell Biology II
courses.comments: Required for MCDB Graduate students
courses.description: Molecular cellular biology in a variety of model systems and contexts from an integrated perspective. A collection of approaches, and a focus on critical thinking and problem solving, will reveal how highly significant biological problems are unraveled using cutting edge technologies. Includes an introduction to bioinformatics, computational, and systems biology. Reading will be assigned from a mix of classic and current peer-reviewed papers.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Preparation and Evaluation of Research Proposals and Scientific Presentations
courses.description: Instruction in preparation writing, and evaluation of research grant proposals. Overview of federal funding mechanisms, ethics in research, the peer review and proposal evaluation processes, and general strategies in communication of scientific ideas including poster and oral presentations. This course is writing based and includes instruction and guidance on applying to NSF and NIH Pre-Doctoral Fellowships.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Signal Transduction
courses.description: A cell's growth is controlled by positive and negative cues from its surroundings. We will discuss the cell's signaling mechanisms that recognize these cues and initiate an intracellular set of events that generates a response.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Signal Transduction and Development in Multicellular Systems
courses.comments: IQB 226 and MCDB 224 are the same course.
courses.description: Cellular and organismal growth and other responses are controlled by positive and negative cues from both internal and external sources. We discuss the signaling mechanisms that recognize these cues and initiate an intracellular set of events that generates a response. We also discuss the molecular mechanisms of pattern formation and cellular differentiation that underlie developmental processes in a variety of important multicellular model systems.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Basic Pharmacology
courses.comments: Graduate students will have separate grading rubrics, with different assignments, and different final assignments.
courses.description: Will cover a wide range of drugs with a focus on drugs used to treat disorders of the nervous and cardiovascular systems, antibacterial agents, antivirals, and anticancer drugs. Will will also look at the pharmacology of inflammation and coagulation. The goal is to understand the underlying physiology behind disorders of these systems and the mechanisms of the drugs used to treat them. Additional out-of-class hours are necessary.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Pharmacology Lab I
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 219AL.
courses.description: Analysis of drug sites and mechanisms of action using isolated tissues, organs, and intact animal preparations.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Basic Pharmacology
courses.description: Receptor signalling mechanisms; pharmacology of neurotransmitter and hormone receptors; molecular and cellular mechanisms of drug-receptor interactions.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Pharmacology Laboratory II
courses.description: An introduction to molecular and biochemical techniques in pharmacology; drug-receptor binding; receptor isolation; pharmacokinetics; techniques to evaluate potency, concentration and effects of hormones and their receptors.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Protein Biochemistry
courses.comments: Same course as BMSE 229.
courses.description: Discussion topics relevant to structure-function relationships in proteins including the chemical reactivity of amino acid side chains, posttranslational modifications, and the covalent and noncovalent interactions of multimeric structures. Case studies involve recent advances in structure-function relationships of mechanoproteins.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: General Microbiology
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A-AL or MCDB 1B-BL or EEMB 2-2L; Chemistry 107A-B and 108, or Chem 130A-B-C, or Chem 109A-B-C.
courses.description: Introduction to biological properties of microrganisms historical foundations of the field of microbiology; a study of major groups of microorganisms, their structure, physiology, cultivation, and pathogenicity.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Bacterial Pathogenesis
courses.comments: MCDB 231 recommended.
courses.description: The mechanisms by which bacterial pathogens cause disease. Investigation ofthe bacterial gene products produced during infection to understand the metabolic, physiological, and genetic factors that contribute to the virulence of bacterial pathogens.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Molecular and Cellular Immunobiology
courses.description: Introduction to, and evaluation of, the current concepts of immunology. Emphasis on immunoglobulin structure and function, cell-cell cooperation in the immune response, and the role of the major histocompatibility complex in regulating immune responsiveness.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Post-Translational Protein Processing
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 108A or MCDB 218A or Chemistry 142A or equivalent.
courses.comments: Same course as BMSE 204 and Chemistry 251.
courses.description: Structure/function relationships in interesting macromolecules isolated from marine organisms. Focus is on well-characterized pathways from horseshoe crabs, abalones, mussels, and fish as well as others.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Stem Cell Biology in Health and Disease
courses.comments: Graduate Course. Qualified undergraduate students may petition to enroll with instructor approval.
courses.description: Basic biology of embryonic and adult stem cells and nuclear transfer, with emphasis on latest findings from the current literature.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Practical Statistics for Biologists
courses.description: Introduces fundamental concepts in biostatistics such as sources of technical and biological variation, types of statistical tests (ANOVA, non-parametric, linear regression), sampling techniques, power calculations, and how to decide which test is appropriate.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Neurobiology I: Cellular Organization and Biophysics of the Nervous System
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A and 1B or equivalent. Completion of both prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Nervous system properties ranging from single cells to whole organisms, using examples from vertebrates/invertebrates studied in terms of morphology, physiology, behavior.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Neurobiology II: Molecular and Cellular Neurobiology
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 251 with a grade of B or better.
courses.description: This second course of a three quarter neurobiology course sequence (251/252/253) will cover both top down systems level approaches and bottom up molecular approaches to major topics in neurobiology. These topics include mechanisms of sensory transduction, processing of sensory information within the brain, mechanisms of muscle control, cell signaling, neuronal plasticity, neuronal polarity, and the mapping of neural information to the brain.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Neurobiology III: Developmental Neurobiology
courses.description: This course begins with fertilization and moves through sequential stages in the development of the nervous system, including cell migration and differentiation, axon outgrowth and pathfinding, programmed cell death, synaptogenesis, learning, memory, neurodegenerative conditions and current strategies for neuronal regeneration.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Neurobiology
courses.description: Literature-based exploration of core concepts in modern neuroscience. Skill in training in critical reading of primary literature, science writing, and presentation. Content focus changes each year: past topics include Neuroethology, Neuronal Identity, Motor Control, Sensory Motor Integration, Optogenetics and Functional Imaging.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Stem Cell Biology
courses.comments: Graduate Course. Qualified undergraduate students may petition to enroll with instructor approval.
courses.description: Focuses on the latest developments in stem cell biology, including ongoing clinical trials using stem cell therapies to treat unmet medical needs. In depth analysis of the current literature in stem cell biology, bioengineering and biophysical analyses is also covered. The discipline of stem cell biology and applications of cell therapy have elements of bioengineering, biomaterials, and biophysics.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Research Strategies in Molecular, Cellular and Developmental Biology
courses.description: A review and critique of relevant literature in advance of the weekly MCBD Biology research seminar. Includes illustrating the significance, identifying the key findings, evaluating data and conclusions, and proposing further directions and questions. Practice of presentation skills. Weekly meeting with seminar speakers.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Literature in Immunology
courses.description: Critical reading and presentation of recent literature in immunology.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Research Progress in Molecular, Cellular and Developmental Biology
courses.description: Research presentations by postdoctoral fellows and advanced Ph.D. students of research progress in the department.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Progress in Biochemistry and Molecular Biology
courses.description: Research seminars presented by invited speakers on current research topics.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Literature in Plant Molecular Biology
courses.description: Critical reading and presentation of the current literature in higher plantmolecular biology, cell biology, and development.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Pharmacology Colloquia
courses.description: Research seminars on current research topics in pharmacology presented by invited speakers.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Programming in Biology
courses.comments: Graduate students will have separate grading rubrics, with different homework assignments, and different final assignments.
courses.description: Studying complex biological systems can be greatly facilitated by modern computing technologies. This course introduces essential computer programming concepts and algorithms to biology major students. Students learn logics of programming and apply it to gene sequence analysis (bioinformatics), simulation of dynamic systems (systems biology), and data analysis (statistics in biology).

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Biological Dynamics
courses.comments: Graduate students will have separate grading rubrics, with different homework assignments, and different final assignments.
courses.description: An introduction to mathematical models and computer simulations used to describe and understand time varying biological systems. Learning Objectives: Survey mathematical methods for describing the dependence on time of biological phenomena. Illustrate how to construct mathematical models to gain insights into complex biological systems. Develop working knowledge of a python code base that enables future evaluation of common classes of models applied to the study of biological dynamics.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Computational Drug Discovery
courses.comments: This course teaches students to read these models critically, use them effectively, and judge their claims with the skepticism of a working biologist. It pairs a technical machine learning spine (vectors, em- beddings, attention, self-supervision, scaling laws) with a tour of biological model families (proteins, structures, genomes, single cells, small molecules, microscopy, pathology, biodiversity). Every lecture closes with a five-question failure-mode box that asks the same five questions of every model: what does it know, what does it not know, what benchmark are we trusting, what experiment would test the limit, and what goes wrong if we trust it too far.
courses.description: Foundation models, large neural networks pretrained on enormous unlabeled corpora, have become the dominant computational tool in biology over the last five years. Protein language models such as ESM-2 and ESM-3 predict 3D structure & design new proteins from sequence alone. Genome-scale models such as Evo 2 predict pathogenicity for clinical variants without supervised fine-tuning. Single-cell models such as Geneformer and Universal Cell Embeddings represent millions of cells across species in shared coordinate spaces. AlphaFold 3 and Boltz-2 unify protein, nucleic acid, and small-molecule structure prediction in single architectures. Phenotypic-profiling models trained on Cell Painting microscopy have entered drug discovery pipelines.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Group Studies
courses.description: Presentation and discussion of current research, to be selected from the following list. (see individual letter designations)

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: C Elegans Development
courses.description: Presentation and discussion of current research, to be selected from the following list. (see individual letter designations)

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Dissecting the Behavior of Mosquito Disease Vectors
courses.description: This course will focus on the latest developments in understanding how mosquito disease vectors find human host, and mate. The focus will be on mechanistic studies, particularly those that combine molecular genetics with behavior.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Developmental Neurobiology
courses.description: Presentation and discussion of current research.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Epithelial Cell Biology and Molecular Renal Pathobiology
courses.description: Presentation and discussion of current research, to be selected from the following list. (see individual letter designations)

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Topics at the Interface of the Physical and Biological Sciences
courses.description: This interdisciplinary course will train students to become competent in communicating research project design, implementation, and data analysis to scientific audiences of their peers. Students will interact directly with the faculty mentor and other members of a laboratory team.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Bacterial Cell Biology
courses.description: ExploreS the recent advances in bacterial cell biology with a focus on uncultivated taxa. Also explores the latest development of cultivation-independent techniques allowing scientists to probe these uncultivated microbes.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Immune Cell Biology and Immunotherapy
courses.description: Focus is on recent literature related to immune cell biology and cancer-immune interactions. Students will read and discuss a paper each week. The students will alternate as discussion leaders. As discussion leader they will prepare a short presentation to facilitate discussion. Some background in immunology, cell biology and genetics is required.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Introduction to Microscopy for the Bio-sciences
courses.description: An introduction to microscopy emphasizing light microscopy techniques and principals. A wide variety of microscopy techniques will be introduced while students gain hands-on experience with transmitted light and fluorescence imaging and exposure to high-end imaging instruments.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Neural Circuits
courses.description: Presentation and discussion of current research in circuit-level neuroscience. Focuses on how neural circuits mediate specific behaviors, drawing on research from a range of species and preparations.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Group Studies
courses.description: Presentation and discussion of current research, to be selected from the following list. (see individual letter designations)

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Systems Medicine
courses.description: Explores systems medicine through computational modeling of physiological circuits. Students will develop Python simulations to understand hormone circuits, immune system behavior, and aging processes. Combines theoretical foundations with hands-on modeling exercises to examine how diseases emerge from circuit fragilities. Through mathematical modeling and computational analysis, students will investigate complex physiological systems and learn disease classification based on signaling topology. Students will gain both theoretical knowledge and applied computational skills while exploring how feedback, robustness, and emergent behaviors influence health and disease.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Computational Methods in Biochemistry-Molecular Biology
courses.description: Survey of computational methods in molecular biology. Topics include analysis and presentation of data, database searching, quantitative image analysis, and protein homology modeling. Emphasis on utilizing accessible software tools that are designed for nonprogrammers.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Bioengineering: Career and Development Opportunities at the Interface between Biotechnology and Engineering
courses.comments: Same as BMSE 294B and CH E 294B
courses.description: Based on presentations by experts from the bioengineering industry. Presenters describe their companies' technologies and developments, including biosensors, therapeutics, tissue engineering, quantum dots and advanced instrumentation. Training and educational requirements for different career tracks are discussed.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Teaching Assistant Orientation
courses.comments: No unit credit allowed toward advanced degree. May be repeated for credit in combination with Biology 500.
courses.description: General orientation regarding the University of California and the Santa Barbara campus; various pertinent regulations, officials and their functions, staff and functions; services available to teaching assistants and to students. Prospective teaching assistants are encouraged to take this course during the fall quarter prior to their employment.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Practicum in Instruction
courses.comments: No unit credit allowed toward advanced degree. May be repeated for credit in combination with Biology 501.
courses.description: Practical experience in teaching within specified areas of biology. Students will have responsibility for one or more laboratory and/or discussion sections. Staff will periodically observe teaching assistants in actual teaching situations. Evaluation forms will be completed by members of the class sections.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Techniques of Teaching and Laboratory Class Supervision
courses.comments: Required of all teaching assistants. No unit credit allowed toward advanced degree. May be repeated for credit in combination with Biology 502.
courses.description: Weekly discussion and readings on techniques of teaching including lecturing, leading discussions, writing and grading exams, student- teacher interactions, classroom dynamics, and teaching philosophy.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Research Practium in Biology
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit in combination with Biology 503.
courses.description: Basic procedures and methods of research in a specific area as determined by consultation between the supervising faculty member and the research assistant. Includes weekly meetings and consultations, and formal evaluations.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: MCDB Literature Seminar
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 36 units. Individual letter designations may be repeated for credit to a maximum of 36 units.
courses.description: A critical review of research in selected fields of biology. Subject matter for these seminars will be selected from the following list: (refer to individual letter designations.)

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Bacterial Genetics
courses.comments: Same course as BMSE 595BG. May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 36 units. Individual letter designations may be repeated for credit to a maximum of 36 units.
courses.description: A critical review of research in selected fields of biology.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Diversity in STEM
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 36 units. Individual letter designations may be repeated for credit to a maximum of 36 units.
courses.description: A seminar-style workshop that introduces students to the contributions, careers, and backgrounds of diverse researchers in STEM fields. The goals of the class are (1) to expose participants to the multicultural and diverse ways of thinking about, performing, and interpreting science; and (2) to foment the appreciation for how We, as a community, can move towards creating a STEM field that is more inclusive of diverse contributions and individuals. Students are responsible for completing short assignments, show-casing a specific scientist, and directed readings on diversity in STEM. Participants are encouraged to reflect on their own experiences and bring their unique perspectives and opinions to each discussion.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Developmental Biology
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 36 units. Individual letter designations may be repeated for credit to a maximum of 36 units.
courses.description: A critical review of research in selected fields of biology.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Discipline-based Education Research in Science
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 36 units. Individual letter designations may be repeated for credit to a maximum of 36 units.
courses.description: A critical reading of the literature in discipline-based educational research in the sciences.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Microbial Pathogenesis
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 36 units. Individual letter designations may be repeated for credit to a maximum of 36 units.
courses.description: A critical review of research in selected fields of biology.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Neural Circuits
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 36 units. Individual letter designations may be repeated for credit to a maximum of 36 units.
courses.description: Presentation and discussion of current research in circuit-level neuroscience. This course will focus on how neural circuits mediate specific behaviors, drawing on research from a range of species and preparations.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Group Studies
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 36 units. Individual letter designations may be repeated for credit to a maximum of 36 units.
courses.description: A critical review of research in selected fields of biology. Subject matter for these seminars will be selected from the following list: (refer to individual letter designations.)

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Directed Reading and Research
courses.description: Hours and credit by arrangement with faculty.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Individual Study for Master's Comprehensive Examinations and Ph.D. Examinations
courses.comments: No unit credit allowed toward advanced degree. Students are limited to 24 units per examination, and 12 units per quarter. May be repeated for credit in combination with Biology 597.
courses.description: Individual study for M.A. comprehensive examinations and Ph.D. examinations.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Master's Thesis Research and Preparation
courses.prereq_text: M.A. (thesis) candidate and consent of committee chair.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit in combination with Biology 598 to a maximum 12 units. No unit credit is allowed toward advanced degree.
courses.description: For research underlying the thesis and writing of the thesis.

courses.subject: MCDB
courses.title: Ph.D. Dissertation Preparation
courses.prereq_text: Ph.D. candidate and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit in combination with Biology 599 to a maximum of 12 units.
courses.description: For writing of the dissertation.

courses.subject: MCDB W
courses.title: Biochemistry - Structure and Function of Macromolecules
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, and EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B; and Chemistry 1A-B-C; and Chemistry 109A-B-C (Chem 109C may be taken concurrently). Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 108A or MCDB 108A. Reduced credit of 2.0 units for those who have completed MCDB 110. Concurrent enrollment in MCDB 110 not allowed.
courses.description: Introduction to the structures and functions of proteins, including enzymes, with emphasis on their basic architecture and biological mechanisms of action and regulation. Methods used for characterizing proteins and analyzing enzyme kinetic data are also emphasized.

courses.subject: MCDB W
courses.title: Human Physiology
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, and EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B with a grade of C or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Biology 100.MCDB W 111 is the online version of MCDB 111.
courses.description: Fundamentals of human physiology at the molecular, cellular and organismal levels. Emphasis on homeostatic mechanisms regulating intercellular communication, muscle function, circulation, metabolism and body fluid balance/composition.

courses.subject: MCDB W
courses.title: Medical Immunology
courses.prereq_text: MCDB 101A OR EEMB 129 with a grade of C or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed MCDB 138.
courses.description: By focusing on recent groundbreaking advances in our understanding of the vertebrate immune system, this course explores the contrasting mechanisms of protective immunity against parasites and cancer with various immune disorders that mainly stem from immune dysregulation, such as autoimmunity, acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS), allergies, and other diseases. By engaging in interactive, case-based computer exercises, students will have an opportunity to emulate the discovery of the underlying biological defects that give rise to these and other immune-related diseases.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Basic Electrical and Electronic Circuits
courses.prereq_text: Physics 7B, or Physics 3 and Physics 3L; and Mathematics 4A, or 4AI, or 3C; open to ME majors only.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed ECE 2A or 2B, or ECE 6A or 6B.
courses.description: Introduction to basic electrical circuits and electronics. Includes Kirchhoff's laws, phasor analysis, circuit elements, operational amplifiers and transistor circuits.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Engineering Graphics: Sketching, CAD and Conceptual Design
courses.description: Introduces hands-on engineering design via lessons on the design process, Computer Aided Design (CAD), free hand sketching, use of a laser cutter, soldering, basic circuits, basic microprocessor programming, motors and gear trains. Makes use of a robotic project to allow students to practice all above topics. Students create dimensioned engineering drawings and present their designs at a final design fair. The focus of the course is to empower students to leverage all engineering tools listed above in their future engineering courses.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Introductory Concepts in Mechanical Engineering
courses.description: The theme question of this course is, "What do mechanical engineers do?" Survey of mechanical engineering applications. Lectures by mechanical engineering faculty and practicing engineers.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Manufacturing Processes
courses.description: Processes used to convert raw material into finished objects. Overview of manufacturing processes including: casting, forging, machining, presswork, plastic and composite processing. Videos, demonstrations, and tours illustrate modern industrial practice. Selection of appropriate processes.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Introduction to Machine Shop
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Mechanical Engineering 156S.Course materials fee required.
courses.description: Basic machine shop skills course. Students learn to work safely in a machine shop. Students are introduced to the use of hand tools, the lathe, the milling machine, drill press, saws, and precision measuring tools. Students apply these skills by completing a project.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Leadership and Equitable Resources
courses.description: Assisting emerging leaders in understanding diversity to advocate, build, and sustain a collaborative culture of learning and opportunities for constituencies. Guides emerging leaders in evaluating the significance and consequences of decisions linked to professional outcomes and accountability systems. An introduction to theoretical and practical frameworks for the engagement and advocacy for social justice leadership.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Statics
courses.prereq_text: Math 2B, or Math 3B, or AP Calculus AB with a score of 5, or AP Calculus BC with a score of 3 or better; and Physics 7A, or Physics 1
courses.description: Introduction to applied mechanics. Forces, moments, couples, and resultants; vector algebra; construction of free body diagrams; equilibrium in 2- and 3-dimensions; analysis of frames, machines, trusses and beams; distributed forces; friction.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Strength of Materials
courses.prereq_text: ME 14 with a minimum grade of C-; open to mechanical engineering majors only.
courses.description: Properties of structural materials, including Hookes law and behavior beyond the elastic limit. Concepts of stress, strain, displacement, force, force systems, and multiaxial stress states. Design applications to engineering structures, including problems of bars in tension, compression, and torsion, beams subject to flexure, pressure vessels, and buckling.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Engineering Mechanics: Dynamics
courses.prereq_text: Physics 7A or Physics 2, and ME 14 with a minimum grade of C-, and Math 6B or Math 5C (may be taken concurrently); open to ME majors only.
courses.description: Vectorial kinematics of particles. Coordinate systems, moving frames, relative and constrained motion. Dynamics of particles and systems of particles. Energy and momentum methods. Collisions. Planar kinematics and kinematics of rigid bodies. Energy and momentum methods for rigid body systems.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Mathematics of Engineering
courses.prereq_text: Engineering 3; open to ME majors only.
courses.description: Introduction to basic numerical and analytical methods, with implementation using MATLAB. Topics include a Matlab review, ordinary differential equations, partial differential equations and boundary conditions, eigenvalue/eigenvectors. Graphic and visualization tools in Matlab.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Toy Product Design
courses.description: Introduction to the product design process with a focus on designing for play and entertainment. It is a project-centric class. Students work in small teams of 5-6 members to design and prototype new toys. Students will be introduced to various design topics, including: brainstorming; estimation; sketching; graphic design; industrial design drawing; sketch modeling; concept development; design aesthetics; prototyping; and written, visual, and oral communication.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Introduction to Mechanical Engineering
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 6 units.
courses.description: Participation in projects in the laboratory or machine shop. Projects may be student- or faculty-originated depending upon student interest and consent of faculty member.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Mechanical Engineering Design Projects
courses.comments: May be repeated for maximum of 12 units.
courses.description: Course offers students opportunity to work on established departmental design projects. P/NP grading, does not satisfy technical elective requirement.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Introduction to Research
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 6 units. Students are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
courses.description: Directed study to be arranged with individual faculty members. Course offers exceptional students an opportunity to participate in a research group.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Professional Seminar
courses.comments: May be repeated for up to 3 units. May not be used as a departmental elective.
courses.description: A series of weekly lectures given by university staff and outside experts in all fields of mechanical engineering.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Finite Elements Analysis of Heat Transfer and Fluid Flow with COMSOL
courses.prereq_text: ME151B and ME152A; or by consent of Instructor
courses.description: Study of modeling and analysis of Heat Transfer and Fluid Flow problems using Finite Elements numerical techniques. Students learn to develop sound numerical models of engineering devices using COMSOL Multiphysics Finite Elements software. Addresses geometry construction, model development, meshing, results generation, and physical analysis.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Dynamical Systems
courses.description: Equations of Motion for Mechanical, Electrical, Heat, Fluid, and Control Systems. Block diagram algebra and interconnections. Laplace transform. Transfer functions and dynamic stability. First and second order systems. Frequency response. Introduction to mechanical vibrations and feedback control design.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Mechatronics
courses.prereq_text: ME 6 and ME 103; open to ME majors only.
courses.description: Interfacing of mechanical and electrical systems and mechatronics. Basic introduction to sensors, actuators, and computer interfacing and control. Transducers and measurement devices, actuators, A/D and D/A conversion, signal conditioning and filtering. Practical skills developed in weekly lab exercises.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Mechanical Engineering Laboratory
courses.prereq_text: ME 151B, ME 152A, ME 103; and MATRL 101 or MATRL 100C.
courses.comments: Quarters usually offered: Spring
courses.description: Introduction to fundamental engineering laboratory measurement techniques and report writing skills. Experiments from thermosciences, fluid mechanics, mechanics, and materials science. Introduction to modern data acquisition and analysis techniques.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Machine Learning
courses.description: Introduces students to machine learning and deep learning. ME 107 is taught at the undergraduate level and teaches students how to identify a machine learning problem in the context of real-world applications, mathematically formulate a learning problem, identify when a learning problem is well-posed, under-determined and overdetermined, and develop algorithms and Python code to solve the problem. Students are introduced to the concepts of learning algorithms, overfitting, under-fitting, statistical measures of estimators, optimization approaches to learning, principal component analysis, regression, support vector machines, and artificial neural networks.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Applications of Finite Element Analysis
courses.description: Modeling and translation into practical FEA using SolidWorks simulation tools. The course focuses on choosing the correct constraints for parts and assembly. Another focus is on moving parts within SolidWorks. If time permits the class considers optimization of mechanical structures based on anticipated loads. This class goes through the cycle of designing, performing FEA, testing and repeat. SolidWorks, including its geometry optimization module, is used in this class as a calculator. This fulfills the need of industry (SolidWorks), while preparing students to Capstone and other courses.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Aerodynamics and Aeronautical Engineering
courses.description: Concepts from aerodynamics, including lift and drag analysis for airfoils as well as aircraft sizing/scaling issues. Structural mechanics concepts are applied to practical aircraft design. Intended for students considering a career in aeronautical engineering.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Energy
courses.prereq_text: Senior Undergraduate or Graduate Student status in the College of Engineering; or consent of Instructor
courses.description: Introduction to the field of Energetics. Topics may include energy sources and production, energy usage, renewable technologies, hardware, operating principles, environmental impact, energy reserves, national and global energy budgets, historical perspectives, economics, societal considerations, and others.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Soft Robotics
courses.comments: May not be taken for additional credit by students who have completed ME 125EH. May not be taken by students who have completed ME 223 or ME 225EH.
courses.description: Learning from the versatility and robustness of bodies in nature, robotic devices are moving away from the traditional rigid form to designs that intentionally and carefully incorporate compliance. We explore this emerging paradigm of robots by 1) modeling the underlying mechanics of soft systems, such as soft actuators, sensors, and bodies, 2) examining current literature and gleaning design principles, and 3) designing and fabricating soft robotic devices in a hands-on laboratory setting. This course includes a final project; students are expected to design, model, fabricate, and test either a subcomponent or a full soft robot.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Special Topics in Mechanical Engineering
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different. Students are advised to consult their faculty advisor before making their course selection.
courses.description: Individual courses concentrating on one area in the following subjects: applied mechanics, cad/cam, controls, design, environmental engineering, fluid mechanics, materials science, mechanics of solids and structures, ocean and coastal engineering, robotics, theoretical mechanics, thermal sciences, and recent developments in mechanical engineering.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Biofluid Mechanics
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different. Students are advised to consult their faculty advisor before making their course selection.
courses.description: Applies the principles of fluid mechanics and transport phenomena to major biological systems, in particular the human body. The course focuses on physiologically relevant flow and transport phenomena from an engineering perspective. Topics covered include blood flow in the cardiovascular system, air flow in the respiratory system, transport processes in joints, and how abnormal fluid mechanics relates to disease. Addresses the rheology of complex fluids, flow through elastic tubes, and transport in porous media. Simple numerical models will be used in the course.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Learning in Model Predictive Control
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different. Students are advised to consult their faculty advisor before making their course selection.
courses.description: Explores the use of data to design safe and effective controllers, through the lens of model predictive control. Introduction to standard optimal control and model predictive control formulations, with emphasis on implementation rather than theory. Introduction to “learning model predictive control”, which then serves as a foundation for evaluating performance and safety of other common data-driven control methods (e.g. Reinforcement Learning and Imitation Learning). The course is implementation-focused through a combination of lectures and simulation-based control design activities. Experience with controls is required; experience with optimization is helpful. Prereqs: 155A or equivalent.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Special Topics in ME: Bio-Inspired Design in Fluid Mechanics
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different. Students are advised to consult their faculty advisor before making their course selection.
courses.description: Students will study evolutionary adaptation as a source for inspiration, extracting design principles to leverage the functionality, adaptability, and robustness of biological systems. The course focuses on Biologically Inspired Design in Fluids to advance student knowledge of natural strategies and facilitate quantitative analysis of the proposed solutions. Over the quarter, the students will learn how biological systems deal with fluids and the bio-inspired design process. The course includes lectures, case studies, and design activities. The final projects aim to share bio-inspired design through STEM programs for K-6 students. We recommend that students take ME152A prior to taking this course.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Special Topics in Soft Robotics
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different. Students are advised to consult their faculty advisor before making their course selection.
courses.description: Learning from the versatility and robustness of bodies in nature, robotic devices are moving away from the traditional rigid form to designs that intentionally and carefully incorporate compliance. We will explore this emerging paradigm of robots by 1) understanding and analytically modeling subcomponents, such as soft actuators, sensors, and bodies, 2) examining current literature and gleaning design principles, and 3) designing and fabricating in a hands-on setting. This course includes a final group project; students are expected to design, model, fabricate, and test either a subcomponent or a full soft robot. Analytical modeling will be at an advanced undergraduate level.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Special Topics: Hydrodynamic Instability and Turbulence
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different. Students are advised to consult their faculty advisor before making their course selection.
courses.description: Hydrodynamic instabilities and turbulent flows are ubiquitous in fluid mechanics, from natural phenomena to industrial and technological applications. The goal of the course is to provide an introduction to the transition to unstable and turbulent flows. We will discuss some classical hydrodynamic instabilities and the analytical tools available to predict their existence and the patterns generated. The second part of the class will focus on turbulence and the methods of statistical analysis available to provide a description of such flows.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Special Topics: Failure Analysis
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different. Students are advised to consult their faculty advisor before making their course selection.
courses.description: Failures lead to investigation, examination, innovation, and redesign into improved, safer, and more efficient components and structures. In this course, we study engineering failures that have occurred across a wide range of disciplines, and examine why they happened. This includes a discussion of the fundamental engineering concepts at play (e.g. stress corrosion cracking, creep, high cycle fatigue), as well as the path by which these factors caused the disaster under study, and the ethics involved in each case.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Special Topics: Li Ion Batteries
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different. Students are advised to consult their faculty advisor before making their course selection.
courses.description: An introduction to lithium-ion batteries (LIB). The course consists of a significant laboratory component where students acquire hands-on experience in handling, analyzing, and studying state-of-the-art (SOA) LIBs. Students also learn how to design, manufacture, and test prototype batteries made using prototype manufacturing equipment. Course Prerequisites: General materials science course background and students must have valid UCSB general laboratory safety certification.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Special Topics in ME: Design and Construction of Scientific Apparatus
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different. Students are advised to consult their faculty advisor before making their course selection.
courses.description: This course applies fundamental mechanical engineering principles to designing and constructing experimental apparatus and scientific measurement systems. A wide range of skills are necessary including mechanical design, fabrication techniques, motion control, sensors, electronics and environmental controls. Application of these skills allows for construction of entire mechanical, electrical, optical, biomechanical and electromagnetic testing equipment. In addition, most of these apparatus require environmental control such as high and low temperature, vacuum, inert gas, and liquid conditions.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Special Topics in Mechanical Engineering: Intro to Design Optimization
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different. Students are advised to consult their faculty advisor before making their course selection.
courses.description: Optimization seeks to extend numerical simulation models, by solving an "inverse problem," to determine a set of design variables that can lead to an "optimized design." In this class we will develop a mathematical foundation for design optimization, and then apply that framework, using modern software tools, to optimize real-world engineering designs.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Special Topics: MEMS Characterization
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different. Students are advised to consult their faculty advisor before making their course selection.
courses.description: Focuses on developing the foundational understanding of experimental approaches and analysis techniques commonly used to characterize MEMS devices. Covered topics will include basic optics principles, optical microscopy (including stereoscopy, fluorescence imaging, confocal systems, and super-resolution techniques), force spectroscopy methods (optical tweezers, magnetic tweezers), electron microscopy, vibrational analysis and scanning probe techniques (AFM), with examples drawn from the use of MEMS devices for biosensor development, metrology, and other engineering applications, including device quality control.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Special Topics in ME: Research Topics in Machine Learning and System Identification
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different. Students are advised to consult their faculty advisor before making their course selection.
courses.description: Introduces students to research topics at the interface of system identification, data science, and machine learning. Reviews linear algebra, probability and information theory, and general concepts from learning algorithms. Introduction to the notion of estimators, maximum-likelihood estimation, stochastic gradient descent, and algorithm design. Provides an overview of deep feedforward networks, regularization strategies for deep learning, and optimization strategies for learning architectures. Introduces topics in system identification and reviews past and present approaches for using neural networks to perform system identification.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Engineering Approaches to Solve Wicked Problems and Global Challenges
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different. Students are advised to consult their faculty advisor before making their course selection.
courses.description: Explores how engineers tackle solving 'wicked problems': problems that are ill-structured, with multiple interdependent variables and no clear optimal solutions.
