Such problems are highly multidisciplinary, often requiring input and innovation across technological, scientific and societal domains. Wicked problems seem to defy standard and structured solutions, and challenge engineers to develop new ways of thinking and communicating. Through case studies, discussions, and projects we will learn from past successes and failures and determine best practices, while exploring how engineers can prepare to lead solutions to the world's most pressing problems.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Soft mechanics: Design and Applications
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different. Students are advised to consult their faculty advisor before making their course selection.
courses.description: We will discuss some applications of soft mechanics to study various complex systems. There will be weekly presentations by students and readings of several classic book chapters and papers from the literature of applied mathematics, soft matter physics, and engineering. Examples of topics include elasticity, fluid mechanics, biophysics, and biomechanics, along with their applications to societal challenges such as epidemiology and health. Each student will work on a project throughout the quarter and is expected to write a research-like manuscript on the investigated topic. The final manuscript could be a review and not (necessarily) original new work.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Special Topics in Mechanical Engineering: Wind and Tidal Extraction Over Large Scales
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different. Students are advised to consult their faculty advisor before making their course selection.
courses.description: Covers the fluid mechanics of wind and tidal energy, with an emphasis on quantitatively estimating available resources and power extracted. Requires prior completion of ME152A/B or similar introductory fluid mechanics course.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Special Topics in Mechanical Engineering: Radiative Energy Transfer
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different. Students are advised to consult their faculty advisor before making their course selection.
courses.description: Investigates the role of thermal radiation in the exchange of energy between engineered surfaces, and the problem of managing overall heat transfer. Topics include the fundamentals of thermal radiation, covering Plank's spectral distribution, Stefan-Boltzmann law, Wien's displacement law, Kirchhoff's law, spectral and total properties of radiative surfaces, including black, diffuse, gray, specular, and nongray surfaces. Analytical methods for analysis of radiative exchange between surfaces are developed using both Radiosity formulations and Network Analogies. Finally, radiative exchange between surfaces is coupled to multimode heat transfer problems, including those having contributions from conduction and convection.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Chemo-Mechanics: The Intersection of Solid Mechanics and Chemistry
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different. Students are advised to consult their faculty advisor before making their course selection.
courses.description: Covers basic thermodynamics, the role of chemistry and mechanics in thermodynamics, and the issue of kinetics when the system is not in thermodynamic equilibrium. Emphasis will be placed on the thermodynamics of deformable solids, with mechanical stress, chemical reactions, other chemical phenomena, and species transport included in the formulation. As indicated above, examples will be selected from oxidation and corrosion, electrochemical energy conversion and storage, the behavior of gels and elastomers, biological cell mechanics, and other topics.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Special Topics in Mechanical Engineering: Waves and Flow
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different. Students are advised to consult their faculty advisor before making their course selection.
courses.description: Waves are one of the most distinct and important phenomena in fluid mechanics. Various aspects of waves and their role in different types of flows will be considered in this advanced undergraduate course. Topics include open-channel incompressible flows and closed-channel compressible flows. Appropriate conservation laws, thermodynamics principles and numerical methods will be developed to support these topics.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Advanced Engineering Thermodynamics
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different. Students are advised to consult their faculty advisor before making their course selection.
courses.description: An extension to ME151A and discusses advanced concepts in engineering thermodynamics, with practical applications in energy generation, transport, conversion, and storage processes. Topics include: free energies, Maxwell relations, refrigeration cycles and technologies, thermodynamics of solar energy, introduction to statistical thermodynamics, and other topics related to renewable energy research. Prerequisite: ME151A or equivalent courses on thermodynamics.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Special Topics: Vehicle Dynamics
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different. Students are advised to consult their faculty advisor before making their course selection.
courses.description: Selected topics in automotive vehicle dynamics, with applications to road or race cars. Introduces fundamental principles and mathematical descriptions, including topics in vehicle kinematics, kinetics, dynamics and handling, tire friction and mechanics, steering dynamics, suspension mechanisms and dynamics, and vehicle models. Select advanced topics may be introduced, such as performance-based control, trajectory optimization, human operator control, or aerodynamics.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Special Topics in Mechanical Engineering: Introduction to interfacial phenomena
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different. Students are advised to consult their faculty advisor before making their course selection.
courses.description: Introduces fundamental and applied aspects of interfacial systems. Covers theory of capillarity, interfacial tensions, Laplace pressure, curvature effects on the equilibrium states of fluids, surfactants, fundamentals of wetting and contact angle, adhesion, cohesion, and spreading, superhydrophilicity and superhydrophobicity. Relevant research fields are be introduced, including oil-water separation, electronics cooling, condensation, and bio-inspired functional surfaces.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Bio-Inspired Design in Fluid Mechanics
courses.comments: May not be taken for additional credit by students who have completed ME 125ED. May not be taken by students who have completed ME 226 or ME 225ED.
courses.description: Students will study evolutionary adaptation as a source for inspiration, extracting design principles to leverage the functionality, adaptability, and robustness of biological systems. The course focuses on Biologically Inspired Design in Fluids to advance student knowledge of natural strategies and facilitate quantitative analysis of the proposed solutions. Over the quarter, the students learn how biological systems deal with fluids and the bio-inspired design process. The course includes lectures, case studies, and design activities. The final projects aim to share bio-inspired design through STEM programs for K-6 students.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Introduction to Mechanisms
courses.description: Generation, analysis, and refinement of the design of electro-mechanical devices for common machine elements including fasteners, joints, springs, bearings, gearing, motors, pneumatics, clutches, couplings, belts, chains, and shafts making use of physics, mathematics, and engineering principles.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Design of Biomedical Devices
courses.prereq_text: Mechanical Engineering 10, 14, 15, 16 or ME W 16, and 153; open to ME majors only.
courses.description: Introductory course addresses the challenges of biomedical device design, prototyping and testing, material considerations, regulatory requirements, design control, human factors and ethics.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Manufacturing and Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing
courses.description: Introduction to manufacturing, surveying a broad range of manufacturing methods and focusing on a few select processes. The course covers some of the considerations and decisions that go into process selection, manufacturing systems, design for manufacture, and design for assembly, as well as how those decisions influence manufacturing quality and cost.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Renewable Energy Technologies
courses.prereq_text: Upper division standing; open to ME majors only.
courses.comments: May not be taken for additional credit by students who have completed ME 125BL. May not be taken by students who have completed ME 233.
courses.description: Focuses on emerging technologies to generate energy from renewable sources, harvest waste energy, and improve the efficiency of existing energy infrastructure. Three main categories of technologies will be discussed: solar energy, thermoelectrics, and solid-state cooling. Thermodynamic principles underlying these renewable energy technologies will be analyzed in detail. Engineering challenges and economic analysis will be provided when relevant.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Projects in Thermal Sciences
courses.description: The focus of the class is on Heat Transfer, Energetics, and Fluid Mechanics. The primary activity will be individual projects on topics selected by each student in associated areas such as Alternative Energy technologies, Manufacturing, HVAC, Engines, Electronic devices, etc. Topics may be related to Senior Capstone projects, professional work, Research, Engineering competitions or clubs, internships, etc. Intended for Juniors, Seniors, and Graduate students in Engineering and the Physics department, with enrollment subject to Instructor approval.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Wind and Tidal Energy
courses.comments: May not be taken for additional credit by students who have completed ME 125PL. May not be taken by students who have completed ME 225PL or ME 235.
courses.description: Actuator disc theory; Blade element momentum theory; Design of optimal rotors; Wind turbine wakes; The atmosphere, and effects of atmospheric stability; Models of large wind farms; Open channel-flows; Energy available in tidal flows.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Numerical Analysis in Engineering
courses.prereq_text: ME 17 with a minimum grade of C-, or Chemical Engineering 132A.
courses.description: Numerical analysis and analytical solutions of problems described by linear and nonlinear differential equations with an emphasis on MATLAB. First and second order differential equations; systems of differential equations; linear algebraic equations, matrices and eigenvalues; boundary value problems; finite differences.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Introduction to Nanoelectromechanical and Microelectromechanical systems (NEMS/MEMS)
courses.prereq_text: ME 16 or ME W 16 and 17; ME 152A and ME 151A (may be concurrent); or ECE 130A & 137A with a minimum grade of C- in both.
courses.description: Introduction to nano- and microtechnology. Scaling laws and nanoscale physics are stressed. Individual subjects at the nanoscale including materials, mechanics, photonics, electronics, and fluidics will be described, with an emphasis on differences of behavior at the nanoscale and real-world examples.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: MEMS: Processing and Device Characterization
courses.comments: ME 141B and ECE 141B are the same course.
courses.description: Lectures and laboratory on semiconductor-based processing for MEMS. Description of key equipment and characterization tools used for MEMS and design, fabrication, characterization and testing of MEMS. Emphasis on current MEMS devices including accelerometers, comb drives, micro-reactors and capacitor-actuators.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Molecular and Cellular Biomechanics
courses.description: Course introduces fundamental concepts in molecular and cellular biomechanics. Will consider the role of physical, thermal and chemical forces, examine their influence on cell strength and elasticity, and explore the properties of enzymatically-active materials.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Thermosciences 1
courses.prereq_text: Physics 7D or Physics 2, and ME 14 with a minimum grade of C-, and Math 6B or Math 5C
courses.description: Basic concepts in thermodynamics, system analysis, energy, thermodynamic laws, and cycles.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Thermosciences 2
courses.description: Introduction to heat transfer processes, steady and unsteady state conduction, multidimensional analysis. Introduction to convective heat transfer.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Thermosciences 3
courses.prereq_text: ME 151B and 152A. Open to ME majors only.
courses.description: Convective heat transfer, external and internal flow, forced and free convection, phase change, heat exchangers. Introduction to radiative heat transfer.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Fluid Mechanics
courses.prereq_text: Math 6B or Math 5C, and ME 16 or ME W 16 with a minimum grade of C-, and Physics 7B or Physics 2
courses.description: Introduction to the fundamental concepts in fluid mechanics and basic fluid properties. Basic equations of fluid flow. Dimensional analysis and similitude. Hydrodynamics.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Fluid Mechanics
courses.prereq_text: ME 152A. Open to ME majors only.
courses.description: Incompressible viscous flow. Turbomachinery. Boundary-layer theory. Introductory considerations for one-dimensional compressible flow.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Introduction to Mechanical Engineering Design
courses.prereq_text: ME 10 and 16 or ME W 16; open to ME majors only.
courses.comments: Course materials fee required.
courses.description: This course introduces engineering design with a focus on an iterative design process. Throughout the course, a group project cements the topics learned through active application to a real design problem. The lectures are broken into three sections. Section 1 introduces a version of this iterative Design Cycle, which comprises four components: 1) Define, 2) Ideate, 3) Prototype & Test, and 4) Analyze. These steps are repeated many times over the course of design development, not always in this order. Section 2 of the course focuses on applying this Design Cycle to the team project. Section 3 wraps up and focuses on presenting the project.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Design and Analysis of Structures
courses.prereq_text: ME 15 with a minimum grade of C-; and, ME 16 or ME W 16 with a minimum grade of C-; open to ME majors only.
courses.description: Introductory course in structural analysis and design. The theories of matrix structural analysis and finite element analysis for the solution of analytical and design problems in structures are emphasized. Lecture material includes structural theory compatibility method, slope deflection method, displacement method, and virtual work. Topics include applications to bars, beams, trusses, frames, and solids.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Control System Design
courses.prereq_text: ME 17 with a minimum grade of C-; ME 103.
courses.description: The discipline of control and its application. Dynamics and feedback. The mathematical models: transfer functions and state space descriptions. Simple control design (PID). Assessment of a control problem, specification, fundamental limitations, codesign of system and control.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Advanced Control Systems Design
courses.description: Dynamic system modeling using state-space methods, controllability and observability, state-space methods for control design including pole placement, and linear quadratic regulator methods. Observers and observer-based feedback controllers. Sampled-data and digital control. Laboratory exercises using MATLAB for simulation and control design.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Control Systems Laboratory
courses.description: Advanced lab course with experiments in dynamical systems and feedback control design. Students design, troubleshoot, and perform detailed, multi-session experiments.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Mechanical Engineering Design - I
courses.prereq_text: ME 14, with a minimum grade of C-; and ME 15, with a minimum grade of C-; and MATRL 101 (or MATRL 100B); or consent of instructor. Open to ME majors only
courses.description: The rational selection of engineering materials, and the utilization of Ashby-charts, stress, strain, strength, and fatigue failure consideration as applied to the design of machine elements. Lectures also support the development of system design concepts using assigned projects and involve the preparation of engineering reports and drawings.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Mechanical Engineering Design-II
courses.prereq_text: ME 156A. Open to ME majors only.
courses.description: Machine elements including gears, bearings and shafts. Joint design and analysis: bolts, rivets, adhesive bonding and welding. Machine dynamics andfatigue. Design reliability and safety. Codes and standards. Topics coveredwill be applies in practical design projects.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Introduction to Multiphysics Simulation
courses.comments: May not be taken for additional credit by students who have completed ME 125CM. May not be taken by students who have completed ME 225CM or ME 257.
courses.description: Introduces students to the concepts of multiphysics simulation. Students are introduced to PDEs, associated analytical solutions, and the finite elements method. Multiphysics problems are solved in multiple domains, and with fluid/structure interactions. Each student conducts a project where multiphysics tools are used to explore details of multiphysical processes.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Computer Aided Design and Manufacturing
courses.prereq_text: ME 10 and ME 12S; open to ME majors only.
courses.description: Emphasis on programming, operation and design of automated manufacturing tools. Students learn to program CNC tools to make parts with G&M Code and Mastercam CAM software. Students make parts in hands-on labs using CNC tools, 3D printers and laser cutters. Select topics in automated tool design and construction.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Introduction to Design Optimization
courses.comments: May not be taken for additional credit by students who have completed ME 125LP.
courses.description: Building a theoretical understanding of various optimization schemes and methods. Numerical simulation of physical design problems with a goal to optimize the design of a system and an emphasis on using COMSOL Multiphysics software package. Gradient-based and gradient-free minimization/maximization of objective functions; parameter optimization, shape optimization; topology optimization; inverse problem-solving.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Engineering Mechanics: Vibrations
courses.prereq_text: ME 16 or ME W 16 with a minimum grade of C-; ME 103; open to ME majors only.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed ME 163B.
courses.description: Topics relating to vibration in mechanical systems; exact and approximate methods of analysis, matrix methods, generalized coordinates and Lagrange's equations, applications of systems. Basic feedback systems and controlled dynamic behavior.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Advanced Strength of Materials
courses.description: Covers the mechanical behavior of engineering materials, with an emphasis on understanding the physical and microstructural origins of material response. Topics include the tensile test, elasticity, crystal structure and defects, phase diagrams, yield and plasticity, fracture mechanics, stress corrosion cracking, fatigue, cyclic crack growth, Weibull statistics, and creep. Theoretical frameworks are connected throughout to real engineering applications and design.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Structural Analysis
courses.comments: May not be taken for additional credit by students who have completed ME W 167.
courses.description: Presents introductory matrix methods for analysis of structures. Topics include review of matrix algebra and linear equations, basic structural theorems including the principle of superposition and energy theorems, truss bar, bean and plane frame elements, and programming techniques to realize these concepts.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Nonlinear Phenomena
courses.prereq_text: Physics 105A or Physics 103; or ME 163 or upper-division standing in ECE.
courses.comments: Same course as ME 169 and Physics 106. Not open for credit to students who have completed ECE 163C.
courses.description: Introduction to nonlinear phenomena. Flows and bifurcations in one and two dimensions, chaos, fractals, strange attractors. Applications to physics, engineering, chemistry, and biology.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Introduction to Robotics: Dynamics and Control
courses.comments: ME 179D and ECE 179D are the same course.
courses.description: Dynamic modeling and control methods for robotic systems. Lagrangian method for deriving equations of motion, introduction to the Jacobian, and modeling and control of forces and contact dynamics at a robotic end effector. Laboratories encourage a problem-solving approach to control.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Introduction to Robotics: Design Laboratory
courses.prereq_text: Engr 3; and ME 6 or ECE 2A. Not open for credit to students who have completed ME 170C or ECE 181C.
courses.comments: Course materials fee required.
courses.description: Design, programming, and testing of mobile robots. Design problems are formulated in terms of robot performance. Students solve electromechanical problems, developing skills in brainstorming, concept selection, spatial reasoning, teamwork and communication. Robots are controlled with micro-controllers using C programming and interfaced to sensors and motors.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Introduction to Robotics: Planning and Kinematics
courses.comments: CMPSC 179P, ECE 179P, and ME 179P are the same course.
courses.description: Motion planning and kinematics topics with an emphasis on geometric reasoning, programming, and matrix computations. Motion planning: configuration spaces, sensor-based planning, decomposition and sampling methods, and advanced planning algorithms. Kinematics: reference frames, rotations and displacements, kinematic motion models.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Crystalline Defects
courses.comments: May not be taken for additional credit by students who have completed ME 125IB. May not be taken by students who have completed ME 225IB or ME 280.
courses.description: An in-depth look into the many classes of defects (e.g., point, linear, and planar) and the role they play in crystalline materials. While we cannot eliminate defects and they are usually seen as a weakness, proper understanding of defects is the best way to design stronger and better materials. Examples of the types of defects we may cover are vacancies, dislocations, grain boundaries, interfaces, and twins. We will study their formation, mobility and interaction in environments where they are commonly found, such as elevated temperatures, mechanical strains, or irradiation.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Materials in Engineering
courses.comments: Same course as Materials 185.
courses.description: Introduces the main families of materials and the principles behind their development, selection, and behavior. Discusses the generic properties of metals, ceramics, polymers, and composites more relevant to structural applications. The relationship of properties to structure and processing is emphasized in every case.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Manufacturing and Materials
courses.prereq_text: ME 151C; and ME 15; and Materials 101 or Materials 100C
courses.comments: Same course as Materials 186A.
courses.description: Introduction to the fundamentals of common manufacturing processes and their interplay with the structure and properties of materials as they are transformed into products. Emphasis on process understanding and the key physical and basic mathematical relationships involved in each of the processes discussed.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Introduction to Additive Manufacturing
courses.comments: ME 186B and Materials 186B are the same course.
courses.description: Introduction to additive manufacturing processes: review ofmanufacturing methods and process selection consideration, economies of production, common additive manufacturing strategies, and brief description of the physics of photopolymerization, extrusion, selective laser melting and e-beam melting fabrication.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Capstone Mechanical Engineering Design Project
courses.prereq_text: ME 103; and ME 151B; and ME 152A; and ME 153; or consent of instructor. Open to ME majors only.
courses.comments: A 3-quarter sequence with grades issued for each quarter. Students may not concurrently enroll in ME 197 and ME 189A-B-C with the same design project.Course materials fee required.
courses.description: Students work in teams under the direction of a faculty advisor (and possibly an industrial sponsor) to tackle an engineering design project. Engineering communication, such as reports and oral presentations, are covered. Emphasis on practical, hands-on experience, and the integration of analytical and design skills.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Capstone Mechanical Engineering Design Project
courses.comments: A 3-quarter sequence with grades issued for each quarter. Students may not concurrently enroll in ME 197 and ME 189A-B-C with the same design project.Course materials fee required.
courses.description: Students work in teams under the direction of a faculty advisor (and possibly an industrial sponsor) to tackle an engineering design project. Engineering communication, such as reports and oral presentations, are covered. Course emphasizes practical, hands-on experience, and integrates analytical and design skills acquired in the companion ME 156 courses.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Capstone Mechanical Engineering Design Project
courses.comments: A 3-quarter sequence with grades issued for each quarter. Students may not concurrently enroll in ME 197 and ME 189A-B-C with the same design project.Course materials fee required.
courses.description: Students work in teams under the direction of a faculty advisor (and possibly an industrial sponsor) to tackle an engineering design project. Engineering communication, such as reports and oral presentations, are covered. Course emphasizes practical, hands-on experience, and integrates analytical and design skills acquired in the companion ME 156 courses.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Internship in Industry
courses.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Prior departmental approval needed.
courses.comments: Cannot be used as a departmental elective. May be repeated to a maximum of 2 units.
courses.description: Students obtain credit for a mechanical engineering related internship and/or industrial experience under faculty supervision. A 6-10 page written report is required for credit. It may NOT be used to satisfy the engineering elective requirement for ME majors.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Independent Projects in Mechanical Engineering Design
courses.comments: May be repeated for a maximum of 12 units. No more than 4 units may be used as departmental electives.
courses.description: Special projects in design engineering. Course offers motivated students opportunity to synthesize academic skills by designing and building new machines.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Independent Studies in Mechanical Engineering
courses.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper-division standing; completion of two upper-division courses in Mechanical Engineering.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 grade-point average for the preceding 3 quarters and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199DC/199RA courses combined. May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units but no more than four units may be used as departmental electives.
courses.description: Directed individual study.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Professional Seminar
courses.description: A series of weekly lectures given by university staff and outside experts in all fields of mechanical engineering.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: M.S. Project
courses.description: A ten-week individual research project on an advanced topic in mechanical engineering.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Advanced Dynamics
courses.description: Newtons laws and symmetries, Newton, Laplace and principle of determinism, qualitative analysis of Newtons equations of motion, Hamiltonian mechanics, one degree of freedom (DOF) systems, two DOF systems, motion in central fields, application to molecular dynamics, control of classical dynamical systems, Lagrangian mechanics, chaos and ergodic theory, rigid body motion.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Operator Theory Methods in Dynamical Systems
courses.description: Geometric mechanics, volume-preserving dynamical systems, molecular dynamics; Infinite dimensional dynamics and finite dimensional approximations including incompressible Euler equations and point vortex theory, transport and fluid mixing, control of measure-preserving systems, equilibrium and non-equilibrium statistical mechanics methods for vortex gases.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Faculty Research Seminar
courses.description: A series of weekly presentations given by ladder faculty members to familiarize graduate students with current department research projects.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Matrix Analysis and Computation
courses.comments: Students should be proficient in basic numerical methods, linear algebra, mathematically rigorous proofs, and some programming language. Same course as Computer Science 211A, ECE 210A, Mathematics 206A, Chemical Engineering 211A, and Geology 251A.
courses.description: Graduate level-matrix theory with introduction to matrix computations. SVD's, pseudoinverses, variational characterization of eigenvalues, perturbation theory, direct and iterative methods for matrix computations.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Numerical Simulation
courses.comments: Students should be proficient in basic numerical methods, linear algebra, mathematically rigorous proofs, and some programming language. Same course as Computer Science 211B, ECE 210B, Mathematics 206B, and Chemical Engineering 211B and Geology 251B.
courses.description: Linear multistep methods and Runge-Kutta methods for ordinary differential equations: stability, order and convergence. Stiffness. Differential algebraic equations. numerical solution of boundary value problems.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Numerical Solution of Partial Differential Equations--Finite Difference Methods.
courses.comments: Students should be proficient in basic numerical methods, linear algebra, mathematically rigorous proofs, and some programming language. Same course as Computer Science 211C, ECE 210C, Mathematics 206C, Chemical Engineering 211C, and Geolgy 251C.
courses.description: Finite difference methods for hyperbolic, parabolic and elliptic PDE's, with application to problems in science and engineering. Convergence, consistency, order and stability of finite difference methods. Dissipation and dispersion. Finite volume methods. Software design and adaptivity.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Numerical Solution of Partial Differential Equations - Finite Element Methods
courses.comments: Students should be proficient in basic numerical methods, linear algebra, mathematically rigorous proofs, and some programming language. Same course as Computer Science 211D, ECE 210D, Mathematics 206D, Chemical Engineering 211D, and Geology 251D.
courses.description: Weighted residual and finite element methods for the solution of hyperbolic, parabolic and elliptical partial differential equations, with application to problems in science and engineering. Error estimates. Standard and discontinuous Galerkin methods.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Pattern Formation and Self-Organization
courses.description: Introductory course to the processes of pattern formation and self-organization in natural systems (physical and biological systems), as well as in engineering. The goal of the course is to explain how ordered spatial structures appear in different systems. We will discuss the common aspects and the differences in the mechanisms that establish the patterns, and introduce various techniques used in different disciplines to study the formation of spatially extended structures.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Applied Dynamical Systems I
courses.description: Phase-plane methods, non-linear oscillators, stability of fixed points and periodic orbits, invariant manifolds, structural stability, normal form theory, local bifurcations for vector fields and maps, applications from engineering, physics, chemistry, and biology.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Level Set Methods
courses.prereq_text: CMPSC 211C or CH E 211C or ECE 210C or ME 210C.
courses.comments: Same course as CH E 226, ECE 226, and CMPSC 216.
courses.description: Mathematical description of the level set method and design of the numerical methods used in its implementations (ENO-WENO, Godunov, Lax-Friedrich, etc.). Introduction to the Ghost Fluid Method. Applications in CFD, Materials Sciences, Computer Vision and Computer Graphics.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Mechanics of Materials
courses.comments: Same course as Materials 207.
courses.description: Matrices and tensors, stress and deformation, compatibility and equilibrium conditions, constitutive equations, and boundary conditions, applications in elasticity, plasticity and fracture.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Fundamentals of Fluid Mechanics
courses.description: Fundamentals of advection and diffusion of mass, momentum, and energy. Index notation. Solution of steady-state and transient 1D and 2D problems: separation of variables, eigenfunction expansions, similarity solutions, and superposition. Lubrication theory. Forced and natural convection.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Fundamentals of Fluid Mechanics
courses.description: Introductory course in fluid mechanics. Basic equations of motion (continuity, momentum, energy, vorticity), coordinate transformations, "potential" flow, this airfoil theory, conformal mapping, vortex dynamics, boundary layers, stability theory, laminar/turbulent transition, turbulence.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Advanced Viscous Flow
courses.description: Review the Navier-Stokes equations in velocity, pressure, and vorticity variables. Analyze details of important low and moderate reynolds number flow applications and then high reynolds number flows with boundary layer phenomena. Compare exact, approximate, numerical, and experimental solutionmethods.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Soft Robotics
courses.comments: May not be taken for additional credit by students who have completed ME 225EH or MAT 594ST. May not be taken by students who have completed ME 125EH or ME 123.
courses.description: Learning from the versatility and robustness of bodies in nature, robotic devices are moving away from the traditional rigid form to designs that intentionally and carefully incorporate compliance. We explore this emerging paradigm of robots by 1) modeling the underlying mechanics of soft systems, such as soft actuators, sensors, and bodies, 2) examining current literature and gleaning design principles, and 3) designing and fabricating soft robotic devices in a hands-on laboratory setting. This course includes a final project; students are expected to design, model, fabricate, and test either a subcomponent or a full soft robot.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Special Topics in Mechanical Engineering
courses.description: Specialized courses dealing with advanced topics and recent developments in one or more of the following areas: dynamic systems, control and robotics, fluid mechanics, materials science and engineering, ocean engineering, solid mechanics and structures, thermal sciences.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: SP: Nanoscale Energy Transport & Conversion
courses.description: A self-contained, application-oriented course covering basic concepts in nanoscale transport and interaction of microscopic energy carriers, mainly electrons, phonons and photons, with an emphasis on new phenomena that emerge at small length and time scales and deviate from macroscopic laws. Topics include (may vary based on time frame): energy levels and statistics of energy carriers; kinetic theory and mean free path; energy transport by waves and the Landauer formalism; near-field radiation; energy transport by particles: Boltzmann transport equation and classical size effect; carrier scattering; energy dissipation. Recent research results and real-world applications are discussed wherever relevant.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Biofluid Mechanics
courses.description: Applies the principles of fluid mechanics and transport phenomena to major biological systems, in particular the human body. The course focuses on physiologically relevant flow and transport phenomena from an engineering perspective. Topics covered include blood flow in the cardiovascular system, air flow in the respiratory system, transport processes in joints, and how abnormal fluid mechanics relates to disease. Addresses the rheology of complex fluids, flow through elastic tubes, and transport in porous media. Simple numerical models will be used in the course.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Learning in Model Predictive Control
courses.description: Explores the use of data to design safe and effective controllers, through the lens of model predictive control. Introduction to standard optimal control and model predictive control formulations, with emphasis on implementation rather than theory. Introduction to “learning model predictive control”, which then serves as a foundation for evaluating performance and safety of other common data-driven control methods (e.g. Reinforcement Learning and Imitation Learning). The course is implementation-focused through a combination of lectures and simulation-based control design activities. Experience with controls is required; experience with optimization is helpful. Prereqs: 155A or equivalent.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Special Topics in ME: Bio-Inspired Design in Fluid Mechanics
courses.description: Students will study evolutionary adaptation as a source for inspiration, extracting design principles to leverage the functionality, adaptability, and robustness of biological systems. The course focuses on Biologically Inspired Design in Fluids to advance student knowledge of natural strategies and facilitate quantitative analysis of the proposed solutions. Over the quarter, the students will learn how biological systems deal with fluids and the bio-inspired design process. The course includes lectures, case studies, and design activities. The final projects aim to share bio-inspired design through STEM programs for K-6 students.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Special Topics in Soft Robotics
courses.description: Learning from the versatility and robustness of bodies in nature, robotic devices are moving away from traditional rigid form to designs that intentionally and carefully incorporate compliance. We explore this emerging paradigm of robots by 1) understanding and analytically modeling subcomponents, such as soft actuators, sensors, and bodies, 2) examining current literature and gleaning design principles, and 3) designing and fabricating in a hands-on setting. Course includes a final group project; students are expected to design, model, fabricate, and test either a subcomponent or a full soft robot. Students prepare a short academic paper based on the results of their project, potentially suitable for submission to a robotics conference.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Special Topics in Biological Computing
courses.description: Introduces the basics of design of synthetic biological systems, including the architecture of genetic networks, circuits, and pathways controlling engineered biological function, as well as single-cell microbial behavior, and microbe population dynamics. Also provides a gentle introduction to workflows in biomolecular engineering, genetic circuit design, genomicediting, as well as principles of experimental design. An overview of various engineered and natural biological functions is provided, including multi-stability, biological oscillations, stochasticeffects in genetic circuits, robustness of circuit performance, and cellular capacity.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Special Topics: Hydrodynamic Instability and Turbulence
courses.description: Hydrodynamic instabilities and turbulent flows are ubiquitous in fluid mechanics, from natural phenomena to industrial and technological applications. The goal of the course is to provide an introduction to the transition to unstable and turbulent flows. We will discuss some classical hydrodynamic instabilities and the analytical tools available to predict their existence and the patterns generated. The second part of the class will focus on turbulence and the methods of statistical analysis available to provide a description of such flows.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Special Topics: Failure Analysis
courses.description: Failures leading to investigation, examination, innovation, and redesign into improved, safer, and more efficient components and structures. In this course, we will study engineering failures that have occurred across a wide range of disciplines, and examine why they happened. This includes a discussion of the fundamental engineering concepts at play (e.g. stress corrosion cracking, creep, high cycle fatigue), as well as the path by which these factors caused the disaster under study, and the ethics involved in each case.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Contraction Theory for Dynamical Systems
courses.description: The course provides a mathematical introduction to contraction theory for dynamical systems. Contractivity is a robust and computationally-friendly stability theory. Special emphasis is given to continuous-time differential equations arising in the study of network multi-agent systems, neural networks, gradient dynamical systems, monotone dynamics, and semi-contracting systems. The course is intended primarily for graduate students interested in nonlinear dynamical systems, control, computation and optimization.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Fluid Mechanics and Soft Matter in Additive Manufacturing
courses.description: The evolution of product design, prototyping, and industrial production is being reshaped by additive manufacturing methods. These innovative techniques play a pivotal role in minimizing material usage for manufacturing, paving the way for significant advancements. The customization potential has particularly revolutionized healthcare, while the expedited prototyping process has shortened product time-to-market and facilitates on-site repairs of essential components. This course will cover fundamental aspects of fluid mechanics and soft matter applied to some methods of additive manufacturing, such as extrusion-based processes.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Special Topics in Mechanical Engineering: Geophysical Fluid Dynamics
courses.description: Drawing from classical journal articles from the scientific literature, this graduate course will review selected mathematical models used to predict the dynamics of such geophysical flows, introduce available analytical solutions that provide useful insight in simplified cases, and numerical approaches to solve the corresponding partial differential equations and get useful insight for realistic scenarios. To best enjoy this course, a good background and enthusiasm for fluid mechanics, applied mathematics, and scientific computing is required.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Haptics: Touch Perception, Interaction, and Engineering
courses.description: Haptics lies at the intersection of robotics, human-computer interaction, and computational and human perception. The term haptics is often used to refer to science and engineering related to the sense of touch. This course introduces human haptics, including sensory specializations and touch perception. It reviews the engineering of electronic technologies for haptic (touch) feedback, emerging technologies, and the design of haptic systems for human-computer interaction, sensory substitution, virtual reality, augmented reality, and other emerging areas. The class involves a mix of readings, hands-on activities, lecture/discussion, and projects.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Advanced Heat Transfer
courses.description: Advanced treatment of fundamental aspects of heat transfer. Covers topics such as conservation laws, steady-state and unsteady-state heat conduction, convection fundamentals, mass transfer including diffusion and phase change, and basic thermal radiation. Problems and examples include theory and applications drawn from a spectrum of engineering design and manufacturing problems.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Special Topics: Li Ion Batteries
courses.description: An introduction to lithium-ion batteries (LIB). The course consists of a significant laboratory component where students acquire hands-on experience in handling, analyzing, and studying state-of-the-art (SOA) LIBs. Students also learn how to design, manufacture, and test prototype batteries made using prototype manufacturing equipment. Course Prerequisites: General materials science course background and students must have valid UCSB general laboratory safety certification.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Special Topics: MEMS Characterization
courses.description: Focuses on developing the foundational understanding of experimental approaches and analysis techniques commonly used to characterize MEMS devices. Covered topics will include basic optics principles, optical microscopy (including stereoscopy, fluorescence imaging, confocal systems, and super-resolution techniques), force spectroscopy methods (optical tweezers, magnetic tweezers), electron microscopy, vibrational analysis and scanning probe techniques (AFM), with examples drawn from the use of MEMS devices for biosensor development, metrology, and other engineering applications, including device quality control.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Special Topics in ME: Research Topics in Machine Learning and System Identification
courses.description: Introduces students to research topics at the interface of system identification, data science, and machine learning. Reviews linear algebra, probability and information theory, and general concepts from learning algorithms. Introduction to the notion of estimators, maximum-likelihood estimation, stochastic gradient descent, and algorithm design. Provides an overview of deep feedforward networks, regularization strategies for deep learning, and optimization strategies for learning architectures. Introduces topics in system identification and reviews past and present approaches for using neural networks to perform system identification.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Engineering Approaches to Solve Wicked Problems and Global Challenges
courses.description: Explore how engineers tackle solving 'wicked problems': problems that are ill-structured, with multiple interdependent variables and no clear optimal solutions. Such problems are highly multidisciplinary, often requiring input and innovation across technological, scientific and societal domains. Wicked problems seem to defy standard and structured solutions, and challenge engineers to develop new ways of thinking and communicating. Through case studies, discussions, and projects we will learn from past successes and failures and determine best practices, while exploring how engineers can prepare to lead solutions to the world's most pressing problems.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Modeling and Optimization of Neural Networks
courses.description: Intended primarily for graduate students interested in (1) the use of neural networks for control, optimization, and machine learning and (2) the use of systems theory to model the dynamics and functionality of neural circuits. Contains an overview of recent research literature and involves a final project to be selected among a number of recent developments in this area.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Soft Mechanics: Design and Applications
courses.description: We will discuss some applications of soft mechanics to study various complex systems. There will be weekly presentations by students and readings of several classic book chapters and papers from the literature of applied mathematics, soft matter physics, and engineering. Examples of topics include elasticity, fluid mechanics, biophysics, and biomechanics, along with their applications to societal challenges such as epidemiology and health. Each student will work on a project throughout the quarter and is expected to write a research-like manuscript on the investigated topic. The final manuscript could be a review and not (necessarily) original new work.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Special Topics in Mechanical Engineering
courses.description: Specialized courses dealing with advanced topics and recent developments inone or more of the following areas: dynamic systems, control and robotics, fluid mechanics, materials science and engineering, ocean engineering, solid mechanics and structures, thermal sciences.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Special Topics in Mechanical Engineering: Radiative Energy Transfer
courses.description: This course investigates the role of thermal radiation in the exchange of energy between engineered surfaces, and the problem of managing overall heat transfer. Topics include the fundamentals of thermal radiation, covering Plank's spectral distribution, Stefan-Boltzmann law, Wien's displacement law, Kirchhoff's law, spectral and total properties of radiative surfaces, including black, diffuse, gray, specular, and nongray surfaces. Analytical methods for analysis of radiative exchange between surfaces are developed using both Radiosity formulations and Network Analogies. Finally, radiative exchange between surfaces is coupled to multimode heat transfer problems, including those having contributions from conduction and convection.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Chemo-Mechanics: The Intersection of Solid Mechanics and Chemistry
courses.description: Covers basic thermodynamics, the role of chemistry and mechanics in thermodynamics, and the issue of kinetics when the system is not in thermodynamic equilibrium. Emphasis will be placed on the thermodynamics of deformable solids, with mechanical stress, chemical reactions, other chemical phenomena, and species transport included in the formulation. As indicated above, examples will be selected from oxidation and corrosion, electrochemical energy conversion and storage, the behavior of gels and elastomers, biological cell mechanics, and other topics.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Scale Analysis of Multiphysics Phenomena
courses.description: For graduate students who already completed introductory courses. Covers techniques of scale analysis for simplifying governing equations, and for deriving tractable models of practical utility. Examples range from single-phase flows, progressing through fluid-structure interaction, multiphase flow, effects of surfactants, phase change, and simple chemical reactions.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Advanced Engineering Thermodynamics
courses.description: This course is an extension to ME151A and will discuss advanced concepts in engineering thermodynamics, with practical applications in energy generation, transport, conversion, and storage processes. Topics include: free energies, Maxwell relations, refrigeration cycles and technologies, thermodynamics of solar energy, introduction to statistical thermodynamics, and other topics related to renewable energy research. Prerequisite: ME151A or equivalent courses on thermodynamics.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Special Topics in Mechanical Engineering: Intro to Interfacial Phenomena
courses.description: Introduces fundamental and applied aspects of interfacial systems. The course covers theory of capillarity, interfacial tensions, Laplace pressure, curvature effects on the equilibrium states of fluids, surfactants, fundamentals of wetting and contact angle, adhesion, cohesion, and spreading, superhydrophilicity and superhydrophobicity. Relevant research fields are also introduced, including oil-water separation, electronics cooling, condensation, and bio-inspired functional surfaces.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Bio-Inspired Design in Fluid Mechanics
courses.comments: May not be taken for additional credit by students who have completed ME 225ED. May not be taken by students who have completed ME 126 or ME 125ED.
courses.description: Students will study evolutionary adaptation as a source for inspiration, extracting design principles to leverage the functionality, adaptability, and robustness of biological systems. The course focuses on Biologically Inspired Design in Fluids to advance student knowledge of natural strategies and facilitate quantitative analysis of the proposed solutions. Over the quarter, the students will learn how biological systems deal with fluids and the bio-inspired design process. The course includes lectures, case studies, and design activities. The final projects aim to share bio-inspired design through STEM programs for K-6 students.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Elasticity and Plasticity
courses.comments: Same course as Materials 230.
courses.description: Review field equations of elasticity and plasticity. Energy principles and uniqueness theorems. Elementary problems in one and two dimensions, stress functions, and complex variable methods. Plastic stress-strain laws; flow potentials. Torsion and bending of plastic flow, slip line theory. Bounding theorems.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Plasticity
courses.comments: Same course as Materials 232.
courses.description: Plastic, creep, and relaxation behavior of solids. Mechanics of inelastically strained bodies; plastic stress-strain laws; flow potentials.Torsion and bending of prismatic bars, expansion of thick shells, plane plastic flow, slip line theory. Variational formulations, approximate methods.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Renewable Energy Technologies
courses.comments: Concurrently offered with ME 133. May not be taken for additional credit by students who have completed ME 125BL or ME 133.
courses.description: Focuses on emerging technologies to generate energy from renewable sources, harvest waste energy, and improve the efficiency of existing energy infrastructure. Three main categories of technologies will be discussed: solar energy, thermoelectrics, and solid-state cooling. Thermodynamic principles underlying these renewable energy technologies will be analyzed in detail. Engineering challenges and economic analysis will be provided when relevant.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Wind and Tidal Energy
courses.comments: May not be taken for additional credit by students who have completed ME 225PL. May not be taken by students who have completed ME 125PL or ME 135.
courses.description: Actuator disc theory; Blade element momentum theory; Design of optimal rotors; Wind turbine wakes; The atmosphere, and effects of atmospheric stability; Models of large wind farms; Open channel-flows; Energy available in tidal flows.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Nonlinear Control Systems
courses.comments: ME 236 and ECE 236 are the same course.
courses.description: Analysis and design of nonlinear control systems. Focus on Lyapunov stability theory, with sufficient time devoted to contrasts between linear and nonlinear systems, input-output stability and the describing function method.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Advanced Control Design Laboratory
courses.prereq_text: ME 243A/ECE 230A and at least one class among the following: ME 243B/ECE 230B, ME 236/ECE 236, ME 256/ECE 232, or ME 254/ECE 271C.
courses.description: A laboratory course requiring students to design and implement advanced control systems on a physical experiment. Experiments from any engineering or scientific discipline are chosen by the student.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Engineering Biomaterials
courses.comments: ME 241 and BIOE 241 are the same course.
courses.description: This lecture-based course provides an overview of material structure-property relationships, processing, and characterization techniques for metals, polymers, and ceramics. We discuss the unique design constraints imposed by the human body and discuss strategies to enhance biocompatibility. Throughout the course, emphasis is placed on applications of biomaterials engineering in medical devices.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Linear Systems I
courses.prereq_text: ME 210A, ECE 210A, CH E 211A, CMPSC 211A, or MATH 206A; may be taken concurrently
courses.comments: ME243A and ECE 230A are the same course.
courses.description: Internal and external descriptions. Solution of state equations. Controllability and observability realizations. Pole assignment, assignment, observers; modern compensator design. Disturbance localization and decoupling. Least-squares control. Least-squares estimation; Kalman filters; smoothing. The separation theorem; LQG compensator design. Computational considerations. Selected additional topics.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Linear Systems II
courses.prereq_text: ECE 230A or ME 243A; and ME 210A, ECE 210A, CH E 211A, CMPSC 211A, or MATH 206A
courses.comments: ECE 230B and ME 243B are the same course.
courses.description: Internal and external descriptions. Solution of state equations. Controllability and observability realizations. Pole assignment, assignment, observers; modern compensator design. Distribance localization and decoupling. Least-squares control. Least-squares estimation; Kalman filters; smoothing. The seperation theorem; LQG compensator design. Computational considerations. Selected additional topics.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Advanced Theoretical Methods in Engineering
courses.comments: Same course as Chemical Engineering 230A.
courses.description: Methods of solution of partial differential equations and boundary value problems. Linear vector and function spaces, generalized fourier analysis, Sturm-Liouville theory, calculus of variations, and conformal mapping techniques.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Molecular and Cellular Biomechanics
courses.description: Course introduces fundamental concepts in molecular and cellular biomechanics. Will consider the role of physical, thermal and chemical forces, examine their influence on cell strength and elasticity, and explore the properties of enzymatically-active materials.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Computational Fluid Dynamics
courses.prereq_text: ME 210C or Computer Science 211C or ECE 210C or Mathematics 206C or ChemicaEngineering 211C.
courses.description: Numerical simulation of fluid flows. Basic discretization techniques for parabolic, elliptic, and hyperbolic conservation laws. Stability and accuracy. Diffusion equation, linear convection equation.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Computational Fluid Dynamics
courses.prereq_text: ME 210C or Computer Science 211C or ECE 210C or Mathematics 206C or ChemicaEngineering 211C.
courses.description: Discussion of appropriate boundary conditions. Nonlinear convection dominated problems, curvilinear coordinates, basics of grid generation. Inviscid flow, boundary layer flow, incompressible Navier-Stokes flows.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Dynamic Programming and Reinforcement Learning
courses.comments: ECE 271C and ME 254 are cross-listed and are the same course.
courses.description: This graduate course provides a comprehensive treatment of dynamic programming (DP) as the fundamental framework for staged optimization problems under uncertainty. Core topics include the principle of optimality, Bellman equations, value and policy iteration, deterministic and stochastic dynamic programming, and Markov decision processes. Applications span linear-quadratic optimal control, inventory control, asset management, hypothesis testing, the Viterbi algorithm, among others. The course concludes with modern reinforcement learning topics including Q-learning, temporal difference learning, and value function approximation, demonstrating how classical DP principles form the theoretical foundation for contemporary AI algorithms.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Robust Control Theory
courses.prereq_text: ECE 230A or ME 243A; and, ECE 230B or ME 243B, or consent of instructor.
courses.comments: Same course as ECE 232
courses.description: Uncertainty modeling; stability of systems in the presence of norm-bounded perturbations; induced norm performance problems; H-infinity and linear quadratic control theory; Integral Quadratic Constraints (IQCs); structured singular value analysis; model reduction; computer aided design projects for control systems.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Introduction to Multiphysics Simulation
courses.description: Introduces students to the concepts of multiphysics simulation. Students are introduced to PDE's, associated analytical solutions, and the finite element method. Multiphysics problems are solved in multiple domains, and with fluid/structure interactions. Each student conducts a project where multiphysics tools are used to explore details of multiphysical processes.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Methods in Mechanobiology and Biofabrication
courses.prereq_text: The course assumes an engineering background but is structured to be accessible to graduate students in life sciences who have a strong physics and math background, and to engineering graduate students with basic biology knowledge.
courses.comments: BIOE 258, IQB 258, and ME 258 are the same course.
courses.description: Cell mechanobiology topics including cell structure, mechanical models, and chemo-mechanical signaling. Review methods for controlling and analyzing the biomechanics of cells using traction force microscopy, AFM, micropatterning, and cell stimulation. Weekly lecture with final project in the form of a research proposal.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Mechanical Behavior of Materials
courses.comments: Same course as Materials 220.
courses.description: Concepts of stress and strain. Deformation of metals, polymers, and ceramics. Elasticity, viscoelasticity, plastic flow, and creep. Linear elastic fracture mechanics. Mechanisms of ductile and brittle fracture.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Composite Materials
courses.comments: Same course as Materials 261.
courses.description: Stress and strain relations in composites. Residual stresses. The fracture resistance of organic and inorganic matrix composites. Statistical aspects of fiber failure. Composite laminates and delamination cracks. Cumulative damage concepts. Interface properties. Design criteria.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Thin Films and Multilayers
courses.prereq_text: Materials 207 (same course as ME 219); consent of instructor
courses.description: The development of stresses in thin films and its relaxation. Edge effects and discontinuities. Cracks in films and at interfaces. Delamination of residually stressed films. Buckling and buckle propagation of compressed films. Cyclic behavior and ratcheting effects.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Network Systems: Dynamics and Control
courses.description: Motivating socio/economic networks, power grids, multi-agent robotics. Perron-Frobenius matrix theory and algebraic graph theory. Fundamental dynamics in networks: averaging dynamics in discrete and continuous time; positive and compartmental systems; robotic coordination problems; coupled oscillator systems; virus propagation models; population dynamic models.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Finite Element Structural Analysis
courses.comments: Same course as Materials 240.
courses.description: Definitions and basic element operations displacement approach in linear elasticity. Element formulation: direct methods and variational methods. Global analysis procedures: assemblage and solution. Plane stress and plane strain. Solids of revolution and general solids. Isoparametric representation and numerical integration. Computer implementation.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Fracture Mechanics
courses.comments: Same course as Materials 234.
courses.description: Analytic solutions of a stationary crack under static loading. Elastic and elastoplastic analysis. The J integral. Energy balance and crack growth. Criteria for crack initiation and growth. Dynamic crack propagation. Fatigue. The micromechanics of fracture.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Crystalline Defects
courses.comments: May not be taken for additional credit by students who have completed ME 225IB. May not be taken by students who have completed ME 125IB or ME 180.
courses.description: An in-depth look into the many classes of defects (e.g., point, linear, and planar) and the role they play in crystalline materials. While we cannot eliminate defects and they are usually seen as a weakness, proper understanding of defects is the best way to design stronger and better materials. Examples of the types of defects we may cover are vacancies, dislocations, grain boundaries, interfaces, and twins. We will study their formation, mobility and interaction in environments where they are commonly found, such as elevated temperatures, mechanical strains, or irradiation.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Physics of Transducers
courses.description: The use of concepts in electromagnetic theory and solid state physics to describe capacitive, piezoresistive, piezoelectric and tunneling transduction mechanisms and analyze their applications in microsystems technology.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Design of Transducers
courses.description: Design issues associated with microscale transduction. Electrodynamics, linear and nonlinear mechanical behavior, sensing methods, MEMS-specific fabrication rules, and layout are all covered. Modeling techniques for electromechanical systems are also discussed.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Group Studies: Controls, Dynamical Systems, and Computation
courses.comments: Same course as ECE 295, Computer Science 592, and Chemical Engineering 295.
courses.description: A series of weekly lectures given by university staff and outside experts in the fields of control systems, dynamical systems, and computation.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Teaching Assistant Seminar
courses.comments: No unit credit allowed toward M.S. or Ph.D. degrees. S/U grading.
courses.description: Discussion-based seminar designed to introduce new teaching assistants to the role and build practical skills for effective teaching. Recommended for all graduate students in mechanical engineering during their first year as a teaching assistant.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Teaching Assistant Practicum
courses.comments: Normally required of students serving as teaching assistants. No unit credit allowed towards advanced degree.
courses.description: Practical experience in the various activities associated with teaching, including lecturing, supervision of laboratories and discussion sections, preparation and grading of homework and exams.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Graduate Student Research Practicum
courses.comments: Will not count as unit credit towards M.S. or Ph.D. degree in mechanical engineering.
courses.description: Practical experience in the various activities associated with research, including experimental work, theoretical work and analyses, and assisting department faculty and other professional researchers in their duties.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Directed Research
courses.comments: Not applicable to course requirement for M.S. or Ph.D. degree. S/U grading.
courses.description: Research, either experimental or theoretical, may be undertaken by properly qualified graduate students under the direction of a faculty member.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Individual Study for Ph.D. Qualifying Examination
courses.comments: No unit credit allowed toward advanced degree. Maximum of 12 units per quarter; enrollment limited to 24 units per examination. Instructor is normally student's major advisor. S/U grading.
courses.description: Individual studies for ph.d. qualifying examination.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Master's Thesis Research and Preparation
courses.comments: No unit credit allowed toward advanced degree.
courses.description: For research underlying the thesis and writing of the thesis.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Ph.D. Dissertation Research and Preparation
courses.comments: No unit credit allowed toward advanced degree.
courses.description: For research and preparation of the dissertation.

courses.subject: ME ST
courses.title: Independent Studies in Medieval Studies
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of at least two upper-division courses in medieval studies.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters. Students are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
courses.description: Special interdisciplinary study in medieval themes.

courses.subject: ME ST
courses.title: Interdisciplinary Approaches to Medieval Studies
courses.comments: Students enroll in the course for the entire Academic year. They attend and write papers on quarterly colloquia. A three- quarter in-progress sequence course with grades for all quarters issued upon completion of Medieval Studies 200C.
courses.description: Students attend and write responses to papers by visiting lecturers on topics in various fields of Medieval Studies. Themes will vary from year to year.

courses.subject: ME ST
courses.title: Interdisciplinary Approaches to Medieval Studies
courses.comments: Students enroll in the course for the entire Academic year. They will attend and write papers on two 2-hour colloquium each quarter. A three- quarter in-progress sequence course with grades for all quarters issued upon completion of Medieval Studies 200C.
courses.description: Students attend and write responses to papers by visiting lecturers on topics in various fields of Medieval Studies. Themes will vary from year to year.

courses.subject: ME ST
courses.title: Interdisciplinary Approaches to Medieval Studies
courses.comments: Students enroll in the course for the entire Academic year. They will attend and write papers on two 2-hour colloquium each quarter. A three- quarter in-progress sequence course with grades for all quarters issued upon completion of Medieval Studies 200C.
courses.description: Students attend and write responses to papers by visiting lecturers on topics in various fields of Medieval Studies. Themes will vary from year to year.

courses.subject: ME W
courses.title: Engineering Mechanics: Dynamics
courses.prereq_text: Physics 7A or Physics 2, and ME 14 with a minimum grade of C-, and Math 6B or Math 5C (may be taken concurrently); open to ME majors only.
courses.comments: May not be taken for additional credit by students who have completed ME 16.
courses.description: Vectorial kinematics of particles. Coordinate systems, moving frames, relative and constrained motion. Dynamics of particles and systems of particles. Energy and momentum methods. Collisions. Planar kinematics and kinematics of rigid bodies. Energy and momentum methods for rigid body systems.

courses.subject: ME W
courses.title: Structural Analysis
courses.comments: May not be taken for additional credit by students who have completed ME 167.
courses.description: Presents introductory matrix methods for analysis of structures. Topics include review of matrix algebra and linear equations, basic structural theorems including the principle of superposition and energy theorems, truss bar, bean and plane frame elements, and programming techniques to realize these concepts.

courses.subject: MES
courses.title: Introduction to Middle East Studies
courses.description: Surveys the peoples, cultures, and societies of the wider Middle East, focusing on social, political, cultural, and religious change. Among the concepts examined are tradition, modernity, autocracy, religious revival, gender, and ethnicity in their different regional contexts.

courses.subject: MES
courses.title: Senior Honors Thesis
courses.prereq_text: Consent of instructor and department; senior standing; open to Middle East Studies majors who have a 3.5 overall GPA and a 3.75 GPA in the major
courses.description: Projects for advanced work in Middle East Studies in conjunction with individual members of the faculty and developed by students. For students who wish to graduate with distinction in the Middle East Studies major.

courses.subject: MS
courses.title: Introduction to Leadership I
courses.description: Introduction to the organization, purpose, and functions of the U.S. Army. Provides the foundation in basic life skills to include fitness,interpersonal communication and ethical behavior using current Army models. Provide insight into the Army's profession of arms and officer's role within that profession.

courses.subject: MS
courses.title: Basic Military Policies and Organizations
courses.description: Introduction to the duties, responsibilities, and authority of military personnel. Provides an understanding of the Army's structure and organization. Identify and discuss the Army's Equal Opportunity policies. Discuss traditions of military and individual values and how professional obligations are related.

courses.subject: MS
courses.title: Basic Leadership and Problem Solving
courses.description: Provides students with a model for understanding their development as leaders. Initial lessons form the building blocks of progressive lessons in values, fitness, leadership, and squad-level tactics. Provides students with a set of broadly applicable problem solving concepts, principles, and procedures. Introduction to problem solving models coupled with concepts of screening, evaluation criteria, and practical exercises in applying the principles of problem solving.

courses.subject: MS
courses.title: Foundations of Leadership I
courses.description: Explores leadership and leadership problems solving case study: A broad analysis of leadership with an emphasis on the modern leader. Familiarization with case study on decision making and the modern army leader. Course is designed to maximize student participation, inspire intellectual curiosity, teach critical "life skills," and stimulate self-study.

courses.subject: MS
courses.title: Foundations of Leadership II
courses.description: Exploration of leadership and leadership problem solving techniques using a variety of instructional methodologies. Introduces complex land navigation techniques, operation orders and effective communication skills. Designed to maximize student participation, inspire intellectual curiosity, teach critical military skills and stimulate self-study.

courses.subject: MS
courses.title: Foundations of Leadership III
courses.description: Continued study of leadership techniques using a variety of instructional methodologies. Introduces students to contemporary military operating environment and advance time management techniques. Elaborates on other small unit techniques. Continues to maximize student participation, inspire intellectual curiosity, teach critical military skills.

courses.subject: MS
courses.title: Basic Military Science Field Study
courses.comments: Sophomore, Juniors, Seniors standing and consent of instructor. Students must meet US Army Officer Enrollment Qualification and Documentation Requirements and have enough time remaining at UCSB to complete the ROTC Advance Course Requirements.
courses.description: Students attend the 28-day paid Leadership Training Course designed to develop leadership and officer potential for the U.S. Army and ultimately contracting into the Army's ROTC advance course program. Training is intentionally stressful and designed to build individual confidence through the accomplishment of leadership opportunities.

courses.subject: MS
courses.title: Basic Military Physical Conditioning
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 3 units.
courses.description: Basic physical conditioning using the United States Army physical training program. Emphasis on cardiovascular system and upper body strength. Focus towards army officer training corps cadets, although not limited to this group.

courses.subject: MS
courses.title: American Military History and the Evolution of Western Warfare
courses.prereq_text: Lower-division standing or Army ROTC Cadets. Department approval required. Email rotcscholar@milsci.ucsb.edu for departmental approval.
courses.description: Surveys American military history and the evolution of warfare from the colonial era through the end of the twentieth century. Course examines the strategies and tactics of warfare throughout this period and explores how social, economic and technological advances contributed to the patterns of war.

courses.subject: MS
courses.title: Independent Studies
courses.comments: This course is limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
courses.description: Selected research under the direction of a faculty member.

courses.subject: MS
courses.title: Tactical leadership I
courses.comments: Leadership labs and field training exercises are required for all students. Enrollment limited to advanced ROTC cadets.
courses.description: Study of military leadership principles, responsibilities, and traits in a small unit, emphasizing adaptability and flexibility. Master technical skills in land Navigation, Troop Leading Producers, Tactical Orders, Battle Drills and Squad Tactics. Gain practical experience by planning and executing small unit military training events.

courses.subject: MS
courses.title: Tactical Leadership II
courses.description: Intermediate study of military leadership principles, responsibilities and traits in a small unit.
