Intermediate study of offensive and defensive operations and their applications. Students gain practical experience by planning and executing training events. Labs and field training required for all students.

courses.subject: MS
courses.title: Applied Leadership
courses.description: Introduction to leadership behavior, styles, peer leadership, stress management, motivating others, principles of war and applying rules of land warfare. Introduced to basic military situations in a non-conventional military operating environment. Leadership laboratory required for all ROTC students.

courses.subject: MS
courses.title: Developmental Leadership I
courses.description: Students study the fundamentals of decision making, command and control problems, staff relationships, counseling,analyzing courses of action. Leadership laboratory required for all ROTC students. Students gain practical experience by planning and executing cadet training and social events. Labs required.

courses.subject: MS
courses.title: Developmental Leadership II
courses.comments: Leadership laboratory required for all ROTC students.
courses.description: Study complex military situations in a contemporary operating environmnet. Explores military professional ethics, military law, improper relationships, and ethics in that environmnet. Gain practical experience by planning and executing cadet training and social events.

courses.subject: MS
courses.title: Adaptive Leadership
courses.comments: Leadership laboratory required for all ROTC students.
courses.description: Learn about small unit leadership dynamics between officers and noncommissioned officers and apply principles of war in a historical battle analysis setting. Learn about financial management, awards processing and installation support services.

courses.subject: MS
courses.title: Advanced Military Science Field Study
courses.prereq_text: Students must have had successfully completed MS 131, 132, and MS 133, and three quarters of MS 22 prior to attending this course. Students must meet US Army Officer contracted Qualification and Documentation Requirements.
courses.description: Students attend the 33-day paid Leadership Development Advanced Course designed to further develop and evaluate leadership and officer potential. The challenges are rigorous and demanding, both mentally and Physically, and will test intelligence, common sense, ingenuity and stamina.

courses.subject: MS
courses.title: Independent Studies
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of at least two upper-division courses in military science; open only to ROTC advanced students approved by the department chair.
courses.comments: Students are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
courses.description: Independent studies with the professor to permit study on a subject agreed by the student and professor, not covered by regular course offerings.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Classical Music Live
courses.comments: Tickets and transportation are provided free of charge. Primarily for non-Music majors. For full course information, please go to: www.music.ucsb.edu/academics/music-1
courses.description: Students meet for a one-hour pre-concert lecture given by Music Department faculty, and then attend world-class symphony concerts sponsored by Santa Barbara's Community Arts Music Association.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Careers in Music
courses.description: Through lectures, discussions, and guest speakers, this course introduces students to various career options in music and the arts, including a practical overview of the skills, knowledge and paths to pursue these goals, culminating in students developing a career portfolio.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Introduction to Music Studies
courses.comments: Designed for Music Majors and Minors. Open to Music Majors, or by permission of instructor. Music minors and non-majors should contact instructor by email for permission to enroll.
courses.description: Introduces students to ways of studying music as a cultural practice situated in society. Methods are drawn from musicology, ethnomusicology, history, anthropology, and sociology. Students will be taught to think critically about music as a universal human expression.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Writing about Music
courses.prereq_text: Music 3A with a minimum grade of C-, or consent of instructor.
courses.comments: Designed for Music Majors and Minors. Open to students who have taken Music 3A, or by permission of instructor. Contact instructor by email for permission to enroll.
courses.description: Acquaints students with different approaches to writing and speaking about music of many traditions. The works of performers, critics, music theorists, ethnographers, musicologists, and historians will all be represented in the selection of assigned readings.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Structures of Music
courses.prereq_text: Open to Music and Music Studies majors, or by consent of instructor. Music minors to contact instructor or advisor for approval.
courses.comments: Designed for Music Majors and Minors.
courses.description: Looking at a variety of music traditions from different parts of the world, the class will survey varying approaches to issues of compositional structure, rhythm, intonation, scales, etc. The class will have listening and practical components.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Musicianship
courses.prereq_text: Placement exam. A grade of at least C- is required in each course of the Music 4 series. Must be taken consecutively, and concurrently with the Music 5 series.
courses.description: A practical course in sight singing, aural analysis, and rhythmic studies.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Musicianship
courses.prereq_text: Placement Exam. A grade of at least C- is required in each course of the Music 4 series. Must be taken consecutively, and concurrently with the Music 5 series.
courses.description: A practical course in sight singing, aural analysis, and rhythmic studies.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Musicianship
courses.prereq_text: Placement Exam. A grade of at least C- is required in each course of the Music 4 series. Must be taken consecutively, and concurrently with the Music 5 series.
courses.description: A practical course in sight singing, aural analysis, and rhythmic studies.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Musicianship
courses.prereq_text: Placement Exam. A grade of at least C- is required in each course of the Music 4 series. Must be taken consecutively, and concurrently with the Music 5 series.
courses.description: A practical course in sight singing, aural analysis, and rhythmic studies.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Musicianship
courses.prereq_text: Placement Exam. A grade of at least C- is required in each course of the Music 4 series. Must be taken consecutively, and concurrently with the Music 5 series.
courses.description: A practical course in sight singing, aural analysis, and rhythmic studies.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Musicianship
courses.prereq_text: Placement Exam. A grade of at least C- is required in each course of the Music 4 series. Must be taken consecutively, and concurrently with the Music 5 series.
courses.description: A practical course in sight singing, aural analysis, and rhythmic studies.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Music Theory and Practice I
courses.description: Theory basics, including rhythm and meter, pitch, intervals, scales, keys, triads, seventh chords, and essentials of harmonic progression.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Music Theory and Practice II
courses.prereq_text: Placement exam or Music 5A with a grade of at least C-. Must be taken concurrently with the Music 4 series.
courses.description: Textural deployments of harmony, tonic and dominant on the small and large scale, contrapuntal influences, cadential progressions, non-chord tones.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Chromatic Harmony and Form
courses.prereq_text: Placement exam or Music 5B with a grade of at least C-. Must be taken consecutively, and concurrently with the Music 4 series.
courses.description: Secondary dominants, diatonic modulation, chromatic chords, sequences.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Jazz Fundamentals
courses.comments: Letter grade required for majors. May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units, but only 2 units may be applied towards the major.
courses.description: Introduction to jazz harmony, scales, and improvization. drill in ear training and beginning keyboard.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Class Composition
courses.comments: Primarily for the music major. May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 18 units.
courses.description: Assignments in basics of music writing.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: History of Western Music from Early Modern Culture through Modernism
courses.description: A survey of Western music and its social contexts from late humanism through the Age of Enlightenment (1545-1745). Topics include Renaissance legacies, music and religious reformations, ancient vs. modern, the rise of opera, patronage, instrumental composer-performers, taste in the Enlightenment.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: History of Western Music from Early Modern Culture through Modernism
courses.description: A survey of Western music and its social contexts from 1745 to 1848. Topics include the rise of public concerts and of the virtuoso soloist, the evolution of the orchestra, music in salons and parlors, and national operatic institutions.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: History of Western Music from Early Modern Culture through Modernism
courses.description: A survey of Western music and its social contexts from 1848 to 1945. Topics include music and nationalism, late romanticism and the limits of tonality, modernism, the impact of popular music on art music, and neoclassicism.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Fundamentals of Music
courses.comments: For the non-major.
courses.description: The study of notes, scales, triads, inversions, rhythm, harmony, and musical terminology. Laboratory activities include keyboard orientation, sight singing, and ear training.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Thinking Historically about Music
courses.description: This course reflects on the process of crafting narratives about the musical past and its impact on our understanding of music in the present. Students learn to analyze diverse sources and practice the construction of music historical narratives.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Constructing Communities through Music: Classical and Beyond
courses.comments: Not open to Music majors.
courses.description: Examines how music builds and sustains communities across historical contexts. Students develop critical and historical thinking using case studies from Europe and the United States to explore musical practices (classical and beyond), socio-economic contexts, and continuities between past and present.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Listening to Jazz: Demystifying Americas Musical Art Form
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Music 191 in spring 2018.
courses.description: Aims to unravel the mystery of Jazzs allure, importance, and performance process, in a manner mostly divorced from technical musical terminology or music theory, through targeted readings, listening assignments, written projects, in-class visits, and concert attendance.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: World Music
courses.comments: No previous training in music required.
courses.description: An introductory course surveying the unity and diversity of folk, traditional, and classical music of the non-western world. Emphasis given to dance, theatre, musical instruments, and the role of music in society.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Elementary Voice I
courses.prereq_text: Music 11 or UCSB Exam 38 (Music Theory Placement Test) with a score of 1 or higher. Placement by audition on the first day of class.
courses.comments: Primarily for the BA Music Major, the BM Instrumental Music Major and the Music Minor.
courses.description: Elementary voice lessons at beginning level. Placement in Music A, B, or C will be determined by the instructor after an audition.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Elementary Voice II
courses.prereq_text: Music 11. Placement by audition the first day of class.
courses.comments: Primarily for the BA Music Major, the BM Instrumental Music Major and the Music Minor.
courses.description: Elementary voice lessons designed for those with a small amount of vocal experience.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Elementary Voice III
courses.prereq_text: Music 11. Placement by audition on first day of class.
courses.comments: Primarily for the BA Music Major, the BM Instrumental Music major and the Music Minor.
courses.description: Elementary voice lessons designed for those who have significant vocal training and experience.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Practicum in World Music Performance
courses.comments: If there is no meeting time listed on the course schedule, contact instructor during first week of quarter to schedule instruction.
courses.description: Applied instruction in non-Western instruments: the Middle Eastern oud (lute) and nay (end-blown flute), Middle Eastern percussion, and dastgah (Persian melodic practice).

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Practicum in World Music Performance: Arabic Maqam
courses.description: Applied instruction in non-Western instruments: the Arabic maqam, the system of melodic modes used in traditional Arabic music.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Practicum in World Music Performance: the nay (Middle-Eastern flute).
courses.description: Applied instruction in non-Western instruments: the Middle-Eastern nay (end-blown flute).

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Practicum in World Music Performance: the oud (Middle-Eastern lute).
courses.description: Applied instruction in the Middle Eastern oud (lute).

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Practicum in World Music Performance
courses.comments: If there is no meeting time listed on the course schedule, contact instructor during first week of quarter to schedule instruction.
courses.description: Applied instruction in a non-Western instrument.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Carillon
courses.comments: Piano audition required. Contact instructor over email to schedule audition.
courses.description: Applied instruction on Carillon (bells in bell tower) performance.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Intermediate Voice
courses.prereq_text: By audition. Departmental approval required prior to registration. Consent of instructor to finalize registration.
courses.comments: Primarily for Music majors. Taken for 3 units per quarter by BM Voice emphasis majors and for 1-2 units per quarter by all others.
courses.description: Intermediate voice lessons.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Intermediate Cello
courses.prereq_text: By audition. Consent of instructor and department.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 27 units. Taken for 3 units per quarter by BM Cello emphasis majors, and for 1-2 units per quarter by all others.
courses.description: Intermediate cello lessons.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Intermediate Viola
courses.prereq_text: By audition. Consent of instructor and department.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 27 units. Taken for 3 units per quarter by BM Viola emphasis majors, and for 1-2 units per quarter by all others.
courses.description: Intermediate viola lessons.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Intermediate Violin

courses.title: Direct Digital Synthesis, Processing and Composition
courses.description: First quarter of general purpose computing for computer music applications. Topics include: introduction to the UNIX operating system and the VI editor, music synthesis using C-music program and score input programs.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Introduction to Electroacoustic Music Thought
courses.comments: Required for Composition majors. Other music majors and non-majors may enroll on a space available basis.
courses.description: An introductory course on electroacoustic music. Historical perspective. Analysis of different types of electronic/acousmatic/mixed compositions. Introduction to different techniques of sound transformation.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Real-Time Digital Synthesis, Processing and Composition.
courses.description: First quarter of a 3-quarter series course in real-time digital synthesis and composition will concentrate on multi-track recording, mixing, digital signal processing using micro-computers and special purpose DSP equipment for music composition.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Real-Time Digital Synthesis, Processing and Composition
courses.description: Second quarter of a 3-quarter series course will concentrate on digital synthesis (primarily frequency modulation, simple and complex; but also amplitude modulation and additive synthesis) using micro-computers, digital synthesizers and processing equipment for music composition.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Real-Time Digital Synthesis, Processing and Composition
courses.description: Third quarter of a 3-quarter series course will concentrate on real-time computer music composition with micro-computers and digital synthesis/processing equipment.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Acoustic/Electroacoustic Instrument Making Laboratory
courses.comments: Lower division students can enroll with consent of instructor.
courses.description: A creative laboratory where students invent and construct new acoustic and electroacoustic instruments, exploring sound as a living material through experimentation, design, and embodied practice.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Contemporary Theories of Music
courses.prereq_text: Theory experience equivalent to Music 5 series. Upper division standing.
courses.description: Examines how modern technologies and acoustical thought reshaped composition, moving from notation toward sound as structure, material, and expressive force.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Seminar in Music Creation
courses.description: A shared studio for exchanging ideas, works-in-progress, and research. Students shape the agenda, engaging in critique, experimentation, and collaboration across styles and technologies to expand their creative practices.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: History of Western Music and its Global Circulations, 1545-1745
courses.description: Explores history of western music and its global circulations from Renaissance through Enlightenment (1545-1745). Topics include musicians’ careers and social life; spirituality; gender, race, emerging subjectivity; music for public stages; commercialism; colonialism; popular music practices. Western music notation experience required.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: History of Western Music and its Global Circulations, 1745-1848
courses.description: Explores history of western music and its global circulations 1748-1848. Topics include a range of composers/performers/listeners and how conceptions of musical practices were shaped by socio-political context, colonialism, class, gender, race, religion, economics. Western music notation experience required.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: History of Western Music and its Global Circulations, 1848-1945
courses.description: Explores history of western music and its global circulations 1848-1945, including its philosophical, artistic, and social contexts. Topics include nationalism; late romanticism and limits tonality; modernism; impact of popular music on western classical music; neoclassicism. Western music notation experience required.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: The History of Opera: 1600-1800
courses.description: An overview of the history of opera from 1600-1800, placing selected works within a social context, and viewing opera as a musical work, dramatic spectacle, and cultural commodity.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Music and Popular Culture in America
courses.description: A survey of the relationships between music and popular culture in America. Music to be discussed includes blues, jazz, and rock, as well as classical music. Emphasis is on cultural, rather than technical aspects of music.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Symphonic Music
courses.prereq_text: Music 15 or Music 3A. Music 3A may be taken concurrently.
courses.comments: Contact departmental advisor for an approval code if concurrently enrolled in Music 3A.
courses.description: A study of selected symphonic works.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: American Music History: From the Colonial Period to the Present
courses.description: An overview of the varieties of American musical experience from the Colonial period to the present. Representative works from several genres are studies with a view to placing them in their cultural context and identifying major aesthetic issues.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: American Experimental Music: John Cage and After
courses.description: A survey of the American experimental tradition in music and related arts, starting with John Cage and continuing through generations of those have followed in his path through the present day. Students will read primary sources by these artists as well as secondary literature from theoretical and historical perspectives; course activities will also include study and discussion of experimental artworks, written responses, and creative activities.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Music and the Mind
courses.description: Introduction to the psychology of music. Topics include music perception and cognition, learning and memory, emotion and meaning, music and language, music and the brain, emergence and development of skills, perspectives from social and cultural psychology, well-being and therapy, and others.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Women’s Voices in Western Music History, from Barbara Strozzi to Beyoncé
courses.description: Examines women’s musical practices from the past millennium to rethink narratives of Western music, past and present. We study musicians from the Middle Ages onward to examine and challenge feminine archetypes in Western music.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Music and Politics
courses.comments: Primarily for non-majors but also open to majors.
courses.description: A study of the interaction between music and politics from the fourteenth century to the present. Includes discussion of relevant art from each period.

courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units, but only 4 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: An introduction to fundamentals of orchestral conducting and score reading.

courses.description: Aspects of choral techniques; including: development of concert programs and rehearsal plans, rehearsal procedures, types of vocal ensembles and seating configurations, acoustical considerations, performance and recording procedures, long-term programming and artistic development, social and organizational aspects of vocal ensemble.

courses.subject: MUS

courses.prereq_text: Music 4C; Music 5C with a grade of at least C-.
courses.description: Analysis of small- and large-scale formal structures in music from the late Baroque through the late Classic period (ca. 1720-1820).

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Twentieth Century Analysis
courses.prereq_text: Music 4C; Music 5C with a grade of at least C-.
courses.description: Analysis of non-tonal and twelve-tone music.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Advanced Tonal Analysis
courses.description: Continuation of Music 160A, advanced tonal analysis through nineteenth century works.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Tuning and Temperament
courses.description: Survey of a number of tuning systems found around the world, including those of Ancient Greece, Europe, India, China, the Arab Middle East, Turkey, and Indonesia. The mathematical, aesthetic, and symbolic bases of each system will be considered.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: The Arabic System of Melodic Modes: The Maqamat
courses.description: An intensive examination of the system of melodic modes (Maqamat) that governs present-day practice in the eastern Arab world. Emphasis given to theoretical issues (quarter tones, tetrachordel structures, and theories of intonation), analysis of standard repertoire, and procedures governing improvisation.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Analysis of Popular Music
courses.prereq_text: Music 5B with a grade of at least C-
courses.description: Explores different approaches to analyzing popular music (specifically post-1960, predominantly American popular music), including not only theory and analysis of harmony and melody, form, timbre, rhythm/meter but also issues of meanings and expression, intertextuality, race and gender.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Choral Literature
courses.prereq_text: Three quarters of the Music 112A-F series.
courses.description: A historical and analytical survey of major choral works from the seventeenth century to the present.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Other Issues in Ethnomusicology
courses.description: A study of other cultural issues in ethnomusicology. Specific issue or topics will vary by quarter and will be announced in advance by the department.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Film Music Cognition
courses.description: A consideration of film music as a medium of communication between the director, composer, music supervisor, editors, performers and the audience. Emphasis given to cognitive psychological theories of meaning in terms of structure and affect in audio/visual contexts.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Music and Documentary Film
courses.description: View global popular music through the lens of documentary film. We will analyze a series of films depicting cultural and political histories, creative performances, and everyday lives of musicians in different representational frames and social contexts.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: The Musical World of the Grateful Dead: from Americana to Psychedelia
courses.description: An examination of the Grateful Dead and its impact on popular culture, festivals and the music business. We study the Dead’s music from folk to improvisational rock as a creative Americana response to the political turbulence of the Sixties.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Creative Arts, Memories and Experimental Performance
courses.comments: Cross-Listing Course with Theater and Dance
courses.description: Through creative arts practices, analysis, workshops and new performance, this course explores processes of transformation and translation of traces of memories and experiences into provocative art works. Experimental performance practices encompass theatrical, movement based, sonic, music-based and visual arts.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Music and Sports
courses.description: In this course, students study connections between the human cultural practices of music and sport. We draw from rich literatures in performance studies, sports studies, and ethnomusicology to consider selected case studies where music and sport intersect.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Birds, sonic arts & environmental sensitivities
courses.description: Focusing on birds and sonic arts, this course engages creative, analytical & experiential activities. Topics include: ecoacoustics, sound maps, deep listening, sensory memory, soundscape ecologies and environmental issues, blurring borders between more-than-human/human interactions, art/science, and local/global.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Umm Kulthum: Her Music, Her Life, Her Times
courses.description: Analysis of the music, life, an times of the predominant Arab singer of the twentieth century. Individual projects may focus on music or text analysis, issues of gender, nationalism, agency, performance practice, and investigation of related arts (film, novels, etc.).

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Understanding Brazilian Music in its Cultural Context
courses.comments: MUS 178BR, C LIT 131B, and PORT 110 are the same course.
courses.description: This course enables students to understand what Brazilian music is, and what is the role of Music in Brazilian culture. It offers a comprehensive panel of the history of music in Brazil. The course also provides students with a full cultural context, discussing the role of music during the two dictatorship periods in Brazil, 1930-1945 and 1964-1985 and the political impact of censorship. It also discusses the contributions of the Africans, brought to Brazil by the Portuguese colonizers, and the impact African culture has both in music and religion. Taught in English.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Music Cultures of the World: The Middle East
courses.description: Arab, Turkish, and Persian music traditions from historical, cultural, and musicological perspectives. Emphasis given to the position of music in Islam, present-day performers, and modal and rhythmic structures.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Music Cultures of the World: India
courses.description: A survey of music traditions of the Indian subcontinent from classical to folk and popular. Emphasis on the position of music in Hindu philosophy, the role of music in society, musical instruments, and modal and rhythmic structures (Raga and Tala).

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Music in Modern Japan
courses.description: This course explores music and culture in modern Japan. What kind of society do we hear in its diverse mix of sounds and musical practices? We explore this question through traditional genres, national politics, and transnational exchanges of popular media.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Music Cultures of the World: Other Regions
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 16 units.
courses.description: A study of music traditions and genres from other regions of the world. Specific regions studied vary by quarter and are announced in advance by the department.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Environmental Sound Arts
courses.prereq_text: Upper division standing, instructor approval required.
courses.description: Environmental Sound Arts focuses on responses to, and uses of environmental sounds in the broadest framework of soundscapes and environmental humanities, encompassing processes of fieldwork listening , analysis, and creation of new environmental sound art for public facing advocacy work.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Music, Community, Wellbeing: Advocacy and Activism
courses.description: Taking a vocational and facilitatory approach, this course uses case studies to explore concepts and processes of generating and sustaining musical activity as community-engaged practice. Topics include: social justice, health and wellbeing, education, senses of place, ecology, and technology.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Studies in Ethnomusicology
courses.description: An introduction to the field of ethnomusicology using theories and methods derived from the social sciences and humanities. Topic areas to include transcription and analysis, musicians, musical instruments, music acculturation, and the function of music in society.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Proseminar in Classical Music
courses.comments: Course designed for majors.
courses.description: A selective study of various stylistic and historical aspects of classical music.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Proseminar in Romantic Music
courses.comments: Course designed for music majors.
courses.description: A selective study of various stylistic and historical aspects of romantic music.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Proseminar in Contemporary Music
courses.comments: Course designed for majors
courses.description: A selective study of various stylistic and historical aspects of contemporary music.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Ethnomusicology Forum
courses.description: A forum for the presentation of research and performance by students, faculty, and visiting scholars and performers.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing and consent of instructor.
courses.description: Special seminar in selected problems of current musicology, ethnomusicology, theory, or performance.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: B.A. Senior Project
courses.prereq_text: Open to B. A. senior Music majors only.
courses.description: Preparation of senior audition, composition, or paper.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: B.A. Senior Project
courses.prereq_text: Open to B.A. senior Music Studies majors only.
courses.description: The first quarter of preparation of senior audition, composition, or paper.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: B.A. Senior Project
courses.prereq_text: Music 192A with a minimum grade of C-.
courses.comments: Open to B.A. senior Music Studies majors only.
courses.description: The second quarter of preparation of senior audition, composition, or paper.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: B.A. Senior Project
courses.prereq_text: Music 192B with a minimum grade of C-.
courses.comments: Open to B.A. senior Music Studies majors only.
courses.description: The third and final quarter of preparation of senior audition, composition, or paper.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Junior Recital
courses.prereq_text: Passing of B.M. sophomore audition; open to upper-division Bachelor of Music Performance Emphasis major only.
courses.description: Preparation of junior recital.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Honors Music
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; honors students only; consent of instructor and department.
courses.comments: For Distinction in the Major must be taken with Music 192 or 197 or 197B.
courses.description: An undergraduate independent research for honor students. Carefully selected topics intended to foster excellence in research, theory, composition, or performance.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Senior Recital
courses.prereq_text: Passing of junior recital; open to senior Music Performance emphasis majors only.
courses.description: Preparation of senior recital.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Senior Composition Portfolio and Recital
courses.prereq_text: Passing of junior composition portfolio; and, consent of instructor; open tsenior BM Composition emphasis majors only.
courses.description: Preparation of senior composition portfolio.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Individual Research in Music
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of three quarters of the Music 112AB-F series; consent of instructor.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined. Students are limited to 4 units per quarter and 16 units total in Music 198/199 courses.
courses.description: Independent research under the guidance of a faculty member in the department. Course offers qualified students the opportunity to undertake independent research or work in a research group in topics in musicology, ethnomusicology, composition, theory, or performance.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Independent Research Assistance in Music
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of three quarters of the Music 112AB-F series; consent of instructor and department.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined. Students are limited to 4 units per quarter and 16 units total in Music 198/199 courses. No more than 4 units in combination with Music 199 may be applied to major.
courses.description: Faculty supervised research assistance.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Bibliography and Research Techniques
courses.comments: Primarily intended for the MM and DMA graduate student in Music.
courses.description: A survey of music bibliography and research methods.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Bibliography and Research Techniques
courses.comments: Primarily intended for the M.A. and Ph.D. graduate student in musicology or theory.
courses.description: Survey and discussion of select historical, methodological, and theoretical approaches to research in musicology.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Bibliography and Research Techniques
courses.comments: Primarily for the M.A. and Ph.D. graduate student in theory.
courses.description: A survey of music bibliography and research methods in theory.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Musicology-Theory Forum
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing in musicology or theory emphasis.
courses.description: Theory students, faculty and visiting scholars present their current research.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Graduate Composition
courses.comments: Required for M.A. and Ph.D. in composition.
courses.description: Individual instruction in composition.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Direct Digital Synthesis, Processing and Composition
courses.comments: Graduate music majors and graduate non-majors in areas of electrical engineering, computer science, physics, and mathematics.
courses.description: First quarter of general purpose computing for computer music applications. Topics include: introduction to the UNIX operating system and the vi editor, music synthesis using C-based computer programs and score input programs.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Introduction to Electroacoustic Music
courses.comments: Required for Composition majors. Music majors and non-majors may also enroll.
courses.description: An introductory course on electroacoustic music. Historical perspective. Analysis of different types of electronic/acousmatic/mixed compositions. Introduction to different techniques of sound transformation.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Real-Time Digital Music Synthesis, Processing and Composition
courses.prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Graduate music majors and graduate non-majors in areas of electrical engineering, computer science, physics, and mathematics.
courses.description: First quarter of a three-quarter sequence course will concentrate on multi-track recording, mixing, digital signal processing using micro-computers and special purpose dsp equipment.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Real-Time Digital Music Synthesis, Processing and Composition
courses.description: Second quarter of a three-quarter sequence course will concentrate on digital synthesis (primarily frequency modulation, simple and complex; but also amplitude modulation and additive synthesis) using micro-computers, digital synthesizers and processing equipment.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Real-Time Digital Music Synthesis, Processing and Composition
courses.description: Third quarter of a three-quarter sequence course will concentrate on real-time computer music composition with micro-computer and digital synthesis/processing equipment.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Introduction to Visual Music
courses.prereq_text: Mus 211B or Mus 109IA or Mus 209IA or Mus 109LA or Mus 209LA or consent of instructor.
courses.comments: Designed essentially for majors. Non-majors may also enroll with the consent of the instructor.
courses.description: Introductory course on Visual Music. Historical perspective. Introduction to Final Cut Pro, After Effects, Cinema 4D and other visual music composition software.Several short exercises will be required during the quarter.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Visual Music Composition
courses.prereq_text: MUS 209TA or consent of the instructor
courses.comments: Designed essentially for majors. Non-majors may also enroll with the consent of the instructor. May be repeated with permission of instructor but used only once for credit in major.
courses.description: Visual Music composition. Mixing, synthesis, animation, sound-image integration. An original Visual Music composition is required after the end of the course.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Contemporary Composition Techniques (Instrumental)
courses.prereq_text: Passing grade on all theory placement examinations.
courses.comments: Designed/required for Composition majors.
courses.description: Study of different compositional techniques based on the analysis of pieces from the repertoire. Rhythm manipulation, harmonic contents, formal aspects, integration between instruments and electronics, extended techniques, gesture control, etc. A short paper explaining the application of one or more of these techniques in an original composition is required after the end of the course.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Contemporary Composition Techniques (Electroacoustic)
courses.prereq_text: Mus 209L or Mus 209IA or Mus 209LA or consent of the instructor
courses.description: Study of different compositional techniques based on sound objects transformations. Analysis of pieces from the repertoire. Synthesis, recording, mixing, sound object transformation techniques, spatialization. An original 5-8 min acousmatic/electronic music composition is required after the end of the course.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Applied Instruction
courses.comments: Not for the performance emphasis in MM or DMA degree programs.
courses.description: Applied vocal or instrumental instruction for graduate students other than in the performance emphasis discipline of MM and DMA degree programs.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: MM/DMA Performance Instruction
courses.prereq_text: Entrance audition for MM or DMA degree program.
courses.comments: Restricted to MM and DMA majors admitted to the performance emphasis in voice or the specific instrument of study in Music 220.
courses.description: Applied instruction in the performance emphasis discipline (MM piano accompanying: instruction in piano) of MM and DMA degree programs.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Practicum in World Music Performance
courses.comments: Graduate standing.
courses.description: Individual or group instruction in non-Western instruments: the Indian sitar, the Middle Eastern `ud (lute) and nay (end-blown flute), and Middle Eastern percussion.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Practicum in World Music Performance
courses.comments: Graduate standing.
courses.description: Individual or group instruction in non-Western instruments: the Indian sitar, the Middle Eastern `ud (lute) and nay (end-blown flute), and Middle Eastern percussion.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Seminar in Ethnomusicology
courses.description: A graduate seminar examining special problems, current theories, analytic procedures, and recent innovations in ethnomusicology.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Orchestral Conducting
courses.comments: Enrollment by audition. May be repeated for credit.
courses.description: Advanced conducting techniques, score reading and analysis, general rehearsal procedures and repertoire for each type of ensemble: symphony, chamber orchestra and large vocal/instrumental ensembles.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Choral Conducting
courses.comments: Enrollment by audition. May be repeated for credit.
courses.description: Advanced conducting techniques, score reading and analysis, rehearsal techniques and repertoire for vocal and choral ensembles.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Choral Techniques
courses.prereq_text: Music 231 (may be taken concurrently) and consent of instructor.
courses.description: Aspects of choral techniques, including: development of concert programs and rehearsal plans, rehearsal procedures, types of vocal ensembles and seating configurations, acoustical considerations, performance and recording procedures, long-term programming and artistic development, social and organization aspects of vocal ensemble.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Seminar in Music Theory
courses.description: Analysis and theory of atonal music.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Seminar in Schenkerian Analysis
courses.prereq_text: Must be taken in consecutive order.
courses.description: Readings in the theory of Schenkerian analysis. Basic analytical techniques.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Viola Orchestral Repertoire
courses.description: The study of the entire standard orchestral repertoire for viola and audition procedures.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Vocal and Instrumental Coaching
courses.prereq_text: Concurrent graduate vocal or instrumental study (Music 220, 219, 235) graduate standing; consent of instructor.
courses.description: Musical preparation of vocal or instrumental works.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Composition Forum
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 6 units toward major.
courses.description: A forum for the presentation and discussion of new works by students, faculty, and guest composers.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Opera/Song Repertoire
courses.description: A detailed study of operatic literature and concert literature (Lieder, melodies, songs, and pieces with instruments). The interpretation of vocal music as a preparation for performance.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Music Cognition
courses.description: Surveys research in music cognition and introduces empirical methods for studying music. Topics include music perception and cognition, memory and expectation, emotion and meaning, emergence and development of skills and performance, perspectives from social and cultural psychology, among others.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Tuning and Temperament
courses.description: The course surveys a number of tuning systems around the world, including those of ancient Greece, Europe, India, China, the Arab Middle East, Turkey, and Indonesia. The mathematical, aesthetic, and symbolic basis of each system will be considered.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: The Arab System of Melodic Modes (Maqamat)
courses.description: Examination of the system of melodic modes (maqamat) governing present-day melodic practice in the eastern Arab world. Emphasis given to theoretical issues (quarter tones, tetrachordal structures, theories of intonation), analysis of pieces in the repertoire, and procedures governing improvisation.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Tonal Analysis Review
courses.description: An in-depth review of elements and procedures of 18th- and 19th-century harmony, aimed at analyzing conventional formal types (binary, ternary, rondo, sonata, sonata-rondo, concerto).

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Other Issues in Ethnomusicology
courses.description: A study of other cultural issues in ethnomusicology. Specific topics vary by quarter and will be announced in advanced by the department.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Music as Media
courses.description: Recorded media are central to the way we hear, create, exchange and experience music in contemporary social life. Topics include the early uses of the phonograph, recording studios, file-sharing, online musical exchange and roles of technological media in globalizing cultures.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Umm Kulthum: Her Music. Her Life. Her Times.
courses.description: Analysis of the music, life and times of the predominant Arab singer of the twentieth century. Individual projects may focus on music or text analysis, issues of gender, nationalism, agency, performance, practice and investigation of related arts (film, novels, etc.).

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Seminar in Musicology
courses.description: Graduate Seminar in Musicology. Topics will vary.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Seminar in Musicology: The Twentieth Century
courses.description: Graduate seminar in music of the twentieth century.

courses.description: Selected topics in musical analysis.

courses.description: A selective study of various stylistic and historical aspects of contemporary music.

courses.title: Ethnomusicology Forum
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Music 222.
courses.description: A forum for the presentation of research and performances by students, faculty, and visiting scholars and performers. Students must be currently involved in a research or performance project.

courses.title: Music Cultures of the World: Middle East

courses.description: Arab, Turkish, and Persian music traditions from historical, cultural, and musicological perspectives. Emphasis given to the position of music in Islam, present-day performers, and modal and rhythmic structures.

courses.description: A survey of music traditions of the Indian subcontinent from classical to folk and popular. Emphasis given to the position of music in Hindu philosophy, the role of music in society, musical instruments, and modal and rythmic structures (raga and tala).

courses.title: Master of Music Performances
courses.prereq_text: Recital audition required. Master of Music students only.
courses.description: Preparation of: a. a full length recital (conducting: the equivalent of a full-length concert.)

courses.description: Preparation of: b. a major performance: chamber music recital or concerto or major opera/oratorio role or another full-length recital (conducting: the equivalent of a chamber ensemble or small ensemble or large ensemble ormixed concert).

courses.title: Performance Literature
courses.description: A study of problems in the analysis and performance of major works in selected repertoire. a: piano b: strings c:voice d: orchestral e: choral f: woodwinds g: brass

courses.title: Performance Literature
courses.description: A study of problems in the analysis and performance of major works in selected repertoire. a: piano

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Doctor of Musical Arts Performances
courses.comments: DMA (including MM Plan 2) students only.
courses.description: Preparation of chamber music recital or concerto or major opera/oratorio role or a full length recital (conducting: the equivalent of a chamber ensemble or small ensemble or large ensemble or mixed concert).

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Doctor of Musical Arts Performances
courses.comments: DMA (including MM Plan 2) students only.
courses.description: Preparation of a full-length recital (conducting: the equivalent of a full-length concert).

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Doctor of Musical Arts Seminar: Historical/Theoretical Aspects of Music
courses.description: A study of selected repertories, not confined to a single genre or period, from the technical perspective of music thoery and history.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Teaching Practicum
courses.comments: Appointment as teaching assistant or associate. No unit credit allowed toward advanced degree.
courses.description: Teaching assistant: leads discussion of topics covered in the lecture. Associate: assumes full responsibility for the teaching of one or more courses.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Dissertation Writing Seminar
courses.description: Designed to serve all A.B.D. graduate students in the academic areas who are at various stages of writing their dissertation thesis. Seminar will be organized as a workshop in which all students will present portions of their writing for discussion. As tailored to each students project, we will discuss a number of dissertation writing challenges and learn how to self-edit and critically evaluate effective thesis writing.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Special seminar in selected problems of current musicology, ethnomusicology, composition, theory, or performance.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Special seminar in selected problems of current musicology, ethnomusicology, composition, theory, or performance.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Music Pedagogy
courses.description: Covers theories, principles, and practical techniques for teaching music, especially in undergraduate-level music classroom instruction. Topics may include learning objectives, assessments, music-specific challenges, inclusive pedagogy, lesson planning, and writing teaching philosophies. Recommended course for all teaching assistants.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Group Studies
courses.description: Critical review of research in selected problems of musicology, ethnomusicology, composition, theory, or performance.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Directed Reading and Research
courses.description: Individual tutorial for research in musicology, ethnomusicology, composition, theory, or performance; instructor will usually be student's major professor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Individual Study for Master's Comprehensive and Doctoral Qualifying Exam- inations for Advancement to Candidacy
courses.prereq_text: Consent of instructor and graduate advisor.
courses.comments: No unit credit allowed toward advanced degrees.
courses.description: Individual study for master's comprehensive and doctoral qualifying examinations for advancement to candidacy.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Preparation for Master's Degree
courses.comments: No unit credit allowed toward advanced degrees.
courses.description: Instructor will be chair of student's committee in musicology, ethnomusicology, composition, theory, or performance.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Ph.D. Dissertation Research and Preparation
courses.comments: No unit credit allowed toward advanced degrees.
courses.description: Instructor will ordinarily be chair of student's doctoral committee.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Preparation for Doctor of Musical Arts Post-Candidacy Recitals
courses.comments: No unit credit allowed toward advanced degrees.
courses.description: Preparation of two full-length recitals (conducting: the equivalent of two full-length concerts) required after advancement to candidacy for the dma degree. Instructor should be student's performance instructor: ordinarily chair of DMA committee.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Preparation of DMA Document
courses.comments: No unit credit allowed toward advanced degrees.
courses.description: Preparation of the DMA document required after advancement to candidacy for the DMA degree. Instructor should be a member of student's doctoral committee.

courses.subject: MUS A
courses.title: Wind Ensemble
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit up to six units. Advanced players only.
courses.description: Masterworks of the literature for ensembles smaller than orchestral or fullband scoring. Although the basic ensembles feature winds, both strings and percussion are utilized.

courses.subject: MUS A
courses.title: UCSB Chamber Choir
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit
courses.description: A select ensemble of voice majors and non-majors, the Chamber Choir prepares musicians for professional ensemble work and offers advanced study in choral literature, techniques, styles and interpretation covering five centuries of choral repertoire.

courses.subject: MUS A
courses.title: UCSB Concert Choir
courses.description: The UCSB Concert Choir is a mixed-voice ensemble open to all voice types (SATB). No audition required. Singers build musicianship and ensemble skills through diverse repertoire, weekly rehearsals, and public performances.

courses.subject: MUS A
courses.title: UCSB Singing Gauchos
courses.description: The UCSB Singing Gauchos is a tenor and bass choir performing fine choral literature representative of various style periods and vocal techniques from the global choral tradition. Regular performances on and off campus.

courses.subject: MUS A
courses.title: Opera Workshop
courses.comments: Letter grade required for majors. May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 6 units.
courses.description: Participation in opera scenes.

courses.subject: MUS A
courses.title: Opera Production
courses.description: Participation in annual opera production.

courses.subject: MUS A
courses.title: The Fundamentals of Popular Guitar
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit up to six units.
courses.description: A skills course designed for developing guitar technique used in folk, rock, blues, classical and jazz styles. The curriculum focuses on strumming patterns, finger picking, chords and their voicings, riffs and soloing. Emphasis is on learning to play songs by ear. Neck geography is taught through relational patterns of scales and modes. All guitar types (acoustic, classical, electric) are welcome, though acoustic/ classical are preferred. This class accommodates a variety of playing levels, from complete beginner to intermediate-advanced shredders and classical players, and everything in-between. Guitar to be provided by the student.

courses.subject: MUS A
courses.title: Ensemble for Contemporary Music
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit up to 6 units.
courses.description: Reading sessions and preparation for performance of contemporary music. There will be two concerts each quarter. Includes departmental scholarship players, and is open to composers who also perform.

courses.subject: MUS A
courses.title: Collaborative Creation Lab: Composers and Performers
courses.description: A living laboratory of collaboration between composers and performers, exploring sound as a shared terrain through the creation of acoustic, electroacoustic, and hybrid works.

courses.subject: MUS A
courses.title: Piano Ensemble
courses.description: Piano duets (1 piano, 4 hands) and duos (2 pianos) in separate sections.

courses.subject: MUS A
courses.title: Orchestra
courses.description: UCSB Chamber Orchestra performs pieces from the traditional chamber orchestra repertoire, as well as more contemporary pieces for chamber orchestra.

courses.subject: MUS A
courses.title: Flute Choir
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit up to six units.
courses.description: The flute choir studies flute literature in depth, perfects technique and interpretation, employs the complete flute family of bass, alto flutes and piccolos. Prepares ensemble for public performances each quarter.

courses.subject: MUS A
courses.title: Chamber Music Ensemble
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit up to nine units.
courses.description: Chamber music ensemble.

courses.subject: MUS A
courses.title: Brass Quintet
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of six units.
courses.description: Participation in scholarship brass quintet.

courses.subject: MUS A
courses.title: Brass Orchestral Repertoire
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 6 units.
courses.description: Intensive exploration of staple brass orchestral repertoire, emphasizing the works of important 19th and 20th century composers. Classes include rehearsal sessions, guided listening and analysis, mock auditions, resume and taped audition preparation.

courses.subject: MUS A
courses.title: Horn Ensemble
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 6 units.
courses.description: Horn ensemble.

courses.subject: MUS A
courses.title: Jazz Ensemble
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit up to 6 units.
courses.description: Instruction in interpretation and performance of jazz music. Improvization is stressed. Audition is required.

courses.subject: MUS CS
courses.title: Group Studies
courses.description: Student-directed discussion and study in a variety of subjects within Music Composition.

courses.subject: MUS CS
courses.title: Individual Instruction in Composition
courses.description: Individual instruction in composition, usually for one hour per week.

courses.subject: MUS CS
courses.title: Analysis: Forms
courses.description: Small group instruction in musical forms and their development.

courses.subject: MUS CS
courses.title: Special Topics in Music Composition
courses.description: Individual or small group instruction in selected subjects related to the study of Music Composition, including but not limited to individual composers and their works, special compositional techniques, performance projects, and topics in technological applications to music.

courses.subject: MUS CS
courses.title: Algorithmic Composition with Max/MSP
courses.description: A formalized journey into the basics of algorithmic composition, using Max/MSP as a tool to aid the artist and engineer alike. We explore how simple algorithmic models can provide intriguing sonic results across all genres. These methods are not only useful for schematic problem solving but can also be good for expanding musical and creative thinking.

courses.subject: MUS CS
courses.title: Art Song
courses.description: Explorations of text setting, repertory, effective accompaniments. Content will vary by instructor.

courses.subject: MUS CS
courses.title: The Classical Guitar in Contemporary Composition
courses.description: A survey of modern classical guitar repertoire, considering the very nature of the genre and its relationship to popular music, the classical tradition, and contemporary composition at large. Classes consist of active listening, discussion, and score-study. The culmination is a short, original classical guitar composition. A background in music helpful, but no specific experience is required.

courses.subject: MUS CS
courses.title: The Electric Guitar in Contemporary Composition
courses.description: A survey of modern electric guitar repertoire, considering the very nature of the genre and its relationship to rock, classical, and contemporary composition at large. Classes consist of active listening, discussion, and score-study. The culmination is a short, original electric guitar composition. A background in music helpful, but no specific experience is required.

courses.subject: MUS CS
courses.title: Favorite Things
courses.description: Students will analyze and present their favorite works, whether acoustic or electronic; tonal or atonal or serial; chamber or orchestral or vocal. Subsequently, students will write music of their own, based on a single, well-defined element from the works they admire.

courses.subject: MUS CS
courses.title: Language Lost: Music Creation and the Destruction of Meaning
courses.description: How can composers maintain expressiveness in vocal music when specific meanings are elusive? We will focus on the manipulation of sound/speech qualities such as pitch, rhythm, phrasing, timbre, and tempo. Our multidisciplinary approach aims to both create and deconstruct language, exploring new technologies to enhance individual expression and innovate in musical communication.

courses.subject: MUS CS
courses.title: Landscape Music
courses.description: A study of music written in response to the natural and the built landscape(s) around us.

courses.subject: MUS CS
courses.title: 1960S MUSICAL REVOLUTIONARIES: MILES DAVIS, JIMI HENDRIX, YOKO ONO, AND KARLHEINZ STOCKHAUSEN
courses.description: Delves into the iconic 1960s, exploring the revolutionary impact of major figures Miles Davis, Jimi Hendrix, Yoko Ono, and Karlheinz Stockausen in their particular and overlapping domains. It offers a mix of music history and performative collaboration, welcoming students from all disciplines, regardless of their musical background.

courses.subject: MUS CS
courses.title: CCS Musical
courses.description: Collaborative class for the creation of new musical theater works. Content will vary by instructor.

courses.subject: MUS CS
courses.title: Questions About Music
courses.description: What is the essence of music? The nature of musical form and communication? What is at the heart of music making and music listening? What is music’s role in society? How do composers think and talk about music? This course explores these and other “questions about music” via the written word, personal reflection, and in-class discussion.

courses.subject: MUS CS
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: This special studies course allows faculty to design and execute courses that reflect their particular research and teaching.

courses.subject: MUS CS
courses.title: Synths and Sci-Fi Cinema
courses.description: Explore the intersection of "synths" and sci-fi cinema in this course. We'll analyze iconic film scores and director/composer collaborations from the 1950s to today, including Kubrick/Carlos and Nolan/Zimmer. The course blends viewing sessions with discussions, presentations, and performances. Students have the opportunity to compose or improvise their own sci-fi soundscapes.

courses.subject: MUS CS
courses.title: CCS Counterpoint
courses.description: Studies in the concepts of counterpoint as they apply to original composition. Content will vary by instructor.

courses.subject: MUS CS
courses.title: CCS Music History
courses.description: Individual or small group instruction in selected topics related to the study of Music History.

courses.subject: MUS CS
courses.title: Snapshots in the History of American Classical Music
courses.description: History of Music in the United States, with a focus on notated traditions. Content will vary by instructor.

courses.subject: MUS CS
courses.title: Fin de Siècle: Music from 1889-1919
courses.description: This course is an historically based exploration of Western Art Music written during the years 1889-1919.

courses.subject: MUS CS
courses.title: The String Quartet
courses.description: A historical survey of string quartet repertory. Content will vary by instructor.

courses.subject: MUS CS
courses.title: Independent Studies
courses.comments: Creative Studies students may enroll in a maximum of 24 units of Independent Studies courses per year, with a total of 45 units counted toward graduation.
courses.description: Serious independent study in music with consenting faculty member.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Short Introduction to Philosophy
courses.description: An introductory course in western philosophy.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Critical Thinking
courses.description: Practical reasoning, argumentation, and the analysis of language as instruments of sound thinking in everyday life.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Introduction to Ethics
courses.description: An examination, at an introductory level, of such ethical issues as: why bemoral, moral relativism, the nature of virtues and vices; and possibly consideration of practical ethical problems such as abortion or war.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Biomedical Ethics
courses.description: An examination of philosophical thinking about moral issues raised by the practice of medicine. Traditional ethical theories and problems will serve as background to, and in turn be illuminated by, such issues as informed consent, paternalism, abortion, euthanasia, and genetic engineering.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: History of Philosophy
courses.description: From Thales to Aristotle.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: History of Philosophy
courses.description: From Medievals to Rationalists.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: History of Philosophy
courses.description: From the Empiricists to Kant.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Ethics
courses.prereq_text: One prior course in philosophy; or, Philosphy 3 (may be taken concurrently)
courses.description: An examination of the fundamental concepts, theories, and problems of moral or political philosophy.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Theory of Knowledge
courses.description: Investigates fundamental questions surrounding the nature of human knowledge and human justification, such as: What do I know? What am I justified in believing? What is it to know something? What is it to hold a justified belief?

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy of Language
courses.description: Introduction to philosophical problems and theories concerning the nature of language. Topics typically include the notion of linguistic structure, theories of meaning and reference, names and descriptions, the relations between languages and thought, necessity and analytic truty, and conversational norms.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy of Mind
courses.description: Discussion of some central questions about the mind: are people identical to their bodies? What is it to feel, believe, or desire something? What distinguishes intelligent thinking from a computer's activities? What is the connection between language and thought?

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Metaphysics
courses.description: Introduction to the philosophical study of the most general and fundamental features of reality. Topics vary, but may include universals, particulars, identity and individuation, substance, the nature of persons, causation, and the nature of time.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Introduction to the Philosophy of Science
courses.prereq_text: One prior course in philosophy; or major in physics, chemistry, or biology.
courses.description: An introduction to the philosophical analysis of the concepts and methods of science, treating such topics as: explanation, confirmation, causation, scientific laws, the interpretation, meaning and reference of scientific theories, theory reduction and theory change, and scientific revolutions.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Meaning and Reference
courses.description: An examination of the classical theories of meaning and reference: John Stuart Mill, Gottlob Frege, Bertrand Russell, and the theory of direct reference. Investigation of solutions to the classical puzzles of meaning and reference.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy of Computing and Artificial Intelligence
courses.prereq_text: A course from PHIL 100A-F, or two prior courses in philosophy.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit up to 8 units with consent of instructor.
courses.description: Advances in artificial intelligence and the widespread use of computers in society confront us with many interesting philosophical questions. What is computation? Is AI really intelligence? Could computers ever think or feel? Is the Turing test a good test? Are we really computers? Are there decisions computers should never make? Do computers threaten our privacy in special ways? Should AI be regulated, and how? We will survey some of the controversies and puzzles that AI has provoked.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Political Philosophy
courses.prereq_text: Major in philosophy, law & society, political science, or global and international studies.
courses.description: Analysis of fundamental political conceptions; the state, sovereignty, political obligation, natural rights, natural law, etc.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy of Science
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit up to 8 units with consent of instructor.
courses.description: What is science? How does it differ from non-science? Course examines both the history of science and the history of philosophy of science in an effort to discover just what science is and what it has to offer.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy of Space and Time
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit up to 8 units with consent of instructor.
courses.description: Is space a thing or a series of relations holding between objects? Does time pass differently for different observers, or in different parts of the universe? Consideration of these and other questions lead to an examination of contemporary physics.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy of Biology
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit up to 8 units with consent of instructor.
courses.description: The biological sciences are distinctively different from the physical sciences. This course will focus on philosophical topics central to biology, such as evolutionary theory and its implications, the proper understanding of concepts such as function, fitness, selection, gene, or the nature of organisms and species.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophical Foundations of Cognitive Science
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit up to 8 units with consent of instructor.
courses.description: What is the mind and how can we model it? Cognitive science offers a distinctive approach to fundamental philosophical questions about the mind. This course begins with the classical foundations of cognitive science and surveys recent developments in the field, including neural networks, theories of embodiment, dynamical systems, and recent statistical approaches to cognition and artificial intelligence.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy and Neuroscience
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit up to 8 units with consent of instructor.
courses.description: The brain is the seat of who we are. This course will focus on topics at the intersection of philosophy and the brain sciences, such as neuroethics, philosophy of neuroscience, representation in the brain, or philosophical and scientific theories of consciousness.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Animal Minds
courses.prereq_text: Philosophy 100D, or two prior courses in philosophy.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit up to 8 units with consent of instructor.
courses.description: The goal of this course is to examine current research in animal cognition with a view to understanding how philosophical and scientific questions about animal minds interact. Topics may include whether nonhuman animals can feel pain; whether they can suffer; whether they have episodic memory; whether they are conscious. We will also consider ethical implications of the answers we find to the above questions.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Social Philosophy
courses.prereq_text: Philosophy 100A; or, two prior courses in philosophy.
courses.description: This course will examine moral problems associated with economic activity; for example, economic justice and the moral basis of property rights.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy of Gender
courses.prereq_text: One course from PHIL 100A-F and one additional course in Philosophy.
courses.description: Philosophical issues involving the concept of gender. Topics may include the distinction between sex and gender, gender and sexuality, theories of gender, gender identity and expression, non-binary and queer genders, and gender subordination and oppression.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Feminist Philosophy
courses.prereq_text: Philosophy 100A; or, two prior courses in philosophy.
courses.description: In this course, we examine philosophical approaches to feminism and feminist issues. Topics covered may include inequality in the workplace and in family structures; global feminism; objectification; pornography; and prostitution.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Freedom and Determinism
courses.prereq_text: Prerequisite: one prior course in philosophy.
courses.description: Determinism is the doctrine that the laws of nature plus the past necessitate the future. Is determinism compatible with the view that we often act freely and are often morally responsible for what we do?

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Applied Ethics.
courses.prereq_text: Philosophy 100A; or, two prior courses in philosophy.
courses.comments: May be repeated with consent of department provided course content is different.
courses.description: Advanced topics in applied ethics, such as the ethics of war; the ethics of procreation; and the ethics of how we treat animals.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: History of Political Thought
courses.prereq_text: Major in philosophy, law & society, political science, or global and international studies.
courses.description: A study of one or more important figures from the history of political thought.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Moral Psychology
courses.prereq_text: Philosophy 4 or 100A; and, Philosophy 100B or 100C or 100D or 100E.
courses.description: An examination of the nature of desires, emotions, the imagination and other aspects of human psychology, and of the ways these bear on the moral evaluation of people and actions.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Contemporary Philosophy
courses.description: Systematic investigation of topics drawn from contemporary analytic or continental philosophy.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Feminist Philosophy
courses.description: Focuses on advanced topics in feminist philosophy, sometimes covering one topic or one author over the course. Content will vary but may include contemporary debates, such as gender, pornography, consent, single authors such as Wollstonecraft, or de Beauvoir, and themes, such as early feminist thinkers, or feminist epistemology.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Normative Ethics
courses.prereq_text: Philosophy 100A; or, two prior courses in philosophy.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units.
courses.description: An examination of what makes actions morally right or wrong and people morally good or bad.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Meta-Ethics
courses.prereq_text: Philosophy 100A; or, two prior courses in philosophy.
courses.description: An examination of problems concerning the meaning and justification of moral judgments.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: History of Ethics
courses.prereq_text: Philosophy 100A; or, two prior courses in philosophy.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units.
courses.description: A study of one or more historically important moral philosophers.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy of Law
courses.description: An introduction to some of the main issues generated by the philosophical question, "What is law?" In what sense is conduct made obligatory by the existence of law? What, if any, is the relationship between law and morals? What are rules? What does it mean to say that a rule exists? Do courts really apply rules or merely pretend to do so?

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Advanced Topics in the Philosophy of Law
courses.prereq_text: Major in philosophy, law & society, political science, or global and international studies.
courses.description: Study of advanced topics in the philosophy of law.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Punishment and Responsibility
courses.description: An examination of some of the philosophical problems of punishment and responsibility: The rationale of punishment and the legal doctrine of Mensrea; the analysis of conditions of responsibility, relations between punishment, responsibility, retribution, guilt, shame, etc.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy in Literature
courses.description: Introduction to major problems at the intersection of philosophy and literature. Issues addressed may include philosophical assessments of literature, authorship and interpretation, truth in fiction, significance of literary works and form for philosophy; texts include imaginative literature and philosophical essays.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Action Theory
courses.prereq_text: One prior course from Philosophy 100B, 100C, 100D, and 100E; or, two prior course in philosophy.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units.
courses.description: An examination of philosophical topics connected with human action, e.g. the role of intentions and desires in the explanation and justification of action and the nature of practical reason.
