courses.title: Advanced Topics in Ethical Theory
courses.prereq_text: Two courses from Philosophy 100A or 100B or 100C or 100D or 100E or 100F.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units with consent of instructor.
courses.description: Advanced topics in ethical theory. Specific subject matter is selected by the instructor and descriptions are available in the department office before each quarter.

courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units with consent of instructor.

courses.title: Kant's Practical Philosophy
courses.prereq_text: Philosophy 100A or two prior courses in Philosophy

courses.title: Hobbes
courses.description: This course examines the philosophy of Thomas Hobbes (1588-1679).

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Frege
courses.prereq_text: Philosophy 183 and another previous course in philosophy.
courses.description: An examination of the work of the German philosopher and logician, Gottlob Frege.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: American Philosophy
courses.description: An examination of the roots and early development of American philosophy with special attention paid to the theory of natural rights, its role in the founding of the nation, and the movement to abolish slavery.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: American Philosophy
courses.description: An examination of the development of American philosophy in the 19th and early 20th century, with special attention paid to Pragmatism (e.g. the philosophical writings of Peirce, James and Dewey) and modifications of the theory of natural rights in response to the Darwinian revolution in biology.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Historical Philosophers
courses.comments: May be repeated with consent of department provided course content is different.
courses.description: Examination of historical philosophers beyond those covered in Philosophy 106 and 151-166.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Beginning Modern Logic
courses.description: An introduction to the concepts and methods of moder symbolic logic. Emphasis is placed on problems of translating english expressions into logical symbols and on the development of skills in using the formal proof procedures of sentential and predicate logic.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Intermediate Modern Logic
courses.description: Further application and development of the predicate calculus, including the calculi of identity and description. An introduction to the metalogical questions of completeness, consistency, and decidability.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Advanced Modern Logic
courses.description: Topics from the theory of formal systems, set theory, recursive function theory, and automata theory.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Theory of Value
courses.description: Study of theories of the nature and structure of the good and of value judgments generally.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy of Love and Sex
courses.prereq_text: Two prior upper-division courses in philosophy.
courses.description: An examination of philosophical theories about the nature and moral significance of romantic love, of sex, and of the relation between the two.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Internship in Philosophy
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing in philosophy; consent of department and instructor
courses.comments: Students must have a 3.0 overall grade-point average. May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units but only 4 units may count toward major.
courses.description: Practical experience and application of analytical skills learned in philosophy as interns with agencies and business. Periodic and final reports required under faculty direction.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Senior Honors Thesis
courses.prereq_text: Enrollment limited to senior honors philosophy majors; by consent of instructor and departmental approval.
courses.comments: Students must have a Philosophy GPA of 3.5 and an overall GPA of 3.3
courses.description: A continuous two-quarter research and writing tutorial designed for senior honors majors. The first term will be spent mainly in selecting and researching a topic for the thesis.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Senior Honors Thesis

courses.description: A continuous two-quarter research and writing tutorial designed for senior honors majors. The second term will be spent mainly in the writing of the thesis.

courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to 8 units with consent of instructor.
courses.description: A research and writing tutorial on some topic relevant to issues in ethics and public policy. A written proposal of the project must be approved by the undergraduate adviser and the instructor.

courses.title: Independent Studies in Philosophy
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division courses in philosophy.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters. Philosophy 199 may be repeated to a maximum of 12 units. No more than 12 units may be applied to the major. Students are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
courses.description: A written statement of the proposed program of study must be presented to the instructor for his or her approval before the student signs up for the course.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Independent Research Assistant
courses.comments: Students must enroll under instructor number and have a minimum 3.0 GPA forthe preceding 3 quarters. Students are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ course combined. Philosophy 199RA may be repeated for credit to a maximum of 5 units.
courses.description: Course work shall consist of faculty supervised research.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Meaning and Reference
courses.description: An examination of the classical theories of meaning and reference: John Stuart Mill, Gottlob Frege, Bertrand Russell, and the theory of direct reference. Solutions to the classical puzzles of meaning and reference are investigated.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy of Computing and Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: Advances in artificial intelligence and the widespread use of computers in society confront us with many interesting philosophical questions. What is computation? Is AI really intelligence? Could computers ever think or feel? Is the Turing test a good test? Are we really computers? Are there decisions computers should never make? Do computers threaten our privacy in special ways? Should AI be regulated, and how? We will survey some of the controversies and puzzles that AI has provoked.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Political Philosophy
courses.description: A study at the graduate level of selected problems in political philosophy.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy of Science
courses.description: What is science? How does it differ from non-science? Course examines both the history of science and the history of philosophy of science in an effort to discover just what science is and what it has to offer.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy of Space and Time
courses.description: Is space a thing or a series of relations holding between objects? Does time pass differently for different observers, or in different parts of the universe? Consideration of these, and other questions leads to an examination of contemporary physics.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy of Biology
courses.description: The biological sciences are distinctively different from the physical sciences. This course will focus on philosophical topics central to biology, such as evolutionary theory and its implications, the proper understanding of concepts such as function, fitness, selection, gene, or the nature of organisms and species.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophical Foundations of Cognitive Science
courses.description: What is the mind and how can we model it? Cognitive science offers a distinctive approach to fundamental philosophical questions about the mind. This course begins with the classical foundations of cognitive science and surveys recent developments in the field, including neural networks, theories of embodiment, dynamical systems, and recent statistical approaches to cognition and artificial intelligence.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy and Neuroscience
courses.description: The brain is the seat of who we are. This course will focus on topics at the intersection of philosophy and the brain sciences, such as neuroethics, philosophy of neuroscience, representation in the brain, or philosophical and scientific theories of consciousness.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Animal Minds
courses.description: The goal of this course is to examine current research in animal cognition with a view to understanding how philosophical and scientific questions about animal minds interact. Topics may include whether nonhuman animals can feel pain; whether they can suffer; whether they have episodic memory; whether they are conscious. We will also consider ethical implications of the answers we find to the above questions.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Topics in Cognitive Science
courses.description: Cognitive science is the interdisciplinary study of how minds work. The project of understanding the mind requires tools drawn from fields that include psychology, computer science, philosophy, linguistics, anthropology, behavioral economics, neuroscience, and even the arts. This course is designed for graduate students from all disciplines wishing to understand the fundamentals of cognitive science. It will introduce you to the major tools and theories from these areas as they relate to the study of the mind. This course is the core requirement of the UCSB graduate emphasis in cognitive science, and It serves as a foundation for continued study in the cognitive sciences.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: The Profession of Academic Philosophy
courses.comments: No unit credit allowed toward degree.
courses.description: Introduces students to the evolving realities of the profession of academic philosophy. It orients students towards success in the Ph.D. program milestones: the qualifying paper, prospectus development, and completion of the dissertation. It also imparts skills that go beyond graduation, such as preparing a CV, crafting a syllabus, delivering research talks, and writing proposals for grants and fellowships. In the course of covering these topics, the class will also provide a forum for students to reflect on issues in academia more broadly. These include pedagogical innovation, work/life balance, the current state of the discipline, the purposes of the university, and how best to support our diverse undergraduate population.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Basic Physics
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 2A or 3A or AP Math AB Exam with a score of 3 or better.
courses.comments: Reduced credit of 2 units will be given to students who have received credit for Physics 20. Not open for credit to students who have completed Physics 20 and Physics 21.
courses.description: Introduction to classical mechanics for students in engineering and the physical sciences. Measurement, units, and foundations of physics; vectors; kinematics; circular motion; forces, mass, and Newton's laws; center of mass; momentum; work and energy; conservation laws; collisions; rotational kinematics.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Basic Physics
courses.prereq_text: Physics 1 with a grade of C- or better; Mathematics 2A-B or 3A-B or AP Math BC exam with a score of 3 or better.
courses.description: Rotational dynamics and angular momentum; equilibrium and elasticity; periodic motion including LRC electrical circuits; gravitation; fluid mechanics; temperature; thermal expansion; heat and the first law of thermodynamics; heat conduction; kinetic theory of gases; entropy and the second law; heat engines.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Basic Physics
courses.prereq_text: Physics 2 with a grade of C- or better; Mathematics 2A-B or 3A-B (AP Math BC Exam score of 3 or better) and 4A.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Physics 23.
courses.description: Mechanical waves, wave interference and normal modes, sound and hearing, electric field, Gauss's law, electric potential, capacitance and dielectrics, current, resistance, electromotive force, DC circuits.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics Laboratory
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Physics 13AH or Physics CS 15A.
courses.description: Introductory laboratory emphasizing periodic motion, sound and basic electronics.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Basic Physics
courses.prereq_text: Physics 3 with a grade of C- or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Physics 24.
courses.description: Magnetic fields, electromagnetic induction and inductance, AC circuits, Maxwell's equations, electromagnetic waves, light and geometrical optics, interference and diffraction.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics Laboratory
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Physics 13BH or Physics CS 15B.
courses.description: Introductory laboratory emphasizing magnetism, circuits and optics.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Basic Physics
courses.prereq_text: Physics 4 with a grade of C- or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Physics 25.
courses.description: Special relativity, blackbody radiation, Compton scattering, photoelectric effect, Bohr model, quantum mechanics, molecules, condensed matter, nuclear physics, elementary particles.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics Laboratory
courses.prereq_text: Physics 4 or 24; and, Physics 5 or 25 (may be taken concurrently).
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Physics 13CH or Physics CS 15C.
courses.description: Introductory laboratory emphasizing atomic spectra, diffraction and basic quantum physics.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Introductory Physics
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 2A or 3A or 34A (may be taken concurrently) or AP Math AB Exam score of 3 or better.
courses.description: Presents concepts and methodologies for understanding physical phenomena, and is particularly useful preparation for upper-division study in the life sciences. Vectors, velocity, acceleration. Newton's laws. Work and energy. Linear momentum. Gravity. Static equilibrium. Rotational motion. Angular momentum.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Introductory Experimental Physics
courses.description: Self directed laboratory course where students seek to discover simple mathematical descriptions of laws governing various physical phenomena. Each student is responsible for deciding what to measure, how to measure it, and what interpretation can be placed on the results.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Introductory Physics
courses.prereq_text: Physics 6A with a minimum grade of C-.
courses.description: Presents concepts and methodologies for understanding physical phenomena, and is particularly useful preparation for upper-division study in the life sciences. Oscillatory motion. Vibrations, waves, sound. Fluids. Electrostatics and DC circuits. Magnetism and magnetic forces. Induction and Faraday's law. AC circuits. If time permits: Heat and thermodynamics.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Introductory Experimental Physics
courses.description: Experiments in the mechanical, electrical and thermal properties of matter,the behavior of light, and quantum phenomena with application to the biological sciences.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Introductory Physics
courses.prereq_text: Physics 6B with a minimum grade of C-.
courses.description: Presents concepts and methodologies for understanding physical phenomena, and is particularly useful preparation for upper-division study in the life sciences. Electromagnetic waves. Geometric optics, optical instruments. Interference and diffraction. Quantum theory of the atom. Nuclear physics. If time permits: Special relativity, elementary particle physics.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Introductory Experimental Physics
courses.description: Experiments in the mechanical, electrical and thermal properties of matter,the behavior of light, and quantum phenomena with application to the biological sciences.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Basic Physics
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 2A or 3A or AP Math AB Exam with a score of 3 or better.
courses.description: Kinematics in 3D, Newton’s Laws, Energy, Momentum and Collisions, Rotation, Statics and Equilibrium

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Basic Physics
courses.prereq_text: Physics 7A with a grade of C- or better; Mathematics 2A-B or 3A-B or AP Math BC exam with a score of 3 or better.
courses.description: Gravity, Periodic Motion and Oscillations, Mechanical Waves and Sound, Coulomb’s Law, Electric Field and Gauss’s Law, Electric Potential, DC circuits

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Basic Physics
courses.prereq_text: Physics 7B with a grade of C- or better; Mathematics 2A-B or 3A-B or AP Math BC exam with a score of 3 or better.
courses.description: Magnetic Forces and Field, Induction, Inductance and AC circuits, Maxwell’s equations and E/M waves, Geometric and Physical Optics

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Basic Physics
courses.prereq_text: Physics 7C with a grade of C- or better; Mathematics 2A-B or 3A-B (AP Math BC Exam score of 3 or better) and 4A.
courses.description: Temperature, Heat, Laws of Thermodynamics, Special Relativity, Photons, Wave-particle duality of Matter, Intro to Quantum Mechanics, Schrodinger Equation in 1D, Hydrogen Atom.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics Laboratory
courses.comments: Physics 3L is the same course as Physics 7L.
courses.description: Periodic motion, sound, and basic electronics, while emphasizing good laboratory techniques such as uncertainty propagation, statistical analysis, developing and testing models, and good report writing.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Introduction to Mathematical Methods for Physics
courses.comments: This course is highly recommended for those students who have not completed AP calculus BC with a score of 5.
courses.description: Single variable functions, derivatives and integrals with applications to kinematics. Taylor series. Introduction to ordinary differential equations and Newtons second law as an ODE. Vectors and scalars with physics applications. Dot and cross products. Matrices and determinants. Unit circle and trigonometric identities. Polar coordinates and kinematics in polar coordinates.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Honors Introduction to Experimental Physics
courses.comments: Quarters usually offered: Fall. Same course as Physics CS 15A. Not open for degree credit to students who have completed Physics 3L, Physics 13AH or Physics CS 15A.
courses.description: Covers the essence of experimental research. Students study three different systems experimentally, and write short Physical Review style articles about the results. Students are responsible for deciding what to measure, how to analyze data, what conclusions can be reached, etc.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Honors Experimental Physics
courses.comments: Not open for degree credit to students who have completed Physics 4L, Physics 13BH or Physics CS 15B.
courses.description: Computer control of experiments. Students learn LabView, and use it to measure and generate analog signals using a data acquisition card and a personal computer. Students ultimately use their computers to measure and control the temperature of a copper rod.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Honors Experimental Physics
courses.comments: Not open for degree credit to students who have completed Physics 5L, Physics 13CH or Physics CS 15C.
courses.description: Design and construction of apparatus, drafting and computer-aided design. Machine shop practice including use of all major machine tools. The class acts as a team to design and, time permitting, build a scientific apparatus for a campus research group.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Experimental Physics
courses.prereq_text: Physics 29 and Physics 23 (may be taken concurrently)
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Physics 3L, Physics 13AH, Physics 13AL or Physics CS 15A.
courses.description: Introduction to Measurement and Experimentation. Basic good practices in note-taking, data collection, data visualization, error estimation, error propagation, curve fitting, and drawing conclusions, all exercised in the context of phenomena from mechanics and electronics.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Experimental Physics
courses.prereq_text: Physics 20AL and Physics 24 (may be taken concurrently).
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Physics 4L, Physics 13BH, Physics 13BL or Physics CS 15B.
courses.description: Introduction to Measurement and Experimentation, continued. Basics of image analysis, technical drawing, additive manufacturing, oscilloscope use, searching and digesting scientific literature, as well as continued practice of skills introduced in 20AL in the context of electromagnetic and optical phenomena.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Experimental Physics
courses.prereq_text: Physics 20BL and Physics 25 (may be taken concurrently).
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Physics 5L, Physics 13CH, Physics 13CL, Physics 25L or Physics CS 15C.
courses.description: Introduction to Measurement and Experimentation, with an emphasis on Scientific Communication and Experimental Design. Searching the scientific literature, reading a scientific paper, proposing and executing a measurement, and formally reporting on a measurement in writing, as well as continued practice of skills introduced in 20AL and 20BL in the context of modern physics phenomena.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: General Physics
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 2A/3A and Mathematics 2B/3B or Physics 8 or AP Calculus BC Exam score of 5.
courses.description: Classical mechanics, kinematics, vectors, Newtons laws, work and energy, conservation laws, rotational kinematics.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: General Physics
courses.prereq_text: Physics 21 with a grade of C- or better.
courses.description: Rotational dynamics, fluid mechanics, gravitation, periodic motion, temperature and heat, thermodynamics.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: General Physics
courses.prereq_text: Physics 22 with a minimum grade of C- or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Physics 3.
courses.description: Mechanical waves, sound, electric charge and electric field, Gauss Law, electric potential, capacitance and dielectrics, current, resistance, electromotive force, DC circuits.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: General Physics
courses.prereq_text: Physics 23 with a minimum grade of C-; Mathematics 4A.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Physics 4.
courses.description: Magnetic fields, electromagnetic induction and inductance, AC circuits, Maxwell's equations, electromagnetic waves, light and geometrical optics, interference and diffraction.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: General Physics
courses.prereq_text: Physics 24 with a minimum grade of C-; Mathematics 6A.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Physics 5.
courses.description: Special relativity, blackbody radiation, Compton scattering, photoelectric effect, Bohr model, quantum mechanics, molecules, condensed matter, nuclear physics, elementary particles.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Introduction to Computer Programming for the Physical Sciences
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 2B or 3B or Physics 8 or AP Calculus BC Exam with a score of 5
courses.description: An introduction to programming and data analysis for the physical sciences. Topics include syntax, goodcoding practice, basic algorithmic structure, plotting, basic data analysis, numerical root-finding and integration.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Readings in Physics
courses.comments: May be repeated to a maximum of 6 units. Students must have a minimum 3.0 cumulative GPA and are limited to 3 units per quarter and 30 units total in 98/99/198/199/199DC/199RA courses combined. No more than 12 units may be earned in all Physics 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
courses.description: Critical reviews and discussions of selected physics subjects, conducted under the supervision of a Physics faculty member.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Introduction to Physics Research
courses.comments: May be repeated to a maximum of 6 units. Students must have a minimum 3.0 cumulative GPA and are limited to 3 units per quarter and 30 units total in 98/99/198/199/199DC/199RA courses combined. No more than 12 units may be earned in all Physics 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
courses.description: Independent research conducted under the guidance of a Physics faculty member. Topic and scope varies, to be specified by student and supervisory faculty member prior to registration.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Methods of Theoretical Physics
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 6B with a grade of C- or better.
courses.description: Linear Algebra: Vector spaces, operators, spectral decomposition. Topics may include Sturm-Liouville equations, special functions. Fourier series and Fourier transforms, Dirac delta-function.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Methods of Theoretical Physics
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 5C or 6B with a grade of C- or better.
courses.description: Analytic functions, contour integrals and branch cuts. Conformal mapping. Laplace transforms. Asymptotic series and the gamma function. Greens functions.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Intermediate Mechanics and Special Relativity
courses.prereq_text: Physics 2 or 22 with a minimum grade of C-. Mathematics 6A (may be taken concurrently)
courses.description: Newtonian mechanics in 3D. Conservation laws. Complex numbers. Oscillations. Inertial reference frames, Lorentz transformations, relativistic momentum and energy, four-vectors.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Advanced Mechanics
courses.prereq_text: Physics 103 with a grade of C- or better.
courses.description: Calculus of variations. Lagrangian and Hamiltonian mechanics. Central force problems and collision theory. Non-inertial reference frames. Coupled oscillations and waves.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Nonlinear Phenomena
courses.prereq_text: Physics 105A or Physics 103; or ME 163 or upper-division standing in ECE.
courses.comments: Same course as ME 169 and Physics 106. Not open for credit to students who have completed ECE 163C.
courses.description: Introduction to nonlinear phenomena. Flows and bifurcations in one and two dimensions, chaos, fractals, strange attractors. Applications to physics, engineering, chemistry, and biology.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Electromagnetism
courses.prereq_text: Physics 5 or 25 with a minimum grade of C-; Mathematics 6B with minimum grade of C-.
courses.description: Electrostatics, Laplace's equation, method of images, separation of variables, multipole expansion, magnetostatics, electric and magnetic fields in matter.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Electromagnetism
courses.prereq_text: Physics 110A with a minimum grade of C-.
courses.description: Electrodynamics, Maxwells equations, conservation laws, electromagnetic waves, potentials and fields for moving charges, radiation, special relativity.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Quantum Mechanics
courses.prereq_text: Physics 5 or 25 and Physics 100A with a minimum grade of C-.
courses.description: The postulates of quantum mechanics, the Schrdinger equation and its consequences, the quantum harmonic oscillator and other one dimensional quantum systems, Hilbert Space and Dirac notation, the hydrogen atom.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Quantum Mechanics
courses.prereq_text: Physics 115A with a minimum grade of C-.
courses.description: Spin and angular momentum, Clebsch-Gordan coefficients, identical particles, symmetries and conservation laws, time independent perturbation theory.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Quantum Mechanics
courses.prereq_text: Physics 115B with a minimum grade of C-.
courses.description: The variational principle, time dependent perturbation theory, the adiabatic theorem. Topics from: WKB approximation, the Dirac equation, Berrys phase, Bells inequality, quantum cryptography, quantum computation.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Group Theory for Physicists
courses.description: The emphasis is on developing some intuition about the role of symmetries in physics, rather than going through rigorous mathematical proofs. Theorems will be proved at the level of rigor customary among physicists.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Thermal and Statistical Physics
courses.prereq_text: PHYS 22 and MATH 6B with a minimum grade of C-
courses.description: Principles of statistical physics, entropy, large numbers, thermodynamic principles, microcanonical ensemble, ideal gas, free energy, chemical potential, selected applications. Canonical ensemble, if time permits.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Thermal and Statistical Physics
courses.prereq_text: Physics 115A and Physics 119A with a minimum grade of C-.
courses.description: Canonical ensemble and partition functions, grand canonical ensemble, quantum statistics, Fermi-Dirac, Bose-Einstein distribution laws. Topics from: Brownian motion, Langevin equation, dissipation and fluctuations, elementary kinetic theory, weakly interacting gases or mean field theory of magnetism, other topics illustrative of the breadth of the subject and/or selected applications.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics of California Waves, Weather, Quakes and Fires
courses.description: Why do the waves hit the beach every five seconds? This course teaches students the relevant fluid dynamics and allows them to apply it to natural phenomena of California: seismic waves, tsunamis, maximum tree heights, fluid flow around fish.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Condensed Matter Physics
courses.prereq_text: Physics 115A with at least a C- or better, and upper-division standing.
courses.description: Classification of solids; crystal symmetry; thermal, electronic, and magnetic properties of metals, semiconductors, and insulators; band theory of electronic states; wave scattering by crystals; semiconductor devices.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Condensed Matter Physics
courses.prereq_text: Physics 115B with a minimum grade of C-.
courses.description: Tight binding model, topological insulator, magnetism, phase transition, introduction to superconductivity.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Elementary Particle Physics
courses.description: Introduction to quarks and leptons and the phenomenology of the particles they comprise; fundamental symmetries, invariance principles, and the associated quantum numbers, strong, electromagnetic, and weak interactions and their relationship.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Laboratory Optics
courses.prereq_text: Physics 24 or 7C with a grade of C- or better, Physics 29 with a grade of C- or better, and Mathematics 6B with a grade of C- or better
courses.description: An introduction to optical phenomena and the methods and instrumentation used to generate, measure, and manipulate light. Experiments will cover imaging and aberrations, coherence, diffraction, interference, interferometry, Fourier optics, reflection and polarization, spectroscopy, lasers, fiber optics, and optical instruments.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Analog Electronics
courses.prereq_text: Physics 13CL or 20CL and Math 3B with a minimum grade of C-.
courses.description: Passive circuits, diodes, transistors, field effect transistors, operational amplifiers, feedback and control. Design, building and testing of analog circuits.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Digital Electronics
courses.prereq_text: Physics 127AL with a minimum grade of C-.
courses.description: Gates, combinational and sequential logic, ?multiplexers, counters, shift registers, memory and microprocessors. Design, building and testing of digital circuitry, including a modern microprocessor based computer system.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Advanced Experimental Physics
courses.prereq_text: Physics 13CL or Physics 20CL or Physics CS 15C. Physics 115A (may be taken concurrently).
courses.description: Selected experiments in physics, i.e. saturated absorption spectroscopy, muon lifetime measurements, pulsed nuclear magnetic resonance, Mossbauer effect. Develop skills in detailing observations in a scientific notebook, data collection and error analysis, operating complex physical apparatus, and scientific communication.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Introduction to Scientific Computation
courses.prereq_text: Physics 5 or 25 with a grade of C- or better, and Mathematics 6B with a grade of C- or better; Physics 29 with a grade of C- or better.
courses.comments: Not open to graduate students.
courses.description: A survey of computers, programming, and computational techniques for the natural sciences. Physical foundations of computation, binary arithmetic, computer architecture, programming languages, operating systems, UNIX shell and filesystems. Programming tools, variables and data structures, expressions, control flow, files, functions and scoping, objects, error handling, debugging, graphics, text processing, networking, data acquisition and transfer. Mathematics and algorithms for data processing and analysis, numerical methods, random numbers and simulation.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Gravitation and Relativity
courses.prereq_text: Physics 103-104 with a minimum grade of C- in each.
courses.comments: Physics 104 may be taken concurrently with consent of instructor
courses.description: An introduction to Einstein's general relativity, the spacetime of special relativity, the principle of equivalence, gravity as geometry, the description of spacetime geometry, the spacetime of a relativistic star, solar system test of general relativity, gravitational collapse, black holes, cosmology.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Stellar Structure and Evolution
courses.prereq_text: Physics 5 or 25 or 115A with a minimum grade of C-.
courses.description: Observed properties and classification of stars, the Hertzsprung-Russell diagram, stellar atmospheres, hydrostatic equilibrium, energy transport, equations of state, thermonuclear reaction rates, origin of the elements, life history of stars, stellar death, compact objects, star formation.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Cosmology
courses.prereq_text: Physics 5 or 25 or 115A with a minimum grade of C-.
courses.description: The geometry, contents and evolution of the universe as a whole. The empirical and theoretical foundations for the Big Bang, the Hubble expansion, Friedmann models, dark matter, dark energy, the thermal history of the universe, the origin of the light elements, the cosmic microwave background, reionization, and structure formation.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Observational Astrophysics
courses.prereq_text: Physics 5 or 25 or 115A with a minimum grade of C-.
courses.description: Techniques and implementation of observational methods in astronomy/astrophysics. Sensors, digital-image processing and analysis, research projects with computer-controlled remote access telescope using a digital image sensor. Studies of variable stars, galaxy morphology, supernovae, etc.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Biophysics and Biomolecular Materials
courses.comments: Same course as Materials 135.
courses.description: Structure and function of cellular molecules (lipids, nucleic acids, proteins, and carbohydrates). Genetic engineering techniques of molecular biology. Biomolecular materials and biomedical applications (e.g., bio-sensors, drug delivery systems, gene carrier systems).

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Galaxies
courses.prereq_text: Physics 2 or 22 with a minimum grade of C-, Physics 104 (may be taken concurrently)
courses.description: The distribution of mass in galaxies, orbits of stars, Boltzmann equation, Jeans theorem, spiral structure & density waves, dynamics of star clusters, galaxy collisions, dynamical friction, gas dynamics, sound & shock waves, gas inflow & accretion, gas outflow & winds.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Planets and Exoplanets
courses.prereq_text: Physics 5 or 25 or 115A with a minimum grade of C-, Physics 104 (may be taken concurrently)
courses.description: An introduction to planets both in and out of the solar system. This course will provide a broad overview of planets in the solar system, the techniques used to detect planets outside the solar system, and demographics and characteristics of exoplanets.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Soft Matter Physics
courses.description: A physics-based approach to study the structure, assembly and dynamical properties of a variety of soft materials, such as simple and complex fluids, colloidal systems, liquid crystals, polymers, granular matter and gels, including biological examples. Topics covered include elasticity, viscosity and viscoelasticity, capillarity and wetting, phases and phase diagrams of soft materials, entropy-driven phase transitions, Brownian motion and active matter.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physical Biology of the Cell
courses.description: The role of physics in biology through quantitative measurements and modeling, the organization of a cell, and exemplary quantitative results of biological model systems. The physics of biologically relevant macromolecules, including DNA, RNA and mechanisms of transcription and translation; introduction to protein folding and the role of electrostatics in biology. The physics of the cytoskeleton including beam theory, persistence length, molecular motors, instrumentation used to characterize motor properties, as well as the role of active stresses in cell biology. If time permits, a brief introduction to cell motility and the structure of epithelial tissue.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Optics
courses.prereq_text: Physics 110B with a minimum grade of C-.
courses.description: Modern geometrical and physical optics. Polarization, coherence, interference, and diffraction phenomena. Fourier transform spectroscopy, intensity correlation interferometry, spatial filtering, and holography. Selected topics on lasers, light scattering, and quantum optics as time permits.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Experimental Research in Condensed Matter Physics
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit.
courses.description: Offers qualified undergraduates the opportunity to work in research laboratories in condensed matter physics.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Experimental Research in Elementary Particle Physics
courses.prereq_text: Physics 5 or 25; and consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit.
courses.description: Offers qualified under graduates the opportunity to work in experimental research in elementary particle physics.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Experimental Research in Biophysics
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit.
courses.description: Offers qualified undergraduates the opportunity to work in research laboratories in biophysics.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Experimental Research in Astrophysics
courses.prereq_text: Physics 5 or 25; and consent of instructor.
courses.description: Offers qualified undergraduates the opportunity to work in experimental research in astrophysics. Each staff member has his/her own course identified by a number listed in the schedule of classes.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Special Topics in Physics
courses.description: Course varies from year to year according to the current interests.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Science for the Public
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units, but only 4 units may be applied to the major. Same course as Engineering 160. Open to graduate students in science and engineering disciplines and to undergraduate science and engineering majors.
courses.description: Provides experience in communicating science and technology to nonspecialists. The major components of the course are field work in mentoring, a biweekly seminar, presentations to precollege students and to adult nonscientists, and end-of-term research papers.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Teaching and Learning Physics
courses.comments: Required for Physics Education Concentration
courses.description: Introduction to basic concepts in education literature and learning theory. The course involves readings of articles and text drawn from general and Physics education research and cognitive science. Students will engage in discussions and reflective activities that apply and relate the ideas from the readings to their own classroom experiences to help them become more effective teachers and learners.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Atomic Physics
courses.description: An introduction to atomic physics. Covers basic atomic structure of one and two valence electron atoms, the Zeeman effect, and the semiclassical treatment of atoms interacting with near-resonant light. We also discuss laser cooling and trapping, as well as selected advanced topics such as atomic clocks, trapped ion dynamics, and the application of atoms in quantum information science.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Directed Reading
courses.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division courses in physics.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in 98/99/198/199/199DC/199RA courses combined. No more than 12 units may be earned in all Physics 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
courses.description: Each staff member has own directed reading course identified by a number code listed in the schedule of classes.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Research in Physics
courses.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division courses in physics.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in 98/99/198/199/199DC/199RA courses combined. No more than 12 units may be earned in all Physics 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined in the major.
courses.description: Directed individual study open to qualified seniors in the department. Each staff member has own independent studies course identified by a number code listed in the schedule of classes.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Independent Research Assistance
courses.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division courses in physics.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in 98/99/198/199/199DC/199RA courses combined. No more than 12 units may be earned in all Physics 198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
courses.description: Undergraduate research for qualified seniors to gain valuable experience in research methodology.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Classical Mechanics
courses.description: Review of lagrangian mechanics. Variational principles. Hamilton's equations. Canonical transformations. Hamilton Jacobi theory. Action angle variables. Time dependent and canonical perturbation theory. Central forcesand scattering. Small vibrations. Rigid body motion. Poincare maps. Non-integrable systems. Hamiltonian and dissipative chaos.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Electromagnetic Theory
courses.description: Electrostatics, magnetostatics, boundary value problems, time varying fields, Maxwell's equations, radiation, multipole fields, scattering, relativistic particle dynamics.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Electromagnetic Theory
courses.description: Electrostatics, magnetostatics, boundary value problems, time varying fields, Maxwell's equations, radiation, multipole fields, scattering, relativistic particle dynamics.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Quantum Mechanics
courses.description: Fundamental principles; Schroedinger equation; angular momentum; perturbation theory; scattering theory, emission, and absorption of radiation; Dirac equation.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Quantum Mechanics
courses.description: Fundamental principles; Schroedinger equation; angular momentum; perturbation theory; scattering theory, emission, and absorption of radiation; Dirac equation.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Quantum Mechanics
courses.description: Fundamental principles; Schroedinger equation; angular momentum; perturbation theory; scattering theory, emission, and absorption of radiation; Dirac equation.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: The Many Body Problem in Condensed Matter Physics
courses.description: Field theoretic methods as applied to (non-relativistic) condensed matter systems. Green's functions and diagrammatic techniques applied to various examples of interacting many body systems, including fermions, bosons, and spins. Relationship of theoretical quantities to physical measurements.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: The Many Body Problem in Condensed Matter Physics
courses.description: Field theoretic methods as applied to (non-relativistic) condensed matter systems. Green's functions and diagrammatic techniques applied to various examples of interacting many body systems, including fermions, bosons, and spins. Relationship of theoretical quantities to physical measurements.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Statistical Mechanics
courses.prereq_text: Physics 205, 215A, and 119B or equivalent taken at another institution.
courses.description: Fundamental principles of classical and quantum statistics. Non-interacting Boltzmann, Bose, and Fermi systems. Virial expansion and other approaches to interacting systems. Phase transitions.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Statistical Mechanics
courses.description: Course will cover some of the following topics: A) critical phenomena-phase diagrams, first and second order phase transitions, scalingtheory, high-temperature expansions, renormalization group; B) nonequilibrium statistical mechanics-stochastic processes. Langevin equations, fluctuation-dissipation theorem, master equations, fluid dynamics.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Relativistic Quantum Field Theory
courses.prereq_text: Physics 205, Physics 210A, Physics 210B, Physics 215A, Physics 215B, and Physics 215C; or consent of instructor.
courses.description: Introduction to the theory of Lorentz covariant quantized fields. Global and local conservation laws. Path integral formulation. Applications to quantum electrodynamics, quantum chromodynamics, and electroweak interactions. Other possible topics include grand unification, the renormalization group, anomolies, current algebra and supersymmetry.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Relativistic Quantum Field Theory
courses.description: Introduction to the theory of Lorentz covariant quantized fields. Global and local conservation laws. Path integral formulation. Applications to quantum electrodynamics, quantum chromodynamics, and electroweak interactions. Other possible topics include grand unification, the renormalization group, anomolies, current algebra and supersymmetry.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Relativistic Quantum Field Theory
courses.description: Introduction to the theory of Lorentz covariant quantized fields. Global and local conservation laws. Path integral formulation. Applications to quantum electrodynamics, quantum chromodynamics, and electroweak interactions. Other possible topics include grand unification, the renormalization group, anomolies, current algebra and supersymmetry.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Concepts and Phenomena of Condensed Matter Physics
courses.description: Lattice and electron dynamics. Elementary excitations and collective phenomena. Transport properties. Disorder and localization. Long-range order and broken symmetries. Magnetism, superconductivity and liquid crystals. Properties and structures of polymers, membranes, and self-assembling systems.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Concepts and Phenomena of Condensed Matter Physics
courses.description: Lattice and electron dynamics. Elementary excitations and collective phenomena. Transport properties. Disorder and localization. Long-range order and broken symmetries. Magnetism, superconductivity and liquid crystals. Properties and structures of polymers, membranes, and self-assembling systems.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Concepts and Phenomena of Condensed Matter Physics
courses.description: Lattice and electron dynamics. Elementary excitations and collective phenomena. Transport properties. Disorder and localization. Long-range order and broken symmetries. Magnetism, superconductivity and liquid crystals. Properties and structures of polymers, membranes, and self-assembling systems.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Elementary Particle Physics
courses.description: The phenomenology of the standard model of particle physics. QED and QCD process.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Elementary Particle Physics
courses.description: Weak interactions; neutrino physics; C, P, and CP violation; electroweak gauge theory and symmetry breaking. Design of detectors and experiments; searches for new phenomena.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Statistical Techniques in Particle Physics
courses.prereq_text: None for graduate students. Consent of the instructor for undergraduates students.
courses.description: Bayesian and Frequentist approaches. Probability distributions used in particle physics. Hypothesis testing. Data fitting. Limit extractions. Confidence/credible intervals. Monte Carlo methods. Applications to realistic problems from current research.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Atomic and Molecular Physics
courses.prereq_text: Physics 215A and Phys 210A; or the consent of the instructor.
courses.description: A survey of major topics in modern atomic physics. Topics in atomic structure include general features of atomic spectra, fine structure, hyperfine structure, the Lamb shift, hydrogen, helium, alkali atoms, complex atoms, excited states, and synthetic atoms. Topics in atom-field interactions and atom atom interactions include the DC Stark effect, the Zeeman effect, transitions, two-level systems, stimulated and spontaneous emission, selection rules, lifetimes, line shapes, broadening mechanisms, the AC Stark effect, multiphoton processes, scattering channels, and Feshbach resonances. Also coversmodern techniques including spectroscopy, laser cooling, atom traps, quantum gases, cold molecules, trapped ions, and atomic clocks.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Gauge Theories of Elementary Particles
courses.description: Quantum theory of non-abelian gauge fields. Local, global, and spontaneous symmetry breaking. Collective phenomena; solitons, instantons, and magnetic monopoles. Effective field theories. Lattice gauge theory. applications to the standard model of elementary particles.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Gauge Theories of Elementary Particles
courses.description: Quantum theory of non-abelian gauge fields. Local, global, and spontaneous symmetry breaking. Collective phenomena; solitons, instantons, and magnetic monopoles. Effective field theories. Lattice gauge theory. Applications to the standard model of elementary particles.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: String Theory
courses.description: Introduction to string theory. Bosonic and super string theories and their spectra. String perturbation theory and conformal field theory. Nonlinear sigma models and spacetime structure. String compactifications and unification of forces. Non-perturbative results and methods; dualities and branes.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: String Theory
courses.description: Introduction to string theory. Bosonic and super string theories and their spectra. String perturbation theory and conformal field theory. Nonlinear sigma models and spacetime structure. String compactifications and unification of forces. Non-perturbative results and methods; dualities and branes.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: General Relativity
courses.description: Gravity as geometry, differential geometry, Einstein's equation, relativistic stars, gravitational collapse, black holes, cosmology, gravitational radiation, and special topics.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: General Relativity
courses.description: Gravity as geometry, differential geometry, Einstein's equation, relativistic stars, gravitational collapse, black holes, cosmology, gravitational radiation, and special topics.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: General Relativity
courses.comments: May be repeated with consent of instructor.
courses.description: Gravity as geometry, differential geometry, Einstein's equation, relativistic stars, gravitational collapse, black holes, cosmology, gravitational radiation, and special topics.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Stellar Structure and Evolution
courses.description: Physics of stellar structure, equations of state and heat transport. Birth of stars and physics of brown dwarfs. Thermonuclear burning and main sequence stellar structure. Evolution of stars and mass loss. Origin, physical structure, and cooling of compact objects.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: The Interstellar Medium
courses.description: Physical processes that regulate the state of diffuse gas in and around galaxies: Ionization and thermal equilibrium; absorption line studies; spectral line formation; properties of dust grains and extinction; molecular gas and star formation; supernova explosions and hydrodynamic shocks.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: High Energy Astrophysics
courses.description: Accretion power in a range of astrophysical contexts, from quasars to galactic black holes. Rapid release of thermonuclear energy, Type I X-ray bursts, classical novae, Type Ia supernovae. Relativistic jets from black holes, non-thermal radiation processes, physics of gamma-ray bursts.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Extragalactic Astrophysics
courses.description: Nebular astrophysics, active galactic nuclei, supermassive black holes, galaxies, clusters, dark matter, gravitational lensing, the intergalactic medium and galaxy formation.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Cosmology
courses.description: Friedmann models, distance measures, cosmological parameters, thermal history of the universe, cosmological density fields, structure formation (top-hat model, Press-Schechter), big bang nucleosynthesis, cosmic microwave background.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Galactic Dynamics
courses.description: Stellar dynamics, Jeans equations, potential theory, orbit theory, linear stability analysis, kinetic theory, dynamical friction, applications to star clusters, galaxy morphology and mergers.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Soft Matter Physics
courses.comments: IQB 238 and Physics 238 are the same course.
courses.description: A physics-based approach to study the structure, assembly and dynamical properties of a variety of soft materials, such as simple and complex fluids, colloidal systems, liquid crystals, polymers, granular matter and gels, including biological examples. Topics covered will include elasticity, viscosity and viscoelasticity, capillarity and wetting, phases and phase diagrams of soft materials, entropy-driven phase transitions, Brownian motion and active matter.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physical Biology of the Cell
courses.comments: PHYS 239 and IQB 239 are the same course.
courses.description: The role of physics in biology through quantitative measurements and modeling, the organization of a cell, and exemplary quantitative results of biological model systems. The physics of biologically relevant macromolecules, including DNA, RNA and mechanisms of transcription and translation; introduction to protein folding and the role of electrostatics in biology. The physics of the cytoskeleton including beam theory, persistence length, molecular motors, instrumentation used to characterize motor properties, as well as the role of active stresses in cell biology. If time permits, a brief introduction to cell motility and the structure of epithelial tissue.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Statistics, Data Analysis, and Machine Learning for Physicists
courses.description: A survey of statistical and machine learning techniques as applied in modern physics research, with extensive applications to real data. Some of the topics covered include Bayesian and frequentist approaches to statistics; formulating and integrating likelihood functions; confidence intervals with and without assumptions of Gaussianity; Markov Chain Monte Carlo; principal component analysis and dimensionality reduction; Gaussian process regression; and time series analysis. Assignments will make use of published research and data sets, and will require the application of analysis techniques covered in class.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Special Topics in Physics
courses.comments: Course may be repeated with a different topic.
courses.description: The course varies from year to year according to current interests.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Colloquium
courses.description: Colloquium.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Graduate Seminar
courses.description: Weekly seminar on topics of research currently being pursued in the department of physics.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics Outreach
courses.description: Active participation in an outreach program that presents physics demonstrations and experiments on the road to local schools in order to provide a valuable learning experience for K-12 students.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Teaching Assistant Seminar
courses.comments: No unit credit allowed toward advanced degrees. Required course for all teaching assistants.
courses.description: Covers development of teaching techniques especially oriented to lower-division physics laboratory instruction. Theoretical aspects covered at beginning of each quarter. Practical techniques discussed including weekly meeting with class instructor, formal evaluation, and videotaping analysis.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Special seminar on research subjects of current interest. Each staff memberhas a seminar identified by a number code listed in the schedule of classes.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Group Studies
courses.description: Each staff member has a group studies course identified by a number code listed in the schedule of classes.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Directed Reading and Research
courses.description: Individual tutorial. Reading and research in special topics including work done as the basis for the dissertation. Each staff member has a directed reading and research course identified by a number code listed in the schedule of classes.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Dissertation Preparation
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit up to 12 units.
courses.description: This course is reserved for writing the dissertation. Each staff member has a research course identified by a number code listed in the schedule ofclasses.

courses.subject: PHYS CS
courses.title: Group Studies
courses.description: Student-directed discussion and study in a variety of subjects within Physics.

courses.subject: PHYS CS
courses.title: Introduction to Experimental Physics
courses.prereq_text: Physics CS 31; consent of instructor; Creative Studies and CCS Physics majors only.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Physics 3HL or 13AH.
courses.description: Covers the essence of experimental research. Students study three different systems experimentally, and write short Physical Review style articles about the results. Students are responsible for deciding what to measure, how to analyze data, and what conclusions can be reached.

courses.subject: PHYS CS
courses.title: Experimental Physics
courses.prereq_text: Physics CS 15A; consent of instructor; Creative Studies and CCS Physics majors only.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Physics 4HL or 13BH.
courses.description: Computer control of experiments. Students learn LabView, and use it to measure and generate analog signals using a data acquisition card and a personal computer. Students ultimately use their computers to measure and control the temperature of a copper rod.

courses.subject: PHYS CS
courses.title: Experimental Physics
courses.prereq_text: Physics CS 15B; consent of instructor; Creative Studies and CCS Physics majors only.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Physics 5HL or 13CH.
courses.description: Design and construction of apparatus, drafting and computer-aided design. Machine shop practice including use of all major machine tools. The class acts as a team to design and, time permitting, build a scientific apparatus for a campus research group.

courses.subject: PHYS CS
courses.title: Newtonian Mechanics
courses.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; creative studies majors only.
courses.description: Vectors. Kinematics. Newton's laws of motion. Work and energy. Conservativeforces. Momentum. Conservation of momentum. Center of mass motion. Collisions. Systems with variable mass.

courses.subject: PHYS CS
courses.title: Mechanics and Waves
courses.description: Oscillatory motion. Rotational Motion. Angular momentum gravity and centralforce motion. Elastic waves.

courses.subject: PHYS CS
courses.title: Waves, Kinetic Theory and Relativity
courses.prereq_text: Physics CS 31 and 32; consent of instructor.
courses.description: Sound waves. Fluid dynamics. Kinetic theory of matter. The Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution. Specific heat. Entropy. The special theory of relativity.

courses.subject: PHYS CS
courses.title: Electromagnetism
courses.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; creative studies majors only.
courses.description: Electrostatics. DC circuits. Magnetostatics. Vector Potential.

courses.subject: PHYS CS
courses.title: Electromagnetics and Optics
courses.prereq_text: Physics CS 34; consent of instructor; creative studies majors only.
courses.description: Faraday's Law of Induction. Magnetic materials. AC circuits. Maxwell's equations. Electromagnetic waves. Ray optics. Wave optics. Diffraction Theory.

courses.subject: PHYS CS
courses.title: Quantum Physics
courses.prereq_text: Physics CS 34 and 35; consent of instructor; creative studies majors only.
courses.description: Wave-particle duality. Photons. Matter waves. The Uncertainty Principle. The Schrodinger Equation. Potential wells and barriers. The quantized simple harmonic oscillator. The hydrogen atom.

courses.subject: PHYS CS
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Lectures on a coherent body of physical topics which are not usually presented in standard undergraduate physics courses.

courses.subject: PHYS CS
courses.title: Special Topics - Tensor Analysis
courses.description: Lectures on a coherent body of physical topics which are not usually presented in standard undergraduate physics courses. Tensor Analysis course focuses on Special Relativity & flat spacetime, and General Relativity & curved spacetime.

courses.subject: PHYS CS
courses.title: Topics in Physics: Vector Analysis with Application to Physics
courses.description: Subjects include: Functions of more than one variable, double integrals, Divergence Theorem, Curl of a Vector function, Stokes' Theorem, and more.

courses.subject: PHYS CS
courses.title: Independent Studies
courses.comments: Creative Studies students may enroll in a maximum of 24 units of Independent Studies course per year, with a maximum of 45 units counted toward graduation.
courses.description: Serious independent study in physics with consenting faculty member.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Introduction to Political Philosophy
courses.description: An introduction to central texts and problems of political philosophy with an emphasis on such concepts as liberty, equality, authority, justice, and obligation.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Introduction to Comparative Politics
courses.description: Introduction to the workings of various political systems with an emphasis on governmental institutions and political processes. Comparison of political systems using some of the basic concepts of political analysis.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Introduction to International Relations
courses.description: An introduction to the basic concepts, theories, and problems of international relations; balance of power, deterrence, the states system, imperialism, realism, idealism, levels of explanation, war and peace.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: American Government and Politics
courses.description: Political ideas, institutions, and processes of American government. The role of congress and the president in policy formation and of the supreme court in interpreting the constitution.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Introduction to Research in Political Science
courses.comments: Designed for majors. Quarters usually offered: Winter, Spring, Summer, Fall. Not open to students who have completed Political Science 104, 104A and 104AL.
courses.description: An introduction to the design and evaluation of political research, from formulating clear questions and gathering appropriate data, to the use of simple statistical techniques for analyzing data and presenting evidence.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Introduction to Research
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
courses.description: Independent research under the guidance of a faculty member in the department. Course offers exceptional students the opportunity to undertake independent research or work in a research group.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Causal Inference in Political Science
courses.prereq_text: POLS 15; or COMM 87 & COMM 88; or PSTAT5A & COMM 88.
courses.comments: POLS 106CI was replaced by POLS 103, and is the same course.
courses.description: This course is about what quantitative political scientists do when they can’t do experiments. You will learn more about when and how political scientists make causal statements about observational data. We will start by reviewing the promise and pitfalls of experiments as a tool for political scientists. Then, we will think about a series of other approaches that political scientists use to tease apart cause and effect in their work.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Special Topics in Political Science
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Lectures in special areas of interest in political science. Specific course titles to be announced by the department each quarter offered.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: American Political Development
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: This reading-intensive course examines the evolution of American political institutions, policies, and ideas. It will consider the interplay between constitutional design, social movements, economic forces, and cultural shifts, from the colonial period to the present.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: American Indian Politics
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: American Indian tribes play a significant role in the contemporary American political system. This is true at the national, state, and local levels. From a historical perspective, interactions between tribes and settler governments also shaped many of the governing institutions in the United States. This class examines the influence of American Indian tribes and their evolving relationship with federal and state governments. Issues and concepts covered include colonization, economic development, resource and environment, tribal sovereignty, assimilation, stereotypes, and American political development. This class is both focused on historical change and contemporary issues.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Special Topics: African American Politics
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Lectures in special areas of interest in political science. Specific course titles to be announced by the department each quarter offered.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: American Social Movements
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Designed to teach students on the social origins and political impact of American social movements on the left and right. We explore the individual, social psychological, and institutional dynamics of movements.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Black Political Thought
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Takes as a point of departure the push for equality among the Black community in the Black community. It surveys the various strategies and approaches undertaken by Black thought leaders toward that end.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Climate Change and Conflict
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: In this course we will learn about how climate change creates conflict around the globe. We will focus on conflict within civil wars and other forms of intrastate violence. Climate change is the single most important long-term threat to the peace and stability of the planet. The conflicts of the sort we look at in this class may be the most important short-term threat. Are they linked? If so, how? By the end of this class, you will be prepared to answer these questions. We will begin by looking the idea of climate change itself, to make sure we understand what exactly that concept means. Next, we will overview conflict and its causes. After that, we will analyze the debates in the academic literature about climate conflict linkages.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Special Topics in Political Science: Causal Inference
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Lectures in special areas of interest in political science. Specific coursetitles to be announced by the department each quarter offered.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Climate Change Law
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Examines the legal frameworks and policies that shape the fight against climate change. It examines key international agreements, federal and state regulations, and economic instruments designed to address climate change. The course also addresses the legal tensions between environmental goals and economic interests, as well as the challenges of enforcing climate change regulations at different levels of government. Through case studies and discussions, students will develop a deeper understanding of how legal systems are adapting to the evolving climate crisis and the role of law in promoting effective and equitable climate protection.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Legislative Politics - US Congress
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: This course will examine the nomination and election of congressmen, constituent relationships, the development of the institution, formal and informal structures, leadership, comparisons of House with Senate, lobbying, and relationship with the executive branch.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: International Relations in Culture
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Explores cultural explanations of international relations with a particular focus on how pop culture contributes to the outbreak of violence. Students will gain an in-depth understanding of how culture and politics interacts, and apply these ideas to current politics.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Special Topics: Democracy and Inequality
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Lectures in special areas of interest in political science. Specific course titles to be announced by the department each quarter offered.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Northeast Asian Politics
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Consider the possibility of an Asian Century and the role that Northeast Asia might play in making that possible, or alternatively in hindering it. The course material and lectures will provide the advanced undergraduate with an introduction to the postwar political and economic developments and regional interrelationships between the major countries of Northeast Asia: China, North Korea, South Korea and Japan.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Climate Politics and Justice
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: How do political issues shape environmental quality in the Global South? Why have some governments been more successful in reducing environmental degradation than others? How do climate change and other forms of environmental degradation impact local communities? In this course, we explore the causes and impacts of environmental degradation, with emphasis on their unequal distribution across and within countries. We also analyze the political obstacles and opportunities to implement successful and equitable environmental policies. Topics include the energy transition, air and water pollution, land use and deforestation, the impact of extractive industries, and environmental justice.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Comparative Political Economy of the Energy Transition
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Using a comparative analysis, the course examines the political economy of the transition to new forms of energy across the world.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Global Indigenous Politics
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: This course explores the contemporary politics of Indigenous Peoples and settler societies. It takes a sociological, legal, political, and anthropological approach to how politics operate within and around Indigenous Peoples. By adopting a comparative and international perspective, it examines the dynamics of critical relationships within the context of national, regional, and global political orders. We look at “standard” settler states often referred to as “neo-Britains,” such as the United States, Canada, New Zealand, and Australia, but also Indigenous Peoples and issues from Europe, Asia, and South America.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Special Topics in Political Science: Gender Rights and Politics
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Lectures in special areas of interest in political science. Specific course titles to be announced by the department each quarter offered.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Special Topics: International Law and Human Rights
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Lectures in special areas of interest in political science. Specific coursetitles to be announced by the department each quarter offered.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Latinx American Political Development
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: This course examines the role of Latinx communities in shaping local, state, and national politics in the United States. It reviews contemporary modes of Latinx political organizing; examines the development of heterogeneous political ideologies among the prevalent subgroups; analyzes public policy issues surrounding citizenship and membership; evaluates the achievements and shortcomings of Latinx empowerment strategies; and it considers the electoral impact of Latinx voting outcomes.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Special Topics in Political Science: Nuclear Security
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Lectures in special areas of interest in political science. Specific course titles to be announced by the department each quarter offered.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: The Politics of the Biosphere: Ecosystem Conservation, Power, and Land
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Forests and other ecosystems are crucial for societal and environmental reasons; nonetheless, they face significant threats across the world. This class explores the economic and political drivers of ecosystem degradation, the solutions that governments and non-governmental actors have implemented to address the issue, and the challenges to their success. Other topics include territorial and political rights of local communities, common-pool resources management, impact evaluation of anti-deforestation policies, and land reforms, among others.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Special Topics in Political Science
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Lectures in special areas of interest in political science. Specific coursetitles to be announced by the department each quarter offered.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Special Topics in Political Science: Psychology in International Relations
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Lectures in special areas of interest in political science. Specific coursetitles to be announced by the department each quarter offered.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Qualitative Methods & Research Design
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.
