courses.description: Introductory, module-based course on political science research design and qualitative methods of inquiry, including participant observation, interview methods, and case studies. Students pursue a topic of their choice deploying each technique to study it. Ideal for students contemplating an honors thesis or graduate school. The course begins by providing students with an introduction to the tools and techniques, strengths and limitations of various qualitative methods. It explores how to craft research designs to provide the greatest explanatory leverage and how to communicate most effectively with your intended audience.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Comparative Regionalism
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Analysis and comparison of regional integration and cooperation across different parts of the world, with a focus on domestic and international economic institutions.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Violence
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Why do societies turn on themselves? Violence, from homicide to civil wars and insurgencies to terrorism and political assassinations to genocide to state repression, shapes societies around the world, and no region is immune, from established democracies to fragile states. This course draws on case studies from across the globe, including both developed and developing nations, to explore three key questions: What forms does violence take? What factors drive it? And how can societies build resilience against it? Students leave with a comparative, global understanding of one of the most pressing challenges facing societies today.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Politics and Literature
courses.description: This course will explore problems concerning alienation, obligation, power,freedom, and fulfillment as treated by ancient and modern authors.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Political Concepts
courses.comments: Can be repeated for additional credit, provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Introduction to some of the main concepts of political theory, such as the individual and the state, freedom and equality, political obligation, and their relevance to modern society and government.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Political Concepts: Critical Theory & Marxism
courses.comments: Can be repeated for additional credit, provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Introduction to some of the main concepts of political theory, such as the individual and the state, freedom and equality, political obligation, and their relevance to modern society and government.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Political Concepts: Civil Disobedience
courses.comments: Can be repeated for additional credit, provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Introduction to some of the main concepts of political theory, such as the individual and the state, freedom and equality, political obligation, and their relevance to modern society and government.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Political Concepts: Defense Against the Political Dark Arts
courses.comments: Can be repeated for additional credit, provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: An exploration of themes in political theory concerned with sinister social forces that undermine good politics - and how to fight back against them. Topics include political manipulation, misinformation, charismatic leadership and rhetoric.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Political Concepts: Environmental Political Theory
courses.comments: Can be repeated for additional credit, provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Introduction to some of the main concepts of political theory, such as the individual and the state, freedom and equality, political obligation, and their relevance to modern society and government.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Democracy and Diversity
courses.description: Introduction to the ancient and modern models of democracy which underpin contemporary democratic life. An analysis of the philosophical bases of democracy, diversity, political obligation, equality, liberty, consent, representation, and rights.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Courts, Judges and Politics
courses.description: The role and significance of the judiciary in the American political system. Such questions as: how cases go through the courts, how "interests" are represented through litigation, the processes by which judges are recruited, and the "independence" of the judiciary will be explored. The course will also entail an exploration of how judges reach decisions and the impacts and consequences of those decisions. The emphasis will be largely on the federal courts, especially the U.S. Supreme Court, and the main focus will be on "public," rather than "private" law.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Comparative Democratic Political Institutions
courses.description: Study of the key political institutional structure of democracy in comparative perspective. Political institutions of the United States and peer democracies covered will include constitutions, the electoral system, the system of government (presidential vs. parliamentary), vertical relations (centralization vs. decentralization), and the legislature. In addition to familiarizing students with the variety and operation of these political institutions, attention will be paid to their advantages and disadvantages, political and policy effects, and implications for the challenges confronting contemporary democracies.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Comparative Social Movement Politics
courses.comments: Not available to students that have taken POL S 106SM.
courses.description: Social movements embody pure politics. They mobilize citizens and are a form of collective action. Scholars have shown that outcomes as wide-ranging as quality of governance, the survival of regimes and nation states, electoral mobilization, citizenship rights, and levels of violence during civil wars can be explained by movements and their attributes.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Comparative Ethnic Politics
courses.description: Examination of the political consequences of ethnicity. Theoretical approaches to issues addressing problems of multiethnic states in the developing world, and the successor states of the Soviet Union.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Ethical Issues in International Relations
courses.comments: Can be repeated for additional credit, provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: An examination of the possibility and desirability of normative international political theory and an exploration of the moral dimensions of statecraft; use of force, nuclear deterrence, humanitarian intervention,distributive justice, and human rights.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Ethical Issues in International Relations: Just War
courses.comments: Can be repeated for additional credit, provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: An examination of the possibility and desirability of normative international political theory and an exploration of the moral dimensions of statecraft; use of force, nuclear deterrence, humanitarian intervention, distributive justice, and human rights.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Negotiation in Theory and Practice
courses.description: This course focuses on negotiation in theory and practice. It uses lectures and hands-on exercises in class to build students skills. It draws on research on negotiation, with a focus on applying these ideas to political contexts and institutions. It also helps build practical skills in communication, leadership and decision-making.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: International Politics
courses.description: An examination of theories concerning the actions, interactions, and relationships among nation-states.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: The Politics of International Monetary Relations
courses.description: The politics of international monetary relations. The aim is to learn how to understand and evaluate the current functioning of money and finance in the global economy.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: International Organizations
courses.description: The nature and function of international organizations, including a study of the United Nations and the European community.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: International Law
courses.description: Nature and sources of international law; international legal personality; nationality, territory, jurisdiction; diplomatic and consular agents; treaties; war; neutrality.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: International Security
courses.description: Examines how states use diplomacy, strategic coercion, and military force to achieve political objectives.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: American Foreign Policy
courses.description: The United States in world politics. Policy making institutions, particularly the presidency, congress, state department, and the military establishment. Interaction between domestic and external politics.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Foreign Relations Between China and the United States
courses.description: The ideological and cultural attitudes of mainland China, with emphasis on general policies both within the communist world and other areas (South Asia, Africa, and America).

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Comparative Military Politics
courses.description: Examines a militarys role in domestic politics by focusing on a diverse set of topics including civil-military relations, militarys role in citizen making, economic progress, conflict management, and nation building.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Relations Between the United States and Mexico
courses.description: A general examination of relations between the United States and Mexico in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries. Emphasis on issues such as the origins of conflict and cooperation, and current issue areas including immigration.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Government and Politics of Japan
courses.description: The organization and operation of Japanese politics, with particular attention to domestic political forces and problems.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Gender Rights in World Politics
courses.description: This class analyzes the state of women’s rights in world politics and how to respond to global challenges. We examine themes from international relations including international political economy, global security, and migration as drivers and locations of gender rights struggles. We also consider the relationship between gender rights and the comparative politics of development, democracy, social movements, and law and society. A feminist analysis will add the complementary issues of the politics of reproduction, rights in the private sphere, and the importance of gender roles and norms as a dimension of power.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Water Politics
courses.description: Climate change and rapidly depleting water resources are the biggest challenges facing humanity in the 21st century. Claims over water by powerful sectors including commercial farming, industrialization and urbanization will get stronger and water scarcity will further marginalize the poor from their livelihoods. This course has examples from around the world, deals with the pressing challenges related to water, and gives the students a better understanding of politics related to water.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Civil War
courses.description: Patterns in the phenomenon of civil war and ethnic conflict. A survey of the causes of these conflicts and an exploration of the consequences. Special attention is given to several key cases of civil conflict to illustrate core concepts.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Foreign Policy Decision Making
courses.description: Examines how leaders and organizations make and implement foreign policy.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Russian Domestic Politics
courses.prereq_text: Political Science 6 and 15; not open to freshmen.
courses.description: The course examines the basic characteristics of the Soviet ancient regime and the forces and institutions which shaped the emerging states and societies. Topics include: parliamentary and economic systems, political parties, interest groups, ethnicity, legitimacy, sovereignty and inter-state relations.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: The European Union
courses.comments: POL S 145 and ITAL 161X are the same course
courses.description: Introduction to the history and organization of the European Union (the institutions, policies, goals, and successes of the EU). Focus on the ongoing process of economical, political, social, and cultural integration in Europe since the Second World War. In English.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Globalization and Politics
courses.description: An examination and assessment of theories of globalization in relation to the distribution of political power on a global scale, future scenarios of global political domination, and the role of the nation-state in the international system of power.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: POLITICS IN DEVELOPING COUNTRIES
courses.description: A comparative analysis of the political system of a selected number of African, Asian and Middle Eastern countries, with particular development and modernization common to all of them.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Israeli Politics
courses.prereq_text: Political Science 6 and 15; not open to freshmen.
courses.description: An introduction to the politics of Israel. Examines both Israeli domestic politics and Israel in comparative perspective.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Politics of the Middle East and North Africa
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to key theoretical debates in the comparative politics and international relations of the Middle East. We cover the major areas of political science research on the region while also building substantive knowledge about the politics of individual countries. This course aims to help students identify broad trends in the political, social, and economic development of the Middle East and critically evaluate existing explanations for those trends.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: American Political Parties
courses.description: The nature, characteristics, and history of American political parties; party organization; political campaigns and finance; nominations, elections, and electoral problems.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Public Opinion
courses.prereq_text: Political Science 15 or 104 or Sociology 3 or 104A or Psychology 5 or Communications 88.
courses.description: A study of the formation and nature of public opinion including: the public's political sophistication; the role of emotion in political thinking; nature of political culture; growth of political alienation and the forms of political participation.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Congress Simulation
courses.prereq_text: Political Science 12; concurrent enrollment in Political Science 155L.
courses.description: The organization, operation, and politics of congress examined through the lens of theory and demonstrated in conjunction with the required simulation lab POLS 155L.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Congress Simulation Lab
courses.prereq_text: Political Science 12; concurrent enrollment in Political Science 155.
courses.description: A simulation of the U.S. House of Representatives designed to teach the operation and politics of Congress, and requires concurrent enrollment in POLS 155 Congress Simulation lecture course.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Asian American Politics
courses.prereq_text: Political Science 12 or Asian American Studies 1 or Asian American Studies 2.
courses.description: Survey of the historical and contemporary political experiences of Asian Americans and their pursuits for immigration, equality, citizenship, political identity, racial justice, cross-racial/ethnic coalition building and incorporation into the U. S. political system.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: U. S. Minority Politics
courses.prereq_text: Political Science 12. Not open to freshmen.
courses.description: A comparative study of recent literature on the historical and contemporary political experiences of the four major racial and ethnic minority groups (Blacks/African Americans, American Indians, Latinos/Hispanic Americans, and Asian Americans) and their interactions with the dominant racial group (non-Hispanic white Americans) in the U.S.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Urban Government and Politics
courses.description: Problems of politics and administration in urban and metropolitan areas.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: US Immigration Politics and Policy
courses.description: Examines the politics of US immigration policy.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Public Policy Analysis
courses.description: The assumptions, goals, content, and consequences of selected domestic policies, concentrating on the period since 1960. Discussion of the nature of collective action, methods of policy analysis and evaluation, and problems of implementation.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Political Communication in the U.S.
courses.description: Political communication in the United States. Covering the interplay of news, social media, and other forms of communication with public opinion and political behavior.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Media and Politics in Comparative and Historical Perspective
courses.description: A comparative examination across countries of the theory and history of media and politics.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Politics of the Environment
courses.prereq_text: Political Science 12 or Environmental Studies 3; upper-division standing.
courses.comments: Same course as Environmental Studies 178.
courses.description: Analysis of environmental policy issues and their treatment in the political process. Discussion of the interplay of substantive issues, ideology, institutions, and private groups in the development, management, protection, and preservation of natural resources and the natural environment.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Energy Politics and Policy
courses.prereq_text: Political Science 6 or 12, or Environmental Studies 1 or 3.
courses.description: Introduces students to the politics and policy of the contemporary global energy system. Covers major public policies and politics related to both the electricity and transportation systems. Students learn energy technology characteristics and understand contemporary political debates over the energy system.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Comparative Environmental Politics
courses.comments: Same course as Environmental Studies 177.
courses.description: Course is structured around the major issues in environmental politics, for example: global warming, nuclear waste, deforestation, and chemical pollution. The roles of economics, technology and social organization are each considered as explanatory variables for understanding environmental problems.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Democracy and the Internet
courses.description: Examines challenges to democratic process and public spheres associated with digital media, including: harms to privacy, misinformation, propaganda, anti-social behavior, political extremism and violence, and corporate power, with an emphasis on the US.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Bureaucracy and Public Policy
courses.description: The nature of American bureaucracy, its organization and culture and its role as a political institution.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Introduction to International Political Economy
courses.comments: Same course as Global Studies 123. Not open for credit to students who have completed Political Science 186A.
courses.description: Introduction to the politics of international economic relations. Examination of alternative analytical and theoretical perspectives for their value in helping to understand and evaluate the historical development and current operation of the world economy.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Classical Political Theory
courses.description: A careful examination of major texts and thinkers in the ancient world and in medieval times.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Modern Political Theory
courses.description: Development of political ideas from the sixteenth century to the nineteenthcentury.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Recent and Contemporary Political Theory
courses.description: A reconstruction of the contending theories of political order with which western intellectuals, from the nineteenth to the present century, have confronted an era of world historical changes.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Field Research in Political Science
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; consent of department prior to enrollment.
courses.comments: Students must have a 3.0 grade-point-average.
courses.description: Directed research on the political process through participant observation and relevant reading. Individually assigned, instructed, and supervised fieldwork. Students will examine first hand behavior in leading political roles in American politics.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Group Studies
courses.comments: Subject to departmental approval, students may repeat this course. Only 4 units may apply to the major.
courses.description: Themes will vary according to instructor.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Senior Seminar in Political Science.
courses.comments: Students should have a recommended minimum grade point average of 3.0 overall.
courses.description: Senior seminar in political science.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Honors Thesis Seminar in Political Science
courses.comments: Requires a 3.3 cum UCSB GPA and 3.6 major GPA for eligibility to apply to the program. A three-quarter course. Final grade issued upon completion of POLS 197C. By petition, 8 units allocated to core concentration, with 4 units toward electives.
courses.description: Political Science 197A-B-C is a three quarter sequence course with the final grade issued upon completion of 197C. Honors students, in three-quarter sequence of seminars, write original theses under close faculty supervision.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Honors Thesis Seminar in Political Science
courses.comments: Requires a 3.3 cum GPA and 3.6 major GPA for eligibility to apply to the program. A three-quarter course. Final grade issued upon completion of POLS 197C. By petition, 8 units allocated to core concentration, with 4 units toward electives.
courses.description: Political Science 197A-B-C is a three quarter sequence course with the final grade issued upon completion of 197C. Honors students, in three-quarter sequence of seminars, write original theses under close faculty supervision.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Honors Thesis Seminar in Political Science
courses.comments: Requires a 3.3 cum GPA and 3.6 major GPA for eligibility to apply to the program. A three-quarter course. Final grade issued upon completion of POLS 197C. By petition, 8 units allocated to core concentration, with 4 units toward electives
courses.description: Political Science 197A-B-C is a three quarter sequence course with the final grade issued upon completion of 197C. Honors students, in three-quarter sequence of seminars, write original theses under close faculty supervision.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Independent Studies in Political Science
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of two prior upper-division courses in political science; major in political science; consent of department.
courses.comments: Students must have a 3.0 GPA for the prior 3 quarters and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 8/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined. No more than 8 units of Political Science 199 may count toward completion of the major requirements.
courses.description: Independent studies in political science.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Independent Research Assistance in Political Science
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division courses in politicascience; consent of instructor and department.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
courses.description: Coursework shall consist of faculty supervised research assistance.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Political Research Methods I
courses.description: An introduction to quantitative political methodology, ranging from probability theory to the basic multivariate linear regression model. Emphasis is placed on the use of statistical software to implement the statistical models covered.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Political Research Methods II
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing; introductory statistics and social scientific research methods.
courses.description: Regression criticism through limited dependent variable models. Emphasis is placed on the use of statistical software to implement the statistical models covered.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Advanced Political Research Methods
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing; introductory statistics, social scientific research methods; and Political Science 206.
courses.description: Advanced techniques of multivariate analysis. Topics determined by students' interest.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Research Seminar I
courses.description: This is the first quarter of a two-quarter research seminar designed to give students experience in the production of a research paper, with a focus on designing theoretically-informed, empirically-tested projects. The seminar is taught in a workshop format focusing on the individual research projects of each student. While not a formal prerequisite, each student is expected to have at least the beginning of a research proposal idea before starting the course.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Research Seminar II
courses.description: This is the second quarter of a two-quarter research seminar designed to give students experience in the production of a research paper. The seminar is taught in a workshop format focusing on the individual research projects of each student.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: International Relations
courses.description: Basic factors shaping the political conflicts and accommodations among nations. Major attention to basic literature on the subject matter.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Comparative Political Systems
courses.description: A general survey of theories of comparative politics with some attention toconcrete applications and to comparative trends in other social sciences and history.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Qualitative Methods
courses.description: Focuses on the logic and purpose of qualitative methods in the social sciences, including the utility of mixed methods in research design. The course covers basic topics such as case selection, process tracing, and management of qualitative evidence, but will also discuss more specialized issues such as the use of interviews, focus groups, survey construction and measurement, field experiments, and content analysis.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Comparative Political Institutions
courses.description: A survey of the major theoretical approaches to the study of political institutions, as well as of the major political institutions, such as the regime type and electoral system. The perspective is primarily comparative, but examples are also drawn from the American politics literature.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Democratization in Comparative Perspective
courses.description: Theoretical issues in research on democratization, emphasizing problems of transition and consolidation and methods of comparison of democratic transitions across regions.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Social Movements and Collective Action
courses.description: An overview of theoretical and empirical literature dealing with social movements and collective action as it relates specifically to problems in popular organization. Readings demonstrate some empirical bias toward LatinAmerica, as well as the United States and Europe.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Seminar in Public Opinion and Political Participation
courses.description: Public opinion, elections, and other forms of participation are considered. Emphasis is on American politics, but theories and research are viewed in comparative perspective.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Seminar in American Political Behavior
courses.description: Intended as a core seminar in American Politics. Covers the literature on individual political behavior in the United States. Topics include theoretical approaches to studying individual political behavior and foundational research on topics such as the nature and consequences of the public's knowledge about politics, persuasion, political identity, ideology, values, tolerance, prejudice, public opinion, participation, and voting.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Seminar in American Institutions
courses.description: This course is intended to be a core seminar in American Politics. Introduces students to the core literature on American political institutions. Topics include theoretical approaches to studying political institutions, and foundational research on institutions like the presidency, Congress, federalism, political parties, interest groups, states, the judicial system, and other political institutions.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Race, Ethnicity and Gender in American Politics
courses.description: This course examines the role of race, ethnicity and gender; their intersections in shaping the opportunity structures and behavioral outcomes of political participation and the incorporation of racial/ethnic minorities and women into the American political processes and institutions.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Contemporary Problems in American Government
courses.description: An in-depth look at current controversies and debates in research on American politics.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Seminar on International Organizations and Society
courses.description: Examines, from a variety of theoretical perspectives, the proposition that there is an international society consisting of laws, norms, institutions, organizations, and cultures that has significant effects on the behavior of states and the character of international relations.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Contemporary Civil War & Political Violence
courses.description: Surveys the scholarly research on civil war's causes, dynamics, termination, and consequences. The material emphasizes theory and includes classic studies of civil war as well as cutting edge research. Designed to be both theoretical and practical, introducing students to the most important and cutting-edge research in civil war while simultaneously preparing them for work in the academy or research.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: War, Diplomacy and International Security
courses.description: The seminar will probe a variety of issues, theoretical and historical (plus quite a few contemporary ones), that touch on war, power, and security studies.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: American Foreign Policy
courses.description: Contemporary issues in U.S. foreign policy

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Comparative Ethnic Politics
courses.description: Examines the political consequences of ethnicity and theoretical approachesinvolved in the study of ethnic politics. Issues addressing problems of multi-ethnic states will be examined in light of cases drawn from the industrialized democracies, developing world, and the successor states of the Soviet Union.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Environmental Politics and Policy
courses.description: This seminar focuses on development of the environmental movement in American politics and the resulting institutional responses. Environmental policy making and implementation is examined in light of relevant theories.Emergence of an environmental ethic in American politics is considered.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Environmental Politics Workshop
courses.comments: ESM 526 and POL S 295 are the same course.
courses.description: An interdisciplinary seminar focusing on research at the intersection of political science and public policy as it pertains to environmental issues. Students specializing in environmental politics will enroll continuously, with differentiated assignments appropriate to stage in the program. Students present their own work, comment on the work of others, and engage in professional development activities.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Comparative and International Environmental Politics
courses.description: Explores the global and comparative political economy of the environment.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Practicum for Teaching Assistants
courses.description: Designed to help teaching assistants learn effective teaching methods and techniques under faculty supervision. assignments normally include conducting discussion sections, grading examinations under the supervision of appropriate faculty members and discussion of relevant pedagogical problems.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Teaching Assistant Training
courses.description: Designed to help graduate students prepare for future assignments as teaching assistants. Course work normally includes discussions with faculty members and past or current teaching assistants, attendance at demonstration exercises, analysis of teacher performance with the use of audio-visual aids, etc.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Practicum for Teaching Associates
courses.description: Designed to help beginning teaching associates improve and refine their teaching methods, techniques and materials through discussions with appropriate members of the regular faculty. The format of the course may vary according to the specific needs of the teaching associates.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Special seminar on research subjects of current interest.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: American Social Movements
courses.description: Social movements and protest have become permanent features of the contemporary social landscape, constantly challenging political institutions and other forms of institutional and cultural authority. These challenges to authority emerge both in contexts where there is little hope for people to gain redress through more conventional means for affecting change, and in democratic contexts where we would expect more readily available direct routes to influence. In this seminar, we examine how and why movements emerge and develop, and what kinds of influence they might create.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Special Topics: Black Political Thought
courses.description: Special seminar on research subjects of current interest.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Citizenship, Culture, and Consent
courses.description: Citizenship is simultaneously an inclusive and exclusive tool states use to preserve social boundaries and establish national belonging. This seminar cross-nationally explores the variation in norms, customs, and values that engender citizenship policy in the US and Europe.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Comparative Politics/International Relations/Political Economy Workshop
courses.description: A seminar focused on work-shopping and discussing cutting-edge work in Comparative Politics, International Relations, and Political Economy. The expectation is that students specializing in CP and IR will enroll continuously, with differentiated assignments appropriate to stage in the program. Students will present their own work, comment on the work of others, and engage in professional development activities. In a typical quarter, the workshop may involve 3 weeks where an outside speaker present on work in progress, 3 weeks where faculty present their work, 3 weeks where graduate students present work, and 1 week of professional development activities.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Race, Class and Gender in American Politics
courses.description: This course examines how conflicts over race, class and gender have shaped the contemporary American political economy.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Directed Applied Writing
courses.description: The course is a lab-style, collaborative faculty-student seminar on applied writing for publication in scholarly journals and public-facing outlets. It carries a substantive focus on the political economy of energy, with particular attention to writing that involves applications of statistical analysis.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Political Economy of Energy and the Environment
courses.description: Seminar comparatively examines the political economy of the world's energy resources its interrelationship with the environment.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: The Political Economy of Land
courses.description: Survey of social science research on the political economy of land and its relationship with the environment across the world. Topics include, among others, land reforms, territorial and political rights of local communities, common-pool resources management, and different ecosystems conservation policies.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Great Books in IR & Comparative Politics
courses.description: In this course, we will read some of the best and most influential works in international relations and comparative politics. In this age of distraction, we will start small and work our way up, while simultaneously looking at the best tools and techniques to train our brains to read, focus, think deeply, and share productively with others.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Political Economy of the Environment in the Global South
courses.description: This course explores the intersection between politics and the environment in the Global South. Students will engage with current theoretical debates and empirical research about how political variables affect environmental quality. Topics include, among others, the politics of energy transition, air and water pollution, land use and deforestation, the impact of extractive industries, and global environmental justice.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: The Politics of Gender and War
courses.description: The seminar examines the politics of gender and war, through an examination of various international conflicts.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Special Topics: Human Rights
courses.description: Special seminar on research subjects of current interest.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: The Politics of International Intervention
courses.description: This graduate seminar explores the politics of international intervention, examining how external actors attempt to shape domestic outcomes through tools such as foreign aid, peacebuilding, post-conflict statebuilding, foreign-imposed regime change, and election interference. We analyze the motives behind these interventions, their design, and their consequences for domestic governance, legitimacy, and stability. Through case studies and theoretical debates, students will develop a critical understanding of the effectiveness and ethical implications of international involvement in sovereign affairs.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Institutions and Politics of Ignorance
courses.description: In this course, we take the well-worn phrase “knowledge is power” and flip it on its head in order to study the ways in which ignorance -- especially in its culturally induced and socially constructed form -- has been harnessed as a political instrument to consolidate power and promote special interests. Ignorance here is much more than the absence of knowledge, or its mere opposite. Rather, our focus is on the ways in which the deliberate production and preservation of ignorance by domestic and/or foreign agents has increasingly become a constitutive feature of the policy making process in democratic and non-democratic societies alike.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Special Topics: Politics and Gender
courses.description: Special seminar on research subjects of current interest.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Special Topics: Plato's Political Thought
courses.description: Special seminar on research subjects of current interest.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Race and Ethnic Politics
courses.description: This graduate and senior seminar explores the historical and contemporary issues surrounding race and ethnicity in political contexts. We explore how race and ethnicity are approached in the subfields of political science (i.e., behavioral, normative, and institutional, among other approaches). The class has an American focus but also draws upon global literature on how racial and ethnic politics are organized and approached.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Partiality, Impartiality, and Politics
courses.description: In this graduate level seminar, we shall inquire whether impartiality is a worthy political goal and whether it can be realized in any but the most rival fashion. We shall also ask what value might take its place if it is indeed unfeasible.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Statebuilding
courses.description: Examines statebuilding in the modern world, with a focus on international efforts to construct states beyond their own borders. Theoretically, the course aims to provide a thorough understanding of the concept of statebuilding and all that it entails. Empirically, the course focuses primarily on statebuilding in the Global South and the unique challenges faced by domestic and international statebuilders in weakly institutionalized settings.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: State Capacity
courses.description: State Capacity, the ability of the state to accomplish policy goals, intersects with concerns of development, governance, and administration. This seminar course introduces students to state capacity and challenges in enhancing capacity with examples from developing countries.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Special seminar on research subjects of current interest.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Special Topics: Violence & Political Theory
courses.description: Special seminar on research subjects of current interest.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Weber, Schmitt & Arendt
courses.description: This advanced seminar in political theory will begin with Max Weber’s seminal early 20th century statements regarding the general limits of reason and science and the central place of violence and the irrational in politics; we will then address the fundamentally contrasting responses to these by Carl Schmitt and Hannah Arendt. Central themes will include existential questions of identity and community, freedom and sovereignty, and, authority and totalitarianism.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Directed Reading and Research
courses.prereq_text: A written proposal for each tutorial must be approved by the instructor andthe department graduate advisor and filed with the department graduate offi
courses.description: Individual tutorial.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Individual Study for Master's Comprehensive Examination and Ph.D Examinations
courses.description: Individual study for Master's comprehensive examinations and Ph.D. examinations.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Master's Thesis Research and Preparation
courses.description: Master's thesis research and preparation.

courses.subject: POL S
courses.title: Ph.D. Dissertation Research and Preparation
courses.description: Ph.D. dissertation research and preparation.

courses.subject: POL SW
courses.title: Introduction to Research in Political Science
courses.comments: POL SW 15 if the on-line version of POLS 15. Not open to students who have completed Political Science 104, 104A and 104AL.
courses.description: An introduction to the design and evaluation of political research, from formulating clear questions and gathering appropriate data, to the use of simple statistical techniques for analyzing data and presenting evidence.

courses.subject: POL SW
courses.title: International Politics
courses.description: An examination of theories concerning the actions, interactions, and relationships among nation-states.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Elementary Portuguese I
courses.comments: No credit can be earned if more advanced credit in the language has already been awarded. Students enrolled in an inappropriate level will be assisted in re-enrolling in the proper course. (PORT W 1 is the online version of PORT 1.)
courses.description: Beginning course in Portuguese establishing fundamental auditory and oral skills, with secondary practice in reading and writing, pronunciation, intensive oral practice. Includes laboratory work.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Elementary Portuguese II
courses.prereq_text: Portuguese 1, or Portuguese 16A, with a grade of P or a grade of C or higher.
courses.comments: No credit can be earned if more advanced credit in the language has already been awarded. Students enrolled in an inappropriate level will be assisted in re-enrolling in the proper course.
courses.description: Continues activities commenced with Portuguese 1.

courses.description: Completes the basic study of the elements of the language.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Portuguese for Spanish Speakers
courses.comments: No credit can be earned if more advanced credit in the language has already been awarded. Students enrolled in an inappropriate level will be assisted in re-enrolling in the proper course.
courses.description: An intensive introductory sequence in Portuguese covering the first full year of Portuguese grammar and also advanced readings in Portuguese. Uses the grammatical structures of the Romance languages, especially Spanish, as a point of departure. Proficiency in all areas of Portuguese (reading, writing, listening, and speaking) are emphasized.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Portuguese for Spanish Speakers II
courses.prereq_text: Portuguese 16A with a grade of P or a grade of C or higher.
courses.comments: No credit can be earned if more advanced credit in the language has already been awarded. Students enrolled in an inappropriate level will be assisted in re-enrolling in the proper course.
courses.description: Intensive introductory sequence in Portuguese covering the first full year of Portuguese grammar and advanced readings in Portuguese. Uses grammatical structures of the Romance languages, especially Spanish, as point of departure. Proficiency in all areas of Portuguese (reading, writing, listening, speaking) are emphasized.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Brazil: Literature, Visual Arts, Music, and Nation
courses.description: This is a multidisciplinary survey course about Brazilian culture and literature. It uses different sources of materials: travel writing descriptions, accounts of visitors and explorers, scientists, visual arts, literary texts, anthropological and ethnographical approaches, history, philosophy and media. This course offers a complete survey of the complex relations involving the origins of Brazil, colonization and slavery by the Portuguese, and the creation of a Brazilian nationality and identity by both adopting the Portuguese language and rejecting the colonial model. It provides the essential readings, historical and cultural backgrounds that form the backbone for informed discussions about the history of Brazilian culture.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Ocean Cultures: People, Routes, and Environments in the Portuguese-Speaking World
courses.description: This course explores the ocean's impact on the history, culture, and societies of Portuguese-speaking nations, including Angola, Brazil, Cape Verde, Mozambique, and Portugal. Through a diverse array of literary worksranging from non-fiction and fiction to poetry, alongside filmswe will explore the ocean's influence from various perspectives across the continents of America, Africa, and Asia. We'll navigate through topics like seafaring, the Atlantic slave trade, coastal community life, and environmental sustainability. The goal of this course is to understand the ocean's role in shaping these nations and how human activities influence marine ecosystems. Taught in English.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Advanced Grammar and Composition
courses.description: Study of the finer points of Portuguese grammar and syntax. Equal stress is placed on written and oral practice of the language. The work in class will consist of careful study of essays and articles.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Survey of Portuguese Literature from the Middle Ages to the Present
courses.comments: Portuguese 105 is the Portuguese version of Portuguese 105E.
courses.description: A survey of the main writers of Portuguese Literature from its beginnings up to the present. Designed to give the student historical, cultural and literary contexts, a chronological panel, in order to prepare the student for more specific and focused courses within the area of Portuguese. Also prepares the student for understanding these contexts in order to apply the knowledge acquired in this survey to other fields of interest.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Survey of Portuguese Literature from the Middle Ages to the Present
courses.comments: Portuguese 105E is the English version of Portuguese 105.
courses.description: A survey of the main writers of Portuguese Literature from its beginnings up to the present. Designed to give the student historical, cultural and literary contexts, a chronological panel, in order to prepare the student for more specific and focused courses within the area of Portuguese. Also prepares the student for understanding these contexts in order to apply the knowledge acquired in this survey to other fields of interest. Taught in English.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Survey of Brazilian Literature from its Beginnings to the Present
courses.comments: Portuguese 106 is the Portuguese version of Portuguese 106E.
courses.description: A survey of the main works of literature produced in Brazil and about Brazil from its beginnings up to the present. Involves travel literature about Brazil, written in the sixteenth century, at the time of its discovery, as well as the literature produced in Brazil up to the present, represented by significant authors and periods. Designed to give the student a historical, cultural and literary context, a chronological panel, in order to prepare the student for more specific and focused courses within the area of Portuguese. Also prepares the student for the understanding of cultural contexts in order to apply the knowledge acquired in this survey to other fields of interest.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Survey of Brazilian Literature from its Beginnings to the Present
courses.comments: Portuguese 106E is the English version of Portuguese 106.
courses.description: A survey of the main works of literature produced in Brazil and about Brazil from its beginnings up to the present. Involves travel literature about Brazil, written in the sixteenth century, at the time of its discovery, as well as the literature produced in Brazil up to the present, represented by significant authors and periods. Designed to give the student a historical, cultural and literary context, a chronological panel, in order to prepare the student for more specific and focused courses within the area of Portuguese. Also prepares the student for the understanding of cultural contexts in order to apply the knowledge acquired in this survey to other fields of interest. Taught in English.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Lusophone Cityscapes: Cultures, Histories, and Urban Imaginaries
courses.comments: Comparative Literature 106 and Portuguese 107 are the same course.
courses.description: This course examines the urban landscapes of cities in the Portuguese-speaking world across Europe, Africa, Asia, and the Americas, exploring their histories, cultural productions, and evolving identities. From Lisbon to Luanda, Rio de Janeiro to Maputo, and Goa to Dili, we delve into the architecture, literature, music, and cinema that shape these urban centers. Themes include colonial and postcolonial transformations, social inequality, migration, and the intersection of urban life with environmental challenges. Students will analyze how cityscapes serve as spaces of memory, resistance, and creativity, revealing the complexities of urban life across this interconnected planetary network. Taught in English

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: How to Read and Why: Brazilian Literature and More
courses.comments: Portuguese 108E is the English version of Portuguese 108.
courses.description: Students are exposed to readings of aesthetic and cultural value, such as literature in all its genres: poetry, short story, cronicas, novels, memorials etc. Also introduces students to the basic concepts of literary theory and aesthetics, and to some specific literary genres like travel literature and satire. Students will acquire skills to engage critically with other aesthetic forms, like the visual arts and architecture, as well as engaging with philosophical texts. Taught in English.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Nature and Environment in Brazilian Culture and Literature
courses.comments: Portuguese 109E is the English version of Portuguese 109.
courses.description: This course aims to understand how Brazilian culture and literature approach its surrounding environment, using different sources of materials: travel writing descriptions, accounts of visitors and explorers, scientists, visual arts, literary texts, anthropological and ethnographic approaches, history, philosophy and media. The course offers a complete survey of the complex relations involving the Portuguese Colonial system of exploration and exploitation of the environment (plantation, monoculture, slavery), land and border occupation of indigenous lands, demarcation, and the 20th occupation of the Amazon. It provides the essential historical and cultural backgrounds of Brazilian engagement with its environment. Taught in English.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Understanding Brazilian Music in its Cultural Context
courses.comments: MUS 178BR, C LIT 131B, and PORT 110 are the same course.
courses.description: This course enables students to understand what Brazilian music is, and what is the role of Music in Brazilian culture. It offers a comprehensive panel of the history of music in Brazil. The course also provides students with a full cultural context, discussing the role of music during the two dictatorship periods in Brazil, 1930-1945 and 1964-1985 and the political impact of censorship. It also discusses the contributions of the Africans, brought to Brazil by the Portuguese colonizers, and the impact African culture has both in music and religion. Taught in English.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Literature of the Portuguese Expansion
courses.description: Literary masterpieces of the Portuguese Golden Age (fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, and part of the seven-teenth century): chronicles of the discoveries, the epic poem Os Lusiadas by Camoes, dramatic narratives of shipwrecks--all translated into English.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Brazilian Literature (in English Translation)
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Significant writers and poets of nineteenth and twentieth century Brazil. Topic or author to be chosen by faculty member. Each course on different topics. Taught in English.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Brazilian Literature in English Translation
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: A dynamic course offering and thorough overview of the most important writers and texts from Brazil, as well as the contexts which generated them. How to read and why read Brazilian literature? The course stresses the role of translation in the transmission of other cultures, ideas and more. Students learn about genres, periods, the context in which works of literature come to be, and what it means to read a work in translation.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Artistic and Interdisciplinary Approaches to Portuguese Language Countries
courses.description: The distinctive features of Portugal, Brazil, and African countries as manifested in institutions, art, music, and literature. Taught in English

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Luso-Brazilian Cinema
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Portuguese and Brazilian films of the past forty years both as an art medium and as a document of changing society. Topic or author to be chosen by faculty member; each course on a different topic. Taught in English.

courses.description: Portuguese films of the past forty years both as an art medium and as a document of changing society. Topic or author to be chosen by faculty member; each course on a different topic. Taught in English.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Portuguese for STEM Students
courses.description: Provides an intermediate level of Portuguese with knowledge of vocabulary, grammar, and culture in the context of the science, technology, engineering, or mathematics (STEM) world. The material and activities revolve around terminology and communication relevant to any STEM field, with a significant focus on biology, healthcare, computer sciences, and engineering. The objective is to equip students with the language tools necessary to collaborate, conduct research, and engage with Portuguese-speaking colleagues and resources within the STEM community. Whether students plan to work in a Portuguese-speaking country, collaborate on international projects, this course will foster global competence and enhance career opportunities.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Business Portuguese
courses.description: Provides students with knowledge of vocabulary, grammar, and culture in the specific context of the business world. The material and activities revolve around topics related to business in the Portuguese-speaking world (money & banking, the market, the company, the stock market, imports & exports, marketing & advertising, society & consumption, and human resources). The objective is to develop advanced language proficiency and a professional register in Portuguese through the explorations of those topics. These two aspects will be creatively explored through the representation of real-life situations in the professional environment, interactive activities, and a group project where students will design their own company.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Studies in Portuguese Literatures
courses.comments: May be repeated to a maximum of 20 units provided the letter designation is different.
courses.description: Topic or author to be chosen by faculty member; each course on a different topic.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Postcolonial Dynamics in Lusophone Africa
courses.comments: May be repeated to a maximum of 20 units provided the letter designation is different.
courses.description: This course, taught in English, explores literatures and cultures through contemporary film, music, and literature from the Portuguese-speaking world in Africa, focusing on Angola, Mozambique, and Cape Verde. We analyze literary, historical, and political texts to deepen our understanding of post-colonial identities and African societies. Discussions center on anti-colonial struggles, nationhood, colonial legacies, ethnicity, trauma, reconciliation, and utopian/dystopian cultural identities.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Senior Honors Independent Research
courses.prereq_text: Admission to the Portuguese senior honors program.
courses.description: The student engages in research leading to a paper of considerable depth and complexity on a topic dealing with the literature and/or language of Portugal, Brazil, or Portuguese-speaking Africa.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Independent Studies in Portuguese
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division courses in Portuguese; consent of department.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA average for the preceding 3 quarters and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
courses.description: Independent studies in selected subjects not covered by course offerings.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Studies on Machado de Assis and the Brazilian Novel
courses.comments: Course content may vary from quarter to quarter and may be repeated for credit with the consent of the department graduate adviser.
courses.description: Machado de Assis' novelistic work; its innovative approach as a basis of modern fiction. Other novelists of his time will also be studied.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Foreign Language Teaching Methodology
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing and appointment as a teaching assistant or student associate in Portuguese.
courses.description: Preparation of students to conduct intitial research in areas related to Applied Linguistics, and the application of both theoretical and practical considerations of the current literature on actual teaching.

courses.title: Research Seminar in Portuguese and Brazilian Literature
courses.description: Primarily intended to train students in techniques, background materials and selection of topics.

courses.description: Comlpetion of research paper, reporting regularly to class on progress of work.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Teaching Assistant Practicum
courses.comments: Units earned do not apply toward completion of advanced degrees. S/U grading only. Required of all teaching assistants in Portuguese.
courses.description: Supervised teaching of lower-division Portuguese courses at UCSB. Participation in occasional workshops related to the field of teaching willbe required.

courses.description: Supervised teaching of lower-division Portuguese courses at UCSB. Participation in occasional workshops related to the field of teaching willbe required.

courses.description: Supervised research in Luso-Brazilian literature, linguistics, or culture.

courses.title: Directed Reading and Research
courses.description: Individual tutorial. A written proposal for each tutorial must be approved by student's program adviser and by the department chair. The number of units which a student may take in this series depends on the nature of the program and the consent of the adviser or the departmental graduate committee.

courses.comments: S/U grading. No unit credit allowed toward advanced degree.
courses.description: Individual study for Master's comprehensive or Ph.D. examinations. Individual study under instructor who is member of the student's program committee.

courses.comments: S/U grading. No unit credit allowed toward advanced degree.
courses.description: Individual study for Master's comprehensive or Ph.D. examinations. Individual study under instructor who is member of the student's program committee.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Ph.D. Dissertation Research and Preparation
courses.comments: S/U grading only.
courses.description: Ph.D. dissertation research and preparation. Research and writing of the dissertation. Instructor should be the chair of the student's doctoral committee.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Ph.D. Dissertation Research and Preparation
courses.comments: S/U grading only.
courses.description: Ph.D. dissertation research and preparation. Research and writing of the dissertation. Instructor should be the chair of the student's doctoral committee.

courses.subject: PORT W
courses.title: Online Elementary Portuguese I
courses.comments: Online version of Portuguese 1. No credit can be earned if more advanced credit in the language has already been awarded. Students enrolled in an inappropriate level will be assisted in re-enrolling in the proper course.
courses.description: Port W1 is the first course of the Elementary Portuguese three-course sequence delivered in a fully online format. The course follows a communicative approach. The online format combines technology-based language instruction with virtual class meetings and live, guided conversation sessions. The course materials and activities focus on consolidating the same array of skills promoted in the regular Elementary Portuguese I course (face-to-face). By the end of this course students are expected to develop basic proficiency in Portuguese at the Novice-mid level.

courses.subject: PORT W
courses.title: Online Elementary Portuguese III
courses.prereq_text: Portuguese 2 with a grade of P or a grade of C or higher.
courses.comments: No credit can be earned if more advanced credit in the language has already been awarded. Students enrolled in an inappropriate level will be assisted in re-enrolling in the proper course.
courses.description: Completes the basic study of the elements of the language.

courses.subject: PSTAT
courses.title: Understanding Data
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students with Statistics AP Exam credit or students who have completed PSTAT 5LS or other introductory statistics courses.
courses.description: Introduction to data science. Concepts of statistical thinking. Topics include random variables, sampling distributions, hypothesis testing, correlation and regression. Visualizing, analyzing and interpreting real world data using Python. Computing labs required.

courses.subject: PSTAT
courses.title: Honors Seminar, Statistics
courses.description: Introduction to a variety of statistics and applied probability applications. Active participation and a 15- minute group presentation or a short (2-3 pages) analytical essay will be required.

courses.subject: PSTAT
courses.title: Statistics for Life Sciences
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students with Statistics AP Exam credit or students who have completed PSTAT 5A or other introductory statistics courses.
courses.description: An introduction to statistics for students interested in the quantitative analysis of problems in the life sciences. The focus is on application; topics include probability, correlation and regression, sampling distributions, confidence intervals, and hypothesis testing.

courses.subject: PSTAT
courses.title: Transition to Data Science, Probability and Statistics
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 3C or 3CI or 4A or 4AI or 4B or 4BI or 5A or 5AI or 5B or 5BI or 5C or 6A or 6AI or 6B with a grade of B or better. Not open to students who have completed Math 8.
courses.comments: Not open for credit for students who have completed Math 8.
courses.description: Introduction to techniques of mathematical logic, proof, and fundamental structures in probability and statistics. The curriculum includes sets, inequalities, functions, continuity, limits, infinity, and random numbers and simulation. Applications to high-dimensional probability, data science, and statistics. Mastery of this material is essential for students continuing to all three PSTAT programs.

courses.subject: PSTAT
courses.title: Principles of Data Science with R
courses.prereq_text: Math 2B or 3B with a minimum grade of C or better.
courses.description: Provides a foundation for the practice of data science, with an emphasis on the statistical thinking and computer programming required to collect, prepare, and analyze data. Students will explore and implement the data science life cycle in locally relevant contexts. Using the R programming language, the course focuses on the fundamental skills of data manipulation, exploratory data analysis, and data visualization. A key component of the curriculum is learning to ethically communicate findings and to consider the broader impacts of data-driven decisions.

courses.subject: PSTAT
courses.title: Independent Studies in Statistics
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA and are limited to 4 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
courses.description: Independent study under the guidance of a faculty member in the department. Course offers exceptional students an opportunity to undertake independent study or work in a group.

courses.subject: PSTAT
courses.title: Data Science Concepts and Analysis
courses.prereq_text: PSTAT 120A; CS 9 or CS 16; and Math 4A, all with letter grade C or better.
courses.description: Overview of data science key concepts and the use of tools for data retrieval, analysis, visualization, and reproducible research in preparation for advanced data science courses. Topics include an introduction to inference and prediction, principles of measurement, missing data, and notions of causality, statistical traps, and concepts in data ethics and privacy.

courses.subject: PSTAT
courses.title: Introduction to Nonparametric Methods
courses.prereq_text: PSTAT 10 and PSTAT 120B both with a minimum grade of C or better.
courses.description: Statistical methods for model-free data analysis, including use of ranks in comparing means and assessing correlation, computer-based permutation and bootstrap calculations for significance tests and confidence intervals, estimation of lifetime survival curves. Emphasis on scientific applications.

courses.subject: PSTAT
courses.title: Introduction to Bayesian Data Analysis
courses.prereq_text: PSTAT 126 with a minimum grade of C.
courses.description: An introduction to the Bayesian approach to statistical inference, its theoretical foundations and comparison to classical methods. Topics include parameter estimation, testing, prediction and computational methods (Markov Chain Monte Carlo simulation). Emphasis on concepts, methods and data analysis. Extensive use of the R programming language and examples from the social, biological and physical sciences to illustrate concepts.

courses.subject: PSTAT
courses.title: Probability and Statistics
courses.prereq_text: Math 3C or Math 4A or Math 4AI or Math 6A or Math 6AI completed with a minimum grade of C or better.
courses.description: Concepts of probability; random variables; combinatorial probability; discrete and continuous distributions; joint distributions, expected values; moment generating functions; law of large numbers and central limit theorems.

courses.subject: PSTAT
courses.title: Probability and Statistics
courses.prereq_text: PSTAT 120A with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Distribution of sample mean and sample variance; t, chi-squared and F distributions; summarizing data by statistics and graphs; estimation theory for single samples: sufficiency, efficiency, consistency, methodof moments, maximum likelihood; hypothesis testing: likelihood ratio test; confidence intervals.

courses.subject: PSTAT
courses.title: Probability and Statistics
courses.prereq_text: PSTAT 120B with a grade C or better.
courses.description: Hypothesis tests for means of independent samples and paired data; likelihood ratio tests; nonparametric hypothesis tests: sign, rank, and Mann-Whitney tests; chi-squared goodness-of-fit tests and contingency tables; Bayesian methods of estimating parameters and credible intervals.

courses.subject: PSTAT
courses.title: Design and Analysis of Experiments
courses.prereq_text: PSTAT 10 and PSTAT 120B both with a minimum grade of C or better.
courses.description: An introduction to statistical design and analysis of experiments. Covers: principles of randomization, blocking and replication; fixed, random and mixed effects models; block designs, factorial designs and nested designs; analysis of variance and multiple comparison.

courses.subject: PSTAT
courses.title: Sampling Techniques
courses.prereq_text: PSTAT 10 and PSTAT 120B both with a minimum grade of C or better.
courses.description: An elementary development of the statistical methods used to design and analyze sample surveys. Basic ideas: estimates, bias, variance, sampling and nonsampling errors; simple random sampling with and without replacement; ratio and regression estimates; stratified sampling; systematic sampling; cluster sampling; sampling with unequal probabilities, multistage sampling. Examples from various fields will be discussed to illustrate the concepts including sampling of biological populations, opinion polls, etc.

courses.subject: PSTAT
courses.title: Regression Analysis
courses.prereq_text: PSTAT 10 and PSTAT 120B both with a minimum grade of C or better.
courses.description: Linear and multiple regression, analysis of residuals, transformations, variable and model selection including stepwise regression, and analysis of covariance. The course will stress the use of computer packages to solve real-world problems.

courses.subject: PSTAT
courses.title: Advanced Statistical Models
courses.prereq_text: PSTAT 126 with a minimum grade of C or better.
courses.description: Exponential family and generalized linear models including logistic and Poisson regression, nonparametric regression, including kernel, spline and local polynomials, and generalized additive models. Other topics as time allows: regularization, neural networks, and support vector machines. Emphasis will be on concepts and practical applications.

courses.subject: PSTAT
courses.title: SAS Base Programming
courses.prereq_text: One upper division course in PSTAT, MATH, Computer Science or ECE.
courses.description: In depth SAS programming course. Topics include importing/exporting raw data files, manipulating/transforming data, combining SAS data sets, generating reports, handling syntax and logic errors. Provides preparation for the SAS Institute Certified Professional (Base Programming) Examination.

courses.subject: PSTAT
courses.title: Introduction to Statistical Machine Learning
courses.prereq_text: PSTAT 120A-B and PSTAT 126 with a minimum grade of C or better.
courses.description: Statistical Machine Learning is used to discover patterns and relationships in large data sets. Topics will include: data exploration, classification and regression tress, random forests, clustering and association rules. Building predictive models focusing on model selection, model comparison and performance evaluation. Emphasis will be on concepts, methods and data analysis; and students are expected to complete a significant class project, individual or team based, using real-world data.

courses.subject: PSTAT
courses.title: Database Management for Data Analysis
courses.prereq_text: PSTAT 10 and PSTAT 8/MATH 8 with a minimum grade of C or better.
courses.description: Database systems concepts and architecture, data modeling by ER, relational model, Structured Query Language (SQL), functional dependencies, normalization, physical database design decisions, transaction processing concepts and theory. Introduction to the non-relational model, NoSQL and NewSQL.

courses.subject: PSTAT
courses.title: Statistical Deep Learning for Artificial Intelligence
courses.prereq_text: PSTAT 126 with a minimum grade of C or higher.
courses.description: Deep learning predictive models, optimization, and sampling algorithms. Emphasis is on learning the probabilistic framework, understanding the ideas behind modern machine learning algorithms, and practicing coding skills to solve real-world problems using computational approaches in artificial intelligence.

courses.subject: PSTAT
courses.title: Statistical Data Science
courses.prereq_text: PSTAT 131 or PSTAT 231 or Computer Science 165B; and Computer Science 9 (preferred) or Computer Science16. A minimum letter grade of C or better must be earned in each course.
courses.description: Applications of advanced data science tools for data retrieval, statistical analysis and machine learning, optimization, and visualization. Multiple case studies will illustrate the practical use of these tools.

courses.subject: PSTAT
courses.title: Big Data Analytics
courses.prereq_text: PSTAT 131 or PSTAT 231 or Computer Science 165B; and Computer Science 9 (preferred) or Computer Science 16. A minimum letter grade of C or better must be earned in each course.
courses.description: Basics in distributed data storage, retrieval, processing and cloud computing. Overview of methods for analyzing big data from both high dimensional statistics and machine learning - topics chosen from penalized regression, classification/clustering, dimension reduction, random projections, kernel methods, network clustering, graph analytics, supervised and unsupervised learning among others.

courses.subject: PSTAT
courses.title: Statistical Process Control
courses.prereq_text: PSTAT 10 and PSTAT 120B both with a minimum grade of C or better.
courses.description: Topics include, statistical quality control charts for mean, standard deviation, range, fraction defective, and number of defects; sampling by attributes and variables; acceptance sampling, choice of acceptable quality level, average outgoing quality limit and lot tolerance percent defective values.

courses.subject: PSTAT
courses.title: Applied Stochastic Processes
courses.prereq_text: Mathematics 4A or 4AI or 5A, Mathematics 8 or PSTAT 8, and PSTAT 120A. A minimum letter grade of C or better must be earned in each course.
courses.description: Discrete probability models. Review of discrete and continuous probability. Conditional expectations. Simulation techniques for random variables. Discrete time stochastic processes: random walks and Markov chains with applications to Monte Carlo simulation and mathematical finance. Introduction to Poisson process.

courses.subject: PSTAT
courses.title: Applied Stochastic Processes
courses.prereq_text: MATH 4B, PSTAT 120B, and PSTAT 160A with a grade of C or better
courses.description: Continuous models. Continuous time stochastic processes: Poisson process, Markov chains, Renewal process, Brownian motion, including simulation of these processes. Applications to Black-Scholes model, insurance and ruin problems and related topics.

courses.subject: PSTAT
courses.title: Introduction to Mathematical Finance
courses.prereq_text: MATH 4B, PSTAT 120A-B, and PSTAT 160A, all completed with a minimum grade of C or better.
courses.comments: PSTAT 170 and Mathematics 170 are the same course.
courses.description: Describes mathematical methods for estimating and evaluating asset pricing models, equilibrium and derivative pricing, options, bonds, and the term-structure of interest rates. Also introduces finance optimization models for risk management and financial engineering.

courses.subject: PSTAT
courses.title: Mathematics of Fixed Income Markets
