courses.description: The class purpose is to survey the Mexico/U.S border regions cultural production of the past century. It pays special attention to aesthetic and ideological discourses that nurture artistic and political ties required to resist state violence at and across the U.S.-Mexico border. It takes an interdisciplinary approach to understand the sociopolitical realities of the most populated merging points between Latin America and the United States. Material includes readings from different disciplines as well as cultural productions: film, visual arts, literature, music, podcasts and performance art to offer a rich and diverse examination of cultural manifestations and socio-political movements from a transborder perspective. Taught in English.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Introduction to Hispanic Linguistics
courses.prereq_text: SPAN 16B or SPAN 25 (may be taken concurrently).
courses.comments: Prerequisite to all other upper-division courses in Hispanic linguistics.
courses.description: Introduction to linguistic theories, methods, and problems as applied to Spanish. Taught in Spanish with Spanish examples.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Advanced Composition through Literature
courses.comments: Required for teaching credential candidates with a major in Spanish.
courses.description: The study of the finer points of Spanish grammar and syntax. Stress is placed on writing critical analyses of literary readings.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Advanced Composition through Literature
courses.comments: Required for teaching credential candidates with major in Spanish.
courses.description: The study of the finer points of Spanish grammar and syntax. Stress is placed on writing critical analyses of literary readings.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Introduction to Hispanic Studies
courses.prereq_text: Spanish 16B or Spanish 25 or consent of instructor.
courses.description: Introduces students to key concepts, methods, and debates in Hispanic Studies, with a focus on literature, media, cultural production, and historical contexts from Spain, Latin America, and U.S. Latinx communities. Students learn to analyze texts and cultural artifacts using interdisciplinary approaches, including cultural studies, history, and critical theory. The course provides a foundation for upper-division coursework and strengthens analytical, writing, and research skills in Spanish. Taught in Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Beyond Advanced Spanish Proficiency
courses.description: Designed to provide students who have completed Span 25 or Span 16B and one additional upper-division Spanish course with the opportunity to practice the four language skills: speaking, listening, reading, and writing. Students will practice different communicative skills, from defending an opinion to mastering transactions and exchanges.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Teaching Spanish for Heritage Speakers
courses.description: Designed for students who have completed Span 100 and who are considering a teaching career. The course covers frequent issues encountered when working with students who have learned Spanish through their family history or place of origin.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Introduction to Latin American and Iberian Studies
courses.comments: SPAN 106, LAIS 100, and HIST 100 are the same courses. LAIS 100S is the Spanish-language version of SPAN 106, LAIS 100, HIST 100 and is a legal-repeat.
courses.description: Designed to acquaint students with current research on the main areas of Latin American and Iberian Studies.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Introduction to Latin American and Iberian Studies - Honors Section
courses.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in SPAN 106 or LAIS 100; honors standing in LAIS or the College of Letters and Science.
courses.description: Eligible students are invited to enroll in the honors seminar, which is generally taught by the course instructor.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Interdisciplinary Approaches to the History and Societies of Latin America and Iberia
courses.comments: ANTH 134A, LAIS 101, and SPAN 107 are the same course. LAIS 101S is a legal repeat of ANTH 134A, LAIS 101, and SPAN 107.
courses.description: Issues central to the study of Latin America and Iberia across the social sciences and history. Topics include nationalism, revolution, politics and the state, economic development and international relations, labor, popular culture, race, gender, religion, migration, environment, imperialism, and colonialism.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Interdisciplinary Approaches to the Cultures, Languages, and Literatures of Latin America and Iberia
courses.comments: LAIS 102, LING 133, and SPAN 108 are the same course. LAIS 102S is the Spanish-language version of LAIS 102, LING 133, and SPAN 108, and is a legal repeat.
courses.description: Issues pertinent to the diverse cultures, languages, and literatures of Latin America and Iberia. Disciplines and approaches may include: pre-Columbian studies, Spanish and Spanish American literatures, Portuguese and Brazilian literatures, translation studies, cultural, gender, and queer studies, romance language and linguistics.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Spanish in the United States: The Language and Its Speakers
courses.description: Study of Spanish used in United States by native and immigrant groups: Mexicans, Chicanos, Cubans, Puerto Ricans and others in Spanish-speaking enclaves. Focus on language and social and cultural manifestations arising in contact between linguistically different groups. Taught in Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Spanish Literature from the Beginning to the Present
courses.description: Medieval Spanish literature.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Spanish Literature from the Beginning to the Present
courses.description: Golden age literature.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Spanish Literature from the Beginning to the Present
courses.description: Eighteenth- and nineteenth-century Spanish literature.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Spanish Literature from the Beginning to the Present
courses.description: Twentieth-century Spanish literature.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Spanish-American Literature from the Beginning to the Present
courses.description: Colonial Spanish-American literature.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Spanish-American Literature from the Beginning to the Present
courses.description: Nineteenth-century Spanish-American literature.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Spanish-American Literature from the Beginning to the Present
courses.description: Twentieth-century Spanish-American literature.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Non-Castilian Literatures of Spain
courses.description: Introduction to Spains medieval linguistic and cultural diversity through literary works written in such languages as Latin, Arabic, Hebrew, Mozarabic, Occitan, Catalan-Valencian, Galician-Portuguese and Galician. Texts read in Spanish or English translation.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Non-Castilian Literatures of Spain
courses.description: Introduction to Spains linguistic and cultural diversity in modern and contemporary times through literary works written in Asturian, Basque, Catalan and Galician. Texts read in Spanish translation.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Introduction to Translation I
courses.comments: Same course as Comparative Literature 102A.
courses.description: Comprises topics necessary to develop skills that are needed for writing at a specialized level and to carry out written translation into and from Spanish, mostly texts on business and medical topics.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Introduction to Interpreting
courses.prereq_text: SPAN 16B or SPAN 25 (may be taken concurrently)
courses.comments: Same course as Comparative Literature 102B.
courses.description: Comprised of topics necessary in developing skills for interpretation to and from Spanish. Intended mostly for proficient Spanish-language speakers.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Specialized Translation - Legal
courses.description: Comprised of topics necessary in developing skills for writing at a specialized level, and with specialized vocabulary, for the legal profession.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Specialized Translation - Technical
courses.comments: Comparative Literature 102C and Spanish 117C are the same course
courses.description: Comprised of topics necessary in developing skills for writing at a specialized level, and with specialized vocabulary and format, for the translation of different types of technical texts (instruction manuals, medical, patents, etc.).

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Spanish Institutions and Culture
courses.description: Study of the development of the Spanish nation, with special focus on key social and political institutions, the arts and major currents of thought.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Psycholinguistics
courses.comments: Spanish 124 is the Spanish version of Spanish 124E.
courses.description: An introduction to core areas of Spanish psycholinguistics: speech perception, word recognition, language comprehension, language production, first language acquisition, bilingualism, language disorders and aphasiology. Goals: 1)to introduce students to the key findings and central debates within psycholinguistic research; 2)to introduce students to the tools and methods of psycholinguistic research; 3)to introduce students to research practice; 4)to manage effective interaction within the intercultural context. Students will develop an experiment design, and collect/analyze data. Depending on their performance, students will be invited to work and/or volunteer at the Bilingualism, Translation, & Cognition Laboratory.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Psycholinguistics
courses.comments: Spanish 124E is the English version of Spanish 124.
courses.description: An introduction to core areas of Spanish psycholinguistics: speech perception, word recognition, language comprehension, language production, first language acquisition, bilingualism, language disorders & aphasiology. Goals: 1)to introduce students to the key findings & central debates within psycholinguistic research; 2)to introduce students to the tools and methods of psycholinguistic research; 3)to introduce students to research practice; 4)to manage effective interaction within the intercultural context. Students will develop an experiment design, and collect/analyze data. Depending on their performance, students will be invited to work and/or volunteer at the Bilingualism, Translation, & Cognition Laboratory. Taught in English.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Introduction to Romance Linguistics
courses.comments: Linguistics 175 and Spanish 125 are the same course.
courses.description: Illustrates principles of comparative-historical linguistic analysis by examining Romance languages (French, Portuguese, etc.) for similarities and differences, and tracing their evolution from Vulgar Latin.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Spanish Cinema
courses.description: Introduces twentieth-century Spain through significant films, analyzing how cinema represents social, political, and cultural issues, as well as key themes, genres, and filmmakers.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Spanish Cinema
courses.comments: Spanish 126E is the English version of Spanish 126.
courses.description: Introduces twentieth-century Spain through significant films, analyzing how cinema represents social, political, and cultural issues, as well as key themes, genres, and filmmakers. Taught in English.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Gastronomy of the Americas through Literature
courses.comments: LAIS/SPAN 127 is the Spanish language version of LAIS/SPAN 127E.
courses.description: An in-depth look at the gastronomy of specific geographical and cultural regions of Latin America through a selection of literary texts and films. From Pre-Columbian to current gastronomical influences from around the world, students will learn about ancient grains, protein alternatives, non-wheat carbohydrates, common herbs and spices in connection with the region in which native people grow, preserve and consume them. Other cultural and culinary influences that have shaped the gastronomy of Latin American today will be emphasized to highlight the fusion and a culinary syncretism observed within the rich and diverse Latin American cuisine. A culinary selection of traditional dishes will be prepared.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Gastronomy of the Americas through Literature
courses.comments: Spanish/LAIS 127E is the English version of Spanish/LAIS 127. LAIS 127E and Spanish 127E are the same course.
courses.description: An in-depth look at the gastronomy of specific geographical and cultural regions of Latin America through a selection of literary texts and films. From Pre-Columbian to current gastronomical influences from around the world, students will learn about ancient grains, protein alternatives, non-wheat carbohydrates, common herbs and spices in connection with the region in which native people grow, preserve and consume them. Other cultural and culinary influences that have shaped the gastronomy of Latin American today will be emphasized to highlight the fusion and a culinary syncretism observed within the rich and diverse Latin American cuisine. A culinary selection of traditional dishes will be prepared. Taught in English.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Creative Writing
courses.description: Designed primarily for students who are inclined to write fictional prose and/or poetry in Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: The Fantastic and Its Development in Spanish-American Short Story
courses.description: Exploration of the multiple manifestations of the Fantastic in Spanish American short story from its origin, linked to nineteenth-century sensationalistic journalism, up to neofantastic mode appearing circa 1950, with its more epistemological goals.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Spanish Golden Age Poetry I
courses.description: Lyric poetry of the sixteenth century: Garcilaso, Luis de Leon, San Juan de La Cruz, and others.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: The Spanish Civil War: Conflict, Culture, and Memory
courses.comments: Spanish 132 is the Spanish version of Spanish 132E.
courses.description: An introduction to the Spanish Civil War (1936-1939), an event that had a tremendous impact over Spains twentieth-century history, culture, and society. Through the study of distinct number of cultural products (memoirs, novels, films, photographs), we cover the social and cultural history of the war, the way it has been represented in different periods of history, as well as why and how it has been the inspiration of many works of art (Picasso), films (Del Toro) and literary pieces (Max Aub) produced all over the world.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: The Spanish Civil War: Conflict, Culture, and Memory
courses.comments: Spanish 132E is the English version of Spanish 132.
courses.description: An introduction to the Spanish Civil War (1936-1939), an event that had a tremendous impact over Spains twentieth-century history, culture, and society. Through the study of distinct number of cultural products (memoirs, novels, films, photographs), we cover the social and cultural history of the war, the way it has been represented in different periods of history, as well as why and how it has been the inspiration of many works of art (Picasso), films (Del Toro) and literary pieces (Max Aub) produced all over the world.Taught in English.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Spanish Laughter: The Politics of Humor in Spain
courses.comments: Spanish 133 is the Spanish version of Spanish 133E.
courses.description: This course presents a historical account of humor in Spain, and the evolution of its political value. Through the analysis of a wide range of cultural artifacts such as short stories, tv shows, films, comic books, and paintings, we will analyze the changing role that humor has played in the Spanish public sphere from the early modern period to the present day, as well as how it has been an important tool that Spaniards have taken advantage of to address different social fears and challenges.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Spanish Laughter: The Politics of Humor in Spain
courses.comments: Spanish 133E is the English version of Spanish 133.
courses.description: This course presents a historical account of humor in Spain, and the evolution of its political value. Through the analysis of a wide range of cultural artifacts such as short stories, tv shows, films, comic books, and paintings, we will analyze the changing role that humor has played in the Spanish public sphere from the early modern period to the present day, as well as how it has been an important tool that Spaniards have taken advantage of to address different social fears and challenges. Taught in English.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Spain at the Crossroads: Tradition and Modernity
courses.description: Selected topics related to the study of the major literary movements and currents of thought in Spanish Literature during the 18th and 19th centuries, such as Enlightenment, "Costumbrismo", Nationalism, Romanticism, Realism, or Naturalism. Analysis of the major poets, playwrights, and novelists of the period. Readings and discussions in Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Modern Mexican Literature
courses.description: Study of texts explaining the development of Mexican culture and literature. Topic and writers: modernism (from Gutierrez Najera to Tablada); the novel of the Mexican revolution (Azuela); and the modern essay (Alfonso Reyes and Octavio Paz).

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Golden Age Drama
courses.description: The classic comedia, by Lope, Tirso, Alarcon, Calderon, and other dramatists.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Golden Age Drama
courses.description: The classic comedia, by Lope, Tirso, Alarcon, Calderon, and other dramatists.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Contemporary Mexican Literature
courses.description: Continued study of major trends in Mexican literature as evidenced in selected works of the following authors: the poetry of Lopez Velarde and Octavio Paz; the contemporaneos (Torres Bodet, Villaurrutia, Pellicer); and contemporary fiction (Yanez, Rulfo, Arreola, and Fuentes).

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: U.S. Latino Literature
courses.description: A comparative study of the literature and culture of the diverse Latino populations of the United States, including Chicano, Puerto Rican, Cuban-American, Dominican-American, and other U.S. Latino groups. Writers, genres, and periods vary from quarter to quarter, emphasizing salient examples of fiction, poetry, drama, the essay, film or art. Taught in English.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Cervantes: Don Quijote
courses.description: Reading and discussion of the first and second parts of Don Quixote.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Contemporary Indigenous Cultures of Mexico
courses.description: Examines the work of writers that have recently provided increased visibility to indigenous languages and cultures in contemporary Mexico, including Nahuatl, Zapotec, and Mayan.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Don Quixote (in English Translation)
courses.description: Reading, examination, and discussion (all in English) of the first part of Cervantes' masterpiece and its reflections on world literature.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Culture and Crisis
courses.description: Traces the ways in which literature represents crisis in different moments of the Spanish history. The course focuses on fundamental concepts like historical memory, bio politics, insecurity and anti-austerity movements in Contemporary Spain.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Spanish for Healthcare
courses.comments: Spanish 145 and LAIS 145 are the same course.
courses.description: Designed for students interested in expanding and applying their knowledge of Spanish to the medical field. Students will learn and apply targeted vocabulary/grammar and develop bicultural/bilingual competency of healthcare issues in Hispanic countries and the US.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Narratives of Identity: Art, Culture and Politics in Spain
courses.description: Focusing on a wide range of its cultural manifestations (Art, Architecture, Cinema, Literature, Language, Gastronomy), this course offers an interdisciplinary approach, conceiving Spain as a multilayered space that is furnished by Roman, French, and Muslim legacies and that drove the shaping of a singular culture.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Business Spanish
courses.description: Real-life situations in the workplace will present students with the appropriate vocabulary for business environments. Students learn to write formal documents, how to express themselves orally, and to assess the business environment of different Spanish-speaking countries from a cultural perspective.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Filmmakers Series
courses.comments: May be repeated to a maximum of 12 units provided the letter designation is different.
courses.description: A focus on some of the most important filmmakers from the Hispanic World (Buuel, Almodvar, Saura, Reygadas). The course follows the development of their careers, analyzing the main topics and contexts

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Almodvar's Spain: Cinema and Society
courses.comments: May be repeated to a maximum of 12 units provided the letter designation is different.
courses.description: This course focuses on analyzing Pedro Almodvar's work in relation to its historical and social context. We will examine some of his most notable films and observe the evolution of his cinematic style. Additionally, we will explore how his films tackle social conflicts that have impacted Spanish society from the end of the Franco dictatorship to the present.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Soccer: The Cultural Impact of a Global Game
courses.comments: Spanish 149 is the Spanish version of Spanish 149E.
courses.description: Soccer is a mirror of our world and an expression of our greatest tragedies and hopes.Thiscourse seeks to use soccer as a tool for learning about politics, economics, culture, society, philosophy, art, literature andthe human condition in the Hispanic world.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Barcelona: The Making of an Urban Landscape
courses.description: Explores the rich history and cultural evolution of Barcelona, one of the most iconic cities in the world. From its humble beginnings as a Roman colony to its current status as a bustling cosmopolitan city, Barcelona has undergone numerous transformations throughout its history. Through a multidisciplinary approach, which includes a combination of films, readings, and other visual materials, we delve into the construction of Barcelona as a modern metropolis and trace the ways in which its cultural legacies are still present in its urban landscape today.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Basque Studies
courses.comments: Spanish 153 is the Spanish version of Spanish 153E.
courses.description: An overview of the cultural and historical characteristics of the Basque Country while analyzing how minoritized groups, such as the Basque, negotiate their identity in the face of globalization.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Basque Studies
courses.comments: Spanish 153E is the English version of Spanish 153.
courses.description: An overview of the cultural and historical characteristics of the Basque Country while analyzing how minoritized groups, such as the Basque, negotiate their identity in the face of globalization. Taught in English.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Basque Language and Culture
courses.description: An intensive course for students with no previous study of the Basque language.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Basque Language and Culture
courses.description: Continues activities commenced in Spanish 154A.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Basque Language and Culture
courses.description: Continues activities commenced in SPAN 154A and SPAN 154B.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Discourses of Love and Desire: from The Book of Good Love to the Present
courses.description: This course sequence (SPAN 155 A - B) traces the literary constructions, elaborations, and treatments of love in Spanish literature from Middle Ages to the present. SPAN 155A (Pre-1700) focuses specifically on the development of courtly love and neoplatonic visions of love in the Iberian Peninsula as they pertain to a variety of literary and cultural forms.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Discourses of Love and Desire: from The Book of Good Love to the Present
courses.description: This course sequence (SPAN 155 A - B) traces the literary constructions, elaborations, and treatments of love in Spanish literature from Middle Ages to the present. SPAN 155B (Post- 1700) explores the psychological and sociological implications and the cultural significance of love in a variety of art forms, poetry, drama, novel and film.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Introduction to Galician Studies
courses.description: The uniqueness of the culture and language of Galicia, its history, ethnography, folklore, and literature, in Galician and Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Exploring Minor Theatrical Genres: Analysis, Writing, and Staging
courses.description: Familiarizes students with a usually understudied field, the "minor" genres of drama during the Golden Age. Combines theory with praxis by asking the students to write and stage their own "minor" texts as a final project for the class. Performances are open to the general public.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Survey of Transborder Cultural Production
courses.description: A general overview of the literature, music, and visual arts created by Transborder cultural producers in the U.S. / México border region. People's socio-historical experiences are examined to understand ethnicity, creativity, and world citizenship.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Literature and Technology in Latin-America
courses.description: Explores how Latin America theoretical discourses have reflected upon technology, including vaccines, agriculture, film and contemporary cyberpunk fiction.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Horror and Mystery
courses.description: A panoramic view of short stories and films belonging to the horror genre in Spain and Latin America. The course offers contextualization and analysis of each story or film. Included are short stories by Espronceda, Bcquer, Ochoa, Zorrilla, Quiroga, Cortzar, Anderson Imbert and films by Gonzlez, Larraaga, Ibez Serrador, Naschy, Franco, Padrn and Brugus.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Nicaraguan Poetry
courses.description: Surveys the poetry of Nicaragua from its origins to the present. It frames key authors and representative poetic texts within their literary and cultural context. Poets include Daro, Corts, Selva, Cuadra, and Belli.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Andean Literature, Music, and Culture
courses.comments: LAIS 165 and SPAN 165 are the same course.
courses.description: This course focuses on literature, music and culture of certain ethnic groups inhabiting the Andean region of South America including, but not limited to, the Aymara and Quechua peoples, their cosmovision and their languages. Through literary texts belonging to different genres, and through films, special attention is placed on expressions of syncretism in seasonal festivals in which pre-Hispanic, European, and African music traditions and religions were shaped due to forced migration, wars and colonization. A strong emphasis on the ecological regions of the nations that share the Andean mountain range contextualizes current indigenous movements of resistance against the degradation of its environment and the impact on its culture.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: The Universe in a Nutshell: J.L. Borges and his Fictions
courses.comments: Spanish 166 is the Spanish version of Spanish 166E.
courses.description: A study of one of the greatest writers of the twentieth century: Jorge Luis Borges. Explores his various creative registers, from his short stories in the vein of fantastic literature, to his poetry and his work as an essayist. The perspective of the course is comparative around topics (some seminal, some relatively unexplored) that Borges treats across a variety of literary genres.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: The Universe in a Nutshell: J.L. Borges and his Fictions
courses.comments: Spanish 166E is the English version of Spanish 166.
courses.description: A study of one of the greatest writers of the twentieth century: Jorge Luis Borges. Explores his various creative registers, from his short stories in the vein of fantastic literature, to his poetry and his work as an essayist. The perspective of the course is comparative around topics (some seminal, some relatively unexplored) that Borges treats across a variety of literary genres. Taught in English.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Posmodernismo
courses.description: Study of the Spanish and Spanish-American Postmodernistas, exploring the link between the culture of modernity and the emergence of a colloquial, prosaic, but lyrical discourse in late nineteenth and twentieth century Spanish and Spanish-American poetry.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Literature and Cultural Identity in the Spanish Caribbean
courses.description: Survey of Spanish Caribbean literature from the standpoint of interaction of culture and race. It traces the counterpoint among the diverse ethnic groups that populate the Caribbean and the manner in which the discourse ofthe oppressor and the oppressed intertwine.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Spain's "Disaster" and the Avant-Garde
courses.description: Focuses on Spain’s political and cultural transformation from the world’s largest empire to an isolated country. The course covers the contentious discussions about the modernization of the country and the irruption of the Avant-Garde

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Latin America on Film
courses.description: An exploration of Latin American film and how this medium represents the cultures, histories and politics of the region. We will study a selection of films encompassing different genres, styles and historical periods, including some key works by influential Latin American filmmakers.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Lorca, Tradition, Modernity, and the Avant Garde
courses.description: A study of Lorcas poetry and theater in the context of the major artistic, sociopolitical and historical transformations of the early 20th century, exploring how traditional Spanish culture and avant-garde innovation intersect each other in his work.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: The Hispanic Novel and Cinema
courses.prereq_text: Spanish 102L OR Spanish 30 (Prerequisite may be taken concurrently).
courses.comments: Same course as LAIS 174.
courses.description: Study of three or four Hispanic novels vis-a-vis their film versions, permitting analysis of narrative in both genres, using existing films and videos based on masterpieces of Hispanic literature. Taught in Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Contemporary Spanish Cultural Studies
courses.description: An interdisciplinary approach to the understanding of present-day Spain, focusing on popular music, TV and literature from the 1960s until today.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Spanish-American Thought
courses.description: Leading social, institutional, intellectual, and artistic trends from the sixteenth century to the present.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Mexican Culture
courses.comments: Not open for credit by students who have taken Spanish 180.
courses.description: Social, institutional, intellectual, and artistic trends in the developmentof modern Mexico.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Chicana/o Novels
courses.comments: Spanish 179 and Chicano Studies 181 are the same course.
courses.description: Reading, analysis and critique of the contemporary Chicano novel as it pertains to the Chicano experience.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Special Topics in Peninsular Literature and Culture
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 20 units, provided letter designation is different.
courses.description: Special topics in Peninsular literature and culture.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Hispanic Poetry: 1900 to 1945
courses.comments: Spanish 181 is the Spanish version of Spanish 181E.
courses.description: Reading and discussion of twentieth-century Spanish and Spanish-American poets and trends in their socio-historical context.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Special Topics in Latin American Literature and Culture
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 20 units, provided the letter designation is different.
courses.description: Special topics in Latin American literature and culture.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Science Fiction in Latin America
courses.prereq_text: Spanish 30 or Spanish 102L (may be taken concurrently).
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 20 units, provided the letter designation is different.
courses.description: An exploration of science fiction narrative and film from Latin America. Through a selection of works by Latin American authors from the early 20th century until the present, we will study how the history, cultures, and traditions of the region have shaped the genre of science fiction, and how this affords a singular perspective to think about topics like technology, neoliberalism, ethnicity, colonialism, the environment, and the future of the planet.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Study of Hispanic Literature by Author or Special Topics
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 20 units, provided letter designation is different. However, only 8 units may be applied towards the Spanish major.
courses.description: Study of Hispanic literature by author or special topics.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Gender in Basque Culture
courses.prereq_text: Spanish 102L or Spanish 30 (may be taken concurrently).
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 20 units, provided letter designation is different. However, only 8 units may be applied towards the Spanish major.
courses.description: Using Basque culture as a case study, this course explores how gender intersects with other crucial issues such as ethnicity, nationhood, and globalization.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Conflict, Memory, and Cultural Production
courses.prereq_text: Spanish 102L or Spanish 30 (may be taken concurrently).
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 20 units, provided letter designation is different.
courses.description: Explores how cultural artifacts like novels and films articulate individual and collective histories of violence.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Basque Studies through Literature and Culture in Translation (Spanish/English)
courses.prereq_text: Spanish 102L or Spanish 30 (may be taken concurrently).
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 20 units, provided letter designation is different. However, only 8 units may be applied towards the Spanish major.
courses.description: Delves deeper into the diversity of topics that make up Basque Studies, and analyses historical, but also contemporary socio-cultural topics related to the Basque country and the Basque diaspora abroad. Can be taken either as a continuation of SPAN 153E or a self-standing course on Basque Studies, where literary and cultural materials are presented in their English, Spanish, and possibly also French translations depending on student interest and language choice.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Basque Film
courses.prereq_text: Spanish 102L or Spanish 30 (may be taken concurrently).
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 20 units, provided letter designation is different.
courses.description: Provides a critical examination of the history and poetics of Basque film from the 20th century to the present.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Contemporary Spanish-American Short Story
courses.description: A study of the trends, themes and techniques of the contemporary Spanish American short story with emphasis on major authors such as Borges, Cortzar, Ocampo, Onetti, Rulfo, Carpentier, Garca Mrquez, and others.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: The Spanish-American Nueva Novela
courses.description: Readings of such authors as Borges, Rulfo Fuentes, Vargas Llosa, Garcia Marquez, Donoso. Emphasis put on the innovative structure and language brought to Hispanic literature by the so-called Nueva Novela.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Selected Topics in Hispanic Linguistics
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 20 units, provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Topics for the course reflect the research interests of faculty members.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Teaching Spanish
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 20 units, provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: An introduction to the field of Second Language Acquisition and Foreign Language Teaching. Special attention will be given to topics that have proved most problematic for native speakers of English who learn Spanish as a second language. After a general overview of Applied Linguistics, the course will cover topics dealing with teaching situations. This course is a theoretical and practical review of how to teach writing, reading, communicative competence, listening comprehension and culture at all levels of Spanish study.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Translation, Technology, and the Mind: An Introduction to Translation and Cognition
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 20 units, provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Translation, Technology, and the Mind is an introduction to technology in translation and interpretation. Students will learn about translation and interpretation, technologies used in the field and in research, and how translation/interpretation is performed in the mind. Throughout the course, students will have the opportunity to reflect on their own uses of technology as they develop their translation and interpretation skills.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Modern Hispanic Drama
courses.description: Representative dramatists of Spain such as Unamuno, Valle-Inclan, Garcia Lorca, Buero Vallejo, and others.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Modernismo
courses.description: Introduction to the poetry and prose of Hispanic Modernismo. Major writers and their most representative works: Marti, Dario, Rodo, Lugones. Lyric poetry, short story, novel, the essay, and other forms are studied.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Vanguard Poetry in Spanish America
courses.comments: LAIS 189 and SPAN 189 are the same course.
courses.description: A survey of the poetry of the Spanish-American avant-guarde focusing on its three main tendencies: colloquial or antipoetic poetry, existentially or politically committed poetry, and self-referential, narcissistic poetry.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Borges and His Precursors
courses.description: This course focuses on Borges the Reader, and traces in particular his affinities with North American and European literatures.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Capstone Seminar - Peninsular Spanish Studies
courses.comments: Recommended major GPA of 3.5 or higher. Recommended cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher.Please see Undergraduate Advisor for approval code.
courses.description: The Capstone Seminar offers outstanding Spanish Majors the opportunity to conduct research alongside M.A. and Ph.D. students in the Department of Spanish and Portuguese. The course aims to improve the students' critical thinking and ability to analyze and contextualize primary and secondary sources within Peninsular Spanish Literature. Students learn to identify and locate reliable sources, compile and present bibliographical data in a consistent format, and improve their ability to write scholarly prose in clear, idiomatic Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Capstone Seminar - Latin American Studies
courses.comments: Recommended major GPA of 3.5 or higher.Recommended cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher.Please see Undergraduate Advisor for approval code.
courses.description: The Capstone Seminar offers outstanding Spanish Majors the opportunity to conduct research alongside M.A. and Ph.D. students in the Department of Spanish and Portuguese. The course aims to improve the students' critical thinking and ability to analyze and contextualize primary and secondary sources within Latin American Literature. Students learn to identify and locate reliable sources, compile and present bibliographical data in a consistent format, and improve their ability to write scholarly prose in clear, idiomatic Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Spanish American Women's Writing
courses.comments: LAIS 194 and SPAN 194 are the same course.
courses.description: An introduction to nineteenth- and twentieth-century Spanish American women's writings. Themes may include women's participation in the formation of national literatures, their engagement with a tradition of women's writing, and issues of authorship and authority.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Senior Honors Independent Research
courses.description: The student will engage in research lead ing to a paper of considerable depth and complexity on a topic dealing with the literature and/or languageof Spain and Spanish America.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Independent Studies in Spanish
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of two upper-division courses in Spanish and consent of department.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
courses.description: Independent studies in selected subjects not covered by course offerings.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Topics in Peninsular Cultural Studies
courses.description: Every iteration of this course will be organized around a different theme. We will include a wide range of cultural productions from Spain, such as films, popular genres, the press, political discourses, and other non-canonical texts and cultural artifacts related to culture as history. The cultural artifacts will be examined by using critical lenses including identity, race, ideology, power, class, andhistorical representation.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Emergency Poetics in Latin America
courses.description: Emergency Poetics in Latin America provides graduate students with the chance to examine art and literature from Latin America and U.S. Latinx communities spanning the 20th and 21st centuries. This approach offers a unique methodology aimed at understanding these cultural expressions within their historical contexts through a transdisciplinary lens. Emergency Poetics utilizes linguistic and formal tools to convey urgent messages in response to imminent dangers, often diverging from established canons. This divergence categorizes works as experimental or impenetrable, allowing them to react dynamically to specific stimuli.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Research Methodologies and Theories of Literatures
courses.description: Approaches and methods for research in Hispanic and Portuguese and Brazilian literatures. Techniques of literary scholarship will also be considered as well as the analysis and application of methods of current literaty theories and criticism.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Women Authors of the Spanish Language
courses.description: An examination of women's strategies of self-figuration, traditions of female expression, women's relationship to authorship and authority, and the relationship of Spanish-language writing to contemporary feminist criticism.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Individual Hispanic Authors and Special Topics
courses.comments: Course may be repeated for a total of 24 units (six courses, each a different author).
courses.description: Intensive study of the work of an individual Hispanic author, to be chosen by the instructor.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Food and Politics in Spain
courses.description: In this graduate seminar, we delve into the complex relationship between food and politics in Spain. We explore how food has played a crucial role in shaping the diverse cultures and national identities within the country. Additionally, we discuss topics such as the significance of "national products" and their role in nation branding, as well as the impact of food scarcity during Franco's dictatorship. Our approach will be multidisciplinary, incorporating scholarly books, cookbooks, and other materials to provide a comprehensive understanding of the topic. Furthermore, we will have guest speakers who will share their expertise and insights on the subject.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Migration, Border Regimes, and Transborder Aesthetics: The U.S.–Mexico Border
courses.description: This graduate seminar examines migration as a structuring force of cultural production at the U.S.–Mexico border. Approaching the border as an aesthetic, political, and epistemological regime, the course analyzes how literature, visual art, film, performance, sound, and digital practices emerge from and intervene in systems of mobility, surveillance, control, and displacement. Drawing on critical migration studies, border theory, decolonial thought, political philosophy, and aesthetic theory, the seminar treats cultural production not just as representation but as a site of theoretical knowledge. While centered on the U.S.–Mexico border, the course situates this region within broader global debates on migration and sovereignty.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Studies in Spanish-American Colonial Literature
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit with the consent of the department graduate adviser.
courses.description: Selected topics from the sixteenth, seventeenth, and eighteenth centuries.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Foreign Language Teaching Methodology
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing and appointment as a teaching assistant or associate in Spanish.
courses.description: Preparation of students to conduct intitial research in areas related to Applied Linguistics, and the application of both theoretical and practical considerations of the current literature on actual teaching.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Capstone Seminar - Peninsular Spanish Studies
courses.description: The Capstone Seminar offers the graduate students from the Spanish and Portuguese Department the opportunity to conduct research alongside upstanding seniors who seek to obtain distinction in the Spanish major. The course offers M.A. and PhD. students the opportunity to hone their critical thinking, oral and writing skills. It also allows the graduate students the chance to mentor their undergraduate classmates by teaching them to analyze and contextualize primary and secondary sources within Peninsular Spanish Literature.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Research Seminar in Spanish-American Literature
courses.description: Primarily intended to train students in research techniques; background material and selection of topic. Completion of research paper, reporting regularly to class on progress of work.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Research Seminar in Spanish-American Literature
courses.description: Primarily intended to train students in research techniques; background material, critical approach, and selection of topic. Completion of research paper, reporting regularly to class on progress of work.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Research Seminar in Spanish Literature
courses.description: Primarily intended to train students in research techniques; background material, critical approach, and selection of topic.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Research Seminar in Spanish Literature
courses.description: Completion of research paper, reporting regularly to class on progress of work.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Topics in Applied Linguistics
courses.comments: Same course as Education 299, French 299, German 299, and Linguistics 299.
courses.description: Specialized topics in the study of applied linguistics.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Teaching Assistant Practicum
courses.comments: Units earned do not apply toward completion of advanced degrees. S/U grading only. Required of all teaching assistants in Spanish.
courses.description: Supervised teaching of lower-division Spanish courses at UCSB. Participation in occasional workshops related to the field of teaching willbe required.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Teaching Associate Practicum
courses.comments: Units earned do not apply toward completion of advanced degrees. S/U grading only. Required of all student associates in Spanish.
courses.description: Supervised teaching of lower-division Spanish courses at UCSB. Participation in occasional workshops related to the field of teaching willbe required.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: A special seminar on research subjects of current interest.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Directed Reading and Research
courses.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; approval of department chair.
courses.description: Individual tutorial. A written proposal for each tutorial must be approved by student's program adviser and by the department chair. The number of units which a student may take in this series depends on the nature of the program and consent of the adviser or the departmental graduate committee.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Individual Study for M.A. Comprehensive and Ph.D. Examinations
courses.comments: No unit credit allowed toward advanced degrees.
courses.description: Individual study for M.A. comprehensive and Ph.D. examinations. Instructor study for M.A. comprehensive and Ph.D. examinations. Instructor should be student's major professor or chair of doctoral committee.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Master's Thesis Research and Preparation
courses.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; approval of department chair.
courses.comments: No unit credit granted toward degree.
courses.description: Only for research underlying the thesis and writing of the thesis.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Ph.D. Dissertation Preparation
courses.description: Ph.D. dissertation preparation. Only for research in preparing and writing of the dissertation. Instructor should be the chair of the student's doctoral committee.

courses.subject: SPAN W
courses.title: Online Elementary Spanish I
courses.comments: No credit can be earned if more advanced credit in the language has already been awarded. Students enrolled in an inappropriate level will be assisted in re-enrolling in the proper course.
courses.description: Span W1 is the first course of the Elementary Spanish three course sequence delivered in a fully online format. By the end of this course students are expected to develop basic proficiency in Spanish at the Novice-mid level.

courses.subject: SPAN W
courses.title: Online Elementary Spanish II
courses.prereq_text: Spanish 1 with a grade of P or a grade of C or higher.
courses.comments: Online version of Span 2 and Span 2SS. Not open for additional units of credit to students who have completed Span 2 and Span 2SS.
courses.description: SPAN W 2 is the second of the three Elementary Spanish courses offered in a fully online format. Its online format combines technology-based language instruction with online class meetings and live guided conversation sessions. Course materials and activities focus on consolidating the same array of skills promoted in the regular Elementary Span II course. Students learn to use Spanish for communication in real, meaningful situations, develop an understanding of basic grammatical concepts and an appreciation of the various cultures of the Spanish-speaking world. Each week, students attend one online class session and one conversation session. There is individual work with the textbook, online materials, and other web-based activities.

courses.subject: SPAN W
courses.title: Online Elementary Spanish III
courses.prereq_text: Spanish 2 with a grade of P or a grade of C or higher.
courses.comments: Online version of Span 3. Not open for additional units of credit to students who have completed Span 3 or Span 3HY. No credit can be earned if more advanced work has been completed.
courses.description: SPAN W3 is the third of the three Elementary Spanish courses offered in a fully online format. Its online format combines technology-based language instruction with online class meetings and live guided conversation sessions. The course materials and activities focus on consolidating the same array of skills promoted in the regular Elementary Spanish III course. Students will learn to use Spanish for communication in real, meaningful situations, develop an understanding of basic grammatical concepts and an appreciation of the various cultures of the Spanish-speaking world. By the end of this course students are expected to develop proficiency at the Novice-high or Intermediate-low level.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Play Analysis
courses.description: Deep study of key concepts used in the analysis of plays in performance, including story, action, genre, liveness, and experience. Includes study of exemplary plays and performances.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Performance in Global Contexts: Africa and the Caribbean
courses.description: Introduction to local performance traditions in Africa and the Caribbean, such as storytelling, ritual, and Carnival. The course also examines how African and Caribbean playwrights put those traditions to social and political uses by incorporating them into post-colonial plays.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Performance in Global Contexts: ASIA
courses.comments: THTR W 2B is the online version of THTR 2B.
courses.description: This course surveys a range of Asian performances across a diversity of locations, from the traditional theater forms of Japanese Kabuki, Indonesian Wayang Kulit, and Indian Kathakali to modern forms in India and Japan to contemporary Chinese performance art. Theater forms like Chinese Jingju and Japanese Noh will prompt us to reevaluate what the performer does in rehearsal and in situations on and off the stage. By exploring recent modern and contemporary performance forms, we will reassess how an actor, dancer, or puppeteer can challenge the status quo and effect change. As we ask these questions, we will situate Asian performance within social, political, and historical contexts to understand its rich functions and significances.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Performance in Global Contexts: EUROPE
courses.description: Introduction to theater and performance practice and traditions in Europe. Topics will include ritual, the rise of a public theater, the political uses of theater, the development of festival theater, and the uses of performance in non-theatrical contexts.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Introduction To Acting
courses.description: An introduction for majors and nonmajors to the multiple problems of the actor's art and craft.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Introduction to Dramatic Writing
courses.comments: THTR 9 and AS AM 79 are the same course.
courses.description: A intensive introduction to playwriting for beginning dramatists. Students will read and analyze the structure of plays, write and stage their own short plays, and gain experience acting in and directing each other's work. Homework for the course includes a series of written and performance-based assignments.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Movement For The Stage
courses.comments: Students must be concurrently enrolled in Theater 15A. Restricted to BFA Acting students.
courses.description: Intense physical training designed to produce a neutral, dynamic, and expressive bodily instrument.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Movement For The Stage
courses.comments: Students must be concurrently enrolled in THTR 15B. Restricted to BFA Acting students.
courses.description: Intense physical training designed to produce a neutral, dynamic, and expressive bodily instrument.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Movement For The Stage
courses.comments: Can be repeated once for credit. Restricted to BFA Acting students.
courses.description: Intense physical training designed to produce a neutral, dynamic, and expressive bodily instrument.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Voice Laboratory
courses.comments: Can be repeated once for credit. Restricted to BFA Acting students.
courses.description: A fundamental approach to voice for the actor with emphasis on vocal production, articulation, and quality; plus physical relaxation techniques.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Voice Laboratory
courses.comments: Can be repeated once for credit. Restricted to BFA Acting students.
courses.description: A fundamental approach to voice for the actor with emphasis on vocal production, articulation, and quality; plus physical relaxation techniques.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Voice Laboratory
courses.comments: Can be repeated once for credit. Restricted to BFA Acting students.
courses.description: A fundamental approach to voice for the actor with emphasis on vocal production, articulation, and quality; plus physical relaxation techniques.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Fundamentals of Acting
courses.comments: Restricted to BFA Acting students. Can be repeated once for credit.
courses.description: Development of the intermediate actor's foundational work in improvisation, technique, scene study, textual analysis, and characterization while exploring creative capacity.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Fundamentals of Acting
courses.comments: Restricted to BFA Acting students. Can be repeated once for credit.
courses.description: Development of the intermediate actor's foundational work in improvisation, technique, scene study, textual analysis, and characterization while exploring creative capacity.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Fundamentals of Acting
courses.comments: Restricted to BFA Acting students. Can be repeated once for credit.
courses.description: Development of the intermediate actor's foundational work in improvisation, technique, scene study, textual analysis, and characterization while exploring creative capacity.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Design Fundamentals for Dance and Theater
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Theater W 19. THTR W 19 is the online version of THTR 19.
courses.description: In this course, you will be introduced to the fundamentals of design for theatre, dance, performance, and live events. You’ll be taught about four disciplines of design including Scenery, Costume, Lighting, and Projection along with a series of approaches to formulate and communicate your own design work to others. Inspired by texts, music, and research, you will create visual designs that express ideas and aesthetic choices while fulfilling practical requirements for the performer or participant in an intentional environment. Through hands-on projects and class activities, you will create designs for live performance through writing, research, 2D media and 3D models.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Scenic Design
courses.comments: Open to non-majors. May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units with instructor consent.
courses.description: Projects in the interpretation of plays through scenic elements with concentration on the design process and the dramatic use of space. Drafting projects including floor plans, elevations and basic perspective drawing.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Stage Lighting Design
courses.comments: Open to non-majors. May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 10 units with instructor consent.
courses.description: Lecture-demonstration in instrumentation, color in light, control equipment, and basic lighting design theories. Technical drawing including light plots, scheduling and organization for lighting design. Some practical application through laboratory and studio exercise.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Dance Lighting Design
courses.description: Lecture-demonstration in instrumentation, color in light, control equipment, and basic lighting theories. practical application through laboratory assignments and studio productions.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Projection Design
courses.description: Exploration of basic elements and principles of projection design for live performance. Projects in the interpretation of plays through visual elements. Introduction to projection, video, and media design for live performance and installation. Projects involve interpretation of plays and music, technical approaches to equipment, and programming equipment for media designs.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Costume Design
courses.comments: Open to non-majors. May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 10 units with instructor consent.
courses.description: In this course students will receive a more detailed, but introductory exposure to the world of costume design. They will learn how costume design plays an essential function in the collaboration of live theatre, opera, television, and film. Students will experience the step-by-step creative process of this design discipline, while implementing strong character analysis skills and recognizing the importance of thematic storytelling. Together, students will learn how to build characters, from the ground up, using the power of dress.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Scenic Practicum
courses.description: Empirical understanding of methods of assembly and materials for stage scenery. Shop organization and operation are experienced during the construction process.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Lighting Practicum
courses.description: Empirical understanding of optical properties of lightin units, available hanging positions and apparatus, lighting control, electrical safety and stage crew organization.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Costume Practicum
courses.description: Empirical understanding of methods of assembly and materials for stage dress. Costume shop organization and operation are experienced during the construction process.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Run Crew Practicum
courses.description: Empirical understanding of backstage organization and operation during live performance.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Costume Construction
courses.description: Introduction to materials and construction techniques used in the production of theatrical costumes.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Theater Games
courses.description: Using theater games, improvisation and storytelling, this course expands the imagination and frees the instincts of the actor. Exercises reflect the work of improvisation icons such as Viola Spolin, Augusto Boal, and Paul Sills. Students also explore techniques for sharing/teaching these games in community settings such as schools, senior citizen centers, etc. Prerequisite: Theater 5 or Instructor's Approval. Highly recommended for students focusing on Theater and Community.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: I.V. Live
courses.comments: A maximum of 16 units of Theater 42 and 142 combined may be accepted for credit in the major.
courses.description: This course produces a weekly performance series in Isla Vista. Students get first-hand experience in the rigors of theatrical production, as they learn to execute all logistical, technical, and promotional details. The course is affiliated with Isla Vista Arts.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Theater Workshop
courses.comments: A maximum of 25 units of Theater 49 and 149 combined may be accepted for credit in the major.
courses.description: Projects in costume, scenery, lighting, acting, directing.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Group Studies For Lower-Division Students
courses.comments: May be repeated for up to 8 units of credit.
courses.description: Special opportunities for study, research, and project preparation.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Introduction to Stage Management
courses.description: Foundational course exploring the full range of duties and responsibilities of a stage manager, a vital role for all theatrical and dance productions.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Playwriting Workshop
courses.comments: ENGL 106A and THTR 104A are the same course. May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units.
courses.description: An exploration of the essential components of playwriting. Exercises focus on writing dialogue, monologue, creating three-dimensional characters, building effective story structures, and developing action through language and stage images. A series of written assignments.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Advanced Playwriting Workshop
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units. Same course as English 106B.
courses.description: A continued exploration of the essential components of playwriting. Writing exercises in dialogue, monologue, character, story structure, action and stage images. Students focus on developing their individual writing voice. A series of written assignments.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Collaboration & Ensemble Devising
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit up to 8 units.
courses.description: Open to playwrights, dancers, directors, actors, and designers. A series of written and ensemble performance-based assignments in which small groups explore different ways of generating and staging new material.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Advanced Movement for the Stage
courses.prereq_text: Theater 10C; concurrent enrollment in Theater 151A. Consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 4 units. Restricted to BFA Acting students.
courses.description: A continuation of the Theater 10 series with increased focus on physical characterization and technical skills.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Advanced Movement For The Stage
courses.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in Theater 151B. Consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 4 units. Restricted to BFA Acting students.
courses.description: A continuation of the Theater 10 series with increased focus on physical characterization and technical skills.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Advanced Movement For The Stage
courses.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in Theater 151C. Consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 4 units. Restricted to BFA Acting students.
courses.description: A continuation of the Theater 10 series with increased focus on physical characterization and technical skills.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Advanced Performance Projects
courses.comments: Restricted to BFA Acting students.
courses.description: Advanced studio projects utilizing the actor's physical and vocal skills to develop original theater.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Advanced Voice Laboratory
courses.comments: Restricted to BFA Acting students.
courses.description: Advanced problems in voice for the actor with continued emphasis on craft, plus the creative and expressive uses of the voice with the body.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Advanced Voice Laboratory
courses.comments: Restricted to BFA Acting students.
courses.description: Advanced problems in voice for the actor with continued emphasis on craft, plus the creative and expressive uses of the voice with the body.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Advanced Voice Laboratory
courses.comments: Restricted to BFA Acting students.
courses.description: Advanced problems in voice for the actor with continued emphasis on craft, plus the creative and expressive uses of the voice with the body.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Senior Voice Laboratory
courses.comments: Restricted to BFA Acting students. May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 4 units.
courses.description: Seminar in advanced voice work for senior students in B.F.A.-Acting program. Concentration on projects to find a personal voice in the theatre.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Design Critical Studies
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 10 units with instructor consent.
courses.description: This course introduces advanced design and directing students to key concepts and skills that promote successful theatrical collaboration. Directing and design teams will research all aspects of a play and develop a proposed unified production using a shared verbal and visual language.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Advanced Scenic Design
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 10 units with instructor consent.
courses.description: This course builds upon tools learned in THTR 22: Beginning Set Design to increase fluency in scenic design approaches and techniques. Focusing on building ideas from texts and music, you will evolve design approaches through research and critiques. Designs will culminate in scale models and supporting materials. Projects in THTR 122 will focus on opera, dance, and musical theatre with unique scenic demands including multiple locations, period detail, and awareness of performance styles and conventions.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Advanced Stage Lighting Design
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 10 units with instructor consent.
courses.description: Lecture-demonstration of controllable properties and functions of light. Includes technical drawing: light plots, scheduling and organization for lighting design, drawing using light and shadow, perspective drawing. Practical application through studio exercise.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Design Portfolio
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 10 units with instructor consent.
courses.description: This course will introduce students to advanced topics in the art and craft of visual media design for projection and video with an emphasis on live performance.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Advanced Costume Design
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 10 units.
courses.description: In this course students will receive an advance and detailed perspective on the art of costume design. Through four different projects, they will explore different character development experiences, with a continued focus on thematic storytelling. Together, students will learn how to craft character, while focusing on the scope of a full production.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Theatre Rendering Techniques
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 6 units with instructor consent.
courses.description: Advanced theatre rendering techniques for the theatre designer. Continued development in drawing and use of different mediums. Concentration on rendering light, shadow, and texture.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: History of Decorative Styles
courses.description: A survey of the evolution of design styles and production trends in western theater, emphasizing the history of design and designers, including a study of both interior and exterior decoration with concentration on furnishing, accessories and the changing patterns of culture.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Puppet Design and Construction
courses.description: Explores the history of various puppet styles and will focus on the design and creation of three iconic puppet forms: Thai shadow puppets (Nang yai), rod puppets (Bunraku), and marionettes. Students will learn both the mechanical aspects and the artistic design elements of puppet creation by creating one of each of these three styles.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Advanced Acting Workshop I
courses.description: Advanced exploration, performances, and criticism of scenes from a broad range of dramatic scripts with focus on the actor's perspective.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Advanced Acting Workshop II
courses.description: Further exploration of performances and criticism of scenes from a broad range of dramatic scripts with focus on the actor's perspective.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: I.V. Live
courses.comments: A maximum of 16 units of Theater 42 and 142 combined may be accepted for credit in the major.
courses.description: This course produces a weekly performance series in Isla Vista. Students get first-hand experience in the rigors of theatrical production, as they learn to execute all logistical, technical and promotional details. The course is affiliated with Isla Vista Arts.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: The People's Voice
courses.comments: A maximum of 8 units of Theater 43 and 143 combined may be accepted for credit in the major.
courses.description: Students and teens from the community collaborate in writing, crafting, and performing an epic myth through the lens of their personal stories.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Shakespeare Production
courses.comments: A 2-quarter, in-progress sequence with both grades given upon completion of Theater 144B.
courses.description: Students study, rehearse and produce one of Shakespeare's plays. The class culminates with performances that are open to the public during the final week. Students can participate as actors, assistant directors, designers or stage managers.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Shakespeare Production
courses.comments: A 2-quarter, in-progress sequence with both grades given upon completion of Theater 144B.
courses.description: Students study, rehearse and produce one of Shakespeare's plays. The class culminates with performances that are open to the public during the final week. Students can participate as actors, assistant directors, designers or stage managers.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Launch Pad: New Plays in Process
courses.description: Working with the artistic director of LAUNCH PAD and 3 professional playwrights, this 3-week intensive course workshops a new play every week. Student actors, directors, designers, dramaturgs, playwrights, and stage managers learn the vital skills of working on new plays in the earliest stages of their development. The workshop culminates in an invited public reading at the end of each week. Over the 3 weeks, participants have the opportunity to take on different functions in the process.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Theatre Workshop
courses.comments: A maximum of 25 units of Theater 49 and 149 combined may be accepted for credit in the major.
courses.description: Projects in costume, scenery, lighting, acting, directing.

courses.subject: THTR

courses.prereq_text: Theater 15C and 188S; concurrent enrollment in Theater 110A and 111A. Consent of instructor.
courses.comments: Can be repeated once for credit. Restricted to BFA Acting students.
courses.description: Scene work and exercises exploring various acting styles which may include Shakespeare, Boal, Artaud, Greek, period comedy and farce, and Absurd.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Advanced Acting
courses.prereq_text: Theater 15C and 188S; concurrent enrollment in Theater 110B and 111B. Consent of instructor.

courses.description: Scene work and exercises exploring various acting styles which may include Shakespeare, Boal, Artaud, Greek, period comedy and farce, and Absurd.
