courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Advanced Acting: Modern Trends
courses.comments: Restricted to BFA Acting students.
courses.description: Study and performance of contemporary acting developments.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Senior Auditions
courses.comments: Restricted to BFA Acting students.
courses.description: Preparation and study of material and techniques for professional and graduate school audition.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Alternate Acting Styles
courses.comments: Restricted to BFA Acting students.
courses.description: Continued work in performance styles and other skills.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Senior One-Person Shows
courses.description: Individually researched performance projects.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Introduction to Stage Directing
courses.description: Basic principles of directing. Lectures, demonstrations, and small practical projects offer the non-specialist and potential directing concentration student a broad understanding of the directorial process.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Techniques of Directing
courses.description: Laboratory in directorial scene work. Students take on scenes from contemporary plays. Focus is on text analysis, visual storytelling, and collaboration with actors.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Advanced Directing
courses.description: Advanced directing techniques and scene work, including departures from realism. Students also learn about collaboration with designers.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Directorial Production
courses.description: Full directorial responsibility for the mounting of a one-act play.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Projects in Directing
courses.description: Full directorial responsibility for the mounting of a second one-act play or other special project.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Projects in Design and Production
courses.description: Special projects in each area of concentration.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Applied Theater/The Artist as Activist - Basics
courses.description: The Artist as Activist Basics introduces the student to the fundamentals of Applied Theater through examination of theory, history and imagining as a preparation for application and fieldwork. The course prepares the student to implement a project in the community. The project can be teaching or performance based. In addition to developing as researchers and theater activists, students will learn about the producing, promotional and ethical dimensions of self-starting a Theater & Community initiative.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: American Drama to 1940
courses.description: History of the American drama and theater from early years to 1940. Important plays, performers, institutions, and styles of production are given selective attention.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: American Drama 1940 to Present
courses.description: History of the American drama and theater from 1940 to the present. Important plays, performers, institutions, and styles of production are given selective attention.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Contemporary American Drama and Theater
courses.description: Close study of major playwrights, directors, solo performance artists, and other artists working in the contemporary American theater, mainstream and avant-garde. Writing assignments focus on developing critical arguments about new work.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Latin American Theater and Performance
courses.description: Survey of Hispanic-American drama and theory including authors like Carballido, Gambaro, Marques, Triana, Valdez, and others.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Culture Clash: Studies in U.S. Latino Theater
courses.description: A survey, in English, of the dramatic literature of U.S. Latinos from 1965 to the present. Includes history and criticism of the theater of Chicano, Puerto Rican, Cuban, and other Americans of Hispanic origin in the U.S.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Asian American Theater
courses.comments: Same course as AS AM 125.
courses.description: Overview of Asian American theater and its political and artistic achievements, from foundational Asian American theater companies and playwrights to contemporary performance artists. Issues addressed include race and ethnicity, gender and sexuality, and intergenerational conflict.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Race, Gender, and Performance
courses.description: Comparative analysis of contemporary American plays and performances by artists of diverse gender, sexual, ethnic, and racial backgrounds. Students learn to perceive and critically respond to race and gender issues in plays and the theatrical production.

courses.subject: THTR

courses.description: Special topics in African and Caribbean performance.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Cross-Cultural Studies in Theater and Drama
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Special topics in cross-cultural studies in theater and drama.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Special Topics in Cross Cultural Studies Theater and Drama
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Sport as Performance: The Climbing Body in Theater and Film. This class examines how rock climbers and mountaineers embody stories in theater and film. Through the lens of performance studies, this class asks how athletic and sporting bodies reinforce, disrupt, or complicate dominant cultural and social narratives.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Performance Studies
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Special topics in performance studies.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Creative Arts, Memories and Experimental Performance
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Through creative arts practices, analysis, workshops and new performance, this course explores processes of transformation and translation of traces of memories and experiences into provocative art works. Experimental performance practices encompass theatrical, movement based, sonic, music-based and visual arts.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Introduction to Performance Studies
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: An introduction to performance studies.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Sport as Performance: The Climbing Body in Theater and Film
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Explores rock climbing and mountaineering as performance in theater and documentary film. Classes consist of lectures, guest speakers, film viewing, and discussion where we interrogate what it means to be a performer in a sport like climbing. In looking at climbers of different lived experiences, this class offers new understandings of the study of sport through performance, how the climbing body informs our understanding of the role of the actor, and how the performing body disrupts or upholds dominant cultural and social narratives.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: History of Performance
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Special topics in the history of performance.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: History of Directing
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Special topics in the history of directing.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Shakespeare on Film and Stage
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: An investigation of Shakespeare's plays through the media of performance; viewing of Shakespearean productions on film and videotape, in calssroom rehearsal, and in stage performances as available; reading and critical analysis of selected Shakespearean plays.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Production Administration
courses.comments: May be repeated for up to six units of credit.
courses.description: Workshop for advanced students functioning as assistants to directors, designers, and technical directors. portfolio, promptbook, or paper required.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Senior Honors Project
courses.comments: Students must have a 3.0 university grade-point average; 3.4 departmental grade-point average, unless exempt by petition; faculty nomination. This course is for students who will complete their projects in one quarter. A final grade will be assigned upon completion.
courses.description: Senior honors project. Advanced thesis project in either academic researchor creative activity, supervised by a faculty adviser. Students successfully completing the project, as evalutated by a three-person committee, will graduate with distinction in the major.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Senior Honors Project
courses.comments: Students must have 3.0 university GPA; 3.4 depart. GPA; faculty nomination.4 to 8 units required in honors sequence; minimum of 2 units per quarter. Course is the 1st in sequence for students who will complete their projects in either 2 or 3 quarters. An "in-progress" grade will be assigned; students may then enroll in either DA 193HB or 193HC.
courses.description: Senior honors project. Advanced thesis project in either academic research or creative activity, supervised by a faculty advisor. Students successfully completing the project, as evaluated by a three-person committee, will graduate with distinction in the major.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Senior Honors Project
courses.comments: Four to eight units required in the honors sequence; minimum two units per quarter. This course is the second in the sequence for students who will complete their projects in three quarters. An "in-progress" grade will be assigned; students will then enroll in Dramatic Art 193HC.
courses.description: Senior honors project. Advanced thesis project in either academic research or creative activity, supervised by a faculty advisor. Students successfully completing the project, as evaluated by a three-person committee, will graduate with distinction in the major.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Senior Honors Project
courses.comments: Four to eight units required in the honors sequence; minimum two units per quarter. This course is the final in the two or three quarter sequence. A final grade will be assigned upon completion.
courses.description: Senior honors project. Advanced thesis project in either academic research or creative activity, supervised by a faculty advisor. Students successfully completing the project, as evaluated by a three-person committee, will graduate with distinction in the major.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Group Studies in Acting and Directing
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 16 units.
courses.description: Intensive study, research, and project preparation in acting and directing.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Group Studies in Design
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 16 units.
courses.description: Intensive study, research, and project preparation in theatrical design.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Group Studies in Literature
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 16 units.
courses.description: Intensive study, research, and project preparation in dramatic literature.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Group Studies in Theatre
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 16 units.
courses.description: Intensive study, research, and project preparation in theatre.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Principles of Stage Management
courses.description: Upper division course that builds upon the foundational information of THTR 95, providing a greater depth and breadth of exploration into the duties of the stage manager from pre-production through strike. Topics include communication, organizational skills, rehearsal procedures, and performance responsibilities. Greater stage management practical experience gained through in-class exercises and outside assignments.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Stage Management Practicum
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 16 units.
courses.description: Production oriented course allowing student practical experience in stage management training. Student will serve as assistant stage manager or stagemanager for a main stage or student directed departmental production.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Dance Production
courses.prereq_text: Theater 19; 22 or 123 or 125; upper-division standing; consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 16 units, only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
courses.description: Exploration of the process of collaboration between dance choreographers and theater designers in the development of designs for dance productions. Final project is a public performance of the choreographers' and designer' work.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Independent Studies in Theater
courses.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; completion of 2 upper-division courses in Theater.
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
courses.description: Independent studies in theater.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Research Methods in Theater, Dance and Performance Studies
courses.description: Introduction to select methods for conducting advanced research in theatre, drama, and performance. Students will read exemplary monographs and statements of method from leading scholars in the field. They will then practically apply those methods to an original, ongoing research project that will culminate in a substantive seminar paper.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Research Methods: Ethnography and Performance
courses.description: Introduction to select methods for conducting advanced research in theatre, drama, and performance. The methodological focus, which varies according to instructor, may include ethnography, historiography, dramatic criticism, phenomenology, or audience reception, among others. Students will read exemplary monographs and statements of method from leading scholars in the field. They will then practically apply those methods to an original, ongoing research project that will culminate in a substantive seminar paper.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Critical Methods
courses.description: This seminar introduces critical methods central to the fields of Theater, Dance, and Performance Studies.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Historiography
courses.description: Covers diverse methods and theoretical approaches of historiography of performance and performance as historiography. Readings trouble ideas of history production and understandings of the past. We explore past assumptions about subject, time, and place central to traditional historiographical methods and identify new approaches and directions. And, we consider how theoretical and methodological approaches under the umbrella of historiography adjust to reflect changes in understandings of people, places, and systems of knowledge.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Theories for Performance, Theater, and Dance Research
courses.description: Introduction to key theories and conceptual frameworks for conduction advanced research in theater, dance, and performance studies. Students will read exemplary theoretical texts from established and newer scholarly voices. Topics vary and may include Marxism, Brecht, Artaud, theories fo the avant-garde, psychoanalysis, critical race theory, feminism, structuralism, post-structuralism, postmodernism, postcolonialism, and transnationalism.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Theories of the Everyday and Performance
courses.description: Examines theories of the everyday that relate to theater, dance, and performance studies.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Theories for Performance, Theater, and Dance Research
courses.description: Examines and reevaluates performance theory and its application with attention to global theater forms and performance practices.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Histories of Theater, Dance, and Performance Studies
courses.description: Introduction to pre-1900 historical time periods in theater, dance, and performance studies. Students read exemplary historical texts and learn key historiographical methods from established and newer scholarly voices. Periods and topics vary and may include material conditions of performance, gender and sexuality studies, global theater and dance, and embodied and dramaturgical approaches to dance and theater history.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Modern and Contemporary Theory
courses.description: A graduate level introduction to twentieth and twenty-first century critical theory. Topics vary and may include Marxism, Brecht, Artaud, theories of the avant-garde, psychoanalysis, feminism, structuralism, post-structuralism, postmodernism, and postcolonialism.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Topics in Dramatic Literature and Theatre History
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit.
courses.description: A survey course that introduces students to a range of historical periods, dramatic work, playwrights, artistic movements, and theatrical trends. Topics vary and may include classics in performance, translating drama, global theatre, violence in drama, dramatic genre, and literature and theatre.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Shakespeare Beyond the Global
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit.
courses.description: Shakespeare has reigned as a global phenomenon in text, performance and film for over thirty years. But why? What is a global Shakespeare? How was a global Shakespeare devised? Can we move beyond the global? Can we think beyond the global? By considering these lines of inquiry, this seminar seeks to investigate the formations of Shakespeare as a global icon, global commodity, and global performance framework. We will also think through the violent histories of colonialism, racialization and empire that undergird the "Global Shakespeare '' movement. Authors and practitioners include: Preti Taneja, Kim F. Hall, Alexa Joubin, Ambereen Dadabhoy, Vishal Bharadwaj, Akira Kurosawa, Madeline Sayet, Sujata Iyengar, Ruben Espinosa, Gauri Viswanathan.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Playwriting and Dramaturgy
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit.
courses.description: An investigation of the art of playwriting in terms of the dramaturgy of how plays work.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Topics in Dramatic Literature, Theatre History, and Performance Practices
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit.
courses.description: This course investigates the intersections between art, literature, philosophy, and performance practices. It may include specific histories of theatre and performance, conceptual frames across cultures, genre studies, issues of translation, postcolonial analysis, and other topics.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: The Fate of Ophelia: Shakespeare and Popular Culture
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit.
courses.description: This graduate seminar examines how Shakespeare circulates through contemporary popular culture. Though rooted in the early modern stage, Shakespeare's characters, plots, and language now form a global cultural vocabulary, appearing across film, television, music, fashion, advertising, and digital media. The course treats Shakespeare not as fixed canon but as a dynamic cultural resource that artists and audiences continually transform to speak to new historical moments. Drawing on adaptation studies, performance theory, and cultural criticism, the seminar explores why Shakespeare remains so culturally influential and how his works move across media and genres

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Special Topics in Performance Studies
courses.description: Varies in content from year to year, but offerings may include studies of the avant-garde and performance art, sport as ritual and performance, theatre on trial, politics and war as performance, embodiment, and global performance traditions.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Border Crossings: Exilic Experience in the Making of American Dance
courses.description: Border Crossing challenges accepted histories of dance modernism to consider how war, inequality, and injustice shaped twentieth century performance art. This graduate seminar bears witness to the exiled and marginalized dance artist - the Unsung - whose artistry, oftentimes invisible, is vital to the history of dance.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Special Topics in Performance Studies
courses.description: Exploration of the history and theory of story and storytelling, both in its relation to dramatic and/or choreographed plot and as a performance mode in itself.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Critical Dance Studies: Special Topics in Dance History and Theory
courses.description: This graduate seminar provides an introduction to the history and critical theory of dance inglobal contexts. The methodologicalfocus may include critical dance studies, historiography,ethnography, feminist theory, critical race theory, body theory - corporealities - art and architectural(site-specific performance) theory, and performance studies. Students read and analyze a widearray of critics, scholars, and artists and demonstrate fluency in critical dance studies through writtenpapers and weekly seminar discussion. Live Performance serves as archival source material.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Defiant Bodies: Art, Dance, Digital Media
courses.description: Defiant Bodies: Art, Dance, Digital Media surveys an interdisciplinary array of visual art, digital media, and live performance. Together, we identify historiographic relationships between protest culture, human philosophy, and performance.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Border Crossings: Exilic Experience in the Making of Modern Dance
courses.description: Border Crossings: Exilic Experience in the Making of American Dance, challenges previous histories of transglobal modernism to consider how war, inequality, and injustice shaped twentieth century performance art. The intellectual, pedagogical, and spiritual embodiment of a bicoastal exhibit and performance series, together as an intellectual community of scholar-artists, we investigate definitions of exile and exilic modernism as each engenders methodologies in the fields of Dance Studies and Performance Studies.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Body and Performance  An Introduction to Critical Dance Studies as Curatorial Practice
courses.description: Body and Performance is meant to introduce students to the fields of Dance Studies and Curatorial Practice, as well as to performative moments in the history of dance. We will learn to theorize the body in performance, and discuss how to curate the body in performance in found spaces. Part dance—history, criticism, ethnography, and body theory—and part curation—site-specific performance art—we will pursue a wide range of texts and performative works of art in a multiplicity of architectural spaces and stylistic genres. Designed as an introduction to dance and museum studies, Critical Dance Studies as Curatorial Practice is ultimately concerned with the historical, artistic, and physical spaces in which performance takes place.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Dancing the Diaspora
courses.description: Dancing the Diaspora traces a genealogy of dance and choreographic practice in the Afro-Caribbean and American worlds. We examine a range of interdisciplinary texts, from theoretical discourses surrounding a range of issues -- diasporic identity, dance histories of religious and concert stage traditions, and art historical texts that deepen our aesthetic understanding of dancing bodies in West African and Africanist religious ritual and secular performance.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Diaspora and Performance: Transnational Studies in Exile, Embodiment, and Visual Art
courses.description: Diaspora and Performance: Transnational Studies in Exile, Embodiment, and Visual Art is a new graduate seminar that considers the historical condition of diasporic performance art. Furthermore, we study the ability of artists to translate exilic experience into artistic identity and materialist phenomenology; or, to be in exile in art.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Diaspora and Performance: Transnational Studies in Exile, Embodiment and Visual Art
courses.description: Diaspora and Performance: Transnational Studies in Exile, Embodiment, and Visual Art is a new graduate seminar that considers the historical condition of diasporic performance art. Furthermore, we study the ability of artists to translate exilic experience into artistic identity and materialist phenomenology; or, to be in exile in art.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Contemporary American Dance During the Cold War Era
courses.description: Contemporary American Dance During the Cold War Era is an interdisciplinary graduate seminar that examines how geopolitics have shaped the American stage. In an era of McCarthyism, overt patriotism, and covert nation-building, we study how the U.S. State Department used dance and dancing bodies to advertise American democracy to the world.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Critical Dance Studies: Special Topics in Dance History and Theory
courses.description: This graduate seminar provides an introduction to the history and critical theory of dance in global contexts. The methodological focus may include critical dance studies, historiography, ethnography, feminist theory, critical race theory, body theory - corporealities - art and architectural (site-specific performance) theory, and performance studies. Students will read and analyze a wide array of critics, scholars, and artists and demonstrate fluency in critical dance studies through written papers and weekly seminar discussion. Live Performance will serve as archival source material.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: The Performance of Physicality
courses.description: The Performance of Physicality explores history’s relationship to and artists’ perception of the body in performance and visual art. Crossing borders and time, we study theories of physicality and assess visual and theatrical representations. We will consider how we come to assess the physical world through visuality.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Performance of Physicality
courses.description: Explores various case studies of the theatrical representation and perception of the human body in Europe, the Americas, and Asia in the twentieth century especially related to the construction of gender, race, class, nation,and sexuality.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Contemporary American Dance during the Cold War Era
courses.description: An interdisciplinary graduate seminar that examines how racism, immigration, imagination, and geopolitics have shaped perceptions of the dancing body in both classical and contemporary dance. Dance Studies course that examines how racism in the United States has shaped and been shaped by the American stage. In an era of overt patriotism and nation-building, we study how the dancers and choreographers themselves contributed to the racialization bodies in motion.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Directing for Graduate Students
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units.
courses.description: An investigation of the fundamentals and techniques of directing, including principles of staging, text analysis, and actor coaching.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Practice in Design
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units.
courses.description: Projects and study in design; practical application to projects.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Practice in Dramaturgy
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units.
courses.description: Projects in dramaturgy; practical applications and projects.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Practice in Directing
courses.prereq_text: Theater 221 or 261; graduate standing; consent of instructor.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units.
courses.description: Advanced problems in directing, practical applications, and projects. Culminates in directing one-act plays.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Practice in Playwriting
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units.
courses.description: An independent study in playwrighting. Students may work on a full-length play, a one act play, a solo performance text.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Practice in Theatre and Dance
courses.description: Projects in various areas of theatre and dance, including acting, stage management, production and directing.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: European Theatre and Drama
courses.description: An examination of theatrical and dramatic traditions of Europe. Offerings vary, but may include ancient and medieval drama and theatre, the Renaissance, Shakespeare, as well as Enlightenment, Sturm and Drang and Romanticism, Realism, Naturalism, and Symbolism.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Theatre and Drama of the United States
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit.
courses.description: An examination of trends and traditions in theatre of the United States. Roots of Broadway, U.S. Latino theatre, Asian American theatre, melodrama, the Group Theatre and its legacy, multicultural theatre and contemporary theater.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Teaching: Methods and Practice
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing and current appointment as a departmental teaching assistant.
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit. Required of all teaching assistants. S/U grade.No unit credit allowed toward advanced degrees.
courses.description: Introduction to the problems and techniques of teaching dramatic art, through teaching responsibilities in departmental courses and through consultation with supervising faculty members.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Directed Reading and Research
courses.description: Individual tutorial. A written proposal for each tutorial must be approved by the department chair.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Master's Thesis Project, Research and Creative
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of eight units. No unit credit allowed toward advanced degrees.
courses.description: Master's thesis project, research and creative.

courses.subject: THTR
courses.title: Dissertation Research and Preparation
courses.prereq_text: Consent of chair of student's doctoral committee. (Repeatable to 108 units - not 99).
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 108 units. S/U grading. No unit credit allowed toward advanced degree.
courses.description: Dissertation research and preparation.

courses.subject: THTR W
courses.title: Performance in Global Contexts, Asia
courses.comments: THTR W 2B is the online version of THTR 2B.
courses.description: This course surveys a range of Asian performances across a diversity of locations, from thetraditional theater forms of Japanese Kabuki, Indonesian Wayang Kulit, and Indian Kathakali tomodern forms in India and Japan to contemporary Chinese performance art. Theater forms like Chinese Jingju and Japanese Noh will prompt us to reevaluate what the performer does in rehearsal and in situations on and off the stage. By exploring recent modern and contemporary performance forms, we will reassess how an actor, dancer, or puppeteer can challenge the status quo and effect change. As we ask these questions, we will situate Asian performance within social, political, and historical contexts to understand its rich functions and significances.

courses.subject: THTR W
courses.title: Design Fundamentals for Dance and Theater
courses.comments: THTR W 19 is the online version of THTR 19.
courses.description: Lectures, demonstrations and projects to provide an understanding of the stage design process for theater and dance. Study of the elements, principles, terminology, and basic techniques. Exploration of the communicative and collaborative process between designer and choreographer/director. Concentration in scenic, costume, and lighting design.

courses.subject: THTR W
courses.title: The People’s Voice/The Odyssey Project
courses.comments: THTR W 43 is the online version of THTR 43.
courses.description: A collaborative theater program between the Theater Department at the University of California, Santa Barbara (UCSB), and County of Santa Barbara Probation. Student participants from both institutions will partner in a work setting that fosters equity to process and perform original performance pieces using analog and digital technology. The framework for this class is ancient Greek canonical literature with healing and heroic dimensions. The Odyssey of Homer provides the template. Through a series of writing and drawing exercises, the participants discover the heroic elements in their lives and how to utilize them to tell the Odyssey story in their own words.

courses.subject: THTR W
courses.title: The People’s Voice/The Odyssey Project
courses.comments: THTR W 143 is the online version of THTR 143
courses.description: A collaborative educational theater program between the Theater Department at the University of California, Santa Barbara (UCSB), and County of Santa Barbara Probation. Student participants from both institutions will partner in a work setting that fosters equity to process and perform original performance pieces using analog and digital technology. The framework for this class is ancient Greek canonical literature with healing and heroic dimensions. The Odyssey of Homer provides the template. Through a series of writing and drawing exercises, the participants discover the heroic elements in their lives and how to utilize them to tell the Odyssey story in their own words.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Issues in Technology, Business, and Society
courses.description: Lecture series where entrepreneurial, technological, business, and governmental leaders share their lessons of experience and discuss current business issues. For anyone interested in entrepreneurship, management, technology development, and commercialization and the impact that innovation has on society.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Fundamentals of Business Strategy
courses.description: An introduction to business strategy, principles and practices required for business success in the competitive market place. Students are exposed to key management theories, models and tools including competitive strategy, finance, planning, new product development, marketing, leadership and others.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Entrepreneurship
courses.description: Learn how to start any type of venture; for profit, non-profit, service, sole-proprietorship, with a focus on high-tech ventures. Analysis of new business opportunities, development of customer-centric value propositions, financing, marketing, selling, and protection of intellectual property.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Principles of Marketing
courses.description: Introduces fundamental principles, processes, and tools of marketing which are used to create, communicate and deliver the value of products and services to customers, clients, partners, and society. This is done with an array of essential topics, such as the identification of customer needs and wants, assessment of the competitive environment, selection of the most appropriate target opportunities, development of an integrated marketing strategy, and disciplined execution.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Fundamentals of Business Finance
courses.comments: Not open to students who have completed TMP X130F through PaCE.
courses.description: Students learn essential tools to understand and analyze financial information and financing strategies for ongoing and new business ventures. This course is designed for those who will be participating in the decision-making processes of a small to large size business organization either as an analyst or an operating manager. Major topics covered include financial analysis and management, time value of money, interpreting financial statements and their analysis, cash flow analysis, capital budgeting, project evaluation, financial decision making, and valuing an existing or new venture. In addition to the practical application of financial theory, you will be asked to solve several business case studies.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Understanding and Managing Technology Organizations
courses.description: Participating in, managing and leading successful careers, teams and organizations. Current theories and practices concerning motivation, organizational culture, communications, effective decision making, team effectiveness and others are presented and discussed.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Introductions to Patents and Intellectual Property
courses.description: Provides emerging inventors, entrepreneurs, and scientists with a working knowledge of intellectual property (patents, copyrights, trademarks, and trade secrets), with the main focus being on patents. Will cover the basic functions of patents, structure of patents, and patent prosecution.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: New Product Development
courses.description: New product development requires technical and non-technical business persons to work across disciplines. Instruction is provided in a wide range of topics concerning customer driven product innovation. Students learn new product development processes, tools, techniques, and organizational skills.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Understanding AI in Business: Core Foundations of Business Strategy
courses.description: Aims to equip students with a fundamental understanding of the relationship between AI technology and business strategy. Begins with the basic mathematical foundations of AI. Introduces the technical foundations of AI, highlighting the roles played by the hardware, infrastructure, and application layers. Building on these dual foundations, students learn to analyze these different AI segments. Various business models will be introduced to help assess the competitive advantages across the AI segments. Finally, explores how AI can be strategically applied across different industries and sectors to drive innovation and business development.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Investment & Financial Management
courses.description: Achieving superior investment results within acceptable risk parameters is often deemed the top challenge for Wealth Managers. This is especially so in the face of fluctuating economics and shifting investor goals. A portfolio's "integrity" e.g., how well it is balanced, often drives performance and volatility. Takes a comprehensive approach to portfolio construction and management and explores how prevailing macro-economic conditions and investor priorities can be translated into viable investment strategies. Theory is balanced with actual case study scenarios to demonstrate how course concepts are practiced in the real world.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Leadership in Technology & Innovation
courses.description: Explores the dynamic intersection of leadership, technology, and innovation. Designed for undergraduate students from all disciplines, it delves into the essential skills and knowledge needed to effectively lead in today's rapidly evolving technological landscape. Students gain a comprehensive understanding of how leadership principles apply within the context of technology creation, development, and implementation.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Negotiation
courses.description: Unlock the art and science of negotiation in this dynamic, hands-on course designed to help you build the skills needed to succeed in both personal and professional settings. Learn how to effectively communicate, identify win-win solutions, and confidently navigate high-stakes discussions. Through interactive case studies, readings, and role-playing exercises, develop strategies for resolving conflicts, influencing outcomes, and creating lasting agreements. Whether negotiating a salary, business deal, or group project, this course equips students with essential tools to negotiate successfully a range of situations. Perfect for students from all majors looking to enhance their career readiness.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Market Research
courses.description: Provides a high level introduction to modern marketing research. Course covers the fundamental principles and techniques for market validation that are critical to launch, grow, and sustain a viable business.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Sport Business Strategy & Innovation
courses.description: An introduction to the creative business strategies of building (planning, organizing, implementing, and evaluating) a sport organization, with a particular emphasis on major and minor league professional sports. Explores traits of creative thinking and decision making theories in application towards selecting a hosting city, site assessment, arena/stadium financials, roster assembly, sales tactics, and marketing initiatives, among other areas. Moreover, students investigate consumer behavior elements to determine target audience criteria and its alignment with brand identity, partnership opportunities, and communication strategies.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Venture Capital / Private Equity
courses.description: Provides an overview of how VC and PE firms operate. Topics include how VC/PE firms are structured and how they manage a fund over the course of its life cycle: raising a fund, sourcing deals, evaluating investment opportunities, valuing businesses, negotiating term sheets with entrepreneurs, adding value to portfolio companies, and exiting investments. White this takes the perspective of the investor, also covers the funding life cycle of a typical start-up with an emphasis on what the roles of VC and PE are relative to other sources of financing. Course material will be presented primarily through case studies and selected readings.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Creating a Market-Tested Business Model
courses.description: Course provides an experiential learning opportunity, showing how a successful business model can be created through the use of customer and market validation process.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Decision Analysis
courses.description: Through lectures, role playing and case studies, students will develop an understanding of how decisions are made, the factors and biases that affect them, the tools that have been developed as a result, and the limitations that remain. The goal is to provide students with a solid foundation in the fundamentals of decision theory. By introducing real world applications that have a direct connection to the students, they can apply what they have learned to their own decisions.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Special Topics in Business and Management
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided there is no duplication of course content.
courses.description: Courses provide for the study of topics of current interest in the areas of, business, technology management, entrepreneurship, and other issues related to management and creation of sustainable businesses.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Understanding AI in Business: Core Foundations of Business Strategy
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided there is no duplication of course content.

Finally, the course explores how AI can be strategically applied across different industries and sectors to drive innovation and business development.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Intellectual Property and Patent Litigation
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided there is no duplication of course content.
courses.description: Patent Litigation is a fact of life for entrepreneurs in high technology. If you have a viable technology in a commercially promising field, you will likely be sued for patent infringement or have to sue someone for infringing your patents. This course presents and discusses many important steps and issues in these legal processes. Illustrations of the role of these components in trials are given based on instructor’s 20+ years of experience as a technical expert witness, including cases involving Intel, Qualcomm, Broadcom, AT&T, Alcatel, Ericsson, Microsoft, and Apple, and common technologies, such as Wi-Fi access points, digital cellular, audio coding, speech coding, video coding, Bluetooth, multimedia protocols, and computer networks.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Managing Social Innovation
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided there is no duplication of course content.
courses.description: Social innovation and social entrepreneurship describe novel approaches to tackling complex social problems. Platforms and emerging technologies offer new possibilities for action. We adopt the perspectives of various actors (individual, non-profits, entrepreneurial companies, large companies, and governments) engaged in social innovation processes, debating the benefits, challenges, and trade-offs associated with their participation. The highly interactive class involves case studies, experiential exercises, and student presentations.

courses.title: Sport Business Strategy & Innovation

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Independent Studies in Technology Management
courses.description: Directed individual study.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Opportunities and Perspectives in Technology, Business, and Society
courses.description: Lecture series where entrepreneurial, technological,business and governmental leaders share their lessons of experience and discuss current business issues. For anyone interested in entrepreneurship, management, technology development and commercialization and the impact that innovation has on society.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Business Strategy & Leadership Skills
courses.description: Course covers business principles relevant to todays increasingly competitive international business environment in four areas: Competitive Strategy and General Management; Accounting and Finance; Marketing and Sales; and Business Ethics.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Managing for Innovation
courses.description: Examination of communication and key management functions; envisioning and strategic planing; creating high performance teams; establishing appraisal/reward systems; innovation and organizational change. Emphasis on leading innovative technical people; leadership that fosters entrepreneurship and intrapreneurship; new forms of organizing.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Entrepreneurship
courses.description: Learn how to start any type of venture; for profit, non-profit, service, sole-proprietorship, with a focus on high-tech ventures. Analysis of new business opportunities, development of customer-centric value propositions, financing, marketing, selling, and protection of intellectual property.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Entrepreneurial Marketing
courses.description: Introduction to basic marketing concepts and how these concepts can be applied to any organization, particularly technology firms. Additionally, they will be introduced to how management of the marketing function within an organization is critical to the organizations success.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: New Venture Finance
courses.description: Provides students with the essential tools to understand and analyze financial information and financing strategies for new ventures. Major topics covered include the analyses of financial information, sources of financing, valuation models, deal structures particular to new ventures, forecasting models, capital budgeting, and risk analysis in investment decisions.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Creating a Market-Tested Business Model
courses.description: Course will provide an experiential learning opportunity showing how a successful business model can be created through the use of the customer and market validation process.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Organizational Behavior
courses.description: Course provides foundation knowledge in Organizational Behavior.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Organization Theory
courses.description: Students gain exposure to various theories of organizing.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Technology Strategy
courses.description: Exposes students to a broad foundation in technology management strategy research.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Networks and Innovation
courses.description: Exploration of how organizing processes enable and constrain the development and use of technology innovations.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Technology and Organizational Change
courses.description: Examines fundamental questions and approaches to the study of technology and organizations including how organizational structures enable and constrain the development of new technologies, and how new technologies enable changes in the process of organizing. The purpose of the course is to provide students with a thorough grounding in various theoretical perspectives on technology development and use.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Teams and Meso-Organizational Theory
courses.description: Organizational science is an interdisciplinary field that draws primarily on psychology, social psychology, sociology, and economics. As such, the field spans from what is often called “micro” (organizational behavior) to “macro” (organization theory). This course introduces students to many of the core theoretical underpinnings of what sits in the middle: “meso” organizational theories. Meso-research generally looks at intra-organizational processes, or what connects individuals and organizations. Using teams as a pro-typical example, teams are groups of individuals where the dynamics between individuals shape organizational outcomes.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Proseminar: Theory, Research, and Practicum
courses.description: Required seminar that offers current advances, foundational, integrative, and socialization content.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Qualitative Methods
courses.description: Qualitative methods are increasingly common in social science fields. In this doctoral seminar, we will explore the research approaches and methodological practices associated with designing, conducting and publishing high-quality field research. We will focus on the processes of observation, interviewing, discovery, justification, theorizing, and writing. The course is relevant for those interested in conducting qualitative research (either by itself or as a mixed methods approach), as well as for readers of publications based on qualitative data. The course will be practicum-based; we will be using these techniques to collect and analyze data.
