Perfect for students from all majors looking to enhance their career readiness.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Work in an Age of Intelligent Technologies
courses.description: We have long predicted radical economic and social transformation given the introduction of ostensibly "intelligent" technologies into the world of work. Using this doctoral seminar, we assess these claims so that we can do more useful research. Focusing on work means we consider analysis from a wide range of disciplines and sources, ranging from economics, organization studies, sociology, human-computer/robot interaction, ethics, law, political science, corporate/public research and beyond.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Readings in Technology, Work and Organizations
courses.description: This seminar focuses on important and notable books in the fields of technology, work and organization studies. The books that comprise the syllabus vary from year to year. The agenda is not only to impart substantive knowledge and promote discussion and debate, but also to provide a venue for a community of scholars interested in technology, work and organizations. Because the seminars content is designed to change with each iteration, students may take this seminar more than once.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Venture Capital and Private Equity
courses.description: This course provides an overview of how VC and PE firms operate. Topics include how VC/PE firms are structured and how they manage a fund over the course of its life cycle: raising a fund, sourcing deals, evaluating investment opportunities, valuing businesses, negotiating term sheets with entrepreneurs, adding value to portfolio companies, and exiting investments. While this course takes the perspective of the investor, it will also cover the funding life cycle of a typical start-up with an emphasis on what the roles of VC and PE are relative to other sources of financing. Course material will be presented primarily through case studies and selected readings.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Discourse and Institutions
courses.description: Gives students a an understanding of how systems of meaning such as cultural frames, discourse systems, categorical logics, rhetorical forms, conventions of understanding, subjective field mappings, collective ontologies or institutional logics operate so as to define the nature of markets, technologies, organizations, and organizational environments.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Digital Marketing
courses.description: This course equips graduate students with modern strategic marketing skills for today’s digital and AI-enabled business environment. Students analyze markets, competitors, customers, and channels to develop actionable go-to-market strategies for startups and established tech companies. Emphasis is placed on upstream strategy, downstream execution, and real-world application through case studies, team projects, guest speakers, and an industry-reviewed capstone presentation.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Strategy for Technology-Driven Companies
courses.description: Business models and structures for value creation, innovation, competitiveness; leadership and decisions. Features case studies and discussions to understand approaches and techniques to manage technological innovation and change within their organizations, including design and incentivization of teams and organizations to promote innovation. Understanding industry and technology impacts on business model selection and evolution. Special emphasis on sustainable business practices and strategies to maintain a competitive global business.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Finance and Accounting for Technology-Driven Companies
courses.description: Covers the major concepts, principles, and analytical tools that support financial-based managerial decision-making. Modules include measuring and analyzing financial performance, planning and budgeting, developing forecasts and financial pro-formas, time value of money, cost of capital, risk/return trade-offs, capital budgeting and investing, cash and working capital management, and cost accounting and analysis. Emphasis will be on applying these concepts and tools in technology businesses.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Data Science and Decision Making
courses.description: Theoretical models and mathematical tools for quantitative analysis, statistics, decision theory, management. Students will learn how various business situations are modeled and optimized effectively using mathematical modeling and quantitative techniques. Examples include time-series analysis, regression, optimization (linear, nonlinear, and discrete), probabilistic modeling, decision analysis, and simulation.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Project Management in New Product Development
courses.description: Provides students with knowledge and tools to manage complex projects and operations to ensure that a project is completed on time, within budget, and with high quality by exploring specific techniques for accomplishing those three goals. Introduction to commonly used business systems and strategies for managing Value/Supply Chains, Information, Human Resources, considerations and strategies for global business operations. Prepares students to manage people, budgets, scheduling, and quality of projects.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Innovation in the Digital Era
courses.description: This course provides students with the knowledge and skills to foster and maintain innovation in firms. The course covers traditional topics in innovation as well as the increasingly central role of digital technologies as both facilitators of innovation and as innovation products.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Creating Value Through Human Capital
courses.description: Explores human capital topics including employee selection, performance management, training and development, compensation, downsizing, and human capital analytics. Provides an understanding of how organizations manage knowledge assets for strategic advantage, and offers skills for managing in knowledge-intensive organizations.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Leading Technology Teams
courses.description: Technology firms rely on teams for critical R&D and project work. Introduces research findings and practical skills to leverage team-based capabilities and avoid the pitfalls of teamwork. Opportunities to hone team leadership and teamwork skills through case analyses and experiential exercises.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Entrepreneurship
courses.description: This course covers the fundamentals of entrepreneurship, including product ideation, forming and building a startup team, market validation, business model development, go-to-market strategies, capital acquisition, and building competitive insulation.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Learning to Work with Intelligent Machines
courses.description: The age of intelligent technologies is upon us, and work will never be the same. Individuals, teams, and organizations that can discover and adapt to new ways of working with technologies such as AI and robotics will enjoy more success than those who do not. Through unconventional, practical use of AI itself, this course explores research-backed approaches that will help us develop skill with intelligent technologies - in ourselves and others. We build managerial ability in this domain as well: the knowhow required to design work that brings humans and intelligent technologies together to produce more valuable outcomes than they could apart.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Digital Transformation
courses.description: Introduces concepts, theories, and evidence about how companies are changing in the digital era. The course examines the drivers of digital transformation and explores the evidence on how successful companies make good strategic decisions in the rapidly changing digital environment, how companies can effectively manage and exploit their data assets, and how to implement digital tools in ways that improve organizational culture and collaboration.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Negotiation for Technology Managers
courses.prereq_text: Only students enrolled in the Master of Technology Management professional degree program may register for this course.
courses.description: The strategy and psychology of negotiation. You will learn about the science underlying the social dynamics of negotiations, gain insights into your own preferences, how to prepare for negotiations, and practice applying these lessons in role-play simulations. By the end of the course, you will have greater understanding and confidence in your abilities to create and claim value through negotiations in your personal and professional life.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Special Issues in Technology Commercialization
courses.description: This course is intended to provide current focused research and theory on newly developing issues in specific technological or managerial subjects.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Special Topics in Technology Management
courses.description: Courses provide for the study of topics of current interest in the areas of, business, technology management, entrepreneurship, and other issues related to management and creation of sustainable businesses.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Leading Teams
courses.description: Technology firms rely on teams for critical R&D and project work. Introduces research findings and practical skills to leverage team-based capabilities and avoid the pitfalls of teamwork. Opportunities to hone team leadership and teamwork skills through case analyses and experiential exercises.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: AI Building Intensive
courses.description: Equips students with hands-on skills in applying AI to core business tasks, including rapid prototyping, preparing data for analysis and running regressions, and building agents for process redesign. Learn to integrate AI tools into real business workflows, moving from experimentation to practical application. At the end of the course, students will submit a professional portfolio of their work, demonstrating their ability to use AI strategically in a business context.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Branding
courses.description: A key part of developing a successful business is to build a well-regarded brand. In this course, students learn the fundamentals of building individual, product and organizational brands. The course emphasizes strategies and tactics for brand building and brand management in technology-based companies.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Special Topics in Technology Management
courses.description: Teaches students fundamentals of business communication, and develops skills for crafting and delivering persuasive and effective messages to different audiences.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Digital Transformation
courses.description: Digital technologies are accelerating the pace of change. To survive and thrive, todays organizations need to use these new technologies to continually innovate and redesign their current work practices. Digital transformation creates the opportunity to radically change the way work is done so that organizations can continue to grow and compete. This course provides a detailed framework for implementing digital transformation to enable fundamental organizational change.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Current Issues in Technology Management
courses.description: Focuses on the latest research and trends in managing technology teams and work. Topics may include those that integrate across other courses, as well introduce new concepts.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: MTM Internship
courses.description: MTM students can gain hands-on, real-world experience through internship positions with technology-driven companies and organizations. The MTM Internship course will provide academic support and professional guidance to students during their internships. Activities include regular check-ins with the instructor, keeping a journal of skills used and learned, and a final paper or presentation based on the internship experience.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Negotiation
courses.description: The strategy and psychology of negotiation. You will learn about the science underlying the social dynamics of negotiations, gain insights into your own preferences, how to prepare for negotiations, and practice applying these lessons in role-play simulations. By the end of the course, you will have greater understanding and confidence in your abilities to create and claim value through negotiations in your personal and professional life.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Capstone Project
courses.description: Students work in teams under the direction of a faculty advisor and industrial sponsor to tackle a management consulting project. Communication, reporting and presentation skills are also covered. Course emphasizes practical, hands-on experience, and integrates skills acquired in courses completed in previous quarter.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Professional Skills and Career Readiness
courses.description: In this course, students will learn skills for effective communication in the workplace, including presenting and public speaking, email etiquette, delivering feedback, and using AI. Students will also participate in career readiness activities such as building LinkedIn profiles, networking, crafting elevator pitches, and career exploration. Finally, students will have the opportunity to improve their fluency with reading financial statements and using common business applications such as Excel.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Field Project
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing, must be enrolled in MTM degree program.
courses.description: Students work in teams under the direction of a faculty advisor and industrial sponsor to tackle a management consulting project. Communication, reporting and presentation skills will also be covered. Course emphasizes practical, hands-on experience, and integrates skills acquired in courses completed in previous quarter.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Field Project
courses.prereq_text: Graduate standing, must be enrolled in MTM degree program.
courses.description: Students work in teams under the direction of a faculty advisor and industrial sponsor to tackle a management consulting project. Communication, reporting and presentation skills will also be covered. Course emphasizes practical, hands-on experience, and integrates skills acquired in courses completed in previous quarter.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Directed Research
courses.description: Individual tutorial. Provides students with supervised research experience including any of the following: reviewing literature, formulating research questions, designing measures, collecting and analyzing data, and writing papers.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Preparation for the Qualifying Exam
courses.prereq_text: Completion of:32 units of theory/research courses16 units of Methods courses8 units of Elective courses
courses.description: Directed group or individual preparation for the doctoral qualifying examination.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Preparation for Qualifying Paper
courses.prereq_text: Completion of: 32 units of Theory/Research courses, 16 units of Methods courses, and 8 units of Elective courses.
courses.description: Directed preparation for the doctoral qualifying paper.

courses.subject: TMP
courses.title: Dissertation Preparation
courses.prereq_text: Consent of department; advancement to candidacy.
courses.description: Course is reserved for writing the dissertation.

courses.subject: TMP W
courses.title: Fundamentals of Business Strategy
courses.description: An introduction to business strategy, principles and practices required for business success in the competitive market place. Students are exposed to key management theories, models and tools including competitive strategy, finance, planning, new product development, marketing, leadership and others.

courses.subject: W L CS
courses.title: Writing and Literature Colloquium
courses.description: UCSB faculty working in Creative Writing, Writing Studies, and Literary Studies present their research or creative work to expose students to examples of topics, theories, and methods in those disciplines.

courses.subject: W L CS
courses.title: First Year Colloquium Seminar
courses.description: Students engage in discussions of the presentations given in the Writing and Literature Colloquium. Focuses on introducing the disciplines and exploring the relationships between the material and the students interests.

courses.subject: W L CS
courses.title: Second Year Colloquium Seminar
courses.description: Students engage in discussions of the presentations given in the Writing and Literature Colloquium. Encourages deeper engagement with the material of the colloquium through reading of complementary texts and exploring application of methods and theories to the work students will commit to in the Mid-Residency Review.

courses.subject: W L CS
courses.title: Mid-Residency Review
courses.description: Students present independent projects as a part of their required Mid-Residency Review.

courses.subject: W L CS
courses.title: Group Studies
courses.description: Student-directed discussion and study in a variety of subjects within Writing and Literature.

courses.subject: W L CS
courses.title: Introdution to Creative Writing
courses.description: Provides an introduction to the major genres of creative writing, including fiction, poetry, and creative nonfiction. Focuses on the vocabulary and techniques of creative writing as well as the writing process.

courses.subject: W L CS
courses.title: Introductory Poetry Workshop
courses.description: Introduction to the craft of poetry writing. Students develop original works of poetry to be read and discussed in a workshop setting.

courses.subject: W L CS
courses.title: Introductory Fiction Workshop
courses.description: Introduction to the craft of fiction writing. Students develop original works of short fiction to be read and discussed in a workshop setting.

courses.subject: W L CS
courses.title: Introductory Creative Nonfiction Workshop
courses.description: Introduction to the craft of creative nonfiction writing. Students develop original works of short creative nonfiction to be read and discussed in a workshop setting.

courses.subject: W L CS
courses.title: Introductory Screenwriting Workshop
courses.description: Introduction to the craft of screenwriting. Students develop original works for the screen to be read and discussed in a workshop setting.

courses.subject: W L CS
courses.title: Introduction to Writing Studies
courses.description: Provides an introduction to the intellectual orientation, practices, and epistemologies of Writing Studies.

courses.subject: W L CS
courses.title: Introduction to Literary Studies
courses.description: Provides an introduction to the intellectual orientation, practices, and epistemologies of Literary Studies.

courses.subject: W L CS
courses.title: Poetry Workshop
courses.description: Students write original poems to be read and discussed in a workshop setting. Students learn the essentials of the craft of poetry as well as strategies to generate and revise work.

courses.subject: W L CS
courses.title: Fiction Workshop
courses.description: Students write original works of fiction to be read and discussed in a workshop setting. Students learn the essentials of the craft of fiction writing as well as strategies to generate and revise work.

courses.subject: W L CS
courses.title: Creative Nonfiction Workshop
courses.description: Students write original works of creative nonfiction to be read and discussed in a workshop setting. Students learn the essentials of the craft of creative nonfiction as well as strategies to generate and revise work.

courses.subject: W L CS
courses.title: Beginning Screenwriting Workshop
courses.description: Students learn the basic techniques of screenwriting. Students write original screenplays to be read and discussed in a workshop setting.

courses.subject: W L CS
courses.title: Advanced Screenwriting Workshop
courses.description: Students learn advanced techniques of screenwriting. Students write original screenplays to be read and discussed in a workshop setting.

courses.subject: W L CS
courses.title: Graphic Novel Workshop
courses.description: Students write and illustrate original comic scripts to be read and discussed in a workshop setting. Students learn the essentials of the craft of graphic novel writing as well as strategies to generate and revise work.

courses.subject: W L CS
courses.title: Multimedia Writing Workshop
courses.description: Students write original multimedia compositions to be read and discussed in a workshop setting. Students learn the essentials of multimedia composing as well as strategies to generate and revise. work.

courses.subject: W L CS
courses.title: Multigenre Writing Workshop
courses.description: Students write original work in multiple genres to be read and discussed in a workshop setting. Students learn strategies to generate and revise work.

courses.subject: W L CS
courses.title: Topics in Literary Studies
courses.description: Intensive study of varying topics in literary studies, including single authors, genres, themes.

courses.subject: W L CS
courses.title: Topics in Literary Studies - Translation
courses.description: Intensive study of varying topics in literary studies, including single authors, genres, themes.

courses.subject: W L CS
courses.title: Reading Like a Writer - Single Author Study
courses.description: Invites students to complete intensive reading the works of a single author from the perspective of a writer. Students focus on how the elements of the craft demonstrated by the author might apply to their own work.

courses.subject: W L CS
courses.title: Reading Like a Writer - Genre Study
courses.description: Invites students to complete intensive reading of a single genre from the perspective of a writer. Students focus on how the elements of the genre might apply to their own work.

courses.subject: W L CS
courses.title: Genre Study - Contemporary Screenwriters
courses.description: Examines how contemporary screenwriters have approached the adaption of novels into film. This course involves study of story structure and full character development into screenplays.

courses.subject: W L CS
courses.title: Genre Study - Film as Literature
courses.description: Introduces students to films and literature in general, screenwriting, how the written word is translated to the screen, how the written word in another language is translated, and cultural and historical aspects of adaptation.

courses.subject: W L CS
courses.title: Advanced Literary Criticism in Theory and Practice
courses.description: This course provides students with an advanced understanding of the theory and practice of literary criticism. Course readings represent a wide range of methodologies and models for interpretation, including New Criticism, New Historicism, Feminism, Queer theory, and Postcolonialism, among others. Students will pursue advanced projects in literary criticism informed by their knowledge of the theoretical basis for their explorations and the practices of other literary and cultural critics. Although there are no specific prerequisites for the course, students will be expected to read and respond to challenging texts in both oral and written discussion, including reading responses and a large-scale (ten pages or more) work of scholarship.

courses.subject: W L CS
courses.title: Reading Like a Writer - Thematic Study
courses.description: Invites students to complete intensive reading on a single theme from the perspective of a writer. Students focus on how the elements of the theme might apply to their own work.

courses.subject: W L CS
courses.title: Topics in Writing Studies
courses.description: Intensive study of varying topics in the field of writing studies.

courses.subject: W L CS
courses.title: Topics in Writing Studies - Creative Writing Studies
courses.description: Study of the practice and theories of creative writing.

courses.subject: W L CS
courses.title: Linguistic Justice
courses.description: W&L CS 160LJ, Linguistic Justice, focuses on how Writing Studies as a discipline approaches issues of language with a focus on justice. Rhetoric is such a key part of Writing Studies, so we will look at rhetorical situations that deal specifically with linguistic choices and expectations. Because this class will be taught at UCSB, which has both HSI and AAPI designations, we will investigate the linguistic injustices facing these communities and others in US classrooms, communities, and the larger political sphere. Issues of accessibility will also be addressed. Students can expect to read a mixture of public and academic scholarship on these topics and to engage in written genres that address both audiences.

courses.subject: W L CS
courses.title: Rhetoric of Reproductive Justice
courses.description: This course is structured around the three major tenets of reproductive justice—the right to have children, the right to not have children, and the right to parent children in safe and healthy environments. Students will engage with each of these tenets through readings and assignments that focus on the rhetorical, cultural, and historical significance of these three core elements to the ever expanding field of reproductive justice.

courses.subject: W L CS
courses.title: Topics in Writing Studies - STEM Stories
courses.description: Drawing upon research in writing studies, this course examines the work that stories (narratives) do within various STEM contexts. All majors, and all levels of STEM expertise, are welcome.

courses.subject: W L CS
courses.title: Topics in Multimedia Writing
courses.description: Intensive study of varying topics in the area of multimedia writing in the field of writing studies.

courses.subject: W L CS
courses.title: Introduction of Literary Publishing
courses.description: Students are introduced to the art and business of literary publishing in preparation for work on Spectrum Literary Journal and careers in writing or publishing.

courses.subject: W L CS
courses.title: Literary Publishing: Selection
courses.description: Students read and select works to be published from submissions to Spectrum Literary Journal. Topics covered include establishing an editorial perspective, developing and soliciting content.

courses.subject: W L CS
courses.title: Literary Publishing: Copyediting and Design
courses.description: Students copyedit works to be published in Spectrum Literary Journal and design the annual issue. Topics covered include promotion, document design and layout, and strategies for copyediting.

courses.subject: W L CS
courses.title: Junior Tutorial
courses.description: Students work independently with their faculty advisor to develop information and expertise necessary for their senior portfolio. May include training in methods, apprenticeship experience, or independent reading and coursework.

courses.subject: W L CS
courses.title: Senior Portfolio
courses.description: Students work independently with their faculty advisor to complete their senior portfolio.

courses.subject: W L CS
courses.title: Internship
courses.description: Academic credit for professional experience with an approved organization or individual.

courses.subject: W L CS
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Serious independent study in writing and literature with consenting faculty member.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Approaches to University Writing
courses.prereq_text: Has not completed the Entry Level Writing Requirement and received a score of 6 or lower on the Analytical Writing Placement Exam.
courses.comments: Open to students who haven't satisfied the Entry Level Writing Requirement. Not open for credit if student completed English 1, Writing 1LK, Writing 1E or passed an AP English exam with a 3 or higher.
courses.description: Principles of critical reading, thinking, and writing in the university. Writing focuses on analysis of academic discourse and development of rhetorical strategies. Completion with a grade of C or better meets Entry Level Writing Requirement.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: ACE Approaches to University Writing
courses.prereq_text: Has not completed the Entry Level Writing Requirement and received a score of 6 or lower on the Analytical Writing Placement Exam or score of 1 on Collaborative Writing Placement Exam.
courses.comments: Open to students who haven't satisfied the Entry Level Writing Requirement. Not open for credit if a student completed English 1, Writing 1, Writing 1LK, Writing 1E or passed an AP English exam with a 3 or higher. Priority enrollment for EOP students.
courses.description: Principles of critical reading, thinking, and writing in the university. Writing focuses on analysis of academic discourse and development of rhetorical strategies. The Academic Communities of Excellence (ACE) version of this course provides a smaller, more dynamic learning environment to support student success at the university. Completion with a grade of C or better meets Entry Level Writing Requirement.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Approaches to University Writing for Engineers
courses.prereq_text: Has not completed the Entry Level Writing Requirement and received a score of 6 or lower on the Analytical Writing Placement Exam.Freshmen only; open to ECE, Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, and Computer Engineering majors only.
courses.comments: Open to students who have not satisfied the Entry Level Writing requirement. Not open for credit if completed English 1, Writing 1, Writing 1LK, or if passed an AP English exam with a 3 or higher.
courses.description: Principles of critical reading, thinking, and writing in the university. Students analyze academic discourse, develop rhetorical strategies for exposition and argument, practice examination writing, and write and revise papers.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Academic Writing
courses.prereq_text: Satisfaction of the Entry Level Writing requirement or Linguistics 12 with a grade of "C" or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed English 2 or Writing 2E or 2LK or have passed AP English exam (Composition and Literature or Language and Composition) with a score of 4 or higher.
courses.description: A writing course focusing on developing analytical skills, synthesizing multiple sources, sustaining coherent arguments, and revising for clarity of style. Reading and writing assignments are drawn from a range of academic disciplines.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: ACE Academic Writing
courses.prereq_text: Satisfaction of the Entry Level Writing requirement or Linguistics 12 with a grade of "C" or better.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed English 2 or Writing 2, 2E, or 2LK or have passed AP English exam (Composition and Literature or Language and Composition) with a score of 4 or higher. Priority enrollment for EOP students.
courses.description: Focuses on developing analytical skills, synthesizing multiple sources, sustaining coherent arguments, and revising for clarity of style. Reading and writing assignments are drawn from a range of academic disciplines. The Academic Communities of Excellence (ACE) version of this course provides a smaller, more dynamic learning environment to support student success at the university.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Academic Writing for Engineers
courses.prereq_text: Satisfaction of the Entry Level Writing requirement or Linguistics 12; freshmen only; open to ECE, Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, and Computer Engineering majors only.
courses.comments: Not open for credit if student has completed English 2, Writing 2LK, Writing 2 or has passed the AP English exam (Composition and Literature or Language and Composition) with a score of 4 or higher.
courses.description: A writing course focusing on developing analytical skills, synthesizing multiple sources, sustaining coherent arguments, and revising for clarity of style. Reading and writing assignments are drawn from a range of engineering disciplines.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Public Speaking
courses.comments: English 18 and Writing 18 are the same course. This course will not count toward the English major or minor requirements.
courses.description: Practical and historical introduction to public speaking in context (e.g., legal, political, professional). Focuses on critical rhetorical analysis of speeches. Students write and deliver original speeches while offering feedback on those of their peers. Students also write an analytical essay.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: The Gabler Professional Writing Seminar
courses.prereq_text: Writing 1 or fulfillment of Entry Level Writing Requirement.
courses.description: A cohort-based seminar focusing on the strategic habits of mind necessary for effective professional leadership and communication. Students cultivate an "executive" toolkit to analyze audiences, manage resources, and execute decisions within diverse professional contexts. The curriculum centers on the creation of a comprehensive Professional Capstone Portfolio, developed through interactive workshops, guest lectures, and weekly consultation with embedded peer mentors. Students emerge with a polished professional identity and a cohesive body of work demonstrating their ability to think and lead strategically.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Gabler Promise Scholars Writing Seminar
courses.prereq_text: Writing 1 or fulfillment of Entry Level Writing Requirement.
courses.description: The Gabler Promise Scholars Writing Seminar is for selected students in the Promise Scholars Program who will take the course each quarter of their sophomore year. The course is designed to help scholars develop strategies for writing effectively in personal/creative, academic, and civic contexts. Mentoring and support through this course is intended to support students development as writers and enhance opportunities for success at UC Santa Barbara and beyond.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Writing and the Research Process
courses.comments: Not open for credit if student completed English 3, Writing 50E or 50LK or passed AP English exam (Composition & Lit. or Lang. & Composition) with a 5. See writing program for section descriptions.
courses.description: A writing course addressing the analytical skills underlying the research processes of various academic and professional communities. Sections vary in topic and disciplinary emphasis.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Writing and the Research Process for Engineers
courses.prereq_text: Writing 2 or 2E or 2LK; freshmen only; open to ECE, Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, and Computer Engineering majors only.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed English 3 or Writing 50 or 50LK or have passed the AP English exam (Composition and Literature or Language and Composition) with a score of 5.
courses.description: A writing course addressing the analytical skills underlying the research process of academic and professional communities within engineering.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Independent Studies in Writing
courses.prereq_text: Lower-division standing; students must have satisfied the Subject A and Writing 2 requirements; consent of instructor.
courses.comments: Students must have at least a 3.0 GPA for the preceding three quarters and are limited to 5 units per quarter, 15 units per year, and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
courses.description: Independent studies in writing.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Writing and Generative AI
courses.description: Study of and practice with writing and generative AI in academic, civic, and professional settings, with emphasis on strategic communication, metacognitive awareness, epistemic development, and ethical decision-making.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Writing Creative Nonfiction
courses.description: Course in creative nonfiction, a prose form whose practitioners consciously merge elements of traditional fiction and nonfiction. Students get extensive practice in reading and composing within this genre.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Writing with Code
courses.description: Design and analysis of texts that integrate both writing and coding components, such as video games, data visualizations, web documents, and interactive narratives. No prior coding experience necessary.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Writing for Change
courses.description: Students apply rhetorical strategies in a series of assignments designed to implement change. Emphasis on writing, speaking, and visuals as a means of effecting change across personal, academic, workplace, and civic contexts.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Writing for Cultural Rhetorics
courses.description: Writing 105CR offers students writing practice that will serve both to advance their undergraduate work in cultural rhetorics and to prepare them for graduate level study or professional activity relating to cultural rhetorics. Students explore central issues and problems within cultural rhetorics scholarship while practicing strategies for evaluating and writing short and long papers.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Writing in Community
courses.prereq_text: Writ 2 or Writ 2E or Writ 2LK or Exam: AP 36 >=4 or Exam: AP 37 >=4 or Exam: WAIV AW >= 1 or Exam: IB BL >= 6 or Exam: IB E >= 6; upper division standing.
courses.description: Analysis and practice of various forms of community-based writing (such as reports and proposals) by and for local groups that promote the social good. Attention is paid to direct interaction with the community, research, metacognitive awareness, genre awareness, and writing conventions.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Grammar and Stylistics
courses.description: Focuses on grammar and stylistics for professional writers and editors. The emphasis is practical and analytical, attending to issues of sentence structure and semantics and stylistics, in order to become more rhetorically effective writers.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Multimedia Writing
courses.comments: WRIT W 105M is the online version of WRIT 105M.
courses.description: Focuses on new modes of writing and publishing enabled by computer technology. Projects involve analyzing, creating, reading about, and reflecting on multimedia writing. Students create works suitable for web or other digital formats.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Writing and Philosophies of Language
courses.description: Introduction to theories of language and communication, with concentration on linguistic structure and the conditions through which meaning is produced and transmitted incommunication situations. Students reflect on writing, and produce written research, in a related area of inquiry.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Writing and Public Discourse
courses.description: Introduction to writing and public discourse in local, regional, national, and global contexts through analysis of writing in civic contexts, political activism, and public policy. Students reflect on, and produce written research in a related area of inquiry.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Writing for Public Speaking
courses.description: Analysis and practice of writing, researching, and delivering oral presentations for various academic and professional audiences. Course efforts focus primarily on creating clear and engaging speech scripts, multimedia support, and related presentation documents.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Rhetoric and Writing
courses.description: Traces the history, theory, and practice of rhetoric (effective persuasion) from classical times to the modern era. Students analyze key works and apply rhetorical strategies in written argumentation.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Writing About Sustainability
courses.description: Analysis and practice of various forms of writing that address sustainability in interdisciplinary contexts. Students will research, write, and reflect on concepts and practices of sustainability, examining the role of words and images in communicating sustainability ideas to diverse audiences.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Writing and Sound
courses.description: Students learn and write about sound in reflective, analytical, and rhetorical ways and incorporate sound or a sonic topic into writing and compositional projects.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Science Writing for the Public
courses.prereq_text: Writ 2 or Writ 2E or Writ 2LK or Exam: AP 36 >=4 or Exam: AP 37 >=4 or Exam: WAIV AW >= 1 or Exam: IB BL >= 6 or Exam: IB E >= 6; upper division standing.
courses.description: Focus on analyzing, practicing, and applying strategies for communicating scientific concepts, research projects, and findings with non-specialist audiences. Students will employ both traditional and new media forms of communicating scientific knowledge.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Writing in Community
courses.prereq_text: Writ 2 or Writ 2E or Writ 2LK or Exam: AP 36 >=4 or Exam: AP 37 >=4 or Exam: WAIV AW >= 1 or Exam: IB BL >= 6 or Exam: IB E >= 6; upper division standing.
courses.description: Analysis and practice of various forms of community-based writing (such as reports and proposals) by and for local groups that promote the social good. Attention is paid to direct interaction with the community, research, metacognitive awareness, genre awareness, and writing conventions.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Writing and Ethics
courses.prereq_text: Writing 2 or 2E or 2LK; upper-division standing; or Exam: AP 36 >=4 or Exam: AP 37 >=4 or Exam: WAIV AW >=1 or Exam: IB BL >=6 or Exam: IB E >=6
courses.description: Focus on ethics in writing, rhetoric, and communication. By researching, analyzing, and composing texts related to ethics in various genres and disciplines, students explore how writing contributes to the good life for individuals and communities.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Writing for Accounting Economics
courses.prereq_text: Writing 2 or 2E or 2LK; Economics 136A (may be taken concurrently); upper-division standing.
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed WRIT 109AC.
courses.description: Writing practices in academic and professional accounting. Research sources include publications, databases, case studies, interviews. Assignments include reports, correspondence, memorandum, presentations. Attention to critical thinking, research techniques, international context, use of information technology, and visual communications.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Business and Administrative Writing
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed English 109C or Writing 109EC.
courses.description: Analysis and practice in business genres that focuses on writing strategy, concise style, and visual aspects of communication. Attention to typical documents such as letters, memos, e-mail, proposals, and collaborative reports. Courses also typically integrate oral presentations, job search documents, and the use of relevant technology.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Digital Journalism
courses.description: Students acquire skills in digital journalism, including writing for web and social media using text, photo, graphics and video. The class forms an editorial group that covers campus events as well as profiles, interviews, blogs, and social media. Course work may be offered to UCSB's College of Letters and Science for publication.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Writing for Environmental Professions
courses.description: Analysis and practice of professional writing in addressing environmental topics such as water management, carbon neutrality, or sustainability. Attention to research methods, audience analysis, document design, conciseness, collaboration, and editing strategies.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Professional Writing for Global Careers
courses.description: Analysis and practice of writing in global contexts related to business, government, and non-governmental organizations. Attention to typical formats such as formal email, proposals, job application materials, and research reports, including a significant collaborative project. Emphasis on factors affecting international research and document design.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Journalism and News Writing
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed WRIT 109JW
courses.description: Analysis and practice of news writing for print, broadcast and digital media, with focus on inverted pyramid and feature style, interview techniques, background research, editing, writing to deadline, and ethical issues.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Legal Writing
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed English 109D or WRIT 109L
courses.description: Practice in applying rules to facts, analyzing issues, and writing clearly, succinctly, and cogently in various forms of legal discourse such as case briefs, law essays, persuasive letters, short office memoranda, mediation and appellate briefs. Fundamentals of legal research are touched upon.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Magazine Writing for Publication
courses.description: Focuses on interviews, writing, reviews, and general articles for print media, and submitting them for publication. Students learn about the audience and the demands of each genre, as well as editing skills and the rigor of deadlines.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Writing for Public Relations
courses.description: Analysis and practice of writing in the field of public relations with focus on the news release, web copy, brochures, media kits, and newsletters.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Technical Writing
courses.description: Analysis and practice in writing for technology users with attention given to task analysis, design principles, and writing strategies. Projects include technology related documents such as instructions, user manuals, online documentation, and web content. Final documents suitable for professional portfolio.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Writing Web Content
courses.prereq_text: Writ 2 or Writ 2E or Writ 2LK or Exam: AP 36 >=4 or Exam: AP 37 >=4 or Exam: WAIV AW >= 1 or Exam: IB BL >= 6 or Exam: IB E >= 6; upper division standing
courses.comments: WRIT 107WC is a legal repeat of WRIT W 107WC
courses.description: Analysis and practice with strategies underlying creation of Web 2.0 content. Students will create common content modalities that may include websites, blogs, email newsletters, and social media as used in professional contexts.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Writing for the Disciplines
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Analysis and practice of various forms of academic and professional writing for and in the disciplines.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Writing for Chicano/a Studies
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.
courses.description: Analysis and practice of various forms of writing and research methods in Chicana/o Studies. Attention to strategies for argumentation, analysis, organization, and documentation used in humanities and social sciences

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Writing for the Teaching Professions
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed English 106WP.
courses.description: Research, discussion, and analysis of current issues in educational theory,practice, and policy. Appropriate for prospective credential students.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Writing for Environmental Studies
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed English 109I.
courses.description: Analysis and practice of professional writing used in addressing environmental topics such as water management, carbon neutrality, and sustainability. Attention to research methods, audience analysis, document design, conciseness, collaboration, and editing strategies.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Writing about Film
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed English 109K or Writing 109FS.
courses.description: Analysis and practice of various forms of writing for film, including argumentative writing, film reviews, critical texts, and essays. Of special interest to majors in film studies, English, and social sciences.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Writing And Gender Studies
courses.comments: WRIT 109GS is the updated course number for WRIT 109WS. This course is considered a repeat of WRIT 109WS.
courses.description: Students research and analyze writing and rhetoric with a particular focus on the methods and theories of gender studies. Attention to strategies for argumentation, analysis, organization, and documentation used in humanities and social sciences. Writing projects incorporate interdisciplinary and multimedia sources.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Writing for Health Professions
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed English 109M.
courses.description: Strategy, analysis, format for various types of academic and professional writing in the health care field. Contemporary topics/issues will be the basis of study, discussion, research, and writing.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Writing for the Humanities
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed English 109H.
courses.description: Writing 109HU focuses on the analysis of various forms of writing for the humanities, both academic and professional. Attention is paid to the modes of argumentation, research methods, stylistic conventions, and development of original inquiry.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Writing for the Social Sciences
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed English 109B.
courses.description: Analysis and practice of various forms of writing appropriate for primary and secondary research in the social sciences. Research writing projects include literature reviews, research proposals, research reports, case studies, and theoretical analyses. Attention to disciplinary resources, formal conventions, and style.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Writing for Science and Technology
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed English 109A.
courses.description: Analysis and practice of various forms of scientific and technical writing,both academic and professional, such as reports, proposals, journal articles, and abstracts. Attention to research methods, design of papers, development of graphics, technical style, and editing strategies.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Writing for the Visual Arts
courses.comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed English 109E.
courses.description: Description, analysis, investigation, and theorization of art and its practice. Students will engage in various forms of critical and generative writing and multimedia composition for the visual arts, such as press releases, artist statements, curatorial statements, proposals, exhibition reviews, analytical essays, and creative projects. Of special interest to majors in the arts, communications, and cultural studies.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: HFA Web and Social Media Internship
courses.description: Students work in a small team to create, maintain and distribute digital content for the website and social media platforms of the Division of Humanities and Fine Arts, including written features, photography, videos and social media posts. This course is part of a year-long, seminar-style series. Registration is subject to instructor approval.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: RAAB Writing Fellow Seminar
courses.comments: Enrollment restricted to students accepted in Raab Writing Fellows program. Students can only receive credit for the program once (through either WRIT 131 or 131A-B-C).
courses.description: Students work on individual projects while consulting with mentors and preparing for the year-end showcase. Classes include workshops on research-based writing, guest lectures, and peer activities. Enrollment restricted to students accepted in Raab Writing Fellows program.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: RAAB Writing Fellow Seminar
courses.description: First course in the seminar-style year-long series for Raab Writing Fellows (WRIT 131A-B-C). Students work on individual projects while consulting with mentors and preparing for the year-end showcase. Classes include workshops on research-based writing, guest lectures, and peer activities. Enrollment restricted to students accepted in Raab Writing Fellows program.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Raab Writing Fellow Seminar
courses.description: Second course in the seminar-style year-long series for Raab Writing Fellows (WRIT 131A-B-C). Students work on individual projects while consulting with mentors and preparing for the year-end showcase. Classes include workshops on research-based writing, guest lectures, and peer activities. Enrollment restricted to students accepted in Raab Writing Fellows program.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Raab Writing Fellow Seminar
courses.description: Third course in the seminar-style year-long series for Raab Writing Fellows (WRIT 131A-B-C). Students work on individual projects while consulting with mentors and preparing for the year-end showcase. Classes include workshops on research-based writing, guest lectures, and peer activities. Enrollment restricted to students accepted in Raab Writing Fellows program.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Internship in Writing
courses.prereq_text: Upper-division standing and consent of department. Must be enrolled in the Professional Writing Minor.
courses.description: Fieldwork experiences to explore professional writing in particular workplace contexts. The professional writing may be in varied genres, in print and/or digital media. Students create documents for the instructor and participate in periodic seminars with the instructor and Minor students.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Copyediting
courses.prereq_text: At least one prior course from Writing 105AA-ZZ, 107AA-ZZ, and/or 109AA-ZZ; upper-division standing. Must be admitted to the Professional Writing Minor for enrollment.
courses.description: Develop expertise in the principles of grammar, punctuation, and copyediting. Application of these principles to a wide range of professional documents. Create style guides and notes to the authorto provide advice to authors on issues of clarity and ambiguityto supplement the copyedited work.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Style and Usage
courses.prereq_text: Writing 151A; upper-division standing. Must be admitted to the Minor in Professional Writing for enrollment.
courses.description: Editing of professional work, including best-selling nonfiction and fiction, with an emphasis on issues of style and usage. Collaborative magazine projectimagined, written, and edited solely by group members. The course concludes with collaborative presentations and a final print or online portfolio of student work.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Advanced Beat Reporting
courses.prereq_text: At least one prior course from Writing 105AA-ZZ, 107AA-ZZ, and/or 109AA-ZZ; upper-division standing. Must be admitted to the Professional Writing Minor for enrollment.
courses.comments: Course required for credit in the minor.
courses.description: The first of two capstone courses in the Journalism track of the Professional Writing Minor. Students pitch, report, write and revise news and feature articles in a particular "beat" area, enhancing their proficiency in journalistic research and writing.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Multiplatform Journalism
courses.prereq_text: Writing 152A; upper division standing. Must be admitted to the Minor in Professional Writing for enrollment.
courses.description: Second capstone course for the Journalism track in the Professional Writing Minor. Focus on creating a long form feature using narrative and multimedia elements (photos, videos, audio, data visualization) and a professional website featuring journalism writing samples suitable for professional audiences.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Civic Engagement and Public Writing
courses.prereq_text: At least one prior course from Writing 105AA-ZZ, 107AA-ZZ, and/or 109AA-ZZ; upper-division standing. Must be admitted to the Professional Writing Minor for enrollment.
courses.description: Focus on defining civic engagement, its forms and genres. Students explore intersections between individual agency and civic issues with an emphasis on public writing. Assignments involve the study and practice of writing by civically engaged citizens.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Writing for Civic Organizations
courses.prereq_text: Writing 153A; upper-division standing. Must be admitted to the Professional Writing Minor.
courses.description: Focus on the writing genres that advance the civic purpose of organizations. Students study and produce print and multi-media documents to meet the needs of civic organizations in management, marketing, public relations, and fundraising.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Document Design and Production
courses.prereq_text: At least one prior course from Writing 105AA-ZZ, 107AA-ZZ, and/or 109AA-ZZ; upper-division standing. Must be admitted to the Professional Writing Minor for enrollment.
courses.comments: Course required for credit in the minor.
courses.description: Information design in print media; focus on grammatical and rhetorical expertise. Projects include flyers, brochures, resumes, and other graphics, with a focus on understanding the intersections of writing and visual design. Project-based course culminating in print portfolio.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Digital Portfolio
courses.prereq_text: Writing 155A; upper-division standing. Must be admitted to the Professional Writing Minor for enrollment.
courses.comments: Course required for credit in the minor.
courses.description: Creation of digital work using software and coding. The major project is the design and production of a professional website, using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, WordPress, and other tools. Focus on developing effective design and communication skills within a digital environment.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Business Communication for Client Projects
courses.prereq_text: At least one prior course from Writing 105AA-ZZ, 107AA-ZZ, or 109AA-ZZ; upper-division standing. Must be admitted to the Professional Writing Minor for enrollment.
courses.description: Development of written, visual, and oral skills for the workplace. Students begin with a unit on personal branding, then move on to experiential learning through a client-based project. Working directly with clients in teams, students develop collaborative writing and project management skills in such professional genres as Gantt charts, style sheets, status reports, promotional plans, news releases, and formal reports. The course culminates in an oral presentation to the class and client on each team’s project.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Strategic Business Communication
courses.prereq_text: Writing 157A; upper-division standing; Must be admitted to the Minor in Professional Writing for enrollment.
courses.description: Through course readings and case study analysis, students will explore business communication strategy in reputation management, corporate social responsibility, crisis communication, and external/internal communication. Students also prepare a variety of professional documents for their final digital portfolio and online presence through the creation of a personal website.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Scientific Literacy
courses.prereq_text: At least one prior course from Writing 105AA-ZZ, 107AA-ZZ, or 109AA-ZZ; upper-division standing. Must be admitted to the Professional Writing Minor for enrollment.
courses.description: The first minor course (Writing 159A) focuses on the literacy skills necessary to understand and critically examine scientific research from across the disciplines. Students learn how to evaluate the quality of scientific information, examine science from inside a wider social context, and explore why the public sometimes resists the scientific consensus. Assignments might include a range of texts—such as academic essays, presentations, short videos, and podcasts—that examine the historical, ethical, and sociocultural dimensions of science.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Science Communication for the Public
courses.prereq_text: Writing 159A; upper-division standing. Must be admitted to the Professional Writing Minor.
courses.description: Second capstone course for the Science Communication track of the Professional Writing minor. Focus on critiquing and composing scientific content for nonspecialist and public audiences, using various genres, media, modes, and technologies. Project-based course culminating in document portfolio.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Theory and Practice of Writing Center Consulting
courses.description: Prepares students to tutor writing at the college level. Students respond to tutoring scenarios, respond to each others writing, learn to work with OWLS (on-line writing labs), and prepare a resource notebook for tutoring.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Digital Storytelling
courses.prereq_text: Must be admitted to the Professional Writing Minor for enrollment.
courses.comments: Elective course for credit in the minor.
courses.description: Analysis and production of multimedia, interactive, digital narratives in a range of genres and using a range of technologies.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Advanced Public Speaking
courses.prereq_text: Must be admitted to the Professional Writing Minor for enrollment.
courses.description: Advanced analysis and practice of writing and delivering oral presentations, including scripts and visual aids, with an emphasis on rhetoric and delivery techniques. Assignments include a career pitch, strategic industry analysis, and TED-style expert lecture for specific audiences and purposes.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Independent Studies in Writing
courses.comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters and are limited to 4 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined. Writing 199 may be repeated for credit to a maximum of 10 units.
courses.description: Writing, reading, and conference with specialized research or focus topic.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Academic Research Writing
courses.comments: Same course as Interdisciplinary 251.
courses.description: Study of and instruction in the writing of graduate academic documents, including proposals, theses, course papers, articles for publication, and C.V.'s. Emphasis on writing clearly and mastering disciplinary conventions.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Public Writing and Advocacy
courses.description: Through the analysis of public discourse, students will articulate their academicresearch expertise in the context of broader public discussions of social issues, with special attention to the writing conventions and genres best suited for advocacy.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Science Communication
courses.description: Provides a foundation in science communication practices that explain, persuade, describe, and entertain to graduate students in both STEM (scientific, engineering, technological and mathematical) and non-STEM disciplines. Coursework focuses on composition, public speaking, graphics designs and numeric representations for creating effective written works, talks, podcasts, blogs, videos, press releases, policy briefs, posters, and reports about scientific topics. Students will learn how to craft scientific stories that are accurate, realistic and compelling.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Introduction to Graduate Writing Expectations
courses.prereq_text: Graduate students must have completed no more than one year of course work to enroll. Should students attempt to enroll in any section of this course other than GRAD/WRIT 280AA, students must ensure that their disciplinary field is included in that special topic of the course.
courses.description: Graduate students who would like to develop their writing skills will have the opportunity to practice drafting and revising a variety of advanced writing assignmentscommon to the graduate experience. Students will first study the rhetorical features associated with various advanced graduate writing genres before producing disciplinary-specific versions of these texts.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Introduction to Graduate Writing Expectations
courses.prereq_text: Graduate students must have completed no more than one year of course work to enroll. Should students attempt to enroll in any section of this course other than GRAD/WRIT 280AA, students must ensure that their disciplinary field is included in that special topic of the course.
courses.description: Graduate students who would like to develop their writing skills will have the opportunity to practice drafting and revising a variety of advanced writing assignments common to the graduate experience. Students will first study the rhetorical features associated with various advanced graduate writing genres before producing disciplinary-specific versions of these texts.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Introduction to Article Writing
courses.prereq_text: Graduate students must have completed the relevant research/scholarship to produce an article. Students who are still in the middle of their research projects will not be admitted. Should students attempt to enroll in any section of this course other than GRAD/WRIT 281AA, students must ensure that their disciplinary field is included in that special topic of the course.
courses.description: Graduate students interested in learning the underlying conventions related to professional academic writing through article writing will have the opportunity to draft and revise a disciplinary-relevant article. Students will first study the rhetorical features associated with articles, by discipline, in order to learn the conventions pertinent to article writing instudents chosen fields. Then, students will produce a discipline and journal-specific draft of an article.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Thesis and Dissertation Structured Writing Communities
courses.prereq_text: Graduate students must have completed at least one chapter of a thesis/dissertation and still need to complete at least one more chapter. Letter of approval stating that the studentmeets the aforementioned conditions and is a good candidate for this course must be submitting by the student�s thesis/dissertation chair.
courses.description: Graduate students who have produced at least one chapter of their thesis or dissertation and who must still complete at least one more chapter will be provided with writing instruction, individual feedback, and writing time to complete their thesis/dissertation. Only advanced graduate writing will be drafted and considered in this course.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Thesis and Dissertation Structured Writing Communities
courses.prereq_text: Graduate students must have completed at least one chapter of a thesis/dissertation and still need to complete at least one more chapter. Letter of approval stating that the student meets the aforementioned conditions and is a good candidate for this course must be submitting by the student's thesis/dissertation chair.
courses.description: Graduate students who have produced at least one chapter of their thesis or dissertation and who must still complete at least one more chapter will be provided with writing instruction, individual feedback, and writing time to complete their thesis/dissertation. Only advanced graduate writing will be drafted and considered in this course.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Preparing for the Academic Job Market
courses.prereq_text: Students have to be, at the earliest, one year away from applying to the job market.
courses.description: Graduate students will have the job market process demystified while preparing a dossier of requested materials. Students will first study the rhetorical features associated with the major documents required for these positions and then produce discipline-specific drafts (with feedback provided).

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Writing Studies: Histories, Theories, and Methods
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to the history, theory, and research considerations of Writing Studies. It focuses on foundational historical movements in composition pedagogy, current trends in Writing Studies, and interdisciplinary approaches to the field, including selected research methodologies.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Writing Studies: Histories, Theories, and Methods
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to the history, theory, and research considerations of Writing Studies. It focuses on foundational historical movements in composition pedagogy, current trends in Writing Studies, and interdisciplinary approaches to the field.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Pedagogies of University Writing: Theory and Practice
courses.description: Explores theoretical foundations and practical approaches to teaching writing at the university and college level. Students will examine pedagogical theories, design writing prompts, and develop strategies for assessment and providing feedback. Assignments include writing teaching philosophies, crafting course materials, facilitating discussion, and reflective writing. By integrating theory and practice, students will gain a deeper understanding of the various facets involved in teaching writing in a postsecondary context.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Pedagogies of University Writing: Theory and Practice
courses.description: Explores theoretical foundations and practical approaches to teaching writing at the university and college level. Examines pedagogical theories, design writing prompts, and develop strategies for assessment and providing feedback. Assignments include writing teaching philosophies, crafting course materials, facilitating discussion, and reflective writing. Integrates theory and practice, for students to gain a deeper understanding of the various facets involved in teaching writing in a postsecondary context.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Directed Teaching
courses.prereq_text: Appointment as teaching assistant or associate title.
courses.comments: Yields no unit credit for advanced degrees.
courses.description: Teaching assistants must register during quarter of service for this course of supervision for instruction.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Academic Writing Instruction Theory and Practice
courses.prereq_text: Application submitted for Writing Program TA appointment.
courses.description: Preparatory orientation and concurrent training in composition theory and pedagogy for newly appointed Writing Program teaching assistants. Topics include theories of composition pedagogy, academic literacies, principles of instructional design and curriculum development, effective classroom practices, and assessment of student writing.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Proseminar in Writing Studies
courses.description: An introduction to the major lines of research and theory in the field of writing studies. The course emphasizes the roles writing plays in knowledge production and social organizations, and the contributions of research on writing to learning, instruction, and practice across disciplines, professions, and fields.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Proseminar in Writing Studies
courses.description: An introduction to the major lines of research and theory in the field of writing studies. The course emphasizes the roles writing plays in knowledge production and social organizations, and the contributions of research on writing to learning, instruction, and practice across disciplines, professions, and fields.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Proseminar in Writing Studies
courses.description: An introduction to the major lines of research and theory in the field of writing studies. The course emphasizes the roles writing plays in knowledge production and social organizations, and the contributions of research on writing to learning, instruction, and practice across disciplines, professions, and fields.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Pedagogies of University Writing: Theory and Practice
courses.description: Explores theoretical foundations and practical approaches to teaching writing at the university and college level. Students will examine pedagogical theories, design writing prompts, and develop strategies for assessment and providing feedback. Assignments include writing teaching philosophies, crafting course materials, facilitating discussion, and reflective writing. By integrating theory and practice, students will gain a deeper understanding of the various facets involved in teaching writing in a postsecondary context.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Directed Reading and Research
courses.comments: May be repeated for credit as determined by department chair.
courses.description: Group or individual tutorial.

courses.subject: WRIT W
courses.title: Rome: The Game
courses.comments: ARTHIW 6R and WRIT W 6R are the same course
courses.description: This online course presented as an adventure game introduces students to the art and archaeology of Rome, with assignments that focus on writing and the research process. The course asks students to determine whether or not a collection of ancient objects from an American museum should remain in the US or be sent back to Italy. Throughout the course, students excavate artifacts at a digital dig site, visit museums, explore Roman monuments, and navigate the shadowy world of the tombaroli (tomb robbers) and mafia-run black market for antiquities.

courses.subject: WRIT W
courses.title: Multimedia Writing Online
courses.comments: WRIT W 105M is the online version of WRIT 105M.
courses.description: Focuses on new modes of writing and publishing enabled by computer technology. Projects involve analyzing, creating, reading about, and reflecting on multimedia writing. Students create works suitable for web or other digital formats.

courses.subject: WRIT W
courses.title: Business and Administrative Writing
courses.comments: WRIT W 107B is the online version of WRIT 107B. Not open for credit to students who have completed English 109C or Writing 109EC.
courses.description: Analysis and practice in business genres that focus on writing strategy, concise style, and visual aspects of communication. Attention to typical documents such as letters, memos, e-mail, proposals, and collaborative reports. Courses also typically integrate oral presentations, job search documents, and the use of relevant technology.

courses.subject: WRIT W
courses.title: Legal Writing
courses.comments: WRIT W 107L is the online version of WRIT 107L. Not open for credit to students who have completed English 109D or WRIT 109L.
courses.description: Practice in applying rules to facts, analyzing issues, and writing clearly, succinctly, and cogently in various forms of legal discourse such as case briefs, law essays, persuasive letters, short office memoranda, mediation and appellate briefs. Fundamentals of legal research are touched upon.

courses.subject: WRIT W
courses.title: Writing Web Content Online
courses.prereq_text: Writ 2 or Writ 2LK or Writ 2E or AP36 >=4 or AP 37 >=4 or WAIV AW >=1 or IB BL >=6 or IB E >=6; upper division standing
courses.comments: WRIT W 107WC is a legal repeat of WRIT 107WC
courses.description: An online course in which students analyze the rhetorical strategies underlying creation of Web 2.0 content. Students create common content modalities that may include Websites, blogs, email newsletters, and social media as used in professional contexts.

courses.subject: WRIT W
courses.title: Writing for Science and Technology Online
courses.prereq_text: Writ 2 or Writ 2LK or Writ 2E or AP36 >=4 or AP 37 >=4 or WAIV AW >=1 or IB BL >=6 or IB E >=6
courses.description: An online class that analyzes and practices various forms of scientific and technical writing, both academic and professional, such as reports, proposals, journal articles, and abstracts. Attention to research methods, design of papers, digital visualizations, technical style, and editing strategies.
